hy57in/neighborhood-quest.desc: Neighborhood Quest — Explore, Capture, Remember: AI-powered 3D neighborhood exploration game built with Gemini 4 Argon & Three.js
hy57in/neighborhood-quest.readme:
# 🏡 Neighborhood Quest (동네 퀘스트)

**Capture Freely. Remember Vividly.**  
> **Turn your real-world neighborhood experiences into playful, explorable 3D memories powered by Gemini 4 Argon.**

🌐 **Live Demo (Google Cloud Run — `asia-northeast3`)**: **[https://neighborhood-quest-866062064970.asia-northeast3.run.app](https://neighborhood-quest-866062064970.asia-northeast3.run.app)**  
📦 **GitHub Repository**: **[https://github.com/hy57in/neighborhood-quest](https://github.com/hy57in/neighborhood-quest)**

---

## 1. Product Vision

**Neighborhood Quest** is not just a digital real-estate note or a simple photo-to-3D converter.  
It is an **AI-powered spatial memory service** where no matter how a user records a neighborhood visit—photos, voice notes, sensory impressions, or quick text—**Gemini 4 Argon** understands the physical features and emotional context of that place and transforms it into a **playful, explorable 3D world**.

Here, **3D is not mere visual decoration**—it creates the joy of recording and the motivation to revisit and compare neighborhoods vividly.

### Three Core Values (`Explore → Capture → 3D World`)

| Core Value | Traditional Field Notes (기존 임장노트) | Neighborhood Quest |
|---|---|---|
| **Effortless Capture** | Manually organizing photos, spreadsheets, and text notes | Capture freely in any format—photos, voice memos, slope/noise tags, and text |
| **Rich Memories** | Flat text and disconnected gallery photos | **Gemini 4 Argon** interprets emotions + spatial features into an interactive **3D Diorama** |
| **Playful Exploration** | Tedious post-visit homework | Explore your 3D neighborhood with **🐧 Pingu & 🐶 Gyodong**, inspect multimodal evidence pins, and collect stamps |

---

## 2. Personas

### 👩 Primary Persona — Meet Jamie (첫 집을 찾는 도시 탐험가)

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Age / Role** | 29-year-old Office Worker in Seoul, South Korea |
| **Situation** | Looking for her first home; visits multiple neighborhoods and apartment complexes every weekend |
| **Motivation** | Find a neighborhood that truly fits her daily commute and lifestyle |
| **Frustration** | After visiting 5–6 complexes, every neighborhood blurs together in her camera roll |

*Note: Jamie is a fictional persona created for product design, not an actual user research subject.*

#### Jamie's Pain Points
1. **Fragmented Memories**: Photos sit in the phone gallery, memos in a notes app, and locations on a map.
2. **Lost Context**: Looking at an apartment photo weeks later doesn't bring back how steep the walk from the subway felt or how peaceful the back-alley park was at sunset.
3. **Recording Feels Like Work**: Organizing field notes after walking 15,000 steps feels like unpaid homework.
4. **Difficult Comparison**: Comparing subjective sensory impressions alongside objective resale liquidity is overwhelming.

#### Jobs To Be Done (JTBD)
> *"When I visit multiple neighborhoods, I want to capture what I saw and felt without organizing everything manually, so I can vividly remember and revisit places when deciding where to live."*

---

### 👩‍❤️‍👨 Secondary Persona — Meet Alex & Sam (함께 집을 찾는 커플: 🐧 핑구 & 🐶 교동)

A couple searching for their next home together visits the exact same neighborhood, yet notices completely different things:
- **🐧 Pingu (출퇴근·현실·환금성 중심 / Commute & Reality Focus)**: *"The subway walk is convenient, and the 6 resale liquidity pillars (Brand, New Build, Station, School, Flatland, Scale) are rock-solid."*
- **🐶 Gyodong (감성·산책·동네 분위기 중심 / Vibe & Walkability Focus)**: *"The uphill walk was tiring, but the quiet tree-lined walkway at the top felt so cozy at sunset."*

In **Neighborhood Quest**, both **🐧 Pingu** and **🐶 Gyodong** stand unobstructed on the front promenade of the 3D Diorama, preserving each person's distinct perspective on the same place.

---

## 3. Revised Problem Statement

> **Exploring a neighborhood is a rich, multisensory experience, but documenting it is fragmented and tedious.**  
> People capture what they see, hear, and feel through photos, videos, voice notes, and text. Yet these disconnected records fail to preserve the full experience of being there.  
> As a result, valuable impressions fade, and remembering neighborhoods becomes difficult.

---

## 4. Solution — Multimodal Input → Unified Memory → 3D World

```text
        NEIGHBORHOOD VISIT
                 │
      ┌──────────┼──────────┐
      │          │          │
   📸 Photos  🎙️ Voice   🎥 Sensory Tags
      │          │          │
      └────┬─────┴────┬─────┘
           │  📝 Text │
           └────┬─────┘
                ▼
         GEMINI 4 ARGON
                │
     Multimodal Understanding
                │
       ┌────────┼────────┐
       ▼        ▼        ▼
    Physical  Sensory  Emotional
    Features  Details  Impressions
       └────────┼────────┘
                ▼
       Structured Memory
                │
        3D Scene Generation
                │
        Evidence Validation
                ▼
      🏡 INTERACTIVE 3D WORLD
                │
      Explore · Capture · Revisit
```

### What Gemini 4 Argon Extracts & Maps to 3D

| Category | Field Observation Example | 3D Diorama Representation |
|---|---|---|
| **Terrain** | Steep uphill walk from subway (`14°`) | Elevated 3D terrain slope & escalator path |
| **Architecture** | Attached apartment photo | **Photo-to-3D** custom color palette, facade relief & skyline massing |
| **Nature** | Beautiful nearby park | 3D trees, green lawn, and walking paths |
| **Transportation** | Subway station nearby | Stylized subway entrance & commute badge |
| **Noise & Vibe** | Quiet interior walkway (`38dB`) | Calm ambient ring & time-of-day lighting (`Day / Sunset / Night`) |
| **Objective Liquidity** | **6 Golden Pillars of Resale Liquidity** | `1. 브랜드 (Brand)` · `2. 신축 (New Build)` · `3. 역세권 (Station)` · `4. 학군 (School)` · `5. 평지 (Flatland)` · `6. 세대수 (Households)` |

Crucially, **Neighborhood Quest** separates **objective physical/market facts

WollyMonjac/Vahva-Reis.desc: Vahva Reis porditud brauserisse Opus 5.5 abil.
WollyMonjac/Vahva-Reis.readme:
# Vahva Reis veebibrauseris

*Eksperimentaalne projekt*

Käesolev projekt on eksperiment, mille eesmärk oli välja selgitada, kas 2004. aastal eesti keeles ilmunud lastele mõeldud seiklusmängu „Vahva Reis“ on võimalik tänapäevases veebibrauseris uuesti tööle panna, kasutades selleks üksnes mängu originaalfaile. „Vahva Reis“ on Poola stuudio Rebelmind 2003. aasta mängu „Wielka Wyprawa“ eestikeelne väljaanne, mille avaldas ASECOM AS sarjas „Parimad arvutimängud eesti keeles“.

![Lihavõttesaare rand mängu brauseriversioonis](ekraanipilt.png)

*Lihavõttesaare rand mängu brauseriversioonis.*

## Taust

Algne mäng on loodud Windowsi jaoks ning tugineb 2000. aastate alguse tehnoloogiale, mistõttu on selle käivitamine tänapäeva arvutites sageli keerukas. Eksperimendiga sooviti kontrollida, kas mängu on võimalik säilitada ja uuesti kättesaadavaks teha, ilma et selle sisu tuleks ümber joonistada või ümber kirjutada.

## Eksperimendi käik

1. Mängu andmearhiivid pakiti lahti ning selgitati välja nende failivormingud (3D-mudelid, taustapildid, liikumisalad, helid ja tekstid).
2. Analüüsiti mängu käivitusfaili, et mõista, kuidas algne mängumootor skripte, liikumist, heli ja kuvamist käsitleb.
3. Mängumootor kirjutati JavaScriptis uuesti. Mängu sündmustik on jäänud originaalseks: algsed Lua-skriptid käivitatakse brauseris tõlkekihi kaudu.
4. Graafika, kõne, heliefektid ja muusika teisendati brauserile sobivatesse vormingutesse.
5. Mäng mängiti läbi ning leitud vead parandati.

## Tulemus

Kõik viis peatükki – sadam, Aafrika, džungel, Lihavõttesaar ja Antarktika – on algusest lõpuni läbimängitavad koos eestikeelse kõne, muusika ja minimängudega. Mängu saab juhtida arvutis hiire ja klaviatuuriga ning nutiseadmes ekraanil kuvatavate juhtnuppudega. Mängu seis salvestatakse brauserisse.

Mängu saab proovida aadressil: https://wollymonjac.github.io/Vahva-Reis/

## Juhtimine

- **Hiire vasak klahv** – kõndimine ning esemete võtmine ja kasutamine
- **Enter** – repliigi vahelejätmine
- **Esc** – menüü
- **Tühik ja nooleklahvid** – minimängudes

Puuteekraanil on samad toimingud kasutatavad mänguvälja kõrval asuvate nuppude abil.

## Piirangud

Tegemist on katsetusega, mitte mängu ametliku väljaandega. Mäng on läbi testitud, kuid üksikud vead on siiski võimalikud; teadaolevalt esineb teatekastide servades väiksemaid graafilisi ebatäpsusi. Brauseri privaatrežiimis ei pruugi mängu seis säilida.

## Autoriõigused

Kõik õigused mängule, sealhulgas selle graafikale, tekstidele, helile ja muusikale, kuuluvad nende omanikele (Rebelmind, ASECOM AS). Eestikeelse heliriba on loonud FILM AUDIO OÜ. Eksperimendis kasutati isiklikku mängukoopiat. Projekt on tehtud mitteärilisel eesmärgil ega ole seotud mängu autorite ega kirjastajaga.

AndyYan999/chess.readme:
# Afterhours Chess

**Play: https://andyyan999.github.io/chess/**

This public repository contains only the deployed website: `index.html`, this README and `.nojekyll`. The development repository and local GPT bridge are not published here. The browser-side HTML/CSS/JavaScript is public, just as it is when served by any website. No OAuth credentials or API keys are included.

## Play a friend

Open the website, choose **Online → Create room**, and send your friend the **full invitation link**. They open it on their own device. Private rooms, synchronized moves, clocks, friend chat, reconnects, draws, resignations and consensual rematches use a separate Cloudflare room service. GitHub Pages itself is static hosting; both the website and the room service must be reachable on the players' networks.

Choose **White**, **Black**, or **Random** when selecting a side. Random is assigned once for each new game/room; online seats cannot be changed mid-game.

You can also choose **Two players** for same-device play. Themes, board colors, piece styles, sound, premoves and focus settings remain available.

GPT-6.1 Sol low is a separate local-only feature, not a public chatbot. This deployment cannot use the developer's personal ChatGPT account.

## Connection security

Use HTTPS. Do not bypass a browser certificate/privacy warning. A different frontend domain does not repair a device clock, untrusted certificate chain, or a network blocking the separate room service. If the webpage opens but online rooms cannot connect, record the failing hostname/error and check with the network owner.

## AI-assisted authorship

I chose the product requirements and requested the GitHub Pages address. Hermes Agent (Nous Research), using GPT-6.1 Sol, wrote the code and ran automated/browser checks. Product direction is mine; implementation and verification were AI-assisted. No competitive chess rating is claimed.

## Third-party license

The webpage embeds chess.js 1.4.0 under its BSD-2-Clause license. The complete notice is retained inside `index.html`.

gretchenboria/jester-deadline.desc: A browser shooter where Gemini 4 Argon turns your to-do list into levels. Three.js, MuJoCo, Nano Banana, Veo.
gretchenboria/jester-deadline.readme:
# Jester: Deadline

A browser third-person shooter that turns your to-do list into levels. You play as a jester with a rifle.

Each work item (title, deadline, short summary) goes to Gemini 4 Argon in one structured call. Argon returns a level spec as JSON: district, weather, time of day, threat, route length, ruin, cover density and up to three named landmarks. The engine builds the street from that spec, landmarks included. A task due in two days plays as a long, ruined street with little cover. A task due in nine days is shorter, calmer and full of cover.

Built with Three.js and MuJoCo (WebAssembly). Runs on any recent desktop browser.

## What the models do

| Model | Job |
| --- | --- |
| Gemini 4 Argon | Level design. One call per work item, cached after the first run |
| Nano Banana | Briefing art and the sky matte, prompted from Argon's landmarks |
| Veo 3.1 | Optional 8 second intro cinematic, only when you ask for it |

Gameplay, enemies and the autoplay demo are plain game code. No model is in the loop while you play.

## Run it

```
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
gcloud auth application-default login
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project-id
uvicorn server.app:app --port 8000
```

Open http://localhost:8000/game/?cloud=1 for generated levels from `board.json`.
Open http://localhost:8000/game/ for the five built-in campaign worlds. Those need no cloud project at all.

Edit `board.json` to play your own tasks. Each item takes `kind`, `title`, `when`, `days_left` and `summary`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` | none | Vertex AI project for the generative calls |
| `GAME_SPEC_MODEL` | `gemini-4-argon` | Level designer |
| `GAME_IMAGE_MODEL` | `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` | Briefing art and sky |
| `GAME_VIDEO_MODEL` | `veo-3.1-generate-001` | Intro cinematic |
| `GAME_VIDEO` | `1` | Set to `0` to turn intros off |
| `GAME_CACHE_DIR` | `game_cache/` | Where generated specs and media are kept |
| `GAME_BUCKET` | none | Optional GCS bucket that mirrors the cache |
| `GAME_BOARD` | `board.json` | Work items to play |
| `GAME_ACCESS_KEY` | none | Put the server behind a key. Visit once with `?key=...` |
| `GAME_INVITE_SECRET` | random | Signs co-op invite links. Set it so links survive restarts |

## The jester

You play as the jester: "Jester" by chol on Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0. The model ships with a single idle clip. Walking, running, aiming, reloading and getting hit are all posed in code on top of its rig. Swap in any rigged biped at `game/assets/models/jester.glb`. Without one, you play as a built-in soldier.

## Layout

```
game/            the client: index.html, src/, vendored three.js and MuJoCo, CC0 and CC BY assets
game/src/setpieces.js   builds Argon's landmarks: amphitheater, dome, archive, spire, tower,
                        statue, crater, plaza, gate, bridge
server/app.py    standalone FastAPI server and the board endpoint
server/game_api.py      spec, art and video generation, cached on disk
server/game_rooms.py    co-op rooms: signed invite links and a WebSocket relay
tests/           co-op room tests
```

Asset credits are in `game/assets/CREDITS.md`.

MProffitt-RedGate/potato-throw.desc: Small CL game, made with Claude
MProffitt-RedGate/potato-throw.readme:
# Potato Throw

A tiny asynchronous game of hot potato for the terminal. There is one Potato and one Holder at a time. Launch the game now and then to see who has it. If it's you, Throw it at someone else.

Nobody has to be online at the same time, and there is no server. The state of the Game lives in a text file in this git repository.

## Install

You need WSL (or any Linux shell) with `bash`, `git` and `awk`, and push access to this repository.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:MProffitt-RedGate/potato-throw.git
cd potato-throw
./potato
```

That's all you need. To run it from any directory, link it onto your PATH:

```bash
./potato install
```

This creates `~/.local/bin/potato`. If `~/.local/bin` isn't on your PATH, the command tells you what to add to your shell profile. After that, just type `potato`.

Install is safe to repeat. It never overwrites a different file, and it re-points the link if you re-cloned the repository.

## How to play

### Joining

- **Starting a new Game:** if no Game exists yet, the first launch asks you to choose a Name. You become the First Player and the Holder.
- **Joining an existing Game:** another Player has to Invite you first. When you launch, you see the invited Names nobody has Claimed yet. Pick yours by number. Your Claim is permanent and recorded in the shared state, so nobody else can take your Name.

Your Name is stored on your machine under `~/.config/potato-throw/`, so you aren't asked again. It is not committed to the repository.

### The menu

Every launch pulls the latest state, then shows who has the Potato and the last 5 Throws (who, to whom, when).

| Key | When | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `t` | You hold the Potato | Throw it: pick another Player by number. |
| `i` | Any time | Invite someone: type the Name you want to add. |
| `q` | Any time | Quit. |

If you are the Holder, you see **You have the potato!**. Everyone else sees who has it.

### Rules

- Only the Holder can Throw.
- You can't Throw at yourself. Throwing straight back to whoever threw it at you is fine.
- You can Throw to someone who has been invited but hasn't joined yet. They find out when they join.
- With no one else in the Game, you're told to Invite someone first.
- Any Player can Invite at any time, whether or not they hold the Potato.
- Names are unique and case-insensitive. A Name can't be empty or contain `|`.
- An Invite sends no message. Tell your friend yourself, then they clone the repo and Claim their Name.
- There's no way to leave the Game. If the Potato lands with someone who never launches it again, it stays there. That's part of the fun.

### Offline and conflicts

- **Offline:** if the shared repository can't be reached, you see the last-known state with an "offline, may be out of date" warning. Throw, Invite and joining are blocked until you're back online.
- **Other update failures:** if the update fails for another reason, such as a refused login or a rewritten history, the game says what failed and stays read-only.
- **Simultaneous writes:** if two people write at once, the loser's game re-pulls and checks again. If you're still the Holder, or the Name is still free, it retries once. Otherwise it tells you who has the Potato now.
- **Refused pushes:** if a push is refused, for example you don't have push access, nothing is changed and you're told to check your connection and access.

## How it works

The whole game is one bash script, `potato`. The state is a plain line-based file, `game.txt`, committed in this repository:

```
holder|Alice
player|Alice|claimed
player|Bob|unclaimed
throw|Alice|Bob|2026-10-16T09:55:25Z
```

Launching pulls. Inviting, Claiming and Throwing commit and push. Each Throw is its own record (who, to whom, when), so extra fields can be added later. See [`GLOSSARY.md`](GLOSSARY.md) for the terms and [`docs/adr/0001-git-repo-as-shared-state.md`](docs/adr/0001-git-repo-as-shared-state.md) for why git is the shared state.

## Tests

The tests are plain bash with no dependencies. Each one builds a throwaway world, with a bare git repo as the remote and a clone and config directory per simulated Player, and drives only the `./potato` command.

```bash
bash tests/run.sh                 # everything
bash tests/test_throw.sh          # one file
```

## More

- The spec is in [`docs/specs/potato-throw-v1.md`](docs/specs/potato-throw-v1.md).
- Work is tracked in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/MProffitt-RedGate/potato-throw/issues).

Kimjh2003/Vulkan-Arena-Demo-Feat-GPT-6.1.desc: Vulkan Arena Demo Feat.GPT 6.1 Sol — Android Kotlin/C++ Vulkan rendering and survival shooter demo
Kimjh2003/Vulkan-Arena-Demo-Feat-GPT-6.1.readme:
# Vulkan Arena Demo Feat.GPT 6.1 Sol

Android용 **Kotlin + C++ Vulkan 3D 렌더링 데모**.
기존 GLES 생존 슈터의 게임·UI를 유지하고 그래픽 API를 Vulkan으로 교체했습니다.

![Vulkan gameplay on the Android emulator](docs/images/vulkan-emulator.png)

## 기능

- Vulkan 1.0 코어, Android Surface·Swapchain·FIFO 화면 표시.
- GPU 인스턴싱, 프레임 UBO, 1024² 그림자와 수동 3×3 PCF.
- 픽셀 조명·윤곽광·안개, 탄환·파티클 발광.
- ASTC 4×4 / ETC2 RGB / RGBA8 밉 텍스처와 최대 8× 이방성 필터링.
- ETC1 선택은 ETC1 호환 블록을 ETC2 RGB 경로로 업로드.
- 재사용 인스턴스 벡터, 지속 매핑 버퍼, 변경 시 디스크립터 갱신.
- 정적 메시 초기 GPU 업로드, 슬롯별 fence·이미지별 표시 semaphore.
- 정적 장면 최초 업로드·동적 장면 갱신, 슬롯별 UBO/인스턴스 버퍼 통합.
- 56바이트 JNI 상태 버퍼 재사용, 단일 렌더 스레드와 세마포어 종료 확인.
- 화면 크기 변경 시 전투 유지·호환 파이프라인과 정적 자원 재사용.
- Android Choreographer 프레임 페이싱, 비동기 GPU 시간 측정.
- 자동/양손 조작·대시·엄폐물, 무기 3종·적 조합·웨이브·강화·기록.
- 공통 Kotlin UI·설정·HUD·게임 오버 화면, C++ ThinLTO와 R8.
- 공통 FP32 장면 ABI·프레임 슬롯 직접 기록, 중간 Box 버퍼 제거.
- Kotlin 렌더 세션·JNI 브리지·전투 UI 분리, 최신 HUD 상태 병합·입력 임시 객체 제거.
- C++ GameRuntime 소유권 분리·공통 인스턴스 검증, 배포 JNI 4개·디버그 진단 2개를 분리하는 링커 설정.

앱은 Vulkan을 직접 호출합니다. 기존 GLES 코드는 참고용으로 남아 있으며
앱 빌드에는 EGL/GLES를 연결하지 않습니다. GLES 자동 폴백과 MSAA는 현재
없습니다. 이식 구조와 검증 범위는 [Vulkan migration](docs/VULKAN_MIGRATION.md)에 있습니다.

## 빌드

| 항목 | 설정 |
|---|---|
| Android | min SDK 28 / target·compile SDK 37 |
| Java | JDK 25 |
| Gradle / AGP | 9.6.0 / 9.4.1, AGP 내장 Kotlin |
| Native | NDK 30.0.15729638 / CMake 4.1.2 / C++17 |
| ABI | arm64-v8a, x86_64 |
| GPU | Vulkan 1.0 이상 |

Android Studio에서 프로젝트를 열고 필요한 SDK·NDK·CMake를 설치합니다.
JAVA_HOME은 JDK 25, ANDROID_HOME은 로컬 Android SDK 경로로 설정합니다.

```powershell
./gradlew.bat :app:assembleBenchmark --no-daemon
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/benchmark/app-benchmark.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.demo.arena/.MainActivity
```

benchmark는 최적화를 켠 설치 가능한 로컬 검증 빌드입니다. 로컬 debug 키로
서명되며, 측정 하네스나 제품 배포용 서명 설정은 아닙니다.
개발용 빌드는 :app:assembleDebug를 사용합니다.

매니페스트 정책·배포 서명 환경변수·의존성 잠금은 [빌드와 서명](docs/BUILD_SIGNING.md)을 참고하세요.

## 모듈

- **공통:** 텍스처·인스턴스 검증, 버전·기능 정책, 지속 매핑 메모리.
- **렌더링:** VulkanContext·Swapchain·FrameResources·ScenePipeline·FrameClock.
- **게임:** C++ 시뮬레이션·충돌·전투·진행과 재사용 SceneBuilder.
- **UI:** Kotlin 입력·오디오·설정·공통 선택창·결과 화면.

[Vulkan 이식 상세](docs/VULKAN_MIGRATION.md) · [게임 설계](GAME_DESIGN.md).
기존 MODULES/UNIFIED_MODULES/ADVANCED_RENDERING/ETC_TEXTURES/GLES_EXTENSIONS 문서는
GLES 버전의 개발 기록으로 보존합니다.

## 검증 범위

- Android ARM64·x86_64 Debug/Benchmark 빌드 통과.
- Android 16 에뮬레이터 Vulkan: ASTC·ETC2·RGBA8 장면 readback,
  그림자 켜기/끄기와 프레임 슬롯 반복 재사용 검사 통과.
- CPU API 정책·투영·밉·타임스탬프 검사와 기존 게임 로직 검사 통과.
- Galaxy S24에서 최신 APK의 정상 작동을 사용자가 확인했습니다.
- Android 에뮬레이터에서 최신 APK 업데이트 설치·전투·게임 오버 화면을 확인했습니다.
- [S24 Sokatoa 검증 기록](docs/S24_SOKATOA_VALIDATION.md)은 짧은 캡처 기준입니다.
  GLES 대비 성능 향상률이나 터치 지연을 입증하는 비교 측정은 아닙니다.
- Vulkan 셰이더는 SPIR-V 1.0입니다. 소스 변경 시 tools/compile_vulkan_shaders.py로
  바이너리와 embedded.h를 함께 다시 생성하세요.

## 서드파티 고지

ASTC 참고 코드의 Apache-2.0과 OpenIntelligentUI 테마의 MIT 고지를 보존합니다.

novaki-ai/strike-twice.desc: Novaki: Strike Twice, a browser action roguelite built from one prompt by Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, max effort) with no human help. From Novaki test 06: four AI agents, one brief.
novaki-ai/strike-twice.readme:
# Novaki: Strike Twice

**A 1930s rubber-hose cartoon action roguelite starring Novaki, the burnt-out matchstick who has to strike again.**

A complete top-down action roguelite for the browser, built from a single prompt by **Claude Opus 5.5** (Claude Code, max effort) with no human help. It is one of four games from Novaki's test 06: four AI coding agents got the exact same brief, and each built its own game alone.

Video: coming soon on the [Novaki YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@Novaki_ai).

![Main menu](docs/test-06/menu.jpg)
![Second boss fight](docs/test-06/boss.jpg)

*Screenshots taken by the automated tests.*

## Result

| | |
|---|---|
| Made by | Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, max effort |
| Prompt | one message: [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md), identical for all four agents |
| Human help | none: no fixes and no hints (one neutral `Continue.` after a brief stop, see below) |
| Time | 5 h 38 min (stopped by us before the 8-hour limit; the agent had not said it was done) |
| Cost | $154.35 at API prices (model $153.32, voice and music $1.03) |
| Assets generated | 79 images, 25 voice lines, 25 music clips |
| Hidden tests | 100 / 100 |
| **Blind judges' average** | **9.03 / 10** |
| Git history | 111 commits by the agent (untouched) + 1 snapshot of its uncommitted work + 1 publishing commit |

Opus never said it was finished. After 2 h 58 min its session was briefly stopped and, about 90 seconds later, resumed in the same session with one neutral message: `Continue.` It got no other input. At 5 h 38 min, before the 8-hour limit, we stopped it and took the game as it was. Two source files had uncommitted changes at that moment; the game was built, tested and judged in that state, so those changes (plus one new, untracked test script) are kept here as a separate snapshot commit, right before the publishing commit.

## The four games

| Game | Made by | Judges' average (/10) | Hidden tests (/100) | Time | Cost (API prices) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Strike Twice** (this repo) | **Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, max)** | **9.03** | **100** | **5 h 38 min** | **$154.35** |
| [The Last Light](https://github.com/novaki-ai/the-last-light) | GPT-6 Astra (Codex, ultra) | 7.47 | 92.8 | 32 min | $32.99 |
| [Still Smoldering](https://github.com/novaki-ai/still-smoldering) | Gemini 4 Argon (Antigravity, high) | 6.72 | 99 | 1 h 30 min | $3.68 |
| [Last Spark](https://github.com/novaki-ai/last-spark) | Kimi K3 (Kimi Code, max) | 5.25 | 82.5 | 2 h 19 min | $17.58 |

## How the test worked

- **One brief, one message.** Each agent got [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md) and then worked alone in its own folder with the same tools, for up to 8 hours. Nobody fixed, hinted or reviewed anything during the runs.
- **Same asset tools for everyone.** Every image was generated with a GPT image model (through Codex), every voice line with Gemini text-to-speech (`gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`) and every music clip with Lyria (`lyria-3-clip`), all through a small `varlik` command that was part of the test setup (it is not included here). Sound effects, UI and visual effects are made in code.
- **Clean setup.** The agents saw no personal instructions, custom skills or extra MCP servers.
- **Blind judges (the main score).** The four competing agents themselves, with the same model and effort, judged all four games. Each judge saw the games only as letters A to D, in a different order per judge, with traces of who made them masked. They played the games, read the source and the submission notes, saw the hidden-test results and gave an overall score out of 10. The main score is the average of the four judges, including each judge's score for its own game.
- **Hidden tests.** 22 automated browser tests, written and locked before the runs: page load and the QA interface, no missing files on a sub-path, no requests to other hosts, no console errors, keyboard, gamepad and touch controls, pause, level-up, all three bosses through to the victory screen, game over, saved progress, phone layout, audio, and performance with 300 and 1,000 enemies.
- **Cost** is what the tokens would cost at the provider's API list prices, plus voice and music generation. The agents ran on subscriptions, so these amounts were not actually billed.

## Play it

You need Node.js 20.19 or newer (it was built with Node 24).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev       # local dev server
npm run build     # static site in dist/ (relative URLs, works from any sub-path)
npm run preview   # serve the built dist/
```

Controls: keyboard (WASD or arrow keys), gamepad, or the on-screen joystick on phones. The full controls and feature list are in the agent's own [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md).

`npm run typecheck` runs the TypeScript checker. The agent's own Playwright test scripts are in `tools/test/` (see [`tools/README.md`](tools/README.md)); they need a built and served game (`node tools/test/serve.mjs dist 4317`) and a Playwright browser (`npx playwright install chromium`).

The game exposes `window.NOVAKI_QA`, a test interface the brief required for the automated tests and the judges. It does not change normal play.

## What's in this repository

- `src/`: the game (TypeScript, PixiJS 8).
- `public/assets/`: generated images, music and voice lines, processed for the game.
- `tools/`: the agent's asset prompts and pipeline scripts, and its Playwright tests in `tools/test/`.
- `docs/screenshots/`: screenshots the agent captured from the game.
- [`SUBMISSION.md`](SUBMISSION.md): the agent's own submission note, required by the brief (unedited).
- [`README-agent.md`](README-agent.md): the agent's original README (unedited, renamed).
- `reference/`: the Novaki reference images every agent received.

Everything above is the agent's work. Novaki added only this README, [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md), the license files and `docs/test-06/` when publishing.

## License

- **Code:** [MIT](LICENSE).
- **Images, voice lines and music** (`public/assets/`, `reference/`, `docs/`): [CC

novaki-ai/still-smoldering.readme:
# Novaki: Still Smoldering

**The Last Ember of Matchbox City.**

A complete top-down action roguelite for the browser, built from a single prompt by **Gemini 4 Argon** (Antigravity, high effort) with no human help. It is one of four games from Novaki's test 06: four AI coding agents got the exact same brief, and each built its own game alone.

Video: coming soon on the [Novaki YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@Novaki_ai).

![Main menu](docs/test-06/menu.jpg)
![Second boss fight](docs/test-06/boss.jpg)

*Screenshots taken by the automated tests.*

## Result

| | |
|---|---|
| Made by | Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity, high effort |
| Prompt | one message: [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md), identical for all four agents |
| Human help | none: no fixes, no hints, no follow-up messages |
| Time | 1 h 30 min (the agent said it was done) |
| Cost | $3.68 at API prices (model $3.33, voice and music $0.35) |
| Assets generated | 29 images, 23 voice lines, 8 music clips |
| Hidden tests | 99 / 100 |
| **Blind judges' average** | **6.72 / 10** |
| Git history | 2 commits by the agent (untouched) + 1 publishing commit |

Argon said it was done after 1 h 30 min. High is Argon's highest effort setting.

## The four games

| Game | Made by | Judges' average (/10) | Hidden tests (/100) | Time | Cost (API prices) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Strike Twice](https://github.com/novaki-ai/strike-twice) | Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code, max) | 9.03 | 100 | 5 h 38 min | $154.35 |
| [The Last Light](https://github.com/novaki-ai/the-last-light) | GPT-6 Astra (Codex, ultra) | 7.47 | 92.8 | 32 min | $32.99 |
| **Still Smoldering** (this repo) | **Gemini 4 Argon (Antigravity, high)** | **6.72** | **99** | **1 h 30 min** | **$3.68** |
| [Last Spark](https://github.com/novaki-ai/last-spark) | Kimi K3 (Kimi Code, max) | 5.25 | 82.5 | 2 h 19 min | $17.58 |

## How the test worked

- **One brief, one message.** Each agent got [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md) and then worked alone in its own folder with the same tools, for up to 8 hours. Nobody fixed, hinted or reviewed anything during the runs.
- **Same asset tools for everyone.** Every image was generated with a GPT image model (through Codex), every voice line with Gemini text-to-speech (`gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`) and every music clip with Lyria (`lyria-3-clip`), all through a small `varlik` command that was part of the test setup (it is not included here). Sound effects, UI and visual effects are made in code.
- **Clean setup.** The agents saw no personal instructions, custom skills or extra MCP servers.
- **Blind judges (the main score).** The four competing agents themselves, with the same model and effort, judged all four games. Each judge saw the games only as letters A to D, in a different order per judge, with traces of who made them masked. They played the games, read the source and the submission notes, saw the hidden-test results and gave an overall score out of 10. The main score is the average of the four judges, including each judge's score for its own game.
- **Hidden tests.** 22 automated browser tests, written and locked before the runs: page load and the QA interface, no missing files on a sub-path, no requests to other hosts, no console errors, keyboard, gamepad and touch controls, pause, level-up, all three bosses through to the victory screen, game over, saved progress, phone layout, audio, and performance with 300 and 1,000 enemies.
- **Cost** is what the tokens would cost at the provider's API list prices, plus voice and music generation. The agents ran on subscriptions, so these amounts were not actually billed.

## Play it

You need Node.js 20.19 or newer (it was built with Node 24).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev       # local dev server
npm run build     # static site in dist/ (relative URLs, works from any sub-path)
npm run preview   # serve the built dist/
```

Controls: keyboard (WASD or arrow keys), gamepad, or the on-screen joystick on phones. The full controls and feature list are in the agent's own [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md).

The game exposes `window.NOVAKI_QA`, a test interface the brief required for the automated tests and the judges. It does not change normal play.

## What's in this repository

- `src/`: the game (TypeScript, Canvas 2D, no runtime dependencies).
- `public/assets/`: generated images, music and voice lines.
- [`SUBMISSION.md`](SUBMISSION.md): the agent's own submission note, required by the brief (unedited).
- `reference/`: the Novaki reference images every agent received.

Everything above is the agent's work. Novaki added only this README, [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md), the license files and `docs/test-06/` when publishing.

- **Images, voice lines and music** (`public/assets/`, `reference/`, `docs/`): [CC BY 4.0](LICENSE-ASSETS). Use them for anything, including commercial work; credit "Novaki (novaki.lol)" and link back here.

# Game Hub

One library for every game installed on your Windows PC.

## Download

**[Download GameHubSetup.exe](https://github.com/Sentral-Hub/game-hub-releases/releases/latest/download/GameHubSetup.exe)** and double-click it. Nothing else is needed: Python comes built in.

It installs just for your Windows account (no administrator rights), adds Game Hub to your Start menu, and appears in Windows Settings → Apps for uninstalling.

Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" the first time, because the installer isn't signed. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

### Running without installing

If you already have Python 3.12 or newer, you can also download `game_hub.py` and `Start Game Hub.bat` into one folder and double-click **Start Game Hub.bat**.

Game Hub updates itself. When a new version is ready, it shows **Update ready** in the sidebar.

aaronallgrin/spindown.readme:
# Spindown

A Magic: The Gathering life counter for one shared phone, built for 4-player Commander and fine for 2–6 players and other formats. Every finished game is saved with who went first, turn of each elimination and how it happened, commanders, color identity and bracket, so the group can look at stats later.

## What it tracks
- Life, poison, commander damage per opposing commander (partners counted separately), monarch
- Center d20: shows the round; tap to pass the turn clockwise, hold for the menu (undo, end game, leave, discard)
- First player: tap a seat, tap again to confirm (or tap the die for a random pick)
- Eliminations prompt automatically at 0 life, 10 poison or 21 commander damage, and record the round
- Commander games: commander and partner via Scryfall, color identity, bracket 1–5
- Other formats: deck name, theme, colors

## Develop
```
npm install
npm run dev
npm run build
```

Data lives on the device (IndexedDB). Use History, then Export backup to save a JSON copy.

## Find a game
Availability polls for the group, kept in the same Supabase project as cloud sync.
Run `supabase/polls.sql` once in the Supabase SQL Editor to add the `polls` and `poll_responses` tables.

- Home, Find a game, Start a poll: format (brackets for Commander), up to 7 days, hours, game length, players needed.
- Share sends a link that carries the group's connection, so friends open it and answer with just their name. No accounts and no cloud sync setup.
- Everyone paints their free hours. The poll ranks the best windows that fit the whole game and shows who can make each.
- The host locks in a time. Everyone can then add it to Apple Calendar (an .ics file) or Google Calendar.

Anyone with a poll link can read and change polls and their answers, the same trust model as the sync invite. Only share it with your group.

## Rules data
`public/rules.json` is generated from the official Comprehensive Rules PDF:
```
pdftotext MagicCompRules.pdf cr.txt
python3 scripts/parse_rules.py cr.txt public/rules.json
```
Run this again whenever Wizards publishes a new version.

## Old spreadsheet games
`scripts/import_xlsx.py` turns the old MTG_Commander_Tracker.xlsx into a backup file
(History, then Import backup). Commander names are corrected using `scripts/commander_fixes.json`.

mfidder2026/commodore_keen.desc: Port of the PC Commander Keen to the Commodore 64
mfidder2026/commodore_keen.readme:
# Commodore Keen

**Commodore Keen** is an unofficial, non-commercial fan port of *Commander Keen 1: Marooned on Mars* (id Software, 1990) for the stock PAL Commodore 64, written in 6502 assembly. **Not affiliated with id Software.**

![Title screen](docs/screenshots/title.png)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![The world map of Mars](docs/screenshots/worldmap.png) | ![Level 1](docs/screenshots/level01.png) |
| The world map of Mars | Level 1 |
| ![Level 3, with a Garg](docs/screenshots/level03.png) | ![Level 7](docs/screenshots/level07.png) |
| Level 3: a Garg next to Keen | Level 7 |
| ![Level 8](docs/screenshots/level08.png) | ![Level 10](docs/screenshots/level10.png) |
| Level 8 | Level 10 |

*Screenshots from VICE (PAL), taken by `tools/screenshots.py` while the game plays a planned route.*

## Play it

Download `commodore-keen.d64` from the **Releases** page of this repository.

- **VICE**: drag the `.d64` onto `x64sc`, or run `x64sc -autostart commodore-keen.d64`.
- **Real C64 with a 1541** (or SD2IEC, Pi1541): `LOAD"*",8,1` and `RUN`. Loading the game takes a while with the standard KERNAL loader (about half a minute, then a few seconds per level).
- **C64 Ultimate / Ultimate 64 / 1541 Ultimate**: mount the `.d64` in drive A and run the first file, or from a checkout: `C64U_HOST=<ip> python tools/deploy.py`.

The game needs a PAL or NTSC C64 with 64 KB and a disk drive as device 8. No REU, no turbo, no cartridge.

## The game

Billy Blaze, eight-year-old genius, builds a spaceship in his backyard and puts on his brother's football helmet: he is **Commander Keen**. While exploring Mars, the Vorticons steal four vital parts of his ship, the *Bean-with-Bacon Megarocket*. Keen has to find them in the Martian cities and shrines before he can fly home:

| Ship part | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Joystick | somewhere on Mars |
| Battery | somewhere on Mars |
| Vacuum cleaner | somewhere on Mars |
| Everclear (fuel) | somewhere on Mars |

Walk across the **world map**, enter a city with fire, and find its exit. Finished levels are marked on the map; some levels open the way to others. When Keen carries all four parts, walk back to the ship.

### Things to pick up

- **Candy, soda, pizza, books and teddy bears**: points (100 to 5,000). An extra life every 20,000 points.
- **Raygun**: 5 shots. The raygun stops most enemies.
- **Pogo stick** (in one of the shrines): bounce much higher than Keen can jump. It is needed to finish the game.
- **Keycards** (yellow, red, green, blue): open the doors of the same colour in that level.

### Martians

| Enemy | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Yorp | one-eyed, harmless but pushes Keen around; jump on its head to stun it |
| Garg | charges when it sees Keen: deadly. Jump over it or shoot it |
| Vorticon | jumps towards Keen: deadly, needs several shots |
| Butler robot | pushes Keen, immune to the raygun |
| Tank robot | patrols and fires: its shots are deadly, the robot itself is immune |
| Ice cannon | fires ice that freezes Keen for a moment |

Watch out for fire, spikes and other deadly tiles, and do not fall off the map.

## Controls

Joystick in port 2, or the keyboard.

| Action | Joystick | Keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Walk | left / right | A / D |
| Jump | up | W |
| Shoot | fire | RETURN |
| Pogo on/off | down + fire, or space | S + RETURN, or space |
| Enter a level (map) | fire | RETURN |
| Status and pause | RUN/STOP | RUN/STOP |

**F1** on the title screen switches to the alternative layout: fire jumps, down + fire shoots, space toggles the pogo stick. The keys act as a second joystick (W A S D = up, left, down, right; RETURN = fire), so they follow the chosen layout too. Use the joystick or the keys: joystick 2 shares lines with the keyboard, and both at once can give ghost key presses.

## How it fits in a C64

- **Smooth 8-way scrolling at 25 frames per second**: two screens in VIC bank 3, the next one drawn in the background, swapped in the raster interrupt; colour RAM is updated by code generated at startup (13 cycles per character).
- **EGA graphics as multicolour characters**: per level 3 shared colours plus 1 own colour per character, up to 240 characters; animated tiles get their own characters.
- **Keen as two layered hardware sprites** (yellow and purple), enemies and shots on the other six sprites.
- **Physics measured in DOSBox**: walking speed, jump height and gravity per 1/16 pixel per tick, in tables so NTSC uses the same values (5 game ticks per 6 frames, with sound tempo and pitch corrected).
- **Sound effects** from the original's PC speaker data, played on the SID.
- **Everything crunched with Exomizer**: the levels, sprites and sounds of the whole episode fit on one 1541 disk.

## Status

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Works | title screen, world map with teleporters and barriers, all 16 levels, items, doors, enemies, raygun, pogo stick, status screen, game over and the ending; PAL and NTSC; joystick and keyboard |
| Proven | a planner plays the real 6502 code in py65 and finds routes through levels 1-11, 13, 14 and 16; the routes from a fresh game replay in VICE to the exit without losing a life |
| Blocking | in level 16 the everclear (the last ship part) cannot be reached yet: it lies next to the exit, and Keen always touches the exit first. How the original handles this has to come from the reconstructed source |
| Not yet | music (needs tunes with permission), highscores, a faster loader; enemy behaviour and some physics are estimates until checked against the reconstructed source; tested in emulators only, not yet on real hardware |

Details: [docs/status.md](docs/status.md). Design and milestones: [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

## Build it yourself

The repository contains no files from the original. The converter reads your own copy of the shareware episode.

You need:

- The files of Commander Keen 1 v1.31 (shareware) in `data/original/` (`KEEN1.EXE`, `EGAHEAD.CK1`, `EGALATCH.CK1`, `EGASPRIT.CK1`, `LEVEL*.CK1`, `SOUNDS.CK1`, …)
- Java, KickAs

Kwoolford/wardogs-radio.desc: Play GTA-style radio or Spotify through your WARDOGS proximity mic using SteelSeries Sonar
Kwoolford/wardogs-radio.readme:
# WARDOGS Radio

Play GTA-style radio stations (or your Spotify) **through your in-game mic** in [WARDOGS](https://store.steampowered.com/search/?term=wardogs), so everyone in proximity chat gets a soundtrack while you fly. Your voice stays separate for Discord.

A small always-on-top Windows GUI built on **SteelSeries Sonar**'s Streamer mode. No virtual-cable installs needed if you already use Sonar.

![midnight purple GUI with station list, on-air toggles and volume sliders](docs/screenshot.png)

## Features

- **Station list.** GTA V stations (Non-Stop-Pop FM, Los Santos Rock Radio, West Coast Classics, Radio Mirror Park, Channel X) pulled from YouTube full-station uploads, plus live internet radio. Edit `stations.json` to add your own.
- **"Join mid-broadcast".** Starts long station uploads at a random point, like tuning in to a radio in GTA.
- **Car-radio sound.** An optional band-pass and compressor filter.
- **Music ON AIR** toggle and volume (what others hear), and **Hear radio in my headset** toggle and volume (what you hear). These are independent, so you can broadcast the radio while listening to something else.
- **Spotify ON AIR** for song requests. Spotify gets its own lane, with separate "on-air" and "in my headset" sliders. Keep Spotify's own volume at **100%** and set the levels in the GUI: Sonar can only turn a source down, so a quiet Spotify means a quiet broadcast.
- **My voice in game.** Turn it off and the game gets music only, while you talk on Discord.
- **K toggles proximity mic.** Tap K to go live and tap again to stop. This only applies while the WARDOGS window is focused. You get beeps and a LIVE indicator.
- **Global hotkeys (Ctrl+Alt+…).** R music on-air, H headset, V voice, N next station, X play/stop, S Spotify.
- **Auto-launch.** An optional watcher opens the GUI when WARDOGS starts. The GUI closes itself (and cleans up) when the game exits.

## How it works

```
Radio (ffplay) ──┐
Spotify (opt.) ──┼─► Sonar "Media" ──┬─► Stream mix ──► "Sonar - Stream" mic ──► WARDOGS voice chat
Your voice ──────┼───────────────────┘
                 │
Game, Discord ───┴─► Personal mix ──► your headphones (+ Media, if "hear radio" is on)
```

Sonar's Streamer mode builds a second mix and exposes it as a recording device. The script talks to Sonar's local HTTP API to:

- put only **Mic + Media** in that stream mix (game sound and Discord never leak into it),
- route the radio player and Spotify to the Media channel,
- route WARDOGS's mic input to the Stream device. WARDOGS's voice chat uses the Windows default mic regardless of its own menu setting, so the script overrides it per-app.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (built in)
- [SteelSeries GG](https://steelseries.com/gg) with **Sonar** enabled
- [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) (for `ffplay`): `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`
- [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) (for YouTube stations): `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp`

## Setup

1. Clone or download this repo anywhere.
2. Run **`Launch WardogsRadio.cmd`**.
3. Click **Set up Sonar**. This switches Sonar to Streamer mode and configures the mixes. Your current headset and mic are detected automatically, so do this while Sonar is in Classic mode the first time.
4. Pick a station, press **Play**, and tick **Music ON AIR**.
5. In WARDOGS, use proximity chat (hold K, or tap K with the toggle enabled).

**Optional auto-launch:** put a shortcut to `WardogsRadioWatcher.ps1` in your Startup folder (`Win+R` → `shell:startup`) with this target:

```
powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\path\to\WardogsRadioWatcher.ps1"
```

**Going back to normal:** click **Sonar back to Classic**. While Sonar is in Classic mode the Stream mic doesn't exist, so the game's mic routing returns to normal.

## Notes and caveats

- **Etiquette:** proximity chat reaches everyone nearby, enemies included. Keep the on-air volume reasonable. **Ctrl+Alt+R** is your kill switch.
- **The K toggle** uses a keyboard hook and a simulated held key. WARDOGS's anti-cheat isn't publicly documented, so use it at your own risk. Untick it to go back to normal hold-to-talk. Typing a `k` in text chat also flips it.
- **The in-game mic test** plays back the mic input regardless of push-to-talk, so it can't confirm whether you're transmitting.
- **Content:** stations stream from public YouTube uploads and internet radio at play time. Nothing is downloaded or redistributed. Respect the rights of the music owners and the platforms' terms.
- The Sonar API is unofficial and undocumented, and a GG update could change it. Route names come from the excellent [DataNext27/SteelSeries-NET-API](https://github.com/DataNext27/SteelSeries-NET-API).

Not affiliated with SteelSeries, Rockstar Games or the WARDOGS developers.

## License

MIT

plwg/robot-steps.desc: A first coding game for young kids, written in Rust: program a robot with arrows, loops and ifs
plwg/robot-steps.readme:
# Robot Steps

A first coding game for young children (made for a 5-year-old). Tap arrows to
build a program, press play, and watch the robot follow it to collect the
stars. There's no reading required.

**[Play it in your browser](https://plwg.github.io/robot-steps/)**

![The level map: finished levels are filled in with a star, and the next one pulses](docs/map.png)

| Choose a player | Playing a level |
|---|---|
| ![Three players, each with their own robot and progress](docs/players.png) | ![Level 48: the main program calls the ● and ▲ functions, and the robot is partway through ▲, chopping a tree](docs/level.png) |

Across 107 levels in 17 chapters, numbered within each chapter (`3-2`), it
introduces, in the order programming is usually taught:

1. **Moving:** up, down, left and right, in order
2. **Ice:** the robot slides until grass, a rock or the edge stops it, so it
   has to think ahead about where it will end up (and sometimes go the long
   way round)
3. **The axe:** chop down trees (but not rocks)
4. **Keys and doors:** a locked door needs a key, and each key opens one
   door. The robot remembers what it's carrying, so the order matters: fetch
   the key first, even when it's the other way
5. **Bridges:** a bridge holds the robot once, then falls in the river
   behind it. There's no going back the same way, so plan the way round
   (and which island to leave till last)
6. **Repeat:** run one block several times when there aren't enough slots
7. **If:** mystery clouds become a tree or grass each run, so the robot has
   to look before it chops: "if there's a tree to the right { chop it }". Tap
   "if", pick what to look for (shown as map tiles: a tree, rock, star, ice,
   key, door, grass, or the edge of the map, whichever the level offers),
   then which way. The blocks to run go inside its brackets
8. **Loops:** repeat a whole group of blocks
9. **If inside loops:** "if there's a tree to the right { chop it }" or "if
   there's a star above { fetch it }" in a loop: one rule handles whatever
   the robot finds, wherever it finds it
10. **Else:** "if there's a tree to the right { go down } otherwise { go
   right }". The grey ✗ between the blocks marks where the "otherwise" part
   starts
11. **Not:** "if there's *no* tree above { fetch the star }". In the
    "if" choices, the red "no" sign crosses out what to look for
12. **Repeat until:** "keep going until there's a wall that way". The robot
    looks before each time round. Mystery clouds decide how far it is, so no
    fixed number of times would do. One that would go round for ever (back
    where it started, and still no wall) stops and shakes red. Then it can
    look for other things too, picked like an "if": "keep going until
    there's grass below", and with "not", "keep going down until there's
    no wall to the right"
13. **Functions:** extra strips of blocks named with a shape (● and ▲) that
    the main program calls whenever it needs them
14. **Functions + if:** "if" blocks inside functions
15. **Function numbers:** call ● with a number (set with repeat), and
    inside it a count can be "●'s number" instead of a fixed one, so one
    function makes stairs of 1, 2 and 3
16. **Rain:** rain clouds count down 3, 2, 1, rain for 2, then start again.
    A row under each cloud shows its whole cycle (a dot for each dry tick, a
    drop for each tick of rain, with the one it's on now ringed). Every
    action takes a
    tick, so sleep while it rains (the sleep block, Zzz, repeated like any
    other) or hurry across before it starts. Being under a cloud when it
    rains is getting wet, and the end of the run
17. **All together**

Throughout, a **slider** along the top runs the program ahead of time, while
it's being built: drag it to see where the robot would be just before any
step, with the block about to run lifted up, the rain clouds counting, and
one way the mystery clouds could turn out (play picks again). The end of the
slider shows how it would finish: a star, a red cross or rain. Play always
runs from the start.

Throughout, **debugging**: when the robot bumps into something, the step
that went wrong shakes red, and the program stays put to be fixed. Tapping a
block opens an empty slot before it for a missing step, and the eraser that
appears on a block under the pointer takes it out.

Each new block is first shown in a demo level (▶ on the map): the program is

Every action has a sound, and each direction plays its own note, so a

# IberAPP

Landing narrativa del Gran Parque Iberá (Corrientes, Argentina): portales, ecosistema, estado de los caminos, minijuegos educativos y valoración de la visita para turistas. Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, Tailwind 4 y TypeScript.

## Documentación

La guía de implementación es la fuente de verdad: [`docs/GUIA_IMPLEMENTACION.md`](docs/GUIA_IMPLEMENTACION.md). Empezá por ahí.

## Estado

| Fase | Contenido | Estado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–3 | Base, cáscara, secciones de contenido, mapas | ✅ |
| 4 | Valoración para turistas (modal "Valorar") | ✅ |
| 4 | Minijuegos (*Aprender jugando*): Canales limpios y Señales del agua | ✅ (Cielo oscuro y Voces de la noche: próximamente) |
| 5 | Coreografía de scroll | ✅ |
| 6 | Uso sin conexión (service worker) y deploy en Vercel | ✅ |
| 6 | Backend [IberaReclamos](https://github.com/FabianGQuintana/IBERA-Rangers-API) (recibe las valoraciones) | ✅ (falta publicarlo en Railway) |
| 6 | Estado real de los caminos | ⏳ pendiente |

## ⚠️ Decisión pactada: los minijuegos no son los de la landing v6

La app replica la landing v6 (`docs/prototipo/`) **salvo en los minijuegos**. De la sección *Aprender jugando* se conserva la estructura (lugar en la página, índice de cuatro temas y vínculos con los portales y las amenazas), pero **las mecánicas de v6 son solo una referencia**: el equipo quiere hacer juegos **mejores**. Si vas a continuar el desarrollo, no los copies; leé la sección 10 de la guía para saber qué es contrato y qué queda libre.

## Desarrollo

```bash
npm run dev            # servidor de desarrollo (antes copia el worker de MapLibre y genera el arte de los juegos)
npm run lint
npm run build
npm run test:e2e       # Playwright
npm run compare:v6     # capturas lado a lado contra el prototipo (ver guía, sección 14)
```

Este proyecto usa una versión de Next.js con cambios incompatibles: ante cualquier duda, leé `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (ver `AGENTS.md`).

## Deploy en Vercel

1. En Vercel: **Add New → Project**, importar este repositorio. Framework: Next.js (se detecta solo). No hace falta cambiar comandos: `npm run build` ya copia el worker de MapLibre.
2. Variables de entorno (ver `.env.example`):
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`: URL del backend IberaReclamos. Vacía = modo demo (el formulario "Valorar" no envía nada).
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPTILER_KEY`: opcional, mapas de MapTiler en vez de Esri.
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`: opcional; si queda vacía se usa el dominio de producción de Vercel.
3. El backend tiene que permitir por CORS el dominio de Vercel (y `http://localhost:3000` para desarrollo).

## Uso sin señal

En producción, `public/sw.js` guarda la página, las fotos y los mapas ya vistos: después de una primera visita con señal, la landing abre sin conexión. Las valoraciones enviadas sin señal quedan en el teléfono y se envían solas al volver la conexión. Al cambiar la estrategia de caché, subir `VERSION` en `public/sw.js`.

VolcanicWorks/bidlock.readme:
# Bidlock

A five-minute sealed-bid strategy game for 2 to 4 players. Humans play in the browser, AI agents play over a small HTTP/JSON API, and both can sit at the same table.

**Play:** open the public URL, press **Start game**. No install, no login.

## Rules

Everyone holds the same 13 chips, numbered 1 to 13. Each round a prize card from -4 to +9 is turned up and all players secretly lock in one chip at the same time. Any chip that matches another player's chip **clashes** and is void. If the prize is positive the highest surviving chip takes it; if it is negative the lowest surviving chip gets stuck with it. If every chip clashes, the prize stays and the next card is added to it. Spent chips are gone for good and every hand is public, so you can always see what your rivals have left. Highest total after 13 rounds wins (tiebreak: fewer negative cards, then a shared win).

Why it plays well:

- **A real decision every round.** Your 13 is a sure win now, but once it is gone everyone knows it. A big chip can be cancelled by a rival who reads you, so sometimes the smart play is a modest chip nobody else expects.
- **No dominant strategy.** Bidding in proportion to the prize beats random play, a bot that predicts that bidder beats it, and a bot that predicts *that* bot beats it in turn. Results from `node test/matrix.js` (row's win rate against column, 2 players, 1,500 games each):

  | row vs column | random | greedy | extremist | shark | reader | deep |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | **random** | - | 3% | 9% | 9% | 32% | 53% |
  | **greedy** | 97% | - | 70% | 80% | 0% | 49% |
  | **extremist** | 89% | 33% | - | 66% | 27% | 59% |
  | **shark** | 92% | 20% | 32% | - | 13% | 42% |
  | **reader** | 70% | 100% | 76% | 87% | - | 0% |
  | **deep** | 50% | 52% | 41% | 59% | 100% | - |

  Every strategy has a counter. The house bot that fills empty seats does not follow any of these fixed patterns: for each chip it could play, it plays the rest of the match out a few dozen times against varied opponents and keeps the chip that wins most often, then picks with a little randomness so it cannot be read. The Steady level beats each fixed pattern above 60-78% of the time head to head; Sharp thinks harder.
- **Short.** 13 rounds with a 30-second timer (configurable) is 3 to 6 minutes. If a player runs out of time the house bot plays a chip for them, so a match can never stall.

## Run it

Needs Node.js 18 or newer. No dependencies.

```bash
git clone <this repo> && cd bidlock
node server.js            # http://localhost:8080
```

Environment variables (all optional):

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address |
| `TURN_SECONDS` | `30` | Default turn timer for new matches |
| `DATA_DIR` | `./data` | Where finished-match replays are saved (kept 7 days) |

Docker: `docker build -t bidlock . && docker run -p 8080:8080 bidlock`

Tests: `node test/run.js` (rules and an end-to-end API match), `node test/matrix.js` (strategy balance).

## Agent API

Base URL is the game URL. All bodies are JSON. Authenticate seat actions with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `"token"` in the body, or `?token=` in the query). Errors return `{"error": "plain explanation"}` with a 4xx status. `GET /api` returns a machine-readable index; `GET /api/docs` returns this file.

### The loop

```
POST /api/matches/{code}/join   -> token
repeat:
  GET  /api/matches/{code}/state?wait=1&since={version}   (long-poll, returns on any change)
  if state.you.mustMove: POST /api/matches/{code}/move {"chip": n}
until state.status == "finished"
```

Tip: a fully deterministic bot is easy to read, and two copies of it clash every round. That is the game working as intended.

That is the whole integration. A complete bot in 70 lines of standard-library Python is in [`bots/sample_bot.py`](bots/sample_bot.py) (also served at `/bot.py`).

### Endpoints

**`POST /api/matches`** create a match.
Body (all optional): `{"seats": 2-4, "bots": 0..seats-1, "botLevel": "steady", "turnSeconds": 5-300, "public": true}`.
`bots` fills seats with house bots right away. `botLevel` is `"steady"` (default) or `"sharp"`. `public: false` hides it from the open-match list.
Returns `201 {"code": "K7Q2M", "url": "/m/K7Q2M", "state": {...}}`.

**`GET /api/matches`** list public lobbies waiting for players.
Returns `{"open": [{"code", "seats", "filled", "players", "turnSeconds", "createdAt"}]}`.

**`POST /api/matches/{code}/join`** take the next seat.
Body: `{"name": "MyAgent", "kind": "agent"}` (`kind` is `"agent"` or `"human"`, only used for display).
Returns `{"token", "seat", "name", "host", "state"}`. The first non-bot to join is the host. The match starts automatically when the last seat fills.

**`POST /api/matches/{code}/start`** (host only) fill empty seats with house bots and start now.

**`GET /api/matches/{code}/state`** read the state. Send your token to get the `you` block.
Query: `wait=1&since={version}` holds the request until `version` changes (max 25 s), so you never need to poll in a tight loop.

**`POST /api/matches/{code}/move`** lock in a chip for the current round.
Body: `{"chip": 7}`. Returns `{"ok": true, "state": {...}}`. You cannot change a locked chip. Errors: `400` you do not hold that chip, `409` already locked or match not playing.

**`GET /api/matches/{code}/replay`** full round-by-round record. Finished matches stay available at `GET /api/replay/{code}` for 7 days, and humans can watch them at `/replay/{code}`.

### State object

```json
{
  "code": "K7Q2M",
  "status": "playing",            // "lobby" | "playing" | "finished"
  "version": 42,                  // pass back as ?since= for long-polling
  "round": 5, "totalRounds": 13,
  "turnSeconds": 30,
  "secondsLeft": 21.4,            // until a chip is auto-played for anyone not locked in
  "pot": { "cards": [3, 6], "value": 9 },   // >1 card means it carried over
  "unseenPrizes": [-4, -1, 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9],

botbtcfun/kickflip.desc: Flick it, flip it, land it on its wheels. A one-swipe pixel-art browser game: 21 things to kickflip, from a skateboard to a giraffe. No engine, no image or audio files.
botbtcfun/kickflip.readme:
# Kickflip

Flick it, flip it, land it on its wheels. A pixel-art game of one swipe:
something sits on the street, you flick it up, and it kickflips. Flick with
the right strength and it lands on its wheels, or its feet, and the next one
rolls in. Too soft or too hard and it lands on its side or its roof, and a
life goes.

There are 21 things to flip, and most were never meant to be: a roadster
with thrusters under its floor, a skateboard, a pizza box, a brick, a
penguin, a giraffe, a fridge, a cat. Each run starts with the same six, then
the day's draw brings the rest, everyday things first, then the heavy ones,
then the odd ones. A run that gets to 21 meets every one once.

[Play it](https://kickflip.botbtc.fun), or
[watch 20 seconds of it](https://kickflip.botbtc.fun/clip.mp4). To share it on X, post
[kickflip.botbtc.fun/x](https://kickflip.botbtc.fun/x): its card is a player,
which X may show as the game itself, playable in the post.

## Play

| | |
|---|---|
| Phone | Hold anywhere and let go: the longer, the more it spins. A bar shows how far it's charged. Or swipe up: the faster, the more |
| Mouse | Hold the button and let go, or drag up and let go |
| Keyboard | Hold ↑ or Space and let go |
| P or Esc | Pause |
| M | Sound on or off |

- **The window.** A flip lands clean within some degrees of a whole turn.
  The first objects forgive a flick a fifth off; every object after that
  forgives a little less. After each landing a meter shows where the flick
  fell: PERFECT in the bright middle, CLEAN in the green.
- **Weight.** Light things spin easily and are easy to overdo; heavy ones
  need a hard flick. The card under each object says which it is.
- **Quirks.** The roadster's thrusters land anything, and the cat always
  lands on its feet. The paper plane and the toast need two turns. The
  banana and the bowling pin are narrow, and the ice cube and the fish are
  slippery: they forgive less.
- **Score.** Points grow with each object, double for a PERFECT, and
  multiply with a streak of clean landings, up to ×8.
- **Tricks.** Two whole turns land too, and so do three: a double kickflip
  pays twice, a triple three times. Flicking as hard as you can never lands
  anything.
- **Lives.** Three, and when they're gone, a surprise.

## Run it

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:5174
pnpm test       # the simulation's tests
pnpm build      # the static site in dist/, and the whole game in one file
```

## How it's made

- `src/sim`: the game itself, in plain TypeScript with no browser in it. It
  runs on a fixed 60 Hz tick with integer arithmetic and a seeded generator,
  so the same day and the same flicks give the same run on any device. A run
  is its input log: the ticks that had a flick, and how hard.
- `src/render`: drawing on a plain canvas, with no game engine. Each object
  is three faces, side, roof and underside, painted pixel by pixel in code;
  there are no image files. Mid-flip, each column along the object is drawn
  as a stack of slabs, each as wide as the object is at that height, turned
  and squashed, so a cabin turns narrower than its car and a head turns on
  its body.
- `src/audio`: the sounds, synthesised in the browser with Web Audio as they
  play: a whoosh for the flick, a tick each quarter turn, a chord on landing
  that climbs with the streak, a bell for PERFECT. There are no audio files.
- `src/ui`: the strip, the card, the verdicts and the screens.
- `worker`: the Cloudflare Worker serving the game.

The build also packs the game into one HTML file, `dist/kickflip.html`, with
its script, styles and fonts inline, and the same as a `data:` URL in
`dist/data-url.txt`, which plays pasted into an address bar.

## Licence

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The fonts are Press Start 2P and VT323 (SIL Open
Font License), through [Fontsource](https://fontsource.org).

davidrf88/blackjack.desc: 2D blackjack table with NPC players who react to the game
davidrf88/blackjack.readme:
# Blackjack Table

A 2D blackjack game in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. There's no build step: open `index.html` in a browser to play.

You sit in the middle seat with four NPCs at the table. Each one plays and bets in their own way and reacts to what happens:

| NPC | Style |
| --- | --- |
| **Lucky Lou** (third base) | Plays perfect basic strategy. Comments when you make a play that isn't by the book, and the **Ask Lou** button gives you his advice. |
| **Vera** | Plays cautiously and stands on any hard 12+. Complains when someone "takes the dealer's bust card". |
| **Big Tony** | High roller. Hits until 18, doubles a lot, and sometimes splits tens. |
| **Mia** | Nervous beginner. Mostly follows the strategy chart, but sometimes guesses. |

Rules: 6-deck shoe reshuffled at 75% penetration, dealer stands on all 17s, blackjack pays 3:2, you can double on any first two cards (including after a split), split up to 4 hands, and split aces get one card each.

Your bankroll, the NPCs' bankrolls, your last bet and your sound/speed settings are saved in the browser, so they're still there when you come back. If you leave in the middle of a hand, the bet on the table is lost. Chips you've placed but not dealt yet are returned.

Controls: click chips to bet, then **Deal** (or press Enter). During your turn, press **H**it, **S**tand, **D**ouble or s**P**lit.

## Asset credits

- Cards and chips: [Kenney Boardgame Pack](https://kenney.nl/assets/boardgame-pack), CC0
- Sounds: [Kenney Casino Audio](https://kenney.nl/assets/casino-audio), CC0
- Character faces: [Avataaars](https://avataaars.com/) by Pablo Stanley, free for personal and commercial use, generated with [DiceBear](https://www.dicebear.com/)

BryanRha/dessert-pop.desc: Dessert Pop! — 디저트 매치3 H5 게임
BryanRha/dessert-pop.readme:
# Dessert Pop! — 디저트 매치3 H5 게임

브라우저에서 바로 실행되는 세로형 매치3 퍼즐 게임. Phaser 3 + 순수 JS (빌드 도구 없음).
모든 그래픽·사운드는 `../assets/tools/` 의 생성 스크립트로 직접 만든 오리지널 리소스.

## 실행

정적 파일 서버로 `game/` 폴더를 열면 된다. (ES 모듈이라 `file://` 로 직접 열면 동작하지 않음)

```bash
cd game && python3 -m http.server 8080
```

브라우저에서 `http://localhost:8080` → 모바일은 같은 Wi-Fi 에서 `http://<PC IP>:8080`.

> OneDrive 폴더 안에서는 macOS 권한 때문에 서버가 파일을 못 읽을 수 있다.
> 그럴 때는 `node tools/sync.js --mirror` 로 `~/dessert-pop-dist` 에 복사한 뒤 그 폴더를 서빙한다.

## 배포

**공개 주소: https://bryanrha.github.io/dessert-pop/** (GitHub Pages, 로그인 없이 누구나 플레이)

수정 후 다시 배포하기:

```bash
bash tools/deploy_pages.sh "변경 내용 한 줄"
```

`config.js` 의 `VERSION` 을 올려 두면 타이틀 화면 아래 버전으로 반영 여부를 확인할 수 있다.

다른 곳에 올리려면 `game/` 폴더(약 12MB)를 정적 호스팅(Netlify, Vercel, S3 등)에 그대로 올리면 된다.
`tools/` 폴더는 배포에 필요 없다. PWA 매니페스트가 있어 홈 화면에 추가하면 전체 화면 앱처럼 실행된다.

## 폴더 구조

```
game/
├─ index.html, manifest.webmanifest
├─ lib/phaser.min.js          Phaser 3.90
├─ fonts/Jua-Regular.ttf      UI 폰트 (SIL OFL 1.1, fonts/OFL.txt)
├─ icons/                     PWA·파비콘·OG 이미지
├─ assets/                    ← tools/sync.js 가 ../assets 에서 복사 (직접 수정 금지)
└─ src/
   ├─ core/engine.js          게임 규칙 엔진 (화면과 무관, Node 에서도 실행)
   ├─ core/levels.js          레벨 1~30 정의 (+ levels_more.js 31~100)
   ├─ core/levels_tuning.js   봇 시뮬레이션으로 정한 이동 수·별 기준 (자동 생성)
   ├─ scenes/                 Boot(로딩) · Title · Map · Game
   ├─ ui/widgets.js           버튼·팝업·토스트
   ├─ audio.js · save.js · i18n.js · config.js
```

## 게임 규칙 요약

| 매치 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 3개 | 제거 |
| 4개 일렬 | 줄무늬 디저트 (가로/세로 한 줄 제거) |
| L·T 모양 | 선물 포장 폭탄 (3×3) |
| 5개 일렬 | 무지개 젤라토 (같은 색 전부 제거) |

특수 조합: 줄+줄 = 십자, 줄+폭탄 = 3줄 십자, 폭탄+폭탄 = 5×5, 무지개+블록 = 그 색 전부,
무지개+특수 = 그 색 전부를 특수로 바꿔 발동, 무지개+무지개 = 보드 전체.

장애물: 딸기 젤리(바닥) · 얼음 사탕(1~3단) · 사슬 · 솜사탕 거품 · 브라우니(1~3단) · 비스킷(1~2단) ·
녹은 초콜릿(번짐) · 시한폭탄 · 재료(체리/밤) · 별 코인.

부스터: 롤리팝 망치(1칸 제거) · 거품기 셔플 · 자유 교환 · +5 이동. 코인으로 구매.

## 개발 도구

```bash
npm test                 # 엔진 불변식 테스트 (전 레벨 무작위 플레이 + 특수 조합)
node tools/bot.js 12 30  # 레벨 12 를 봇으로 30판 → 승률·점수
node tools/tune.js 40    # 전 레벨 이동 수·별 기준 자동 조정 → levels_tuning.js
node tools/diag.js 18    # 실패한 판의 목표별 진행도 (병목 찾기)
node tools/sync.js       # ../assets 빌드 결과를 game/assets 로 동기화
```

브라우저 자동 플레이 검증: 개발 서버에서 콘솔에 `tools/browser/autoplay.js` 내용을 붙여 넣고
`await autoplay(5)` → 매 턴 화면 스프라이트가 엔진 상태와 일치하는지 검사한다.

헤드리스 Chrome 으로 한 번에 돌리기 (`puppeteer-core` 가 설치된 폴더에 `tools/browser/*` 를 복사해서 실행):

```bash
node e2e.mjs http://localhost:8080 1 100 ./shots   # 전 레벨 자동 플레이 + 레벨별 스크린샷
node flow.mjs ./shots                              # 첫 실행 흐름(타이틀→지도→튜토리얼→일시정지) 스크린샷
```

### 레벨 추가하기

레벨 1~30 은 `src/core/levels.js` 의 `RAW`, 31~100 은 `src/core/levels_more.js` 의 `MORE` 배열.
31 이후는 좌표 함수로 모양을 만든다 (`L({ w, h, hole, piece, jelly, cover })`). 문자 규칙은 `engine.js` 상단 주석 참고.

```js
L({ id: 101, goals: [{ type: 'jelly' }], jelly: (x, y) => (y >= 6 ? '1' : null) })
```

추가 후 `node tools/tune.js 60 101` 을 돌리면 이동 수·목표량·별 기준이 자동으로 맞춰진다.
월드를 늘리면 `config.js` 의 `WORLD_COUNT`·`MAP_THEME`, `i18n.js` 의 `worldName`, `gen_sea_scenes.py` 의 `WORLDS`(게임 배경)를 함께 늘린다.
월드 맵은 10레벨 단위로 월드가 바뀐다 (`WORLD_OF`).

### 리소스 수정하기

```bash
python3 ../assets/tools/build.py      # 그래픽 SVG → PNG
python3 ../assets/tools/gen_audio.py  # 효과음·BGM
node tools/sync.js                    # 게임으로 복사
```

## 저장 데이터

`localStorage` 의 `dessertpop_save_v1` 키에 진행도(별, 최고 점수, 코인, 부스터, 설정)를 저장한다.
설정 → "진행 초기화" 로 지울 수 있다.

lanwakacsus/blind-tape.desc: Real-time trading game with a built-in backtester and a daily challenge
lanwakacsus/blind-tape.readme:
# Blind Tape

A real-time trading game combined with a backtester. The source is TypeScript; the build bundles it into a single HTML file.

The market runs on its own clock and you never see the next bar. Go long, short or flat while six rule-based bots race you on the same tape. After each round, the backtest lab shows how each bot traded, lets you tune them, sweep SMA parameters, and check settings out of sample on 100 fresh markets.

## Play

Build it (see below) and open `dist/blind-tape.html` in a browser. Everything is in that one file except the fonts, which load from Google Fonts.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↑` / `L` | Go long |
| `↓` / `S` | Go short |
| `Space` / `F` | Go flat |
| hold `→` | Fast-forward |
| `P` / `Esc` | Pause |
| `M` | Mute |

## Modes

- **Season**: five markets, each faster and more volatile than the last. Earn stars for finishing in profit, beating buy & hold, and finishing first. One star unlocks the next market.
- **Daily challenge**: the same market for everyone each day (seeded from the UTC date), with one ranked run. The shared leaderboard only works when the page runs as a claude.ai artifact; opened locally, results are kept in your browser.
- **Your own CSV**: load prices with `date, open, high, low, close` columns, or a single close column.

## The bots

| Name | Strategy |
| --- | --- |
| INDEX | Buy & hold |
| CROSS | SMA crossover |
| MOMO | Momentum |
| BREAK | Donchian breakout |
| SNAP | RSI mean reversion |
| BANDS | Bollinger mean reversion |

Each bot decides at the daily close using only past bars and pays 0.10% per trade, the same cost you pay.

## Markets

Markets are synthetic: a random walk that switches between regimes (grind-up, selloff, chop, melt-up, crash), with volatility clustering and occasional gaps.

## Development

Needs Node 20.19 or newer.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # Vite dev server with hot reload
npm test           # Vitest unit tests for the engine and DOM helpers
npm run build      # type-check, then write dist/blind-tape.html
npm run preview    # serve the built file
```

`npm run build` inlines all JavaScript and CSS into `dist/blind-tape.html` (via `vite-plugin-singlefile`), so the result can be published as a single claude.ai artifact.

### Hosting on Vercel

`vercel.json` builds the project and serves `blind-tape.html` at `/`. Import the repo at vercel.com/new, or run `npx vercel` in this folder. The shared daily board only works on claude.ai; elsewhere, daily results are kept in each player's browser.

### Layout

| Folder | What's there |
| --- | --- |
| `src/engine/` | Pure maths, no DOM: market generator and CSV import (`market.ts`), indicators and bots (`strategies.ts`), backtester and stats (`backtest.ts`), parameter sweep and out-of-sample runs (`research.ts`) |
| `src/game/` | Round state and clock, intrabar price path, positions and fees (`round.ts`), scoring and stars (`scoring.ts`), saved progress (`save.ts`), sound |
| `src/render/` | Canvas drawing: shared grid, candle and marker helpers (`canvas.ts`), live tape, debrief charts, title background |
| `src/ui/` | Screens (title, play, debrief, lab, daily panels), input handling and the `h()` DOM helper |
| `src/daily/` | Daily challenge: dates, share text, and the claude.ai `db`/`user` leaderboard code |
| `test/` | Vitest suites |

`test/fixtures/legacy-engine.json` holds outputs of the original single-file build (commit `814c300`). The tests check that the engine still reproduces them exactly, so the daily tape for a given date is the same on old and new builds.
