# Coast Road GP

A pseudo-3D arcade racer that runs in the browser. One HTML file, no build step, no dependencies.

## Play

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. To serve it locally instead:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then visit http://localhost:8000
```

## The race

- 3 laps of a 3.6 km coastal circuit with hills, S-bends and two hard corners.
- 5 AI rivals. You start from the back of the grid.
- Three fields: Rookie, Pro, Legend (AI pace rises with each).
- Nitro gives about 3 seconds of boost per full tank and refills slowly.
- Leaving the tarmac costs most of your speed. Trees, rocks, signs and lamp posts stop you dead.
- Best lap, best race time and wins are saved per field in the browser (`localStorage`).

## Controls

| Action   | Keyboard            | Touch          |
|----------|---------------------|----------------|
| Throttle | Up arrow / W        | Gas            |
| Brake    | Down arrow / S      | Brake          |
| Steer    | Left/Right / A, D   | Arrow buttons  |
| Nitro    | Space / Shift       | Nitro          |
| Pause    | P / Esc             | Pause button   |
| Sound    | M                   | Sound button   |

## How it works

- Classic segment-based pseudo-3D road renderer on a 2D canvas: the track is a list of 200-unit segments carrying curve and elevation; each frame projects ~300 of them and draws back to front.
- All art (cars, palms, pines, billboards, gantry, sky, mountains) is drawn procedurally; there are no image assets.
- Fixed 60 Hz simulation step, independent of display refresh rate.
- Engine, gravel and crash sounds are synthesized with the Web Audio API.

# X Algo Quest

Every change to the X For You algorithm, turned into a pixel game. Plain words, real numbers straight from [X's open source code](https://github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm), scanned every day.

**Play it:** https://xalgoquest.vercel.app

## How it stays up to date

1. **Every morning on GitHub** (`.github/workflows/daily-scan.yml`): clones `xai-org/x-algorithm`, rebuilds `public/index.html`, and commits. Every push makes Vercel redeploy production, so the live site updates daily even when nothing changed (the "last scan" stamp moves).
2. **Score changes and new factors are automatic.** `tools/build.py` reads every ranking weight in `home-mixer/params` at each commit day, so a changed number or a brand new factor shows up with no manual work.
3. **Plain-English notes** live in `copy.json`. A daily Claude task on Maya's Mac fills in notes for any new day and pushes. Until then, a new day shows an automatic placeholder plus its real number changes.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `template.html` | The page: styles, layout, game logic, and the how-to tour |
| `copy.json` | Hand-written titles and stories per day, names for each factor |
| `tools/build.py` | Reads the algorithm repo, merges `copy.json`, writes `public/index.html` |
| `tools/record.mjs` | Records the site tour (`public/xalgoquest-tour.mp4`), the square X cut (`--promo`, `public/xalgoquest-x.mp4`), and `public/og.png` |
| `DAILY.md` | Step-by-step for the daily notes job and the writing rules |

## Run it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm.git .cache/x-algorithm
python3 -I tools/build.py .cache/x-algorithm
open public/index.html
```

Re-record the video (needs Chrome and an ffmpeg with libx264; set `FFMPEG_DIR`):

```bash
cd tools && npm install && npm run record && npm run og
```

Fan made. Not affiliated with X.

# Downshaft

A 3D descent game for [start.ng](https://start.ng), inspired by the classic NS-Shaft.
The ledges keep rising toward a ceiling of spikes, so keep dropping down without falling into the dark.

- **Stone** +1 HP · **Spikes** −4 HP · **Conveyor** carries you · **Spring** bounces you · **Cracked** gives way
- The ceiling costs 4 HP and knocks you through the ledge you're on

Controls: ← → or A D to move, P to pause, M for sound. On touch screens, hold the left or right side.

Plays as your start.ng character and saves your deepest floor to the start.ng leaderboard.
Static files only (three.js from jsDelivr), so there's no build step: open `index.html` through any static server.

The character model is adapted from start.ng's [Hangout](https://github.com/Blackburn0/startng-hangout) example.

# ZONE Z

Game bắt zombie bằng camera của THEZONE (Phú Tân, An Giang). Bản test trên điện thoại.

- Chơi: https://zonezgame.github.io/
- Một file `index.html`, không cần cài đặt. Dữ liệu chơi lưu trên máy người chơi.
- Cần mở qua https để điện thoại cho dùng camera và cảm biến xoay.

## Tài khoản (Firebase)
1. Dán `firebaseConfig` vào `firebase-config.js` (thay `null`).
2. Firestore → Rules: dán toàn bộ `firestore.rules` → Publish.
3. Firestore → tạo collection `config`, document `staff`, field `emails` (array) chứa email Google của nhân viên.
4. Nhân viên mở `staff.html` để quét mã tại quầy.

Khách đăng nhập bằng nickname tự do (có dấu, ký tự đặc biệt) + PIN 4 số; quên PIN thì tạo nickname mới (cần bật Email/Password và Anonymous trong Authentication). Nhân viên dùng Google cho trang quầy.

Chưa có cấu hình thì game vẫn chạy, dữ liệu lưu trên máy.

A single-player pixel RPG set in the world of the Bloodlines board game. The design lives in
`../docs/quest/QUEST-BUILD-GUIDE.md`. This folder is a self-contained project: its own
`package.json`, `node_modules`, TypeScript, Vite, Vitest and oxlint configs. It does not touch the
board game app; the site's build runs `npm ci && npm test && npm run build` here and serves the result
at `/quest/`.

**Status:** Phase 1 (skeleton) and Phase 2 (the Echo, puzzles, and Act I in Zetwal) are done, plus a
playability pass from the owner's phone test: an 8-direction analog stick, a 320 x 180 (16:9) screen,
readable drawings for every story object, interaction markers, name labels and Echo-change feedback.

## Run

```sh
cd quest
npm install
npm run dev            # http://localhost:5180 (add -- --host to open it on a phone on the same Wi-Fi)
```

URL options: `?map=test-village` starts a new game (when there is no save) on another map;
`?hintms=3000` makes Anissa's first hint come after 3 s instead of 3 minutes; `?touch=1` forces the
touch overlay.

**Phones play from the home screen.** On a phone or tablet in the browser the quest shows how to add it to
the home screen instead of starting (owner decision, Oct 16; `src/engine/install.ts`). Computers play in the
browser. The dev server (`npm run dev`) skips the screen so a phone on the same Wi-Fi can test in the
browser; `?install=1` shows it anyway, `?install=0` skips it.

Controls:

| Action  | Keyboard                        | Gamepad (standard)       | Touch                          |
|---------|---------------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|
| move    | arrows / WASD (two = diagonal)  | left stick / D-pad       | analog stick (left third)      |
| confirm | Z / Enter / Space               | A                        | A                              |
| cancel  | X / Backspace                   | B                        | B                              |
| run     | hold Shift (or X)               | hold B (or R)            | push the stick all the way, or hold B |
| echo    | E                               | X                        | Echo                           |
| menu    | Escape / M                      | Start                    | Menu                           |

The touch overlay appears on touch devices (force it with `?touch=1`).

**Moving in eight directions.** Movement is still tile by tile, but a step can be diagonal. A diagonal
step needs the target tile and both straight tiles it passes between to be open (no cutting a wall's
corner, no squeezing between two blocked tiles, no slipping past a person), so diagonals only shorten
walks straight steps could already make: they never open a way around a puzzle
(`tests/diagonal.test.ts` checks every map in both eras, and the puzzles' cheat lists include diagonal
cheats). A diagonal step takes 1.41 times as long. When held input asks for a refused diagonal, the
player slides along the wall (the horizontal part, else the vertical part). Diagonal steps onto a door
or a trigger work like straight ones. Sprites have four facings, so a diagonal shows its horizontal
side; A (and the name label) looks at the diagonal tile first, then the tile the sprite faces.

**Smooth walking.** The logic still moves one tile at a time, but the picture glides
(`src/engine/motion.ts`, `tests/motion.test.ts`): a constant speed in pixels (walk 4.5 tiles a second,
run 8, the same on diagonals, in `src/config.ts`), driven by the frame's delta time. While a direction
is held, the next step starts in the very frame the last one ends and carries that frame's leftover
distance, so there is no pause at tile edges at any frame rate; a direction tapped in the last 90 ms of
a step is kept for the next one. A tap always walks one tile (taps are how puzzles are solved, so
there is no turn-in-place delay). The walk frame comes from the distance walked (step A, stand, step
B, stand every two tiles), so the cycle carries on across tiles and Anissa walks in step. The camera
is placed by hand each frame on the same whole pixel as Gianna, so nothing shimmers.

**The touch stick** floats: it rests at the bottom left, and wherever a thumb lands in the left third
of the screen the ring jumps there (kept on screen) and the knob follows the thumb inside it. A 25%
dead zone, eight 45 degree sectors, and leaning past 85% runs (B still runs too). The gamepad's left
stick uses the same eight sectors (`stickDirection` in `src/input/actions.ts`); its D-pad and the
keyboard make diagonals by pressing two directions together.

**What the player sees.** Every story object has its own drawing (`src/assets.pixels.ts`), with
before and after states where the story changes it: the Gaze lamp (unlit, lit with a pulsing light),
the chain winch and the pawl (oiled in the Echo, rusted today, pinned once Patricio drives the pin),
the Chain Bridge (raised upright against the island, lowered across the chasm), the collapsed rope
bridge, the map table (dust sheet today, war map in the Echo), the loose floorboard, doors, signs, the
Marshal's Stone (and its cut stones in the Echo), name stones, shrines, wells, crates. A bobbing "!"
floats over people with something new to say (talking would change a flag; `GameLogic.markers` dry-runs
their dialogue), and a sparkle over things not used yet; both go away once used. Facing a person,
object or door shows a name label ("Gaze Lamp", "Chain Winch (rusted)", "Rope Bridge (collapsed)",
"Elodie Limyè, Mother"; names in `src/data/npcs.ts` and `src/data/objects.ts`). A on an object with no
dialogue of its own shows a one-line description. Comi

benllados/writ340-game.readme:
# The Game That Builds Itself Around You

A small browser game for a recorded WRIT 340 presentation (Benjamin Llados). It is a **scripted
demonstration of generative AI concepts**: every line of dialogue is pre-written, and no AI model runs.
Player choices still change real game state.

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no dependencies, accounts, API keys or network access. All art is drawn in code.

## Run it

**Option A (simplest):** double-click `index.html`. It works offline.

**Option B (local server):**

```bash
cd "/Users/benjaminllados/WRIT-340 Game"
python3 -m http.server 8340
```

Then open <http://localhost:8340>. For recording, press **F** for fullscreen. The stage stays 16:9.

### Deep links (skip the title screen)

| URL hash | Starts |
| --- | --- |
| `#ch=1` … `#ch=8` | that chapter, with its starting conditions |
| `&inherit=returned` | Chapters 4–8 as if you returned the bag (default: kept) |
| `&bridge=intact` | Chapter 8 as if you took the ferry (default: bridge collapsed) |
| `&auto=0` | rehearsal mode (slides do not open by themselves) |

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys / WASD | Walk |
| Space / Enter | Talk, pick up, advance dialogue |
| 1 / 2, or ↑ ↓ then Space | Choose an option |
| **Slides** | Space or → next · ← back · at the end press **Enter** to return to the game · Esc returns at any time |
| ↑ ↓ (Chapter 2 map slide) | Change the generator seed |
| **E** | Reopen the most recent explanation |
| **T** | Optional score details for Mara's memory (after the lantern scene) |
| **P** | Toggle slides: Auto (default) / Rehearsal (checkpoints stay closed; press E) |
| **C** | Chapter menu. In the menu, **K** switches the earlier bag choice, **J** the bridge outcome, for direct entry |
| **L** (title screen) | Continue from the last saved chapter checkpoint (only when you press it) |
| **B** | Full references (numbered as in the article); from a slide it returns to that slide |
| Driving (Chapter 6) | Arrow keys; no failure states |
| **R R** | Reset the current chapter to its entry state (the on-screen Reset button resets immediately) |
| **G** | Show the reserved webcam area (bottom-right 500×300) |
| **H** | Hide the top-right buttons and key strip |
| **F** | Fullscreen |

Slides freeze the game. Keys held while a slide closes are ignored until pressed again.

## Walkthrough (Chapters 1–5)

1. **Introduction:** Mara meets you at the gate. Walk to the **mapmaker by the fountain** and press Space.
2. **Generating content:** slides open: a live seed-based map with three rule checks (↑ ↓ changes the seed), then a prepared "learned generation" preview, then a comparison slide. Return, then walk east.
3. **Character memory:** Mara spots a bag and steps into view. Pick it up, then give it back or keep it. At the church plaza the sea gate is locked. Turn to Mara and ask for her lantern. Her answer depends on the retrieved memory, and two slides follow.
4. **Speaking versus acting:** walk to the house with the ladder, west of the church, and talk to Mara. She agrees but doesn't move (failure example), and a slide opens. Return, choose **Enable it**, and she walks the route and climbs onto the roof.
5. **World generation:** talk to the **guitarist** at the church steps. The grate beside the church opens. Walk up the lane into the tunnel, follow it east, and climb out on the harbour road. The world-model slide opens.
6. **Functional objects:** talk to the **mechanic** at the workshop and request the car. Advance through Appearance → Geometry → Parts with Space. You get in, and holding the arrows does nothing. Then Behavior is added: drive east along the cape road until the road ends at the bridge. The "Making a car work" slide opens.
7. **Persistent consequences:** the ferry pilot offers the dock. Choose **Use the damaged bridge** (you and Mara cross, then it collapses) or **Take the ferry**. With the bridge collapsed, the merchant reroutes to the ferry dock and the span blocks movement. The "Remembering a changed world" slide opens. Walk east to the lighthouse.
8. **Meaning and conclusion:** talk to the **keeper** to deliver. Three islanders make the same generic request, then Mara responds to your bag choice and the bridge. Four slides follow. Walk back to the island ferry dock (south) and take the ferry (or, if the bridge stands, walk back over it). Mara remarks on the bridge, a short transition returns you to the church, and the recap and closing slide follow. The closing slide stays up until you press Enter.

**Checkpoints:** every chapter entry is saved in the browser. **Space** on the title screen always starts a fresh run. **L** continues from the saved chapter. **R R** resets to the current chapter's entry state. If browser storage is blocked, everything still works for the session.

## What is live and what is scripted

| Live (computed from this playthrough) | Written by hand |
| --- | --- |
| Mara's memory stream (stored only within 5 tiles) | All dialogue, reflections and plans |
| Memory ranking: recency + importance + relevance (simplified) | Importance values and relevance tags |
| Lantern holder, Mara's position and behavior, tunnel access | The tunnel itself (an authored space, switched on by a script) |
| Car stages, collision and driving; bridge state, its collision and the merchant's route | The car's look at each stage (prepared art, not generated) |
| Procedural map and its three rule checks (Chapter 2) | The "learned generation" preview (prepared in advance) |

## Project layout

```
index.html        page shell (1920x1080 stage)
css/style.css     game UI + presentation (slide) styles
js/config.js      sizes, speeds, viewer preferences
js/pixelfont.js   5x7 pixel font for headings
js/art.js         all pixel art (tiles, buildings, props, characters)
js/world.js       town map, tunnel region, objects, collisions
js/state.js       game state + memory stream and retrieval scoring
js/story.js       chapters, beats, dialogue,

# Neon Hive Survivors 霓虹虫巢幸存者

A neon survivor-style browser game. You only move: your weapons fire on their own. Survive 15 minutes of the bug swarm and defeat the final boss, the Void Lord.

**Play online: https://machuiwen.github.io/swarm-survivor/**

Works on desktop, iPad and phones, in landscape or portrait. The game is in English and Chinese. It shows Chinese when your browser language is Chinese; switch any time with the language button on the main menu.

## Controls

| | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | WASD or arrow keys | Touch and drag anywhere (floating stick) |
| Pick an upgrade | 1 / 2 / 3, R to reroll | Tap a card |
| Pause | P or Esc | Pause button, top right |
| Sound on/off | M | Speaker button, top right |

## How to play

- Enemies drop XP gems. Level up and pick one of three: a new weapon, a weapon upgrade, or an item.
- 8 weapons and 12 items. Carry up to 6 of each.
- **Evolution**: get a weapon to max level (6) and own its matching item, then open a chest to evolve it. The upgrade card tells you which item you need.
- Elites (gold ring) and bosses drop chests. Bosses come at 5:00 and 10:00; the final boss arrives at 14:00.
- Pickups: hearts (heal), magnets (pull in every gem), skulls (clear the screen), coins.
- Spend coins in Upgrades for permanent boosts, and unlock new heroes under Heroes. Achievements also give coins.

## Tips

- Keep moving. Circle the swarm to bunch it up, then mow it down.
- Level your starting weapon first. The early game gets much easier.
- Grab a Gravity Core early so gems come to you.
- Follow the gold arrows at the screen edge to chests. A chest may evolve a weapon.
- Boomers explode when they die and hurt nearby enemies. Don't let one blow up next to you.
- Revival in the shop is expensive, but it can save a run.

## Notes

- Plain static site, no build step. All art and sound are generated in code. The Orbitron font is bundled in `fonts/` (SIL Open Font License, see `fonts/OFL.txt`).
- Progress is saved in the browser (localStorage). Clearing site data wipes it. On CrazyGames it is saved through the CrazyGames SDK instead.
- On iPhone / iPad the silent switch mutes the game. If there is no sound, check it and the speaker button.

## CrazyGames build

`tools/build-crazygames.sh` makes `dist/neon-hive-survivors-crazygames.zip` with `index.html` at the zip root. The game uses the CrazyGames HTML5 SDK v3 (`js/platform.js`) for loading and gameplay events and for saving. It shows no ads. Outside CrazyGames the SDK is skipped.

---

## 中文说明

霓虹风格的割草生存游戏。你只管走位，武器会自动开火。在 15 分钟的虫潮里活下来，打败最终首领「虚空之主」。

电脑、iPad、手机都能玩，横屏竖屏都可以。浏览器语言是中文时自动显示中文，主菜单的语言按钮可以随时切换。

### 操作

| | 键盘 | 触屏 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 移动 | WASD 或方向键 | 按住屏幕任意位置拖动（浮动摇杆） |
| 选择升级 | 数字键 1 / 2 / 3，R 刷新 | 直接点卡片 |
| 暂停 | P 或 Esc | 右上角暂停按钮 |
| 声音开关 | M | 右上角喇叭按钮 |

### 玩法

- 击杀敌人掉落经验宝石，捡起来升级。每次升级三选一：新武器、武器升级或被动道具。
- 共 8 种武器、12 种道具。最多带 6 件武器和 6 件道具。
- **进化**：武器升到满级（6 级），再拥有对应的道具，打开宝箱时就会进化成超级形态。升级卡片上会提示需要哪个道具。
- 精英怪（金色光圈）和首领会掉宝箱。5:00 和 10:00 有首领，14:00 最终首领登场。
- 地上还会掉落：爱心（回血）、磁铁（吸走全屏宝石）、骷髅（清屏）、金币。
- 金币可以在「强化商店」买永久强化，在「角色」里解锁新角色。完成成就会奖励金币。

### 小技巧

- 别停下来。绕着敌群转圈走，把它们聚成一团再收割。
- 前期优先升级初始武器，开局会轻松很多。
- 早点拿一个「引力核」，捡宝石省心很多。
- 看到宝箱指示箭头（屏幕边缘的金色箭头）就去捡，可能直接进化。
- 爆破虫被打死会爆炸，能炸到周围的敌人，但别让它贴着你自爆。
- 商店里的「复活」很贵，但能救命。

### 说明

- 纯静态网页，没有构建步骤。所有画面和音效都由代码实时生成。
- 存档保存在浏览器本地（localStorage）。清除网站数据会清空进度。
- iPhone / iPad 上，声音受静音开关影响。没声音的话请检查静音开关和右上角喇叭按钮。

# Ludum Dare 60
Theme: TBC

Built with [CraftyJS](http://craftyjs.com/api/) 0.9.0 (loaded from cdnjs).

## Run locally
Serve the folder over HTTP (asset loading fails from `file://`):

```
py -m http.server 8000
```

(`py` is the Windows launcher; use `python3` elsewhere.)

Then open http://localhost:8000.

## Layout
- `constants.js`: screen size, music track, credits list
- `game_state.js`: per-run state, reset with `resetGameState()`
- `assets.js`: sprites and audio preloaded by the Loading scene
- `scenes/`: Loading, Start, Game (placeholder: reach the green square), End
- `components/`: `AudioController` (global `audioController`), `MuteButton`, `GameTimer`, `PlayerNotification` (`Crafty.trigger("InstructionText", msg)`), `Button`, `CreditsText`
- `camera.js`: `makeCameraTrackEntity(entity, yOffset)`
- `analytics.js`: `track(event, params)`, a no-op until the GA4 snippet in `index.html` is enabled

Give an entity the `HUD` component to keep it fixed on screen while the camera moves.

## Deploy
Every push is synced by CircleCI to `s3://ludum-dare-60/<branch>/`, so `main` is served at `/main/index.html`.

CircleCI needs `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` set on the project, and the `ludum-dare-60` bucket must exist with public static hosting.

## Useful links
- [https://codeshack.io/images-sprite-sheet-generator/](https://codeshack.io/images-sprite-sheet-generator/)

ReasonedClub55/tictactoe-5x5.readme:
# tictactoe-5x5

A terminal game: tic-tac-toe on a 5x5 board where **four in a row** (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) wins. You play against the computer at one of four difficulty levels.

## Requirements

Python 3.12+. Standard library only: nothing to install, no network, no files written.

## Run

```
python3 -m tictactoe5
```

## How to play

- You are X, the computer is O. Columns are letters `a`-`e`, rows are numbers `1`-`5`.
- Enter a move as letter + number, for example `b3` (case does not matter).
- At the start of each game a menu asks for the difficulty (`e`asy, `m`edium, `h`ard, e`x`pert; default medium) and who goes first (`y`ou, `c`omputer, `r`andom). Press Enter to accept the default.
- The computer announces its move, and says when it blocks your threat (medium and up).
- Type `q` (or `quit`, Ctrl-C, or end of input) at any prompt to quit. A running score is shown across games, and you are asked whether to play again after each one.

## Difficulty levels

| Level | What it does |
|---|---|
| easy | Mostly random, leaning towards the centre and towards cells that extend its own lines. Takes a win if one is available, but does **not** block yours. |
| medium | Looks one move ahead with a threat-based score and picks among its top three moves. Takes wins, always blocks an immediate loss, and grabs a double threat when it sees one. |
| hard | Fixed-depth search, 4 plies (alpha-beta), choosing randomly among equally good moves. Takes wins and blocks. |
| expert | Iterative-deepening alpha-beta search with a transposition table and a time budget per move (default 1.5 s), keeping the result of the deepest search that finished. Takes wins and blocks. |

Expert is a strong search, not a solved game: it is **not** guaranteed to be unbeatable, and a slow machine means a shallower search. A draw against hard or expert is a real result.

## Tests

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## AI tournament

`scripts/tournament.py` plays the levels against each other (every pairing, alternating who moves first) and prints wins/draws/losses from the first-named level's point of view.

```
python3 scripts/tournament.py --games 4 --seed 1
```

Options: `--games` per pairing (default 6), `--budget` expert seconds per move (default 0.2), `--seed`.

Example, observed on one run with `--games 4 --budget 0.2 --seed 1` (about 12 s). With only four games per pairing this is a sanity check, not a strength measurement:

```
pairing                W   D   L
easy vs medium         0   0   4
easy vs hard           0   0   4
easy vs expert         0   0   4
medium vs hard         0   0   4
medium vs expert       0   1   3
hard vs expert         0   4   0
```

## How it was built

The idea was discussed in a Dream Team session (Eon, Joss), then planned and built with the engsys lite profile: Jody wrote the spec, Isabelle implemented, Patricia wrote the docs. The spec and plan are in `docs/specs/tictactoe-5x5.md`.

# wg: wasmga.me native games in Rust

The engine for [wasmga.me](https://wasmga.me)'s own games written in Rust:
the Rust side of the C games' `wg.h`, `wgfb.h` and `wgview.h`. A game
implements `wg::Game`, calls `wg::game!(MyGame)` once, and gets every `wg_*`
export the wasmga.me play page reads,
smooth drawing at the screen's own size, and the same Inter font as the C
games (`sdf_font.h`). The games themselves live in
[wasmga-me/games](https://github.com/wasmga-me/games), one folder each;
`wgdemo` there is a whole small game to copy.

```toml
[dependencies]
wg = { git = "https://github.com/wasmga-me/wasmgame-wg" }
```

Each game's `Cargo.lock` pins the engine commit; `cargo update -p wg` moves a
game to the latest one.

## New game

1. In the games repo, `cp -r wgdemo <id>`, rename the package in its
   `Cargo.toml` to `<id>` (the module is built as `public/games/<id>/<id>.wasm`),
   delete its `target/` (keep `Cargo.lock`, it pins the engine).
2. Write the game (below), then `sh build.sh` (or
   `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` in the folder while
   iterating; `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` once).
3. On the site: a catalog entry with `engine: "native"`, `setup`, `stats`, `pointer: true`
   if it takes clicks or touches, and `swipe: true` for swipe games. Commit
   the built `.wasm` and the game's `Cargo.lock`: Workers Builds has no Rust,
   so build.sh keeps the committed build there.

## The Game trait

- `type Save`: a `#[repr(C)]` struct of integers, floats, arrays, `wg::Rng`
  and `wg::KeyRepeat`, with `unsafe impl wg::Plain for Save {}`. It is the
  whole save (autosave, Resume, Saves, cloud), copied byte for byte, so no
  bool, enum, Vec or references; keep a version number in it. Options live
  in it too (`opt: [i32; N]`, returned by `options()`, with `CHOICES` saying
  how many each has, in catalog `setup` order).
- `new()` makes the game with default options; `start(seed)` starts a run
  with the options picked (the runtime keeps `options()` as they were).
- `update(&Input) -> u32` moves it on: `held`/`pressed` button bits
  (`wg::UP`, `A`, ...) and `dt` in ms (0 means the page only wants the
  picture). Returns `wg::EV_*`; return `EV_GAMEOVER` once when the run ends
  (the page then shows game over and posts `score()`).
- `pointer(&Pointer) -> u32`: mouse and touch in plan units, with `pressed`
  and `released` worked out (`M_LEFT`, `M_RIGHT`, `touch` set for fingers).
- `draw(&mut Screen)`: draws the whole picture. It runs only when
  `picture()` changed (by default a hash of the save; override it when the
  save holds a timer that isn't shown every millisecond, or when `draw`
  reads anything outside the save), when `moving()` is true, or after a
  resize or a load.
- `over()` is true from the moment the run is lost or won (no autosave then,
  no Resume); `stat(i)` gives the catalog `stats` in order (-1 hides one).
- Levels: a catalog `setup` option with `"levels": N` (no `choices`; they
  are made as Level 1..N) is a level picker. Give it N in `CHOICES`, start
  the run at the level picked, and return the level the run is on from
  `reached()` (0 for the first). The page keeps the furthest level reached on
  this device and shows a level select (a grid of levels, locked past the
  furthest reached, each with the player's best on it). Each level has its
  own scoreboard too: return `EV_LEVEL` from `update` when a level is
  cleared (the last one as well) and the level and the score made on it
  alone from `cleared()`.
- `loaded()` checks a save just copied in: return false to drop it, and
  rebuild anything that follows from the save (and reset animations).
- `PLAN` (or `plan(w, h)` to lay out differently on a tall phone) is the
  size in the game's own units; `Screen` scales it to fit and centres it.

Panics go to the page's error screen with the game's stack (`wg_panic`).

## Screen

All in plan units: `clear`, `rect`, `rect_grad`, `shadow`, `shadow_hollow`,
`line`, `line_grad`, `disc`, `ellipse`, `ring`, `poly`, `tri`, `text`,
`text_c`, `text_r`, `text_width`, `fit_size`; `visible()` is the area the
screen shows (wider or taller than the plan), `hair()` one pixel. Colours are
`wg::hex(0xRRGGBB)` or `wg::rgb(r, g, b)`, `wg::mix` blends two.

Keep frames under ~10 ms at 2.4 MP: draw what stays still (a board, a table)
once with `s.background(key, |s| ...)`, which redraws only when `key`
changes, and things drawn many times the same (card backs) once into a
`wg::Sprite` with `sprite_make`, then `s.sprite(&sp, x, y)`.

Also: `set_clip`/`no_clip`, `background_edit` (redraw one square of the
background inside a clip, without redrawing the board), `sprite_make_alpha`
(soft-edged sprites: drawn over black and white, blended when put), and for
games drawing their own rows (a road): `span_px`, `row_px` with `wg::blend`,
`px`, `size_px`.

Keys the pad lacks (digits, Backspace) reach `Game::key(code)` through the
optional `wg_key` export, when the page sends them.

The font's characters are those in `sdf_font.h`; add more with
`tools/sdf-font.py` (Pillow and NumPy) and copy the file to
[wasmgame-wg-c](https://github.com/wasmga-me/wasmgame-wg-c) so the C games
get them too.

## Working on the engine

`src/lib.rs` holds the events and re-exports; `game.rs` the `Game` trait and
`Plain`, `input.rs` buttons, pointer and key repeat, `rng.rs` the `Rng`,
`runtime.rs` the exports and `game!`, and `screen/` the drawing (`mod.rs`
the screen and its clip, then `shapes.rs`, `text.rs`, `background.rs`,
`sprite.rs`, `colour.rs`).

`cargo test` draws one of everything through the exports and checks the
pixels by hash, so a change that should leave the picture alone proves it;
when a change means to alter it, update the hashes the test prints. Run
`cargo fmt` before committing.

# Hollow Pines — vertical slice

Stylized frontier open-world game. Three.js (r128), plain JavaScript, no build step beyond concatenation.

**Design direction:** gameplay, combat and graphics ideas come from Red Dead Redemption 2 (systemic open world, honor and witnesses, hold-ups, gunplay, golden-hour light, weather). Sneaky Sasquatch was only early inspiration for the rounded look; everything else is our own.

## Layout
- `src/shell.html` — HUD, menus, touch controls, styles
- `src/01_core.js` — utilities, noise, input (keyboard/mouse/touch), synthesized audio
- `src/02_world.js` — terrain heightfield, water shader, colliders and line of sight, procedural wood textures, building generator
- `src/02c_grass.js` — the dense wind-blown grass field around the camera
- `src/03_rig.js` — character and quadruped rigs, animator (blending, layered actions, foot IK, squash and stretch), horse gaits
- `src/03b_gltf.js` — imported character model and `ClipAnimator` (AnimationMixer clips, crossfades, leg IK)
- `src/03c_animstate.js` — locomotion state machine (`LocoFSM`) shared by the player and NPCs
- `src/04_state.js` — items, persistent world state `S`, inventory, reputation, save/load
- `src/05b_skills.js` — skills and perks (Gunslinger, Brawler, Survivalist, Horseman), honor standing, phone vibration
- `src/05_systems.js` — interaction prompts, law and witnesses, dialogue engine, mission framework
- `src/06_entities.js` — player, horse, NPC AI (schedules, witnesses, combat, cover), wildlife
- `src/06b_brawl.js` — counters, grabs and shoves, hit reactions (limp, disarm, flinch), squad tactics (flank, suppression, rushes)
- `src/07_content.js` — sky, time and weather, world layout, containers, clues, doors
- `src/07c_interiors.js` — furnished interiors for every building
- `src/08_story.js` — cast, reactive dialogue, missions, encounters
- `src/08b_ch4.js` — Chapter 4, Night at Willow Bridge (tail, eavesdrop, confrontation)
- `src/08c_ch5.js` — Chapter 5, The Ledger (Survey Camp 3, allies, four endings)
- `src/08d_side.js` — bounty board, stranger missions, road encounters, travelers, landmarks
- `src/08f_town.js` — the living town (gunfire panic, the law's response), bounty hunters, Wren's wanted poster, road events, duels
- `src/08e_riders.js` — NPCs on horseback: posses, fleeing outlaws, mounted ambushers
- `src/09_ui.js` — HUD, panels, map, shop, camp, fishing
- `src/09b_post.js` — post-processing: ambient occlusion, bloom, colour grade, vignette, grain, anti-aliasing
- `src/10_main.js` — boot, camera (including the two-shot conversation camera), main loop, test hooks (`window.HP`)

Placeholder art lives in the factory functions (`makeHumanoid`, `makeQuad`, `building`, `World.*`), so models can be swapped without touching gameplay code.

## Build and test
```
python3 build.py                     # writes game.html (CDN three.js) and test.html (local three.min.js)
cd tests
python3 test_mechanics.py            # 50 checks: movement, skeleton and gait, camera, touch UI, climbing, gathering, store, horse, hunting, camp, fishing, law, NPCs, doors, day/night, encounters, save slots
python3 test_story.py                # 91 checks: two full playthroughs with opposite choices, plus failure and retry
python3 test_controller.py           # 54 checks: movement, frame-rate independence, animation states and crossfades, camera, collision, real touch input, retargeted clips
python3 test_pwa.py                  # 6 checks: manifest, icons, installability, offline play
python3 test_camps.py                # 15 checks: traveler camps (routine, night theft, waking sleepers, hold-ups) and outlaw hideouts (takedowns, clearing, loot, reoccupation)
python3 test_gunplay.py              # 10 checks: aim-in speed, camera keeping up with the mouse, soft lock, hit zones, misses, recoil, spread
python3 test_ch4.py                  # 34 checks: Chapter 4 start, unseen tail, eavesdropping, four endings, failure, retry and reload
python3 test_riders.py               # 17 checks: posses, riders shooting from the saddle, seated hitboxes, throwing riders, mounted runners and ambushers, weather sight/noise/lightning/mud
python3 test_gfx.py                  # 11 checks: sun arc and golden hour, dark nights, dawn mist, muzzle smoke, impacts, blood, gallop dust
python3 test_side.py                 # 27 checks: bounty board (alive, dead, runner), three stranger missions, road encounters, travelers, landmarks
python3 test_ch5.py                  # 23 checks: Chapter 5's four endings, allies fighting, silent takedown, quiet rescue, fail/retry, reload
```
Tests need Playwright with Chromium (set `PW_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome` to use a specific browser build) and `three.min.js` (r128) next to `test.html`. Each playthrough saves, reloads the page, presses Continue, and verifies the decisions survived.

## Camps
Gameplay follows Red Dead Redemption 2. `src/07b_camps.js`:
- **Traveler camps** (Teague's Camp, Holt Hunting Camp): trappers work near camp by day, sit at the fire in the evening and sleep at night. Greet them, ask about the area (they'll mark the outlaw hideout on your map), or rob them. Sneak in crouched to loot their satchel and lockbox: sleepers only notice someone standing right beside them, and walking upright past a bedroll wakes them. Anyone who sees a theft is a witness, which brings honor loss and a bounty through the normal law system. Aim at someone until their hands go up, then choose **Rob** (a witnessed robbery: honor -8, bounty). They remember you.
- **Outlaw hideout** (Rattlesnake Hollow, Crane gang): two sentries patrol and two outlaws sit at the fire facing inward. Crouched, you aren't noticed from behind, so a punch from behind is a silent takedown; otherwise it's a shootout using the cover AI. Downed outlaws stay down. When nobody's left standing the hideout is cleared and its lockbox (gold, cash, ammo) is free loot; breaking it open while the gang is still around makes them suspicious. Killing outlaws costs

Githyot/mine-clone.readme:
# Mine Clone

A Minecraft-like block game written in **Rust**, built for speed. Rendering uses **wgpu** on
Vulkan (Windows/Linux), Metal (macOS) or DirectX 12. No Java, no Mojang code, art or music:
everything here is original, and the design comes from public descriptions of the game.

> **Português:** veja [docs/COMO-JOGAR.txt](docs/COMO-JOGAR.txt) para controles e como usar suas
> músicas e pacotes de textura, e [docs/plan/RESUMO.md](docs/plan/RESUMO.md) para o plano completo.

![screenshot](docs/screenshots/demo.png)

## Download

Every push builds the game for Windows, Linux and macOS in GitHub Actions
(**Actions → build → Artifacts**). Unzip and run `mine-clone`. Pushing a tag like `v0.1.0`
publishes the same files as a GitHub Release.

## Build from source

```sh
# Linux needs: libasound2-dev libxkbcommon-dev libudev-dev
cargo run --release -p game
```

## What works (phases 0 and 1 of the [roadmap](docs/plan/roadmap.md), plus the start of phase 2)

- Infinite world with biomes (plains, forest, birch forest, taiga, snowy plains, desert, beach,
  ocean, mountains), caves, lava lakes, ores (coal, copper, tin, iron, silver, gold, redstone,
  lapis, diamond, emerald), trees, flowers, cactus, pumpkins and melons.
- Creative mode: walk, sprint, sneak (no falling off edges), fly, swim; break, place and pick
  blocks; inventory with every block; falling sand and gravel.
- Sky light and block light (torches, glowstone, lava) with smooth lighting and ambient occlusion.
- Day/night cycle with a square sun and moon, stars, sunsets and drifting blocky clouds; fog;
  underwater fog.
- Worlds save automatically (only edited chunks are stored, compressed with LZ4).
- Classic music system: rare, calm tracks with long silences, 7 original tracks, plus your own
  music folder (only yours, only the game's, or both). Procedural block sounds and footsteps.
- Resource packs, including Minecraft texture packs of any resolution, switchable in-game.
- Shader packs (Esc > Shaders): built-in "Realçado" (bloom, sun rays, colour grading,
  vignette, distance haze, waving plants, rippling water) and "Suave", plus your own WGSL
  post-processing packs in `shaderpacks/` (see the generated `LEIA-ME.txt` and
  `shaderpacks-examples/sepia`).
- Distant terrain (LOD): a low-detail heightmap from the world generator drawn 256–1024
  blocks past the render distance, built on worker threads.
- Debug screen (F3), screenshots (F2), crash log, settings file.
- Mobs from `packs/vanilla/mobs.ron`: pig, cow, sheep, chicken, zombie, skeleton, stalker (our
  own exploding mob) and spider, with box models, walk animations and skin layers that stand off
  the body as real 3D relief. Animals spawn on grass in the light, monsters in the dark.
- Survival mode (toggle in the pause menu): health, fall, lava and drowning damage, mob attacks,
  explosions, death and respawn.
- Game controllers: DualShock 4 and DualSense read directly over USB/Bluetooth HID (touchpad,
  gyro aiming, light bar, rumble), other pads through gilrs; full button remapping in-game.
- 3D clouds (ray-marched, idea from Better Clouds), bigger sun and moon.
- Paintings: 16 original pictures plus your own PNGs in `paintings/`; aim at a wall and press P.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `crates/voxel` | World core with no GPU code: block registry, paletted chunks, world generation, lighting, meshing, physics, ray casting, saves. Fully unit tested. |
| `crates/game` | The game: window, renderer and shaders, chunk streaming on worker threads, HUD and menus, audio. |
| `packs/vanilla` | The base game as a data pack: `blocks.ron`, `mobs.ron`, `paintings.ron`, 16×16 block textures, 64×128 mob skins and paintings. Mods use the same format. |
| `assets/music` | Original music (generated by `tools/compose_music.py`). |
| `tools/` | Texture and music generators. |
| `docs/plan` | Full design: inventory of Minecraft content, architecture, roadmap, mods, magic/RPG and Terraria ideas. |

## Performance notes

- Chunks are generated, lit and meshed on all CPU cores; the main thread only uploads results.
- Sections are stored with palettes (an empty section costs a few bytes).
- Faces between solid blocks are never built; vertices are packed into 12 bytes.
- Sections outside the view frustum are skipped; opaque geometry is drawn front to back.
- `cargo run --release -p voxel --example bench` times generation, lighting and meshing.

Belendali/wanaka-mobile-demo.readme:
# Wanaka Mobile · 可点击 Demo

**在线 demo**：https://belendali.github.io/wanaka-mobile-demo/ （电脑上显示手机框预览，手机上全屏）
**Figma**：[Wanaka Studio · 1015 分区](https://www.figma.com/design/PWtgAaGdl6znpuQykrnIbb/Wanaka-Studio?node-id=48522-18034)

这是用来演示交互和流程的原型，不是生产代码。视觉以 Figma 为准，两者不一致时请找设计确认。

## 流程

| Tab | 能点的 |
|---|---|
| **Home** | 上下滑刷视频（滑动时顶栏变小变淡）；点卡片出现 Play / Remix，`···` 里是 Download / Report；点 Play 或长按卡片，伴随震动和“进入世界”动效，全屏进入游戏；游戏内 `···`：Remix / 分享 / 重玩 / 下载 / Play as me |
| **Discover** | 推荐卡直接 Play；运营位进入 3D Snap；往下滑时搜索栏和 chips 吸顶；点网格里的游戏进入带返回按钮的 Feed |
| **Create（中间小猫）** | 默认 Create with AI：Inspiration 里的 prompt 点一下填入输入框、换一个、语音（模拟）；“+” → 相机 / 相册多选 / 我的资产；发送 → 生成进度 → 对话式结果，继续修改生成 v2、旧版本收起，Publish |
| **3D Snap** | 在 Create 里左右滑或点切换器进入；拍照 → 选风格（默认风格 + 社区风格）→ 生成 3D → 结果：拖动旋转、换风格、对话修改、Save 到 Assets、删除 |
| **Friends** | 好友在玩什么、动态（简版） |
| **Me** | 会员卡（免费次数）、Games / Assets / Saved / Downloads；下载、发布、保存的内容会同步出现在这里 |

## 说明

- 生成过程都是模拟的；相机画面是一张静态照片。
- 游戏视频是参考素材（各截 10 秒），自带字幕和平台水印，之后换成干净的录屏即可。
- 震动只在支持的安卓浏览器上生效。

## 文件

```
app.html     页面本体（样式 + 脚本都在里面）
build.sh     把 app.html 包成完整的 index.html
index.html   GitHub Pages 用的页面（由 build.sh 生成，不要直接改）
media/       视频、封面、3D 模型图、头像、吉祥物
```

改完 `app.html` 后运行 `./build.sh`，再提交。

machuiwen/robo-strike.readme:
# Robo Strike 机器人大作战

一个卡通风格的第一人称射击小游戏。打败一波又一波的机器人和无人机，它们被击中后会碎成火花、螺丝和零件，没有任何流血内容，适合小朋友。

**在线游玩：https://machuiwen.github.io/robo-strike/**

电脑、iPad 和手机都能玩，横屏竖屏都可以。

## 操作方法

| | 电脑 | 触屏（iPad） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 移动 | W A S D 或方向键 | 左边拖动摇杆 |
| 转视角 | 鼠标（先点一下画面） | 右边滑动 |
| 开火 | 鼠标左键 | 「开火」按钮（按住还能同时转视角） |
| 瞄准镜 | 鼠标右键 | 「瞄准」按钮 |
| 跳 / 蹲 | 空格 / C | 「跳」/「蹲」按钮 |
| 换弹 | R | 「换弹」按钮 |
| 换枪 | 数字键 1-5、鼠标滚轮、Q（上一把） | 「换枪」按钮，或点上方的武器栏 |
| 商店 | B（两波之间） | 「商店」按钮 |
| 开始下一波 | 回车 | 「开始下一波」按钮 |
| 暂停 | Esc 或 P | 左上角暂停按钮 |
| 声音开关 | M | 左上角喇叭按钮 |

## 玩法

- 一共 8 波，最后一波有首领「巨无霸机甲」。
- 打中机器人的头会造成更多伤害（爆头），还能多拿金币。
- 打败机器人可以得到金币，在两波之间的商店里买护甲、修复包、弹药、新武器和升级。
- 绿色方块是修复包，橙色箱子是弹药，蓝色六边形是护甲。
- 机器人的子弹飞得比较慢，看到亮亮的光球就躲开它！
- 「简单」难度适合小朋友：机器人更少更慢，伤害很低，有 3 次机会，生命值还会慢慢恢复，并且有瞄准辅助。
- 最高分保存在你的设备上。

## 武器

- 激光步枪：自动射击，最常用。
- 光子手枪：子弹无限。
- 泡泡炮：发射大泡泡，爆开时可以打到周围的机器人。
- 散射炮（商店购买）：近距离威力很大。
- 电磁狙击枪（商店购买）：可以开镜，一枪穿透好几个机器人。

## 技术说明

- 纯静态网页，没有构建步骤，用任何静态服务器打开 `index.html` 即可。
- 使用 CDN 上的 [three.js](https://threejs.org/) 0.160.0。
- 所有声音都用 Web Audio 实时合成，所有贴图都用代码画出来，没有音频和图片文件。
- iPad 需要较新的 Safari（16.4 或更新）。在 iPad 上如果没有声音，请检查静音开关。

cogwizzle/Alphabet-Flashcards.desc: Flash card game for kids to help learn letters and sounds.
cogwizzle/Alphabet-Flashcards.readme:
# Alphabet-Flashcards

Flash card game for kids to help learn letters and sounds. It is a Progressive Web App made for touch screens: install it on an iPad or phone and it works offline.

- **Cards**: one big card per letter. Tap the letter to hear its name; tap the picture to hear its sound and a word that starts with it. Swipe or use the arrows to change letters, or tap a letter in the strip at the bottom to jump to it.
- **Find it**: the app says a letter's name or its sound, and she taps the matching letter out of four. Each right answer earns a star; ten stars is a win.
- **ABC / abc**: switches every letter between uppercase and lowercase.

The look comes from [Modern Styles](https://github.com/cogwizzle/Modern-Styles), and letters use [Andika](https://software.sil.org/andika/), a typeface made for early readers. Every word the app says is a short recorded clip in `audio/`, so it sounds the same on every device and works offline.

## Install on an iPad

1. Open the site in **Safari** (other browsers on iPad can't install web apps).
2. Tap the **Share** button, then **Add to Home Screen**, then **Add**.
3. Open it from the home screen. It runs full screen, and after the first open it works without internet.

If there's no sound, check that the iPad's silent mode is off and the volume is up.

## Run it locally

It is a plain static site with no build step. Serve the folder with any static server, for example:

```sh
npx http-server -c-1 .
```

## Publish

`.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys the repository to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`. One-time setup: in the repository settings, under Pages, set the source to **GitHub Actions**. The site is then at <https://cogwizzle.github.io/Alphabet-Flashcards/>.

## Changing things

- Letters and picture words are in `letters.js`. Each letter's clips are `audio/<letter>-name.mp3`, `-sound.mp3` and `-word.mp3`; the phrases ("Let's play!", "Find", "Yes!" and so on) are next to them.
- When you change any file, bump `VERSION` in `sw.js`, or installed copies keep the old version.
- Icons are drawn in `icons/icon.svg`; the PNGs next to it are renders of it.

## Credits

The voice clips were made with [Piper](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) (MIT license), using its `en_US-libritts-high` voice model. That model is trained on the [LibriTTS](https://www.openslr.org/60/) corpus, which is licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Each letter sound was cut out of a longer word and trimmed, so it is a clean sound on its own.

wpknox/ti4-table.desc: Phone-first Twilight Imperium 4 companion: rules search, map fairness checks, and a group game log
wpknox/ti4-table.readme:
# TI4 Table

A phone-friendly companion site for a group that plays *Twilight Imperium 4*.

## What's in it

| Section | Status |
|---|---|
| **Rules** | Built |
| **Map** | Built |
| **Games** | Built, not deployed yet |
| **Ask** | Planned |

- **Rules:** search the Living Rules Reference, with Dane's official rulings highlighted.
  - Type a rule number (`58.3`), a term (`sustain damage`), shorthand (`AFB`), or a whole question (`can I retreat into an empty system`).
  - Tap any paragraph number to copy or share a link straight to it.
  - Install it to your home screen and it works offline.
- **Map:** paste a map string and get a plain-English fairness report for each seat. It covers resources, influence, tech skips, distance to Mecatol, and shared or contested systems. Each report has a hex map with that seat's slice outlined, and you can switch to the real tile art.
- **Games:** the group's shared game log and stats.
  - **Sign-in:** friends sign in with invite codes from an admin. There are no public accounts.
  - **Logging:** after a game, log the seats, factions, points and winner, plus an optional map string and TI Assistant link. Games with a map show it on their page, labelled with each player and faction.
  - **Planned games:** set a game up ahead of time from the Map page by picking a player and, optionally, a faction for each seat. Enter the results after the game.
  - **Stats:** wins, factions played, head-to-head and seat effects. Planned games don't count until they're finished.
- **Ask** *(planned)*: plain-English rules questions answered with links to the exact paragraph.

## Running locally

Rules and Map are static, so they need no install and no build step:

```bash
node scripts/serve.mjs        # http://localhost:8787
```

Games needs the API (Cloudflare Pages Functions and a D1 database), so run it through wrangler:

```bash
npm install
npm run db:migrate:local      # create the local database
npm run db:seed:local         # optional: fake games for trying stats
node scripts/invite.mjs --local "Your name" admin   # prints a sign-in code
npm run dev                   # http://localhost:8788, then sign in at /games/join
```

## Checks

There are no unit tests yet. These scripts check the parts that are easy to get wrong:

```bash
node scripts/check-map.mjs        # map string parsing against real maps
node scripts/check-analysis.mjs   # seat analysis against hand-checked fixtures
node scripts/check-map-svg.mjs    # map drawing
node scripts/check-stats.mjs      # stats against a hand count of the seed data
npm run check:api                 # the games API, including security checks
```

## Deploying

The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, with Pages Functions and D1. It isn't deployed yet. The first deploy is:

```bash
npx wrangler pages project create ti4-table --production-branch main
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply ti4-table --remote
npx wrangler pages deploy
node scripts/invite.mjs --remote "Your name" admin
```

After that, sign in at `/games/join` with the printed code. Invite friends from the Admin page in Games. Most friends should be **editors**: editors log games and edit the ones they created or played in. Give one other person **admin** as a backup.

## Updating the rules

Rules come from a local clone of [tirules-search](https://github.com/wpknox/tirules-search):

```bash
node scripts/build-rules.mjs path/to/tirules-search   # or set TIRULES_DIR
```

## Credits and licence

Full credits are in [`CREDITS.md`](CREDITS.md). In short:

- **Rules text:** [tirules-search](https://github.com/wpknox/tirules-search), a fork of [dangothemango/tirules](https://github.com/dangothemango/tirules) by dangothemango and BradleyΣ, with Dane's rulings. It's GPL-3.0, so this project is GPL-3.0 too (see `LICENSE`).
- **Map tile data:** converted from the [TI4 Tabletop Playground mod](https://github.com/darrellanderson/TI4-TTPG-TS) and cross-checked against [AsyncTI4](https://github.com/AsyncTI4/TI4_map_generator_bot). Both are under the Unlicense, which covers their code and data but not their art. Details are in `docs/research/tile-data.md`.
- **Faction symbols and tile images:** artwork © Fantasy Flight Games, used under the Asmodee fan content policy for a free, non-commercial fan site. The art will be removed promptly if its owner asks.
- **Space backdrop:** the Hubble eXtreme Deep Field (NASA, ESA, and the HUDF09 Team), CC BY 4.0.
- **Fonts:** [Saira](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Saira) and [Atkinson Hyperlegible Next](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Atkinson+Hyperlegible+Next), both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

*Twilight Imperium* is © Fantasy Flight Games. This is an unofficial fan site and isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Fantasy Flight Games or Asmodee.

# TUX 64 — The Kernel Castle Adventure


KERNEL CASTLE GROUNDS — お城の庭
KERNEL CASTLE — サイバー空間のお城の中

AURORA SEA RALLY — ダッシュブーツで氷海ラリー
FROSTCLOUD SKYWAY — 雲海の上をロケットで飛行

STARDUST ORBIT — 宇宙を高速ロケットで駆けるリングラン
SEGFAULT'S LAIR — 最終ボスのステージ
Linux のマスコット **Tux** が主人公の 3D アクションゲームです。 「スーパーマリオ64」のゲームシステム（3Dアクション・スター収集・お城のハブ・ワープ・ボス戦など）を、 キャラクターと世界観を Linux / カーネル風に置き換えて **すべてオリジナル** で実装しています。 世界全体が **雪と氷** のモチーフで統一されています（雪原・凍った池・氷山の浮かぶ極海・吹雪の砦・氷のピラミッド・凍てつく虚空のラストステージなど）。 * 言語: C (C99 / gnu99) * 描画: OpenGL 1.1（固定機能パイプライン） * 外部ライブラリ: **不要**（テクスチャ・モデル・効果音・BGM はすべてプログラムで生成） * 対応 OS: Linux (X11 + GLX + ALSA) / Windows (Win32 + WGL + waveOut, MinGW でビルド) --- ## ビルド方法 ### Linux 必要なもの: `gcc`, `make`, X11 / OpenGL の開発ヘッダ（例: Debian/Ubuntu なら `libx11-dev libgl1-mesa-dev`） ```sh make # ./tux64 が生成されます ./tux64 ``` サウンドは実行時に `libasound.so.2`（ALSA）を動的に読み込みます。無い環境でも無音で動作します。 ### Windows（MinGW） **Linux からクロスコンパイル**（`x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` が必要）: ```sh make windows # ./tux64.exe が生成されます ``` **Windows 上の MinGW-w64 / MSYS2 でネイティブビルド**: ```bat mingw32-make (Makefile が Windows_NT を自動判別します) または build.bat ``` 生成される `tux64.exe` は単体で動作します（opengl32 / gdi32 / winmm / user32 のみ使用、 XInput は存在すれば実行時に読み込み）。 ### 配布パッケージ ```sh make package # または tools/package.sh 1.2.3（バージョン指定、既定は 1.0.0） ``` `dist/` に次の 3 つが作られます（`7z`, `dpkg-deb`, `rpmbuild`, MinGW が必要。Ubuntu なら `sudo apt install p7zip-full rpm`）。 | ファイル | 内容 | |---|---| | `tux64-VERSION-windows-x64.7z` | `tux64.exe` と README。展開した場所でそのまま実行 | | `tux64_VERSION_amd64.deb` | Debian / Ubuntu 用（`/usr/games/tux64`、メニュー登録・アイコン付き） | | `tux64-VERSION-1.x86_64.rpm` | Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE 用（`/usr/bin/tux64`、メニュー登録・アイコン付き） | Linux パッケージは glibc 2.34 以降（Debian 12、Ubuntu 22.04、RHEL 9 以降）で動作します。 依存は OpenGL / X11 のみで、ALSA（libasound2 / alsa-lib）は推奨扱いです。 --- ## 操作方法 | 操作 | キーボード | ゲームパッド (XInput / Linux joystick) | |---|---|---| | 移動 | WASD / 矢印キー | 左スティック | | ジャンプ (A) | Space / K | A | | アクション (B): パンチ・ダイブ・つかむ・話す・投げる | J / X / 左Shift | B / X | | しゃがみ・ヒップドロップ (Z) | Z / L / C / 左Ctrl | LT / RT / LB | | カメラ回転 | Q / E | 右スティック / 十字キー左右 | | カメラ距離 | R / F (PageUp / PageDown) | 右スティック上下 / Y | | カメラを背後へ | Tab / V | RB | | ポーズ・決定 | Enter / Esc | START | | フルスクリーン切替 | F11 / Alt+Enter | | | BGM ON/OFF | M | | | スクリーンショット | F12（`screenshot_000.bmp`…） | | ### Tux のアクション（マリオ64相当） * 歩き/走り（スティックの倒し具合・慣性・急ブレーキ「スキッド」） * ジャンプ → 着地直後に **2段ジャンプ** → さらに **3段ジャンプ**（宙返り） * **バック宙**（しゃがみ + A）、**側宙**（走りながら逆方向 + A） * **幅跳び**（走り + Z + A）、**壁キック**（壁に当たった瞬間に A） * **ダイブ**（走りながら B）→ **腹ばいスライディング**（ペンギンらしく！）→ A で起き上がりジャンプ * パンチ → パンチ → キックの **3連コンボ**、空中キック * **ヒップドロップ**（空中で Z）— 落下ダメージを無効化できます * **しゃがみ歩き**、**崖つかまり**（壁際の段差を落下中につかむ → A/前で登る） * **ポール/木登り**（空中で触れる → 上下で登り降り、A でジャンプ） * **水泳**（A: 浮上 / Z: 潜る / B: ペンギン魚雷ダッシュ、水中では体力=息が減る） * **持ち上げ・投げ**（B でつかむ → B で投げる / Z で置く） * **トランポリン**: マットに触れる直前に A を押すと、うまく押せるたびに高く跳ねる（3段階。マットへのヒップドロップは一気に2段階） * **ロケットパック**（ロケットの木箱を壊して取得）: 空中で A で点火、**A を押し続ける間だけ噴射**して飛行 （スティック前で機首下げ・後ろで上昇。噴射をやめると放物線を描いて落ち、また空中で A を押せば再点火） * 坂・氷・すべり台での自動スライディング、極寒の水での凍えジャンプ、落下ダメージ、パウダースノー（沈む雪） * 吹雪の突風（壁の陰に隠れるか、しゃがんで踏ん張ると耐えられる）、温泉（浸かると回復） 体力は 8 セルの **バッテリーゲージ**。魚コイン（Fish）や充電スタンドで回復します。50 匹ごとに 1UP。 --- ## 言語（日本語 / English） タイトル画面で **← / →（A / D キー、スティック左右）** を押すと、表示言語を日本語と英語で切り替えられます。 選んだ言語は `tux64.cfg` に保存されます。初回起動時は OS の言語設定（Linux は `LANG` などの環境変数、 Windows は UI 言語）が日本語なら日本語、それ以外なら英語で始まります。 * 翻訳は `tools/translations_ja.py`（英語原文 → 日本語）にまとめてあります。 * 日本語の文字は実行時にフォントを読み込まず、使用している文字だけをビットマップ化して `src/font_ja.h` に埋め込んでいます。 * 翻訳を編集したら `python3 tools/gen_lang.py` を実行すると `src/lang_ja.c` と `src/font_ja.h` が再生成されます （Python 3 + Pillow と Noto Sans CJK JP フォントが必要。ゲームのビルド自体には不要です）。 --- ## ゲームの流れ 城の庭 → カーネル城の内部（**サイバー空間**）→ 壁に開いた **アプリウィンドウ** に飛び込むとコースへ。 城の中はネオングリッドの床とデータの雨が降るサイバー空間で、各ウィンドウの上にはコース名と取得スター数が表示されます。 スターを取るとお城に戻ります（ハブの隠しスターを除く）。 スター数が足りないと **スタードア** は開きません。 | コース | 入口 | 必要スター | スター | |---|---|---|---| | PENGUIN PEAK | ロビー西のウィンドウ | 0 | 6 | | BITSTREAM BAY | ロビー東のドア奥 | 1 | 6 | | BLIZZARD FORTRESS（吹雪の砦） | 2階 北のドア奥 | 4 | 6 | | ZOMBIE PROCESS MANOR | 2階 東のドア奥 | 6 | 5 | | DAEMON DRIFTS（雪の吹きだまり） | 入口横のウィンドウ | 8 | 5 | | ICICLE SPIRE（つららの塔） | 1階 入口そば 西の壁のウィンドウ | 5 | 4 | | WHITEOUT LABYRINTH（ホワイトアウトの迷宮） | 1階 入口そば 東の壁のウィンドウ | 7 | 3 | | AURORA SEA RALLY（オーロラ海ラリー） | 1階 南の壁 入口の西側のウィンドウ | 10 | 5 | | FROSTCLOUD SKYWAY（フロストクラウド スカイウェイ） | 2階 バルコニー 北の壁のウィンドウ | 12 | 4 | | STARDUST ORBIT（スターダスト オービット） | 2階 バルコニー 北の壁 西側のウィンドウ | 14 | 6 | | SECRET ICE SLIDE | 2階 西端の隠し穴 | 0 | 2 | | CASTLE SECRETS | 城の庭 / ロビー | – | 2 | | SEGFAULT'S LAIR（最終） | 1階 バルコニー下のドア | 16 | グランドスター | 全 54 スター。最終ステージでラスボス **Segfault**（壊れたメモリブロックの巨人。直接攻撃は効かない）を倒すとエンディング。 アリーナのトゲ機雷の後ろに立って突進を誘い、直前で横に避けて機雷に激突させる（3回）。 ### スター一覧 * **PENGUIN PEAK**: King Daemon of the Peak（ボス: キングが fork() してくる爆弾を拾って投げ返す×3）/ Race the Quick Gnu（山頂までレース）/ Red Fish on the Floating Isle（トランポリン3段バウンスで浮島へ）/ Crusher Bridge Crossing（油圧プレスの橋）/ Behind the Watchdog's Gate（飛びかかってくる番犬ロボを、息切れしている隙に3回キックして「watchdog をリセット」）/ 100 Fish * **BITSTREAM BAY**（流氷と氷山の極海）: Treasure of the Sunken Ship / Red Fish of the Reef / Climb the Lighthouse / The Clam's Secret / Swim Through the Rings / 100 Fish * **BLIZZARD FORTRESS**（濃霧と横殴りの雪、周期的な突風）: Top of the Fortress（エレベーター）/ The Orphaned Child Process（みなしごの子プロセスを親の init まで運ぶ）/ Red Fish on the Sliding Platforms / Push t

bunditks/hangman-nodejs.readme:
# Hangman

A Hangman word game for the browser, built with Node.js and Express.

The server picks the secret word and checks every guess, so the answer never
reaches the browser until the game is over: no peeking in DevTools.

## Features

- **4 categories:** Animals, Countries, Fruits and Sports (or Random). The category is shown as a hint.
- **3 difficulty levels**

  | Difficulty | Word length | Wrong guesses allowed |
  |------------|-------------|-----------------------|
  | Easy       | 3–5 letters | 8                     |
  | Medium     | 6–8 letters | 6                     |
  | Hard       | 9+ letters  | 5                     |

- **Score tracking:** wins, losses, current streak and best streak
- **Keyboard support:** click the on-screen letters or type on your keyboard; press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to play again
- Works on phones, and supports light and dark mode

## Requirements

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 18 or newer (developed on Node 22)

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

Then open <http://localhost:3000>.

To restart the server automatically when you edit server code:

```bash
npm run dev
```

To use a different port:

```bash
PORT=8080 npm start
```

## Running the tests

```bash
npm test
```

The tests use Node's built-in test runner and cover the game rules and word lists.

## Project structure

```
server.js          Express app: serves the page and the game API
src/
  game.js          Game rules: create a game, apply a guess, hide the word
  words.js         Word lists per category
  store.js         In-memory storage for games and player scores
public/
  index.html       Page layout and the hangman drawing (SVG)
  style.css        Styles, including dark mode and phone layout
  app.js           Browser code: talks to the API and draws the game
test/
  game.test.js     Unit tests
```

## API

| Method | Path                     | Body                                   | Returns                          |
|--------|--------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| GET    | `/api/options`           |                                        | Categories and difficulties      |
| POST   | `/api/games`             | `{ category, difficulty, playerId? }`  | `{ playerId, game, stats }`      |
| POST   | `/api/games/:id/guesses` | `{ letter }`                           | `{ result, game, stats }`        |

`game.pattern` lists the word's letters, with `null` for each one not guessed yet.
`game.word` is only included once the game is won or lost. `result` is
`"correct"`, `"wrong"` or `"repeat"`.

## Game rules

- Guessing a letter you've already tried is free.
- Starting a new game after making a guess counts as a loss, so you can't
  protect your streak by quitting a game you're about to lose.
- Scores are kept in server memory, so they reset when the server restarts.

commits.msg:
Add Hangman web game with Node.js and Express

Single-player Hangman where the server holds the secret word and checks
guesses through a small JSON API, so the answer never reaches the browser
until the game ends.

- Categories (Animals, Countries, Fruits, Sports, Random)
- Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty controlling word length and lives
- Win/loss/streak tracking per player, kept in server memory
- On-screen and physical keyboard input with queued guesses
- Responsive layout with light and dark mo

tylerq05-maker/ridgeline-jets.readme:
# Jet City

Open-world jet flight in the browser: a real-scale Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), 22 landmarks to discover,
dogfights, missions, challenges, replays and photo mode, plus online multiplayer for up to 4 pilots.

**Play:** open the site and pick a mode. Nothing to install.

## Playing with friends

1. Click **MULTIPLAYER → HOST GAME**. You get a lobby code like `BLADE-57`.
2. Click **Copy invite link** and send it to your friends (or just tell them the code).
3. Friends open the link (or click MULTIPLAYER, type the code and press **Join**).
4. When everyone is in, the host picks the mode and presses **START**.

No accounts are needed. The host's browser runs the lobby, so the match ends if the host leaves.
Matchmaking uses the free public [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com) server; games then connect browser to
browser. Some school, work or public Wi-Fi networks block this; a home network or phone hotspot usually works.
If codes won't connect, **Direct connect** on the multiplayer screen is a backup that swaps codes by hand.

Built with three.js (r128). PeerJS is MIT-licensed (see `vendor/PEERJS-LICENSE.txt`).

darkharasho/hml.readme:
# hml

HML (Haro's Mod Loader) is a desktop mod manager modeled closely on r2modman, built as an Electron app with a modern Tailwind UI. Users can search for and subscribe to mods from Thunderstore or Nexus Mods, with per-game profiles. Its defining feature is GitHub integration: paste a repo URL and HML pulls the latest release zip, installs and configures it, and keeps it updated automatically.

## Development

```
npm install
npm run dev     # launch the app with hot reload
npm test        # run unit tests (vitest, 2 workers)
npm run build   # typecheck and build
```

PhamVanDat98/gamekit.readme:
# GameKit

Plugin skill + script cho dây chuyền **port game từ engine bất kỳ sang web game JS/TS, reskin và phát hành lên portal**. Dùng được trên Claude Code (plugin) và Codex (skill + AGENTS.md).

Bản này là **dự án con 1 — khung plugin**: trạng thái `game.yaml`, pipeline 6 pha có cổng, template game, interface platform + `dev-mock`, script validate / provenance / pack / release-check, dựng song song bằng worktree (fanout / integrate / check-ownership), tích hợp IDE.

**Game của ai.** Mặc định GameKit coi game là **của bạn** (`source.ownership: own`): giữ nguyên hình, âm thanh, tên; asset gốc gắn nhãn `own` và được phát hành; P3 là chuyển sang web (điều khiển, bố cục, nén asset). Làm lại game của người khác thì `init … --third-party`: asset gốc chỉ là tư liệu, bắt buộc reskin, chặn tên gốc. Mục cổng chỉ áp cho một loại game ghi `{only: own}` / `{only: third-party}`.

## Cài

Người dùng thử: xem [DUNG-THU.md](DUNG-THU.md).

Cần Node ≥ 20 và git.

```bash
cd gamekit && npm install
```

**Claude Code**
```
/plugin marketplace add /đường/dẫn/tới/gamekit
/plugin install gamekit@gamekit-dev
```
Sau khi cài: hook SessionStart nạp `using-gamekit`; có `/gamekit:status` và `/gamekit:next`.

**Codex**: game tạo từ template có sẵn `AGENTS.md`. Chép hoặc symlink `skills/` vào thư mục skill của Codex nếu muốn Codex tự nạp skill.

**Dòng lệnh** (tuỳ chọn): `npm link` trong thư mục plugin để có lệnh `gamekit` toàn cục.

## Dùng nhanh

```bash
node scripts/gamekit.mjs init my-game --title "Tên Mới" --engine unity --dir ~/games
cd ~/games/my-game
npm run dev                 # chơi thử với dev-mock (?ad=fail|skip|none|slow)
npm run gk -- status        # pha hiện tại, việc còn mở, skill tiếp theo
npm test                    # parity + replay + platform
npm run gk -- parity        # mọi nghĩa vụ trong spec/obligations.yaml đã có test xanh?
npm run gk -- gate          # kiểm tra cổng; --advance để sang pha sau
npm run gk -- pack --all --zip
npm run gk -- release-check
```

Trong VS Code: Ctrl+Shift+B = pack, task "GameKit: …" cho các lệnh khác, debug Chrome với dev-mock có sẵn trong `.vscode/`.

## Lệnh

| Lệnh | Việc |
| --- | --- |
| `init <tên>` | Tạo game từ `templates/game`, git init, cài hook, cài dependency. Hỏi thông tin (TTY) hoặc `--set k=v`; `--questions --json` in câu hỏi cho agent; `--third-party` khi làm lại game người khác |
| `config [--portal p] [--set k=v]` | Điền thông tin portal còn thiếu hoặc thêm portal (chép checklist vào `gates/P4.md`) |
| `status` / `next` | Pha, thời gian ở pha (cảnh báo vượt dự kiến), việc còn mở, skill tiếp theo |
| `gate [--advance]` | Chấm `gates/<pha>.md`: mục `{auto: …}` chạy script, mục `(bạn)` chỉ người dùng tick |
| `validate [--stage Px]` | Schema `game.yaml`, `params/*.json` (mọi giá trị có `source`; `confidence` = observed/derived/inferred, inferred cần `tolerance` từ P2), `spec/obligations.yaml`, `spec/oracles/*.json`, provenance, `module-plan.yaml`, `asset-manifest.json` |
| `parity [--report file.json]` | Chạy vitest, đóng từng nghĩa vụ trong `spec/obligations.yaml` bằng test gắn thẻ `[id:case]`. Test đỏ, skip/todo, thiếu case hay thẻ lạ đều tính là chưa đạt |
| `provenance add <file…> --label …` | Nhãn `reference / generated / own / licensed / placeholder` |
| `pack [--portal] [--all] [--version V] [--compress] [--zip]` | `builds/<YYMMDDNN>/<portal>/{index.html, preview.html, version.txt, <v>/…}` + `builds/<v>/manifest.json` (+ zip) |
| `release-check [--version V] [--portal p]` | Mặc định bản mới nhất. Kiểm bố cục az-v1, footer bản quyền, chặn asset reference/placeholder, tên game gốc, link ngoài, đường dẫn tuyệt đối, vượt ngân sách tải |
| `fanout --wave N` | Mỗi module một worktree `../<game>.worktrees/<id>` trên nhánh `mod/<id>` + `BRIEF.md` |
| `check-ownership` | Module chỉ sửa trong thư mục được giao, không đụng vùng shared |
| `integrate --wave N [--cleanup]` | Merge theo phụ thuộc, test sau mỗi merge, đỏ thì hoàn tác |
| `precommit` | Git hook: chặn `reference/`, `decompiled/`, code decompile, asset chưa nhãn |

## Cấu trúc plugin

```
.claude-plugin/   plugin.json, marketplace.json
hooks/            SessionStart → using-gamekit + gamekit status
commands/         /gamekit:status, /gamekit:next
skills/           using-gamekit, rebuild-game, module-plan, integrate, platform-sdk, package-web-build, release-check
portals/          vỏ portal dùng chung: azgames, dev-mock (portal.yaml, kit.mjs, shell.html, loader.entry.js, Icons/), shared/
scripts/          CLI gamekit.mjs + lệnh; lib/
schemas/          game, params, provenance, module-plan, asset-manifest (JSON Schema)
templates/game/   Vite + TS: core/ (deterministic), view/, platform/ (interface, PauseBus, dev-mock), contracts/, tests, gates, .vscode, AGENTS.md

- `src/core/` logic thuần: `Rng` có seed, fixed timestep, input ghi/phát lại. ESLint chặn DOM, `Math.random`, `Date.now`, thư viện render và số lạ.
- `src/platform/`: `Platform` (game gọi) và `PortalAdapter` (mỗi portal một file mỏng). `createPlatform()` lo pause + tắt tiếng khi ad, gameplay start/stop cân bằng, không chồng ad, lọc tên event, save fallback. Build chỉ bundle adapter của portal đang đóng gói (`virtual:gk-adapter`).
- Game demo (né vật rơi) để pipeline chạy được từ đầu đến cuối; thay bằng game thật ở P2.

## Nâng cấp game cũ

Game tạo từ template trước bố cục az-v1 build ra `index.html` + `Build/` (hoặc `dist/`); `pack` bây giờ dừng với lỗi "vite.config.ts của game là bản cũ". Chép từ `templates/game/` của GameKit sang game (giữ phần code gameplay của bạn trong `src/core/`, `src/view/` nếu đã sửa — so sánh rồi gộp):

1. `vite.config.ts` (ra `framework.js`, `css/style.css`, `assets/{img,art,audio,fonts}/`).
2. `package.json`: thêm `esbuild`, `javascript-obfuscator` vào `devDependencies`; script `"preview": "vite preview --outDir builds"`. Rồi `npm install`.
3. `src/main.ts`.
4. `src/platform/`: `index.ts`, `types.ts`, `create-platform.ts`, `gm-globals.d.ts`, `dev-loader.t

t3rrey/friendslopped.readme:
# FRIENDSLOPPED

A monorepo of N64-flavoured party games. You join with a name, pick a game cartridge, then host or join a lobby.

```
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # web on http://localhost:5173, server on :3001
pnpm bots         # bots host their own lobby and play a full game
pnpm bots ABCD 5  # 5 bots join lobby ABCD (any game) so you can test alone
GAME=tunedin MODE=teams pnpm bots   # bots play a full game of another game/mode
pnpm test         # rules engine tests
pnpm build && pnpm start   # production: one server on :3001 serves the client too
```

Each browser tab is its own player (the session lives in `sessionStorage`), so you can test with several tabs. Refreshing the page puts you back in your lobby.

## Layout

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/shared` | Lobby protocol shared by every game (messages, lobby state) |
| `packages/mafia` | Mafia rules engine: pure, deterministic and unit-tested |
| `packages/tunedin` | Tuned In (a Wavelength-style game) rules engine and spectrum deck |
| `apps/server` | WebSocket server: sessions, lobbies, host controls, game registry (`src/games`) |
| `apps/web` | React client with a low-poly Three.js village rendered at low resolution |

### Adding a game
1. Write the rules as a package (see `packages/mafia`).
2. Register a `GameDefinition` in `apps/server/src/games/index.ts`.
3. Register the client UI (`Settings`, `Rules`, `Game`) in `apps/web/src/games.tsx`.

Lobbies, hosting, invite codes, reconnects and the lobby browser then work for the new game as well.

## Mafia rules (the same every game)
The host sets the number of **killers**, **detectives** and **healers**. Everyone else is a villager. Modes only change phase length (Classic, Speed, Marathon).

- **Night:** Killers choose a victim. The most votes wins, and a tie goes to the earliest-seated killer's pick. Each healer protects one player, and can't protect the same player two nights in a row. Each detective privately learns whether one player is a killer.
- **Dawn:** The victim is revealed with their role, unless a healer protected them.
- **Day:** Players discuss. Voting opens when the timer ends, when everyone alive is ready, or when the host skips ahead.
- **Vote:** Voting is public. A player is eliminated only with strictly more votes than every other player *and* than skip.
- **Win:** The town wins when no killers remain. The killers win once they equal or outnumber the town.
- Dead players become ghosts. They see every role and get their own chat. A player who leaves mid-game dies with their role revealed.

## Tuned In rules
Each round shows a card with two opposites, like *Cold ↔ Hot*. A target is hidden somewhere on the dial between them. Only the **psychic** can see it. They give one clue, like "Lukewarm tea", and can swap the card once per round.

- **Party** (3+ players): everyone else drags their own needle in secret. A bullseye scores 4, close scores 3 and nearby scores 2. The psychic earns the rounded average, so good clues pay off. Everyone is psychic once (or up to 3 times). The highest score wins.
- **Teams** (4+ players): teams are dealt randomly. The psychic's team shares one needle, and anyone on the team can move it. The other team then calls whether the target is left or right of the needle, and a correct call steals 1 point (no steal after a bullseye). Teams take turns. The first team to reach the target score (default 10) at the end of a round wins, and ties play on.

SulphurS16/ACFA-Port.readme: # ARMORED CORE for Answer: unofficial PC port A native Windows version of ARMORED CORE for Answer (PS3, USA, BLUS30187). The game's own PS3 code is translated into a real Windows program, built on your PC from your own copy of the game. This project contains no game data, no game code and no keys, and it decrypts nothing. Not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by FromSoftware, Ubisoft, Sony Interactive Entertainment or any other rights holder. ARMORED CORE is a trademark of its owners. ## Highlights - Native, not emulated. The whole game runs as a 64-bit Windows program. - Resolution options. The game draws at your screen's own resolution, in borderless, windowed or fullscreen. - Render scale from 50% to 200%. - High frame rates. 30, 60, 120, 144, your monitor's refresh rate or uncapped and the same game speed at every frame rate. Menus and movies stay at 60. - Full mouse support. The mouse moves the camera with raw input. Your AC turns after it at its own speed, as with the stick. - PC SETTINGS inside the game. An entry in the game's own SYSTEM menu, where HDD INSTALL was on the PS3: display, frame rate, mouse and keys settings all ingame. ## How it works Static recompilation. A recompiler reads the game's ~4.5 million PowerPC instructions and turns them into C++: about 71.000 functions, with every indirect jump resolved. Your PC's compiler then builds a native 64-bit Windows program. SPU programs are translated ahead of time too, with an interpreter as a safety net. The RSX command stream becomes Direct3D 11, and the game's shaders become HLSL, drawn at your resolution. Graphics, audio, input, files and saves are reimplemented in C++. a few complex firmware parts run as recompiled code from your own system files, so they behave exactly as on the console: the SPU task system and the movie and audio decoders. It shares this runtime with the Armored Core 4 port. The two games share an engine family and middleware. Nothing from the game is in this repository. Everything game-derived is generated on your PC from your own copy. Setup downloads a compiler toolchain (about 250 MB) once and takes a few minutes. ## Install ### What you need - Your own copy of ARMORED CORE for Answer (US disc, BLUS30187). You need the disc's files, meaning the folder that contains 'PS3_GAME'. - RPCS3, used once during setup to decrypt a few of your game files. - The PS3 system software 4.93 file 'PS3UPDAT.PUP' from [Sony's PS3 system software page](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps3/system-software/). - Optional: the game's update 01.35 package, placed in the game folder or next to 'PS3UPDAT.PUP'. - About 4 GB of free disk space and an internet connection. ### Steps 1. Download `ACFA-Port-.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/SulphurS16/ACFA-Port/releases/latest). 2. Right click the zip, choose **Extract All...**, and pick a folder with enough space, for example 'C:\Games\ACFA-Port'. 3. Open that folder and start 'ACFA-Launcher.exe'. 4. Under **Game folder**, choose the folder that contains 'PS3_GAME'. 5. Click **Prepare files** and choose your 'rpcs3.exe' and 'PS3UPDAT.PUP'. The launcher uses your RPCS3 to decrypt the files the port needs. When RPCS3 asks "Install firmware?", click **Yes**; if you have the update, click **Install** when it asks about the package. This takes about a minute and doesn't change your RPCS3. 6. Click **Set up**. It downloads the build tools and builds the game. This takes a few minutes and is only needed once. 7. Choose whether you want a desktop shortcut and a Start menu entry. 8. Click **PLAY**. From now on, you can start the game from the shortcut. > [!NOTE] > Already decrypted the files yourself? Skip step 5 and choose their folder under **Decrypted files** instead. **More... > Which files does the port need?** lists them. ## Update Unzip the new release into a new folder or over the old one, start its launcher and click **Set up**. It finds your earlier install and rebuilds only what changed; your settings and saves stay. If your game data is in the old release's folder, keep that folder, or choose **Move it beside this launcher**. ## Uninstall **More... > Remove game data...**, then delete the launcher's folder. Saves and settings stay unless you tick their box; they then go to a backup folder. ## Controls Controllers work like the PS3 pad and can be connected at any time: - **PlayStation** (DUALSHOCK 4, DualSense, DualSense Edge; USB or Bluetooth): Options = START; Share / Create or the touchpad click = SELECT. No extra program needed. No vibration yet. - **Xbox and other XInput controllers:** A = Cross, B = Circle, X = Square, Y = Triangle, LB / RB = L1 / R1, LT / RT = L2 / R2, Menu = START, View = SELECT, stick clicks = L3 / R3. With several controllers connected, the first one plays (Xbox-style controllers first). # Mouse and keyboard support Keyboard and mouse in missions (defaults, for the game's SIMPLE control layout): | Action | Keys | | --- | --- | | Move | W A S D | | Camera | Mouse | | Left / right arm weapon | Left / right click | | Shoulder weapon | E | | Switch right / left weapon | C / Ctrl | | Boost (hold to rise) / quick boost / overed boost | Space / Shift / Q | | Reset view | V | | L3 | Middle click | | Pause | Tab or Escape | | SELECT / D-pad | Enter / arrow keys | | Release the mouse | F1 | | Fullscreen | F11 or Alt+Enter | The mouse moves the camera directly (raw input), and the AC turns after it at its own speed. In menus: - **Mouse:** point and click; right-click goes back; the wheel scrolls; drag sliders. - **Keys:** arrows or W A S D move, Enter or Space choose, Escape or Backspace go back. - **PS3 buttons:
