SkerbMcDuck/skyrim-companion.readme:
# Skyrim Companion

A live map and character readout for Skyrim Special Edition that runs in a browser window, so you can keep it on a second monitor while you play.

## What it shows

A second-monitor HUD, MMO style:

- **World map**, always open: your position and facing, discovered map markers with their in-game icons, and a trail of where you've walked. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, "Follow" to lock on.
- **Mini map** that rotates with you. Outdoors it shows the map around you; indoors it traces your path.
- **Compass**, location, and in-game time and date.
- **Vitals**: health, magicka, stamina, plus combat, sneak, and mounted status.
- **Active effects**: every effect on you with its icon, strength, time left, description, and source (potion, spell, enchanted item, or who cast it).
- **Survival** (Survival Mode): live hunger, cold, and fatigue meters with stage names.
- **Equipment**: both hands, ammo count, shout/power, every worn piece with armor values and enchantments, total armor rating, resistances, and carry weight.
- **Consumables**: potions grouped by what they do (Restore Health, Magicka, Stamina, cures, resistances, and so on), food, and poisons, with counts.

Undiscovered places stay hidden unless you turn on "Undiscovered".

## Game visuals (assets pack)

The map picture, icons, and font come from your own game install (your map mod, CoMAP, SkyUI, and your UI font). They are packaged separately as "Skyrim Companion - Assets" and are not part of this repository. Install that pack in Vortex alongside the plugin. Without it the window still works, with plain shapes instead of icons.

## Requirements

- Skyrim Special Edition on Steam, launched through SKSE64
- Address Library for SKSE Plugins (Gate to Sovngarde already includes it)

## Install with Vortex

1. Download the latest build (see "Getting a build" below). It's a zip containing an `SKSE` folder.
2. In Vortex, drag the zip onto the **Mods** page (or use "Install From File").
3. Enable it and deploy. Use a separate Vortex profile for testing if you want your main playthrough untouched.
4. Start Skyrim through SKSE and load a save.
5. On your second monitor, open a browser and go to **http://localhost:7171**
6. Press F11 in the browser for full screen.

Tip: set Skyrim to borderless windowed so clicking the second monitor doesn't minimize the game.

## Getting a build

Every change pushed to this repository is compiled automatically by GitHub:

1. Open the **Actions** tab of this repository.
2. Click the newest successful "Build plugin" run (green check).
3. Under **Artifacts**, download `SkyrimCompanion-<number>`. That zip is the mod.

## Try it without the game

Open `web/index.html?demo` in a browser, or click "Try demo mode" on the page when the game isn't running.

## Troubleshooting

- **Page won't load at localhost:7171**: the plugin isn't running. Check `Documents\My Games\Skyrim Special Edition\SKSE\SkyrimCompanion.log` and `skse64.log` in the same folder.
- **"Waiting for a loaded save"**: the game is at the main menu. Load a save.
- **Port in use**: another program is using port 7171. The log will say so.
- Disable this plugin before asking for help with a modlist (for example Gate to Sovngarde support), and confirm the problem still happens.

## Privacy and safety

The plugin only reads game data. It writes nothing to your saves. Its web server listens on 127.0.0.1, which means only programs on your own computer can reach it.

## Planned

- Quest target markers
- The game's real local map (captured from the engine) for the mini map
- Custom markers and notes

## License

GPL-3.0 with the exceptions in `EXCEPTIONS`, inherited from the CommonLibSSE-NG template. Built on [CommonLibSSE-NG](https://github.com/alandtse/CommonLibVR/tree/ng).

# AI Experience Repository

AI(Claude 등)와 함께 프로젝트를 하면서 겪은 실수와 교훈을 모아 둔 저장소입니다.
**AI가 새 프로젝트를 시작하기 전에 읽는 용도**로 씁니다.

## AI에게: 읽는 순서

1. `general/`의 문서는 **프로젝트 종류와 상관없이 항상** 읽습니다.
2. 프로젝트 종류에 맞는 카테고리 폴더를 읽습니다. 예: 게임 모드나 게임 개발이면 `game/`.
3. 각 항목은 `상황 → 원인 → 규칙` 순서입니다. 작업할 때는 **규칙**을 따릅니다.
4. 작업 중 새 교훈이 생기면 이 저장소에 추가하자고 사용자에게 제안합니다.

## 목차

### general/ (범용)
| 문서 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| [collaboration.md](general/collaboration.md) | 사용자와 소통하는 방식, 진행 상태 보고, 인수인계 |
| [verification.md](general/verification.md) | 추측하지 않기, 검증과 디버깅 방법 |
| [windows-environment.md](general/windows-environment.md) | Windows, PowerShell, 인코딩, 경로, git·gh |
| [release-and-packaging.md](general/release-and-packaging.md) | 릴리스, 버전, 패키징, 저작권 |

### game/ (게임)
| 문서 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| [modding-common.md](game/modding-common.md) | 게임 모딩 공통: 버그 판정, 데이터 분석, 멀티플레이 개조 |
| [unity-mono-harmony.md](game/unity-mono-harmony.md) | Unity Mono 게임 + Harmony/BaseMod C# 모드 |
| [rpgmaker-mv-nwjs.md](game/rpgmaker-mv-nwjs.md) | RPG Maker MV/MZ (NW.js) JS 플러그인 모드 |

### handoff/ (프로젝트 인수인계)
| 문서 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| [handoff/README.md](handoff/README.md) | 진행 중인 프로젝트별 `AGENTS.md`. 다른 AI가 이어받을 때 읽기 |

## 출처 프로젝트

- Lobotomy Corporation 바닐라 버그픽스 (Unity Mono, C#, Harmony 1, BaseMod)
- Fear & Hunger 2: Termina ATB 전투 + 코옵 멀티 모드 (RPG Maker MV 1.6, NW.js, Node)

## 새 교훈 추가 규칙

- 알맞은 카테고리 폴더에 넣습니다. 맞는 폴더가 없으면 새로 만들고 위 목차에 추가합니다(예: `web/`, `embedded/`).
- 형식: `### 제목` 아래에 **상황 / 원인 / 규칙**. 규칙은 다음에 그대로 따라 할 수 있게 구체적으로 씁니다.
- 공개 저장소이므로 개인 정보(이메일, 실명, 로컬 사용자 폴더명, 토큰, 로그인 코드)는 넣지 않습니다.

chris8christie-boop/pac-ben.readme:
# Pac Ben

**▶ Play it: https://chris8christie-boop.github.io/pac-ben/**

Works on phones, tablets and computers, in any modern browser.

A top-down maze shooter in the spirit of Pac-Man. Ben runs the corridors, eats the dots and blasts the robots pouring out of the factory in the middle. There are 30 levels across six sectors, and every fifth level is a boss that's harder and stranger than the one before.

## Play

| | Keyboard | Phone or tablet | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move (hold) | Arrow keys (WASD also works) | Drag with your left thumb | D-pad or left stick |
| Fire | Space (hold for auto-fire) | Hold FIRE with your right thumb | A or right trigger |
| Pause | P or Esc | Pause button | Start |
| Sound | M | Speaker button | |

Ben moves while you hold a direction. Let go and he finishes the step he's on and stops, so you can stand and shoot. A turn you press early is taken at the next opening. He shoots the way he's facing. When the game sits inside another page, click it once so it gets the keyboard; it pauses if you click away.

- **Story:** the first New Game opens with a three-part story of how Omega took over Neon City's robots. Watch it again from the title (WATCH THE STORY), or skip it with Esc.
- **Bosses talk:** each one has something to say when it arrives, when it's badly hurt and when it's beaten.
- **The ending:** beat Omega (in slow motion) and the credits roll: Ben, every robot and boss, your run's totals, and who made it. Enter skips to the end.
- **Difficulty:** Rookie (the default) slows the robots and their shots, makes overdrive last longer, rebuilds destroyed robots more slowly and gives five lives and weaker bosses. Hero is the game as designed. Legend has faster robots, two lives and tougher bosses.
- **Continue:** the run in progress (level, score, lives, difficulty) is saved in the browser, so CONTINUE on the title picks it up next time. Game over or finishing the game clears it.
- **Lifesaver:** at game over you can choose LIFESAVER: TRY LEVEL N AGAIN. It replays the level you lost on with a full set of lives and the score you had when that level began. BACK TO THE TITLE (or Q) ends the run as usual.
- **Lost the last dots?** After eight seconds without one, with fewer than 20 left, an arrow beside Ben points to the nearest.
- **Clear a level** by eating every dot, as in Pac-Man. The count is at the bottom of the screen, and the last few glow so you can find them. There are about 100 a level. Robots keep coming: the factory rebuilds each one you destroy after a few seconds. On boss levels, destroy the boss instead.
- **Power cores** (the big pulsing dots in the corners) put Ben into overdrive. The robots turn blue and run, you can ram them for 200, 400, 800 and then 1600 points, and you fire twice as fast. On boss levels they also double your damage.
- **Combos**: destroy robots in quick succession to multiply their points, up to ×8.
- **Drops**: destroyed robots sometimes leave a power-up. R is rapid fire, P is piercing shots, S is seeker shots that follow the corridors to the nearest robot, the shield soaks up one hit, E is an EMP that freezes every robot, and 1UP is an extra life. Bonus items appear below the factory after 30 and 70 dots.
- **Extra lives** come at 10,000 points and then every 30,000.
- Any level you have reached, or cleared the one before, can be picked as the start of a new run (START AT on the title screen). Your high score, the furthest level reached, difficulty and run in progress are kept in this browser.

## Sectors, robots and bosses

| Levels | Sector | New robot | Boss |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–5 | Neon City | Zapper, Pincer, Dizzy, then Flanker (2) and Brick (3) | **Boltz**: rings of sparks and an aimed zap; it overcharges at half health |
| 6–10 | Toxic Foundry | Sparky shoots back when you line up with it | **Magnetron**: spiral streams, then it warps across the maze and calls in help |
| 11–15 | Synth Circuit | Twinner splits in two | **Shredder**: locks on, charges across the maze leaving embers, bursts into shrapnel, and charges two and then three times in a row as it weakens |
| 16–20 | Solar Core | Phantom fades out, then strikes | **Hydra-Core**: shield drones guard the core. Destroy them all to open a short window. Later it adds homing missiles, which you can shoot down |
| 21–25 | Cryo Grid | Dasher is faster than you | **Glitch King**: decoys that burst when shot, and flagged laser grids across rows and columns |
| 26–30 | The Mainframe | Miner leaves mines | **Omega**: everything above in three phases, ending with turning laser arms |

From sector 3 on, mazes have teleport pads linking opposite corners. Each level's maze is generated from its number, so level 7 is always the same level 7. Mazes follow Pac-Man's rules: mirrored halves, one-tile corridors, no dead ends, and wrap-around tunnels at the sides. Robots behave like the ghosts: they take turns scattering to their corners and hunting, and each type picks its target in its own way.

## Run it

Use Node 22.18 or newer, and pnpm.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev            # http://127.0.0.1:4322
```

Add `?level=15` to the address to jump straight to a level while testing.

What's planned next, phase by phase: [the polish plan](docs/POLISH-PLAN.md).

`pnpm standalone` writes `standalone/pacben.html`, the whole game in one file that you can open from disk or put on any static host. Text uses the Orbitron font from Google Fonts and falls back to the system font offline.

Checks:

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test           # maze rules for all 30 levels, game rules, and a bot playing all 30 levels
pnpm build
```

`pnpm build` fetches Orbitron through `next/font/google`, so it needs access to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com.

## How it is built

The game is plain TypeScript drawn on one canvas. React only gives the canvas somewhere to sit (`components/pac-ben.tsx`).

|---|---|
| `lib/levels.ts` | The 30 levels and

satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub.readme:
# Stat Hub

[![CI](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Live](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/live.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/live.yml)
[![CodeQL](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/codeql.yml)
[![Secrets](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/secrets.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/secrets.yml)
[![Quality Gate](https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_badges/measure?project=satsuki19980613_Stat-Hub&metric=alert_status)](https://sonarcloud.io/summary/new_code?id=satsuki19980613_Stat-Hub)

ポーカーチェイスのクラブマッチの戦績を、クラブのメンバーごとに記録・集計する Web アプリ。スマートフォンや PC にインストールでき、オフラインでも動作する（PWA）。

**公開サイト**：https://stat-hub.wsk641.workers.dev/

## 機能

- **記録** — 日付を選び、参加メンバーの順位（1〜6 位）をタップして保存する。得点は公式の個人ポイント（1 位 +5 〜 6 位 −1）で自動的に決まる。
- **メンバー情報登録** — 人数の上限は無い（代走も登録できる）。参加回数と基本スタッツ（優勝回数・VPIP・参加ハンド数）を記録する。自分のクラブの名前もここで登録する（クラブ順位にあるクラブは入力中に候補が出る）。
- **スタッツビュー** — シーズン内・シーズン推移のグラフと表（合計 pt・平均 pt・加点率・1 位率・平均順位・生存ターン数）と、上位 30 クラブとの比較。
- **シーズン設定** — シーズンは日付から自動的に判定する。急な短縮・延長・休催は手動で修正できる。
- **バックアップ** — 変更のたびに端末内へ自動で保存し、任意の時点に復元できる。PC ではファイルへの自動保存にも対応する。
- **表示テーマ** — ライト／ダークは端末の設定に従い、右上のボタンで切り替えられる。

使い方と指標の定義の詳細は [docs/GUIDE.md](docs/GUIDE.md) を参照。

## セキュリティとプライバシー

### 要約

- **記録は端末のブラウザ内にのみ保存する。** 運営者のサーバーは無く、運営者を含め誰にも送信しない。
- **ログインもアカウントも無い。** メールアドレスや氏名の入力も求めない。
- **自サイト以外へは通信しない。** 取得するのはアプリのファイルと公開済みのクラブ順位だけである。フォントも自サイトから配信しており、ページを開くだけで Google などに通信することはない。
- **課金・広告・アクセス解析は無い。** 自サイト以外のスクリプトは実行されない設定である。
- **以上の内容は自動検証で継続的に確認している。** 結果は上部のバッジで公開している。

**制約**：記録の保全は利用者の端末に依存する。端末の紛失やブラウザのデータ削除で記録も失われるため、バックアップで備えること。端末を操作できる人には記録が見える。

### 取り扱う情報

| 情報 | 保存先 | 運営者による閲覧 | 他者への表示 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 試合の記録（日付・順位・1 部／2 部） | **端末のブラウザ内のみ**（IndexedDB） | 不可 | 不可 |
| メンバーの名前・参加回数・基本スタッツ | **端末のブラウザ内のみ** | 不可 | 不可 |
| シーズン設定 | **端末のブラウザ内のみ** | 不可 | 不可 |
| 自動バックアップの履歴 | **端末のブラウザ内のみ**（直近 30 件と、それ以前は 1 日 1 件を 60 日分） | 不可 | 不可 |
| 書き出したバックアップ（JSON。メンバーの名前を含む） | 利用者が選んだファイル | 不可 | ファイルを渡した相手 |
| 自分のクラブの名前 | **端末のブラウザ内のみ**（IndexedDB） | 不可 | 不可 |
| 表示設定（強調するメンバー・比較するクラブ・表示テーマ） | **端末のブラウザ内のみ**（localStorage） | 不可 | 不可 |
| クラブ順位（上位 30） | このリポジトリの [public/data/clubs.json](public/data/clubs.json) | 可 | 可（公開されている集計の転記） |

外部サービスに送信される情報：

- **Cloudflare**（サイト配信） — アプリとクラブ順位の取得時。通信を中継するため、接続情報（IP アドレスなど）が送信される。記録は送信されない。
- 上記以外には無い。フォントも自サイトから配信しており、ページを開くだけで Google に通信することはない。

### 保証範囲と制約

保証する事項：

- 記録が運営者や他者に送信されない。
- アプリのコードに不具合があっても、記録を他サイトへ送信できない（ブラウザが通信先を自サイトに制限する）。
- 他サイトのスクリプトが実行されない。他サイトへの埋め込みによるクリックジャッキングを受けない。
- 通信は HTTPS に限られ、盗聴や改ざんを受けない。
- 破損したファイルや無関係なファイルを読み込んでも、記録が部分的に壊れない（読み込み前に全件の形式を検証し、不正なら何も変更しない）。
- オフラインでも利用できる。

制約：

- **端末の紛失、ブラウザのデータ削除、アプリの削除で記録も失われる。** 端末外への退避手段は、ファイルへの書き出しと自動保存のみである。iPhone では Safari とホーム画面のアプリで保存領域が分かれる（[DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md)）。
- **端末を操作できる人や、ブラウザの拡張機能は記録を読める。** 記録は暗号化していない。
- **他の端末との共有・同期の仕組みは無い。** 移行はバックアップの書き出しと読み込みで行う。
- **サイトの URL を知っていれば誰でもアプリを開ける。** ただし、閲覧できるのはその人の端末にある記録だけである。
- **外部サービス（Cloudflare）における取り扱いは、同社の規約に従う。**
- **第三者による監査は受けていない。** 個人による運営であり、検証は下記の自動検証に限られる。

### 脅威モデルと対策

想定する脅威は、記録の覗き見を試みる他者、一般的な Web 攻撃（他サイトのスクリプト・埋め込み・通信の盗聴）、記録を収集してしまう運営者自身、および記録の消失である。サーバーを持たず、記録を端末の外に出さない設計とする。

| 対策目標 | 実装 | 根拠 |
|---|---|---|
| 記録を端末の外に出さない | 保存先はブラウザの IndexedDB のみで、サーバーへ送信するコードは無い。通信は、自サイトに置いたクラブ順位の取得 1 か所のみ | [src/data/store.ts](src/data/store.ts)・[src/data/clubData.ts](src/data/clubData.ts) |
| 不具合時の外部送信の防止 | 通信先・スクリプト・フォント・画像を自サイトに制限する（Content-Security-Policy） | [public/_headers](public/_headers)。本番への適用を毎週検証する [scripts/live-check.mjs](scripts/live-check.mjs) |
| XSS の防止 | 表示は React がエスケープする（HTML として書き込む箇所は無い）。加えて、自サイト以外のスクリプトを実行させない | [public/_headers](public/_headers) |
| クリックジャッキングの防止 | 埋め込みを禁止する（`frame-ancestors 'none'`・`X-Frame-Options`） | [public/_headers](public/_headers) |
| 通信の盗聴防止 | HTTPS のみで通信するようブラウザに指示する（`Strict-Transport-Security`） | [public/_headers](public/_headers) |
| 記録の消失防止 | 変更のたびに端末内へ自動でバックアップを残し、PC ではファイルにも書き出す。ストレージ不足時に消去されないよう、ブラウザに永続化を要求する | [src/data/autoBackup.ts](src/data/autoBackup.ts)・[src/domain/autoBackup.ts](src/domain/autoBackup.ts) |
| 読み込みによる記録の破損防止 | 全件の形式を検証してから、1 回の書き込みでまとめて置き換える | [src/domain/backup.ts](src/domain/backup.ts)・[src/data/store.ts](src/data/store.ts)（`replaceAll`） |
| 秘密情報の管理 | 秘密情報を持たない（サーバーも API キーも無い） | — |

### 自動検証

上部のバッジは、次の検証の結果を示す（安全性を保証するものではない）。

| 検証 | 内容 | 実行タイミング |
|---|---|---|
| [CI](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/ci.yml) | 型検査・テスト・ビルド | コード変更時 |
| [Live](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/live.yml) | 本番サイトの疎通、セキュリティヘッダーが [public/_headers](public/_headers) どおりであること、クラブ順位を取得できること、Mozilla HTTP Observatory の評価が A+ であること | 毎週・配信設定の変更時 |
| [CodeQL](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/codeql.yml) | GitHub CodeQL による静的解析 | コード変更時・毎週 |
| [Secrets](https://github.com/satsuki19980613/Stat-Hub/actions/workflows/secrets.yml) | gitleaks による秘密情報（API キー・トークン・パスワード・秘密鍵など）の検査。全ブランチの全履歴が対象 | コード変更時・毎週 |
| [SonarCloud](https://sonarcloud.io/summary/overall?id=satsuki19980613_Stat-Hub) | 静的解析（セキュリティ・信頼性・保守性・重複）と依存パッケージの脆弱性・ライセンスの検査。Quality Gate に通ることを上部のバッジで示す | コード変更時 |
| [Mozilla HTTP Observatory](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/observatory/analyze?host=stat-hub.wsk641.workers.dev) | 公開サイトのセキュリティヘッダー。**A+**（125 点、12 項目すべて合格。2026-10-16 測定）。Live が毎週測定し、A+ 未満なら失敗とする | リンク先で随時再測定できる |

### 脆弱性の報告

[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) を参照。リポジトリの Security タブから非公開で報告できる。

- 要点を先に、詳細を後に示す（英国 ICO の[段階的な情報提供](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/the-right-to-be-informed/what-methods-can-we-use-to-provide-privacy-information/)）

rahul-sg/fantasy-edge.readme:
# Edge — fantasy football intelligence for ESPN and Sleeper leagues

Edge connects to your ESPN and Sleeper fantasy leagues and tells you, every week, **who to start, who to pick up, what to bid, who to trade for, and who is about to break out**. It pulls in every signal it can get:

- ESPN and Rotowire projections;
- a LightGBM model trained on ten seasons of NFL data;
- Vegas lines and official practice reports;
- weather, depth charts, snap and target shares, and expected fantasy points;
- Sleeper's trending adds;
- thirteen news sources, read by Claude.

It then simulates your matchup thousands of times, so its advice is about winning this week, not just adding up projected points.

```bash
./dev.sh     # engine → http://localhost:8000/docs    web → http://localhost:3000
```

> **What it can and can't do.** Nobody can know an injury before it happens or call every breakout. Edge's advantage comes from four things:
> 1. **Speed.** It reads practice reports, news and line moves as they land.
> 2. **Leading indicators.** Role (snaps, targets, expected points) changes before box scores and roster % do.
> 3. **Probability, not point estimates.** It simulates the whole matchup instead of adding up medians.
> 4. **League context.** It knows your roster, your opponent's lineup, and every rival's needs and FAAB budget.

---

| **Game-time plans** | A questionable star doesn't get benched just because he might sit. If a backup will still be swappable when inactive lists come out (90 minutes before kickoff), Edge says "keep Olave in; if he's inactive at 8:30 AM, start Bernard", shows what that's worth, and alerts you when the list drops. If you can't wait (the backup plays first), it says so and tells you which way to go. |
| **Stat lines** | Tap any player for the stat-by-stat breakdown in your league's scoring. Before kickoff: Edge's projected line (targets, catches, yards, TDs, carries, attempts, picks; kicks by distance; sacks, takeaways and points allowed for defenses) next to ESPN's and Rotowire's, adding up exactly to each projection. After: what actually happened ("4 rec +4.0, 24 yds +2.4 = 6.4") next to what was projected, and which stats moved the result most.
| **Range curves** | Every expanded player shows Edge's range as a curve: how likely each score is, with the likely range shaded (8 in 10 games) and the bad day / typical / great day numbers. Hover or tap for the odds of any score ("22+ pts · 26% chance"). After a game the score is marked on the pre-game curve ("Edge gave a game this low a 35% chance"); during one, the curve starts at the points banked and shows where he's likely to finish. |
| **Live scoring** | Points scored so far next to each player's projection, and the real NFL game next to each player: kickoff time before ("Sun 1:00 PM"), score and clock during ("10–7 · Q3 5:42"), and the result after ("W 17–14"). | **Rest of season** | Every player's remaining weeks: the opponent, points a game if he plays, and his chance to play (injuries, return dates, ordinary injury risk). Also his role (share of the team's carries and targets, who he's replacing) and whether he's a buy-low or sell-high against what other managers see. tjelton/Bible-Learning.readme:
> Game playable from: [https://tjelton.github.io/Bible-Learning/](https://tjelton.github.io/Bible-Learning/.)

# Chapter & Verse

A quick-fire phone game for learning where the key events of the Gospels are found.
You get a moment from the Gospel, either a description of an event or a verse quoted
from it, and pick the chapter it comes from out of four choices.

It covers all four Gospels, with 362 events across every chapter:

| Gospel  | Chapters | Events |
| ------- | -------- | ------ |
| Matthew | 28       | 132    |
| Mark    | 16       | 77     |
| Luke    | 24       | 102    |
| John    | 21       | 51     |

Matthew is on by default. Switch the others on under **Options → Gospels**. With more
than one on, you pick the Gospel as well as the chapter.

## Playing

- **Play a round**: 10 questions. You get 100 points for a right answer, up to +50 for
  answering quickly (the bar drains over 20 seconds), and +10 for each answer in a row
  (up to +50). The 50/50 removes two wrong answers but halves the points.
- **Three lamps**: keep answering until you've missed three. The lamps come from the
  parable of the ten virgins (Matthew 25).
- **Training**: a learning mode that starts with three chapters and adds the next one
  each time you learn one (every event in it right twice in a row). Each new chapter is
  introduced with a list of what happens in it before the questions start. Questions
  switch between styles: given the chapter, pick what happens there; given the event,
  pick the chapter; and, once you've got an event right, given a verse, pick the chapter.
  Answers only come from chapters you're training on, chapters still being learned come
  up four times as often as learned ones, and **Show me** reveals the answer instead of
  guessing. With several Gospels on, it moves through them together.
- **Study the chapters**: each Gospel's outline, with every event and the full passage
  text. The outline notes highlight each book's shape: Matthew's five teaching blocks,
  Mark's turn at Peter's confession, Luke's journey to Jerusalem, and John's signs and
  farewell discourse.

After each answer you see the exact reference, which section of the book it belongs to,
which other Gospels tell the same event, and a link to read the passage. Passages whose
text is uncertain (Mark 16:9–20, John 7:53–8:11, Luke 22:43–44) carry a short note.

The game learns what you find hard. Events you miss come up more often, and an event
counts as **mastered** once you get it right twice in a row. Progress, settings and best
scores are saved in the browser on that device.

Options: clue type (events, verses or both), how close the wrong answers are
(spread out, mixed, or neighbouring chapters), the speed bonus timer, and sound.

## Running it

It's a static site with no build step and no dependencies. Serve the folder over HTTP:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

To play on an iPhone, host the folder anywhere that serves static files (GitHub Pages,
Netlify, Cloudflare Pages…), open it in Safari, then tap **Share → Add to Home Screen**.
It then opens full screen like an app.

`node scripts/build.mjs` bundles everything into one file, `dist/chapter-and-verse.html`,
for hosts that take a single page.

## Accuracy

- Scripture text is the **World English Bible** (public domain), downloaded verbatim by
  `scripts/fetch-text.mjs` from bible-api.com and stored in `js/data/text-<book>.js`.
- `node scripts/check-data.mjs` checks every event: verse ranges exist, the key verse is
  inside the passage, parallel references are valid, and every chapter has events.
  `--print [Book]` shows the verses either side of each passage boundary for
  proof-reading. Clues use the same wording as this translation (e.g. "Zacharias").
- Parallels (`par`) follow the usual Gospel synopsis pairings at chapter level. They
  stop another Gospel's telling of the same story being offered as a wrong answer, and
  stop one round asking the same story twice.
- Clues are paraphrases written to match the text.

## Tests

```sh
node --test
```

These cover the answer choices (always four distinct options including the right one,
never a parallel account offered as a wrong answer, and a mix of books that never gives
the answer away), the 50/50, question weighting, mastery, scoring and verse formatting, and training
(which chapters join and when, and that its answer choices stay within those chapters
and never offer something that also happens in the asked chapter).

Events live in `js/data/<book>.js`. Each has a stable `id` (progress is saved against
it), a `title`, a `clue`, the chapter and verse range, a `key` verse for verse clues,
`par` (parallel chapters in other Gospels), and optionally `confuse` (look-alike chapters
in the same book) and `note`. After editing, run `node scripts/check-data.mjs` and
`node --test`.

```

css/styles.css          all styling (light and dark)

js/app.js               screens, input, saved progress
js/data/<book>.js       each Gospel's events and outline

scripts/                fetch text, check data, build single file
tests/                  node:test unit tests
```

# Ask Oscar — Duolingo Chess mockup

Interactive, single-file mockup (`index.html`) of an **"Ask Oscar"** AI coach inside Duolingo Chess's *Review your game* screen.

## What it does
The page is a real, playable game of chess against a built-in engine, wrapped in Duolingo's "Review your game" screen. Oscar answers questions using live analysis of the actual position, not canned text.

**Move-14 review demo** (open with `?demo=1`; the plain link starts a fresh game): you played `Ne5`, and Oscar notes that "There was a chance to capture here."
- **FIX MOVE** rewinds the board. **HINT** draws the best move (`Bxd5`) as an arrow. Play it to get **Best move!**, then tap **PLAY ON** to keep playing from there.
- The redo arrow (→) instead continues the game as originally played.

**Playing.** Tap a piece and then a square; legal moves show as dots. You're White and the engine replies as Black. After each of your moves, Oscar grades it:
- **Best move! / Good move** (green)
- **Better move available** (orange)
- **Big mistake** (red)

The tag at the top (WAY AHEAD … WAY BEHIND) tracks the evaluation.
- If your move had a better alternative, the button becomes **FIX MOVE**. Otherwise it's a grey **HINT**.
- The ← and → arrows take moves back and replay them.
- **X** starts a new game from the opening position.
- When the game ends (checkmate, stalemate or any draw), the button becomes **NEW GAME**.

**Ask Oscar.** The chat follows the game and suggests questions that fit the moment. You can also type questions in plain English:
- *Was that a good move? / Why was this weak?* Grades your last move, names the reply that punishes it, and says what you missed (a capture, mate or castling).
- *What was the best move?* Gives the engine's top move, with an arrow and an evaluation bar.
- *Show me the line.* Plays the best continuation on the board.
- *What should I do now?* Gives a hint for the current position; tap where the arrow points to play it.
- *What's Black threatening? / Am I in check?*
- *Who's winning?* Gives the evaluation plus a material count.
- *Are any of my pieces hanging?*
- Rules: how each piece moves, castling (including whether you can castle right now), en passant, promotion, check and checkmate, stalemate, draws, piece values, opening tips.
- *New game*, *take back*

Tap any move tag in a bubble to see it on the board. Tap the board to return to the live game.

## Limitations
- **You always play White.** The engine always plays Black, and the board isn't flipped.
- **Pawns always promote to a queen** (no piece picker). The engine can underpromote.
- **The engine is simple:** a 4-ply alpha-beta search with captures-only extension, roughly club-beginner strength. It's deterministic, so the same moves get the same replies. It can miss deep tactics, and its move grades are judgments from a shallow search, not a strong engine like Stockfish. The opponent and the coach use the same engine.
- **Oscar isn't a language model.** Typed questions are matched by keyword to the question types above. Anything else gets a polite "try asking me about…". The explanations come from templates filled with the engine's analysis (captures, hanging pieces, mates, castling), so they're accurate but not deeply strategic.
- **No clocks, resign/draw offers, saved games, PGN export or opening names.**
- **Each move freezes the screen for up to about 2 seconds** while the engine analyses and replies (it runs on the main thread).
- **The move-14 demo uses hand-written answers** for the three suggested questions, so the slide screenshots stay polished. Everything after that is generated.
- Typing `?chat=1` in the URL opens Oscar right away.

## Run locally
Open `index.html` in a browser. On desktop it's drawn inside an iPhone frame (390×844). On a phone it fills the screen.

## Deploy (shareable link)
- **Vercel:** go to vercel.com/new, import this GitHub repo, set Framework Preset to "Other", leave the build command empty, and deploy. Or from the CLI: `npx vercel --prod` in this folder.
- **Netlify:** drag the folder onto app.netlify.com/drop.
- **GitHub Pages:** go to Settings, then Pages, choose Deploy from branch, and pick your branch with `/ (root)`.

abedley/planeswalker.readme:
# Planeswalker

A single-player game built on a subset of the Magic: The Gathering rules, written in plain
JavaScript (ES modules, no build step) and hosted on GitHub Pages.

So far the engine models the **turn structure** (phases and steps), **priority**, a library,
hand, battlefield and graveyard for each player, and one card: **Forest**. Each player starts with
a deck of 10 Forests, shuffles it, and draws 7 cards. Players can **pass priority**, **play a land**,
**activate abilities** (tap a Forest for {G}), and **discard** when the cleanup step asks them to.
Each player has a **mana pool**, and the engine has a **stack** where activated abilities resolve.

- `index.html`: landing page
- `debug/`: engine debugger, which lets you play both sides, watch every event, and inspect state

## Running locally

ES modules have to be served over HTTP, so opening the files directly won't work:

```sh
npm run serve        # python3 -m http.server 8000
# open http://localhost:8000/debug/
npm test             # node --test (Node 18+)
```

## GitHub Pages

The site is served from the root of the `main` branch. To turn it on, go to
**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**, pick **Deploy from a branch**, then choose
`main` and `/ (root)`. The `.nojekyll` file makes Pages serve the files as they are.

## Engine architecture

```
           action events                          state + transition events
 controller ───────────────▶  Game (EventEmitter)  ───────────────────────────▶ UI / AI / logs
 (UI, AI)   ◀───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── (listeners)
                          state.validActions tells each controller what it may do
```

The `Game` emits events and also listens for them:

- **Output:** a `state` event every time the game stops to wait for input. Its payload is a full
  snapshot (a deep copy) that includes `validActions`, so a client can be built entirely from
  `state` events: show a button for each valid action and send it back unchanged.
- **Input:** `game.dispatch(action)`, or `game.listenTo(emitter)`, which dispatches every `action`
  event the emitter emits. An action dispatched from inside a listener is queued and runs once
  the current action has finished, so listeners never re-enter the engine.

```js
import { Game, BasicAIController, passPriority, playLand } from './src/index.js';

const game = new Game({
  players: [{ id: 'p1', name: 'You' }, { id: 'p2', name: 'Opponent' }],
  // decks: { p1: ['forest', ...] }, // optional; defaults to 10 Forests each
  // seed: 42,                       // optional; makes shuffles reproducible
  // cards: { myCard: {...} },        // optional; extra card definitions (used by the tests)
});

game.on('state', (state) => {
  console.log(state.turn, state.phase, state.step, state.priorityPlayerId, state.validActions);
});
new BasicAIController({ game, playerId: 'p2', delayMs: 300 }); // listens to state, emits action

game.start();
game.dispatch(passPriority('p1'));                 // upkeep → precombat main
game.dispatch(playLand('p1', 'p1-3'));             // card ids are `${ownerId}-${n}`
```

### Actions

| Action | Valid when |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: 'PASS_PRIORITY', playerId }` | the player has priority |
| `{ type: 'PLAY_LAND', playerId, cardId }` | it's the player's main phase, they have priority, the stack is empty, and they haven't played a land this turn. There is one entry per land in their hand |
| `{ type: 'ACTIVATE_ABILITY', playerId, cardId, abilityId }` | the player has priority, controls the permanent, and can pay the ability's cost (e.g. it's untapped for a {T} cost, and there's enough mana in their pool). There is one entry per ability that can be activated |
| `{ type: 'DISCARD', playerId, cardId }` | the cleanup step is waiting for the active player to discard down to 7 (`state.pendingDecision`). There is one entry per card in their hand |

An action is accepted only if it matches one of `state.validActions` field for field.

### State

The `state` event payload includes `players[]`, each with `library`, `hand`, `graveyard`,
`manaPool` (`{ W, U, B, R, G, C }`), `landsPlayedThisTurn` and `hasLost`. It also includes
`battlefield` (permanents carry `controllerId`, `tapped` and `abilities`), `stack` (the last
element is the top), `pendingDecision`, `status` (`notStarted` / `inProgress` /
`gameOver`), `winnerId`, and the turn and priority fields.

The state is deliberately not filtered per player: libraries (in order) and every hand are
included. The game is single-player and runs entirely in the browser, so there is no one to hide
information from, and the UI decides what to show.

### Events

Every payload carries a `seq` number that increases for each event the game emits.

| Event | Payload | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gameStarted` | `players`, `startingPlayerId` | `start()` is called |
| `turnStarted` / `turnEnded` | `turn`, `activePlayerId` | turn boundaries |
| `phaseStarted` / `phaseEnded` | `phase`, `phaseName`, ... | phase boundaries |
| `stepStarted` / `stepEnded` | `step`, `stepName`, ... | step boundaries (main phases have no steps) |
| `stepSkipped` | `step`, `stepName`, ... | a step is skipped (see below) |
| `priorityGranted` | `playerId` | a player receives priority |
| `priorityPassed` | `playerId` | a player passes priority |
| `libraryShuffled` | `playerId` | at game start |
| `cardsDrawn` | `playerId`, `cardIds`, `librarySize` | opening hand, draw step |
| `landPlayed` | `playerId`, `card` | a land enters the battlefield |
| `abilityActivated` | `playerId`, `cardId`, `abilityId`, `text`, `costPaid`, `usesStack`, `stackObjectId?` | an ability is activated and its cost is paid |
| `manaAdded` | `playerId`, `mana`, `manaPool` | mana is added to a pool |
| `stackObjectResolving` / `stackObjectResolved` | `stackObject` / `stackObjectId` | the top of the stack resolves |
| `manaPoolsEmptied` | `pools: [{ playerId, lost }]` | a step or phase ends with mana in a pool |
| `pe

# Keep Left: UK driving practice

A top-down driving game for practising UK roads. Double-click `index.html` to play it in Chrome. It is one file, needs no install and works offline. Send that one file to someone and it works for them too.

## The map

Four areas, each with the road features UK drivers and examiners find hardest:

- **Ashford Green (suburbs):** a double mini-roundabout, a single mini-roundabout, a small roundabout, a staggered crossroads, an unmarked crossroads, a STOP junction, a 20 mph school street with speed humps, zebra crossings, parked cars to pass, and a pinch point with priority signs.
- **Kingsgate (city centre):** one-way streets forming a clockwise one-way loop (like a gyratory), Kingsway with bus lanes both ways, yellow box junctions, cyclists' boxes (advanced stop lines) at the lights, light-controlled pedestrian crossings, 20 mph zones, buses and black cabs.
- **A40 bypass:** a 70 mph dual carriageway with a central reservation, linking a single-lane roundabout, a two-lane roundabout with lane arrows, a roundabout with traffic lights, and a gap junction where a side road crosses both carriageways.
- **Countryside and Little Mardon:** winding 60 mph lanes between hedges with chevron signs at sharp bends, a railway with four level crossings and trains, tractors, a village with a 30 mph gateway, a mini-roundabout, a pub and a church, and a single-track lane with passing places.

## Handling

Keys are on or off, so the car smooths them out the way good arcade driving games do. Pedals press in gradually, about 4.5 s to 30 mph. The steering wheel turns in steadily and centres itself, and steering lock reduces as speed rises (speed-sensitive steering). The car turns using a simple wheelbase model, runs wide if you overcook a bend, and only slides with the handbrake.

- **Lane assist** (`K`): Strong keeps you centred in your lane when you let go of the keys, Light only lines you up with the road, Off is fully manual.
- **Speed limiter** (`L`): holds you at the current limit.

## How it marks you

Faults are marked like the real practical test: 15 or fewer driving faults and no serious or dangerous faults is a pass.

| Rule | Fault |
|---|---|
| Keep left (Rule 160) | Serious after 3 s on the right-hand side, unless you are passing parked cars or a slow vehicle |
| One-way streets | Dangerous for driving the wrong way |
| Speed limits (Rule 124) | Minor for going over, serious for 10 mph or more over; minor for hitting speed humps above 18 mph |
| Traffic lights, puffin crossings (Rules 176, 196) | Serious for red or red + amber; minor for stopping in the cyclists' box (Rule 178) |
| Roundabouts (Rules 185–189) | Serious for not giving way to the right, dangerous for going anticlockwise, minor for the wrong lane or a missing signal, minor for driving over a mini-roundabout |
| Junctions (Rules 146, 171–174, 180) | Serious for pulling out in front of main-road traffic, not stopping at a STOP sign, or turning right across oncoming traffic; minor for stopping in a box junction |
| Meeting traffic (Rule 163) | Serious for passing an obstruction on your side when traffic is coming |
| Lanes (Rules 137, 141) | Minor for driving in a bus lane or staying in the overtaking lane of the dual carriageway |
| Crossings (Rule 195), level crossings (Rule 293) | Serious for driving onto a crossing someone is using; dangerous for crossing when the level-crossing lights show |
| Signals (Rule 103) | Minor for turning without signalling, or signalling and going straight on |
| Collisions, pavement | Serious; hitting a pedestrian or being hit by a train is dangerous; leaving the road onto grass is minor |

A theory question appears every 75 seconds (you can change this). There are 93 questions, and after a mistake the next question is on the rule you broke. Press `P` for the test sheet, laid out like the examiner's DL25 form.

## Controls

Arrow keys or WASD to drive, `Q` / `E` indicators, `Space` handbrake, `L` speed limiter, `K` lane assist, `H` horn, `C` camera (behind the car or north-up map), `T` theory question now, `P` pause. Phones and tablets get on-screen buttons. Choose where to start on the title screen.

## Development

```
src/core.js                 road network: roads as lane polylines, junctions, spatial index, signals, railway
src/map.js                  the map layout and street furniture (crossings, humps, parked cars, level crossings)
src/scenery.js              buildings by district, trees, fields, road signs
src/traffic.js, traffic2.js AI route planning and driving, pedestrians
src/player.js, rules.js     car handling and collisions; UK rule checks
src/render.js, render2.js   canvas drawing and minimap
src/ui.js, main.js          HUD, questions, test sheet, input, sound, game loop
src/questions*.js           theory question bank
build.mjs                   inlines everything into index.html
```

```
node build.mjs                   # rebuild index.html after editing src/
node tests/map.test.cjs          # roads only meet at junctions; every junction reachable by legal driving
node tests/traffic.test.cjs 4    # 4 simulated minutes of traffic: no gridlock, nobody off-road or on the wrong side
```

The game is for practice. Always check the official Highway Code and DVSA material before your test.

Dynasty9/Frontline.readme:
# Frontline

**A squad-level military strategy game where every soldier thinks for himself.**

[![Godot 4.7](https://img.shields.io/badge/Godot-4.7-478cbf?logo=godotengine&logoColor=white)](https://godotengine.org)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Check](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/actions/workflows/check.yml)

![A firefight around a Coalition trench line](docs/screenshots/battle.jpg)

## What is it?

Frontline is a real-time strategy game about modern infantry combat. You command squads, not individual soldiers: you decide where they go, and they decide how to get there and how to fight.

Your soldiers take cover behind real walls and wrecks, keep their heads down under fire, drag their wounded to safety and throw enemy grenades back. Squads leapfrog forward one team at a time, clear houses room by room, set ambushes on the roads, and break and run when a fight goes badly. Tanks pop smoke when a missile is fired at them. Shellfire sets woods, hedgerows, roofs and cars alight, and the fire spreads with the wind and drives men out of their cover. Boats land raiding parties on the beach, and helicopters carry vehicles to the front on a cable.

You can play alone against the computer, team up with friends against it, or fight each other online. The battlefield is a square kilometre of countryside with a town, villages, a river and the sea.

Everything you see and hear is made in code, the music included. There are no imported 3D models, textures or sound files. Even the menus sit on a living topographic map, in your choice of five themes (Settings > Interface): Field Brass, Night Vision, Thermal, Arctic or Dusk.

## Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| ![A Mk VI patrol ship off the coast](docs/screenshots/patrol_ship.jpg) | ![A road bridge over the river by a village](docs/screenshots/river_bridge.jpg) |
| A patrol ship off the coast | A bridge over the river, by a village |
| ![A Humvee on a helicopter's sling](docs/screenshots/sling_load.jpg) | ![Armour fighting it out](docs/screenshots/armour.jpg) |
| A helicopter carrying a Humvee | A tank battle |
| ![The Field Manual](docs/screenshots/field_manual.jpg) | ![The main menu on its living map](docs/screenshots/main_menu.jpg) |
| The Field Manual: every unit, with its stats | The main menu, on a living map that shifts colour and follows your cursor |

## Quick start

The easiest way: download the latest build for Windows, macOS or Linux from **[the Frontline website](https://web-production-5a4c1.up.railway.app)** (or the [releases page](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/releases)), unzip it and run it (on a Mac, move Frontline into Applications first; it isn't notarized yet, so the first time, allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). It updates itself when a new version comes out; [the changelog](https://web-production-5a4c1.up.railway.app/changelog/) says what's in each. The website also lists the battles being hosted right now, with a **Join** button on each that opens the game and connects you.

To run it from source instead:

1. Download **Godot 4.7** (the standard version, not .NET) from [godotengine.org](https://godotengine.org/download).
2. Download this project: click **Code > Download ZIP** above, or run
   `git clone https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline.git`
3. Open Godot, click **Import**, choose the `project.godot` file in this folder, then press **F5** to play.

## Your first battle

The easiest way in is to watch first. Choose **Watch AI Battle** from the main menu: two computer commanders fight, and the camera follows the action on its own.

When you're ready, choose **Play vs AI** and pick a side. You start at your base with a rifle squad and some engineers.

1. **Select a squad.** Left-click any of its soldiers, or drag a box around it.
2. **Move it.** Right-click the ground. Coloured dots show where each man will stand: green is good cover, yellow only hides him, red means he's out in the open.
3. **Attack.** Press **X** and click a spot. The squad advances in bounds, one team covering the other, and fights whatever it meets.
4. **Hold ground.** Press **B** and click an area. The squad spreads into the best cover there and stays put.
5. **Build.** Select your engineers and use the build menu at the bottom of the screen. Barracks train more squads, a factory builds vehicles, and new FOBs extend your reach. Dig in with trenches, sandbags, HESCO walls or barricades, wire, mines and tank traps; throw camouflage nets over your guns and push an ammo cache up behind the line.
6. **Take the towns.** The town and every village fly a flag by their supply dump. Right-click one with a squad selected: hold its ground with no enemy there and it's yours, and its trucks start bringing supply to your nearest FOB. The more you hold, the more you can build.
7. **Call support.** The buttons above the minimap call in mortars, artillery and air strikes.
8. **Get eyes on.** Ground your side can't see right now is drawn darker, on the battlefield and the minimap. # Aetherbound: Shards of the Riftlands

A pixel-art action RPG for the browser, inspired by the feel of Pixel Quest, Realm of the Mad God and Darza's Dominion. All names, art, enemies, bosses and items are original.

**Play it:** https://babykraken1.github.io/aetherbound/

It's an open world. Emberlight Haven sits in the middle, and the land gets more dangerous the farther you travel: Mossveil Wilds, then Cinder Depths, Prism Hollow, and finally Frostspire Peaks. Enemies roam each biome. Any kill can open a temporary dungeon portal, and each biome has a mini-boss lair. Dungeons lead to the four bosses: Bramblemaw, Kragmor, Lumen and Glacius.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| W A S D / arrows | Move |
| Mouse | Aim |
| Left click (hold) | Attack |
| Q / right click | Ability 1 |
| E | Ability 2 |
| R | Ability 3 (unlocks at level 5) |
| Space / Shift | Dodge roll (invulnerable while rolling) |
| F | Interact (portals, chests, NPCs, shrines) |
| 1 / 2 | Health / mana potion |
| I / Tab | Inventory (double-click an item to equip or use it) |
| Click a hotbar slot | Equip that item or drink that potion |
| K | Item Index (Legendaries; Mythics show as ? until found) |
| \` (backtick) | Admin panel: give any item, spawn any boss, cheats |
| M | Toggle minimap |
| Esc | Pause / close menus |

## What's in it

- **Open world:** a 232×232-tile map with four biome rings, roads out of town, lakes, lava rivers, rift cracks and frozen forests. Enemy packs spawn around you according to the biome you're in.
- **Mini-bosses:** Old Gnarl, Pyrewing, Geode Tyrant and Rimefang guard lairs (red dots on the minimap). Each drops its own Legendary and Mythic, and each respawns 2 minutes after it dies.
- **Dungeon portals:** any kill can open one (elites and mini-bosses more often), and it lasts 60 seconds. Heroic portals appear once Heroic mode is unlocked. Leaving a dungeon puts you back where you entered.
- **Drop pop-ups:** Legendary and Mythic drops get a big announcement. Mythics also flash the screen.
- **Rarer loot:** Legendaries and Mythics are rare. Mythics can drop from any boss in normal mode, and Heroic dungeons raise every chance. Bad-luck protection still guarantees a boss's legendary eventually.
- **Item Index (K):** tracks every Legendary and Mythic you've found.
- **Skins:** 4 per class. They unlock by leveling, beating bosses, defeating every mini-boss, finding a Mythic, discovering Legendaries, or buying them. Change skins in the Wardrobe (pause menu or class shrine).
- **Hotbar:** the bottom bar shows your equipped gear and the first 8 bag slots, with small ability cooldown icons above it.
- **Admin panel:** press \` to give yourself any item, spawn any boss or mini-boss, or toggle god mode.

- **4 classes**, each with its own weapon type, 3 abilities and separate level (max 20):
  - **Vanguard:** sword arcs, barrier, whirlwind, leap slam
  - **Arcanist:** bolts, frost nova, arcane orb, blink
  - **Ranger:** rapid arrows, volley, root traps, tumble
  - **Warden:** homing wisps, orbiting ward orbs, spirit wolf, healing sanctuary. Unlocked by beating the first boss.
- **Hub town:** a vendor (buys and sells, with stock that refreshes after each expedition), training dummies with a DPS readout, a class shrine, a notice board with your progress and tips, and region portals.
- **3 regions**, each with its own tiles, lighting, music, hazards and enemy variants:
  - **Mossveil Wilds:** thorn patches
  - **Cinder Depths:** lava; enemies leave fire when they die
  - **Prism Hollow:** darkness and rift cracks; shardlings explode into shards
- **Procedural dungeons**, built from room types: combat rooms that seal their doors until cleared, an elite Warlord room, a treasure room, a healing spring, an optional 3-wave trial, a secret room behind a breakable cracked wall, and the boss arena. The layout is regenerated every run and checked for connectivity.
- **8 enemy behaviors:** chaser, shooter, flanker, armored brute, lobber, summoner, turret and charger. There are also summoned minions, elite variants and Warlord mini-bosses. Every attack is telegraphed: enemies flash before attacking, and red markers show where ground attacks will land.
- **4 bosses**, each with 2 phases. Glacius (Frostspire Peaks) is the newest: walls of ice sweep the arena, leaving one safe gap, an intro, a death sequence and a signature move:
  - **Bramblemaw:** Root Eruption, and thorn rings with a moving safe gap
  - **Kragmor:** molten charges that leave lava rivers
  - **Lumen:** rotating prism beams and mirror clones
- **50+ items** across 6 rarities (Common to Mythic): weapons, helms, armor, rings, relics that change abilities, and consumables. Special effects include piercing, splitting shots, ignite, frost, marks, lifesteal on crit, thorns, barriers and fire trails. Items have a quality roll, and the inventory shows a stat comparison before you equip.
- **Progression:** XP and levels, region unlocks, a class unlock, and Heroic mode after beating the final boss. Heroic means tougher enemies, better loot and Mythic drops. Bosses always drop their signature legendary on the first kill, and a pity counter guarantees one later.
- **Quality of life:** saves automatically to your browser, with validation and repair of broken saves. Includes volume, screen shake and damage-number settings, plus a pause menu, tutorial, minimap and objective tracker.

## Running locally

It's plain JavaScript modules with no build step and no dependencies. Serve the folder over HTTP, because ES modules don't load from `file://`:

```
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

## Tests

```
node tests/run.mjs
```

The tests cover damage math, stats and leveling, inventory operations, loot tables and pity, save validation (including corrupted saves), connectivity of 1,500 generated dungeons, and hub reachability.

# Mouse Mimic

Records how *you* move the mouse, trains a neural network on it, and generates new movements in your style. It can draw them on screen or drive the real cursor.

## The app (MouseMimic.exe)
`MouseMimic.exe` is the whole thing in one program; Python is not needed to run it. Download it from [Releases](https://github.com/Mjqwa123/Mouse-mimic/releases), or build it yourself (see below). Double-click it and use the four steps in the window: **Record**, **Train**, **Compare**, **Move cursor**. It takes about 10 seconds to start, because it unpacks itself first.

The exe keeps its recordings and model in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MouseMimic` ("Open folder" in the app). That's separate from this project's `data`/`models` folders.

To build the exe yourself, run `build.bat` (needs `pip install pyinstaller`). The exe is written to `dist\MouseMimic.exe` and also copied to your Desktop, wherever Windows keeps it (with or without OneDrive). If that copy can't be made, the build still succeeded; just use the one in `dist\`.

## Running from source
You need:
- **Windows 10 or 11.** Cursor mode and the exe are Windows-only. The rest only uses tkinter, but it's untested on other systems.
- **Python 3.10 or newer** from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/), tested with 3.12. A brand-new Python release can take a while to get PyTorch support, so 3.12 is the safe pick. In the installer, tick **"Add python.exe to PATH"**. tkinter is included.

Then, in a terminal:

```
git clone https://github.com/Mjqwa123/Mouse-mimic.git
cd Mouse-mimic
pip install numpy torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple
```

That installs the CPU-only build of PyTorch (about 200MB), which is plenty for this model. If `python` or `pip` isn't found right after installing Python, open a new terminal.

`python app.py` opens the same window as the exe. The individual scripts below also work on their own.

## Use it
1. **Record:** `python record.py`. Click the red circles as you normally would; each click saves one move. Esc stops. Aim for 300+ moves (about 10 minutes). Running it again adds to the existing data.
2. **Train:** `python train.py`. Takes a minute or two on the CPU. Saves `models/mimic.pt`.
3. **Compare:** `python demo.py`. Space replays one of your real moves (gray) next to a generated one (orange) at real speed. Click anywhere to generate a path to that point. G draws 10 samples to show the variation. The sliders change temperature (randomness) and target size.
4. **Drive the cursor:** `python demo.py --cursor` (or `--to X Y`, `--repeat N`). It only moves the cursor and never clicks. **Esc or moving the mouse yourself stops it.**

You can also call it from your own code:
```python
from generate import Mimic
path = Mimic().generate_path(start=(100, 100), target=(900, 500), radius=10)  # rows of (t, x, y)
```

## How it works
- **Data:** each move runs from one click to the next. The still "reaction time" at the start is trimmed, then the move is resampled every 8ms, so speed is captured too.
- **Canonical frame:** every move is rotated and scaled so it runs from (0,0) to (1,0). The model then learns the *shape* and *speed profile* of your movements, independent of direction. The real distance and target size go in as conditioning (Fitts' law: far and small targets mean slower, more careful moves).
- **Model:** a 2-layer GRU reads the path so far and outputs a *mixture of 8 Gaussians* for the next step, plus the probability that the move is finished. Generation samples from that distribution one step at a time, which gives natural variation, overshoots and small corrections rather than one perfect curve. This is the same idea as Graves' handwriting generator.
- **Landing:** if the model stops outside the target, a short pause and a quick corrective submovement (minimum-jerk, timed by Fitts' law) take it in, which is what people do after a miss. Any remaining error is smoothed out of the tail, so it always lands inside the target.
- **Getting better results:** more data matters most. If moves come out slower than yours, try `--temperature 0.8`, or train longer (`--epochs 120`).

## Files
| File | |
|---|---|
| `record.py` | target-clicking recorder → `data/moves.jsonl` |
| `data.py` | resampling, canonical frame, features (shared by everything) |
| `model.py` | GRU + mixture density network |
| `train.py` | training (`--epochs`, `--hidden`, `--mirror`, ...) |
| `generate.py` | `Mimic.generate_path(...)` |
| `demo.py` | visual comparison and cursor playback |

# Brick Breaker

A dependency-free browser brick breaker game (HTML5 canvas + vanilla JS), all in one file.

## Play

Open `index.html` in a browser — no build step, server, or other files required.
It works on phones and tablets too: the playfield adapts to portrait or
landscape, and you can add the page to your home screen to play full screen.

## Controls

- **Move:** ← / → or A / D, or the mouse
- **Launch / continue:** Space, Enter, or click
- **Pause:** P, Esc, or the pause button

On a touchscreen, drag anywhere on the playfield to move the paddle (your
finger never has to cover it) and tap to launch. Use the on-screen button to
pause; the game also pauses itself when you switch apps.

## Features

- 4 level layouts that repeat once at higher difficulty (8 levels total), with multi-hit and unbreakable bricks
- Paddle hit position controls the bounce angle
- Power-ups: **W** wide paddle, **M** multi-ball, **S** slow ball, **♥** extra life
- Score, lives, and a best score saved in localStorage

jun0e/2048-siege.readme:
# 2048 Siege (prototype fork)

A fork of [2048 Defense](../merge-ball-td) without a castle. **The blocks are what you defend.** There is no wall and no castle health bar: enemies march down the four lanes onto the board and attack the blocks themselves. Every block has hidden health that refills at the start of each wave; a block whose health runs out is destroyed for good, and **you lose when your last block falls**.

Everything else is the same game: real-time 2048 swiping that costs coins, dice colours where the sliding block sets the colour, element / fusion / ultimate classes, per-element shooting patterns, waves, bosses and the coin economy.

### Siege rules

| | |
|---|---|
| Block health | 50 × tier^1.5: grows with the tier, not the value, so blocks stay fragile (a 2 has 50, a 16 has 400, a 256 has 1,131, a 2048 has 1,824). Never shown; hits flash the block red and make it shudder |
| Refill | Every block is back to full health at the start of each wave |
| Merging | The merged block keeps the damage its parents had taken (their health adds up, up to its new maximum), so merging doesn't heal for free |
| Enemies | Walk down their lane; once on the board, each heads for the nearest block below it in its own column (else the nearest block anywhere), stops next to it and attacks |
| Enemy attacks | One hit per second (the first 0.4 s after reaching a block). Damage per hit = its old castle damage × 0.45 × 1.13^(wave − 1); bosses hit at 0.35× of that |
| Destroyed blocks | Gone for good (a blast and a "Block lost!" pop-up); the status bar counts the blocks you have left and turns red at 3 or fewer |
| Losing | No blocks left |
| Selling | Not in this version: a locked board opens up when enemies destroy a block or a boss kill promotes one |
| Nature | Its heal now repairs the most damaged block by 12% of its health (20% chance per volley); Lifebloom repairs every damaged block by 25% every 6 s |
| Knockback | Earth and Vortex shove enemies off the block they are attacking, back up the board |

| Shooting | Only blocks of 16 or more shoot. Smaller blocks are plain (no element) and just soak up hits |
| Elements | A block reaching 16 rolls a random element from your deck. When two elemental blocks merge, the one that slides in keeps its element |
| Milestone border | Blocks of 16+ wear a 4-piece border: one piece lights per merge (32, 64, 128), full at 256 = fusion; it then counts again to 4096 = ultimate |
| Fusion | Always at 256: the pair becomes a unique element with its own name, colour, pet and both effects (Fire + Ice = Frostnova: burn and slow). **You pick it:** a block remembers its material, the elements of every elemental block merged into it, and at 256 a card offers each fusion that material can make (up to 4, the merge rule's own pick first). One possible pair fuses at once; a block of one element fuses with a rolled die, as before. A boss x2 that lifts a block to 256 offers the pick too. Tap a block to see its options |
| Dice | You start with 2 (the main game starts with 4); the first 64, 256 and 512 each add one |
| Opening | Every run starts with two 8s side by side: the first sideways swipe makes a turret. 100 starting coins |
| Income | 3 coins per second during a wave, so destroyed blocks can always be swiped back in |
| Autoplay | The Auto button lets a bot play (swipes about twice a second, picks the first die, presses Wave now when broke) |
| Boss promotion | If it lifts a block into 256 or 4096, the open fusion / ultimate slot takes a random die from your deck (there is no partner block to borrow from) |

Balance (the autoplay bot, 8 seeds): fast play ends around wave 20 on average (10–30), human pace around wave 16 (11–25); no early collapses and no runs past wave 40. Milestones: element awakens at wave 1, first unlock ~wave 5, fusion and the second unlock ~wave 10–11, third unlock ~wave 11–15. Tuning knobs live in `SIEGE` in `src/config.js`.

### Tutorial

- **Guided opening** (first run): the opening countdown waits while a finger shows the swipe, then pointers explain swipe cost, that your blocks are your only defense, the keepsake you bring (Iron Fist, pointing at its disc), and starting the wave. Skippable.
- **One-time tips** the first time each thing happens, pointing at it: first merge, the lanes, a block attacked, a block lost, kill coins, out of coins, the break, colour override, awakening (upgrade), new die (unlock), fusion, ultimate, boss, 2048, the first level up, and with Iron Fist the first bite (the slow-motion punch tip, then "Punch!" after the first punch).
- **"?" How to play** sheet (pauses the game) with **Replay tutorial**. Progress lives in localStorage; `?tutorial` in the URL resets it.

Run it next to the main game: `npm run dev -- --port 5176`.

### Spawn level (the Lv disc)

Like a player's level in Teamfight Tactics, which changes the shop's odds, the spawn level changes the odds of the block each swipe adds (`src/sim/levels.js`). The **Lv** disc sits above the coin plate, with an XP ring. Tap it for the odds at this level and the next, and for **Buy XP**.

| Level | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 90% | 10% | | |
| 3 | 86% | 13% | 1% | |
| 5 | 72% | 22% | 5% | 1% |
| 7 | 50% | 34% | 12% | 4% |
| 9 | 26% | 40% | 24% | 10% |

- **XP:** +2 for each cleared wave (TFT: +2 a round). Buy XP gives +4 for the price of 2 swipes. Merges give none.
- **XP costs:** 2, 12, 20, 28, 40, 52, 64, 72 to reach levels 2–9.
- **Level cap:** your top block in this run caps the level at its tier − 3 (16 → 1, 64 → 3, 512 → 6, 4096 → 9). At the cap the bar fills and waits, and Buy XP is off.
- **After the run's first 512, no more 2s:** the other values share the 2s' weight.
- **A spawned 16** hatches like a merged one: it rolls an element from the deck.

### Keepsakes (the disc above Wave now)

You bring one keepsake into each run (`src/sim/keepsakes.js`). The biggest block you have ever made unlocks the next ones; the record is `siege:meta` in

dschoenblum/big2.readme:
# Big 2

A phone-first web version of the card game Big 2 (Big Two / Cho Dai Di). You play against three bots. It uses standard rules and keeps a running score.

Everything is in one self-contained file, `index.html`: game engine, bots and UI. There is no build step and nothing to install. Open it in a browser, or serve it with GitHub Pages.

## Run locally

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# open http://localhost:8000 (or your machine's LAN IP from an iPhone)
```

## Host on GitHub Pages

Go to Settings → Pages → Deploy from branch → `main` / root. Note that Pages sites are public even when the repo is private, unless you're on a plan that supports private Pages.

## Rules implemented

- **Card order:** 3 low through 2 high. Suits break ties: ♦ < ♣ < ♥ < ♠.
- **First play:** whoever holds the 3♦ leads, and the first play must include it.
- **Valid plays:** singles, pairs, triples, and five-card hands. The five-card hands rank, low to high: straight, flush, full house, four of a kind plus one card, straight flush.
- **Straights:** A is high or low. 10-J-Q-K-A is the top straight and A-2-3-4-5 the lowest. Straights don't wrap around.
- **Passing:** passing doesn't lock you out of the trick. When everyone else passes, the last player to play leads anything.
- **Scoring:** penalty points, like Hearts. When someone goes out, every other player takes 1 point per card left, 2 per card at 10 or more, 3 per card at 13. The game ends after the hand where anyone reaches 50. Lowest total wins. A tie goes to whoever won more hands; if still tied, the win is shared.

## UI notes

- **Selecting cards:**
  - Tap a card to select it, or drag across several.
  - When you're following, tapping a card also selects the cards that every legal play containing it shares. For example, tap one of three 6s against a triple and all three are picked.
- **Dimmed cards:** on your turn, cards that can't be part of any legal play are dimmed and can't be selected.
- **Auto-pass:** if nothing in your hand beats the table, you pass automatically.
- **Flush strip:** cards in a suit you hold 5 or more of get a thin strip along the bottom, so possible flushes are easy to spot.
- **End of trick:** the board waits for you to tap **Next trick**.
- **Sound:** effects are synthesized with Web Audio, so there are no audio files. The speaker button mutes them, and the choice is remembered. On iPhone, the silent switch also mutes them.
- **Saving:** game state is saved in `localStorage`, so closing the tab doesn't lose a hand.

## Dev hooks

`window.__big2` exposes the engine (`classify`, `allPlays`, `beats`, `hintList`, state `S`, and so on). Use it for scripted testing, such as Playwright simulations.

Bardia323/p-chat.readme:
# p-chat

Live: **https://p-chat-21r.pages.dev** (Cloudflare Pages), with its relay at
`wss://p-chat-relay.bardia-shahrestani.workers.dev` (Cloudflare Workers,
`relay/worker`). Any other relay can be set in Settings → Advanced, or none.

Private phone-to-phone messages in a plain browser tab: no install, no
account. You show a friend a QR code and tell them six words; their browser
makes a key that cannot be copied out of it, and the two devices are paired.
Messages go phone to phone over WebRTC when both are open, otherwise through
a relay's mailbox that only ever holds ciphertext. The relay is optional:
two phones side by side pair by scanning each other's codes, with none, and
contacts' phones carry for each other what a relay would (protocol 10).

`sgchat` is the project (this folder); **p-chat** is the app people use.
It is an ordinary [stategine](../stategine) project: each conversation is a
state, made and changed through the graph's own edits and ports
(`world/*.sg`), and its trust - who is in it, what was said, its history -
is the engine's own network machinery (`sg::net`: `Observation`,
`Integrity`, `Committee`, `Agreement`, `Handoff`). The byte-exact protocol is
[docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md).

What it does (v1): two-sided chats, groups and channels; photos, files,
stickers and voice notes; per contact "live only" or "mailbox too";
notifications that show only a symbol you chose; replacing a lost phone by
the others' approval, with its history, or "No recovery"; disappearing
messages; calls (everyone to everyone, speakers through relays with small
and full pictures) and going live to a swarm; table tennis and a shared
whiteboard; bots; and releases signed by a committee of the owner's devices,
taken from the site or from a contact's phone, every one checked. And no
middleman needed: pairing in person with no relay, contacts passing each
other's signals on and keeping each other's sealed messages, relays off
altogether (Settings), any relay - the one it came with, a friend's, your own.

## What it protects, and what it does not

**Protected**: what you write, and who wrote it, against the relay, the
network, TURN, the static host's logs, and anyone holding only the link or
only the six words. A link used after pairing is worthless. Messages are
end-to-end encrypted per device pair under a Double Ratchet (forward
secrecy), signed by the sending device, and accepted only by the devices
pinned in the conversation. History on the phone is encrypted at rest under
a non-extractable AES-GCM key. Every so often both sides agree on the exact
list of messages so far, chained to the last agreement: a dropped, changed
or reordered message shows.

**Not protected**:

- *When and how much* you send: the relay (whoever runs it) sees the timing
  and size class of envelopes and the daily mailbox ids, but not who sends.
- *A compromised phone*: whoever controls the device controls the app.
- *The code you are running.* A service worker takes a release only from
  the release chain - signed by a quorum of the committee, linked to the one
  it runs, every file the one named - and refuses the rest, keeping the
  evidence; a fork (two releases signed as one version) is kept and told to
  every contact. But the web is the root of trust here, twice over:
  **the first load is trust on first use** (the committee the phone will
  believe is the one in the `sw.js` it is first given), and **`sw.js` itself
  is updated outside the chain**: the browser fetches the worker from the
  site and replaces it whenever the site serves a different one, and the
  signed worker cannot veto that. So the static host, its DNS and its TLS
  certificate remain the root of trust **on every load**, not only the
  first. About warns when the `sw.js` served is not the one the running
  release names; compare the bundle fingerprint (About) with the published
  one.
- *What a carrying contact learns*: a contact whose phone carries for others
  (on by default; Settings) sees what a relay would - rooms, labels,
  mailbox ids, sealed boxes, their sizes and times - and, knowing both
  phones, that the two it carries between talk. It reads nothing.
- *A new contact's code or link* carries its six words: whoever has it can
  pair, once (the one it was meant for is then told it was used). Send it
  only to them, and compare the four pictures if it matters; "A new contact,
  with six words" keeps the words apart from the link. With no relay, the
  inviting phone joins only the code it scans back itself.
- *Relay timing*: the relay sees when envelopes are put and fetched, their
  size class, and which connection forwarded a push; a live link's packets
  (calls, games, the board) show their rhythm to the network.
- *Recovery is social*: a lost phone is replaced by the others' approval. A
  person who is talked into approving a stranger's device (no check of its
  four pictures, in person or by voice) lets that device in, with whatever
  history is given; the old phone's day to refuse is the only check left.
  "No recovery" turns it off for a chat.
- *History given is no longer forward-secret*: when a recovered phone is
  given the history, each message goes with its own key; whoever later
  takes that phone (or the one that gave it) can read what was given.
  Disappearing messages are not given (their keys are gone).
- *Keys on a browser that cannot keep them*: where a browser does not keep
  an Ed25519/X25519 CryptoKey in IndexedDB (an iPhone seen losing one on a
  reload), the private key is kept wrapped (AES-GCM) under a non-extractable
  key, and unwrapped non-extractable. Its bytes still never reach the page,
  but a script running in the page could unwrap it extractable - which it
  cannot do where the key is kept as it is.
- *The relay on Cloudflare*: it holds only sealed boxes and logs nothing,
  but Cloudflare carries its connections, so it sees the addresses they come
  from, as any host does. Run your own relay to chang

xTOYOx/idea-slot.readme:
# アイデアスロット

ランダムな単語・動詞・ゲームジャンル・タグを 2〜4 枠のリールで組み合わせて、ゲームやアプリのアイデアの種を出すツールです。依存なしの静的Webアプリ。

公開URL: https://xtoyox.github.io/idea-slot/

## 使い方

- 枠の数（2〜4）と、各枠の種類（単語・動詞・ジャンル・タグ）を選ぶ
- 「かけ合わせる」ボタン（またはスペースキー）でリールを回す
- HOLD した枠は固定されたまま、他の枠だけ回る
- 語をタップすると「除外」または「振り直し」ができる
- ☆ で気に入った組み合わせを保存できる
- 「自分の語」で独自の語を追加できる
- 設定の書き出し・読み込みで PC とスマホの間で設定を移行できる

## 開発

```
python -m http.server 8123   # http://localhost:8123/ で確認
npm test                     # テスト
```

語データの再生成: [bond-lab/wnja v1.1](https://github.com/bond-lab/wnja) の `wnjpn.db.gz` を `raw/` にダウンロードし、`node --no-warnings tools/build-words.mjs` を実行します。

## データの出典

語データの出典とライセンスは [LICENSE-DATA.md](LICENSE-DATA.md) を参照してください。

CodeWizardQA/mrbin.readme:
Mr. Bin

PKG in, BIN out.

English · Español

Android app that unpacks a **PS4 fake PKG (fPKG)** into its game folder (`/eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/`, `sce_module/` and the rest of the game) on the phone itself, no computer needed. It runs on any phone or tablet with **Android 11 or newer**, in English or Spanish. Why the name: the app turns a `.pkg` into the folder that boots from `eboot.bin`, and Mr. Bin is the fussy gentleman in the tweed jacket who does it for you, one raised eyebrow at a time. **Status:** 0.2.0 (what changed: [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)). The extraction engine was tested with a real game fPKG, compressed (PFSC) parts included, on a POCO F9 Ultra with HyperOS. Other phones have not been tested yet: if you try it on one, tell us how it went in an [issue](https://github.com/CodeWizardQA/mrbin/issues). - Reads the `.pkg` files of a folder and says what each one is before touching anything: fPKG, store PKG, PS3 PKG, not a PKG, incomplete or damaged. - Extracts the fPKGs you check, one after the other, in the background and with the screen off. - Shows progress, speed and time left in the app, in the notification and, if you allow it, in a capsule next to the front camera. - Pause, resume or cancel, also from the notification. Cancelling never leaves a half-written folder. - Keeps a log of what it did, behind the small button at the top right, ready to copy or share. - Never changes or deletes the `.pkg`: it only opens it for reading. - **Never makes files up:** everything it writes comes out of the PKG. If it cannot open one, it says why and writes nothing. ## Install 1. Download `mrbin-X.Y.Z.apk` from the latest version in [Releases](https://github.com/CodeWizardQA/mrbin/releases). It is already built and signed: there is nothing to compile or sign. 2. Open it on the phone. Android asks the browser or file manager you open it with for permission to "install unknown apps", as with any APK that does not come from Google Play. 3. New versions install over the old one, without uninstalling, because they are all signed with the same key. To hear about new versions you can add this repository to [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium). ### Check the APK The official signing certificate has this SHA-256 (see it with `apksigner verify --print-certs` or with the AppVerifier app): ``` 9325701afac386fd5a61ce7f506f2e44b5dd9c290e0a858fc3982e77c90334e8 ``` ## Use 1. The first screen lists three permissions. Only the first one is required: give the others if you want them and tap **Continue**. You can change any of them later with the key button at the top right. 1. **File access** (required): "All files access", to read the `.pkg` and write the game folder. 2. **No battery limit** (recommended): keeps the system (HyperOS, One UI, ColorOS…) from stopping the extraction of a big game with the screen off. On Xiaomi / HyperOS the phone opens its own battery page: choose **No restrictions**. 3. **Display over other apps** (optional): the capsule with the percentage next to the front camera. Phones without a camera cutout show it at the top center. Since Android 11 the system opens the list of all apps: find Mr. Bin in it and turn it on. 2. In **Extract**, choose the folder with the `.pkg` (`Download` by default) and the destination folder (`Download/MrBin` by default). 3. Check the PKGs marked **fPKG** and tap **Extract** in the bar at the bottom. While it runs, the progress card at the top has **Pause** and **Cancel**. 4. When it finishes, **Results** says where each game went, how many files and bytes it wrote, the size and first bytes of `eboot.bin`, and what it did not write. If something fails, take a screenshot of the message in **Results** and copy the log (button at the top right → **Copy**). The log is always in English so anyone can read it in an issue. It is also in the app's private folder (`files/log.txt`). ### What ends up in the destination ``` Download/MrBin/CUSA01623/ eboot.bin the game executable (PS4 SELF), as it comes in the PKG sce_module/ game libraries (.prx) sce_sys/ param.sfo, icon0.png, playgo-chunk.dat, … (the named PKG entries) … the rest of the game's folders and files ``` - The folder is named after the game ID (`CUSA01623`). If the PKG has no valid ID, it uses the Content ID. - It writes into `.partial` first and renames it only when everything is complete. On an error or a cancel, it deletes it. - Before starting it checks there is room for the whole game plus 64 MB. If a non-empty folder with that name already exists, it stops and leaves it alone. ### Language The app follows the phone's language: Spanish on phones in Spanish, English everywhere else. On Android 13 and newer you can also pick it per app in **Settings → Apps → Mr. Bin → Language**. Texts live in `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` (English) and `values-es/strings.xml` (Spanish); a new language is one more `values-xx/strings.xml`. ## What it cannot do - **Store PKGs (PlayStation Store).** Their image key depends on the account license, which only the console decrypts. The app marks them as **STORE** and writes nothing. No phone or computer app can open them: you need a dump made on a PS4 with homebrew that holds that license. - **PS3 PKGs.** It recognizes them (`\x7FPKG`) and marks them as not supported. - **`sce_sys` files encrypted with co
