sd-codebase/star-jar.readme:
# ⭐ Star Jar

A colorful habit-tracking game for kids. Children tap their avatar, enter their birthday PIN (DDMM),
and tap activities to earn (or lose) stars, walk the Treasure Road, and unlock badges + real gifts.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
```

First visit: tap **Parents** → create a parent PIN → add your children (name, birthdate, avatar, color).

## Deploy to Vercel

Push this folder to GitHub and import it at vercel.com/new (no env vars needed), or run `npx vercel`.

## Where is the data?

All data is stored in the **browser's localStorage** on the device being used.

- ✅ Survives new deployments (as long as the domain stays the same).
- ❌ Not shared between devices, and lost if the browser's site data is cleared.
- 💾 Use **Parents → Settings → Download backup** regularly; **Restore backup** loads it on any device.

## Rules (editable in Parents → Settings)

- Each activity: max **2 times per day**
- Same activity: at least **10 minutes** apart
- Any activity: at least **1 minute** apart
- Parents can add entries from **Log & Gifts** without limits, and undo mistakes.

## Code map

- `src/app/page.tsx`: home (avatar picker + PIN)
- `src/app/kid/[id]/page.tsx`: kid dashboard (jar, activities, treasure road, badges, timeline)
- `src/app/parent/page.tsx`: parent zone (kids, activities, milestones, log, settings, backup)
- `src/lib/defaults.ts`: default activities, milestones, avatars
- `src/lib/messages.ts`: random happy/sad feedback lines
- `src/lib/rules.ts`: star totals and tap limits
- `src/lib/fx.ts`: sounds (Web Audio), voice (speech synthesis), and confetti

inticoy/snapshoot-classic.readme:
# SnapShoot Classic

[SnapShoot](https://github.com/inticoy/snapshoot)(스와이프 승부차기)의 클래식 모드. 브라우저에서 키보드·터치로 하는 3D 11대11 축구. 105×68m 경기장과 4-3-3 포메이션.

**플레이:** https://inticoy.github.io/snapshoot-classic/

Three.js + cannon-es + Vite + TypeScript.

## 실행

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:5180
pnpm typecheck  # 게임·테스트 타입 검사
pnpm test       # 브라우저 없이 고정 시드 경기/물리 회귀 검증
pnpm build      # dist/ 에 정적 파일 생성 (GitHub Pages 등에 그대로 배포 가능)
```

## 자동 검증

`pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build`로 전체 회귀 검증을 실행한다.
배포 워크플로도 빌드 전에 타입 검사와 테스트를 실행하며, 실패하면 배포하지 않는다.

테스트는 실제 `Match.update`와 cannon-es 물리를 사용한다. `Match` 생성 옵션으로
선수 모델 팩토리(`createPlayerModel`)와 `new Random(seed)`를 주입할 수 있다.
`goalVisuals: false`는 골망 시각 갱신만 생략하고 충돌체를 유지하며,
`userControl: false`는 양 팀을 AI로 진행한다. 기본 옵션은 브라우저 게임 동작을 유지한다.
재현하려면 같은 시드·입력·고정 스텝(`PHYSICS.step`)·보조 설정·물리 프리셋을 사용한다.
보조 설정과 활성 물리 프리셋은 기존처럼 모듈 전역이므로 서로 다른 설정의 경기를
같은 프로세스에서 동시에 검증할 때는 격리가 필요하다.

브라우저 확인은 `pnpm dev` 실행 후 별도 터미널에서 `pnpm test:browser`를 실행한다.
macOS에서는 Playwright 캐시의 Chrome for Testing 경로를 자동으로 찾으며,
필요하면 `CHROMIUM_PATH`로 실행 파일을 지정한다. 메뉴 → 경기 시작 → 일시정지/재개 →
D 키 슛 → 득점을 검사하고 `.artifacts/browser-smoke/`에 캡처를 남긴다.
득점 검증에는 고정 시드와 골문 앞 선수 배치를 사용한다.
`pnpm test:browser --update-og`로 실제 경기 화면의 공유 이미지도 다시 생성할 수 있다.

수치와 브라우저 확인 상태는 [0단계 검증 기록](docs/roadmap/phase-0-validation.md)에 정리한다.

2단계 화면·성능 검증은 `pnpm test:phase2`로 실행한다. 중계 화면·전체 경기장·네 코너 확대를
`.artifacts/phase-2/`에 저장하고, 스킨드 캐릭터 22명의 10초 프레임 측정 결과를 JSON으로 기록한다.
현재 환경의 실행 제한과 자동 검증 수치는 [2단계 검증 기록](docs/roadmap/phase-2-validation.md)을 참고한다.

## 조작 (FC 온라인 키보드 기본 배치 기준)

| 공격 | | 수비 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 방향키 | 이동 | D (꾹) | 압박 |
| E | 질주 | Q (꾹) | 동료 압박 |
| D (꾹 → 떼기) | 슛 (80% 넘기면 뜸) | C (꾹) | 견제 |
| Z + D | 감아차기 | Space | 스탠딩 태클 |
| Q + D | 칩슛 | A | 슬라이딩 태클 |
| S | 짧은 패스 | S | 선수 변경 |
| W | 스루 패스 | | |
| Q + W | 로빙 스루 패스 | | |
| A | 로빙 패스 | | |

Esc 일시정지 · V 카메라 · M 사운드. 공이 오는 중에 슛/패스를 미리 누르면 원터치로 처리된다.

세트피스(스로인 · 코너킥 · 골킥): 방향키로 조준, S 짧게 / A 길게 (꾹 눌러 세기).

설정에서 **패스 보조 / 슛 보조**를 보조 · 세미 · 수동으로 바꿀 수 있다. 정확도와 세기는 선수 능력치에 따라 달라진다.

남은 작업은 [docs/CHECKLIST.md](docs/CHECKLIST.md) 참고.

## 구조

```
src/
  config.ts              모든 튜닝 값 (경기장 크기, 공 물리, 선수 속도, AI)
  core/Game.ts           렌더러, 고정 스텝 루프(120Hz), 이벤트 → 사운드/HUD
  core/Input.ts          키보드 상태 + 눌림/뗌 엣지
  physics/PhysicsWorld.ts  cannon-es 월드, 재질별 반발/마찰
  entities/Ball.ts       공: 공기저항, 마그누스 효과, 구름 저항, 드리블 carry
  entities/Player.ts     선수: 관성 있는 이동, 스태미나, 태클/다이빙 상태
  entities/SkinnedPlayerModel.ts  스킨드 캐릭터: 이동 클립 블렌딩 + 킥/태클/다이빙 뼈 오버레이 + 유니폼 셰이더
  entities/PlayerModel.ts  절차적 휴머노이드 (캐릭터 로드 실패 시 대체)
  data/Teams.ts          가상의 팀/선수 데이터 (이름, 등번호, OVR, 주발, 개인기)
  entities/Goal.ts       골대 충돌체 + 출렁이는 그물
  environment/Stadium.ts 잔디/라인(캔버스 텍스처), 광고판, 관중(InstancedMesh), 조명탑
  gameplay/Match.ts      경기 규칙, 소유권, 슛/패스/태클, 키퍼 선방, 골 판정
  ai/TeamAI.ts           필드 플레이어 AI (소유자/압박/서포트 역할)
  camera/CameraRig.ts    중계 / 선수 뒤 카메라
  ui/Hud.ts              FC 스타일 HUD: 스코어보드, 인디케이터, 파워 게이지, 하단 선수 이름 바, 레이더, 골 자막
  ui/Menu.ts             메인 메뉴 / 일시정지(경기 기록) / 경기 결과
  audio/Sound.ts         WebAudio 효과음 + 합성 휘슬
```

선수는 물리 엔진이 아니라 코드로 직접 움직이고(키네마틱), 공만 물리 엔진에 맡긴다.
조작감 튜닝이 쉬워지고, 대부분의 축구 게임이 쓰는 방식이다.

## 에셋

- 공 모델, 효과음: [snapshoot](https://github.com/inticoy/snapshoot)
- 선수 캐릭터와 애니메이션: [Quaternius Universal Animation Library](https://quaternius.com/packs/universalanimationlibrary.html) (CC0).
  필요한 클립 7개만 남기고 meshopt로 압축 (4.9MB → 295KB). 킥/태클/다이빙은 라이브러리에 없어서 코드로 덧입힌다.

## 다음 단계 아이디어

- 킥/태클/헤더 전용 모션 캡처 클립 (Mixamo 등에서 받아 같은 리그로 리타겟)
- 포메이션 선택, 전술 설정, 오프사이드
- 로빙 패스, 스루 패스, 칩슛
- 난이도 설정, 게임패드 지원

# NIGHT SURVIVORS — 어둠의 생존자

뱀파이어 서바이버즈 스타일의 웹 게임입니다. 순수 HTML + CSS + JavaScript(Canvas 2D)로 만들었고,
외부 라이브러리·빌드 도구·이미지/사운드 파일이 없습니다. 효과음은 Web Audio API로 실시간 합성합니다.

## 실행 방법

- `index.html`을 **더블클릭**해서 브라우저로 열면 바로 실행됩니다.
- (선택) 로컬 서버로 열기: `npx serve .` 또는 `python3 -m http.server` 실행 후 표시된 주소로 접속

## 조작법

| 동작 | 키 |
|---|---|
| 이동 | WASD / 방향키 (모바일·마우스: 화면을 누른 채 드래그 → 가상 조이스틱) |
| 공격 | 자동 |
| 일시정지 | ESC / P (화면 우측 상단 II 버튼) |
| 음소거 | M (우측 상단 소리 버튼) |
| 시작 무기 선택 | 카드 클릭 또는 1 ~ 6 (ESC: 뒤로) |
| 레벨업 선택 | 카드 클릭 또는 1 / 2 / 3 |
| 재시작 (게임오버) | R 또는 Enter |
| FPS 표시 | F (또는 주소 뒤에 `?debug`) |

창이 비활성화되면 자동으로 일시정지됩니다. 최고 기록과 음소거 설정은 localStorage에 저장됩니다.

## 게임 규칙

- **게임 시작 시 6종 무기 중 하나를 골라 시작**합니다. 마지막 선택은 기억되며, 게임오버 후 `R`은 같은 무기로, "무기 바꾸기"는 다시 선택 화면으로 갑니다.
- 적은 화면 밖에서 나타나 플레이어를 쫓아옵니다. 시간이 지날수록 스폰 수·체력·공격력이 오릅니다.
- 1분마다 사방에서 적이 몰려오는 **포위 공격**, 2분마다 **보스**가 등장합니다.
- 적을 처치하면 경험치 젬이 떨어지고, 가까이 가면 자석처럼 빨려옵니다. 레벨업하면 게임이 멈추고 3개 중 1개를 고릅니다.
- 가끔 떨어지는 아이템: **빨간 십자**(체력 20 회복), **파란 자석**(맵의 모든 젬 흡수).
- 체력이 0이 되면 게임오버. 생존 시간·처치 수·도달 레벨이 표시됩니다.

## 적

| 이름 | 특징 |
|---|---|
| 구울 (빨간 원) | 기본형 |
| 박쥐 (보라 삼각형) | 빠르고 약함. 30초쯤부터 등장 |
| 골렘 (초록 사각형) | 느리지만 단단하고 아픔, 넉백에 강함. 2분부터 등장 |
| 밤의 군주 (보스) | 2분마다 등장. 돌진 전 붉은 예고선을 표시하고, 주기적으로 탄환을 원형으로 발사. 처치 시 대량 젬 + 회복 + 자석 |

## 무기 (최대 6종, 각 Lv 1~5)

| 무기 | 설명 | 레벨업 효과 |
|---|---|---|
| 마법탄 | 가장 가까운 적에게 탄환 발사 | 데미지·발사 수·관통 증가, 쿨다운 감소 |
| 수호 오브 | 플레이어 주위를 회전하며 닿는 적 공격 | 구슬 수·반경·크기·회전속도 증가 |
| 화염 노바 | 주기적으로 주변에 폭발, 적을 밀어냄 | 데미지·범위 증가, 쿨다운 감소 |
| 관통 칼날 | 이동 방향으로 적을 꿰뚫는 칼날 | 개수·관통 수 증가 |
| 천둥 번개 | 화면 안의 무작위 적에게 낙뢰 (범위 피해) | 낙뢰 수·범위 증가 |
| 회전 도끼 | 위로 던져 포물선을 그리며 모든 적 관통 | 개수·크기·데미지 증가 |

## 무기 진화

무기를 **최대 레벨(Lv5)** 까지 올린 상태에서 **짝이 되는 패시브를 1레벨 이상** 가지고 있으면,
다음 레벨업 때 빛나는 **★ 무기 진화 ★** 카드가 나타납니다. 선택하면 화면이 멈추고 진화 연출이 펼쳐진 뒤,
주변 적을 날려버리는 충격파와 함께 무기가 진화합니다. (진행 상황은 일시정지 화면의 "진화 도감"에서 확인)

| 무기 | + 패시브 | → 진화 무기 | 효과 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 마법탄 | 시간의 모래 | **아케인 스톰** | 무지개 꼬리를 남기며 적을 쫓아가는 유도 마탄을 난사 |
| 수호 오브 | 강철 심장 | **성역의 태양** | 맥동하는 바깥 고리 + 역회전하는 안쪽 고리, 적중 시 가끔 체력 회복 |
| 화염 노바 | 힘의 반지 | **지옥불 노바** | 거대 화염 폭발 후 주변에 연쇄 폭발 |
| 관통 칼날 | 신속의 장화 | **폭풍 칼날** | 회전하는 거대 수리검을 전방위 8방향으로 발사 |
| 천둥 번개 | 자력의 부적 | **뇌신의 심판** | 낙뢰가 주변 적에게 연쇄로 튀어 다님 |
| 회전 도끼 | 힘의 반지 | **학살자의 도끼** | 거대 도끼 8개가 나선을 그리며 퍼져나감 |

## 패시브 (각 Lv 1~5)

| 패시브 | 효과 (레벨당) |
|---|---|
| 신속의 장화 | 이동속도 +10% |
| 강철 심장 | 최대 체력 +20 (즉시 회복) |
| 시간의 모래 | 모든 무기 쿨다운 -8% |
| 자력의 부적 | 젬 흡수 범위 +35% |
| 힘의 반지 | 모든 무기 데미지 +10% |

모든 무기·패시브를 최대로 올리면 레벨업 보상으로 **생명의 물약**(체력 40 회복)이 나옵니다.

## 밸런스 조정

`game.js` 맨 위의 `CONFIG` 객체에 모든 수치(플레이어 스탯, 경험치 곡선, 스폰 속도·난이도 곡선,
보스 주기, 드랍 확률, 적·무기·패시브·진화 무기 수치)가 모여 있습니다.

## 파일 구조

- `index.html`: 캔버스와 UI 오버레이(시작·무기 선택·레벨업·일시정지·게임오버)
- `style.css`: UI 스타일
- `game.js`: 게임 전체 (CONFIG, 오브젝트 풀, 공간 분할 그리드, 사운드, 입력, 게임 로직, 렌더링)

# Grave Shift

A spooky 1-vs-3 voxel game for phones: one robber digs up graves and banks the loot before dawn, while three guards hunt him through a pitch-black graveyard with flashlights.

**Play:** https://ilovefree1s.github.io/graveyard-shift/

## Online with friends
1. Open the link on your phone, tap **Play online with friends** and enter your name.
2. One person taps **Host a lobby**. Everyone else taps **Join a lobby** and picks that lobby from the list. (**Quick match** drops you into any lobby with a free seat.)
3. Pick a seat (the robber or one of the three guards), or tap **Random robber** to spin everyone's names through the seats and let the wheel decide. Empty seats are played by bots.
4. The person who opened the room taps **Start the night**.

The room creator's phone runs the match, so it should stay on the game (not in the background) while you play.

Online play uses Supabase Realtime (broadcast and presence, no database tables). The project URL and publishable key are in `index.html` under `SUPA`.

## Offline
Play as the robber or a guard against bots without an internet connection to the game server.

BringOutTheRainn/space-app.readme:
# Stardust Empire

A space-themed incremental clicker for phones, in the spirit of Cookie Clicker. Tap a lonely asteroid
for Stardust, build an industry of 14 generators from Mining Drones to the Universe Compiler, catch
comets, then collapse the universe for Dark Matter and do it all again, faster.

The full design and milestones are in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Play it

```sh
npm install        # TypeScript and Capacitor
npm run build      # compiles src/ into www/js/
npm run serve      # then open http://localhost:8080
```

Any static web server pointed at `www/` works once it is built. The game is made for portrait phones
and also works on desktop (wide screens get a side panel).

## Android

GitHub Actions builds an installable debug APK on every push and pull request (the **Android build**
workflow; download `stardust-empire-apk` from the run's Summary page). To build locally you need
JDK 21 and the Android SDK:

```sh
npm install
npm run android    # writes build/stardust-empire.apk
```

`tools/android.sh` creates the Capacitor project in `android/` (not committed), copies in the icon and
splash from `resources/android/`, locks the app to portrait and runs Gradle. A Play Store release
needs a signing key in the repository secrets; see [docs/RELEASE.md](docs/RELEASE.md).

## Tests

```sh
npm test                          # builds, then runs tests/*.test.js with Node's test runner
node tools/simulate.mjs 12 3      # a greedy bot plays 12 hours at 3 taps/s and prints milestones
npm run screens                   # headless Chromium screenshots at phone size into screens/
```

## How it is organised

```
src/
  data/        Content: generators, upgrades, achievements, cosmic tree, expeditions, news
  core/        Rules as pure functions over one GameState object (no DOM), unit tested
  ui/          Screens: the sky canvas, panels, modals, sound, phone wrappers
  main.ts      Builds the page, loads the save and runs the game loop
www/           index.html, styles.css, icons; compiled JS goes to www/js/
resources/     Icon and splash sources and the Android PNGs made from them
tools/         Screenshots, icon rendering, pacing simulation, Android build
tests/         Rule tests
```

| To do this | Edit |
|---|---|
| Rebalance or add a generator | `src/data/generators.ts` (upgrade tiers and achievements follow automatically) |
| Add an upgrade line | `src/data/upgrades.ts`, with an effect from the `Effect` type |
| Add an achievement | `src/data/achievements.ts` |
| Add a cosmic upgrade | `src/data/cosmic.ts` (x and y place it in the tree) |
| Add a headline | `src/data/news.ts` |
| Change the app icon | `www/icon.svg` and `resources/icon-foreground.svg`, then `npm run icons` |

Saves live in local storage under `stardust-empire-save`, are versioned, and migrate through
`MIGRATIONS` in `src/core/save.ts`. Players can copy and load a save code from Settings.

The previous Godot city builder is still in the git history on `main` before this rewrite.

# Chess by Chaos ♟️

**A personal chess gym, open source for anyone who wants to learn by playing.**

[Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Specification](docs/SPECIFICATION.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [UI/UX](docs/UI_UX.md) · [MCP design](docs/MCP.md) · [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) · [Issues](https://github.com/omar-Suleiman14/chess/issues)

> **Status: playable, pre-release.** Every roadmap package has code and automated tests, and production is deployed. Real-device iPhone measurements, human rating validation and live ChatGPT/Claude OAuth runs remain open. See [what's verified](#whats-verified-and-whats-not). Home: `https://chess.chaos.fail`.

## The idea

Open the site, see the board, and play against **Sherine**: Stockfish 19 Lite running locally in a browser Web Worker. Lose, learn, undo, replay, and try again. ChatGPT and Claude are optional coaches through MCP; the board never moves into a chat.

## What's in the app

| Area | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Full Power** (`/`) | Boot screen with real engine-download progress, then unhandicapped Stockfish 19 Lite, shown as **Sherine · 3000**. That's a nominal label, not a measured Elo. Fast / Standard / Deep thinking time, unlimited full-turn Undo (old lines are kept as variations), ‹ › move review without undoing, resign, colour choice, eval bar, resume after reload. |
| **The Climb** (`/climb`) | 11-level ladder: four scripted beginner bots below Stockfish's weakest setting, then limited Stockfish, then Full Power. Glicko-2 provisional rating, applied exactly once per eligible game. Undo, hints or the eval bar make a game unrated, permanently. |
| **Timed** (`/timed`) | Clock presets picked before the game (3+2, 5+3, 10+5, 15+10). Monotonic clock, increments, timeout adjudication with insufficient-material draws. The server re-checks rated timeouts. One rating pool per time control. |
| **Time Machine** (`/time-machine`) | Animated replay, drag scrubber, play/pause/speed, move list, branch switching, on-device analysis with mistake markers, **Continue from here** (a new linked unrated game; the original is untouched), PGN export, and PGN import with variations. |
| **Learn** (`/learn`) | Fixed micro-path (pieces → special moves → check → mate → tactics → endgames → opening principles), curated topics (Queen's Gambit, Sicilian, Italian, Ruy Lopez, London, French, Caro-Kann, forks, pins), progressive hints, explanations of wrong moves, and spaced-repetition practice built from your own analysed mistakes. |
| **Sherine** | Pixel-art sprite, short rate-limited lines, playful disable confirmation with an immediate "Turn off", grudges when re-enabled, achievements, and validated data-only upgrade packs. She never chooses moves. |
| **Profile** (`/profile`) | Separate Chess identity card (alias, blobatar avatar, hue, theme, tilt/flip, optional public `/u/<alias>`), AI-coach permissions with audit log and revocation, JSON export, full data deletion. |
| **Settings** | Ivory / Sage / Slate / Blue boards, five open-licensed piece sets, recorded move/capture sounds and volume, iOS-style switches and sliders, haptics (Android), reduced motion. |

Offline: games live in IndexedDB first and sync through an idempotent operation queue. Guests can play and their games upload after sign-in. Concurrent edits from two devices become separate branches instead of overwriting each other.

## Development

### Search visibility and public policies

See [SEO and launch operations](docs/SEO.md) for metadata, sitemap and indexing rules, site search, public policy pages, Google/Bing verification, and the production crawl check. The public support address is `support@wareed.io`; activate the mailbox before publishing it.

Requirements: Node 22+, pnpm, a Convex project and a Clerk application (both Chess-only).

```bash
pnpm install
```

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

```bash
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` runs `convex dev` (pushes functions and regenerates types) together with `next dev`. Other commands:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm test` | Vitest: rules, engine controller, PGN/tree, Glicko-2, clock, lessons, Sherine, and Convex backend tests (ownership, idempotency, branching, rating ledger, MCP gating) |
| `pnpm lint` | ESLint (Next, TypeScript, Convex rules) |
| `pnpm typecheck` | TypeScript, whole repo |
| `pnpm build` | Typecheck, then production Next build |
| `pnpm calibrate -- --games 40 --pairs 0-10` | Bot-vs-bot Climb calibration; writes evidence to `docs/calibration/` |
| `pnpm slice-fatma <sheet.webp>` | Regenerates the Sherine sprite atlas |

Convex needs these environment variables (`npx convex env set ...`): `CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN` and `MCP_SERVICE_SECRET` (the same value as in `.env.local`).

### Deploying (Vercel)

1. Import the repo in Vercel and set the variables from `.env.example`, with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://chess.chaos.fail`.
2. Set the build command to `npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm build'` with a Convex production deploy key.
3. Add the `chess.chaos.fail` domain in Vercel. Production builds send a CSP and HSTS (see `next.config.ts`).

## Connecting ChatGPT or Claude (web, desktop and mobile)

The MCP server is a **remote** Streamable HTTP endpoint at `https://<your-domain>/mcp` with OAuth through Clerk. Remote connectors work in the web, desktop and mobile apps of both ChatGPT and Claude, because the AI provider's servers make the connection, not your phone.

1. **Clerk dashboard → Configure → OAuth applications → enable "Dynamic client registration".** ChatGPT and Claude register themselves this way. It's currently off on the dev instance.
2. **Claude:** Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste `https://<your-domain>/mcp`. **ChatGPT:** Settings → Apps & Connectors → Create (developer mode) → paste the same URL. Add it once on the web; it then shows up in the mobile apps on the same account.
3. In Chess by Chaos → **Profile → AI coaches**, switch on the scopes you want (`ches

# Dezio

A Discord bot for music, Last.fm stats, video downloads, games, AI chat, moderation and logging.
Every command works as a slash command (`/help`), and most also work with the `D!` prefix.

**Website and dashboard:** https://archlinux.tail7c4f5e.ts.net

![The Dezio website](docs/images/site.png)

## Features

- **Music**: plays YouTube, SoundCloud, Bandcamp and more in voice channels, with a live player card and buttons, a queue, loop, seek and volume. Playlists and YouTube mixes work too.
- **Last.fm**: `/fm` now-playing cards, top artists, albums and tracks, recent plays, profiles, charts, "who knows" and lyrics.
- **Downloads**: `/download` grabs videos, songs, playlists and photo posts from almost any site. Video is always sent as H.264, so it plays everywhere in Discord, and files too big for Discord are sent as a link.
- **Games**: Wordle, chess, Connect 4, tic-tac-toe, rock-paper-scissors, hangman, minesweeper, 2048, Akinator, cookie clicker, casino games and a Game Boy emulator.
- **Fun**: anime GIF actions (`/interact`), animal pictures, quotes, confessions, phone calls between servers and AI chat.
- **Utility**: web, image and Wikipedia search, a dictionary, a calculator, weather, translation, user and server info, and snipe.
- **Moderation and logging**: ban, kick, timeout and purge commands, role menus, welcome messages, and audit-aware logs that credit the right moderator.
- **Web dashboard**: sign in with Discord to change your own settings and, if you have Manage Server, your server's settings.

![The settings dashboard](docs/images/dashboard.png)

## Project layout

| Folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `main.py` | Starts the bot with an interactive console (`--headless` for plain logs) |
| `core/` | Bot class, card UI helpers, storage, audit matching, dashboard server, self-test |
| `core/media/` | yt-dlp lookup workers, the download worker and video/audio compression |
| `cogs/admin/` | Moderation, logs, purge, role menus, welcome, channels, dashboard, self-test |
| `cogs/music/` | Music player and Last.fm |
| `cogs/media/` | Downloads, images, quotes, emoji |
| `cogs/fun/` | GIF actions, animals, AI, confessions, phone |
| `cogs/games/` | Arcade, minigames, casino, Game Boy |
| `cogs/utility/` | Help, info, search, tools, snipe, embeds |
| `web/site/` | The public website |
| `web/dashboard/` | The settings dashboard |
| `assets/` | Fonts, images and data files (ROMs aren't included; add your own to `assets/roms/`) |
| `dev/` | Offline checks that never log in to Discord |

## Running it

1. Install Python 3.14 (what the bot is tested on) and `ffmpeg`, then run `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
2. Create `.env` with at least `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=...`. The dashboard also needs `DASHBOARD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DASHBOARD_URL`, `DASHBOARD_PORT` and `DASHBOARD_HOST`.
3. Run `python main.py`.

The bot writes its runtime data (settings, balances, logs) to `data/`, which isn't part of this repository.

# YouEdu Math — Pulau Ninja (Fasa 1)

Prototaip navigasi interaktif untuk permainan matematik murid Tahun 1. Dibina dengan React + CSS + SVG, dan semua teks antara muka dalam Bahasa Melayu.

## Cara jalankan

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

Browser akan terbuka sendiri. Untuk versi produksi: `npm run build`, kemudian `npm run preview`.

## Aliran

Peta Dunia → Kawasan Topik → Subtopik → Pratonton Misi → Permainan → Keputusan → Kembali ke Kawasan

- 8 kawasan boleh dibuka. Hanya **Nombor Bulat → Bilang Objek** boleh dimainkan (5 soalan, kira objek 1–10).
- Kawasan lain memaparkan "Pratonton Latihan" (aktiviti akan datang).
- Kemajuan, lokasi terakhir dan tetapan bunyi disimpan dalam `localStorage` (`youedu-pulau-ninja-v1`). Untuk mula semula, padam kunci ini dalam DevTools.

## Struktur

| Fail | Kandungan |
|---|---|
| `src/data/topics.js` | Kawasan, topik, subtopik (boleh disunting; `available` untuk peraturan buka kunci) |
| `src/lib/storage.js` | Simpanan kemajuan dan status misi |
| `src/lib/questions.js` | Penjana soalan Bilang Objek |
| `src/lib/sound.js` | Bunyi lembut (Web Audio) |
| `src/lib/usePanZoom.js` | Muat peta, zum dan geseran peta |
| `src/components/` | `WorldMap`, `RegionMap`, `TopicMarker`, `MissionPreview`, `CountingGame`, `ResultsScreen`, `NinjaCharacter`, `Art` (seni SVG) |
| `src/styles.css` | Warna, butang, panel dan animasi dikongsi |
| `legacy/` | Mockup lama "Jom Kira!" (HTML biasa) |

Label topik dan subtopik ialah kandungan cadangan prototaip, bukan kurikulum rasmi.

kirhgoff/lord-of-light.readme:
# Lord of Light

An arena where a Pantheon of self-styled gods fights a Power-matched Horde of monsters. Every Combatant's body is a graph of Parts, and its Orders come from Laya (System 1 classifier) or the built-in Reflex. Written in C11 with raylib and Clay. Terms: [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md).

## Requirements

- macOS with `clang` and `make` (the Makefile links Cocoa/OpenGL frameworks), or Linux (below)
- Linux: `clang`, `make`, and `sudo apt-get install libcurl4-openssl-dev libx11-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libxrandr-dev libxinerama-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev`
- libcurl (ships with macOS)
- Optional: [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to run a local Laya server; required for `make format`, `format-check` and `tidy`, which run pinned clang-format and clang-tidy through it
- `make cppcheck` needs `cppcheck` (`brew install cppcheck` or `apt-get install cppcheck`)

raylib 5.5, Clay v0.14 and cJSON are vendored in `vendor/`, so nothing else needs installing.

## Run

```sh
make run                                   # build and open the arena (seed 1, Reflex decider)
build/game --seed 42                       # another Battle
build/game --decider laya                  # Laya picks Stance + Appraisals
```

The game decides with the Reflex unless you pass `--decider laya`. Laya servers are listed in `data/laya.json`: first the LAN host, then `127.0.0.1:8765`. To run one locally:

```sh
make laya-local                            # laya-serve on 127.0.0.1:8765, CPU
```

If Laya is unreachable or slow, the Reflex takes over.

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space | Lineup screen: begin the Battle |
| Space | Pause / resume |
| Arrows | Pan |
| `-` / `=` | Zoom out / in |
| Mouse hover / click | Show a Combatant's Briefing and Decision |
| T | Tech view: overlays and the Battle Log panel |
| M | Mute |
| F5 / F9 | Save to `saves/` / load the newest save |
| R | After a Battle ends: start a new one (seed + 1) |
| Esc | Quit (confirm with Enter/Y, cancel with N) |

### Other game flags

```
build/game [--seed N] [--ticks N --screenshot out.png] [--xray] [--select N]
           [--decider laya|reflex] [--replay dump.json]
```

`--replay` plays a dumped Battle back from its log of Decisions.

## Headless

```sh
make headless
build/headless --seed 1 --ticks 300 --dump mid.json   # run and save state
build/headless --load mid.json --ticks 300             # continue from a state
build/headless --replay mid.json                       # replay its Decisions
build/headless --seed 1 --ticks 300 --dump-requests build/requests-seed1.jsonl   # Decision request bodies + Reflex answers
uv run --python 3.12 python tools/bench_jev_vs_laya.py --corpus build/requests-seed1.jsonl --size 60   # benchmark Jev vs Laya
```

## Development

```sh
make test          # unit tests
make asan          # tests + headless runs under ASan/UBSan
make screenshots   # PNGs of a few seeds in build/shots/
make balance       # Power balance report
```

### Checks

```sh
make test asan format-check tidy cppcheck   # what CI runs on every PR and push to main
make format                                  # apply clang-format to src/ and tests/
git config core.hooksPath .githooks          # pre-commit: format-check on staged .c/.h files
```

- Game data (Parts, Body Plans, Pantheons, Elements, Power weights) is JSON in `data/`
- `src/sim/` is the simulation and never includes raylib ([ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-simulation-never-sees-raylib.md)); `src/view/` draws it; `src/laya/` is the Laya decider
- Decisions are in `docs/adr/`, research in `docs/research/`, and the plan and tickets in `docs/plan/`

Shagg88/Athelas.readme:
# Athelas I'm Shagg and I created this project with the help of Claude (Anthropic). This is a free, unofficial launcher for three Lord of the Rings games, so you can play your own copies on a modern Windows PC from one place. Tolkien created an amazing world that deserves to be lived and experienced in every way possible. I used to play this with my siblings and friends for hours on end, day after day and it's an absolute shame they're not distributable today, so that's why I'm here. (Athelas is kingsfoil, the healing herb). After the release of the War in the North "remaster" I decided to really take on this project. This is my first ever project of this magnitude so I expect there to be a few bugs. I have a Windows PC that I tested this on, that's about it. It's supposed to run on Linux and Steam Deck(Mac and Android maybe in the future) but only time will tell. Mods and Texture packs are supported but I have not done any of those. I'll be open to accepting public contributions and pull requests as well. - **The Return of the King (PC, 2003)**, through **ROTK Fix** (This is the recommended way to play The Return of the King, at least in my opinion) - **The Return of the King (Xbox)**, through a native PC port - **The Two Towers (Xbox)**, through a native PC port Download it from [Releases](../../releases): one zip with the launcher, ROTK Fix and both ports. > Not affiliated with or endorsed by Electronic Arts, New Line Cinema, Warner Bros. or the Tolkien Estate. > No game files are included. You need your own copy of each game: the PC game installed, or your own Xbox disc as > an `.iso` or extracted files (US releases). ROTK Fix doesn't change or bypass the PC game's copy protection. The > Xbox ports skip the console's check for an original Xbox disc, which a PC can't answer as it has no Xbox drive; > the games' own files are never decrypted or changed. ## Screenshots

*The background pictures in these screenshots are artwork from the games themselves. They aren't included in the download: Athelas reads them from your own copy of a game, so you'll only see them once the launcher has found one of your games. Until then, or if you choose "None" under About → Background pictures, the launcher shows its own drawn landscape instead. All game and film artwork belongs to its owners.* ## In this repository | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `launcher/` | Athelas, the launcher | | `src/`, `build.sh` | ROTK Fix, for the PC game | | `ports/two-towers/` | The Two Towers PC port ([its README](ports/two-towers/README.md)) | | `ports/rotk-xbox/` | The Return of the King Xbox PC port ([its README](ports/rotk-xbox/README.md)) | | `dist-files/README.txt` | The README that comes in the download, with every setting | | `docs/` | Release notes and engine notes | | `scripts/` | Packaging the release zip | | `third_party/`, `licenses/` | Bundled libraries and every licence | ## ROTK Fix: what it does - **Any screen:** widescreen and ultrawide without stretching (menus and HUD stay at most 16:9), any resolution, borderless/fullscreen/windowed with ultrawide window sizes, Alt-Tab that works - **Smooth:** 60 to 240 fps at normal game speed, even frame pacing, V-Sync aware - **Sharper:** anti-aliasing, texture filtering, sharpening, working brightness in borderless - **Controllers:** Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and most others; button remapping; the right button names in hints - **Co-op:** two controllers on one PC, or online by streaming with Steam Remote Play Together or Parsec (see README.txt) - **Movies:** cutscenes fill widescreen screens with correct proportions; optional logo skip; a sound delay setting for Bluetooth speakers - **Texture packs:** dump the game's textures to PNG and load replacements from a folder (no game art included) - **Screenshots:** `\` or Print Screen saves a PNG - **Gameplay:** damage taken, enemy damage, and every level and character unlocked (off by default) - **Achievements:** in all three games, earned as you play (and from what your saves already hold), with a note on screen and the list in the launcher - **Launcher:** every setting in one place, with presets (Original, Balanced, High, Ultra) ## Requirements - Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), or Linux / Steam Deck through Proton (tested in a Deck-like setup, not yet on a real Deck; see README.txt). - Your own US copy of each game. No game files are included. - **The Return of the King (PC):** a Vulkan 1.3 graphics driver is recommended. Without one, the game runs through Windows' Direct3D 8 with the DXVK-only options (sharpening, colour looks, texture filtering) turned off. The launcher's About tab shows which renderer you'll get. - **The Two Towers and The Return of the King (Xbox):** a DirectX 12 graphics card. ## The Two Towers (Xbox) Played through its PC port, `TwoTowers.exe`, started from the launcher. - Supported: the US Xbox release, as a disc image (`.iso`) or the extracted files. Other releases are recognised, with a warning before they start. - Keyboard and mouse or a controller. `F10` (or both stick clicks) opens an in-game settings menu; every setting is also on the launcher's page or in `settings.toml`. - The ga

yahya123467/Pax-history-s-.readme:
# Pax History

A browser-based, AI-driven alternate-history grand strategy game. Pick a nation and a start date, write your orders in plain language ("remilitarise the Rhineland", "propose an alliance with Japan"), and an LLM game master decides how the world reacts. The map redraws to match.

- **Map:** Natural Earth borders, coloured by owner, rendered with MapLibre GL. Click a region to see its owner.
- **Turns:** each **End Turn** resolves your orders, generates 1–3 moves by AI nations, and advances one month.
- **Diplomacy:** chat with any nation's leader in character. Concluded talks are summarised into the event log.
- **Rules engine:** the AI proposes changes; code validates each one before applying it (unknown provinces and nonexistent nations are rejected and shown to you).
- **Memory:** once the log passes 30 events, older events are folded into a "history so far" paragraph.
- **Save/load:** SQLite. Every turn is autosaved, and you can make named saves.
- **Works offline:** with no API key, a mock engine is used, so you can try the whole loop for free.

![Pax History — Germany, April 1936](docs/screenshot.png)

## Quick start

Requirements: **Node.js 20.6+** (22 LTS recommended) and npm.

```bash
git clone <this repo> && cd Pax-history-s-
npm install                 # installs root + server + client workspaces
cp .env.example .env        # then edit .env (see below)
npm run dev                 # server on :3001, client on :5173
```

Open **http://localhost:5173**.

### `.env`

```ini
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...          # from https://openrouter.ai/keys  (server-side only)
OPENROUTER_MODEL=openai/gpt-4o-mini   # any OpenRouter model slug that handles JSON well
```

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | *(empty)* | No key means the **offline mock engine** is used. |
| `OPENROUTER_MODEL` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, `google/gemini-2.5-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat` |
| `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. |
| `AI_MOCK` | `0` | `1` forces the mock engine even if a key is set. |
| `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` | Per-request timeout. |
| `PORT` | `3001` | API server port. |
| `DATABASE_PATH` | `./data/pax.sqlite` | Relative to `server/`. |

The key is read only by the Express server (`server/src/config.ts`) and used only in `server/src/ai/client.ts`. The browser calls `/api/*` on your own server and never receives the key. Vite only exposes `VITE_*` variables to the client, so don't rename it to that.

### Other commands

```bash
npm test             # rule-validation unit tests (node:test)
npm run typecheck    # server + client
npm run build        # production build of the client
npm start            # serve API + built client on :3001
npm run geo          # rebuild the province layer from Natural Earth (outputs are committed)
npm run prompts      # regenerate docs/PROMPTS.md from the prompt source
```

## How to play

1. **New game**: pick *Europe, 1936*, a start month, and any of 33 playable nations.
2. **Orders** (right, top): describe what your government does this month. Be as specific or as bold as you like. The engine judges plausibility, so a Baltic state can't conquer the USSR in a month.
3. **End Turn**: read the report (narrative, foreign reactions, and the mechanics applied or rejected). The map and event log update.
4. **Diplomacy** (right, bottom): pick a nation, or click it on the map and choose *Open talks*. Make concrete offers. Leaders act in their own interest. Press **Conclude talks** to record agreements in the log. Open talks are concluded automatically at End Turn.
5. **Save game** in the top bar. **Menu → Load game** lists named saves and autosaved games.

## Project structure

```
.
├── shared/
│   └── types.ts                 # World-state schema + AI contract + API DTOs (types only)
├── server/                      # Node + Express + TypeScript (run with tsx)
│   ├── data/provinces.json      # generated: province ids, names, centroids, neighbours
│   ├── scripts/
│   │   ├── build-geo.ts         # Natural Earth -> provinces.geojson + provinces.json
│   │   └── dump-prompts.ts      # writes docs/PROMPTS.md
│   └── src/
│       ├── index.ts             # Express app (also serves client/dist in production)
│       ├── config.ts            # env -> config (API key stays here)
│       ├── routes/api.ts        # HTTP routes (thin)
│       ├── services/gameService.ts  # turn loop, diplomacy, memory, saves
│       ├── state/
│       │   ├── world.ts         # pure state helpers (relations, dates, lookups)
│       │   ├── summary.ts       # compact world summary for prompts
│       │   └── provinces.ts     # loads province metadata
│       ├── scenarios/
│       │   ├── europe1936.ts    # the preset scenario
│       │   └── index.ts         # scenario registry + initial-state builder
│       ├── ai/
│       │   ├── client.ts        # OpenRouter client, retry/backoff, JSON repair
│       │   ├── prompts.ts       # ALL prompts (engine, diplomacy, summaries, memory)
│       │   ├── engine.ts        # resolveTurn, summarizeHistory
│       │   ├── diplomacy.ts     # chatReply, summarizeTalks
│       │   └── mock.ts          # offline engine with the same JSON contract
│       ├── validation/
│       │   ├── changes.ts       # zod shape check + rule validation/application
│       │   └── changes.test.ts
│       └── db/database.ts       # SQLite (games + saves tables)
├── client/                      # React + Vite + TypeScript + MapLibre GL
│   ├── public/geo/provinces.geojson
│   └── src/
│       ├── App.tsx, main.tsx, styles.css
│       ├── lib/api.ts, lib/format.ts

hammaad2002/shrek2-team-action-web.readme:
# Shrek 2 Team Action — in your browser (bring your own disc)

Play your own copy of *Shrek 2 Team Action* (PC, 2004) in a desktop browser.

This repository and the site built from it contain **no game files and no game code**. Each
player chooses their own disc image (`SHRK2TMA_1.iso`); the browser unpacks it into its private
storage and translates the game's x86 program to WebAssembly on the player's own machine. The
translated code runs on a re-implementation of the Windows, Direct3D 9, DirectSound, DirectInput
and Bink interfaces the game uses.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Activision, DreamWorks Animation or Beenox.

## Playing
- **Your disc image:** make an .iso of your own *Shrek 2 Team Action* PC CD — on Windows with a
  free tool such as AnyBurn (“Copy disc to image file”), on a Mac with Disk Utility (File → New
  Image → Image from the CD, format “DVD/CD master”, then rename the .cdr to .iso), on Linux with
  `dd if=/dev/sr0 of=shrek2.iso bs=2048`. The image never leaves your computer.
- **Browsers:** current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, in a normal (not private)
  window. About 1 GB of storage is needed. Unpacking takes under a minute (Firefox: about three
  minutes), once; translating the game takes a few seconds the first time.
- **Controls:** the game's own keys (arrows to move, Space jump, Z use, X attack, C special, A/S
  switch character, D HUD, Esc pause, numpad camera). Press F1 in game, or **Controls** on the
  start page, for the full list.
- **Controllers:** up to four Xbox-style controllers, one per player, in the order they are
  connected (press a button so the browser reports it). Player 2–4 join with Start.
- **Settings** (the original Launcher's options): resolution, shadows, distance clipping, mouse
  camera, and keyboard and controller bindings for every player.
- **Saves** stay in the browser that made them. **Back up saves** downloads them as a ZIP;
  **Restore saves** reads that ZIP or the `save.bin` files of a Windows installation.
- **Fullscreen** from the button at the top right of the game. Browsers keep Esc for leaving
  fullscreen (Chrome and Edge let the game have it); the substitute key (` by default) works as
  Esc everywhere.

## How it works
1. `installer/` reads the ISO 9660 image, the MSI database and the LZX cabinet and writes the
   installed tree into the Origin Private File System, checking every file against the MSI's
   MD5 hashes.
2. `recomp/` translates `Shrek 2.exe` (identified by SHA-256; `metadata/` holds address-only
   analysis hints for the supported executable) into one WebAssembly module, cached in OPFS.
3. `runtime/` (C++, Emscripten) provides the Windows API, Direct3D 9 on WebGL 2 / OpenGL ES 3,
   DirectSound, DirectInput (keyboard, mouse, four virtual gamepads) and Bink (FFmpeg's
   decoders). The game runs on worker threads; the page renders and handles input.
4. `web/` is the page: install, settings, saves, controls, fullscreen.

`docs/JOURNAL.md` records how each part of the game's behaviour was worked out.

## Building
Requirements: Node.js 24, Emscripten 6.0.12 at `work/tools/emsdk`, the FFmpeg 7.1.1 source at
`work/tools/ffmpeg-dl/ffmpeg-7.1.1`, and for the native build SDL2, FFmpeg and OpenGL ES headers.

```sh
npm install
tools/build-web.sh                       # engine (and FFmpeg for the web on first run) -> web/public/engine
cd web && npx vite                       # development server on http://localhost:5173
REPO_URL=<repository URL> tools/build-release.sh   # deployable site in web/dist, with release checks
```

Development tools (they need a disc image and run against the dev server):
`tools/web-smoke.mjs` (a session with scripted keys and frame captures), `tools/web-ui-test.mjs`
(saves, fullscreen, mouse capture, controls list), `tools/web-pad-test.mjs` (settings and
controller play) — each takes `--browser chrome|firefox|webkit`. The native build
(`runtime/`, SDL2) runs the installed game with scripted input (`SHREK2_INPUT`, `SHREK2_PAD`).

`work/` and `research/` are git-ignored: game files, extracted data and anything derived from
them never enter the repository or the site. `tools/scan-dist.mjs` checks a build for any byte
sequence shared with the game's files before release.

## Licenses
The code in this repository is under the MIT license (`LICENSE`). The engine statically links
FFmpeg 7.1.1 (LGPL 2.1 or later; minimal build by `tools/build-ffmpeg-web.sh`, source at
https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-7.1.1.tar.xz). Also used: iced-x86 (MIT), Emscripten and its
libraries (MIT; LLVM libc++/compiler-rt under Apache 2.0 with LLVM exceptions), dlmalloc
(MIT-0), Khronos headers (MIT), Vite (MIT). The site's `licenses.html` lists them.

andyqueyl/fathom.desc: Free daily-dive trivia game: name something, rarer answers sink deeper
andyqueyl/fathom.readme:
# Fathom

A free, offline take on the daily trivia game Krillion. Each day you get seven prompts like "Name a country in South America" and 25 seconds to answer each one. Obvious answers barely score. Rare ones sink you deeper, at 10 metres per point, and a perfect 700 reaches the trench at 7,000 m.

A personal fan project, not affiliated with Krillion. Everything here is free: today's dive, the archive of past dives, themed packs and unlimited play.

**Play it:** https://andyqueyl.github.io/fathom/

## How to play

Open `index.html` in a browser. Double-clicking it works and needs no server and no internet. Without internet the custom fonts don't load, so you get system fonts instead.

- **Daily dive:** the same seven prompts for everyone on a given day, playable once. Dive #1 was 15 Oct 2026.
- **Archive:** any past dive, also once each.
- **Themed packs:** seven random prompts from one category.
- **Unlimited:** seven random prompts from everything. Practice modes skip the next 7 days of daily prompts and show you unseen prompts first.
- **Play with friends:** host a lobby, send the 4-letter code or invite link, and up to 8 people play the same 7 prompts at the same time. Everyone sees who has answered, then all the answers side by side, then live standings.
- **Stats:** dives played, average, deepest, streak, recent scores, how rare your answers are, and your flagged answers. Stats live in this browser only (localStorage).

During a round you can **Pass**, see the guesses that got rejected, and **flag** a rejected answer you think is right. Flags collect on the Stats page with a Copy button, so you can send them over to get added. After each round you see your answer's rarity, and you can open the full answer list if you want it.

Typing an answer that isn't on the list doesn't cost you anything. You get "not on the list" and can try again until the clock runs out. Case, accents, punctuation, apostrophes, a leading "the" and plural "s" are ignored, and numbers can be typed any way ("Toy Story 2" = "Toy Story II" = "Toy Story Two", "Henry the Eighth" = "Henry VIII"). Typos are forgiven only a little: one slip in a word of 6+ letters, two in 10+, or two swapped letters ("balck"). Each word has to keep its first letter, and numbers have to match ("Shrek 5" is not "Shrek 2"). That's strict on purpose: a rejected typo can be retyped, but a wrong answer that sneaks through can't be undone.

### Scoring

| Rarity | Points | Roughly how many players would say it |
|---|---|---|
| Common | 10 | over 15% |
| Popular | 30 | 5-15% |
| Decent | 50 | 2-5% |
| Rare | 75 | 0.5-2% |
| Abyssal | 100 | under 0.5% |
| Missed | 0 | time ran out |

## What it can't do (read this)

- **Rarity is estimated, not measured.** The real game scores you against what other players actually typed. Fathom has no players to count, so every answer carries a hand-assigned tier (written with Claude). Expect some tiers to feel wrong. Fix them in the `data/pack-*.js` files.
- **Only answers on the list count.** Every prompt is a closed set (countries, elements, Pixar films...) with a list that's meant to be complete, but some correct answers will be missing. If one gets rejected, add it to the pack.
- **Friends lobbies are peer to peer.** Browsers connect directly using PeerJS (its free public server only introduces them). The host's tab runs the game, so it has to stay open. Some strict networks (school, cellular, office) block direct connections. Tested with two tabs on one computer, not yet across two devices.
- **There's no global leaderboard and no accounts.** "Same prompts for everyone" holds because the daily schedule is computed from the date, so friends opening their own copy get the same dive. Scores aren't shared.
- **The schedule shifts when you add prompts.** Days are dealt from a seeded shuffle of all prompt ids, so adding or removing prompts changes which prompts upcoming (and past) dive numbers show.
- With 410 prompts, the daily cycle repeats after 58 days (reshuffled). Heavy unlimited play uses up prompts before they come round in the daily.
- **Typo matching still lets a few wrong answers through.** `node scripts/false-matches.cjs` lists every case where an answer from another prompt would typo-match (about 1,800 across 37,600 answers). Most are fair, like demonyms ("Austrian" for Austria) or spacing ("Heilong Jiang"). A few aren't, like "Indians" counting as the Indiana Pacers.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/game.js` | The game. |
| `js/match.js` | Answer normalising and typo matching, shared with the validator. |
| `data/pack-*.js` | 410 prompts and about 37,600 answers in 11 packs: geography (50), science & nature (50), pop culture (49), food & everyday (49), sports & history (48), games (34), Film & TV (30), words & language (36), brands (26), famous people (20), music (18). |
| `data/FORMAT.md` | How to write or edit a pack, and how tiers are defined. |
| `scripts/validate.cjs` | `node scripts/validate.cjs` checks every pack (ids, tiers, alias collisions). |
| `scripts/false-matches.cjs` | Typo-matching audit (about 2 minutes). Lists wrong answers that would still score. |

## Adding prompts

1. Add an entry to a pack (or a new `data/pack-<name>.js`, plus a `<script>` tag in `index.html`), following `data/FORMAT.md`.
2. Run `node scripts/validate.cjs` and fix it until it reports 0 errors.
3. Reload the page.

duongtuankiet-se/SirLocked.desc: A two-player cooperative detective game featuring real-time investigation, role-based gameplay, and AI-assisted case generation. Built with ASP.NET Core, MongoDB, SignalR, and Phaser 4.
duongtuankiet-se/SirLocked.readme:
# SirLocked

AI-assisted cooperative detective game MVP.

## Stack

- Backend: ASP.NET Core Web API, MongoDB, JWT, SignalR
- Frontend: Vite JavaScript SPA, with Phaser 4 + TypeScript for the gameplay renderer
- AI case generation: OpenAI preview/truth approval flow, validation and publishing; optional xAI cinematic videos

## Cinematic presentation

Visual-novel dialogue, NPC idle, independent cutscenes, audio, recap and cooperative pings are available with legacy-case fallbacks. Optional xAI generation is off by default and requires explicit budget/pricing configuration. Paid text/image calls also require configured usage reservations. See [setup, authoring, cost accounting and verification](docs/CINEMATIC_PRESENTATION_VI.md).

## Requirements

- .NET SDK 9
- Node.js 20+
- Access to the MongoDB instance configured in `.env` (local or remote). Docker Desktop or a local MongoDB installation is only needed when using a local database.

## Configuration

Create `.env` in the repository root. The backend loader accepts ASP.NET-style double-underscore keys:

You can start from `ai-game-docs/.env.example`.

```env
MongoDb__ConnectionString=mongodb://localhost:27017
MongoDb__DatabaseName=SirLockedDb
GameplayV3__Enabled=true
GameplayV3__PlaytestInstrumentationEnabled=false
Playtest__PseudonymKey=replace-with-at-least-32-characters
Playtest__RetentionDays=30
# Unset follows the case mechanics version; true/false forces it everywhere.
Accusation__RequireConsensus=
AiCaseV3Preset__Enabled=true
Email__FrontendUrl=http://localhost:5173
Cors__AllowedOrigins__0=http://localhost:5173
Swagger__Enabled=false
CaseCache__AbsoluteExpirationSeconds=300
CaseCache__SlidingExpirationSeconds=60
Jwt__Secret=replace-with-at-least-32-characters
Jwt__Issuer=SirLocked
Jwt__Audience=SirLockedUsers
OpenAI__ApiKey=
OpenAI__LogicModel=gpt-5.6-sol
OpenAI__ImageModel=gpt-image-2
OpenAI__CutoutImageModel=gpt-image-1.5
OpenAI__BaseUrl=https://api.openai.com/v1
OpenAI__TimeoutSeconds=900
```

`OpenAI__ApiKey` is required for the AI case creator. Keep real keys in local `.env` files or deployment secrets only.
Paid case creation also requires AI quota and dated model prices. Cloudinary storage is required when generating images; JSON-only testing can leave it disabled. See [AI case setup and repair workflow](docs/AI_CASE_SETUP_VI.md) and the [5 USD JSON-only configuration example](config/ai-generation.json-only.example.json).
Swagger is always available in `Development`; outside Development it is disabled unless `Swagger__Enabled=true` is explicitly configured.
The case cache is process-local and intended for the current single-instance deployment. Use a distributed cache or coordinated invalidation before scaling the API to multiple instances.

### Playtest telemetry

Playtest telemetry is off by default. It is written only when `GameplayV3__Enabled` **and** `GameplayV3__PlaytestInstrumentationEnabled` are both `true`, and only for cases running the V3 paired-confrontation mechanics; otherwise the no-op sink stays registered and nothing is stored.

- No raw identifiers are persisted. Rooms become `sessionPseudonym` and players become `userHash`, both HMAC-SHA256 values keyed by `Playtest__PseudonymKey`. The user hash is salted with the room, so the same person in two rooms cannot be linked.
- `Playtest__PseudonymKey` must be at least 32 characters. Outside `Development` the API refuses to start without it; in `Development` a random per-process key is generated and a warning is logged.
- Documents live in the `playtestEvents` collection and are deleted automatically by a TTL index after `Playtest__RetentionDays` days (default 30). Keep this at or below 90 days.
- Aggregates are readable by admins at `GET /api/admin/playtest/summary?from=&to=` (UTC ISO, defaults to the last 7 days, maximum 90); the endpoint returns 404 while instrumentation is off. A summary folds at most 200,000 events; past that it answers `isTruncated: true` with `eventCount` so a wide window degrades instead of loading an unbounded result set.
- `POST /api/game/rooms/{roomId}/playtest-events` is limited to 120 accepted calls per minute per user; the UI emits far fewer, and the cap keeps a looping client from inflating the collection.

### Accusation consensus

The final accusation is the one decision that ends the match, so on V3 cases it takes both detectives. One player writes the whole proposal and the other reviews it as a block:

- `POST /api/game/rooms/{roomId}/accusation` opens a proposal. Writing it counts as its author's confirmation.
- `PUT /api/game/rooms/{roomId}/accusation/{attemptId}` amends it. The revision increments, every earlier confirmation is voided, and the editor becomes the only confirmer of the new revision.
- `POST /api/game/rooms/{roomId}/accusation/{attemptId}/confirm` agrees to a revision. Every command carries `expectedRevision`; confirming a revision that has since been edited returns 409 `ACCUSATION_STALE_REVISION` instead of silently agreeing to something else. Confirming twice is a harmless retry.
- `POST /api/game/rooms/{roomId}/accusation/{attemptId}/cancel` withdraws the proposal and lets either player start a new one.

The case ends the moment both players have confirmed the same revision. That final confirmation and the completed room are written together under the existing `gameplayState.version` check, so two simultaneous confirmations still produce exactly one `gameResults` document; the losing request gets a coded 409.

A proposal is reviewed by both players, but its evidence ids still respect the V3 knowledge boundary. A claim backed by a clue only the proposer discovered reaches the partner with `evidenceId: null` and `isUndisclosed: true`, so the partner sees the full shape of the accusation without being handed an id the paired-confrontation disclosure path never gave them.

`Accusation__RequireConsensus` decides who is subject to this. Leave it unset (the default) to follow the case: V3 cases require consensus

viruztt/subscroll.desc: Every game you already pay for, in one place. Desktop app showing which games are in Game Pass, PS Plus, Switch Online, EA Play, Ubisoft+, Netflix and Apple Arcade, by tier.
viruztt/subscroll.readme:
# Subscroll

**Every game you already pay for, in one place.**

![Browsing the Switch Online library](docs/screenshots/browse.jpg)

| Your played and completed games | Roll a game when you can't decide |
|---|---|
| ![My games](docs/screenshots/my-games.png) | ![Roll a game](docs/screenshots/roll.png) |

![Statistics](docs/screenshots/stats.png)

A desktop app that shows which games are in Xbox Game Pass, PlayStation Plus, Nintendo Switch Online, EA Play, Ubisoft+, Netflix Games and Apple Arcade, by tier. You pick the plans you have, mark games as played or completed, and see what's leaving soon. Everything you set is saved on your PC, in `%APPDATA%\Subscription Catalogue` (the app's earlier name).

## Install

1. Download the latest `Subscroll-<version>.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/viruztt/subscroll/releases).
2. Double-click it. There's no installer; the exe is the whole app, so keep it wherever you like.
3. The first time, Windows may say "Windows protected your PC", because the app isn't signed with a paid certificate. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

Your plans and marks stay on your PC and carry over when you download a newer version. To move them to another PC, use **Save backup** in Settings.

## Where the game lists come from

| Service | Source | Leaving dates |
|---|---|---|
| Xbox Game Pass (Essential, Premium, Ultimate, PC) | Microsoft's catalogue service (`catalog.gamepass.com` + `displaycatalog.mp.microsoft.com`), the same lists xbox.com uses | Microsoft's "leaving soon" list flags games, but has no date |
| PlayStation Plus (Essential monthly games, Extra catalogue, Premium classics) | playstation.com's game lists (`/bin/imagic/gameslist`) | Not published in any feed |
| Nintendo Switch Online (+ Expansion Pack) | Wikipedia's [Nintendo Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Classics) article, which lists every game per system with the date it was added (Nintendo has no feed). Box art comes from [libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails) via the GitHub API | Games almost never leave |
| EA Play, Ubisoft+ (Classics, Premium) | Microsoft's catalogue service, which lists both subscriptions' Xbox and Microsoft Store editions (`eaaccess`, `nakuconsole`/`nakupc`, `ubisoftplus`) | None |
| Netflix Games | Netflix's own developer account on the App Store (Apple's public lookup API). Games published under a partner's account and TV-only cloud games are missing | None |
| Apple Arcade | Wikipedia's [Apple Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Arcade) article. Icons, descriptions and screenshots come from Apple's App Store search, a few games a minute in the background (Apple limits it), cached in `catalog/appstore/` | None |

If a live source fails, the app falls back to community mirrors on GitHub ([catabox](https://github.com/nanhopper/catabox), [ps-plus-games-list](https://github.com/ppazour/ps-plus-games-list)), and if those fail too it keeps the last list it had. A snapshot ships with the app so it works offline from the first launch.

Game Pass Ultimate includes EA Play and Ubisoft+ Classics, and PC Game Pass includes EA Play, so those games count as in your plans when you have Ultimate or PC Game Pass.

A game offered by several services gets one card with a tag for each (dimmed when it's not in your plans), so A Way Out shows once with Game Pass, EA Play and PS Plus. Titles are matched ignoring platform suffixes and edition names; Switch Online games are kept apart, since each is a specific old console version, except for regional versions of the same game ("Adventures of Lolo (NA)" and "(JP)"), which share one card marked NA + JP. Marking the game marks it everywhere.

The **Coming soon** page lists announced games with their date: Game Pass from Microsoft's per-plan join dates, Switch Online and Apple Arcade from dates in their Wikipedia lists. PS Plus, EA Play, Ubisoft+ and Netflix don't publish dates in a form the app can read.

Catalogues refresh automatically once a day, including while the window is closed: Subscroll stays in the system tray (right-click the icon to refresh, turn options on or off, or quit) and can start with Windows, minimised to the tray. After each refresh it sends a notification when games join a service in your plans or games in your plans start leaving, leaving out games you've completed or ignored; clicking it opens the right page. These are under **Background** in Settings. Every refresh is compared with the previous one, so the "New & departed" page shows what was added and what left.

Clicking a game shows a short description and a few screenshots. Game Pass gets both from Microsoft's catalogue; PS Plus reads the game's PlayStation Store page; Switch Online games get title screens and gameplay shots from libretro-thumbnails and the opening of the game's Wikipedia article. Looked-up details are cached for 30 days in `details.json`.

The toolbar filters by service, played status, platform, **genre** and **length** (under 5 or 10 hours, 10 to 20, 20 to 40, over 40, by How Long To Beat's main story). Each store names genres differently, so they're mapped onto one list (`renderer/genres.js`); Switch Online games count as Retro. The length filter only shows games that have a time.

Cards show the **Metacritic** score and the **How Long To Beat** main-story time, and the list can be sorted by score or from shortest to longest. # Arknights Tier List VN

Phiên bản tiếng Việt (không chính thức) của [An Arknights Operator Tier List](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1E7HmgKWiV8pKpJpvpVzziYxnaQTP01Vtw_PXEdL7XPA/), kèm thông tin chi tiết từng operator (Trait, chỉ số E2, Skill M3, Talent, range) đã dịch sang tiếng Việt.

Web tĩnh, không cần build: mở bằng bất kỳ static server nào.

```bash
python -m http.server 8765
```

## Cấu trúc

| File | Nội dung |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Toàn bộ giao diện (HTML + CSS + JS) |
| `data.js` | Tier list + nhận xét (từ Google Sheet) |
| `details.js` | Thông tin chi tiết operator đã dịch (sinh bởi `_build/build_details.py`) |
| `glossary.js` | Từ điển thuật ngữ cho tooltip |
| `TRANSLATION_GUIDE.md` | Guideline dịch thuật |
| `i18n/` | Bản dịch tiếng Việt theo từng đợt |
| `_build/` | Script trích xuất & build dữ liệu |

## Cập nhật dữ liệu operator

```bash
B=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArknightsAssets/ArknightsGamedata/master/en/gamedata/excel
for t in character_table skill_table handbook_team_table uniequip_table char_patch_table range_table; do curl -sL "$B/$t.json" -o _build/n_$t.json; done
python _build/extract.py && python _build/build_details.py
```

Đoạn mô tả mới chưa có bản dịch sẽ hiển thị tiếng Anh cho tới khi được thêm vào `i18n/`.

## Nguồn

- Tier list & nhận xét: nhóm tác giả AK Tier List ([X](https://x.com/AKTierList) · [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/aktierlist.bsky.social)).
- Dữ liệu game: [ArknightsAssets/ArknightsGamedata](https://github.com/ArknightsAssets/ArknightsGamedata).
- Hình ảnh: [yuanyan3060/ArknightsGameResource](https://github.com/yuanyan3060/ArknightsGameResource).

Arknights © Hypergryph / Yostar. Dự án fan, phi thương mại.

juricmatej/palmetto-run.readme:
# Palmetto Run

**Play now:** https://palmetto-run.palleto.workers.dev

A neon open-world crime sandbox that runs in the browser. Steal cars, fly an attack helicopter or a fighter jet, run missions, rob the casino, pull a co-op bank heist, and fight your friends in real time. Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) r128 and plain JavaScript: no framework, no bundler, no dependencies.

The game is published as a **Claude Artifact**, which gives it live multiplayer. It also runs as a normal web page (single-player).

> Mature themes: guns, gangs, a strip club, gambling, and drug and alcohol use as game mechanics.

## Play

| Where | Multiplayer | How |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudflare (public site) | Yes, one shared lobby for everyone | https://palmetto-run.palleto.workers.dev (no account needed) |
| Claude Artifact | Yes, everyone with the page open shares one city | Open the artifact link (must be signed in to Claude and have access) |
| Locally with the lobby | Yes | `npm run preview`, then open http://localhost:8787 in two tabs |
| Locally, quick | No (solo) | `npm run dev`, then open http://localhost:8080 |

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Mouse | Look and aim (click the game to lock the mouse, Esc to free it) |
| WASD / arrows | Walk or drive |
| E | Steal or leave a vehicle, use things indoors, climb ladders |
| Click / Space | Shoot |
| Shift | Sprint or handbrake |
| Hold Tab | Weapon wheel (or 1–8 / Q) |
| Right-click / Z | Sniper scope |
| G | Detonate sticky bombs |
| Space / Shift | Helicopter or jet up / down |
| X | Flares (break missile locks) |
| N | Use white powder (super strength) |
| M | Sound on/off |

Phones get an on-screen joystick and buttons.

## Develop

Requires Node 18 or newer. There is nothing to install.

```bash
npm run dev     # build, then serve dist/ on http://localhost:8080
npm run check   # syntax-check the game code
npm run build   # write dist/artifact.html, dist/index.html and dist/2d.html
```

Edit files in `src/`, then run `npm run dev` again and reload the page.

### Project layout

```
src/
  page.html     HTML markup: HUD, menus, start screen. Contains /*@@STYLE@@*/ and /*@@SCRIPT@@*/ placeholders
  style.css     All CSS
  game.js       The whole game (one IIFE)
legacy/
  palmetto-run-2d.html   The original top-down 2D version (separate artifact)
worker/
  index.js      Cloudflare Worker: serves dist/ and runs the multiplayer lobby
scripts/
  build.mjs     Inlines style.css and game.js into page.html
  check.mjs     Syntax check
  serve.mjs     Local static server
dist/           Build output (not committed)
```

### How `game.js` is organized

The file is split into sections marked `// ---------- name ----------`. Search for these to find your way around:

| Section | What it does |
|---|---|
| world | Map grid (`N`×`N` blocks of size `B`), districts, building generation, collision |
| state | Player, interiors (`mkRoom`), doors, interaction spots |
| cars, peds | Traffic AI on the road grid, parked cars, pedestrians |
| Rustwater Vipers / Low Palms Kings | Gang spawning (`gangPop`) and AI (`gangStep`) |
| combat | Bullets, rockets, explosions, damage |
| attack helicopter, fighter jets | Flight models and weapons |
| robberies, sticky bombs, blackjack, roulette, slots, Union Job | Activities |
| jobs | Mission types (`newJob`, `jobStep`) |
| input | Keyboard, mouse, pointer lock, touch |
| multiplayer | Claude `room` inside the artifact, or `wsRoom()` (the Cloudflare lobby) elsewhere |
| ui | HUD, hints, menus |
| update | Main simulation step |
| 3D scene, models | Three.js scene, procedural meshes, static batching (`staticBatch`) |
| minimap, boot | Radar and startup |

Coordinates: game logic is 2D on the ground plane (`x`, `y`) with a separate height `z`. In Three.js that maps to `(x, z, y)`.

### Multiplayer

When the page runs inside Claude, `window.claude.use('room')` returns a live room. Each player publishes a small presence object about 15 times a second: position, vehicle, health, last shot, damage dealt to others, heist progress and so on. Every client simulates its own traffic and pedestrians. Damage is decided by the shooter and applied by the victim when they see it in the shooter's presence. Outside Claude, `room` is unavailable and the game runs solo. The badge above the minimap shows the reason.

## Publish as a Claude Artifact

The artifact is a single HTML page. `npm run build` produces it as `dist/artifact.html`.

**Update the existing artifact (keeps the same link)**

1. `npm run build`
2. In Claude Code (desktop app or CLI), opened in this folder, ask:
   > Publish dist/artifact.html to https://claude.ai/artifact/3pU67sVhffYYZVpghHwU3S

   Claude reads the current version, then republishes. The `room` capability (multiplayer) is kept automatically.

Only the artifact's owner, or someone the owner gave **edit** access to, can update that link.

**Publish your own copy (contributors)**

1. `npm run build`
2. In Claude Code, ask:
   > Publish dist/artifact.html as a new artifact with the `room` capability

The `room` capability is what turns on multiplayer. Without it the artifact runs solo.

**Playing with friends:** in the artifact's **Share** menu, invite each friend by email. Friends must be signed in to Claude. Visitors who arrive through a public link cannot join the shared room.

## Host it on Cloudflare (free, with multiplayer)

`worker/index.js` is a Cloudflare Worker that serves `dist/` and runs **one shared lobby** in a Durable Object at `/ws`. When the game is not running inside Claude, it connects there automatically (`wsRoom()` in `game.js`).

```bash
npx wrangler login   # once
npm run deploy       # builds and deploys
```

`npm run preview` runs the same thing locally on http://localhost:8787. Configuration is in `wrangler.jsonc`. The lobby holds up to 32 players.

### Automatic deploys

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys to Cloudflare on every push to `main`, which includes merged pull reques

# Projet VR EVA — Escape game sous-marin

Escape game VR mono-joueur pour l'arène **EVA** (piste 31 × 16,5 m), sur **Meta Quest 2**.
Projet d'évaluation de fin de module, en binôme.

## Démarrer

1. Installer **Unity 6000.3.23f1** (6.3 LTS) avec le module **Android Build Support** (OpenJDK + SDK/NDK).
2. Installer Git LFS **avant** de cloner :
   ```bash
   brew install git-lfs && git lfs install
   ```
3. Cloner puis ouvrir le dossier `Projet/` dans Unity Hub.
4. (Recommandé) Activer le Smart Merge Unity pour les scènes/prefabs :
   ```bash
   git config merge.unityyamlmerge.name "Unity SmartMerge"
   git config merge.unityyamlmerge.driver "'/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/6000.3.23f1/Unity.app/Contents/Helpers/UnityYAMLMerge' merge -p %O %B %A %A"
   git config merge.unityyamlmerge.recursive binary
   ```
   (Windows : `C:/Program Files/Unity/Hub/Editor/6000.3.23f1/Editor/Data/Tools/UnityYAMLMerge.exe`)

## Règles de travail en binôme

- **Une scène = un propriétaire à la fois.** Prévenir l'autre avant de modifier une scène partagée ; travailler de préférence dans des **prefabs** ou des scènes de niveau séparées (chargement additif).
- Branches courtes : `feat/<sujet>`, merge sur `main` dès que ça marche sur le casque.
- `git pull` avant de commencer, commit + push en fin de session.
- Ne jamais commiter `Library/`, les builds (`.apk`) ou les réglages perso — le `.gitignore` s'en charge.
- Vérifier Unity : *Project Settings → Editor* → **Asset Serialization = Force Text**, **Version Control = Visible Meta Files**.

| [CONSIGNES.md](CONSIGNES.md) | Énoncé et contraintes à respecter |

Kalaith/auto_resolved.readme:
# Auto-Resolved

You are starting your IT career the same week PATCH, a new AI assistant, is
released. Keep a multi-floor office running: walk the floors, ride the
elevator, fix what breaks, and decide how much to trust PATCH. Stay until you
quit or are fired, spend what you earned upgrading PATCH, and take the next
job: a bigger company, better pay, a building that looks nothing like the last.

- Design: [Auto_Resolved_Game_Design_Document.md](Auto_Resolved_Game_Design_Document.md)
- Plan and architecture: [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md)
- Agent rules: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)

Godot 4.2.2, Compatibility renderer, web and Windows exports.

## Setup

The shared toolkit must be linked once (a junction, ignored by Git):

```powershell
..\godot_toolkit\tools\Link-Toolkit.ps1 -ProjectDir .
```

## Run

```powershell
.\Run.ps1
```

The game opens on the title: start a new career or continue one. Each job
is a run of workdays; at the end of a day you can hand in notice, and every
job ends with an exit interview, PATCH's update and the job board.

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Click / tap | Walk there, riding the lift if needed; tap a broken device to fix it, a person to see their card |
| A / D, arrows | Walk |
| E, Space | Fix what is beside you; at the lift: call it, board, or go to the picked floor; at the IT desk: open PATCH |
| W / S | Inside the lift: pick a floor |
| Ticket list | Tap a ticket to walk to the nearest place to fix it; AI asks PATCH about it |
| PATCH button | Talk to PATCH: a ticket, a recurring category, the queue, running automations |
| Incident alert | Open the incident view: timeline, recoveries, guardrails |
| Eat button, kitchen fridge / vending | Eat (resets hunger, calms you down; costs office time) |
| Games button (in the IT office) | Play games at the IT desk: a big stress drop for 30 office minutes |
| P, 1 / 2 / 3 | Pause, normal, double, fast |
| Tab | Whole-building overview |
| Esc, Menu | Hand in notice, settings, quit to title |
| F1 / F2 / F6 (debug builds) | Force PATCH's next execution to succeed / backfire / pick the backfire |
| F3 / F4 (debug builds) | Open a random ticket / skip to the end of the day |

Your own state matters: every fix uses office minutes (the clock races
while you work), so a day only holds so many manual fixes. Fixes and a
backlog raise your stress, hunger makes it worse, and wandering about idle
outside the IT office costs confidence. The first job's first day has a
skippable tutorial.

The career saves to `user://career.json` at the end of each workday and at
every step between jobs.

## Checks

```powershell
$godot = '..\small_following\exports\tooling\Godot_v4.2.2-stable_win64_console.exe'
& $godot --headless --path . --editor --quit                          # import and parse
& $godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/sim_checks.gd       # behaviour checks
& $godot --path . --script res://tools/capture.gd -- captures --size=1280x720   # screenshots (--only=career|buildings|day|patch|menus)
& $godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/headcount_report.gd  # staff per archetype
& $godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/day_report.gd        # tickets vs hand-fixing capacity per day
```

Captures need a window (not `--headless`); write them outside the project or
under `docs/` so Godot does not import them.

## Publish

```powershell
.\publish.ps1 -BuildOnly    # export web + Windows to builds/, no deploy
.\publish.ps1 -DryRun       # show what a publish would do
```

# yaseen369.github.io

Personal portfolio of Yaseen Abdelrhman, live at **https://yaseen369.github.io**.

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks, build step or dependencies. Open `index.html` through any static server to run it locally:

```bash
python -m http.server 8000   # then visit http://localhost:8000
```

## Structure

```
index.html      page content and structure
css/style.css   all styles; colours, light and dark themes and fonts are CSS variables at the top
js/hero.js      particle name in the hero
js/demos.js     the four project demos
js/game.js      the "Fix my bugs" game
js/main.js      cursor, scroll effects, counters, contact interactions
js/interact.js  quiet interactions: tips, skills, headings, shortcuts
assets/         CV and Recrify screenshots
```

## How the interactive parts work

| Feature | File | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Particle name | `hero.js` | Draws "YASEEN" on a hidden canvas, samples its pixels into target points, then each frame springs every particle toward its target and pushes it away from the pointer. Pauses when the hero is off screen. |
| Recrify ranking demo | `demos.js` | Recomputes `resume × w + interview × (1 − w)` for each row, re-sorts the list, and animates rows to their new places with the FLIP technique and the Web Animations API. A second tab rebuilds the HR report table (same columns and summary sentence as the real report) and can download it as CSV through a `Blob`. |
| CleanCut demo | `demos.js` | A canvas waveform with word timestamps. A `requestAnimationFrame` loop moves the playhead, reveals words, and turns a Web Audio oscillator on over flagged words when sound is enabled. |
| Performance Tester demo | `demos.js` | "Run a test" plays a simulated load test (1, 5, 10 and 20 users) and draws average and 95th-percentile times on a canvas chart. "Real report" shows the summary of a real run from the tool's `Test results` folder. |
| Activity system demo | `demos.js` | A before/after view of the legacy servlet design and the layered refactor. Class names come from the real code; pressing a box explains what it does. |
| Dark mode | `index.html`, `main.js` | A small script in `<head>` picks the saved theme or the system setting before the first paint. The toggle (or the `D` key) switches the CSS variables and remembers the choice. |
| Horizontal project scroll | `main.js` | The section's height is set to the sideways distance plus one screen. A sticky container stays pinned while vertical scroll progress is mapped to `translateX`. |
| Word reveals, timeline fill | `main.js` | One `requestAnimationFrame`-throttled scroll handler reads positions with `getBoundingClientRect`. |
| Number counters | `main.js` | Each digit is a column of 0–9 that slides into place when it enters the screen (IntersectionObserver). |
| Contact headline | `main.js` | Each letter's variable-font weight and width depend on its distance from the cursor. |
| Custom cursor, magnetic buttons | `main.js` | Mouse-only, eased with linear interpolation each frame. |
| "Fix my bugs" game | `game.js` | A 15-second canvas game. Bugs come in five shapes, each tagged with a language and a real error, and each squash shows a joke about that error; hitting a feature gets you roasted. A coffee slows every bug for three seconds, and a "legacy code" boss takes four hits. Spawn rate and speed grow with time and board size. Combos, ranks, a personal best in `localStorage` and a share button (Web Share API, or clipboard as a fallback). |

### Quiet interactions (`interact.js`)

Nothing moves on its own; each effect answers a hover, focus, tap or key press.

- **Tips on tech tags and terms:** one floating tooltip, positioned above or below the element, shown on hover and keyboard focus, and tapped open on touch screens.
- **Skills to projects:** pointing at a skill lists the projects that use it, with links that scroll to them (and to the right panel inside the sideways section).
- **Headings:** letters near the pointer get lighter, using the variable font's weight axis.
- **Demo cards:** a 3° tilt and a soft light that follow the pointer, frozen while a button is held so clicks always land.
- **Numbers:** pointing at one rolls its digits again.
- **Reading progress:** a thin line at the top of the window.
- **Keyboard shortcuts:** press `?` to see them (W, E, G, C, T, D).

## Accessibility and performance

- Text content is real HTML and readable without JavaScript; the demos and the game need it.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` turns off the particle animation, horizontal scroll and transitions.
- The custom cursor appears only on devices with a fine pointer; touch devices get touch-friendly versions of every demo.
- Animation loops pause when their section is off screen.

# 🏎️ KART RACER

카트라이더 스타일의 3D 카트 레이싱 게임입니다 (three.js). 별도 설치나 빌드 없이 `index.html` 하나로 실행됩니다.

## 실행 방법
`index.html` 파일을 브라우저로 열면 바로 플레이할 수 있습니다. (PC 키보드 / 모바일 터치 모두 지원)
three.js를 CDN(cdnjs)에서 불러오므로 인터넷 연결이 필요합니다.

## 조작법
| 키 | 동작 |
|---|---|
| `↑` / `W` | 가속 |
| `↓` / `S` | 브레이크 / 후진 |
| `←` `→` / `A` `D` | 조향 |
| `Shift` | 드리프트 (방향키와 함께) |
| `Ctrl` / `Z` | 니트로 부스터 사용 |
| `Space` / `X` | 아이템 사용 (아이템전, 모바일: 아이템 버튼) |
| `T` / `Backspace` | 잔디·벽에 걸렸을 때 트랙 복귀 (모바일: 복귀 버튼) |
| `R` | 재시작 |
| `Esc` | 메뉴 |
| `M` | 소리 켜기/끄기 |

## 친구와 함께 (멀티플레이)
1. 메뉴에서 **친구와 함께** → 이름 입력 → **방 만들기**
2. **링크 복사**로 초대 링크를 친구에게 보내기 (또는 5자리 초대 코드 알려주기)
3. 친구가 링크를 열고 **참가하기** → 방장이 트랙을 고르고 **레이스 시작**

- 최대 6명, 빈자리는 컴퓨터 레이서로 채울 수 있어요.
- 서버 없이 브라우저끼리 직접 연결합니다 (PeerJS/WebRTC, 연결 중개는 PeerJS 공개 서버 사용). 방장 브라우저를 닫으면 방이 끝나요.
- 회사·학교 네트워크처럼 P2P 연결을 막는 곳에서는 연결이 안 될 수 있어요.

## 아이템전 / 스피드전
메뉴의 **모드**에서 고를 수 있어요 (기본: 아이템전). 트랙 3곳에 있는 **? 상자**를 지나가면 아이템을 얻고, 최대 2개까지 보관합니다. 순위가 낮을수록 강한 아이템이 잘 나와요.

| 아이템 | 효과 |
|---|---|
| 🚀 부스터 | 즉시 가속 |
| 🍌 바나나 | 뒤에 떨어뜨림 — 밟은 카트는 빙글빙글 미끄러짐 |
| 💧 물폭탄 | 앞으로 던짐 — 떨어진 자리의 카트를 물방울에 가둠 |
| 🎯 미사일 | 바로 앞 순위 카트를 추적 — 맞으면 공중제비 |
| 🛡️ 실드 | 6초 동안 공격 한 번을 막음 |

## 부스터 & 효과
- **드리프트 2단계 순간 부스터**: 0.5초 이상 유지하면 파란 불꽃, 1.2초 이상이면 주황 불꽃 → 떼는 순간 더 강한 부스터
- **슬립스트림**: 앞차 바로 뒤에 붙어 달리면 바람 효과와 함께 부스터
- **점프대 & 착지 부스터**: 트랙마다 점프대가 하나 있어요
- 부스터 스피드 라인, 미사일 경고, 폭발·물보라·꽃가루 효과

## 게임 특징
- **캐릭터 5종** (방울·토끼·곰·고양이·로봇 후드)과 **카트 4종** 선택 — 레이스 상황에 따라 표정이 바뀌어요 (부스터: 신남, 충돌: 화남, 복귀: 슬픔)
  - 레이서: 균형형 / 포뮬러: 최고속도↑ 가속↓ / 버기: 잔디에서 빠름 / 클래식: 가속·부스터 충전↑
- **드리프트 & 부스터 게이지**: 드리프트하면 게이지가 차고, 가득 차면 니트로를 1개 얻습니다 (최대 2개).
- **순간 부스터**: 드리프트를 0.4초 이상 유지한 뒤 떼면 짧은 가속.
- **출발 부스터**: 카운트다운 GO 직전에 가속키를 누르면 빠르게 출발.
- **부스터 패드**: 트랙 위 파란 화살표 패드를 밟으면 가속.
- 3개 트랙 (숲속 서킷 / 사막 캐니언 / 설원 스피드웨이), 3단계 난이도, 5명의 AI 라이벌
- 3랩 레이스, 실시간 순위, 미니맵, 랩 타임, 트랙별 최고 기록 저장
- 3인칭 추적 카메라, 실시간 그림자와 조명, 아스팔트/잔디/모래/눈 텍스처
- 빨강·흰색 연석, 가드레일, 타이어 방벽, 출발 신호등 게이트, 관중석, 광고판
- 스키드 마크, 타이어 연기, 부스터 불꽃, 효과음 (Web Audio)

## Vercel 배포
빌드 과정이 없는 정적 사이트라서 설정 파일 없이 바로 배포됩니다.

1. https://vercel.com/new 에서 GitHub 저장소 `hungungworld/kart-racer`를 Import 합니다.
2. Framework Preset은 **Other**, Build Command와 Output Directory는 비워 둡니다 (루트의 `index.html`이 그대로 서비스됩니다).
3. **Deploy**를 누르면 끝. 이후 `main` 브랜치에 푸시할 때마다 자동으로 다시 배포됩니다.

CLI를 쓰는 경우: 저장소 폴더에서 `npx vercel` (미리보기) 또는 `npx vercel --prod` (프로덕션).

## 파일 구성
| 파일 | 설명 |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | 게임 전체 (HTML·CSS·JS 한 파일, three.js는 cdnjs에서 로드) |
