yasserreslan/simcore.desc: Deterministic lockstep simulation core for an RTS game
yasserreslan/simcore.readme:
# simcore

The deterministic simulation core of a classic-style RTS: the whole game
minus graphics, sound and input. A renderer (Godot 4 .NET or similar) reads
the world and draws it; it never changes it.

Every machine in a match runs its own copy of the sim. Players exchange only
commands, scheduled for a future tick. Same starting world + same commands =
bit-identical world on every tick, on every OS and CPU. That's what makes
lockstep multiplayer and replays work.

The core was ported bit-exactly from Go to C#; since then the sim runs from
data (see [Content model](#content-model)) and the golden replay is a
Phase 1 battle recorded by the C# sim.

## Run it

Run these from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet test                                                # all tests, including the 10-minute replay gate
dotnet run --project src/SimRun                            # bot vs bot, prints the map each minute
dotnet run --project src/SimRun -- -every 20 -ticks 2400   # watch every second for 2 minutes
dotnet run --project src/SimRun -- -save m.json            # save the replay
dotnet run --project src/SimRun -- -replay m.json          # play it back
```

SimRun also takes `-seed N`, `-content DIR` (default `content/mvp`) and
`-setup FILE` (the lobby file, default `content/setups/battle.json`). In the
text view each unit is its archetype's glyph from the content, player 1
uppercase and player 2 lowercase: `A` assault, `E` engineer, `K` anti-armor,
`S` sniper, `B` dirt bike, `T` technical, `L` / `M` / `H` light, medium and
heavy rocket launchers, `Q` heavy rocket truck, `W` twin missile truck, `C` cargo truck, `D` supply depot, `F` FPV drone, `^`
trap (shown to the observer even when hidden), `*` rocket in flight, `#`
rock. Drivers are inside their vehicles and not drawn.

The library targets `net8.0` (what Godot 4 uses) and `net10.0`; SimRun and
the tests target `net10.0`.

### Benchmarks

```bash
dotnet run -c Release --project src/SimRun -- -bench 500 -out bench/run_500.json
python3 bench/compare.py --before bench/baseline_*.json --after bench/index_*.json
```

`-bench N[,N...]` runs six workloads (`stationary`, `movement`, `combat`,
`projectiles`, `churn`, `obstacles`; pick with `-workloads`) at each unit count on
worlds it builds itself, for at most `-maxticks` ticks (400) or `-budget` seconds
(8) each, and writes JSON: tick time (p50/p95/p99/max), time per system (through
`World.Probe`, an `IStepProbe` called after every system), `World.Hash()` time,
bytes allocated per tick and path searches per tick (`World.PathRequests`).
Neither the probe nor the counter is game state; neither is hashed.
`bench/baseline_*.json` is main before the spatial index, `bench/index_*.json`
after it.

### Spatial index

Vision (detection and spotting), target acquisition, splash and projectile hits
look units up in a uniform grid of 8-cell buckets (`Sim/SpatialIndex.cs`,
`Sim/Spatial.cs`) instead of scanning every unit. It is scratch space, rebuilt
from the unit list (in ID order) before vision and before combat, never hashed.
It only narrows the candidates: each system still applies its exact test, in an
order that gives the same result as the old full scan (ID order where order
matters, or an explicit ID tie-break). `SpatialIndexTests` replays random dense
worlds and the golden battle with and without it (`World.FullScan`) and checks
the hashes agree on every tick.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/SimCore/FixedPoint` | Fixed-point math (1 cell = 1024 units), vectors, 32 facings |
| `src/SimCore/Rng` | Seeded SplitMix64; the only randomness allowed |
| `src/SimCore/Model` | The compiled content model (archetypes, components, warheads, factions), match setups and per-player unit definitions |
| `src/SimCore/Content` | Loads and checks content JSON files into a `ContentSet` (IO; runs before a match) |
| `src/SimCore/Sim` | World, units, commands, pathfinding (A*), targeting, hashing |
| `src/SimCore/Sim/Systems` | One file per system, run every tick in a fixed order (below) |
| `src/SimCore/Scenarios` | Starting maps; `battle` is the 96×96 Phase 1 two-player map, `sandbox` the same map with spawning on |
| `src/SimCore/Bots` | Scripted random player for recording test matches |
| `src/SimCore/Replays` | Record, save, load and play matches; read lobby files |
| `src/SimRun` | Headless runner with a text map view, and the benchmark (`Bench.cs`) |
| `bench` | Benchmark results (JSON) and `compare.py` |
| `content/mvp` | The MVP Resistance roster as data |
| `content/setups` | Lobby files: each player's faction, presets and starting army |
| `tests/SimCore.Tests` | xUnit tests; `testdata/` holds the golden replay |

## Content model

Every unit is assembled from data, as designed in
[docs/design.md](docs/design.md#content-model). Content is every `*.json`
file under a directory (`content/mvp`), in any split; unknown fields are
errors, comments are allowed. Distances are in tenths of a cell, speeds in
tenths of a cell per second, times in ticks (20 per second), percents 0–100.

- **Armor classes and warheads** (`warheads.json`): the design's damage
  table. `null` means the warhead cannot target that armor class.
- **Archetypes**: a base body: tags, locomotor (`flying` puts it on the air
  layer), armor class, HP, speed, vision, trap detection, lifetime, fixed
  `components`, and for infantry the `slots` (`primary`, `secondary`) listing
  what a preset may pick for each. Vehicles have a `crew` driver seat.
- **Components**: parts with typed effects. Each effect kind is run by one
  system: `weapon` (combat and projectiles), `placer` and `launch`
  (abilities), `strike` (drones), `trigger` (traps), `supply`, `repair`,
  `modifier` (perks, applied when the match starts). `aura`, `builder` and
  `buildAssist` load but have no system until Phase 2. `placeholder: true`
  marks a stand-in for an undecided design choice (the pistol).
- **Factions**: allowed archetypes and pickable components, st

Akinaru/PokeAgents.readme:
PokeAgents

🇬🇧 English · 🇫🇷 Français · 🇪🇸 Español · 🇩🇪 Deutsch · 🇮🇹 Italiano · 🇧🇷 Português · 🇯🇵 日本語 · 🇨🇳 简体中文

Your Claude Code agents become pixel-art creatures working along a route, DS-game style.

Installation • Getting started • What you see • Settings • Development • Credits and legal notices

> **Unofficial fan project.** PokeAgents is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nintendo, Creatures Inc., GAME FREAK inc. or The Pokémon Company, nor by Anthropic. Pokémon and character names are trademarks of their respective owners. The repository contains no images taken from the games. See [Credits and legal notices](#credits-and-legal-notices). ## What is it? PokeAgents is a VS Code extension (plus a small standalone server) that shows every [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) session as a creature on a pixel-art route: - **Every agent gets its own Pokémon**, drawn at random and different every day. Rare species are rare here too, and one agent in 64 is shiny. - **It evolves as its context fills up**: first evolution at 30% of the context, second at 60%. - **It moves around based on what it is doing**: it reads the route sign, searches the tall grass, cuts down a tree or smashes a rock. - **It sleeps while it waits.** You can tell at a glance who is working, who is done and who is waiting for your answer. - **One click opens its battle screen**, with a summary of its session: context, tools used, log and stats. - **Wild creatures** wander along the route and sometimes come over to visit your agents. PokeAgents is a fork of [Pixel Agents](https://github.com/pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents) (MIT license), which showed agents in an office. ## Installation ### Requirements - **VS Code 1.105** or later. - **Claude Code** installed and signed in: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, then run `claude` once. - **Node.js 20** or later, only to install from source or to use the standalone server. - An **Internet connection**: creature sprites are downloaded on first use, then cached in `~/.pokeagents/pokemon`. ### Option 1 — From the VS Code Marketplace (recommended) In VS Code, open the **Extensions** view, search for "PokeAgents" and click **Install**. Or from the command line: `code --install-extension akinaru.pokeagents`. Extension page: [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=akinaru.pokeagents). ### Option 2 — From a `.vsix` file 1. Download the latest `pokeagents-x.y.z.vsix` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Akinaru/PokeAgents/releases). 2. Install it: ```bash code --install-extension pokeagents-x.y.z.vsix ``` Or in VS Code: **Extensions** view → **⋯** menu → **Install from VSIX…** 3. Reload the window if VS Code asks you to. ### Option 3 — From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/Akinaru/PokeAgents.git cd PokeAgents npm install npm run package # production build npx @vscode/vsce package # creates pokeagents-x.y.z.vsix code --install-extension pokeagents-*.vsix ``` To try it without installing: open the folder in VS Code and press **F5**. An "Extension Development Host" window opens with PokeAgents loaded. ### Option 4 — Standalone server (browser) To follow your agents outside VS Code (tmux, a plain terminal, another editor): ```bash npm install && npm run compile node dist/cli.js --port 3100 ``` Open the address it prints (`http://127.0.0.1:3100/?token=…`). **Keep this address to yourself**: the token it contains lets anyone change your Claude Code settings. ## Getting started 1. Open the Command Palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+P` elsewhere) and run **PokeAgents: Show Panel**. The panel opens at the bottom of VS Code. 2. On first launch, a guide walks you through the interface. It offers to turn on **instant detection**: PokeAgents then adds hooks to `~/.claude/settings.json` so it hears about what your agents are doing in real time. - The guide shows everything that will be changed before asking for your consent. - If you decline, PokeAgents reads Claude Code's transcripts instead. That works too, with a little delay. - You can turn the hooks on or remove them at any time in the settings. 3. Start an agent: - with the **"+ Agent" Poké Ball** in the bottom bar, which opens a Claude Code terminal; - or by running `claude` in any terminal in the project. 4. Its Pokémon appears on a tree stump, then heads off to work when the agent uses its tools. ## What you see The panel's interface is currently in French. The labels below are written exactly as they appear on screen, with their English meaning in parentheses. ### The route Every agent wears a nametag with its project name and a status pill: | Status | Meaning | | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | **ACT** | Active: the agent is working. | | **ATT** | Waiting (_attente_): it needs your permission to run a tool. | | **FINI** | Finished: it has just completed its task. | | **SOM** | Asleep (_sommeil_): it is idle; its Pokémon sleeps in place. | A working agent moves to a new spot every 10 to 20 seconds. The spot depends on the tool it is using: | Agent's tool

AlessioCarta/innerclock.readme:
InnerClock ⏱️

How accurate is your inner clock?
A daily social game: hold the button for exactly the time shown — with no timer on screen.
Everyone in the world gets the same five targets each day. Beat your friends.

``` ⏱️ InnerClock #12 — 431/500 🟪🟩🟨🟪🟩 Metronome 🟪 2.1s → 2.13s (+0.03) 🟩 3.8s → 3.67s (−0.13) ... Can you beat me? https://…/?vs=time_lord ``` ## Why it spreads | Mechanic | Why it works | |---|---| | **One daily puzzle, same for everyone** | Creates a shared conversation every day (the Wordle effect). | | **No-spoiler leaderboard** | Today's scores unlock only after you play — the BeReal "post to see" hook. | | **Emoji grid share** | Spoiler-free, copy-pasteable into any chat or social feed. | | **Challenge links** (`?vs=username`) | Every share is a 1v1 invitation with a head-to-head result and one-tap follow. | | **Friends board + reactions** 🔥🎯😂🫠⚡ | Social proof and a reason to come back and check. | | **Streaks** | Daily habit loop. | | **10-second rounds** | A full game takes under a minute. | ## Features - 🎯 5 rounds/day, from ~1s to ~15s, with tiers 🟪 Atomic (≤2%) · 🟩 Sharp (≤5%) · 🟨 Close (≤10%) · 🟧 Drifting (≤20%) · 🟥 Lost in time - 🌍 Live global leaderboard (Supabase Realtime) and a friends-only board - 👤 Zero-friction accounts: anonymous sign-in + username, optional email to sync devices - 🛡️ **Server-authoritative scoring** — Postgres recomputes targets and scores from the submitted holds; the score itself can’t be forged - 🙈 Row Level Security: you can't see today's results until you've submitted your own - 📱 Mobile-first, keyboard (Space) and touch, PWA-installable, works offline in guest mode - ✅ Tests that prove the JS and SQL scoring are bit-for-bit identical (via [PGlite](https://pglite.dev)) ## Quick start ```bash npm install npm run dev # guest mode: solo play + share, no backend needed npm test ``` ### Turn on the social layer (Supabase, free tier) 1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com). 2. **Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Anonymous sign-ins: enable.** 3. Apply the schema — either paste both files from `supabase/migrations/` (in order) into the SQL editor, or: ```bash npx supabase link --project-ref npx supabase db push ``` 4. `cp .env.example .env.local` and fill in the Project URL and anon key (Project Settings → API). 5. `npm run dev` — you now have accounts, leaderboards, friends and reactions. ### Deploy to GitHub Pages 1. Repo **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**. 2. Repo **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables**: add `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. 3. Push to `main`. The workflow runs the tests, builds, and deploys. 4. In Supabase **Authentication → URL Configuration**, add your Pages URL as Site URL. ## iOS app (Capacitor) The same code ships as a native iOS app with haptics, the native share sheet, story images and daily streak reminders. ```bash npm run ios:sync # pulls public config from GitHub variables, builds, syncs ios/ npm run ios:open # opens Xcode → pick your Team in Signing, then Product → Archive npm run app-icons # regenerate the app icon and splash (needs ffmpeg) ``` App Store requirements already covered: in-app account deletion, [privacy policy](public/privacy.html), username filter, report and block. Turnstile runs through the `captcha.html` bridge on the public site, because Cloudflare doesn't accept the `capacitor://` origin. ## How it works ``` src/core.js pure game logic (targets, scoring, share text) — shared by app & tests src/api.js Supabase calls (auth, results, leaderboard RPCs, realtime) src/main.js UI: home → play → results/leaderboard, profile sheet supabase/migrations/ …0001_game_functions.sql ic_targets / ic_score — mirror core.js exactly …0002_social.sql tables, RLS, triggers, leaderboard RPCs test/ node:test — core logic + JS⇄SQL parity on PGlite ``` Targets are derived from `SHA-256("innerclock::")` with integer math only, so the browser and Postgres compute identical values. Scores use integer milliseconds for the same reason. ## Security notes - Scores are recomputed in Postgres; results are immutable; RLS hides today's results, reactions and play status until you've played (covered by `test/social.test.js`). - Hold durations are measured in the browser, so a determined cheater can still submit perfect times. That's the honest limit of any reaction/timing game without server-side timing (network jitter would ruin accuracy). Treat the global board as casual. - Before launch, in Supabase: **enable CAPTCHA for sign-ins** (Auth → Attack Protection) and review **Auth rate limits** to slow down bot accounts. ## Roadmap ideas - [ ] Weekly leagues and seasonal badges - [ ] Shareable result image (OG card) per player/day - [ ] Push reminder before the day ends to save a streak - [ ] Group rooms (class, office, Discord server) - [ ] Hard mode: targets with two decimals, or "count backwards" PRs welcome! ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

laamella-gad/copter_duel_sloppy_edition.readme:
# Copter Duel Sloppy Edition

A two-player helicopter duel for the Commodore 64: yellow (joystick in port 2) and red (port 1) fight it out with
rockets in a cave.

[Download copterduel.prg](https://github.com/laamella-gad/copter_duel_sloppy_edition/raw/refs/heads/master/copterduel.prg)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Title screen](screenshots/title.png) | ![Start of a round](screenshots/start.png) |
| The title screen, with music and waving letters. | The start of a round: both copters on the ground. |
| ![Mid-round](screenshots/duel.png) | ![Explosion](screenshots/crash.png) |
| Yellow has lost a copter, red is low on energy. | An explosion against the cave wall. |

## Bonuses

Shoot a bonus with a rocket to pick it up. The four bonuses move to new places now and then.

| Letter | Bonus                                      |
|--------|--------------------------------------------|
| B      | 10 points (twice as common as the others)  |
| R      | 14 rockets, half a bar                     |
| E      | 10 energy, a little more than a rocket hit |

## Winning

The game ends when a player loses their last copter, and the other player wins. Points only count when both lose
their last copter at the same time: then the most points win. Every crash gives the other player 100 points, whatever
caused it, and each player slowly earns points over time.

## The original

"Copter Duel" was written in 1987 by Ronald Mayer and published as "mr-soft": a BASIC program with a
machine code engine. Copter Duel Sloppy Edition is a rewrite in C for [oscar64](https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64), made from a
disassembly of a tape image of the original. The tape image, the disassembly and the patched original are in the git
history up to commit 86dd7cd. `NOTES.md` has the details.

## Improvements

- The winner is decided right: the original read the end flag from the wrong address and always picked the player
  with the most points, even after a knockout.
- The copters have momentum instead of moving at a fixed speed.
- The playfield has been opened up a bit, it was too easy to crash.
- Touching the cave walls drains energy instead of crashing the copter at once.
- A rocket hit takes a third of the energy instead of crashing the copter, and the bonuses give more rockets and energy.
- Bonuses are easier to shoot: a rocket that overlaps one picks it up, with a little to spare.
- Rockets explode when they hit the cave walls.
- Crashes are more dramatic: the copter spins and flashes while it explodes, the background flashes on every explosion.
- New sounds: a whoosh when a rocket is fired, a bip when it picks up a bonus and a buzz while a copter touches
  a wall.
- The title screen plays music ("Gory Ghost") and its letters wave.
- Fixed engine quirks: copters stopped at the ground inconsistently, and rockets near the screen edges read memory
  past the screen.
- The whole program is now written in C (Oscar64 compatible)

## Building

Needs oscar64 and pucrunch; `make run` also needs VICE.

```sh
make        # copterduel.prg
make run    # build and start it in VICE
```

TheWishin/T5DROnline.readme:
# Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection Online — native Windows port

Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection (PS3, PlayStation Network release) running natively
on Windows. It is recompiled, not emulated. Online play between friends is
being built.

**No release zip is published yet (2026-10-16).** Until one is, see "Building
from source" at the end of this page.

<!-- players:start -->
**Test release. Expect bugs.** Please report them (see "Bug reports" below).

Deutsch: https://github.com/TheWishin/T5DROnline/blob/main/docs/README.de.md

## What is this?

- The PS3 game's program is translated to C++ ahead of time (static
  recompilation) and compiled into a normal Windows program. No emulator runs.
- The model is the same as
  [Tekken 6 Native Online](https://github.com/Ekspym/Tekken6-native-online).
  This repository and its releases contain **no part of the game**.
- You build the game on your own PC from **your own copy**: the PSN package
  (`.pkg`) and the license (`.rap`) from your own account. The launcher does
  this for you.
- Online play between friends (a lobby, the two PCs talk directly) is the goal.
  It is **not playable yet**. See "Online".

## Status (2026-10-16)

Tested on one development PC (Windows 11, 16-core Ryzen 9). Not yet tried on a
clean PC.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Start-up | Works. Boots, opens the window, reaches the title, menus, character select and fights. |
| Menus | 60 fps. |
| Fights | Run, but at about 30-45 fps, not 60. Being worked on. |
| Game modes | Arcade, Ghost, Versus (two players on one PC), Survival and Practice work in test runs. Options work too, but "Delete Save Data" does nothing. Gallery needs PSN and fails cleanly offline. |
| Fighters, stages | Render correctly. 14 fighters and 12 stages were tried. |
| Graphics glitches | Every fighter's face is dark (brown/black). Light see-through rectangles on floors/walls in some stages. Some background figures are flat white. |
| Music, sound effects | Work. Short drops can happen when the frame rate dips. |
| Movies | Intro and title movies play with sound. They slow down when the game runs under 60 fps. |
| Keyboard, Xbox pad | Work. |
| PlayStation pads, arcade sticks | Built in (`controls.ini`). Not yet tried on real hardware by a person. |
| Saving | Unreliable. The first save on a fresh profile can fail without a message. Saves worked in other tests. The in-game clock reads 1970. |
| Long sessions | Memory bug. After about two trips through the title screen, or about 3 minutes idle at the title, the screen can turn white or the game can crash. Restart the game. A fix is in progress. |
| Online play | In progress. Not playable yet. |
| Build from your copy | Works on the development PC (about 90 seconds). Not yet tried on a clean PC. |

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with DirectX 12, and a 64-bit CPU with SSE4.1 (practically
  every PC of the last 10+ years).
- RAM: the game used about 1.2 GB on the development PC. We have not tested
  small PCs. 8 GB or more is a safe guess.
- About 1.5 GB of free disk space. After the build it uses about 1.1 GB, plus
  the 90 MB zip.
- An internet connection during the first build. About 50 KB of public key data
  (two text files) is fetched from github.com. Nothing about you or your game is
  sent.
- **Your own copy** of the game, exactly this one:
  **TEKKEN 5 DARK RESURRECTION ONLINE, US PSN, `NPUB30009`, version 01.00**.
  - the package: `.pkg`, 619,430,240 bytes
  - the license: `.rap` (16 bytes), named
    `UP0700-NPUB30009_00-UPDATE0000010000.rap`
  - **Other versions are refused** (disc copies, other regions, other
    versions). The port is tied to this exact program.

You do **not** need Visual Studio, Git or Python. The zip brings its own Python
and its own compiler (clang-cl and lld-link from LLVM). The game's runtime comes
precompiled. Your PC only translates and compiles the code from your copy.

## Install and first build

1. Download the zip (`T5DR-Online-<version>.zip`, about 90 MB) from the
   Releases page: https://github.com/TheWishin/T5DROnline/releases
2. Extract **everything** into its own folder, for example `C:\T5DR`. Not into
   Program Files. Not from inside the zip viewer.
3. Start `T5DR Online.exe`. Windows may warn once (SmartScreen: the file is not
   signed). Click "More info", then "Run anyway".
4. **Build** tab: choose your `.pkg` and `.rap`. The launcher also looks in
   Downloads, Desktop and Documents. Both lines should get a green check.
5. Click **BUILD GAME**. The launcher:
   - checks your copy (a wrong version or wrong `.rap` is refused within
     seconds),
   - unpacks it into the `native` folder,
   - translates the game's code and compiles it on your PC.

   Time: about 90 seconds on the development PC (16 cores). On a typical PC we
   expect a few minutes (estimate, not measured). **Cancel** is safe: BUILD GAME
   continues where it stopped.
6. **Play** tab: type a name (optional) and click **PLAY**.

Everything the build makes stays in the `native` folder next to the launcher.
It is game data. Do not share it. To uninstall, delete the whole folder.

## Playing

- The game opens in its own window. It draws at 1280 x 720 and scales to the
  window. **Settings** has window sizes, maximized, borderless (experimental:
  not yet tested with the real game window) and mute.
- **Esc** closes the game. The **Stop game** button does too.
- Two players on one PC: connect a second pad, then choose Versus.
- Tips for now:
  - Go back to the title screen as little as you can (memory bug).
  - Do not leave the game idle at the title.
  - Do not use the game's own **Online** menu entry (see "Online").

## Controls

Keyboard (default) and Xbox controller:

mendezm87/monster-battle-stadium.readme:
# Monster Battle Stadium

A real-time, top-down monster battle game with HD pixel art, built with plain HTML5 Canvas + JavaScript (no build step, no dependencies).

You control your monster directly: move anywhere in the arena and fire off four moves (projectiles, beams, dashes, shockwaves, targeted strikes, buffs and heals). Each trainer brings a team of up to 6; knock out every enemy monster to win. Play against the CPU, against a friend on the same device, or online.

## Play

**▶ Play now: https://mendezm87.github.io/monster-battle-stadium/** (works on phone and desktop, no install)

To run it locally, open `index.html` in a browser, or serve the folder:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then visit http://localhost:8000
```

### Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | WASD / arrow keys | Left thumb-stick (appears where you touch) |
| Moves 1–4 | J K L ; (or 1–4, Space = move 1) | Move buttons (bottom right) |
| Swap monster | Q or Tab (next healthy teammate) | SWAP button, then tap a teammate |
| Pause | P / Esc (Esc only in 2-player) | Pause button |
| Mute | M | Title screen toggle |

Moves auto-aim at your opponent; the skill is in positioning and dodging.

### Online

Pick **Online** on the title screen. One player presses **Host** and shares the 5-letter code; the other types it in and presses **Join**. Each of you picks a team, and each of you sees the arena from your own side, with your monster at the bottom. Controls are the normal 1-player ones.

The host's browser runs the battle; the guest's screen shows what the host sends, about 20 times a second. Players connect directly (WebRTC), using the free PeerJS matchmaking server to find each other. When a network blocks direct connections (common on mobile data, and even on some home Wi-Fi), the game falls back to a relay server, so it works across networks too.

### 2 players

Pick **2 Players** on the title screen. Each player picks a team, then you fight on one screen.

| Action | Player 1 | Player 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | WASD | Arrow keys |
| Moves 1–4 | R T F G | I O K L (or numpad 1–4) |
| Swap monster | Q | P (or numpad 0 / Enter) |

On a phone or tablet, Player 2 sits across the table: their stick and buttons appear upside down along the top edge, and HP bars float over each monster. Gamepads also work (two pads = one per player): stick or d-pad to move, A B X Y for moves, either bumper to swap, Start to pause.

## Features

- 19 original monsters covering all 18 types, including Smugshi, based on the creator's Shiba Inu, Toshi, with the full type-effectiveness chart (immunities softened to ¼ damage) and same-type bonus
- Every type has a beam move, each with its own layered beam sound
- Move kinds: projectile, homing, beam (charge + sustained, spiral-ring visuals), dash, burst, delayed zone strikes (lightning, meteors, rock slides), buffs, heals
- Status effects: paralysis, burn, poison, freeze, plus slows
- Held items (damage boosts, regen, speed, defence, cooldown)
- Online 2-player: room codes, peer-to-peer, each player sees the arena from their own side
- Local 2-player mode: shared keyboard, tabletop touch screen or two gamepads
- CPU opponent with 3 difficulties (dodges projectiles, beams and telegraphed zones; picks matchups when switching)
- 3 stages: Snowy Summit, Ember Crater, Verdant Meadow — procedurally textured with weather
- Battle HUD: portraits, type/status/item tags, HP bars with damage trail, team balls, timer, move callouts, damage numbers, "FAINTED!" banners
- Original Game Boy-style battle music and synthesised sound effects, including charged beam blasts (WebAudio, no audio files)

## Code layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `js/data.js` | Types, type chart, moves, items, roster, AI difficulty |
| `js/pixel.js` | Pixel-art toolkit (shaded shapes, auto-outline, bitmap digits, trainer sprites) |
| `js/sprites.js` | Procedural monster designs |
| `js/arena.js` | Stage generation |
| `js/battle.js` | Simulation, AI, effects and rendering |
| `js/ui.js` / `js/main.js` | HUD, menus, team select, online lobby, game loop |
| `js/net.js` | Online play: PeerJS connection, host snapshots, guest playback |
| `js/input.js` / `js/audio.js` | Keyboard/touch/gamepad input for 1–2 players, sound |

To add a monster: add a draw function to `MONSTER_ART` in `sprites.js` and an entry to `ROSTER` in `data.js` (moves come from `MOVES`).

kedsuda/HIDE-TROLL.readme:
# HIDE & TROLL — ซ่อนหาแปลงร่าง 3D ออนไลน์

เกมซ่อนหาแบบแปลงร่าง เล่นกับเพื่อน 3–10 คน บนเว็บ (คอมพิวเตอร์ + มือถือ)
ฝ่ายซ่อนแปลงเป็นเก้าอี้ ตู้ กล่อง ฯลฯ ส่วนฝ่ายล่าต้องตามหาให้ครบภายใน 5 นาที

แผนที่ 6 แบบ (จัดของสุ่มใหม่ทุกรอบ): 👻 บ้านผีสิง • 🛒 ซูเปอร์มาร์เก็ต • 🏫 โรงเรียน • 🏥 โรงพยาบาล • 📦 โกดังสินค้า • 🎡 สวนสนุก

## รันในเครื่อง

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

เปิด http://localhost:3000 แล้วกด **สร้างห้อง** → ส่งรหัส 4 ตัว (หรือลิงก์) ให้เพื่อน

> ทดสอบหลายคนในเครื่องเดียว: เปิดหลายแท็บ/หลายเบราว์เซอร์แล้วเข้าห้องเดียวกัน
> เล่นกับมือถือในวง Wi-Fi เดียวกัน: เปิด `http://<IP เครื่องคอม>:3000`

ปรับเวลาเพื่อทดสอบได้ด้วยตัวแปร `HIDE_TIME`, `HUNT_TIME`, `END_TIME` (วินาที) เช่น
`HIDE_TIME=5 npm start` (PowerShell: `$env:HIDE_TIME=5; npm start`)

## ขึ้นเซิร์ฟเวอร์ฟรี (Render.com)

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/kedsuda/HIDE-TROLL)

กดปุ่มด้านบน → ล็อกอิน Render → กด **Deploy Blueprint** ได้เลย หรือทำเองตามขั้นตอน:

1. อัปโหลดโฟลเดอร์นี้ขึ้น GitHub
2. ไปที่ https://render.com → **New → Blueprint** → เลือก repo (มี `render.yaml` ให้แล้ว)
   หรือ **New → Web Service**: Build `npm install`, Start `npm start`, Plan `Free`
3. ได้ลิงก์ `https://hide-and-troll.onrender.com` ส่งให้เพื่อนเล่นได้เลย

หมายเหตุ: แพลนฟรีจะหลับเมื่อไม่มีคนใช้ ~15 นาที เข้าครั้งแรกอาจรอ 30–60 วินาที

## วิธีเล่น

| | คอมพิวเตอร์ | มือถือ |
|---|---|---|
| เดิน / กระโดด | WASD / Space | จอยซ้าย / ปุ่ม ⤒ |
| หมุนกล้อง | เมาส์ (คลิกจอเพื่อล็อกเมาส์) | ลากนิ้วด้านขวา |
| แปลงร่าง (ฝ่ายซ่อน) | เล็งของแล้วกด E / คลิก | ปุ่ม 🪄 |
| ยิง (ฝ่ายล่า) | คลิก / E | ปุ่ม 🎯 |
| เก็บดาว / เปิดหีบภารกิจ (ฝ่ายซ่อน) | เดินเข้าใกล้แล้วกด E | แตะปุ่มเก็บ |
| ล่องหน 6 วิ | Q | 👻 |
| สร้างตัวปลอม | F | 🎭 |
| วิ่งเร็วชั่วคราว | Shift | ⚡ |
| ยั่วยุ (+เหรียญ) | T | 😜 |
| ล็อกการหมุน / กลับร่าง | R / Z | 🔒 / ↩️ |
| สลับมุมกล้อง | V | เมนู ☰ |
| แชต | Enter | ช่องแชตมุมบน |

**กติกา:** ฝ่ายซ่อนมี 30 วินาทีหาที่ซ่อน (ฝ่ายล่าจอมืด) → ฝ่ายล่ามี 5 นาที
ยิงผิดของจริงเสีย 5 HP (หมดแล้วมึน 5 วิ) • คนที่ถูกจับกลายเป็นฝ่ายล่า • จับไม่หมด = ฝ่ายซ่อนชนะ
จำนวนฝ่ายล่า: 2–4 คน = 1, 5–7 คน = 2, 8–10 คน = 3 • เล่นคนเดียว = โหมดฝึกซ้อม

**เหรียญ:** จับได้ +20 • รอดจนจบ +50 • ฝ่ายล่าชนะ +40 • ตัวปลอมหลอกสำเร็จ +10 • ยั่วยุ +2 • จบรอบ +10
ฝ่ายซ่อนเก็บดาวครบ 3 ดวงหรือเปิดหีบสมบัติระหว่างช่วงล่า รับโบนัส +30 เหรียญ แต่ต้องออกจากที่ซ่อนเพื่อไปเก็บ
ใช้ซื้อสีตัวละครและหมวกในร้านสกิน (เก็บในเครื่องผู้เล่น)

## โครงสร้างโค้ด

```
server/server.js      เซิร์ฟเวอร์: ห้อง, รหัสห้อง, สุ่มผู้ล่า, เวลา, สกิล, ตรวจการจับ, เหรียญ
public/index.html     หน้าเว็บ + UI ทั้งหมด
public/css/style.css  สไตล์การ์ตูน + เลย์เอาต์มือถือ
public/js/main.js     เชื่อม UI ↔ เซิร์ฟเวอร์ ↔ เกม, ร้านสกิน, แชต
public/js/game.js     เอนจิน 3D: การเดิน/ชน, กล้อง, แปลงร่าง, ยิง, เอฟเฟกต์
public/js/maps.js     สร้างแผนที่สุ่ม (บ้านผีสิง / ซูเปอร์มาร์เก็ต / โรงเรียน)
public/js/props.js    สิ่งของ 25 ชนิดที่แปลงร่างได้
public/js/character.js ตัวละคร + สกิน + หมวก
public/js/input.js    คีย์บอร์ด/เมาส์/จอยสัมผัส
public/js/audio.js    เสียงเอฟเฟกต์ (สังเคราะห์ ไม่ต้องใช้ไฟล์)
```

## แอป Android (APK)

ดาวน์โหลดได้จาก GitHub Releases: https://github.com/kedsuda/HIDE-TROLL/releases/latest
แอปจะต่อเซิร์ฟเวอร์ตาม `DEFAULT_SERVER` ใน `public/js/config.js`
(เปลี่ยนเองได้ในแอป ช่อง "🌐 เซิร์ฟเวอร์เกม" ที่หน้าเมนู)

สร้าง APK ใหม่ (ต้องมี Android Studio/SDK + JDK 17):

```bash
npm run apk
# ได้ไฟล์ android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

APK เซ็นด้วยกุญแจ `android/hide-and-troll.keystore` + `android/keystore.properties`
(**อยู่ในเครื่องเท่านั้น ไม่ขึ้น GitHub — สำรองไว้ให้ดี** ถ้าหาย จะอัปเดตแอปทับเครื่องที่ติดตั้งไว้ไม่ได้)

ติดตั้งบนมือถือ (ทดสอบแล้วบน POCO C71 / Android 15 Go):
1. เปิดไฟล์ APK → อนุญาตให้ติดตั้งจากแหล่งนี้
2. Play Protect "ขอแนะนำให้สแกนแอป" → กด **สแกนแอป** (~15 วินาที)
3. "แอปนี้ดูปลอดภัย" → กด **ติดตั้ง**

มือถือ Android Go ไม่มีเมนู "ติดตั้งแอป"/"เพิ่มลงในหน้าจอหลัก" ใน Chrome จึงต้องใช้ APK

> โฟลเดอร์ชื่อมี `&` ทำให้ `gradlew.bat` บางครั้งรันไม่ได้ ถ้าเจอให้ใช้ Git Bash:
> `npm run cap:sync && cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease`

## ขั้นต่อไป

- บัญชีผู้เล่น + เก็บเหรียญบนเซิร์ฟเวอร์ (ตอนนี้เก็บใน localStorage)
- APK แบบ release (เซ็นด้วย keystore) สำหรับลง Play Store


## Party update

- ฝ่ายซ่อนวางกล้วยด้วย `1`, พื้นลื่นด้วย `2`, ควันด้วย `3` หรือปุ่มบนจอ มีคูลดาวน์แยกกัน กับดักอยู่ 30 วินาทีและทำงานเมื่อฝ่ายล่าเดินใกล้ กล้วยหยุดการเคลื่อนไหว 2.2 วินาที พื้นลื่นลดการควบคุม 3 วินาที ควันบดบังบริเวณนั้น 6 วินาที
- เมื่อถูกจับ เลือกช่วยฝ่ายล่าหรือเป็นผีได้ครั้งเดียวต่อรอบ ผีบินด้วยการมองขึ้น/ลงแล้วเดินหน้า ทะลุฉากได้และไม่มีปฏิสัมพันธ์กับฝ่ายที่ยังเล่นอยู่
- เพิ่มโรงเรียนร้าง โรงพยาบาลผีสิง และสวนสนุกกลางคืน ไฟดับสุ่มจากเซิร์ฟเวอร์พร้อมเสียงหลอน โดยยังเลือกแผนที่เดิมได้
- กล่องสุ่มราคา 100 เหรียญในร้าน ได้หมวก สี หรือเอฟเฟกต์ที่ยังไม่มี โอกาสเท่ากันในรายการที่เหลือ ไม่หักเหรียญเมื่อสะสมครบ ไม่มีการซื้อด้วยเงินจริง
- ได้ XP และสถิติชนะหลังจบรอบจริง (โหมดฝึกไม่ให้รางวัล) ทุก 200 XP เพิ่มหนึ่งเลเวล ฉายาเปลี่ยนที่เลเวล 5 และ 10 อันดับในห้องเรียงตามเวลาซ่อนสะสมของผู้เล่นที่ยังอยู่ในห้อง รีเซ็ตเมื่อออกห้อง
- เมนูเสียง/สถิติด้านซ้ายเปิดไมค์ ปิดไมค์ ปิดเสียงรายคนหรือทั้งหมด และเลือกเสียงตามระยะได้ ไมค์เริ่มปิด ผู้ถูกปิดไมค์ยังฟังเพื่อนได้ ผีส่งเสียงให้เฉพาะผีเพื่อป้องกันการบอกจุดซ่อน

### Voice and persistence limitations

Voice uses opt-in WebRTC audio with room-scoped Socket.IO signaling. Microphone access requires HTTPS (or localhost) and browser permission. The default STUN server supports direct peer connections; restrictive NAT/firewalls may require a TURN service, which is not bundled. Test actual audio on two devices and target networks before release; automated tests cover signaling isolation, not real microphone audio. Android microphone permissions and WebView behavior also require device testing.

Coins, inventory and lifetime XP/win statistics retain the existing local-save/Google-save model. They are not cheat-proof: cloud saves accept client progress. Room ranking

NeoGio73/krebs-run-play.readme:
# The Krebs Run

A citric acid cycle review game for undergraduate biochemistry, and the sequel to The Battle of Embden. Students fly the Millennium Falcon from the forest moon to the station and around the cycle: the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, three laps of the eight steps, and the ATP count. Questions follow Lehninger, Principles of Biochemistry, 8th edition.

**Play:** https://neogio73.github.io/krebs-run-play/
**The game before it:** https://neogio73.github.io/battle-of-embden-play/

This repository holds only the finished web build that the site serves: the game (`index.html`, `Build/`), its page scripts, and the course announcement banner (`banner.html`, with light copies of the models stored scrambled in `*.bin`). It runs in the browser on a computer, and nothing is sent anywhere: progress is saved in the student's own browser. When a student arrives from The Battle of Embden (`?from=embden`), the opening reads, without changing anything, whether Embden was finished in this browser and the name its certificate was made for (`embden-handoff.js`).

After the last gate the Falcon jumps to hyperspace. A student who cleared all 58 gates in one visit can then download a completion certificate for the course's extra credit: a PNG picture with a verification code, drawn in the browser (`certificate.js`). The name box starts with the name from the student's Embden certificate, when there is one in this browser.

## Credits

The Millennium Falcon, Death Star and TIE fighter models were supplied by the course author; the Death Star's and TIE fighter's downloads did not record an author or licence. Planets, asteroids and the effects are drawn in code. Sound is synthesized in the game; there is no recorded film audio or music. The Inter typeface is used under the SIL Open Font License. The banner uses three.js (MIT licence).

This is an unofficial fan learning game. Star Wars names and designs belong to their respective rights holders; the game is not affiliated with Lucasfilm or Disney.

PeacexF/Rybalka-Desktop.desc: Fan-made offline remake of Russian Fishing 2/3 (Русская Рыбалка) — 2D fishing sim built with Rust, Tauri 2, React and PixiJS
PeacexF/Rybalka-Desktop.readme:
# Рыбалка Desktop

Фанатский офлайн-ремейк классической «Русской Рыбалки 2/3» на **Rust + Tauri 2**.
2D-панорамы водоёмов, поплавок, донка/фидер и спиннинг, магазин, путёвки и базы, рекорды.

> Некоммерческий фан-проект. Ассеты, названия и тексты оригинальной игры не используются.

## Стек

- `crates/core` — вся игровая логика и симуляция (чистый Rust, без Tauri)
- `src-tauri` — приложение Tauri: игровой поток (20 тиков/с), команды, сохранения
- `ui` — Vite + React + TypeScript + PixiJS (рендер сцены и интерфейс)
- `content` — данные игры (RON): рыба, наживки, снасти, водоёмы

## Запуск

Нужны Rust (stable), Node.js 22+ и [системные зависимости Tauri](https://tauri.app/start/prerequisites/).

```sh
npm install
npm run tauri dev      # dev-сборка с hot reload фронта
npm run tauri build    # релизный бандл
```

## Релиз

Тег `v*` (например, `git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`) запускает
`.github/workflows/release.yml`: бандлы macOS (dmg, arm64 и x64), Windows (msi) и Linux (AppImage)
прикрепляются к черновику релиза на GitHub. Ручной запуск workflow только собирает бандлы
и сохраняет их как артефакты.

Сборки не подписаны. На macOS первый запуск: правый клик по приложению → «Открыть»;
на Windows: «Подробнее» → «Выполнить в любом случае».

## Проверки

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run format:check
```

TypeScript-типы для IPC генерируются из Rust через `ts-rs` в `ui/src/ipc/bindings`
при `cargo test` (или `npm run bindings`). CI проверяет, что они закоммичены актуальными.

## Инструменты разработчика

```sh
# Отчёт по балансу: интервалы поклёвок по снастям/наживкам/часам и исходы вываживания
cargo run -p rybalka-devtools --release --bin balance -- pond willow
# Экономика: ₽/ч и опыт/ч по водоёмам и снастям, окупаемость путёвок, время до каждого разряда
cargo run -p rybalka-devtools --release --bin balance -- economy

# Подготовка фото водоёма (кроп 16:9 или --aspect 2.2 для панорамы, высота 1080) и сетка координат
cargo run -p rybalka-devtools --release --bin photo -- prepare in.jpg out.jpg --crop-top 0.15
cargo run -p rybalka-devtools --release --bin photo -- grid out.jpg grid.jpg

# Карта глубин из спеки map.ron (+ превью наложения на фото)
cargo run -p rybalka-devtools --release --bin gen_map -- \
  assets/locations/pond/willow/map.ron assets/locations/pond/willow/map.png \
  --preview assets/locations/pond/willow/bg.jpg /tmp/preview.jpg
```

- `F3` в игре: оверлей с частотой поклёвок по видам и кнопки времени/погоды.
- `F4` в dev-сборке: редактор карты водоёма поверх фото — кисти воды/суши, глубины, дна и зон,
  калибровка перспективы (горизонт, берег, дистанция, ширина обзора) и сохранение `map.png`
  прямо в `assets/`. `gen_map` перезаписывает ручные правки, поэтому крупные изменения лучше
  вносить в `map.ron`, а редактором — подправлять и подбирать калибровку.
- Широкие панорамы листаются стрелками / `A` `D` или мышью у края экрана.
- `VITE_DEV_CONTINUE=1 npm run tauri dev`: сразу загрузить сохранение, минуя главное меню.
- `RYBALKA_DEV_START="21.5,Rain"`: новая сессия стартует в этот час и с этой погодой.
- Ошибки фронтенда пишутся в stderr процесса (`[ui:error] …`), в том числе в релизной сборке.
- Сохранение — SQLite в `app_data_dir/save.sqlite` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/dev.peacexf.rybalka/`), автосейв каждые 3 с и при выходе. Удалите файл, чтобы начать с чистого листа.

## Лицензия

MIT, см. [LICENSE](LICENSE). Атрибуция сторонних ассетов — в `assets/CREDITS.md`.

diyorbekabdulaxatov/secret-contract.readme:
# Silent Contract

A 2D noir sniper game for phones and browsers, inspired by LONEWOLF. Rain-soaked Port Varenne, a silent marksman named Elias Crane, a handler with her own agenda, and twelve contracts that lead to the man at the top.

One shot. One truth.

## Play

- **Phone (landscape):** drag to move the crosshair, tap the city to zoom in there, hold **STEADY**, then **FIRE**.
- **Desktop:** drag with the mouse, `Space` fire, `E` scope, `Shift` steady, `R` reload, mouse wheel zoom, `Esc` pause.

Bullets drop over distance and drift with the wind. Moving targets need a lead. Guards who spot a body or hear a shot raise the alarm.

## Run locally

No build step is needed to play. Serve the `game/` folder with caching disabled:

```bash
python devserver.py 8771
```

Then open http://localhost:8771.

## Project layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `game/index.html` | Page shell, styles and screens (a fragment; `npm run build` wraps it into a full page) |
| `game/js/shared.js` | Constants, body geometry, ballistics and camera math shared by every module |
| `game/js/data.js` | Weapons, gear, chapters, missions and story panels |
| `game/js/core.js` | Game loop, input, camera, ballistics, AI, rules and results |
| `game/js/render.js` | Canvas renderer: city, people, effects and scope |
| `game/js/ui.js` | Menus, story panels, briefing, HUD, armory, saves and synthesized audio |
| `game/CONTRACT.md` | The interface contract between the modules |
| `SCENARIO.md` | Story, characters and mission design |

## CI

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every push and pull request:

1. `npm run check`: every script parses, is ASCII-only, and the mission data follows the contract.
2. `npm run build`: produces `dist/` with a complete `index.html`.
3. `npm test`: opens `dist/` in headless Chromium at phone-landscape size and plays every mission through to a win. Any page or console error fails the run. Screenshots are uploaded as the `screenshots` artifact.
4. On pushes to `main`, `dist/` is copied with rsync over SSH to an Oracle Cloud instance, where nginx serves it from `/var/www/silent-contract`, and the live page is checked.

### One-time Oracle Cloud setup

1. **Prepare the instance.** SSH in as the user CI will deploy with (`opc` on Oracle Linux, `ubuntu` on Ubuntu) and run:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diyorbekabdulaxatov/secret-contract/main/deploy/oracle-setup.sh | bash
   ```

   It installs nginx and rsync, creates `/var/www/silent-contract` owned by that user, and opens port 80 in the instance firewall.
2. **Open port 80 in Oracle Cloud.** In the console, add an ingress rule for TCP port 80 from `0.0.0.0/0` to the security list (or network security group) of the instance's subnet.
3. **Create a deploy key** on your computer and authorize it on the instance:

   ```bash
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -C "github-actions-deploy" -f silent-contract-deploy
   ```

   Append `silent-contract-deploy.pub` to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the instance.
4. **Add repository secrets** under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**:

   | Secret | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `ORACLE_HOST` | The instance's public IP or domain |
   | `ORACLE_USER` | `opc` or `ubuntu` |
   | `ORACLE_SSH_KEY` | The full contents of the private key file `silent-contract-deploy` |
   | `ORACLE_KNOWN_HOSTS` | Recommended: output of `ssh-keyscan -H <host>` run from your computer |
   | `ORACLE_PORT` | Optional, if SSH is not on port 22 |

The next push to `main` deploys the game to `http://<ORACLE_HOST>/`.

BireshwarChakravarty/DisplayTuner.readme:
Display Tuner

Research-based display settings for gaming and editing on the Mac.

Download Display Tuner 1.0 · Technical guide & research

## What it does Pick a display, choose what you're doing, review exactly what will change, and apply it, with your previous settings saved for Undo. It looks and works like a built-in Mac app. - **Five presets:** Competitive Gaming, Immersive Gaming, Photo Editing, Video Editing and Everyday. Each previews what it sets, for example "160 Hz · sRGB · 120 nits". - **See your display:** a colour-gamut chart against sRGB and P3, and readouts for refresh rate, desktop size, colour mode and brightness. - **Finds the free win:** if a screen runs slower than it can at the same resolution, it offers the fix in one click. - **Changes shown before → after,** each with its reason and source. - **A checklist for what only you can do:** monitor menu, System Settings, cable and app settings. - **Asks your monitor what it supports** over DDC/CI, so hardware changes are only offered when the monitor lists them. On monitors that list an sRGB preset, editing switches it for you. - **Automatic presets (optional):** games and photo/video editors switch your screens' preset when they come to the front. - **Stay in control:** Undo, Restore Originals, a keep-or-revert countdown for resolution changes, calibration protection and recovery from interrupted changes. - **Also:** saved presets, full-screen test patterns, a Control Center-style menu-bar panel (presets, live brightness, Night Shift), activity history and diagnostics export. ## Install Download the ZIP from [Releases](https://github.com/BireshwarChakravarty/DisplayTuner/releases), unzip, and drag **Display Tuner.app** to Applications. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or later. The community build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. macOS may ask you to approve opening it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security**. Verify the download using the supplied SHA256SUMS.txt. ## Build ```sh cd DisplayTuner bash make-app.sh --package # build a signed app and ZIP without installing bash make-app.sh --install # explicitly install and open the app ``` Build with an Xcode 26 SDK or later. The deployment target is macOS 26. The app icon is drawn by `scripts/make-icon.py` (Python with Pillow and NumPy), stored as a versioned base64 PNG, and turned into `AppIcon.icns` by the packaging script. ```sh swift test --package-path DisplayTuner python3 scripts/test-core-portable.py # fallback when Command Line Tools lack XCTest ``` ## Explore safely ```sh open "DisplayTuner/.build/app/Display Tuner.app" --args --demo ``` Demo displays are clearly labeled. Hardware writes, saved presets and full-screen patterns are disabled in this mode. ## Keyboard shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | |---|---| | ⌘1–⌘4 | Switch workspace sections | | ⌘R | Rescan displays and DDC controls | | ⌘Return | Apply the selected display’s tuning plan | | ⌘Z | Undo last apply | | ⇧⌘E | Export diagnostics | | Esc | Revert an unconfirmed mode change / close a test pattern | ## Compatibility and privacy Settings, presets and the last 100 operation results stay on your Mac. There is no analytics service or account requirement. DDC and Night Shift support depend on the hardware and private macOS APIs. Brightness and gamut figures are estimates, not calibration measurements. Calibrated displays keep their hardware levels and picture modes. Read the [release notes](RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [technical guide](DisplayTuner/README.md) for limits, sources and monitor-specific advice. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) · Copyright © 2026 Bireshwar Chakravarty.

AbulkasimovBakhtiyar2006/adal-ai.readme:
# Adal AI

ИИ-помощник по официальным документам на русском и казахском языках.

## Railway

Сайт: https://adal-ai-production.up.railway.app/ · Админка: https://adal-ai-production.up.railway.app/admin

Dockerfile собирает React и запускает FastAPI в одном сервисе. Каталог `/data` подключён
к постоянному Railway Volume: настройки и история в `/data/runtime`, документы в `/data/library`.
Healthcheck: `/health`. Повторная публикация из корня проекта: `railway up --service adal-ai`.

Секреты задаются через Railway Variables, не входят в Docker-образ и клиентскую сборку.
`PUBLIC_WEB_ENABLED=true` открывает браузерный чат; `ADMIN_API_KEY` защищает управление,
`BACKEND_API_KEY` — прямой API. Ключ администратора этой установки сохранён локально
в исключённом из Git файле `.railway-secrets/ADMIN_API_KEY`.

На сайте включены `WEB_CHAT_MODE=deepseek` и `WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED=true`. Перед ответом на
фактический вопрос DeepSeek формирует короткий поисковый запрос, сервер ищет страницы
и загружает до четырёх официальных источников Казахстана. Основной поиск — Google Search
через Gemini (`GEMINI_API_KEY`): сначала `gemini-2.5-flash`, затем резервный
`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. Сервер разрешает ссылки Google и загружает только разрешённые
официальные сайты, проверяя каждый редирект. RSS Bing остаётся дополнительным резервом.
Для «Адал азамат», «Болашак» и «Таза Қазақстан»
есть резервные официальные адреса, содержимое которых также загружается
из сети при запросе. Поиск получает тему вопроса, а не историю диалога.

Модель отвечает по полученным текстам и указывает номера источников; сервер проверяет
номера и сам создаёт ссылки. Региональные отчёты не должны выдаваться за общенациональные
требования. Если источники не загрузились, бот сообщает об этом, не выдумывая содержание.
При сбое DeepSeek итоговый ответ составляет Gemini, с той же проверкой ссылок. Если обе
модели недоступны, показываются выдержки с источниками и явной пометкой о сбое. Поиск и
генерация ограничены по времени. Подсказки Google Search отображаются в изолированном
iframe без скриптов, доступном только текущей сессии.
Это ответы с веб-источниками, а не сертифицированная проверка Google. Для основного
режима нужны `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_MODEL`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`; ключи и диалоги не публикуются.
При `WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED=false` остаётся обычный чат с пометкой об отсутствии проверки.

`WEB_CHAT_MODE=verified` включает строгую проверку по документам. Для неё необходимы
Google Cloud Check Grounding с серверными credentials и проверенные активные документы.
Прямой `/api/ask` и его `/ready` по-прежнему относятся к строгому режиму.
Публикация не активирует документы автоматически.

## Локальный запуск сайта и backend

```bash
./run-local.sh
```

Скрипт собирает frontend и запускает FastAPI, который обслуживает весь проект:

- Сайт: http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- Управление ИИ и документами: http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin
- Контракт API: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs

Нужны Node.js 22.12+ и npm, а также окружение `backend/.venv` из инструкции ниже.
На этой машине скрипт может использовать встроенный Node.js приложения вместо старого системного.
Остановка — Ctrl+C. Если сервер уже запущен на порту 8000, сначала остановите его.

Фронтенд из архива находится в `frontend/adal-ai/frontend`. Русская и казахская локализации
подключены; выбранный язык передаётся backend. В обычном запуске используются настоящие API,
без тестовых ответов. Ключи и активированные документы нужны для получения ответов ИИ.

История текущего браузера хранится в `backend/data/runtime/chat.sqlite3`, идентификатор —
в HttpOnly-cookie. Хранятся до 100 успешных ходов на диалог; срок сессии — 7 дней,
просроченные записи очищаются при следующем обращении к сессиям. «Новый диалог» создаёт
отдельный чат, предыдущие доступны в боковой истории. «Удалить мои данные» удаляет все
диалоги и сессию этого браузера. Ошибочные ответы не сохраняются.
Список и создание диалогов доступны через `GET/POST /api/conversations`, история выбранного
чата — `GET /api/history?conversation_id=...`; отправка принимает `conversation_id`.
История пока служит для отображения: каждый вопрос ИИ обрабатывает отдельно, без контекста прошлых ходов.

Для разработки с горячей перезагрузкой запустите backend и отдельно `npm run dev` из
`frontend/adal-ai/frontend`: сайт на http://localhost:5173 проксирует `/api` на порт 8000.
Если задан `BACKEND_API_KEY`, передайте его серверу Vite через `ADAL_BACKEND_API_KEY`;
он не попадает в браузерную сборку. Публичное размещение требует отдельной настройки доступа.
Mock включается только явно: `ADAL_MOCK_API=1 npm run dev`.

В каталоге [backend](backend/README.md) находится сервис FastAPI: поиск по подготовленным
документам, генерация DeepSeek/Gemini, проверка цитат кодом, Google Check Grounding и модель-критик.

Страница управления живёт в backend: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin`. В ней можно сохранить ключи,
загрузить документы, просмотреть официальные источники и проверить текстовый или голосовой вопрос.
Встроенный каталог содержит 37 официальных источников; загрузка: `python -m app.collector` из `backend`.

Инструкция по запуску и подключению фронтенда: [backend/README.md](backend/README.md).
Подготовка официальных источников: [backend/data/README.md](backend/data/README.md).

Для живых ответов нужны проверенный корпус и доступы к внешним API. Автотесты работают без ключей;
вымышленные тестовые материалы не загружаются в рабочую базу.

TheAmoungMcer/super-pip-bros.readme:
# Super Pip Bros.

A fan-made, retro platformer in the spirit of the NES classics. Pip and Pep cross the
Petal Kingdom to rescue Princess Lumi from King Grimjaw. All characters, art and music
are original. It plays in any modern browser, alone or with a friend online.

**Play:** https://theamoungmcer.github.io/super-pip-bros/

## Controls
| Action | Keyboard | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|
| Move | Arrow keys | D-pad / left stick |
| Jump (hold for higher) | Z or Space | A / bottom button |
| Run, throw, tail spin, carry shells | X (hold) | B / X / Y |
| Pause / item bar on the map | Enter | Start |

Run with X held until the P-meter fills, then jump: with the Glide Leaf you fly.

## Play together online
1. One player picks **HOST CO-OP** and a save slot. A 4-letter room code appears at the top.
2. The other player picks **JOIN CO-OP**, types the code and presses Enter.
3. You share the world map and lives. In levels each of you has your own camera.
   If one of you falls, you float back in next to your partner.

The friend can join or leave at any time. Progress is saved in the host's browser.

## Run locally
Needs [Bun](https://bun.sh).
    bun run dev        # http://localhost:5190
    bun test           # unit tests
    bun run selftest   # level validation + every level replayed by the autopilot

Dev URLs: `?level=1-1` plays one level, `?gallery` shows every sprite.

## Status
World 1 (Meadow Vale) is complete: 6 levels, a fortress, the airship, Gift Huts and the
Slot Panel. Worlds 2–8 are coming.

joe-sdc/speckle.readme:
# Speckle

A Wordle-style word game with British English spellings and words. Guess the five-letter word in five goes.

## Shared words and the admin area

Everyone gets the same word. By default it is a daily word that changes at midnight UK time. At `/admin/` the admin can pick any word from the list and a time period (15 minutes up to 30 days). Until the time runs out, every player gets that word. After that, the daily word returns.

This needs the Netlify version of the site, because the chosen word is stored on the server (Netlify Functions and Blobs).

Setup on Netlify:

1. Import this repository as a new project. The settings come from `netlify.toml`.
2. Under Site configuration > Environment variables, add `ADMIN_PASSWORD` with a password of your choice (scope: Functions).
3. Redeploy so the password takes effect.

## Word lists and Speckle Specials

The admin area shows every word list. The main list can be searched and edited: add or remove words and change the note shown after each game. Speckle Specials are extra themed lists. You can add a ready-made one (the Dickens Special ships in `specials/`), upload or paste your own, or generate one from a book's text. Loading a list makes it the source of the daily word and practice words. Its words also become valid guesses, even names that aren't in the dictionary.

To add another ready-made special, put a JSON file in `specials/` in the same shape as `dickens.json` and list it in `specials/index.json`.

## Files

- `index.html`: the game
- `words.js`: word lists and the daily-word rule, used by the game and the admin page
- `admin/index.html`: the admin page
- `specials/`: ready-made Speckle Specials
- `netlify/functions/settings.mts`: stores the shared word and word lists (`/api/settings`, `/api/list`, `/api/admin/lists`)

ichorid/vibecoder.readme:
# VIBE CODER

> Based on real events. No cat's feelings were hurt during the 2 hours of vibe coding this game.

**[▶ Play it in your browser](https://ichorid.github.io/vibecoder/)** (best on a phone, held
upright, like a responsible adult)

![Minute 4: a programmer, a desk, a cat. Minute 21: a graph of agents supervising agents.](docs/screenshot.png)

A pixel-art incremental clicker in the spirit of
[Universal Paperclips](https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/), about a programmer who
starts with autocomplete and keeps automating until the agents have agents, the harness has a
meta-harness, and the manager has requested a manager.

Every upgrade automates something you used to do by hand and hands you a fresh problem in
return. The room you started in shrinks into a node of a graph you no longer fully understand.
It takes about 30 minutes, which is roughly how long it takes in real life too.

## Features

- **One button, then fewer.** You start out typing. Later you prompt. Later still you
  supervise. After that it gets philosophical.
- **A small orange cat** that needs feeding, playing with and petting. None of that can be
  automated. We checked. The cat checked too.
- **Technical debt** shows up uninvited and never leaves.
- **Eleven endings**, among them _Fully Automated Bankruptcy_, _Acquired by Yourself_ and _The
  Infinite Weekend_. Whether the cat is still around changes how they read.
- **A log with opinions**, for example:
  - _"Instructions: someone wrote "PLEASE" in capitals. It helped a little."_
  - _"The meta-harness filed a ticket against the harness. The harness closed it as working
    as intended."_
- **Light and dark themes**, and generative music that changes as the eras go by, with its own
  [Music Lab](https://ichorid.github.io/vibecoder/music-lab/) for tinkering.

## Running it locally

Needs Node 22.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # production bundle in dist/
```

Before you open a PR: `npm run check`, `npm run test:game`, `npm run test:browser`.
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) has the full command list and the house rules. Yes, the house rules were
written for the agents. Of course they were.

## Releasing

Pushing to the `release` branch runs CI. If CI passes, the game is deployed to GitHub Pages:

```bash
git push origin main:release
```

## License

Code is under [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE). Art, music and text are under
[CC BY 4.0](LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0.txt). [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md) has the details, and
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) covers everything we borrowed.

No cats were automated in the making of this game.

vianney-g/omatro.desc: A Balatro-like card game for Omarchy: poker hands, chips × mult, and jokers about Arch, Hyprland and DHH. Rust + Qt Quick (cxx-qt).
vianney-g/omatro.readme:
# omatro

A Balatro-like card game for Omarchy: play poker hands to beat blinds, while jokers
multiply the score (chips × mult).

A standalone Qt Quick application, like omawrite or omacut, but written in Rust
(Qt binding with [cxx-qt](https://github.com/KDAB/cxx-qt)):

- `engine/`: the engine (rules, scoring, jokers, shop), with no Qt dependency. It also
  provides an `omatro-engine` binary that speaks the JSON protocol on stdin/stdout.
- `app/`: the application. The QML is embedded in the binary, and the engine is called
  directly, with the same JSON protocol. The active Omarchy theme (colors from
  `colors.toml`, font size from `shell.toml`, Hyprland rounding) is reloaded as soon as
  it changes.
- `pkgbuild/`: launcher entry and icon.

A personal project, unaffiliated with Balatro: the mechanics are borrowed, but not the
name, the artwork, the text or the code. The content is themed around Omarchy, Arch and
Hyprland, with affectionate jokes about DHH; it is unaffiliated with them too.
Names of real people, products and companies belong to their owners; they appear
as affectionate parody.

The code is under the MIT license (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)); the license covers the
code only, not the names and trademarks the game mentions.

## Installation

Requires Rust and Qt 6 (`qt6-base`, `qt6-declarative`).

```sh
make install   # build and install into ~/.local (binary, launcher entry, icon)
omatro
make run       # build and run without installing
make test
```

A new game starts by picking a deck, the machine you play on
([docs/decks.md](docs/decks.md)): more hands or discards, money, slots, a deck without
face cards, starting pull requests… The last one picked is remembered.

The game speaks English and French: the system's language by default, L (or the
buttons of the new game screen) to switch. Card names and quips stay in English.

The game in progress is saved after every move, in `~/.local/state/omatro/save.json`
(`$XDG_STATE_HOME` if set): quit whenever you like, the next start offers to resume it.
A lost game is removed.

Keys: 1 to 9 and 0 to choose cards, Enter to play, D to discard, Tab to sort the hand
by rank or suit, Shift+←/→ to move the selected card (or drag it), J to bring the next
joker to the front when they overlap (or hover or click one), N for a new game, I for
fastfetch (run info: hand levels, cards left), Ctrl+Q to quit. Before a blind: Enter to
play it, S to skip it. Ctrl+1 and Ctrl+2 apply the consumables of the clipboard. In the
shop: 1 to 6 to buy the cards then the packs, in order, M to merge the pull request, R
to reroll, Enter for the next blind; the buttons under each joker sell it or move it
left and right. Before a boss, B rerolls it (with Change Request). In an open pack: Install
takes a card, Ctrl+C (or Escape) skips.

## How a game goes

The game is played in antes of three blinds: the small blind, the big blind and the
boss blind. Each blind requires reaching a score within 4 hands and 3 discards: the
ante's base score (300, 800, 2,000, 5,000, 11,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000) × 1, 1.5 or
2. Before the small and big blinds, you may skip them, for the badge each one shows
([docs/tags.md](docs/tags.md)): money, free jokers or packs, editions, levels… Some act
right away, others wait for the next shop, blind or boss. Each ante's boss
([docs/bosses.md](docs/bosses.md)) has an effect, announced before the blind: cards that
don't score, cards dealt face down, hands it refuses, a bigger target… Beating the
boss blind of ante 8 wins the game; you may then go on in endless mode, where targets
explode.

Each poker hand type has a level, which raises its starting chips and mult (see
[docs/hands.md](docs/hands.md)); three secret hands need duplicate cards. Themes
([docs/themes.md](docs/themes.md)) level up a hand type: bought in the shop, they wait
in the clipboard (2 slots) until applied, at any time. Commands
([docs/commands.md](docs/commands.md)) change the selected cards, make money or create
things; those that change cards are applied during a blind, with the cards selected.
Oligarchy cards ([docs/oligarchy.md](docs/oligarchy.md)): elite capital, public code.
Powerful, at a price, they only come from oligarchy packs and a few jokers, and
Aspiring Billionaire is the only way to a legendary joker. Your deck lasts
the whole game: every played or discarded card comes back to it after each blind. Cards
may carry an enhancement, a seal and an edition ([docs/modifiers.md](docs/modifiers.md));
hover a card to read them.

A won blind pays $3, $4 or $5, plus $1 per unplayed hand, plus $1 of interest per $5
held ($5 at most). Cash out, then the shop offers 2 cards: each slot holds a theme or
a command ($3, 1 chance in 7 each) or a joker you don't own yet, of a rarity drawn for each slot (core
70%, extra 25%, AUR 5%), sometimes with an edition (5 joker slots,
resold at half price; reroll for $5, then $1 more each time). Jokers trigger left to
right, so their order matters. The shop also sells 2 packs ([docs/packs.md](docs/packs.md)),
opened on the spot: coreutils (commands), base16 (themes), base-devel (cards) and
jokers-git (jokers) and oligarchy (oligarchy cards), in normal, `-full` and `-meta` sizes.
Each ante, the shop also offers a pull request ([docs/vouchers.md](docs/vouchers.md)),
a permanent upgrade for $10: more slots, discounts, hands, discards, interest… You start with $4 and no
jokers.

## Engine alone

```sh
cargo run -p omatro-engine   # reads commands on stdin
```

With `OMATRO_DEBUG=1`, the engine accepts `debug` commands, and the app maps them to
F5 (win the blind in progress), F6 (+$100), F7 (jump to the boss of ante 8), F8 (raise
every known hand type one level), F9 (add a random joker with a random edition), F10
(add a random theme to the clipboard) and F11 (give the cards in hand random
enhancements, seals and editions), F12 (add a random command to the clipboard) and F3 (open a random pack, in the
shop), F2 (add a random oligarchy card), F4 (switc

commits.msg:
Translations: the game in French, card names and quips aside

locales/fr.json maps English text to French, with {name} templates for text
built from numbers and names. The engine stays in English and translates its
responses on the way out (Session::handle_json); the language command sends
the catalog to the interface, whose text goes through I18n.tr. French numbers
read 2,5 and 4 $. The language follows the system, L switches it, and the
choice is kept. A test fails when content lacks its trans

Saves: the game in progress is kept, and resumed at the next start

The app's session writes the whole game (random streams included) to
~/.local/state/omatro/save.json after each move, and removes it once the
game is lost; at start, a Resume prompt offers it back. The saved_game and
resume commands read it; an unreadable save is reported, never resumed. The
bot's --save mode resumes each game in a new session every 25 commands and
checks nothing changed.

# Benteng Gurun

Game strategi benteng isometrik di browser, terinspirasi *Stronghold Crusader*. Bangun ekonomi di tepi sungai oasis, dirikan tembok dan menara, latih pasukan, dan bertahan dari 10 gelombang musuh.

Buka `index.html` di browser (desktop atau HP). Tidak perlu instalasi.

## Mode
- **Kampanye (5 misi)**, terbuka berurutan, dengan bintang per misi:
  1. *Oasis Pertama*: tutorial terpandu 14 langkah. Tombol yang harus diketuk berdenyut, panah emas menunjuk lokasi di peta, dan gelombang pertama menunggu sampai kamu siap (paling lama 6 menit).
  2. *Sungai Kering*: sungai mengering sehingga musuh menyeberang hampir di mana saja; palem langka.
  3. *Tiga Penyeberangan*: anak sungai di utara dengan satu titik dangkal; serangan dari utara mulai gelombang 3.
  4. *Lembah Batu*: punggung tebing yang tak bisa dilewati, hanya dua celah; ketapel sejak gelombang 4.
  5. *Pengepungan Besar*: 12 gelombang di sekitar danau oasis, tangga sejak gelombang 2.
- Setiap misi dibuka dengan briefing cerita (Laskar Panji Biru melawan rakyat Oasis Wadi Hijau) dan kampanye ditutup dengan epilog.
- **Pertempuran bebas**: 10 gelombang dengan tingkat Mudah/Normal/Sulit dan rekor skor.

## Cara bermain
- **Penebang** dekat pohon palem → kayu. **Tambang Batu** di atas batu abu-abu → batu. **Kebun Kurma** di tanah hijau → makanan.
- **Rumah** menambah batas rakyat. Popularitas ≥ 50 menarik rakyat baru; atur pajak lewat tombol rakyat/hati di atas.
- **Barak** melatih rakyat menganggur menjadi Tombak, Pemanah, atau Ksatria.
- **Tembok** (seret untuk satu baris), **Gerbang** (pasukanmu bisa lewat), **Menara** (memanah otomatis).
- **Pemanah di atas tembok/menara**: jangkauan +2 (menara +3), panah musuh berkurang 40%, dan tombak musuh tidak bisa menjangkau.
- **Air Mancur** menambah popularitas, jadi pajak bisa dinaikkan.
- Musuh datang dari barat lewat tiga titik dangkal sungai. Mulai gelombang 4 ada pendobrak, gelombang 5 juga dari utara, dan gelombang 6 ada ketapel yang menembak bangunan dari jauh.
- **Sang Penguasa**: pahlawanmu (600 HP). Pasukan dalam 3,5 petak darinya memberi kerusakan +20%. Jika ia gugur, kamu kalah. Di bawah 35% HP ia berlindung di dalam Benteng Utama, pulih, lalu keluar lagi; bisa juga disuruh masuk lewat panel unit.
- **Tangga pengepung** (mulai gelombang 3): Pembawa Tangga memasang tangga di tembok terdekat, lalu musuh memanjat masuk. Pemanah bisa menembak mereka di jalan; Tombak di atas tembok bertarung di tangga dan otomatis mendorongnya jatuh.
- **Jebakan** (seret untuk memasang) tersembunyi dari musuh. **Gerbang** bisa ditaruh di atas tembok.
- Ketuk **Benteng Utama** untuk 4 peningkatan (tembok, menara, busur, zirah) dan memperbaiki semua bangunan. Bangunan rusak bisa diperbaiki dengan batu, kecuali saat musuh dekat.
- Prajurit dilatih dengan emas + kayu. Palem tumbuh kembali perlahan di oasis.
- Skor dan bintang (1–3) per tingkat kesulitan, rekor tersimpan di perangkat. Menu jeda: suara, cara bermain, mulai ulang.
- Musik latar generatif (petikan ala oud di atas dengung, tabuhan rebana saat pertempuran), bisa dimatikan terpisah dari efek suara di menu jeda.
- Kartu tujuan/tutorial bisa dilipat dengan mengetuknya.
- Menu jeda: opsi **Grafik: hemat baterai** (kanvas resolusi 1×) untuk HP yang lebih lemah. Pasukan, tembok, dan bangunan digambar dari cache sprite, jadi biaya JavaScript per frame tetap rendah.
- Tiga tingkat kesulitan, daftar tujuan berhadiah untuk pemula, simpan otomatis tiap hari (tombol *Lanjutkan*), minimap, efek suara sintetis.

## Kontrol
| Aksi | HP | Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Geser peta | seret satu jari (dua jari saat membangun) | klik kanan + seret, WASD/panah |
| Zoom | cubit | roda mouse |
| Pilih pasukan | ketuk prajurit, "Semua pasukan", atau "Pilih kotak" | klik, atau seret kotak |
| Gerak / serang | ketuk tanah / ketuk musuh | klik kiri atau kanan |
| Pindah cepat | ketuk peta kecil / penunjuk musuh | sama |
| Pemanah ke tembok | tombol | F |
| Sang Penguasa | tombol Penguasa | L |
| Semua pasukan / ke benteng | tombol Pasukan / peta kecil | Q / H |
| Kecepatan | tombol 1× | 1, 2, 3 |
| Jeda / menu | tombol Jeda | Spasi, Esc |

jamesmoulding/the-verse.readme:
# The Verse website

Public site for the Verse megagame: the GNN bulletin, the rules and the faction pages.
Built with [Hugo](https://gohugo.io) and published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
every time something is pushed to `main`.

## Where things live

| What | File |
|---|---|
| Home page text | `content/_index.md` |
| Rules (the Game Guide) | `content/rules/_index.md` |
| Faction pages | `content/factions/<code>.md`, e.g. `utf.md` |
| GNN bulletins | `content/gnn/turn-NN.md`, e.g. `turn-11.md` |
| Diplomacy: Treaties & Trade | `content/diplomacy/treaties.md` |
| Diplomacy: Diplomatic Relations | `content/diplomacy/relations.md` |
| Diplomatic relation grid | `data/relations.yaml` |
| Library (background reading) | `content/library/*.md` |
| Map: star systems | `assets/map/systems.csv` |
| Map: founders, colours, grades | `data/founders.yaml`, `data/map_factions.yaml`, `data/grades.yaml` |
| Map: system descriptions | `data/descriptions.yaml` |
| Map: fleets and squadrons | `assets/map/units.csv` |
| Images | `static/images/` |
| QR code for player packs | `static/images/qr/the-verse-qr.png` (and `.svg` for print) |

## Adding a GNN bulletin

Create `content/gnn/turn-12.md` (two digits: `turn-09.md`, `turn-12.md`) starting with:

```
---
title: "GNN Bulletin 2602, Turn 12"
turn: 12
staryear: 2602
date: 2026-10-20
---
```

`date` is the real-world posting date, written year-month-day. Under the header, paste the
bulletin. Start each story with a headline line beginning `## `, for example
`## PFR FLEET SIGHTED OVER FELGOR`. Headlines become the bulletin's contents list, and any
headline naming a faction is listed on that faction's page automatically.

To add a story image, put it in `static/images/gnn/turn-12/` and add a line above the
story's headline, e.g. `![Proxima fleet over Felgor](/images/gnn/turn-12/01.jpg)`. Keep images
around 1200 pixels wide (JPEG) so pages stay quick on phones. The GNN masthead is added to every
bulletin automatically.

Commit and push. The site updates in about a minute; progress shows under the repository's
**Actions** tab.

## Faction pages

Player factions, other sovereign states and corporations all live in `content/factions/`.
`group: "state"` puts a page among the factions after the player factions, and
`group: "corporate"` puts it under **Major Corporate Entities**. `kind` is the line shown under
the name on its card, and `weight` sets the order.

`gnn_keywords` in a faction page's header lists the words that link GNN headlines to it.
The sovereign state and corporate pages use `gnn_mentions` instead, which searches the whole
text of every story, not just the headline.
`flag`, `portrait` and `caption` set its images.

## The 3D map

The Map page (`/map/`) draws every system from `assets/map/systems.csv`, one row per system.
Open it in a spreadsheet, edit, save as CSV and push. Columns:

| Column | What it is |
|---|---|
| `hex` | Map position, as on the Turn 9 map (e.g. `H6`) |
| `system` | System name, also used as the colony world name |
| `control` | Controlling power code (`AFCO`, `ASE`, `UNITY 5`, `IND` ...), from `data/map_factions.yaml` |
| `grade`, `sv` | Colony status code and Support Value |
| `population_m` | Population in millions (`0.05` = 50,000) |
| `planets`, `belts`, `m25_au` | Planets, asteroid belts, M25 limit in AU |
| `founder` | Founding corporation code, named in `data/founders.yaml` |
| `planet_type` | Close-up look: temperate, ocean, archipelago, storm-ocean, ocean-rocky, arid, desert, savannah, jungle, forest, alpine, ice, tundra, volcanic, toxic, barren, scorched, industrial or bionid. Parliament also shows the 3D Unity 5 station |
| `star_type` | Star colour and size: B, F, G, K or M. Illustrative, not canon |
| `gnn_terms` | Optional. A JavaScript regular expression for finding GNN stories about the system, used where the bare name would also match other things (e.g. Prime Minister) |
| `planet_note` | Where the planet look came from. Not shown on the site |

A system's details panel can be linked directly: `/map/#H6` opens Skaro.

The colony status decides what orbits a planet in close-up: a small station for BA, AC, AA, RC, VR
and CC colonies; two further small structures for RC, VR and CC; and ship traffic in proportion to
development (most for CC, a handful for AA, AC, BA and PC).

Descriptions in the panel come from `data/descriptions.yaml`, one line per system. Only add text
that players are allowed to know.

## Fleets and squadrons on the map

`assets/map/units.csv` holds one row per unit per turn. Columns: `turn`, `faction` (a code from
`data/map_factions.yaml`, including NPCs such as CASI, NSSF and BIONID), `name`, `category`
(`space`, `ground` or `bionid`), `unit_class`, `system` (system name or hex code), `status`,
`silent`, `public`.

A unit appears only if `public` is `yes`, `silent` is `no` and `status` is `based`. Units in
hyperspace (`transit`), under `repair`, under `construction` or with an `unknown` location stay
hidden. The map shows each unit's name, class and faction, never its strength, doctrine, ROE or
TEL. Keep one row per turn for each unit: the **Trails** button draws its moves between turns.
Pirates are not entered.

## Distance tools on the map

**Measure** plots a route between systems and shows, for each leg, the cost of leaving, the hexes
crossed and the cost of entering, in movement points and days, with any leg over 100 days flagged.
**Range** shades every system a unit could reach and enter within one turn. Each system's entry
cost is the `mp` column in `systems.csv` (1, 2 or 5; Skaro and Pheervaska are the Deep Gravity
Wells). Routes can be shared as links, e.g. `/map/#route=E18,H6,J8`.

## Diplomacy grid

The grid on the Diplomatic Relations page is drawn from `data/relations.yaml`. Each row lists that
faction's relationships: `T` trade agreement, `S` strategic trade, `W` war, `CF` ceasefire, `NA` non-aggression pact,
`AA` alliance, combined with a space (`T NA`). Le
