# Padel Legends

Tarayıcıda çalışan 3D padel oyunu (Three.js). 1–4 oyuncu, boş koltuklara AI, arkadaşlarla online.

## Hızlı başlangıç

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173 — tek başına / AI'ya karşı / aynı PC'de gamepad ile
npm run online     # build + oyun ve WebSocket sunucusu tek portta: http://localhost:8080
npm test           # kurallar, fizik, AI, replay testleri
```

İnternetten arkadaşlarla: `npm run online` sonra `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080`, çıkan linki paylaş. Herkes aynı **oda kodunu** girer, ev sahibi "MAÇA BAŞLA"ya basar. Boş koltuklar ve maç ortasında ayrılan oyuncular AI'ya geçer.

## Tarayıcıda oyna (GitHub Pages)

`main` dalına her yüklemede `.github/workflows/pages.yml` testleri çalıştırır, oyunu derler ve GitHub Pages'te yayınlar:
**https://mesut-outlook.github.io/Padel_Game/** — kurulum gerekmez, linki paylaşmak yeterli.

İlk kez açmak için depoda **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions** seçilmeli.
Pages sürümünde bilgisayara karşı maç, eğitim, menü ve kol desteği çalışır; **online mod** bir oyun sunucusu
(`npm run server`) ister — adrese `?server=wss://sunucu-adresi` eklenerek kendi sunucuna bağlanabilir.

## Kontroller

| Tuş | Eylem | Gamepad (Xbox) |
|---|---|---|
| WASD / oklar | hareket | sol çubuk |
| Space / J | vuruş (duruma göre drive/vole/bandeja/smaç) | A |
| K | lob (globo) | B |
| L | smaç | Y |
| U | chiquita | X |
| I | víbora | RB |
| F | slice servis | LB |
| O | contrapared: kendi camına vur, sekip karşıya geçsin (A/D basılı = sol/sağ yan cam, boş = arka cam) | RT |
| WASD (servis öncesi) | servis yerini kaydır (kendi yarısında, servis çizgisinin gerisinde) | sol çubuk |
| A/D (vururken) | topun yönü | sol çubuk |
| C | kamera: TV, oyuncu arkası, yan, tepe, top, drone, serbest | View (Back) |
| R / Esc | son sayının tekrarı / tekrarı geç | R3 / B |
| M | sesi aç/kapa | |
| Enter (maç bitince) | ana menüye dön | Start |

Menüdeki **Kontrol** seçimi 1. oyuncu için: *Klavye + Xbox kolu* (ikisi birden), *Sadece klavye* veya *Sadece Xbox kolu*. Diğer insan oyuncular kalan kolları sırayla alır.

**Servis:** yan duruş, raket başın arkasında, top öndeki elde → top bırakılır, yere seker ve bel altında alttan vurulur (FIP kuralı).
Menüdeki **Oyun hızı** (Yavaş / Normal / Hızlı) temel tempodur; üstüne AI seviyesi eklenir (Çaylak daha yavaş, Efsane daha hızlı) ve maç ilerledikçe tempo her oyunda biraz artar (en çok %12). Çaylak/Kulüp/Profesyonel seviyede, yön vermediğin anlarda oyuncun AI'nın duracağı yere doğru kendiliğinden yanaşır (yardım Efsane'de kapalı); vuruşları hep sen seçersin. Online maçlar sunucu hızında oynanır.

Uzun ralli, smaç veya camdan dönen toptan sonra yavaş çekim tekrar otomatik açılır.

## Eğitim

Menüde **🎓 EĞİTİM**: 14 derslik seri, gerçek oyun fiziği ve kurallarıyla (top makinesi topları sana atar, vuruşun gerçekten karşı sahaya düşerse sayılır). Talimatlar son kullandığın cihaza göre klavye ya da Xbox kolu tuşlarını gösterir; ilerleme tarayıcıda saklanır, Enter / Start dersi atlar.

Hareket · Servis · Slice servis · Forehand · Backhand · Yön verme · Lob · Chiquita · Vole · Smaç · Camdan oyun · Contrapared · Kamera ve tekrar · Mini maç (Çaylak AI'a karşı 3 sayı).

Kolun tarayıcıda nasıl göründüğünü test etmek için: http://localhost:5173/tools/padtest.html

## Özellikler

- **Giriş ekranı** (`src/menu.js`, `src/thumbs.js`): 5 sekmeli görsel menü (Mod · Oyuncu · Mekan · Raket · Maç). Karakter portreleri, mekan ve raket görselleri oyunun kendi 3D modellerinden üretilir. Solda seçili oyuncunun dönen 3D önizlemesi var. Fare, klavye ve Xbox koluyla gezilir (LB/RB sekme, A seç, B geri, Start başla).

- **Kurallar** (`src/rules.js`): FIP kortu, alttan çapraz servis, let, altın sayı / avantaj / Star Point (FIP 2026), tie-break (sonraki seti ilk karşılayan açar), süper tie-break, cam ve tel kuralları, servise vole yasağı.
- **Fizik** (`src/physics.js`): sürtünme, Magnus (topspin/slice), zemin/cam/tel ayrı sekme katsayıları, camda spin etkisi, filenin iki yanında yan kapılar (sekmeden sonra kapıdan çıkan top vurana sayı).
- **Vuruş pozları** (`src/player.js`): top yaklaşırken forehand / backhand / üstten (smaç, bandeja) hazırlığı, alçak topta eğilme; her vuruş hazırlık → temas → takip.
- **Vuruş koçu** (`src/main.js`): sana servis çizgisinin içinde üstten vurulabilecek bir top gelirse oyun yavaşlar, kamera oyuncunun arkasından topa bakar ve altta tuş önerisi çıkar (SMAÇ L · VÍBORA I · BANDEJA Space; kolda Y / RB / A). Gerideki yüksek toplarda, camdan dönen toplarda (bajada) ve rakipler fileyken (lob) yalnızca öneri gösterilir.
- **His** (`src/audio.js`, `src/main.js`): smaçta vurucunun arkasından alçak açı + yavaş çekim, hızlı topta hız izi ve yanından geçerken "vuuş" sesi; dosyasız WebAudio sesleri (raket, zemin, cam, tel, file, alkış), vuruşta kısa duraklama, smaçta kamera sarsıntısı, oyuncuların kısa sözleri (konuşma balonu + tarayıcı sesi).
- **AI** (`src/ai.js`): 4 seviye (çaylak → efsane), çiftlerde birlikte fileye çıkma/çekilme, top tahmini, vuruş seçimi, boşluğa nişan.
- **Karakterler** (`src/player.js`): kadın/erkek ince-atletik tenisçi gövdesi, 6 vücut tipi (ince, atletik, kaslı, iri, uzun, minyon), ten rengi, her karaktere özel görünüm (`data/characters.json`): saç (uzun, küt, topuz, at kuyruğu, kısa, seyrek, kel, samuray topuzu) ve rengi, sakal (tam / hafif / keçi) ve rengi, gözlük, makyaj, yüz genişliği, omuz genişliği, saç bandı / vizör, gerçek forma ve şort (vücutla hareket eden, yuvarlak yakalı, şeritli kumaş modelleri; kumaş vücut hatlarını göstermez), padel ayakkabısı, elde raket (yüzü önde, sap avuçta), solak/sağlak.
- **İçerik** (`data/`): 10 ülke/mekan, 26 karakter, 12 raket (yuvarlak/gözyaşı/elmas), turnuva formatları (Americano, Mexicano, King of the Court, lig, eleme) ve amatörden Premier Finals'a kariyer basamakları.

Geliştirici ve ana sponsor: **Mesut** (kort reklamları, file bandı, menü, skor tabelası).

# realroad

**🇫🇷 [Français](#-français) · 🇬🇧 [English](#-english) · 📘 [Tutoriel / Tutorial](docs/TUTORIAL.md) · 📍 [État / Status](docs/STATUS.md)**

Routes réelles → pistes de simulation, générées automatiquement à partir de
données ouvertes. / Real-world roads → driving-sim tracks, generated
automatically from open data.

Auteur / Author : **Aymeric Duchene**

| En jeu — départ de Saint-Vallier / In game — leaving Saint-Vallier | Après l'épingle / After the hairpin |
|---|---|
| ![start](docs/img/ingame/01-start.jpg) | ![hairpin](docs/img/ingame/02-after-hairpin.jpg) |

*Premier essai (v0.1) : géométrie réelle, textures du terrain encore à régler. / First drive (v0.1): real geometry, terrain textures still to fix.*

![Bords mesurés / Measured edges](docs/img/edges_overlay.png)

![Marquages réels / Real markings](docs/img/road_markings.png)

*Marquages détectés (rouge : rive droite, vert : axe, bleu : rive gauche) sur l'orthophoto « déroulée » ; en haut, tout le tracé : blanc = continu, jaune = pointillés, gris = rien. / Detected markings (red: right edge, green: centre, blue: left edge) on the unrolled orthophoto; top, the whole road: white = continuous, yellow = dashed, grey = none.*

| Profil LiDAR de la route / LiDAR road profile | Route « déroulée » / Unrolled road |
|---|---|
| ![profile](docs/img/road_profile.png) | ![unrolled](docs/img/edges_unrolled.png) |

---

## 🇫🇷 Français

### L'idée

Rouler dans un simulateur (Assetto Corsa) sur les routes qu'on connaît, avec
leur vraie géométrie : pente, dévers, virages, bosses. Au lieu de modéliser
chaque route à la main pendant des mois, `realroad` la génère à partir des
données publiques de l'IGN (LiDAR HD, BD TOPO, orthophotos) et
d'OpenStreetMap.

Premier tronçon : **Route Napoléon (D6085), Saint-Vallier-de-Thiey →
Escragnolles** (17,4 km, Pas de la Faye à ~980 m).

### Installation (Windows)

```powershell
cd realroad
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Utilisation

Le tronçon se décrit dans `config.yaml` (points de départ/arrivée, numéro de
route, largeur du couloir…). Ensuite, une seule commande :

```powershell
python realroad.py --install "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\assettocorsa"
```

Elle enchaîne toutes les étapes, qu'on peut aussi lancer une par une :

```powershell
python fetch.py osm      # tracé (OpenStreetMap, sinon BD TOPO IGN)
python fetch.py mnt      # relief LiDAR HD 50 cm (~16 Mo par km²)
python fetch.py ortho    # photos aériennes 20 cm
python fetch.py lidar    # nuage de points du couloir (~10 min, ~120 Mo gardés)
python fetch.py far      # relief et photos à basse résolution sur ~8 km (l'horizon)
python fetch.py mnh      # hauteur de la végétation (LiDAR HD) pour les arbres
python fetch.py buildings  # bâtiments BD TOPO (emprise, hauteurs)
python fetch.py streetview # photos 360° Panoramax le long de la route
python road_profile.py   # vrai profil de la chaussée : altitude, dévers, ponts
python road_edges.py     # vrais bords de la chaussée : largeur et centre réels
python road_markings.py  # vrais marquages : ligne centrale et lignes de rive
python trees.py          # vrais arbres : position, hauteur, couronne, essence
python build_track.py    # géométrie de la piste (route, marquages, terrain, départs AC)
python kn5_export.py --install "<dossier assettocorsa>"   # piste AC complète
python streetview_sheet.py # planche « vue conducteur » tous les 250 m, pour comparer avec le jeu
```

`kn5_export.py` écrit directement le `.kn5` (plus besoin de Blender ni de
ksEditor), l'AI line, la minimap, les caméras de replay et les vignettes de
Content Manager. `python realroad.py --from build_track` ne relance que les
dernières étapes.

Les téléchargements reprennent là où ils s'étaient arrêtés.
Les données vont dans `data/<nom-du-tronçon>/` (ignoré par Git).

### Comment ça marche

| Étape | Source | Détail |
|---|---|---|
| Tracé | OSM (Overpass) ou BD TOPO | Plus court chemin entre départ et arrivée sur les tronçons portant le numéro de route ; les ronds-points sans numéro sont recousus (≤ 60 m). |
| Relief | MNT LiDAR HD | Dalles 1 km², GeoTIFF float32 au pas de 50 cm, listées par la couche WFS `IGNF_LIDAR-HD_METADONNEE:metadata`. |
| Ponts | MNT | Le MNT est le sol nu et plonge sous les ponts : creux étroits repérés et interpolés (aperçu). La vraie altitude viendra des points LiDAR classe 17. |
| Profil route | Nuage LiDAR | Stations tous les 1 m ; droite robuste z = z0 + c·t sur ±2,5 m autour de l'axe → altitude, dévers, rugosité. Tabliers de pont (classe 17) prioritaires ; axe signalé suspect si dévers > 12 % ou rms > 12 cm. |
| Bords de chaussée | LiDAR + orthophoto + BD TOPO | Lignes de rive (pics d'intensité LiDAR + blanc sur l'ortho) → bord = ligne + 0,3 m ; ligne cachée reconstruite par symétrie autour de la ligne centrale ; saut d'intensité LiDAR dans le relief sinon ; BD TOPO comme garde-fou. Largeur médiane 7,35 m (6,3–9 m) sur la Route Napoléon. |
| Marquages | Orthophoto + LiDAR | Ligne centrale et lignes de rive suivies mètre par mètre (pic blanc sur l'ortho + pic d'intensité LiDAR), découpées en tronçons continus / pointillés / absents ; pointillés gardés là où ils sont vus, complétés au pas local. Bandes blanches 2 cm au-dessus du bitume. |
| Arbres | MNH LiDAR HD + orthophoto | Sommets = maxima locaux de la hauteur de végétation lissée (fenêtre qui grandit avec la hauteur), rayon de couronne lu sur le MNH, pin / feuillu / arbuste selon la hauteur et la couleur sur l'ortho ; billboards croisés (shader ksTree), textures générées dans les couleurs de l'ortho. ~50-120 arbres/ha mesurés sur le tracé. |
| Bâtiments | BD TOPO | Emprise extrudée du sol à l'égout (altitude_minimale_toit), toit à deux pans jusqu'au faîtage réel sur les emprises quasi rectangulaires, toit plat sinon ; toits texturés par l'orthophoto (vraies couleurs), façades génériques. |
| Photos de rue | Panoramax (IGN, Etalab 2.0) | Photos 360° de la route (IGN, avril 2026, tout

Add road_edges.py: measure the real carriageway edges from the LiDAR

The width came from BD TOPO (one value per segment, rounded to the metre:
7 m almost everywhere). road_edges.py measures it: ground points within
+/-10 m are binned per 1 m station in 12.5 cm bins (mean height and laser
intensity), pooled over 5 stations. Walking outwards on each side, a bin is

rupertclaw/questionable-journey.readme:
# Questionable Journey

A fantasy trivia board game for 1 to 6 players on one device. Answer a question correctly to roll the die and march along the road from the village of Hearthmoor, through Whisperwood, the Frostfang Peaks and Mirefen Marsh, to the gate of the Dragon's Keep. Answer the Gate Riddle to win.

Each player picks a level, so kids and grown-ups can play together:

| Level | Ages | Questions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Young Adventurer | 5–9 | Our own kids' pack, three answer choices |
| Adventurer | 10–14 | Open Trivia DB "easy" |
| Sage | 15+ | Open Trivia DB "medium" and "hard" |

## Files

- `index.html` — the whole game (board, rules, sounds). No build step, no server.
- `questions.js` — the question bank the game loads. **Generated; don't edit by hand.**
- `data/kids-pack.txt` — our own questions. Add more here, one per line: `question | right answer | wrong 1 | wrong 2 | wrong 3`.
- `data/opentdb-raw.json` — the Open Trivia DB download.
- `tools/build-bank.js` — rebuilds `questions.js` from the two data files: `node tools/build-bank.js`
- `tools/fetch-opentdb.js` — re-downloads Open Trivia DB (about 10 minutes): `node tools/fetch-opentdb.js`
- `tools/serve.js` — plays the game locally at http://localhost:5179: `node tools/serve.js`

## Credits

Questions for the Adventurer and Sage levels come from [Open Trivia DB](https://opentdb.com), licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). If you change or add to those questions, that question set must be shared under the same licence. The kids' pack in `data/kids-pack.txt` is original.

carinaburana/gotta-match-em-all.desc: A satirical alien dating-app game about engagement-driven matchmaking. React + TypeScript + Vite.
carinaburana/gotta-match-em-all.readme:
# Gotta Match 'Em All 👽💜

A playful, mobile-first web game that satirises dating apps, "AI-powered" matchmaking and
engagement-driven algorithms.

Players create an alien dating profile, pick three interests, watch a (completely fake) AI
matchmaking sequence and get introduced to **THE ONE** — their supposedly perfect match. Then they
swipe through alien profiles for 60 seconds, collecting points for matches and losing points for
matching with unverified profiles.

**The twist: THE ONE never appears.** The app keeps you swiping for someone it will never show you.
See [docs/GAME_DESIGN.md](docs/GAME_DESIGN.md) for the idea behind it.

This is a single-session demonstrator (about 1–2 minutes), not a real dating platform. There is no
backend, no accounts, no real AI and no data collection.

## Tech stack

| Purpose     | Tool                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| UI          | React 19 + TypeScript (strict)    |
| Build / dev | Vite                              |
| Styling     | Tailwind CSS v4                   |
| Animation   | Motion for React (`motion/react`) |
| Code style  | ESLint + Prettier                 |
| Content     | Local JSON files in `src/data/`   |
| Hosting     | Vercel (static site)              |

## Requirements

- **Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+** (22 recommended — see `.nvmrc`)
- npm (comes with Node)

## Getting started

```bash
git clone <repo-url>
cd gotta-match-em-all
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the URL Vite prints (usually http://localhost:5173). To try it on your phone, run
`npm run dev -- --host` and open the "Network" URL on a phone in the same Wi-Fi.

## Commands

| Command             | What it does                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | Start the dev server with hot reload                             |
| `npm run build`     | Type-check and create a production build in `dist/`              |
| `npm run preview`   | Serve the production build locally                               |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check only                                            |
| `npm run lint`      | ESLint (`npm run lint:fix` fixes what it can)                    |
| `npm run format`    | Format everything with Prettier (`format:check` only checks)     |
| `npm run check`     | **Run before every PR:** typecheck + lint + format check + build |

There are no automated tests by design; quality comes from static checks, a successful build and
manually playing through the game.

### Reproducible runs

Add `?seed=1234` to the URL (e.g. `http://localhost:5173/?seed=1234`) to get the same deck every
time — handy for demos and bug reports. A default seed can also be set in `src/game/config.ts`.

## Deploying to Vercel

1. Push the repository to GitHub.
2. In Vercel, **Add New → Project** and import the repository.
3. Framework preset: **Vite** (detected automatically).
4. Build command: `npm run build` · Output directory: `dist`.
5. Deploy. Every push to `main` redeploys; pull requests get preview URLs.

No environment variables are needed.

## Where things live

| You want to…                              | Go to                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Change timer, points, probabilities, deck | `src/game/config.ts`                                                        |
| Edit names, cities, bios, interests       | `src/data/*.json` ([how](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#editing-content-json))        |
| Change a screen                           | `src/screens/`                                                              |
| Change the swipe card                     | `src/components/cards/`                                                     |
| Change colours / fonts                    | `src/styles/index.css` (`@theme` block)                                     |
| Understand the code structure             | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)                                |
| Understand the rules                      | [docs/GAME_MECHANICS.md](docs/GAME_MECHANICS.md)                            |
| Visual direction                          | [docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md](docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) · mockups in `docs/mockups/` |
| Team workflow (branches, PRs)             | [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)                                |

## Adding assets

- **Alien portraits:** add `public/aliens/alien-001.webp` … and list each file in
  `src/data/alien-portraits.json`. Details: [public/aliens/README.md](public/aliens/README.md).
- **Player avatars:** `public/avatars/` + `src/data/player-avatars.json`.
- **THE ONE teaser video:** save it as `public/videos/the-one-teaser.mp4`. Until then a placeholder
  is shown. Details: [public/videos/README.md](public/videos/README.md).

## Implementation status

| Area                       | Status                                                          |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App flow (6 screens)       | ✅ Working                                                      |
| Profile setup              | ✅ Name, exactly 3 interests by category, 1 of 4 avatars        |
| Deck generation            | ✅ 100 cards, seeded, 70% normal / 10% special / 20% unverified |
| Swipe loop, score, timer   | ✅ Drag, buttons and ←/→ keys; 60 s countdown                   |
| Match feedback             | 🟡 Simple placeholder overlays                                  |
| AI searching sequence      | 🟡 Placeholder radar animation, configurable text               |
| THE ONE teaser             | 🟡 Video slot + placeholder (video not supplied yet)            |
| Results screen             | 🟡 Placeholder stats list — final ending not decided

pratik-j-mahajan/The-Jantar-Mantar-Run.readme:
# द जंतर मंतर रन — The Jantar Mantar Run

**Play it:** https://the-jantar-mantar-run.vercel.app

A satirical, comic-style arcade run down a Delhi road to Jantar Mantar. It looks 3D but is drawn on a plain 2D canvas. You pick a protester and weave past police bus blockades, riot units, barricades and the orange-shirt stick squad, while a YouTube reporter and his camera person chase the story along the footpath.

Created by **Pratik Mahajan**, Product Designer · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pratik-j-mahajan/)

---

## How to play

Reach the Jantar Mantar gate at the end of the road.

| | Desktop | Phone |
|---|---|---|
| Move left / right | hold ← → (or A / D) | hold ◀ ▶, or swipe for a quick dash |
| Run forward / step back | hold ↑ / ↓ (or W / S) | hold ▲ / ▼ |
| Jump | Space | JUMP button, or swipe up |
| Back to character select | Esc, or the ← BACK button | ← BACK button |
| Start / retry | Enter | tap the placard |

**Rules**
- **Barricades:** jump over them. Buses, vans, trucks and water cannons are solid, so go around them.
- **Police and paramilitary:** if one catches you, you're **detained**. Two officers carry you into a van (5 seconds), then you sit through a 5-second countdown and are released a little way back.
- **Stick squad:** a hit costs **50% जान** (health). A second hit means **game over**.
- **Jumping:** you can't be caught while high in a jump.
- **Your pace:** there's no auto-run. You choose when to sprint and when to wait for a gap.

## What's in the game

- **Five characters:** Neha, Abhijit, NSUI, GenZ and the Ex Minister. Each has its own design and props, and speed varies slightly.
- **Delhi street, golden hour:** shopfronts with Hindi/English signboards, AC units and hanging wires, colonnaded government buildings, neem trees, autos ("Horn OK Please"), chai stalls, dharna tents, a protest stage, flags and slogan banners.
- **A chowk:** a roundabout with a fountain and a tall tricolour about halfway along.
- **Police presence:** DTC and Dilli Police buses parked across the road as blockades, lines of officers with shields, blue- and olive-camo riot units, troop trucks, water cannons, and police vans that charge at you.
- **Media crew:** "Samdish · Unfiltered" and "Camera Person Parth" run along the footpath with police on their heels. When you're detained, they rush in to film and interview.
- **Finish:** the Jantar Mantar compound, with the Samrat Yantra, the curved quadrants and the Ram Yantra, plus marigold petals and a "जंतर मंतर / GenZ" win banner.
- **Soundtrack:** generated live. A daphli protest beat, call-and-response chants ("In-qui-lab! / Zin-da-baad!", "Hum de-khen-ge!", "Aa-waaz do! / Hum ek hain!"), crowd claps, bansuri and harmonium, plus police whistles, sirens, auto horns and a temple bell. The mute button is in the HUD.

This is a lighthearted satire. Every character is a generic cartoon, and the music is original, not copied from any real recording or song.

---

## Tech

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no framework and no image or audio assets. The art is drawn with canvas vector code and cached as sprite frames; the sound is synthesized with WebAudio.

```
index.html            page, screens, HUD, GA4 snippet, social meta tags
style.css             comic-poster UI (banner title, placard buttons, HUD, panels)
js/audio.js           music + sound effects (daphli, chants, bansuri, harmonium, whistle, siren, bell)
js/sprites.js         characters, police, paramilitary, stick squad, crowd, media crew; sprite cache
js/engine.js          2.5D renderer: chase camera, lit boxes, texture-mapped faces, billboards,
                      shadows; adaptive quality levels
js/props.js           textures: Delhi facades, buses, vans, trucks, autos, barricades, banners,
                      tents, trees, asphalt, pavers
js/world.js           level layout (blockades, chowk, set dressing) + world rendering
js/game.js            game states, input, AI, detention sequence, media crew, effects, HUD,
                      analytics, idle sprite pre-rendering
fonts/                self-hosted, subsetted woff2 (Yatra One, Bangers, Baloo 2)
og-image.jpg          1200×630 share preview, rendered from the game itself
apple-touch-icon.png  home-screen icon
sw.js                 service worker (repeat visits load from the device)
build.mjs             production build → dist/
vercel.json           Vercel build + cache headers
netlify.toml          Netlify build config
```

### Run locally

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Then open http://localhost:8080. The source files run as-is, with no build needed.

### Production build

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

`dist/` gets one minified JS file and one CSS file with content-hashed names, the fonts, the images, a versioned service worker, and cache headers for Vercel and Netlify. The first visit downloads about **45 KB gzipped of code** plus about **90 KB of fonts**. Code and fonts are cached for a year, so repeat visits load from the device. If esbuild is missing, the build still succeeds; it just skips minification.

### Deploy

- **Vercel** (current host): import the repo at vercel.com/new and click Deploy. `vercel.json` sets everything up, and every push to `main` redeploys.
- **Netlify:** connect the repo; `netlify.toml` builds automatically.
- **Cloudflare Pages:** set the build command to `npm run build` and the output to `dist`.

### Performance

- **Built for heavy traffic:** everything runs in the player's browser, so there is no game server to overload; the CDN just serves static files.
- **Fast start:** fonts are preloaded from the same origin, and Google Analytics loads only after the game is ready. The game is playable in under a second on a normal connection.
- **No stutter mid-run:** character poses are pre-rendered in idle time.
- **Resolution budget:** big and Retina screens render at a capped pixel count (about 2.4 MP at full quality) and are upscaled smoothly, so a 4K monitor cos

# Backstage

Crew scheduling for High Five Games, at **https://backstage.highfive.games**.

- **Showtimes**: day grid like the old Google Sheet: 15-minute rows, an Unscheduled column and one column
  per crew member. Schedulers click an empty slot to add a game there.
- **Games**: upcoming, unscheduled and past games, with search.
- **My games**: your upcoming games and history.
- **Crew**: everyone's details (schedulers); approve accounts and change roles (super admin).
- **Profile**: name, phone, preferred payment method and payout email/handle. No bank details.
- **Time zones**: the clock dropdown in the top bar switches every time on the site to any time zone
  (remembered per device; defaults to the device's zone). Games are stored as exact instants, so
  everyone sees the same game at the right local time, including across daylight saving changes.

## Roles

| Role | Can |
|---|---|
| Super admin | Everything, including approving accounts and changing roles |
| Scheduler | Add/edit/delete games, assign anyone (including themselves), see crew contact info |
| Crew (employee) | See the schedule and all games, see their own history, edit their own profile |

New sign-ups are **pending** and see nothing until a super admin approves them on the Crew page.
Permissions are enforced by the database (row-level security), not just hidden in the page.

## How it's built

Static site (GitHub Pages) + Supabase for accounts and the database. No build step.

```
index.html               page shell
assets/app.js            the app (screens, schedule grid, game editor)
assets/api.js            data layer: Supabase, or an in-memory demo with ?demo
assets/config.js         Supabase URL + anon (public) key
supabase/schema.sql      tables, roles and security rules, run once in the Supabase SQL editor
supabase/test/           local tests for the security rules (stub of Supabase auth + checks)
```

Try it without signing in: open `/?demo` (sample data, nothing saved). `?demo&as=u3` shows the
employee view, `as=u2` the scheduler and `as=u5` a pending account.

## Setup (one time)

1. **Database**: Supabase → SQL Editor → New query → paste `supabase/schema.sql` → Run.
2. **Auth settings**: Supabase → Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email: turn **Confirm email**
   off (accounts are approved by a super admin instead). Under Authentication → URL Configuration set
   **Site URL** to `https://backstage.highfive.games`.
3. **First super admin**: sign up on the site, then in the SQL Editor run:
   `update public.profiles set role = 'super_admin', active = true where email = 'you@example.com';`
4. **Domain**: DNS CNAME `backstage` → `highfivegamesdev-cell.github.io`; repo Settings → Pages → deploy
   from `main` / root, custom domain `backstage.highfive.games`, then Enforce HTTPS.

Password reset emails use Supabase's built-in mailer, which only delivers to a few addresses and a few
emails per hour. For the whole team, add your own SMTP (Authentication → Emails → SMTP settings).

## Testing the security rules locally

```sh
cat supabase/test/supabase_stub.sql supabase/schema.sql supabase/test/policies_test.sql | psql <fresh database>
```
Ends with `ALL POLICY TESTS PASSED`.

# sqfangame — 「아보르 프로토콜」(가제)

아틀라스 「세계수의 미궁(Etrian Odyssey)」 시리즈의 비공식 팬게임. 신작을 기다리던 팬이 직접 만드는 2차 창작 후속작으로, 1인칭 그리드 탐사·손으로 그리는 지도·FOE·5인 직업 파티와 원작의 그림체를 이어받아 "사이버네틱한 세계수의 미궁"을 그린다: 사이버네틱 몸 위에 홀로그램으로 판타지 기사·마법사의 모습을 투사한다.

- 비영리 팬 프로젝트이며 ATLUS·SEGA와 관계없는 비공식 2차 창작이다.
- 원작 스타일(그림체·UI 문법·세계관 모티브·시리즈 용어)을 레퍼런스로 삼아 드러낸다. 그림·음악·문장은 새로 만들고, 원작 게임에서 추출한 파일은 넣지 않는다.
- 엔진: Godot 4.7.2-stable (`godot` 명령, 경로를 바꿀 때는 `${GODOT:-godot}`)
- 1차 대상: 웹 빌드 (확인 편의). 렌더러는 웹에서 동작하는 Compatibility(WebGL 2)를 쓴다.

## 문서

- `docs/design/00-decisions.md`: 사용자 결정 기록
- `docs/research/`: 원작 시리즈 시스템 조사 자료 (`README.md`에 작성 경위와 원문 대조 기록)
- `docs/design/01-game-design.md`: 게임 기획 (방향, 범위, 탐색·전투·직업·마을·성장·저장 규칙)
- `docs/design/02-tech-plan.md`: 기술 계획 (Godot 웹, 코드 구조, 데이터, 시험, 배포)
- `docs/design/03-production-plan.md`: 그림 에셋 제작과 단계(M0~M3)별 수용 기준
- `docs/design/04-world-and-art-direction.md`: 세계관(사이버펑크 + 마법)과 아트 방향
- `docs/CLOUD_TESTS.md`: 무거운 시험을 클라우드로 보내는 기준과 방법

## 개발

| 할 일 | 명령 |
|---|---|
| 처음 한 번(가져오기) | `godot --headless --import` |
| 규칙 시험 | `godot --headless -s tests/run.gd` (실패하면 종료 코드 1) |
| 웹 빌드 | `tools/export_web.sh` → `build/web/` |
| 웹 캡처 | `npm install` 뒤 `flock /tmp/voxel-test-heavy.lock xvfb-run -a node tools/shot.mjs build/shot.png 1280x720 20` |
| 컨셉 그림 비교 시트 | `python3 tools/concept_sheet.py <출력.jpg> "<이름>=<그림>" ...` (아랫줄에 게임 화면 크기 판을 붙임, `assets/concept/compare/`) |
| 텍스처 이음새 | `python3 tools/tile_check.py check <그림>...` / `preview <그림> <출력>` / `fix <그림> <출력> --size 512` |
| 휴대폰 확인 | `python3 tools/serve_web.py` (127.0.0.1:8765, 큰 파일 gzip) 뒤 `cloudflared` 임시 주소 (`docs/CLOUD_TESTS.md`) |
| 클라우드 시험 | `tools/cloud/test.sh --push --wait` (`docs/CLOUD_TESTS.md`) |

- 글꼴: `assets/fonts/NotoSansKR-Regular-subset.otf` (Noto Sans CJK KR에서 ASCII·한글 음절·자모·문장부호만 남김, SIL OFL 1.1, `assets/fonts/OFL.txt`).
- 그림의 `.import` 설정을 손으로 고치면 `godot --headless --import` 가 다시 가져오지 않는다. `.godot/imported/<파일 이름>-*` 를 지우고 가져온다.
- Godot 는 프로젝트 폴더 전체를 가져온다. `node_modules/`·`build/`·`tmp/` 에는 `.gdignore` 를 둔다(`docs/CLOUD_TESTS.md`).

ldo2x/dahoom.readme:
# منصة دحوم v2 — ألف نقطة + خلية الحروف

موقع ثابت (HTML/CSS/JS) بدون سيرفر. افتح `index.html` في المتصفح، أو شغّله بسيرفر بسيط:
`python -m http.server 5517` وافتح http://localhost:5517

النسخة القديمة محفوظة كما هي في مجلد `dahoom ن1`.

## وش الجديد في v2
- **هوية جديدة:** صالة أركيد بنفسجية ليلية، خطوط Reem Kufi + IBM Plex Sans Arabic + Bungee للأرقام، وبطاقات تريدنق هولوغرافية.
- **صفر إيموجي:** كل الأيقونات من game-icons.net (CC BY 3.0) في `assets/icons`.
- **46 بطاقة بأسماء ترندات ونكت ومقولات سعودية** (`data/cards.js`) — جاك بوت، شلوطة تايم، اصرمني، يا سلام، الجمرة، روح انت أول، أراهنك، نسخ لصق، عين وصابتك، القطة، الواسطة… وصورها منوعة: مقاطع سعودية (تلفاز11)، قيمنق، أفلام، رياكشنز، وبطاقات على شكل تغريدة.
- **أصوات التطبيق كلها قيمنق وميمز** (`assets/sfx/game`): مذيع Unreal Tournament للسلاسل (Double Kill لين Godlike)، Finish Him لما أحد يوصل الهدف، تنبيه Metal Gear للسرقة، موسيقى Jeopardy للمؤقت، وأصوات سعودية لكل بطاقة.
- **خمس أنواع بطاقات:** هجوم، دفاع، دعم، فوضى، ورد فعل (تنلعب برا دورك لحظة الهجوم: العب غيرها، طنّش).
- **ميكانيكيات جديدة:** شلوطة تايم وعين وصابتك (تضرب المتصدر)، كأنك يا بو زيد ما غزيت (تمسح آخر كسب)، روح انت أول (تبديل الدور)، الجمرة (تنتقل لين تنفجر)، أراهنك، نسخ لصق، يا سلام، طقطقة (تختار الهدف)، خذ وهات، القطة، الواسطة، هياط، مقلب، سواليف، دمج السودا، ودفعة الرجعة للفريق المتأخر 300+.
- **ميمز اللحظات:** ردود فعل GIF بصيغة webp في `assets/memes` + أصوات ميمز للصح/الغلط/السرقة/الفوز.

## التحكم من الجوال
- الرابط: https://ldo2x.github.io/dahoom/ — افتحه على الشاشة/التلفزيون.
- اضغط **الجوالات** (في صفحة اللاعبين أو أثناء اللعب) يطلع كود من 4 حروف و QR.
- كل فريق يفتح `remote.html` من جواله (أو يصوّر الـQR) ويختار فريقه.
- الجوال: زر **BUZZ** (السرقة، بدون كلام، خلية الحروف)، بطاقات الفريق سرّية ويلعبها من الجوال، ويجاوب على الرهان وردود الفعل واختيار الهدف.
- الاتصال مباشر بين الأجهزة (WebRTC عن طريق PeerJS وسيرفره المجاني) — يحتاج إنترنت بس، ما فيه سيرفر خاص.
- لو جوال فصل، الشاشة تعرض زر "اختيار من الشاشة" فاللعب ما يوقف.

## ميزان البطاقات (تقريبي، بالنقاط مقارنة بالخصم)
| الفئة | العدد | نسبة السحب | القيمة |
|---|---|---|---|
| حمراء | 7 | 8% | 120–180 |
| ذهبية | 16 | 26% | 60–100 |
| زرقاء | 18 | 50% | 30–50 |
| سودا | 5 | 16% | 0 (ادمج سودتين = زرقا) |

**مراحل المباراة:** البداية (المتصدر تحت 35% من الهدف) والوسط (لين 75%) والنهاية. بطاقات كل مرحلة تنسحب أكثر بوقتها وتلمع باليد، وبعضها أقوى فيه (رأس مال، زاد الطريق بالبداية · خلك برا السالفة وخذ وهات بالوسط · الضربة القاضية، على وين؟، ما بقى شي بالنهاية).

كل النسب والخيارات (رد الفعل، الدمج، دفعة الرجعة، المؤثرات) تتعدل من الإعدادات قبل المباراة.

## تحديث المحتوى
نفس صيغة v1 في `data/questions.js` و`charades.js` و`challenges.js` و`letters-*.js`.
بطاقة جديدة: أضف سطر في `data/cards.js` وحط صورتها `assets/cards/<id>.webp` و`<id>_s.gif`.
ميم جديد للحظات: حط الملف في `assets/memes` واكتب اسمه في `data/memes.js`.

## المصادر
- صور البطاقات والميمز: GIPHY (معرّفاتها في `assets/cards/_giphy_ids.json`)
- أصوات الميمز والقيمنق والمقاطع السعودية: myinstants.com — أصوات اللعب الأساسية: Mixkit
- الأيقونات: game-icons.net (CC BY 3.0) — الأفاتارات: DiceBear Big Smile (CC BY 4.0)

Pineman-PPAP/ECHO.readme:
# ECHO

**A horror escape game played in total darkness, controlled only by your voice and your head.**
No keyboard, no mouse, no controller: a webcam and a microphone are the whole input.

- **Sound is sight.** A clap, click or knock sends out a sonar wave that briefly reveals the cave. Louder = further.
- **Every clap is a bet.** The Hollows are blind and hunt by sound: every creature in earshot runs to where you clapped. See the cave, then move.
- **Humming wakes the fireflies.** You carry a visible jar of fireflies in your left hand throughout play. A steady hum wakes them: they swirl and glow, lighting the rock all around you (louder = brighter and further). Only a Hollow right next to you hears a hum. Stop humming, and their glow gently diminishes to darkness over about 1.5 seconds; the jar remains held on screen.

## Status: finished ✅

ECHO is complete and playable start to finish, hands-free:

- **Input:** face tracking (head turn + lean to walk) and audio (claps, clicks, hums), with a guided calibration for each new player.
- **Game:** a tutorial and three levels (Awakening, The Listener, The Choir), blind Hollows that hunt by sound, the Hush, breakable pots and the Stalker.
- **Look and sound:** sonar-lit rock caves, creature artwork, a filmed jumpscare when you are caught, and 3D positional audio.
- **Quality:** typecheck + unit tests (`npm run check`) and the production build pass.

Quick start: `cd echo && npm install && npm run assets && npm run dev`, then open http://127.0.0.1:5173 in Chrome with headphones on.

---

## Controls

| You do | The game sees | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Clap / tongue click / knock | Mic: sharp rise followed by a short percussive decay | Sonar pulse; loudness sets its radius and how far creatures hear it (4–34 m). Hollows in earshot run to that spot |
| Hum a steady note | Mic: pitch (YIN) + steadiness + level | Fireflies in the jar wake and light the cave around you; loudness → brightness and reach (3.5–9 m), pitch → how excitedly they swirl. Heard only within ~5 m |
| Turn your head | Head yaw | Turn left / right |
| Lean toward / away from the screen | Face distance vs. calibrated rest | Walk forward / back. A gentle lean is silent; a full lean makes footsteps heard up to 10 m |
| Leave the camera | No face for 0.4 s | Game pauses |

Menus are hands-free too: **clap = confirm**. The only mouse click is "Begin" (browsers require a click before granting camera, mic and audio).

---

## Run it

Requirements: Chrome or Chromium, a webcam, a microphone, **headphones (required: on speakers the game hears its own sounds)**, and a lit face. Built and tested on an Intel i7-13620H laptop with integrated graphics (Linux).

```bash
cd echo
npm install
npm run assets   # one-time: downloads the MediaPipe runtime + face model into public/ (then it runs offline)
npm run demo     # production build, opens full-screen Chrome/Chromium on http://127.0.0.1:4173
```

| Script (in `echo/`) | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Dev server on `http://127.0.0.1:5173` |
| `npm run demo` | Build + preview server + full-screen browser with its own profile. `npm run demo -- '?debug=1'` adds the pipeline panel. Close the window to stop |
| `npm run assets` | Fetches the MediaPipe wasm and `face_landmarker.task` (no network needed at runtime) |
| `npm run check` | TypeScript check + 170 unit tests (vitest) |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck + production build into `dist/` |

**URL flags:** `?debug=1` pipeline/debug panel (toggle with the backtick key) · `?level=N` start at level N (0 = tutorial) · `?skipcal=1` skip calibration · `?manual=0` skip the Field Manual · `?sim=1` keyboard input, **development only**.

**New player:** reload the page (F5) and click Begin; that reruns calibration. Venue setup (power mode, mic gain, symptom → setting table): [`DEMO_TUNING.md`](DEMO_TUNING.md).

---

## How it works

### Pipeline (one animation frame)

```
webcam 640x480@30 ─▶ MediaPipe FaceLandmarker (GPU) ─▶ head yaw, face depth, presence  ─┐
                                                                                             ├─▶ IntentBuilder ─▶ PlayerIntent ─▶ World.update() ─▶ Renderer (three.js)
mic (no AGC / noise suppression) ─▶ MicAnalyzer: 128-sample hops ─▶ noise floor, onsets,   ─┘    + calibration                    (pure game logic)   Sfx (Web Audio, HRTF 3D)
                                     YIN pitch, hum detector                                                                                         HUD + debug panel
```

The game logic never touches a sensor: it only receives a `PlayerIntent` (turn rate, move speed, pulses, hum, face present). The same intent can come from the keyboard (`?sim=1`) for development, which is how the game logic is unit-tested.

### Input processing (`echo/src/input/`)

- **Face** (`face/`): MediaPipe Tasks Vision 0.10.35, GPU delegate with CPU fallback. The face transformation matrix gives head yaw and depth; both are smoothed with One-Euro filters. Yaw drives a turn *rate* (dead zone, then a curve), so you can keep looking at the screen while turning. Lean = rest depth / current depth − 1.
- **Mic** (`audio/`): processed in 128-sample hops. A percentile noise floor tracks the room. A sharp rise starts a clap candidate, which must decay at least 8 dB for 5 ms within 75 ms and have a percussive peak before it emits an **onset**. This rejects sustained room-noise increases and abrupt hums; measured claps usually confirm in a few tens of milliseconds. The player's calibrated clap also filters out much fainter transients. Actual nearby claps can still resemble player claps to a single microphone. A **hum** is a voiced YIN pitch that stays steady (small pitch spread) above the floor.
- **Calibration** (`calibration.ts`, ~45 s, hands-free): face check, quiet room (noise floor), neutral pose, look left (measures the yaw sign), a normal clap and a normal hum (loudness references), and a speaker-leak test. Each step first says wha

jasisz/ceo-tycoon.readme:
# CEO Tycoon

Satirical isometric tycoon where you're a C-level exec whose real goal is FIRE — via an honest IPO
or by quietly wiring "consulting fees" to Zug. An LLM sits inside the game engine as the game master.

![CEO Tycoon gameplay](docs/demo.gif)

## Run

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # put your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY there
npm install
npm run dev
```

Don't feel like typing? Every free-text box has a **Ghostwriter**: pick a tone (honest, visionary,
corporate, vague, ruthless) and a comms agency writes it for you, for $5k of company money per draft.

Without a key the game still runs with a dumb heuristic "mock GM". Progress autosaves to localStorage.

## Offices

You start in your aunt's garage. You set your own salary — the board and the team compare it to
the company's size every quarter. Garage → coworking → open space (+ east wing) → glass campus, or go remote-first and run the
company as a Zoom grid. Hire beyond your desks and people hot-desk on beanbags (morale tanks).
The office shop sells perks with trade-offs, plus four LLM-invented "specials" per quarter tailored to
your company (bought ones show up in the office as props) (climbing wall, beer fridge, AI receptionist, valuation
LED wall...), all visible in the office and known to the LLM's office gossip. Perks cost upkeep
every quarter, and the novelty wears off: after a few quarters nobody notices the upside (the
downsides stay).

## Things come back to bite you

- **Company systems** (infra, billing, product, sales) are each understood by exactly one person, who
  is paid accordingly. Fire them to save money and the system rots; below 30 it's a crisis and the
  board calls you in to explain yourself (in writing, judged by the LLM).
- **People remember.** Every employee keeps a history of promises, broken promises, 1:1s and who got
  fired. The LLM reads it in every conversation.
- **Alumni** hold grudges, post Glassdoor reviews, join competitors, and can be rehired as contractors
  at 3x — if your phone call convinces them. Whoever processed your Zug invoices may blow the whistle.
- **Investor KPIs**: numbers you throw around in a pitch get written down and checked later.
- **Term sheets**: you pick the ask and the valuation (fair, optimistic, delusional) and can sweeten
  it with a board seat, a 2x liquidation preference or a personal guarantee. The LLM plays the fund:
  accept, counter or pass. The engine enforces what you signed — the preference eats your IPO, the
  guarantee eats your savings, the board member sticks around.
- **Org chart**: decide who reports to whom and hand out titles (Team Lead → Chief … Officer), then
  announce the reorg and watch the politics. More than 6 direct reports eats one of your decisions
  every quarter; managers' moods leak into their teams; too many layers cost revenue in meetings;
  promote your best engineer to manager and nobody maintains infra anymore. Skip-level 1:1s get noticed.
  Get it right and it pays: few direct reports plus happy managers frees up an extra decision, good
  managers squeeze 10% more out of their teams, and a manager inherits the systems of whoever quits.
- **Hiring**: the LLM sends three candidates with CVs, red flags and whatever they've heard about you.
  Pick one, set salary and a sweetener, make your case. They can say no.
- **Herr Brunner**: money moves to Zug through a scheme of your choice (consulting invoice, Alpine
  "retreat", Cyprus licensing, crypto "treasury"), and he wants a cover story for the auditors.
- **The board** meets every 4 quarters with a motion of its own: appoint a CFO who watches every
  payment, freeze your salary, cut staff, sell the perks, or a vote of no confidence. You argue, they
  vote, the engine enacts it. Every board seat you traded for money is a vote against you.
- **Lifestyle**: every quarter the LLM curates fresh, personal picks next to the classics (a vest, a Lambo,
  a penthouse, a private jet that buys you an extra decision). Pay from your own savings
  (FIRE slips away) or put it on the company card (suspicion, someone in finance sees the receipt, and
  auditors who find it make you pay it back). Investors like a CEO who looks successful; the team doesn't.
- **Media**: podcasts, a journalist who asks about whatever she's heard (Zug included), LinkedIn
  posts, paid features. The team reads it too.

## How the LLM is wired in

- `server/llm.ts` — game master: judges free-text actions (all-hands, investor pitch, 1:1s, custom
  event responses), invents quarterly events with choices, writes office gossip.
  Uses structured outputs; every number it returns is clamped.
- `src/game/state.ts` — rule-based simulation (economy, promises, audits, win/lose). The LLM can
  only propose deltas; this owns the numbers.
- `src/scene/OfficeScene.ts` — Phaser isometric office drawn with code (no assets).
- `vite.config.ts` — mounts `/api/*` on the dev server so the key never reaches the browser.

Default game master model is `claude-sonnet-5-5` (judgements, events, epilogues); flavour text (gossip,
ghostwriting, shop catalogues, candidates) runs on `claude-haiku-5-5`. Override with `CEO_MODEL` and
`CEO_FAST_MODEL` in `.env`, or per task (`CEO_MODEL_EVENT`, `CEO_MODEL_JUDGE`, `CEO_MODEL_GOSSIP`... see `.env.example`). The slow-changing part of the game state (who's who, the story so far) is sent as a
cached system block, so calls within a quarter mostly read it from the prompt cache. The dev server logs
tokens, cache hits and a running cost estimate for every call (`[llm] ...`).

**What a game costs:** with the defaults, about 5 cents per quarter (measured: 4 quarters with an
event, a speech, a pitch or interview and some shopping each came to $0.23), so a full run to FIRE
(20–40 quarters) is roughly **$1–2** in API credits. Free-text judgements and events are ~95% of it.

## License

MIT

riddhisingla2028-cpu/chaos-theory.readme:
# Chaos Theory

A neon arcade survival game for the browser where the rules keep breaking.

You steer a small shape around an arena while hazards close in. Every few seconds a **chaos event** rewrites the rules: your controls flip, the walls close in, gravity drags you sideways. Survive, collect orbs, and work through ten levels to a final boss fight. It plays on desktop and phone, with no install and no account.

## Game modes

| Mode | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Levels** | A 10-level campaign. Each level has four escalating phases, its own objective, mechanic, colour and difficulty, and clearing one unlocks the next. |
| **Endless Modes** | Four always-unlocked modes: **Classic Survival**, **Orb Rush**, **Chaos Survival** and **Boss Rush**, each with its own personal bests. |
| **Daily** | One seeded run per day with a daily twist (for example *Overclock* or *Swarm*), the same for every player. |
| **Trials** | Two bonus challenges (*Orb Frenzy*, *Hard Core*), available through the free Chaos+ cosmetics preview. |

### The 10 levels

Every level runs through four phases (introduce the mechanic, raise the pressure, a harder variation, then a final mastery test), announced on screen as each begins.

| # | Level | Objective | Phases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Beginner | Survive 15s | Learn to move → Hazards arrive → Crossfire → Final test (slip through a wall) |
| 2 | Speed Rush | Survive 24s | Three speed waves → Final sprint |
| 3 | Orb Hunt | Collect 10 orbs | Gather → Further out → Hunted (seekers, gold orbs) → Last orb under rain |
| 4 | Reverse Control | Survive 24s | Normal → Reversed → Weavers (normal controls) → Flip storm |
| 5 | The Vanishing Zone | Survive 28s | The floor vanishes in more and more tiles, always with a warning |
| 6 | Double Chaos | Collect 12 orbs | One rule → Rules in pairs → Overload → Last orb |
| 7 | Glitch Attack | Survive 28s | Swerves → Teleports (ghost warnings) → Signal storm → Blackout |
| 8 | Shrinking Arena | Survive 30s | The walls close in step by step while hazards increase |
| 9 | Chaos Combo | Collect 15 orbs in 50s | Mixed rules → Combos → Everything (vanishing floor too) → Finale |
| 10 | Final Showdown | Defeat the Core (10 hits) | Awakening → Enraged (beams) → Shockwave → Desperation (twin beams); visible health bar, shielded phase changes |

### Endless Modes

| Mode | Objective | Personal bests |
|---|---|---|
| Classic Survival | Survive as long as possible; new rules join at milestones | Time, score |
| Orb Rush | Collect as many orbs as possible; gold orbs are worth triple but expire | Orbs, score |
| Chaos Survival | A constant stream of announced, randomly chosen chaos events that pair up over time | Score, events survived |
| Boss Rush | Defeat Core after Core; each has more health and new attacks | Boss streak, score |

Locked levels show a short live preview with their objective, difficulty and an "Unlock by playing" progress bar. Each level awards 1–3 stars: one for clearing, two and three for high scores built with near misses, orbs and combos.

### Chaos events

Inversion, Collapse, Afterimage, Gravity Shift, Surge, Scanline, Phantom, Event Horizon and Glitch. Every event is announced with a warning banner before it starts, and hazards slow down briefly when a rule changes so players can adapt.

## Features

- **Fair, gradual difficulty:** every run starts with a slow warm-up, difficulty ramps in smoothly, and Endless introduces one rule at a time.
- **Scoring:** points for survival time, near-miss combos up to ×5, orb bonuses and milestone rewards.
- **Instant retry:** a large one-tap Retry button, plus a comparison with your last attempt and how close you came to the objective.
- **Progression:** stars, 19 achievements, unlockable player skins and colour themes, a records screen with lifetime stats and a top-10 for each mode, and per-mode personal bests that never go down.
- **Polish:** an animated neon lobby, phase announcements, a boss health bar, particles, screen shake, a completion celebration, and sound effects and menu music generated in code with the Web Audio API (no audio files).
- **Mobile sound:** audio starts on the first tap (as iOS and Android require), recovers after the app is backgrounded, and shows a "Tap to enable sound" control if the browser is still blocking it. The mute preference is saved.
- **Mobile:** a phone-first layout that also adapts to landscape, a floating or fixed touch joystick (configurable), and protection against scrolling, zooming and accidental refresh during play.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard play throughout, visible focus states, and reduced motion when the device asks for it.
- **Saved locally:** all progress and settings are stored in the browser (`localStorage`), and the game still works if storage is blocked.

### Chaos+ Ad-Free (coming soon)

Chaos+ Ad-Free is a planned optional upgrade that removes ads and adds cosmetics, with no gameplay advantage. **Purchasing is not available yet:** the button shows "Coming soon", and no payment can be made. A free, clearly labelled *cosmetics preview* lets players try the premium skins, themes and trials; it is not a purchase and does not remove ads. Players stuck on a level for three attempts can skip it for free (a skipped level gives no stars).

### Advertising (disabled)

The game has reserved, provider-agnostic ad slots on the home screen, level select and every results screen. There are never ads during gameplay or over the arena. **Ads are disabled:** no ad network, no third-party scripts and no tracking are included. Production builds render no ad slots at all; development builds show clearly marked placeholders.

To enable ads in future, after choosing and approving a provider:
1. Implement the `AdProvider` interface in `src/monetization/ads.ts` and set `AD_PROVIDER`.
2. Build with `VITE_ADS_ENABLED=true`.

Ad-free status comes only from `src/monetization/entitlements.ts`, which trusts nothing but a server-verified purchase (`PURC

# 🫧 Steal a Slime! — движок «фабрики плейсов»

Игра целиком в коде: карта, слаймы, UI, экономика, монетизация. Новый плейс на этом движке =
новый `Config.luau` + `Pets.luau` + тема карты в `MapBuilder.luau`.

## Как играется
- Слаймы выезжают из портала по дороге → покупаешь → он прыгает на твою базу и приносит $/сек.
- Можно **украсть** слайма с чужой базы (зажать E) и донести до своей. Хозяин может догнать и **бонкнуть битой** — слайм вернётся.
- **Замок базы** (кнопка на полу или в меню) — 60 сек защиты.
- Прокачка скорости, ребёрты (+50% дохода навсегда), ежедневная награда со стриком, офлайн-доход.
- Редкости Common → Secret, варианты GOLD (x3) и RAINBOW (x8), объявления на весь сервер о редких спавнах.

## Монетизация
| Тип | Что |
|---|---|
| Game Pass | 2x Cash, VIP, +4 слота, Mega Lock |
| Dev Product | Cash Pack, Cash Vault (масштабируются от дохода), Lucky Spawn, Server Luck x2 |

Покупки защищены от двойной выдачи (история чеков), сохранения — от дюпа между серверами (сессионный лок).

## Автоматика без участия человека
- **Авто-ивенты по расписанию** (`Config.Schedule`): Lucky Rain, Golden Rush, Cash Storm — крутятся сами.
- **LiveOps** (`tools/liveops.sh`): мгновенно меняем удачу/доход/объявления на всех серверах.
- **Автодеплой** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`): push в репозиторий → игра собирается и публикуется.
- **Режим съёмки шортсов**: F6 — спрятать UI, F7 — кинокамеры (облёт, слежка за редким слаймом, пролёт).

## Разовая настройка (≈15 минут)
1. Создать игру на create.roblox.com (можно пустой Baseplate), в настройках: **Max Players = 8**,
   включить **Studio Access to API Services**. Записать **Universe ID** и **Place ID**.
2. Open Cloud → API Keys → ключ с правами `universe-places:write` и
   `universe-messaging-service:publish` для этой игры.
3. Репозиторий на GitHub с этим проектом → Secrets: `ROBLOX_API_KEY`, `UNIVERSE_ID`, `PLACE_ID`.
4. Вписать свой UserId в `Config.Admins` (для камеры шортсов).
5. Позже: создать пассы/продукты и вписать ID в `Config.GamePasses` / `Config.Products`.

## Локальная проверка
```
rojo build -o game.rbxl        # собрать
rojo serve                     # live-sync в Studio (плагин Rojo)
```

PetreLuca05/gameengine.readme:
# Deadground

First-person co-op zombie survival foundation in **C11** on **SDL3 + Vulkan 1.3**, with
Jolt physics (via `joltc`), ENet LAN networking and an optional Steam transport.
Milestone 1 is a **DevRoom**: a 60×60 m test level that exercises every core system.

Characters (players, test zombies, dummies) are skinned FBX models on one shared skeleton:
* a data-driven animation controller;
* procedural IK and weapon holding;
* per-body-part damage;
* Jolt ragdolls;
* character LODs.

Zombie AI is still a test wander / attack behaviour. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md),
[docs/ANIMATION.md](docs/ANIMATION.md), [docs/DAMAGE.md](docs/DAMAGE.md),
[docs/ANIMATION_NET.md](docs/ANIMATION_NET.md) and [docs/RECOIL.md](docs/RECOIL.md).

---

## Build requirements

Exact build used for this repository (Windows, from a shell with `cl`, `cmake`, `ninja` and
`glslangValidator` / `glslc` on `PATH`; `build.bat` sets this up from `.toolchain\env.bat` if present):

```bat
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build
```

Not vendored, install separately: a C/C++ compiler (MSVC 2019+ / clang-cl, or GCC / Clang on Linux),
CMake 3.24+, Ninja, a GLSL compiler (`glslc` from the Vulkan SDK, or `glslang`), a Vulkan 1.3 driver.
SDL3, Vulkan-Headers, Jolt / joltc and ENet are downloaded by CMake FetchContent at configure time
(network needed on the first configure); everything else is vendored in `third_party/`.


| | Windows | Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Compiler | MSVC 2019 16.11+ (`cl`), or clang-cl | GCC 11+ or Clang 14+ |
| CMake | 3.24+ (4.x works) | 3.24+ |
| Generator | Ninja (recommended) or Visual Studio | Ninja or Make |
| GLSL compiler | `glslc` (Vulkan SDK) **or** `glslang`/`glslangValidator` | same |
| GPU | Vulkan 1.3 driver | Vulkan 1.3 driver |
| Optional | Vulkan SDK (validation layers) | `libvulkan-dev`, validation layers |
| Linux packages | — | SDL3 build deps: `libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxss-dev libwayland-dev libxkbcommon-dev libdecor-0-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev` |

All other dependencies are fetched or vendored:

| Library | Version | How |
|---|---|---|
| SDL3 | `release-3.4.18` | FetchContent (static) |
| Vulkan-Headers | `vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0` | FetchContent |
| volk | 1.4.350 | `third_party/volk` |
| VulkanMemoryAllocator | v3.4.0 | `third_party/vma` |
| Jolt Physics | v5.6.0 (pulled in by joltc) | FetchContent |
| joltc (C binding) | `886e088` | FetchContent |
| ENet | v1.3.18 | FetchContent |
| cgltf | v1.15 | `third_party/cgltf` |
| stb_image / stb_image_write / stb_vorbis | stb `2c980bb` | `third_party/stb` |
| miniaudio | 0.11.25 | `third_party/miniaudio` |
| cJSON | v1.7.19 | `third_party/cjson` |
| mbedTLS | 3.6.4 LTS | FetchContent (phone companion server: TLS, certificates) |
| qrcodegen (Nayuki) | `3c6d0b3` | `third_party/qrcodegen` |
| minih264 / minimp4 | `b0baea7` / `2a3014a` | `third_party/minih264`, `third_party/minimp4` (phone videos) |
| quirc | `927d680` | `third_party/quirc` (tests only) |
| Nuklear | v4.13.3 | `third_party/nuklear` |
| FastNoiseLite (C) | `785f37a` | `third_party/fastnoise` |
| Steamworks SDK | your copy | `STEAM_SDK_DIR` (optional) |

The build only needs **C++** for third-party code behind C APIs: Jolt + joltc, VMA, and the
two shims `third_party/jolt_shim` and `third_party/steam_shim`. Game code is pure C11.

---

## Building

### Windows

From an *x64 Native Tools Command Prompt* (or any shell where `cl`, `cmake`, `ninja` and a
GLSL compiler are on `PATH`):

```bat
build.bat                 :: RelWithDebInfo -> build\bin\deadground.exe
build.bat Debug           :: Debug          -> build-debug\bin\deadground.exe
```

Or by hand:

```bat
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build
```

clang-cl:

```bat
cmake -S . -B build-clang -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl
cmake --build build-clang
```

`build.bat` also looks for a local `.toolchain\env.bat`. That's how this repo was built on a machine
with only VS 2019 Build Tools, plus portable CMake, Ninja and glslang. It's optional and git-ignored.

### Linux

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build
./build/bin/deadground
```

### Steam (optional)

Point `STEAM_SDK_DIR` at the Steamworks SDK `sdk` folder, the one containing
`public/steam/steam_api.h` and `redistributable_bin/`:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DSTEAM_SDK_DIR=/path/to/steamworks/sdk     # or set the env var STEAM_SDK_DIR
```

Configure prints `Deadground: Steam transport ENABLED`. The steam_api DLL/SO is copied next to the exe
and `steam_appid.txt` is written with AppID **480** (Spacewar) for development. Put your own AppID there
for release. Without `STEAM_SDK_DIR`, the build is LAN-only and the Steam UI entries are disabled.

### Shaders

GLSL lives in `shaders/` and is compiled to SPIR-V at build time into `build/bin/shaders/`.
In dev builds the game watches `shaders/*` and **hot-reloads** on save. It recompiles with the
compiler found at configure time and rebuilds the pipelines. `r_reloadshaders` forces a reload.

### Placeholder assets

`assets/` is generated by `python tools/gen_assets.py`. It's pure Python with no packages and produces
WAV sounds, a PNG crate texture, a KTX2 texture and a glTF barrel. The generated files are committed.

### Character and animation assets

`assets/human/*.fbx` (the canonical rig `Dummy.fbx` and its clips) load directly through ufbx.

* **Bake cache.** On first load they're baked into `assets/cache/`, keyed by file hash. Edited files
  re-bake automatically. `--rebuild-cache` forces a full re-bake.
* **Tools.** `bake_anim` bakes offline and prints a report. `validate_rig <fbx|dir>` checks rigs
  against the canonical skeleton.
* **Data.** Characters are `assets/characters/*.json`. Controller, anim sets, clip metadata, ragdoll
  and hitboxes live in `assets/human/*.json`. See [docs/ANIMATION.md](docs

Need for Speed: Carbon — Nintendo Switch port (nfscarbon-nx)

An **unofficial, work-in-progress** native Nintendo Switch port of the Xbox 360 version of **Need for Speed: Carbon** (2006). It is not an emulator. The PowerPC code of the game's `default.xex` is statically recompiled to C++ with [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk), compiled for the Switch with devkitA64, and the game is drawn by a native Vulkan renderer running on NVK (Mesa). > [!IMPORTANT] > **This is a starting point, not a finished port.** The game boots, the menus work and races are playable, but at > the Switch's stock clocks it runs at **13-25 FPS** and the sound breaks up in crowded races. With an overclock it > holds 30 FPS. The repository is public so that others can pick it up and take it further: see > [How to help](#how-to-help). > [!NOTE] > **Made with Claude.** This port was put together by someone without a background in recompilation, GPU drivers > or console development, working step by step with [Claude](https://claude.ai) (Anthropic's AI assistant): Claude > wrote and changed the code and the build scripts, and the testing on a real console, the logs and the decisions > were mine. Treat the code accordingly, review it, and do not assume something is right because it is here. > Corrections are very welcome. ## Where it stands Tested on a Switch Lite (handheld, 1280x720), USA disc version, all settings as shipped in `nfscarbon.toml`. | Clocks (CPU / GPU / RAM, MHz) | Menus | Canyon race | Race Wars (crowded) | Sound in Race Wars | |---|---|---|---|---| | **1020 / 460 / 1331 (stock)** | ~25 FPS | 16-19 FPS | 13-18 FPS | breaks up | | 1683 / 844 / 2133 | 30 FPS | 25-30 FPS | 25-30 FPS | fine | | 1785 / 921 / 2133 | 30 FPS | 30 FPS in most places | 30 FPS in most places | fine | | 1963 / 1152 / 2133 (max) | 30 FPS | steady 30 FPS | steady 30 FPS | fine | The game is locked to 30 FPS by design, as on the Xbox 360. Where the time goes at stock clocks (Race Wars, measured on the console; details in [docs/measurements.md](docs/measurements.md)): the three CPU cores are 270-290 % busy out of 300 %. The renderer thread needs 45-50 ms per frame, the GPU 35-44 ms (budget: 33 ms). The game's own threads (frame preparation, main thread, audio mixer) fill the rest. There is no single big bug left: it is many medium-sized costs. ### Known issues - **Slow frame rate at stock clocks**, above all in crowded races (Race Wars). - **Sound breaks up in crowded races at stock clocks** ("slow motion", popping). The game's mixer keeps only two 5 ms blocks ahead, so any delay on a saturated CPU loses a block. Fine with an overclock. - **Intro videos (EA logo, attract) play slowly at stock clocks**, normal with an overclock. - **A second car shadow**: a dark patch beside and behind the player's car, as if an invisible car were next to it. - **A short freeze when the player takes control** at the start of a race. - **The first race stutters** while it compiles graphics pipelines. They are saved on the SD card (`cache/carbon_gpu`), and later sessions start smoothly. - **Only the USA edition** is supported (see [Edition](#edition)). ## What you need - A Switch that can run homebrew (custom firmware, Atmosphère). - **Your own copy** of the Xbox 360 game, USA edition: a disc image (`.iso`) or the extracted disc with its `default.xex`. No game files (graphics, sound, video, data) are included here or in the releases. ## Install (prebuilt NRO) 1. Download `nfscarbon-nx.nro` and `nfscarbon.toml` from the [Releases](../../releases) page. 2. Put them on the SD card with the files of your disc: ```text sdmc:/switch/nfscarbon-nx/ nfscarbon-nx.nro nfscarbon.toml (settings) game_root/ (the files of your disc: default.xex, NFS/, MOVIES/, ...) ``` A `.iso` next to the NRO also works instead of `game_root/`. To extract a disc image on a PC: `python3 tools/fase1_extraer.py path/to/game.iso -o game_root`. 3. Launch it with **title takeover** (hold **R** while starting any installed game) or with a forwarder that uses a **39-bit address space**. Album (applet) mode does not give enough memory. Logs are written to `sdmc:/switch/nfscarbon-nx/logs/`. Saves go to `nfscarbon/` next to the NRO. ## Build from source Linux or WSL (Windows). Tested on WSL with Ubuntu. You need: - [devkitPro](https://devkitpro.org/wiki/Getting_Started) with `switch-dev` (devkitA64 and libnx); - CMake 3.25+, Ninja, Python 3.10+, Clang 20 or newer for the PC tools, Docker (for Mesa); - about 16 GB of RAM (32 GB recommended) and 40-60 minutes for the final link with LTO. | Step | Command | Time | |---|---|---| | 1. Third-party sources | `python3 tools/fetch_thirdparty.py` | a few minutes | | 2. Extract your game to `assets/game_root` (ignored by git) | `python3 tools/fase1_extraer.py path/to/game.iso -o assets/game_root` | a few minutes | | 3. NVK driver (Mesa, in Docker) → `out/mesa-sdk` | `bash tools/build_mesa_wsl.sh` | ~1 hour the first time | | 4. Code generator for your PC → `sdk/out/linux-amd64/rexglue` | `CLANG=clang CLANGXX=clang++ bash tools/build_rexglue_wsl.sh` | ~15 minutes | | 5. Translate the game to C++ → `app/generated/` (ignored by git) | `bash tools/codegen.sh` | ~5-7 minutes | | 6. Build the NRO → `app/out/switch/nfscarbon.nro` | `bash tools/build.sh ~/nfscarbon-nx/out/mesa-sdk 4` | 40-60 minutes | Notes: - **Step 3**: `tools/build_mesa_wsl.sh` clones [mesa-switch](https://github.com/danfromtico/mesa-switch) at commit `1a8c1a66d6f`, applies `mesa/mesa-switch-nfsmw.patch` (from nfsmw-nx), fixes two problems of mesa-switch's Docker build (the Rust parts were built for the wrong CPU, and the archive index was broken) and checks the result. The driver is built from source on purpose, so anyone can see and change it. - **Step 4**: the script's header lis

mmisbaah/scitabletop-arcade.readme:
# SciTabletop

Four science strategy games on Science Island, an animated world map you walk around. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules. No framework, no bundler.

| Game | Science | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| **Elemental Alchemy** | Chemistry: valence and bonding. Build molecules from atoms, fight the CPU over a shared atom market, race to discover each molecule first | 1 player vs CPU |
| **Ecosystem Builder** | Ecology: the 10% energy rule, keystone species, biodiversity. Keep a food web alive through droughts, fires, disease and invasive Kudzu | Solo sim |
| **Immune Defense** | Immunology: innate vs adaptive immunity and immune memory. Stop viruses and bacteria before they multiply | Solo wave defense |
| **Quantum Leap Chess** | Physics: superposition, measurement, photon absorption and emission | vs CPU or 2-player hotseat |

Three age groups, picked on first launch and changeable from the top bar:

| Group | What changes |
|---|---|
| **Explorers (5–7)** | Simpler versions: Molecule Match (copy the picture), Feed the Forest (no invasive plants or disasters, 6 seasons), Germ Busters (tap a germ and the right cell goes after it, 3 waves), Quantum Hop (gentle CPU and a Hint button). Bigger tap targets, short kid-friendly facts, read-aloud. Stars for how well you did. |
| **Investigators (8–11)** | The real games, a bit gentler: 7 molecules to 100 points, 8 seasons, slower germ growth. |
| **Scientists (12+)** | Full rules and the full difficulty range. |

Every game has **levels**. Winning (or earning 2+ stars as an Explorer) unlocks the next, and each level is a bit harder: new molecules and hidden atom hints in Molecule Match, a higher target and smarter CPU in Alchemy, more seasons and disasters in Ecosystem, bonus waves and faster-growing germs in Immune, and a stronger CPU in Quantum chess. Pick any unlocked level from the map card.

What every game has:
- **Lab Notes**: a science fact for whatever just happened
- **End screen**: your score, personal best, stats, and every fact you met that round
- **Easy / Normal / Hard** (header toggle; it applies the next time a game resets)
- **Best scores** on the hub
- A **How to play** popup the first time you open each game

Settings and best scores are saved in the browser's localStorage.

## Project layout

```
index.html                  page shell and the markup for every screen
css/
  styles.css                design tokens (light + dark), layout and components
js/
  main.js                   router, settings, end screen, click delegation
  core/
    audio.js                Web Audio sound effects
    ui.js                   toast, logs, meters, inline icon renderer
    icons.js                the 22 Lucide icons used (generated)
    storage.js              localStorage settings and best scores
    progress.js             XP, levels, stars, achievements, fact journal
    age.js                  age groups and kid-friendly wording
    art.js                  molecule models, cartoon germs, the mascot (inline SVG)
    anim.js                 motion toolkit: FLIP moves, flying sprites, bursts, ripples, screen shake
    confetti.js             win celebration
    speech.js               read-aloud
    difficulty.js           Easy/Normal/Hard lookup
    facts.js                Lab Notes and the "what you learned" list
    endscreen.js            results screen
  world/
    world.js                Science Island map, locations and the walking character
  data/
    rules.js                hub cards and rules text
    chemistry-data.js       recipes, valence, atom facts, deck
    species.js              ecosystem species, events, tuning
    pathogens.js            pathogens, waves, abilities, memory facts
    quantum-data.js         quantum facts
  games/
    chemistry.js            Elemental Alchemy
    ecosystem.js            Ecosystem Builder
    immune.js               Immune Defense
    quantum.js              Quantum Leap Chess UI
    quantum-engine.js       Quantum chess rules and CPU (no DOM)
scripts/build-icons.mjs     regenerates js/core/icons.js from the lucide package
```

Each game module exports `init()`, `handle(action, arg, el)` and `setGameOverHandler(fn)`. Buttons declare what they do with `data-action="game:verb"` and `main.js` routes the click, so there are no inline `onclick` handlers.

## Run locally

ES modules need a web server (opening the file directly won't work):

```bash
npm run serve      # http://localhost:8000
```

There is no build step. `npm install && npm run build:icons` regenerates `js/core/icons.js` if you add an icon name to `scripts/build-icons.mjs`.

## Deploy

Pushing to `main` runs `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, which publishes the site to GitHub Pages. One-time setup: in the repo go to **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.

Callzik/fart-together.readme:
# Fart Together

![Скриншот](screenshot.png)

Кооперативная 3D-аркада для ПК: четыре зверя на надувном плоту несутся по водной горке.
Плот двигается только газом: зверь пукает, и плот летит в противоположную от него сторону.
Плот крутится, так что кто сейчас «спереди», всё время меняется.

Цель: доплыть до финиша как можно быстрее. Там, где нет бортиков, можно вылететь с горки
(+3 секунды и возврат на чекпоинт). Мешают качающиеся молоты, крутящиеся шипастые палки и морские мины.

## Запуск

**Windows:** скачай `FartTogether-Setup.exe` со страницы
[Releases](https://github.com/Callzik/fart-together/releases/latest) и запусти. Установщик сам всё поставит
(Python не нужен, права администратора тоже), создаст ярлык на рабочем столе и в меню «Пуск».
Если Windows покажет «Windows защитила ваш компьютер», нажми «Подробнее» → «Выполнить в любом случае»
(так бывает со всеми неподписанными программами).
Удалить: «Параметры → Приложения» или ярлык «Удалить Fart Together» в «Пуск».

Без установки: там же есть `FartTogether-windows.zip`, распакуй и запусти `FartTogether.exe`.

**Как выпустить новую версию:** на GitHub открой **Actions → Build Windows exe → Run workflow**,
впиши версию (например `v2.1`) и нажми **Run workflow**. Игра соберётся, и появится релиз с zip.
Можно и тегом: `git tag v2.1 && git push origin v2.1`.

**Из исходников** (Python 3.9+, движок [Panda3D](https://www.panda3d.org/)):

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
python fart_together.py
```

Собрать `.exe` самому: `build_exe.bat` (или `python setup.py build_apps`).

Файлы: `sim.py` — физика и трасса, `gfx.py` — 3D-модели (всё строится кодом, без внешних моделей),
`net.py` — сеть, `fart_together.py` — игра, камера, интерфейс.
Шрифт DejaVu Sans (`assets/`), лицензия в `assets/DejaVu-LICENSE.txt`.

Звуки пуков (12 штук: короткие, басовые, мокрые, писклявые, очередью) синтезированы кодом
`tools/make_farts.py` и лежат в `assets/sfx/`. У каждого зверя свой набор: лягуха мокрая,
мишаня и бегемот басовые, мартын писклявый. Перегенерировать: `pip install numpy scipy`,
`python tools/make_farts.py`.

## Управление

| Режим | Клавиши |
|---|---|
| 1 — Соло | Стрелки / WASD: нужные звери пукают сами, чтобы толкнуть плот в эту сторону |
| 2 — Вместе (до 4 игроков за одной клавиатурой) | Лягуха **Q**, Мишаня **P**, Бегемот **Z**, Мартын **M** |
| 3 / 4 — Онлайн (до 4 игроков на разных ПК) | **Пробел**: пукает твой зверь |
| 5 — Сменить ник | Ник видно над твоим зверем в онлайне, игра его запоминает |

У каждого зверя ограниченный запас газа (полоска внизу), он восстанавливается, пока зверь отдыхает.
`Esc` — пауза, `R` в паузе — заново. Лучшее время сохраняется в `~/.fart_together.json`.

## Онлайн

Один игрок создаёт игру (**3**), остальные подключаются (**4**) и вводят его адрес. До 4 игроков,
у каждого свой зверь. Хост считает физику, остальные присылают только свои нажатия, поэтому
отдельный сервер не нужен. Используется TCP-порт **5555**.

1. Хост жмёт **3**. На экране появятся его адреса, например `192.168.1.5:5555`.
2. Друзья жмут **4**, вводят адрес и Enter.
3. Когда все подключились, хост жмёт **Enter**.

Windows при первом запуске хоста спросит про брандмауэр: нужно разрешить доступ.

**Как подключиться через интернет.** Если вы не в одной Wi-Fi сети, проще всего поставить всем
бесплатную виртуальную сеть: [Radmin VPN](https://www.radmin-vpn.com/ru/) или
[ZeroTier](https://www.zerotier.com/). Создайте там общую сеть, хост создаёт игру, а друзья вводят его
адрес из Radmin/ZeroTier (например `26.12.34.56`).
Другие варианты:
- проброс порта 5555 на роутере хоста (друзья вводят его внешний IP);
- туннель [playit.gg](https://playit.gg) для TCP 5555 (друзья вводят выданный адрес вида `xxx.playit.gg:12345`).
