aricburkert/nebula.readme:
# The Nebula from Hell — online

An online multiplayer version of the party board game *The Nebula from Hell*: create a room, share the link, and race your friends to FINISH. Deploys to Cloudflare.

## Where things are

- `docs/rules.md` — the rules spec the game implements, with open questions.
- `docs/card-review.md` — which cards work online as is, as a chat version, only on a video call, or not at all.
- `data/cards.json` — all 108 cards, transcribed.
- `data/board-standard.json` — the Standard Edition board: 33 spaces, colors, fork, warps.
- `data/spinner-standard.json` — the spinner's 8 segments.
- `src/engine/` — the game itself: rules, board, every card's script, and a bot. It runs on the server and replays from its input log, so a game survives restarts.
- `src/worker/` — the Cloudflare Worker (`/api/rooms`) and the `Room` Durable Object that holds each game, its chat and its players.
- `src/client/` — the React app: home page, lobby, prompts, hand, chat and log. `Board.tsx` is the flat 2D board, used when WebGL isn't available.
- `src/client/three/` — the 3D game (three.js via react-three-fiber): the board with a raised track, the illustrations standing up off it as pop-up cardboard standees, pawns, decks, dice and spinner. `director.ts` turns each new game state into a timeline of animations so everyone sees the same dice, card and hop in order; it never changes the game.
- `public/assets/` — the real card art, board, spinner, pawns and logos. `board3d/` is generated from the board SVG (see below).

## Run it locally

```sh
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173 (Worker and Durable Object run locally too)
npm test         # engine tests: every card, plus 60 simulated games
npm run build    # typecheck and production build
```

Open the site in two browser windows (or one normal, one private) to play against yourself.

The 3D board art is cut out of `public/assets/board/standard.svg` by a script that needs a browser (for exact bounding boxes). Rerun it only if the board SVG changes:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome node scripts/board-art.mjs
PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome node scripts/board-art.mjs deep-space "Deep Space Edition.svg" "Deep Space Spinner.svg"
```

It writes the flat board (`public/assets/board3d/flat.svg`), one SVG per standee (`public/assets/board3d/pieces/`), and `src/client/three/boardArt.json` (piece positions plus the track, river, star and shield outlines). The Deep Space run writes the same under `public/assets/board3d/deep-space/` and `boardArt-deep-space.json`, plus `public/assets/board/deep-space.jpg` (the 2D board) and `public/assets/spinner/deep-space.jpg`. Its source SVGs (130 MB, mostly an embedded starfield photo) aren't kept in the repo.

The game shows cards from small WebP copies (`public/assets/cards/webp/`), which load much faster than the SVGs. Rerun this if a card SVG changes:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome node scripts/card-images.mjs
```

The host picks Standard or Deep Space in the lobby. Both boards have the same spaces and rules; each has its own six pawns (every Deep Space pawn is a twin of a Standard one, so switching boards swaps everyone to their twin).

The settings menu in a game switches 3D quality (High adds bloom and sharper textures), the auto camera, and sound.

## Deploy to Cloudflare

It's a single Worker with static assets and one Durable Object; `wrangler.jsonc` has everything.

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard go to **Workers & Pages → Create → Import a repository** and pick `aricburkert/nebula`.
2. Build command: `npm run build`. Deploy command: `npx wrangler deploy`. Root directory: `/`.
3. Save and deploy. Every push to `main` publishes again.

If pushes stop publishing, check **Settings → Build** on the Worker. A banner saying the project is disconnected from your Git account means the Cloudflare GitHub app lost access. Click **Manage**, allow the repo, and refresh.

No secrets or environment variables are needed. The Durable Object migration (`v1`, class `Room`) is applied on the first deploy.

# debuff docs

Source for [debuff.jp](https://debuff.jp): the home page, guides, examples, benchmarks, roadmap and API reference. Built with [VitePress](https://vitepress.dev); the API reference is generated from the [debuff](https://github.com/debuffjp/debuff) sources with TypeDoc.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/debuffjp/debuff ../debuff   # API reference reads its sources
(cd ../debuff && npm ci)
npm install
npm run dev
```

| Path | What's there |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/` | Guides, served at `/docs/` (old `/guide/*` links redirect via `public/_redirects`) |
| `examples/` | Live demos embedded in pages, such as the plinko board (typechecked in `npm run build`) |
| `public/play/` | Production builds of playable example games |
| `.vitepress/theme/` | Theme components: `PlinkoHero`, `PlayEmbed`, `CopyCommand` |

`npm run build` also writes the sitemap, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. `npm run deploy` publishes to the Cloudflare Worker behind debuff.jp, and a GitHub Pages mirror is built by CI.

Fix anything you spot: every page has an "Edit this page" link.

# ReDusted

woohoo one of the first mods!!!

## Features

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Borderless windowed | Done (hooks window creation/styling and D3D9 device creation) |
| `.ini` settings | Done (`dist/ReDusted.ini`) |
| 30 fps cap removal | Done |
| Frame limiter / vsync control | Done |
| Fixed-rate terrain/water simulation (60+ fps without fast physics) | Done, tested in game |
| Skip startup logos / cutscenes (separate ini toggles) | Done, tested in game |
| Subtitles for voice lines | Not needed: the game already shows the shaman's lines as text (checked in game) |
| New levels | Planned |

## Install

1. Install [Ultimate ASI Loader](https://github.com/ThirteenAG/Ultimate-ASI-Loader)
   (32-bit) into the game folder as `dinput8.dll` (the game imports DINPUT8).
2. Copy `ReDusted.asi` and `ReDusted.ini` next to `From_Dust.exe`.
3. Set the game to windowed mode for borderless.
4. Check `ReDusted.log` if something doesn't work. With the simulation fix
   working it shows `Simulation hook: active at 30 Hz` once a level loads.

Things to look at in the first playtest at 60 fps: water, lava and sand should
flow at the same speed as at 30 fps, and the breath's take/drop rate should
feel the same. If something is off, set `FixedSimulation=0` to get the
original behaviour back, and include the log with the report.

## Build

On Windows with Visual Studio or the Build Tools (C++ workload), run
`build.bat`; it writes `build\ReDusted.asi`. `tests\run.bat` builds the
mod plus a fake simulator DLL and checks the fixed-rate simulation offline.

Cross-compile from Linux (32-bit MinGW):

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/mingw-i686.cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
```

Or with Visual Studio, configure a Win32 (x86) build with CMake.

## Reverse-engineering notes (From_Dust.exe, build of 2011-09-05)

### From_Dust.exe

- `0x5C1960` main frame tick: counts frames per one-second window and skips
  the frame while `frames / elapsed > 30.0f` (constant at `0x8A3104`, shared
  with other code). Patched by repointing the `comiss` operand at `0x5C19E3`.
- `0x5106F0` engine clock: real per-frame delta time stored at `0x92975C`,
  clamped to 1/6 s, scaled by `0x90C824` * `0x90C828`; fixed-dt override at
  `0x929764`. Passed to the main update at `0x5C1AC3`.
- `0x5D9CA0` loads `GalileoKernel.dll` (job system), `GalileoTexture.dll` and
  `GalileoSimulatorWater.dll` from a CPU-specific subfolder (`SSE41`/`SSSE3`/`SSE3`).
  The water sim is created via ordinal 1 (`0x91C238`) and destroyed via
  ordinal 2 (`0x91C23C`); the instance is kept at `[manager+0xC]`.
- `0x4136E0` returns the simulator (`[[0x921534]+0xC]`).
- Command-line options include `-fullscreen`, `-vsync`, `-msaa`, `-res`.

### GalileoSimulatorWater.dll (PDBs ship with the game)

The SSE3, SSSE3 and SSE41 builds differ in code addresses but share the class
layout and the `SimulatorWater` vtable:

- Ordinal 1 `sCreate`, 2 `sDestroy`, 3 `sStaticInit`. The exe resolves them
  with `GetProcAddress` by ordinal.
- Vtable slot 53 `UpdateSimulatorAndDisplay` (thiscall, 17 args, `ret 0x44`)
  launches the frame's kernel jobs. The simulation jobs (`SimulatorGanja` and
  three `SimulatorWater` passes) only start while the "simulate" flag at
  `+0x930` is set. Display, particles, vegetation display, paths, sound and
  perception jobs run either way.
- Slot 55 `SyncSimulator` waits for those jobs and, if `+0x930` is set,
  increments the double-buffer frame counter at `+0x92C`.
- `Modify` (slot 9) applies brush edits (add/remove water and lava, soft and
  hard ground) straight to the current buffer.

The exe calls `UpdateSimulatorAndDisplay` from its simulation driver at
`0x455CC0` (thiscall, one arg, called from `0x41D859`). The driver has its own
cap: it skips while it ran more than 35 times a second (`35.0f` at `0x90C488`,
2 s window, check at `+0x79`). `SyncSimulator` runs every frame. At 30 fps
that is one update and one sync per frame. Above 30 fps the driver runs in
uneven bursts (about 35/s) and every extra sync flips the buffers with no new
step behind it, so the water crawls and stutters.

The fix:
- Hooks the driver and runs it only when a step is due at `SimulationHz`
  (real time, small early tolerance, deficit carried). The 35/s check is
  repointed at a huge threshold.
- Patches vtable slots 53 and 55 (via the `sCreate` wrapper from a
  `GetProcAddress` hook): a sync may flip the buffers only once per launched
  step, so syncs without a new step keep `+0x930` clear while they wait.
- Measured in game at 60 fps: 30 driver runs, 30 steps, 60 syncs and 30 flips
  per second, the same step and flip rate as the stock game at 30 fps.

If the DLL or the driver code does not match the expected instructions,
nothing is hooked and the 30 fps cap comes back. The frame limiter runs in the
game's own frame tick (`0x5C1960`), because Present hooks only saw the first
frame.

### Videos

The game plays videos with Bink through its own player (`0x5E0060`), which
opens them from the bigfile (`BinkOpen` with a custom IO, flags `0x02004400`)
and stops once `bink->FrameNum` (`+0xC`) reaches `bink->Frames` (`+0x8`,
check at `0x5E0163`). A skipped video is cut to one frame right after
`BinkOpen`. Looping videos get their length back in `BinkSetWillLoop`, which
the player calls before the first frame. The first video of a session is the
startup logos (1280x720, 179 frames); the cutscene after choosing a map is the
next one (532 frames).

The age-rating screen before the logos cannot be skipped: it is a loading
screen. The boot scripts call `WOR_LoadDynamicGroup` and then poll
`WOR_IsLoading` while the main-menu world loads (about 5 s), and the logos
follow once it is done. Running game time 10x faster during boot (engine time
scale `[0x90C828]`, which the clock init at `0x5104E0` resets to 1.0) did not
shorten it.

# bpex maniac

Shove-first aggro bot for Lean Poker (TypeScript).

## Strategy

Built on one observation: the other bots fold too much, so pressure wins.

- **Push/fold from 20 big blinds down**: any two cards go all-in when nobody has raised. Folding is a leak.
- **Opens**: deeper than 20 big blinds we open 6.5 big blinds with pairs, any ace and broadway cards, so a call is
  always expensive.
- **Calling all-ins**: only QQ+ and AK. Their shoves are never bluffs, so we don't pay them off.
- **Postflop**: big bets (pot-sized and above) only with two pair or better; we never bluff big. Small bets are a
  mix of value and semi-bluffs.
- **Heads-up**: shove every hand under 25 big blinds.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

# Night Shift Ward 7


**Play:** https://supassk.github.io/Before-They-Wake-/ (works on phone and computer, no install)

**Course:** 273411 Communicative English for Computer and Information Technology: Practical Project

## Target learners
University students with English at **A2–B1** level (CEFR). Thai translations are optional and can be turned off.

## Language goals
- **Reading for detail (main goal):** compare what a patient says with written records (a referral, a nurse chart and a medical history) and find the sentences that contradict each other.
- **Vocabulary:** everyday health words for sleep, mood, worry, energy and the body. Players tap yellow words to see the Thai meaning, and each night ends with a vocabulary check.
- **Grammar in context:** each night has a focus: present simple → frequency words → past simple → *for / since / ago* → giving reasons (*because, so, might, probably*). From Night 3, players build each question from word tiles.
- **Listening (optional):** text-to-speech reads every answer aloud. Listening mode hides the text.

## How to play
You are a trainee doctor at the night-shift nurses' station of a psychiatric hospital. You look into an observation room, check each patient's papers, and decide.
1. A patient comes to your observation window and tells you their problem.
2. Open the **Interview Sheet** and choose questions. The number of questions is limited, and each one uses 10 minutes of the night.
3. Read the documents on your desk: the **Referral** (with an ID photo), the **Nurse Chart** and the **Medical History**.
4. If everything matches, stamp **ADMIT** and choose a diagnosis with the **Field Guide**.
5. If something does not match (the story, a document, or the photo), stamp **FLAG** and tap the **two pieces of evidence** that contradict each other.
6. See every patient before **6:00 AM**. A wrong decision or a patient left waiting costs 1 Trust. If you lose all 4, your shift is over.

## Core loop
**Input** (read the patient's words and the documents) → **Action** (ask questions, compare, then stamp ADMIT or FLAG with evidence) → **Feedback** (Correct / Wrong call, *why* the answer is right, the key evidence, and the signs you missed) → **Reward** (points, Trust, a night report and a vocabulary check). There are 5 nights with 15 patients, and each night is harder than the last: fewer questions, word-tile questions, and more patients to flag (0 → 1 → 1 → 1 → 2).

## AI and tools used
| Tool | What we used it for |
|---|---|
| Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) | Wrote the HTML/CSS/JavaScript code, the SVG code that draws the patients, and the Web Audio sound effects. Drafted the patient dialogue, the documents and the Thai translations. Helped us proofread the English. |
| Web Speech API (built into the browser) | Reads English text aloud. |
| *[add any other tools you used]* | |

**Our own work:** the game concept and design decisions (target learners, language goals, the FLAG/evidence mechanic, the shift clock, difficulty across nights, and a sensitive tone for mental health topics), checking every English sentence and Thai translation (see [LANGUAGE_REVIEW.md](LANGUAGE_REVIEW.md)), and playtesting.

## Inspiration
The "check the papers, then let them in or not" mechanic is inspired by *That's Not My Neighbor* (Nacho Sama) and *Papers, Please* (Lucas Pope). We did not use any of their art, characters, logos or text. We changed the idea for language learning:
- The player must **point to the two pieces of evidence** that contradict each other, so they have to read closely.
- Feedback **explains the reason** in English.
- The setting is a hospital, with our own art drawn in code.
- Patients are **never shown as monsters**. "Impostors" are people faking an illness or documents with errors, so the game does not stigmatize mental illness.

*Note:* the conditions in this game are simplified for language practice. It is not a medical tool.

# chili-doom

Doom for the ChiliChip VGC Zero (RP2350, 128x128 OLED), built on the
[32blit SDK](https://github.com/chili-chip/32blit-sdk) like every other ChiliChip game.

Status: shareware Doom plays at the console's native 128x128 on desktop and on the VGC Zero
(`vgc-blit`), with sound effects and OPL music. Setting music volume to 0 in the in-game menu
turns the music synth off to save CPU.

## Bring your own WAD

This repo contains no id Software game data, and builds published from it never will.
(The ThumbyDOOM submodule carries upstream's `doom1.whx`; chili-doom never builds it in.)
To play, convert your own copy of the shareware `DOOM1.WAD` (version 1.9) before building:

```
tools/make_whd.sh /path/to/doom1.wad    # writes data/doom1.whd (git-ignored)
```

On Ubuntu or Debian the shareware WAD comes in the `doom-wad-shareware` package
(`/usr/share/games/doom/doom1.wad`). Without `data/doom1.whd` the game still builds and
shows "No WAD built in".

## Building (desktop)

The engine comes in as a git submodule, so clone with `--recursive`
(or run `git submodule update --init` in an existing clone).
Check out [32blit-sdk](https://github.com/chili-chip/32blit-sdk) next to this repo, then:

```
cmake --preset linux
cmake --build out/build/linux
./out/build/linux/chili-doom.elf
```

## Building for the VGC Zero

Check out [32blit-sdk](https://github.com/chili-chip/32blit-sdk) and
[pico-sdk](https://github.com/chili-chip/pico-sdk) next to this repo, make `data/doom1.whd` as above, then:

```
cmake --preset vgc-blit
cmake --build out/build/vgc-blit
```

Copy `out/build/vgc-blit/chili-doom.blit` onto the console's **CHILICHIP** drive to install it.
A `.blit` built with your WAD contains id Software's game data: keep it to yourself.

RAM is the tight part: games get 448 KB and Doom uses almost all of it. To make room, the
screen shows Doom's 128x128 frame directly instead of a copy (see `init()` in
`src/doom_blit.cpp`), and the screen-melt snapshot doubles as the menu backdrop.

Controls: arrows move and turn, A fires, B uses, Y and X strafe, MENU opens the Doom menu.
On a keyboard: Z = A, X = B, C = X, V = Y, Esc = MENU (the 32blit SDL defaults).

## How it fits together

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `vendor/ThumbyDOOM/` | Submodule: our fork [chili-chip/ThumbyDOOM](https://github.com/chili-chip/ThumbyDOOM) of [ThumbyDOOM](https://github.com/austinio7116/ThumbyDOOM). We build its `vendor/rp2040-doom/` (kilograham's [rp2040-doom](https://github.com/kilograham/rp2040-doom), Chocolate Doom for RP2040, with a native 128x128 renderer), its `port/` platform layer and its `host/` stand-ins for the pico SDK headers. |
| `src/doom_blit.cpp` | The 32blit game: `init` starts Doom, `update` runs one frame per 35 Hz tic, `render` copies the 128x128 frame to the screen. |
| `tools/make_whd.sh` | Builds `whd_gen` and converts a WAD into the compressed WHD blob that gets linked into the game. |

Changes for chili-doom live on the fork and are marked `CHILI_BLIT` or `chili-doom`. The fork is based on ThumbyDOOM `22070a1`
(rp2040-doom `29a453c`).

## Licence

GPL v2, inherited from Chocolate Doom and rp2040-doom; see `LICENSE`. The 32blit SDK is MIT.
DOOM is a trademark of id Software; this project is not affiliated with id Software.

animeliodas/SeriousSpeedrun.desc: Speedrun timer (RTA, IGT), LiveSplit autosplitting and a speedometer for Serious Sam Classic - one-click install, works on the unmodified game
animeliodas/SeriousSpeedrun.readme:
# SeriousSpeedrun — таймер для спидрана Serious Sam Classic

Таймер RTA и IGT, LiveSplit и спидометр для Serious Sam Classic (The First Encounter 1.05, The Second Encounter
1.07). **Игру не меняет**: подходит для забегов обычной игры, работает и вместе с другими модами (например,
[SeriousHL](https://github.com/animeliodas/SeriousHL) — движение Half-Life). Плагин
[Serious Sam Classics Patch](https://github.com/SamClassicPatch/SuperProject) 1.9.4; порт
[SeriousBridge](https://github.com/animeliodas/SeriousBridge) (таймер — его модуль ядра `core/sam/Speedrun`).

> Сделано с помощью Claude Code (ИИ). Проверено скриптом в настоящих играх (TFE и TSE, `tools/test_speedrun.py`,
> ниже); с настоящим LiveSplit — проверено пользователем.

## Установка (один клик)

1. Скачай `SeriousSpeedrun-<версия>.zip` со страницы [Releases](https://github.com/animeliodas/SeriousSpeedrun/releases),
   распакуй куда угодно.
2. Запусти `Install.cmd`: сам найдёт TFE и TSE в Steam (или GOG; или перетащи папку игры на `Install.cmd`), поставит
   Classics Patch 1.9.4, если его нет (с его страницы релизов на GitHub, SHA-256 проверяется), положит
   `SeriousSpeedrun.dll` в `Bin\Plugins` и ярлык на рабочий стол.
3. Играй через Classics Patch (ярлык, `Bin\SeriousSam_Custom.exe` или в Steam параметр `+game ClassicsPatchMod`).

Удаление — `Uninstall.cmd`. Вручную: `TFE\SeriousSpeedrun.dll` / `TSE\SeriousSpeedrun.dll` в `<игра>\Bin\Plugins\`.

## Таймер

Встроенный таймер игры раннеры не используют; этот считает сам:
- **RTA** — настоящее время (часы ПК) от старта: загрузки, меню и пауза входят;
- **IGT** — время игры: её тики (по 1/20 с), пока идёт забег. Загрузки уровней, пауза, меню и Netricsa не идут
  (в одиночной игре на них нет тиков), загрузка сохранения не сбивает.

Старт — первое управление игроком после новой игры (после заставки и Netricsa; `sr_iStartOn 0` — сразу на новой
игре). Сплит — конец каждого уровня (когда игра пишет его статистику; или смена уровня без неё). Финиш — конец
игры. Новая игра сбрасывает забег. На экране справа сверху — `RTA` и `IGT` (`LS` — LiveSplit подключён, `#N` —
сплитов). Заставка меню и демо забегом не считаются.

## LiveSplit

Правой кнопкой по LiveSplit → Control → **Start TCP Server** (порт 16834; в старых версиях — компонент LiveSplit
Server). Игра подключится сама (пробует раз в 3 с) и будет запускать таймер, ставить сплиты, финишировать и
сбрасывать. **Game Time** в LiveSplit всегда равно IGT — для забега по IGT сравнивай по Game Time (правой кнопкой →
Compare Against → Game Time). Сплитов в LiveSplit — по одному на уровень. Без LiveSplit таймер работает сам.

## Спидометр

Под прицелом — скорость по земле: м/с (`sr_iSpeedUnits 1` — юниты Half-Life, для SeriousHL); зелёная — быстрее
бега Сэма (10 м/с).

## Консоль (`~`)

| Команда | По умолчанию | |
|---|---|---|
| `sr_bShowTimer` | 1 | таймер на экране |
| `sr_bShowSpeed` | 1 | спидометр |
| `sr_iSpeedUnits` | 0 | 0 — м/с, 1 — юниты HL |
| `sr_bLiveSplit` | 1 | связь с LiveSplit |
| `sr_strLiveSplit` | `127.0.0.1:16834` | его адрес |
| `sr_iStartOn` | 1 | 1 — старт на первом управлении, 0 — на новой игре |
| `sr_Status()` | | состояние |

Команд, которые меняли бы время забега, нет (тестовые — только в режиме разработки, `SERIOUSBRIDGE_DEV=1`).

## Сборка и проверка

VS 2022 Build Tools (v143, x86); рядом — ядро и SDK Classics Patch:
```
<папка>/seriousspeedrun      этот репозиторий
<папка>/seriousbridge        git clone https://github.com/animeliodas/SeriousBridge seriousbridge
<папка>/_deps/SuperProject   git clone --branch 1.9.4 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/SamClassicPatch/SuperProject.git
```
`plugin/build.sh` → `plugin/dist/Release_TFE105|Release_TSE107/SeriousSpeedrun.dll`; `python tools/make_release.py` →
`release/SeriousSpeedrun-<версия>.zip`.

Оракул — `python tools/test_speedrun.py --game "<папка игры>" --launch` (вместо LiveSplit — заглушка на порту 16834,
записывает команды; один забег по шагам, на обычной игре):

| Проверка | TFE | TSE |
|---|---|---|
| старт на управлении; LiveSplit: reset, starttimer, game time на паузе и задано | PASS | PASS |
| IGT идёт как реальное время (1.000); на паузе стоит, RTA идёт | PASS | PASS |
| Game Time LiveSplit = IGT (setgametime 10 раз в секунду) | PASS | PASS |
| выход с уровня → сплит (и в LiveSplit); загрузка в IGT не входит | PASS | PASS |
| конец игры → последний сплит, таймер стоит | PASS | PASS |
| новая игра → сброс | PASS | PASS |

## Лицензия

GPL-2.0, как Serious Engine 1 и Classics Patch.

Shazookie/Mop-Mania-Ultra-Deluxe.readme:
# Mop Mania Ultra Deluxe

Seamus's edition of *Mop Mania: The Purging of Le' Hospitale*, the text RPG by
Joshua Fouch, Seamus Sommers, and Eljay Jimenez. See `CHANGELOG.md` for what is
different from the original.

The original only ran on Windows through Visual Studio. This copy also runs on
macOS and Linux, and in any modern web browser. The game code in `game/` started as the team's
code and is where Ultra Deluxe changes are made.

## Play it in a browser

Open `dist/index.html`. That single file is the whole game, so you can also
put it on any static web host to share it:

- **GitHub Pages:** make a repo, add `dist/index.html` as `index.html`, then
  turn on Pages under *Settings → Pages* (deploy from the main branch).
- **Netlify / Cloudflare Pages:** drag the `dist` folder onto their deploy page.

## Play it in a terminal (macOS / Linux)

```sh
./build.sh
cd game && ../build/mopmania
```

Run it from inside `game/` so it can find `endcredit.txt` (and `sounds/`, below).
On a Mac, install the compiler first with `xcode-select --install`.

On Windows, play the browser version, or build in WSL (Ubuntu on Windows) with the steps above.
Ultra Deluxe's new features (like Putrid's snake game) need the files in `platform/`, so the old
Visual Studio setup won't build this edition.

## Sound

The sounds are MP3s in `dist/sounds/` (recovered from the original repo's history and converted
from WAV). The web page plays them from a `sounds/` folder next to `index.html`, so host that
folder along with the page. The terminal version finds them there too; on Linux it needs
`ffplay` or `mpg123` installed.

## How the port works

| Folder | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| `game/` | The original C++ source, untouched. |
| `platform/Windows.h`, `platform/platform.cpp` | A stand-in for `<Windows.h>`: console colors become ANSI colors, `system("pause")` / `system("CLS")` / `system("Color ..")` become portable versions, and `PlaySound` plays files from `sounds/`. |
| `platform/web/thread` | The browser build's `std::this_thread::sleep_for`. |
| `web/` | The browser runtime (`mopmania-runtime.js`), the page template, and the compiled `mopmania.wasm`. |
| `dist/index.html` | The finished, self-contained web page. |
| `test/` | Scripts that play the web build automatically. |

The web version compiles the same C++ to WebAssembly with
[wasi-sdk](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-sdk), then runs Binaryen's
Asyncify pass so the page can pause the game while it waits for your answer
or sleeps between lines. To rebuild it, see the top of `build-web.sh`.

Two files from the original repo are left out of the build because they were
leftovers with their own copies of functions: `testercharactercode.cpp`
(a separate test program with its own `main`) and `Game_Tester_Menu.cpp`
(a duplicate of `Game_Menu_Test` in `utility.cpp`).

### Known limit

Every move between rooms calls `gameMap::play()` again without returning, so
the call stack grows the whole game. In a browser that allows about 3,000
room moves in one session before the page runs out of stack. A normal
playthrough uses far fewer.

Bolotaure/Geography-test.readme:
# Geography-test

## Capy's Map Safari

A kids' geography game, recreated from [Capy's State Safari](https://cappystates.lovable.app),
with two more tests added: the 18 regions of France (13 in mainland France + 5 overseas)
and the 47 prefectures of Japan (Okinawa in a box, as on Japanese school maps).

Open `index.html` and pick a test with the **🇺🇸 US States / 🇫🇷 French Regions / 🇯🇵 Japanese Prefectures** buttons
(or the *Activities* menu, or the `#us` / `#fr` / `#jp` URL hash).

- Click the place Capy names. Streaks give bonus points; every level unlocks a squishy.
- Two misses make the answer glow. Missed places go into **Practice Missed**.
- **Explore Mode** names whatever you tap; **Name Tags** shows short labels.
- **Ask Capy for a hint** gives direction, neighbours, water and spelling hints, all worked out in the
  page (the original used an online AI for hints).
- Zoom the map with the **+ / −** buttons, a two-finger pinch, or ctrl + mouse wheel.
- Score, best score, missed list and squishies are saved per test in the browser.

Libraries in `lib/` (d3, topojson-client, canvas-confetti, all ISC licence) are stored in the repo so the game also runs through
[htmlpreview.github.io](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/Bolotaure/Geography-test/blob/main/index.html), which only loads scripts kept in GitHub.

US map: `us-states.js`, from `us-atlas`. France map: `fr-regions.js`, simplified from
[gregoiredavid/france-geojson](https://github.com/gregoiredavid/france-geojson) (Licence Ouverte / Etalab).
Japan map: `jp-prefectures.js`, simplified from [dataofjapan/land](https://github.com/dataofjapan/land).

jessicasogge/snackerpillar.readme:
# Snackerpillar 🐛

A browser game about a very hungry caterpillar made of circles. Every dot he eats adds a new circle to his back, in that dot's color. Grow as long as you can, and don't bump into anything!

## How to play

- **Move** with the arrow keys. He only moves while you're steering him, and turns sharply enough to U-turn without running into himself. On a touch screen, drag anywhere on the grass like a trackpad: he moves the way your finger slides, so your finger never hides him.
- **Eat the colored dots** to grow. He starts with one purple circle behind his head. Each one adds a circle to the end of his body in its color, and a new dot appears somewhere else a moment later.
- **Don't bump into rocks, mushrooms or his own body.** Any of those ends the level. The edges of the garden are safe: he just stops there, and you can slide him along them.

### Levels

There are 10 levels. Level 1 has 3 obstacles and you play until he's 15 circles long. Each level after that adds one more obstacle and 5 more circles:

| Level | Obstacles | Grow to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3 | 15 circles |
| 2 | 4 | 20 circles |
| 3 | 5 | 25 circles |
| 4 | 6 | 30 circles |
| 5 | 7 | 35 circles |
| 6 | 8 | 40 circles |
| 7 | 9 | 45 circles |
| 8 | 10 | 50 circles |
| 9 | 11 | 55 circles |
| 10 | 12 | 60 circles |

At the end of every level, a pop-up tells you how it went:

- **Level complete:** **Play level 2** (and so on) takes you to the next level. After level 10, **Play again** goes back to level 1.
- **Game over:** it says what he ran into, and **Try level 3 again** (or whichever level you're on) starts it over. Past level 1 there's also **Start over**, which goes back to level 1.

**Restart level**, under the garden, starts the level you're on over at any time. The levels are set in `LEVELS` in `public/game/config.js`.

## Running it locally

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22 or newer.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open <http://localhost:3007>. To use another port, set `PORT`, like `PORT=4000 npm run dev`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Runs the server on port 3007 and restarts it when the server code changes |
| `npm test` | Runs the tests once |
| `npm run test:watch` | Re-runs the tests as you edit |
| `npm run typecheck` | Checks the server's TypeScript |
| `npm run build` then `npm start` | Builds the server and runs the built version |

## How it's put together

The server (`src/index.ts`) is a small Express app that serves the `public/` folder and a `/health` check. The game itself runs entirely in the browser, as plain JavaScript modules in `public/game/`:

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `config.js` | Sizes, speeds and counts: how big a circle is, how many dots there are, and each level's obstacles and goal |
| `game.js` | A level's state, and moving it on one frame at a time: eating, growing, finishing the level, and game over |
| `steer.js` | How the arrow keys and dragging move him |
| `trail.js` | The path his head has taken, which his body follows |
| `field.js` | Keeping him on the field, and placing obstacles and dots |
| `collide.js` | Whether he's touching a dot, an obstacle or his own body |
| `draw.js` | Drawing the lawn, dots, rocks, mushrooms and him on the canvas |
| `main.js` | Connecting it all to the page: input, the animation loop, the level and length counter, and the end-of-level pop-up |

Tests live in `test/` and run with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). GitHub Actions runs them on every push and pull request.

The Fredoka and Nunito fonts are included under the SIL Open Font License (`public/fonts/*-OFL.txt`).

ethaserm/Golf-Game.readme:
# Fairway Legends ⛳

A low-poly 3D golf game for the browser (PC and phone), rebuilt from the ground up after
studying the Roblox game **Realistic Golf / Blox Golf** by Sharkie212. Same kind of game, with
its own art style, courses and characters. Nothing is copied from Roblox. See
[`docs/REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md`](docs/REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md) for what was researched and how
each feature maps across.

- **Swipe swing:** drag down to power up, swipe up to hit. Faster and straighter is better.
  Tilt the swipe to push or pull the ball; curve it to draw or fade.
- **Real ball physics:** drag, spin lift, wind, landings that bite into the turf, backspin that
  pulls the ball back on greens, sloped greens, trees, flagstick hits, lip-outs.
- **Two original courses:** *Timber Valley* (18 holes, par 72, pine valley) and
  *Willow Creek* (9 holes, par 36, rolling meadows with a creek).
- **Six golfers**, each with their own look, outfits and stats (power, accuracy, spin, putting).
- **Walk, drive a golf cart, or teleport** to your ball. Practice mode lets you place the ball anywhere.
- **Modes:** Free Play, Competitive (leaderboards), Practice, and Online (stroke play or scramble).
- **Shop:** Pro and Tour club sets (Tour adds spin control), Distance or Tour Soft ball,
  putters, and outfits. Coins come from playing.

## Play it on your PC

The game is plain HTML + JavaScript with no build step, but it has to be served by a web server
(opening `index.html` by double-clicking won't work). In **PowerShell**, from the game folder:

```powershell
py -m http.server 8000
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000> in Chrome or Edge. Leave the PowerShell window open while you play.

## Put it online (GitHub Pages)

1. On GitHub open the repo → **Settings** → **Pages**.
2. Under *Build and deployment* pick **Deploy from a branch**, choose your branch and `/ (root)`, then **Save**.
3. After a minute the page shows your link, e.g. `https://ethaserm.github.io/golf-game/`.
   It works on your phone too (add it to the home screen for full screen).

## Controls

| | PC | Phone |
|---|---|---|
| Walk / run | `WASD`, hold `Shift` to run | Joystick (push to the edge to run) |
| Look around | Drag with the mouse, wheel to zoom | Drag the screen |
| Address the ball | `E` when you're next to it | **Address** button |
| Golf cart | `C` to get in, `E` to get out | **Drive** / **Get out** |
| Teleport to your ball | `T` | **To Ball** |
| Aim | `A`/`D` (`Shift` = fine), right-drag, or tap the minimap | ◀ ▶ buttons or tap the minimap |
| Club | `Q`/`E` or mouse wheel | ‹ › on the club card |
| Launch angle | `W`/`S` | ▲ ▼ |
| Spin (Tour Set) | `I` `J` `K` `L` or click the spin ball | Tap the spin ball |
| Swing | Hold left mouse: drag down, then swipe up | Drag down, then swipe up |
| Scorecard / menu | `Tab` / `Esc` | ≡ / ❚❚ |
| Practice extras | `P` place ball, `R` retry shot | **Place Ball**, **Retry Shot** |

The **PIN** marker on the power meter shows roughly how hard to hit to reach the flag,
taking slope and wind into account. On greens it's worked out by simulating the actual roll.

## Online multiplayer

Online play uses a free **Firebase Realtime Database**. To test without any setup, open the game
in **two browser tabs** and use **Online → Same device**.

To play with friends on other devices:

1. Go to <https://console.firebase.google.com> → **Add project** (Analytics not needed).
2. **Build → Realtime Database → Create database** → pick a location → start in **locked mode**.
3. In the **Rules** tab paste the contents of [`database.rules.json`](database.rules.json) → **Publish**.
4. **Project settings** (gear icon) → *Your apps* → **Web** (`</>`) → register the app (no hosting needed).
5. Copy the `firebaseConfig` object it shows into [`js/net/firebase-config.js`](js/net/firebase-config.js)
   (replace `null` with the object; there's an example in the file). Make sure `databaseURL` is included.
6. Push the change. **Online** now creates rooms with a 5-letter code that friends can join, and
   competitive scores also go to the online leaderboards.

The rules allow anyone with the game link to create rooms and post scores, which is fine for
playing with friends. Don't put anything private in the database.

## Project layout

```
index.html            entry page (import map points "three" at the vendored copy)
css/style.css         all UI styling
js/main.js            boot + developer views (?view=hole, ?view=chars)
js/game.js            menus, profile, shop, round lifecycle, main loop
js/round.js           a round: holes, players, shots, rules, cameras, HUD wiring
js/physics.js         ball flight / bounce / roll / cup physics (pure JS, tested in Node)
js/shot.js            swing -> launch model, carry tables, club recommendation
js/clubdata.js        clubs, club sets, balls, putters
js/course/            terrain + surfaces (terrain.js), scene builder, props, course data
js/characters/        procedural golfer mesh, IK rig, animation, roster
js/net/               Firebase / same-device backends, rooms, lobby, leaderboards
js/vendor/            three.js r170 (MIT) + BufferGeometryUtils
tests/run.mjs         Node test suite (physics calibration, shots, every hole)
tools/*.mjs           Playwright scripts used to screenshot and smoke-test the game
```

## Tests

```powershell
node tests/run.mjs
```

230 checks: launch-monitor-accurate carries, wind, curve, green speed (stimp 10), putt
breaks, the cup, water, trees, determinism (multiplayer depends on it), character balance,
and every hole of both courses.

## Developer views

- `index.html?view=hole&c=0&h=3&cam=tee|green|top` shows a hole
- `index.html?view=chars&pose=top&club=D&cam=front|dtl|face` shows the golfers in a pose
  (`stand`, `walk`, `run`, `address`, `half`, `top`, `impact`, `follow`, `finish`, `celebrate`, `sad`)

# Eraly

> Project status, decisions and to-dos: see [`NOTES.md`](NOTES.md).

A daily pixel-art time-travel game. Seven moments from history, one guess each, 25 seconds on the clock — the closer your year, the further your traveller walks through the eras.

**Prototype:** plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step. Open `index.html` in a browser. Add `?day=2` or `?day=3` to play the other test days.

- `js/questions.js` — the daily questions, generated by `pipeline/schedule.mjs` from `questions.json`
- `js/scene.js` — the pixel world, traveller and animations
- `js/game.js` — game flow, scoring, timer, sharing (scoring explained in `SCORING.md`)

## Question pipeline (in progress)

1. `node pipeline/fetch.mjs` — pulls ~11k famous, dated candidates from Wikidata (via the free QLever mirror) into `pipeline/candidates/`. They are committed, so this only needs re-running a couple of times a year. Run `npm ci --prefix pipeline` once first. 14 categories: births, deaths, battles, wars, events, inventions/discoveries, nations, companies, books, films, songs, artworks, buildings, treaties.
2. Claude filters, verifies years, and writes prompts, context hints and reveal facts → `questions.json`, following `pipeline/WRITING.md`.
3. `node pipeline/schedule.mjs` — gives each verified question a permanent day (balanced mix of categories, eras and difficulty) and regenerates `js/questions.js`. Already-scheduled days never change.
4. **Every month** a scheduled Claude routine follows `pipeline/MONTHLY.md`: fresh candidates → batches → questions (`pipeline/add.mjs`) → Wikipedia check → schedule, then opens a pull request "Questions for <Month>". Review it and merge to deploy.

12akakor/MazeOfGalious-Haiku.readme:
# Maze of Galious for Haiku and RenkuOS

A native Haiku and RenkuOS port of the Brain Games remake of
*Knightmare II: The Maze of Galious*, the 1987 Konami classic for the MSX.

![Castle Greek with the naramura graphics and the xBR filter](docs/images/screenshot-naramura-xbr.png)

## The game

*The Maze of Galious* was developed and published by **Konami** in 1987
for the MSX computer, with a Famicom version later that year. It is the
second part of the Knightmare trilogy.

Popolon and Aphrodite travel through Castle Greek to free their unborn
child Pampas from the evil priest Galious. The castle is a large maze in
which the entrances to ten worlds are hidden, each with its own map. You
play both heroes and switch between them: Popolon pushes stones, opens
heavy doors and can vary the height of his jump; Aphrodite stays under
water longer and fires more projectiles. Along the way you collect
weapons, items, keys and money, and you visit shrines for help and to
save the game.

The original game is © 1987 Konami. This project is not affiliated with
or endorsed by Konami.

## The remake

The remake by **Brain Games** (2002 to 2009) keeps the original maps and
gameplay and adds new graphics and music, with several graphic and sound
sets to choose from.

- Website: <https://mog.jorito.net/>
- Coding: Santi Ontañón and Jorrith Schaap
- Graphics: Santi Ontañón, Boltian, Hinox, MP83 and Naramura
- Music and sound effects: Rob Powelse, Jorrith Schaap, Bart Roijmans,
  Wolf_ and Randy Wintjes
- Maps: Santi Ontañón

This port is based on the last nightly source snapshot of the remake,
`mog-svn-20120228` from the Brain Games nightlies
(<https://braingames.jorito.net/nightlies/>), whose game code matches
release 0.63 (build 1548). The unchanged snapshot is kept in
`upstream/nightly-20120228/`.

![The same room with the original graphics and the xBR filter](docs/images/screenshot-original-xbr.png)

## What this port changes and adds

The remake was written for SDL 1.2 with SDL_mixer, SDL_sound and
SDL_image. This port replaces all of that with the native Haiku API, adds
features that make it nicer to play on a modern screen, and fixes some
bugs. The game logic itself is unchanged: an automated test plays a
scripted 1400-frame session and compares every frame with the original
SDL version, and they are identical.

**Native Haiku / RenkuOS**

- Only the system kits are used: `libbe` (window, keyboard), `libmedia`
  (sound through BSoundPlayer) and `libtranslation` (PNG screenshots). No
  SDL or other external libraries.
- Own sound mixer with WAV and Ogg Vorbis decoding (stb_vorbis included).
- Haiku package (`.hpkg`) with the standard layout and a Deskbar entry,
  plus a separate package with the extra graphic and sound sets.
- New vector (HVIF) application icon.

**Picture**

- The game draws at 640x400. The port scales this to any window size or
  to full screen, keeping the 16:10 shape.
- Three filters, switched with F3:
  - **xBR** (default): Hyllian's xBR-lv2 filter, ported from the libretro
    shader to C++, for smooth outlines that keep the pixel art character.
  - **sharp**: sharp bilinear, crisp pixels at any size.
  - **nearest**: whole-number scaling with black borders.
- The "original" set is 320x200 art stored with doubled pixels; the port
  detects this per set, so xBR works on the real art resolution.
- xBR only recalculates the parts of the picture that changed, and
  spreads a full-screen change (a new room) over a few frames, so the game
  stays smooth even on a virtual machine with one CPU.
- Waits for the screen refresh before drawing where the graphics driver
  supports it.

**Sound**

- High-quality resampling (windowed sinc filter) of the 11 and 22 kHz sound
  sets to 44.1 kHz, instead of linear interpolation.
- Music files are opened without blocking the sound output, so music
  does not stutter on room changes.

**Convenience**

- Starts in a window as large as fits on the screen; the window can be
  resized and zoomed. Alt+Enter switches to full screen.
- Remembers the window size and position, full screen and the chosen
  filter.
- The default sets are graphics **naramura** and music **jorito**.
- Screenshot key (S by default, can be redefined) that saves exactly what
  you see as a PNG file in your home folder.
- Timing display (F4) with filter and drawing time, frames per second and
  the vertical sync state.
- The key screen (K on the title screen) lists the extra keys of the
  port.

**Bug fixes in the remake**

- Crash after the Konami logo when the saved settings named a graphic or
  sound set that is not installed.
- Reading past the end of the set list when fewer sets than expected are
  installed.
- `fclose(NULL)` when a picture file is missing, and some compiler
  warnings.

## Keys

These are the defaults. The game keys and the screenshot key can be
changed with K on the title screen.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Cursor keys | Walk, jump (up), climb |
| Space | Sword |
| M | Secondary weapon |
| F1 | Item screen |
| F2 | Pause |
| F5 to F9 | Save the game in slot 1 to 5 (at the Demeter shrine) |
| Esc | Back to the title screen |
| PgUp / PgDn | Zoom |
| F10 or 9 | Next graphic set |
| F11 or 0 | Next sound set |
| F3 | Next filter (xBR, nearest, sharp) |
| F4 | Show or hide the timing display |
| S | Screenshot |
| Alt+Enter | Full screen on or off |
| F12 or Alt+Q | Quit |

On the title screen, Space starts the game, K redefines the keys and L
lets you enter a password.

## Installing

Download `mazeofgalious-<version>-x86_64.hpkg` from the
[Releases](../../releases) page and double-click it, or in Terminal:

    pkgman install ./mazeofgalious-<version>-x86_64.hpkg

The optional package `mazeofgalious_extras-<version>-any.hpkg` adds the
graphic sets hinox, boltian, alternate and alfonso and the sound sets
Bart, Rob and wolf.

The game appears in the Deskbar under Applications. Settings are kept in
`~/config/settings/MazeOfGalious/`. To remove the game:

    pkg

cev64/chainmates.readme:
# Chainmates

A daily teammate-chain trivia game. You get two players, for example *Brett Favre → Josh Jacobs*, and connect them through a chain of teammates in as few links as possible. Hard mode (the default) hides every team; par is the shortest chain + 2, so the shortest chain is an eagle. Easy mode shows each player's teams and years, with par = shortest + 1. You have 3 downs: a wrong guess is an incompletion. You share a spoiler-free result card.

It starts with the NFL (2002 onward, via [nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse), CC-BY 4.0) and is built to add other sports.

*Unofficial fan game. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the NFL, NFLPA, or any team.*

## Layout

```
web/      static single-page app (vanilla JS), plus the legal pages
core/     handoff-core.js: all game rules (UMD, no deps), with node:test tests and shared test vectors
data/nfl/ generated players.json and puzzles.json (committed)
tools/    build_data.py (nflverse → data), test_data.py, build_site.sh, dev.sh
docs/     spec.md (contract), decisions.md, design-notes.md, research.md
.github/  weekly in-season data refresh, plus a manual Pages deploy
```

## Develop

```sh
npm test                      # core tests, including validation of every stored puzzle
python3 tools/test_data.py    # data sanity checks
tools/dev.sh                  # build _site/ and serve it on http://localhost:8765
```

Rebuild the data (downloads are cached in `.cache/`):

```sh
pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python3 tools/build_data.py            # refresh players and extend puzzles; past puzzles stay frozen
```

To pin a puzzle to a date, add it to `tools/puzzle_overrides.json`.

## Deploy

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages from `main`.
- Every push to `main` that touches `web/`, `core/` or `data/` deploys it (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`).
- The daily data refresh deploys after it commits new data (`.github/workflows/update-data.yml`, August through February).
- To deploy by hand: Actions ▸ Deploy site ▸ Run workflow.
- One-time setup: Settings ▸ Pages ▸ Source: **GitHub Actions**.

The live URL is https://cev64.github.io/chainmates/. Share cards link to it, via `CONFIG.shareUrl` in `web/app.js`.

kobi2132/lumda.readme:
# הלומדות שלי

אתר סטטי (HTML/JS בלבד, בלי שרת ובלי build) שמרכז לומדות לילדים לפי נושא וגיל. מתאים לפרסום ב-GitHub Pages.

## מבנה

```
index.html                     מסך הבית: קטלוג עם סינון לפי גיל ונושא
apps/catalog.js                רשימת הלומדות והנושאים
apps/<id>/index.html           כל לומדה בתיקייה משלה
```

## איך מוסיפים לומדה חדשה

1. יוצרים תיקייה `apps/<id>/` ושמים בה `index.html` של הלומדה.
2. מוסיפים רשומה ל-`LUMDA_APPS` ב-`apps/catalog.js`: `id`, `title`, `description`, `subject`, `ages: [מגיל, עד גיל]`, `icon`, `path`.
3. נושא חדש מוסיפים ל-`LUMDA_SUBJECTS` באותו קובץ.
4. בתוך הלומדה, קישור חזרה למסך הבית הוא `../../index.html`.

כל לומדה שומרת התקדמות ב-localStorage עם מפתחות בקידומת משלה (למשל `melody-`), כדי שלא יתנגשו.

## הלומדות

| id | שם | נושא | גיל |
|---|---|---|---|
| melody-english | מלודי לומדת אנגלית | אנגלית | 3–6 |
| numbers | מספרים וחשבון | חשבון | 4–7 (נושאי גן למלודי, נושאי כיתה א' לים) |

## פינת ההורים (melody-english)

לוחצים לחיצה ארוכה (2 שניות) על הכותרת למעלה. שם רואים התקדמות ומילים לתרגול, מכבים או מאטים את הדיבור, שומרים ומשחזרים גיבוי לקובץ, ומאפסים התקדמות.
אפשר גם לכבות את התרגום לעברית בכרטיסי המילים, לכבות את המיקרופון במשחק Say it! (הזיהוי נעשה בשרתים של גוגל), ולקבוע תזכורת להפסקה אחרי 15, 20 או 30 דקות.

## הנושאים והמשחקים (melody-english)

19 נושאים, ביניהם אותיות ABC (כל אות עם מילה מוכרת), פעלים, רגשות ומשפטים קצרים. כל נושא מחולק לשלבים של כ-5 מילים.
המשחקים בכל שלב: Find it, Balloons, Memory, What's this? (שומעים שתי מילים ובוחרים את זו שמתאימה לתמונה) ו-Say it! (אומרים את המילה והטלפון מקשיב). בצבעים יש גם Magic Dress / Magic Armor, ובפעלים יש Do it! (עושים את הפעולה עם הגוף).

## הילדים (kids.js)

מסך הבית מתחיל ב"מי משחק היום?". לוחצים על הדמות, שומעים ברכה ("ברוכה הבאה מלודי" או "ברוך הבא ים"), ואז מופיעות הלומדות של אותו ילד לפי השדה `kids` ב-`apps/catalog.js`.
הילד שנבחר נשמר ב-localStorage במפתח `lumda-kid`. כל לומדה יכולה לקרוא אותו עם `LUMDA_KID()` (מ-`../../kids.js`) ולהתאים שם, לשון פנייה, קול ודמות. הדמויות נמצאות ב-`assets/kids/`.

jamesparser/naga-atelier.readme:
# AgentAsia Voxel

**Talk it into the room. Sculpt it with your hands.**

AgentAsia Voxel is a seated mixed-reality block studio for Meta Quest 3. It runs in the browser (WebXR, nothing to install). Talk to **Naga**, the coiled-serpent companion, and your hands do the rest.
You say what you want and Naga, a small coiled-serpent companion, drafts it on your real desk in passthrough.
Then you fix it with your hands: pinch, slide, snap, tap, drop it in the bin, undo. You never need to pick up a controller.

> **Agent drafts, human sculpts.** AI placement won't always be right, and that's expected.
> Correcting it by hand isn't a fallback. It's the product.

Built for the Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026 (Productivity track, New Experience division).

**Try it:** open **https://naga-atelier.vercel.app** in Quest Browser on a Quest 3 / 3S.

## The 60-second loop

1. Open the URL in Quest Browser and tap **Enter**. Passthrough fades in and a build grid sits on your desk.
2. Pinch the glowing block and drag it. It snaps to the grid with a soft *thunk*.
3. Tap the mic and say **“Build a small house.”** Naga answers out loud and the cottage pops in layer by layer.
4. Pinch the roof and slide it off. Hold a wall block still to pop it free, then drop it in the bin. Tap **undo** to bring it back.
5. Say **“Make the roof red,”** **“a bit bigger,”** **“rotate it,”** or **“build a tower on the left.”**

## Hand interactions (no controllers)

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| Pinch a block and move | Carries its whole part (roof, walls, tower…), snaps to a 4 cm grid on release, settles under gravity |
| Pinch a block and hold still (~0.8 s) | Pops that single block free from its part |
| Quick pinch-tap on a block | Paints it with the active colour |
| Quick pinch-tap on empty desk | Places a block (it stacks onto whatever is below) |
| Release over the red bin | Deletes what you are carrying |
| Invalid drop (out of bounds, blocked) | Springs back with an audio cue |
| Poke (or pinch) a dock button | Mic · Undo · Redo · 8 colours · ★ draft a blueprint · Re-centre desk |

Hand tracking has no haptics, so every action has a sound: pickup tick, snap thunk, delete whoosh, undo chime.
Everything sits within about 60 cm of a seated user, and the dock is in the lower field of view.

## Tetris mode

Tap **TETRIS** on the mode bar (or say **“let's play Tetris”**) and the desk turns into a 10 × 4 × 14 neon well.
The room dims, a hue-cycling vector tunnel and a warp starfield stream out behind the well, and a synthwave loop speeds up with every level.
The same cube blocks fall as the seven classic tetrominoes. Fill a straight row from left to right and it blows up
in sparkles. Fill a whole layer and you get a big bonus. Blocks above a cleared row fall into its slice.

| Action | Keyboard | Mouse / touch | Quest hands | Quest controller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Move left / right | ← → (or A/D) | drag sideways, or Left / Right buttons | pinch and move your hand | thumbstick left / right |
| Back row / front row (4 deep) | ↑ ↓ (or W/S) | drag up / down the screen, or Back row / Front row | pinch and move away / toward you | thumbstick up / down |
| Spin · Flip · Tilt | Q or E · R · F | quick tap = spin, or the buttons | quick pinch = spin; pinch + twist wrist = flip / tilt | A/X · B/Y · press stick |
| Fall faster · Drop now | hold Shift · Space | Faster (hold) · Drop | pull down · flick down | hold grip · trigger |
| Pause · Help · Back | P · ? · Esc | buttons in the control bar | poke PAUSE / BACK on the desk | press the desk buttons |

**Pick how deep the well is: 1–4 rows.** 1 row plays like classic Tetris (↑ rotates, ↓ falls faster); 2–4 rows add the 3D back/front rows. Use the row buttons on screen, keys 1–4, or poke **ROWS 1-4** on the desk. Changing rows starts a new game, and your choice is remembered (default: 1 row).

Your build desk is untouched while you play. Say **“back to building”** to return to it. Your best score is saved on the device.

## Angry Sling

Tap **ANGRY SLING** on the mode bar (left edge of the desk), or say **“angry sling”**. A tabletop physics puzzle appears:
pull back the slingshot, let a glowing pebble fly, and knock down glass, wood and stone towers to pop the purple
*gloomlings* hiding in them. There are **12 levels** (First flight → Citadel), 3 stars each, and progress is saved on the device.

- **Hands:** pinch (on the pebble or anywhere), pull back toward you, release. The dotted arc shows where it will go.
- **Controller:** hold the trigger, pull back, let go.
- **Look from any angle:** lean in or walk around, or use the dock to **turn the arena** 45° left/right and **zoom** (1.15× ↔ 1.8×).
- **Clearing a level moves you straight to the next one** (after a 3-second celebration). After level 12 it starts over. **Dock:** back · retry · skip level · turn left · turn right · zoom · voice.
- **Desktop:** left-drag to pull (wheel while pulling aims higher), right-drag to orbit, R retry, N next, Q/E turn, Z zoom.

The physics (cannon-es) is simulated at full scale (1 m blocks) and rendered at 1:10, so towers fall with real weight.
Glass shatters easily, wood takes a few hits, stone is tough. Every level is unit-tested to stand still until hit and not collapse on its own.

## Arcade (7 more games)

Tap **ARCADE** on the mode bar (or say **“open the arcade”**, **“play galago”**, **“mike penguin”**…) and seven tiles appear on the desk. Poke or pinch one, press 1–7, or click the buttons. Every game works with hands, Quest controllers, mouse, touch and keyboard. Each one has its own synthesised theme tune and sound effects, its best score is saved on the device, and a How to play card is on the desk and on screen.

| Game | What you do | Hands | Keyboard |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Galago** | Space shooter: an alien swarm hovers at the back of the desk and dives at you in 3D curves | pinch + move to fly, hold to fire | arrows + Space |
| **Marble Maze** | Tilt a wooden board to roll

fapivnytsia/zonk.readme:
# ZONK

Кости на 6 костей: бросаешь, откладываешь очковые и решаешь — рисковать дальше или записать очки хода. Побеждает тот, кто первым наберёт цель.

Объёмные кубики, звук, история партии и соперник с двумя характерами — осторожный или азартный, выпадает случайно в начале партии.

## Файлы

| Файл | Что это |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | разметка |
| `style.css` | вид |
| `app.js` | логика страницы и анимации |
| `engine/` | правила, ход партии и соперник |
| `fonts/`, `fonts.css` | шрифты Unbounded, Golos Text, JetBrains Mono (лицензия OFL, тексты рядом) |

## Приватность

- Страница не делает внешних запросов: шрифты лежат здесь же.
- В браузере сохраняются только настройки игры (цель и звук) — в `localStorage`.

# Белка

Казахстанская карточная игра двое на двое: вы и партнёр против двух ботов. Мобильное веб-приложение: ставится на главный экран, работает без интернета, помнит партию.

## Запустить на компьютере

```bash
python -m http.server 8080
```

Откройте http://localhost:8080. Офлайн-кеш работает только на `localhost` и по HTTPS.

## Тесты

```bash
node tests/engine.test.mjs
node tests/storage.test.mjs
node tests/game.test.mjs
node tests/manifest.test.mjs
node tests/sw.test.mjs
node tests/css.test.mjs
```

`package.json` нужен только для того, чтобы Node читал файлы `js/*.js` как ES-модули. Зависимостей нет, `npm install` не нужен.

## Опубликовать на GitHub Pages

1. Создайте на GitHub пустой репозиторий, например `belka`.
2. Отправьте код:
   ```bash
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<аккаунт>/belka.git
   git push -u origin feat/pwa-v1:main
   ```
3. В репозитории: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → `main` и `/ (root)` → Save.
4. Через минуту приложение откроется по адресу `https://<аккаунт>.github.io/belka/`.

## Выпуск новой версии

1. Внесите изменения и прогоните тесты.
2. В `sw.js` увеличьте `VERSION`, например `1.0.0` → `1.0.1`. Если добавили новый файл, допишите его в `ASSETS`.
3. Сделайте коммит и `git push`. У игроков внизу появится «Доступна новая версия — Обновить».

## Иконки

Исходник — `icons/icon.svg`. PNG пересобираются командой `node tools/make-icons.mjs`.

## Проверить на телефоне

- **iPhone (Safari):**
  - откройте адрес;
  - «Поделиться» → «На экран "Домой"»;
  - запустите с иконки: панелей Safari нет, системная строка не перекрывает шапку, полоска «Домой» не перекрывает руку;
  - включите авиарежим, закройте и откройте снова — игра загружается.
- **Android (Chrome):**
  - откройте адрес;
  - нажмите значок «Установить» в шапке или «Установить приложение» в меню Chrome;
  - запустите с иконки и проверьте то же, что на iPhone.
- **Сохранение:** начните раздачу, смахните приложение из списка недавних, откройте снова — партия продолжается.
- **Поворот:** поверните телефон боком — появится просьба держать его вертикально.

## Устройство проекта

| Файл | Что делает |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | страница приложения и все мета-теги для iPhone и Android |
| `manifest.webmanifest` | название, иконки и режим запуска при установке |
| `sw.js` | офлайн-кеш и обновления |
| `css/app.css` | дизайн стола и карт |
| `js/engine.js` | правила, раздача и боты, без DOM |
| `js/i18n.js` | тексты на русском и казахском |
| `js/storage.js` | настройки, язык и сохранение партии в памяти телефона |
| `js/game.js` | ход партии: фазы, таймеры ботов, подсчёт глаз |
| `js/ui.js` | отрисовка и нажатия |
| `js/app.js` | запуск, офлайн-кеш, установка, обновления |
| `belka.html` | исходная версия-артефакт, оставлена для справки |

yvettege728/kiki-bouba-pilot.desc: Kiki/bouba warm-up task for eye-tracking pilots
yvettege728/kiki-bouba-pilot.readme:
# Kiki / Bouba eye-tracking pilot

A short warm-up task for getting participants used to an eye tracker (SCI 6384, Harvard GSD).

**Play in the browser:** https://yvettege728.github.io/kiki-bouba-pilot/

**Run offline:** download `kiki-bouba-pilot.html` (or Code > Download ZIP) and open it in Chrome. No install, no internet needed.

## Flow (about 3 min)

1. Follow the dot: 9 positions, 1.5 s each (accuracy check against the tracker)
2. Practice: 2 trials with feedback
3. Round 1, easy: clear kiki vs. bouba, keys `F` / `J`
4. Round 2, varied: kikis and boubas with different spike counts, sizes, irregularity and rotation, keys `F` / `J`
5. Round 3, sort: one shape at a time goes into the KIKI house or the BOUBA house (keys `F` / `J`, or mouse drag). Shapes run from round to spiky, plus hybrids that are half spiky, half round. Ambiguous shapes have no right answer: the point is to see which features people look at before deciding
6. Results screen with CSV / JSON download

## Controls built in

- 800 ms central fixation cross before every trial
- Parametric shapes with equal area, positions counterbalanced
- Keyboard responses, cursor hidden, 10 s timeout, 500 ms blank between trials
- Sync patch in the bottom-left corner turns white while a stimulus is on screen (for aligning tracker recordings)
- Pixel AOI coordinates for every shape are logged per trial; hybrids also log separate spiky and round AOIs
- House sides (kiki left or right) are randomized per participant
- Drag mode logs both grab time (decision) and drop time
- `Esc` stops the session and still lets you save data

## Settings

Edit the `CFG` block at the top of the script to change timings or the number of trials.

The game does not connect to the eye tracker. Record gaze in the tracker software and align it using the sync patch and timestamps.

muhammadsamir11/game.readme:
# Brick Racers

Build a car from toy bricks, then race it! Made for playing on an iPad.

## Start the game (on the Mac)

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

The terminal prints the addresses, for example:

```
On this computer: http://localhost:8080
On the iPad (best, same Wi-Fi): http://Your-Mac.local:8080
Or by number: http://192.168.1.23:8080
```

Use the `.local` address on the iPad: it stays the same even when your router gives the Mac a new number, and the saved cars belong to the address they were made on.

## Play on the iPad

1. Make sure the iPad is on the same Wi-Fi as the Mac and the Mac is running `npm start`.
2. Open Safari on the iPad and type the "On the iPad (best)" address.
3. Tap the Share button → **Add to Home Screen** so it opens full screen like an app.
4. From now on, always start the game from that home-screen icon. Safari can clear cars made in a normal Safari tab if the site isn't visited for a while; the home-screen app keeps them.
5. Hold the iPad sideways.

### Play offline (from your Dokploy site)

Offline play needs the game's **https** address (your Dokploy domain). It can't work from the Mac's `http://….local` address above: browsers only allow offline copies on secure (https) sites.

1. On the iPad, open the https address in Safari → Share → **Add to Home Screen**.
2. Open the game **once from the new home-screen icon while online**. It saves a copy of itself, and from then on it works with no internet.
3. Build and play from that icon. The home-screen app keeps its **own** saves: cars made in a normal Safari tab (or at the Mac's `.local` address) don't show up in it, and the other way round.
4. When you deploy a new version, the app picks it up by itself the next time it's opened online.

On a computer or Android, Chrome shows a **⬇ Install** button on the game's home screen (or an install icon in the address bar).

(While you run it on this Mac at `localhost`, the offline copy is switched off so changes show straight away.)

## Play together (iPad + Android, or friends at their homes)

Up to 4 players can drive around the city together or race each other, each on their own tablet.

1. Every tablet opens the game from the **same https Dokploy address** (the home-screen app installed from it is fine). The Mac's `http://….local` address also works, but only for tablets on the same Wi-Fi as the Mac.
2. One player taps **🤝 Play together → ✨ Make a room**. Four big pictures appear, for example 🦖🍕🚀⭐ (🔊 reads them out).
3. The others tap **🔑 Join a room** and tap the same four pictures.
4. The 👑 player picks **🏙 City** or **🏁 Race**, and everyone goes there together.

In the city with friends:
- You see each other's cars and figures with name tags, and can bump into each other.
- **😀 Stickers** pop above your head on everyone's screen. Nothing can be typed, so there's no chat.
- Honks, sirens, boost and confetti show and sound on friends' tablets.
- Tap a friend's face on the left to **zap** next to them.
- Driving through the 🏁 arch asks "Race everyone?"
- **🎮 Games** has four games:
  - **Treasure hunt:** be first to the chest; the arrow and the beeping help.
  - **Coin rush:** grab the most sparkly coins.
  - **Police tag:** the police catches someone by driving up to them.
  - **Follow the leader:** stay close to the ⭐ leader to earn stars.

In a race together, computer cars fill the empty places, and everyone gets the same countdown and podium.

For grown-ups:
- **Safety.** Rooms are private: there is no list of rooms, only the four-picture code. The 👑 player can **Send out** anyone from the room screen, and someone sent out can't come back to that room.
- **Losing Wi-Fi.** A tablet that loses Wi-Fi gets its place back if it returns within 30 seconds. The game also reconnects by itself the next time it's opened.
- **Server.** Play together runs on the same `server.js` as the game, at `/play`. It needs the `ws` package, so the deploy must run `npm install` (or `npm ci`). Without it the game still works, just alone.
- **Dokploy.** Its proxy (Traefik) passes WebSockets through by default. If **Play together** says "needs the internet" while the game itself loads fine, check that the domain's proxy allows WebSocket upgrades.
- **Offline.** Single-player stays fully offline. Only Play together needs the internet.

## How to play

- **First time:** make your own figure — hair or hat, face, skin, shirt and pants — and type your name. Your figure drives all your cars. Tap your face at the top of the home screen to change it or make friends.
- **Build** → pick a car and follow the steps (🔊 reads them out loud), or choose **Free Build** and make your own. A race car needs 4 wheels at the corners, an engine and a seat.
- **Supercars** → Lamborghini Aventador and Huracán, Ferrari SF90 Stradale and LaFerrari, Bugatti Chiron and McLaren P1 are at the top of the build list — the fastest cars in the game (the Bugatti is fastest of all). The 🏎 Supercar tab has the noses, scoops, wings, scissor doors, V12 engines, super wheels, badges and name plates to make your own; tap a badge to pick its brand.
- **Race** → ◀ ▶ to steer, **GO** to drive, **STOP** to brake (hold it to go backwards). Stuck upside down? Press **Flip me!**
- **City** → a little city with your garage! Walk around as your figure (thumb stick or arrow keys), walk up to one of your cars and tap **Get in** (or E). Drive around town, up the ramps of the parking garage, and stop in a numbered spot, then **Get out** to park it there. Drive through the 🏁 arch to race. **🚗 My cars** lists your cars to race, change or delete.
- In the city: grab gold coins 🪙, try the jumps in the stunt park (in the air, tap GO to flip, ◀ ▶ to spin), and drive into the glowing ring at the pizza shop for a mission.

On a computer the arrow keys (or W A S D) drive too.

## For grown-ups

- `npm test` runs the rule tests (snapping, instructions, saving, laps, AI, physics, offline file list, play-together rooms and games).
- The offline f

# Scrawl

A multiplayer draw-and-guess game for friends. It runs entirely in the browser: no server and no accounts.

**Play:** https://harshgaba1196.github.io/scrawl/

## How it works

1. Open the page, pick a name and click **Create a room**. You're the host, so keep that tab open.
2. In the lobby, click **Copy invite link** and send it to your friends.
3. They open the link, type a name and press **Join**.

Players connect to the host's browser directly over WebRTC, using [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com/) to find each other.

## Features

- Easy, medium and hard words, worth 1×, 1.3× and 1.6× points
- Pen, eraser, fill bucket, line, rectangle, ellipse, undo and redo
- Letter hints over time, close-guess alerts, streak bonuses
- Live emoji reactions and a "Love this drawing" button
- Nine word packs plus secret custom words
- Podium and a gallery of every drawing at the end

manishkshtriya/linefollower-ai.readme:
# AI line follower car

**Live demo (3D car driven by the trained network): https://manishkshtriya.github.io/linefollower-ai/**

**Game: [Be the AI](game/README.md)**: drive the car yourself against the network (`python3 game/line_follower_game.py`).

**New: the network learned to drive in the simulator** (clean runs 141 → 205 of 240 random cars). Video: [`sim/ai_learns_the_fix.mp4`](sim/ai_learns_the_fix.mp4), details: [`learn/README.md`](learn/README.md)

**Simulation video (the real firmware driving a virtual car):** [`sim/line_follower_sim.mp4`](sim/line_follower_sim.mp4)

![Simulation preview](sim/preview.gif)

A two-wheel car with a caster wheel in front. Four IR sensors look at the floor, a small neural network
(4 inputs, two hidden layers of 7, 2 outputs) turns the sensor pattern into a left and a right motor speed.
The whole network is 107 numbers (428 bytes), so it runs on an ESP32 and needs no Jetson.

The goal is to follow solid, dashed and dotted lines and to come back to the line when it drifts off.

## Output (simulation)

Screenshots from the browser simulator, running the trained network on the same sensor layout as the car.
The red dots are the four sensors, the panels below the track show the live sensor reading, motor speeds, laps and lost-line count.
These are simulation outputs only. The firmware has not been run on a real car yet.

**Demo loop** (solid, dashed, solid, dotted, solid)

![Demo loop](docs/track-demo.png)

**Oval**

![Oval](docs/track-oval.png)

**Winding track**

![Winding track](docs/track-winding.png)

**Long gap (70 px, 189 mm) on dashed tape.** The car starts losing the line, which is the known limit.

![Gap of 70 px](docs/gap-70px.png)

## What is in this folder

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `training/train.py` | Trains the network with numpy and writes `weights.h` and `weights.json` |
| `firmware/sensor_test/sensor_test.ino` | Step 1: prints the four sensor readings so you can check the wiring |
| `firmware/linefollower/linefollower.ino` | The car program: reads sensors, runs the network, drives the motors |
| `firmware/linefollower/nn.h` | The network forward pass in C |
| `firmware/linefollower/weights.h` | Trained weights (generated, replace after every training run) |
| `docs/` | Project website (`index.html`, served by GitHub Pages) and simulation screenshots |
| `game/` | Desktop game (pygame): race the network, hard mode with only the 4 sensor lamps, draw your own track |
| `learn/` | The network learns by itself in the simulator (evolution strategy). The firmware now uses these learned weights |
| `sim/` | Firmware-in-the-loop simulator: runs `linefollower.ino` unchanged against a virtual car. See `sim/README.md` |
| `wokwi/` | Ready-made Wokwi ESP32 circuit: run the real firmware in the browser with switches as sensors |
| `tests/check.py` | Checks that the C code gives the same answers as the Python network |

## Hardware

- ESP32 DevKit board (Arduino-ESP32 core 3.x)
- 4 IR reflective sensor modules (TCRT5000 type) or one 4-channel array, mounted **about 20 mm apart** (centre to centre) for 19 mm tape
- TB6612FNG motor driver
- 2 geared DC motors with wheels, 1 caster wheel, chassis
- Battery pack for the motors, 5 V supply (power bank or regulator) for the ESP32
- Black electrical tape on a light floor

### Wiring

| ESP32 pin | Connects to |
|---|---|
| GPIO 34, 35, 32, 33 | Sensor outputs S1 (far left) to S4 (far right), looking forward |
| GPIO 25, 26, 27 | TB6612 PWMA, AIN1, AIN2 (left motor) |
| GPIO 4, 16, 17 | TB6612 PWMB, BIN1, BIN2 (right motor) |
| GPIO 23 | TB6612 STBY |
| 3V3 | Sensor VCC and TB6612 VCC |
| GND | All grounds joined: sensors, TB6612, battery, ESP32 |

Motor battery goes to TB6612 VM. Left motor on output A, right motor on output B.

## Steps

1. **Check the sensors.** Flash `sensor_test.ino`, open the Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and slide the car over the tape.
   You should see patterns like `0110` when the line is in the middle. If 1 and 0 are swapped, set `LINE_IS_HIGH` to `false`
   in both sketches. Turn the small potentiometer on each module until it switches cleanly.
2. **Train.** `cd training && python3 train.py --out ../firmware/linefollower/weights.h` (needs only numpy).
3. **Check the C code.** From this folder run `python3 tests/check.py`. It should print `OK`.
4. **Flash** `linefollower.ino` with the wheels off the ground first. If a wheel turns the wrong way, set
   `LEFT_REVERSED` or `RIGHT_REVERSED` to `true`. Raise `MIN_DUTY` if the motors do not start at low speed.
5. **Test on the floor**, starting with a solid line, then dashed, then dotted.

## Firmware-in-the-loop simulation

`sim/hil_sim.cpp` compiles the real `linefollower.ino` on a PC and connects its pins to a virtual car with motor
stall, motor lag, sensor spot size, weak-motor and noise faults. It found that **sensor spacing is the most
important build choice**: with 19 mm tape, sensors 20 mm apart passed 11 of 12 hard scenarios, and sensors 30 mm
apart passed only 5. With 20 mm spacing the car ran clean on solid, dashed and dotted tape, with an 8% weaker motor,
with 3% wrong sensor reads and with gaps up to 135 mm. Gaps of 189 mm still lose the line. Details and commands are in
[`sim/README.md`](sim/README.md).

## Training on the real car (recommended)

The built-in table has 16 rows, one per sensor pattern, labelled by a hand-written rule. That is enough to get the car
moving, but it only copies the rule. To make the network learn from the real car, log driving data and train on that:

1. Drive the car along solid, dashed and dotted tape (by hand, remote control or a slow version of the rule)
   and log one row per control step: `s1,s2,s3,s4,left,right`.
2. Save it as `my_drive.csv` and run `python3 train.py --csv my_drive.csv`.

The sensor inputs can also be made analog (read the sensor with `analogRead`, scale to 0 to 1) so the network sees
how much line is under each sensor. This gives it much more to work with tha

# STEP Onboarding — Red Light, Green Light

A multiplayer Red Light, Green Light game for the SPRINT-STEP onboarding.

- **Big screen:** open the game link on the projector laptop and choose **Host the game**.
- **Players:** scan the QR code on the big screen, type a name, pick Boy or Girl, and tap **Join**. No login needed.
- Up to 20 players. The first 3 across the safe line win.

The live connection between the big screen and the phones runs on Supabase Realtime
(project "Online Games", see `config.js`). No database tables are used.

Hosted with GitHub Pages: every push to `main` publishes the site automatically
(Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**).

lambsubstitute/cozy-cat-sanctuary.readme:
# Cozy Cat Sanctuary

A cosy pixel-art living room for your own cats. They nap by the fire, chase the laser and the mouse, watch the birds, knock things off the mantelpiece, dream, make friends, and react to the weather outside, which can be the real weather where you live.

**Play it:** https://lambsubstitute.github.io/cozy-cat-sanctuary/

Everything is in one file, `index.html`. There's nothing to install or build: open it in a browser and it runs.

## What's in the room

- **Your own cats.** On your first visit you choose how many cats live here (1 to 4) and design each one: name, coat, pattern, eyes, character, voice, and grown-up or kitten. Or move in with the originals: Moe, Mr Mews and Joe.
- **A life of their own.** Naps, zoomies, grooming, cuddle piles, play-fights, games of chase, knocking things over, asking for food and fuss. Each cat has needs (food, energy, love) and a mood.
- **Your hand.** Pet, give treats, brush, or get the laser pointer out. Release a mouse, toss the yarn, put down a cardboard box, sprinkle catnip, fill the bird feeder, play hide and seek.
- **The view outside.** Real time of day, seasons (with Halloween, Bonfire Night and Christmas), and either made-up weather or **the real weather where you live** (Settings ⚙️). Birds and squirrels by day; an owl, moths, a fox, shooting stars and the very occasional UFO at night. Thunderstorms and fireworks send the nervous ones under the sofa.
- **Friendships and dreams.** Pairs of cats grow closer and become best friends. Sleeping cats dream about what happened today.
- **A stray kitten** may turn up at the window, soaked if it's raining. Let it in and it joins the family.
- **The diary, photos and screensaver.** Everything memorable is written in the diary; snap a polaroid; or go full screen and just watch.

Everything is remembered in your browser (local storage) between visits. **Settings ⚙️ → Start over** wipes it and lets you choose your cats again.

## Real local weather

In Settings ⚙️, choose "The real weather where I live" and search for your town (or use your location). The window then shows the real rain, snow, fog, cloud, storms, temperature and sunrise/sunset, checked every 15 minutes. Weather data comes from [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) (free, no key needed).

It works on the GitHub Pages link above, or when you open `index.html` straight from your computer. It doesn't work inside a Claude artifact, because those pages aren't allowed to go online.

## Making changes

The whole game is `index.html`: the HTML at the top, then one script holding the room, the cats and everything else, in clearly commented sections. Edit it, open it in a browser, and refresh.

Libraries are loaded from CDNs: [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) (play CDN) for the page styling, and the [Press Start 2P](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Press+Start+2P) and [VT323](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/VT323) fonts from Google Fonts.

## Tests

The `tests/` folder has automated checks that run the game headlessly in Chromium with a fixed random seed and fast-forward it frame by frame, checking that cats never overlap, never stand anywhere they shouldn't, only make legal jumps, and never throw errors. See [tests/README.md](tests/README.md).

Built with Claude.
