Ermes-x86/MW2-GTA-Beta.readme:
# MW2-GTA (Beta)

> ⚠️ **WARNING: this mod is in beta and still contains bugs.** Expect the
> player to sometimes get stuck on geometry, camera or control glitches, and
> missing or unfinished features. Back up your GTA San Andreas saves before
> playing, and press F6 at any time to return to normal GTA controls.

> **Note:** this README was (mostly) AI generated. If something in the
> installation doesn't work, please let me know by
> [opening an issue](../../issues).

**Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) gameplay inside GTA San Andreas.**

MW2-GTA is a passthrough mod. Press F6 in GTA San Andreas and you play in
first person with MW2's own movement, weapons, animations, HUD and combat
sounds, in GTA's world: GTA's NPCs, police, vehicles, wanted level, health
and explosions all react to you.

It is not a recreation of MW2's controls. The mod runs a modified
[IW4L](https://github.com/vladtrc/iw4L), an open-source MW2 runtime that loads
your own MW2 installation, alongside GTA. A native GTA plugin (`MW2GTA.asi`)
connects the two:

```
GTA SA (x86) + MW2GTA.asi            IW4L runtime (x64)
  world, NPCs, police, health  <-->    MW2 movement, weapons, animations,
  vehicles, damage, effects             camera, HUD, combat audio
```

- MW2 sprint, jump, crouch, prone, ADS, recoil and bob, with collision against
  GTA's world.
- Bullets, melee and explosions hit GTA NPCs and vehicles with native blood,
  damage, impacts and police reactions.
- An F8 weapon menu with MW2's guns, attachments and equipment: claymore, C4,
  throwing knife, flash, concussion and smoke grenades.
- Javelin and Stinger lock onto GTA vehicles; Javelin also locks onto ground.
- MW2-style health regeneration and optional infinite ammo.
- The mod steps aside for cutscenes, menus and vehicles (press F near a car to
  get in) and resumes on foot.

> **Beta.** Expect bugs. Mission scripts are not specifically
> supported yet.

## Requirements

- **GTA San Andreas 1.0 US** (Steam / Rockstar Launcher copies must be
  downgraded to 1.0 US).
- **An ASI loader** in the GTA folder. The easiest way to get one is the MixMods
  [SA Essentials pack](https://www.mixmods.com.br/2019/06/sa-essentials-pack/)
  (Silent's ASI Loader, SilentPatch and more).
- **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009)**, installed, with its multiplayer data
  (`zone\<language>\common_mp.ff`).
- Windows 10/11 64-bit and a DirectX 12 capable GPU.

## Install

1. Download `MW2-GTA-<version>.zip` from [Releases](../../releases) and extract it
   anywhere.
2. Close GTA San Andreas.
3. Run **`Install-MW2GTA.bat`**. It:
   - finds GTA San Andreas (or asks you to pick the folder) and warns if
     `gta_sa.exe` is not 1.0 US;
   - checks for an ASI loader and, if none is found, offers to open the MixMods
     Essentials pack page;
   - finds Modern Warfare 2 in your Steam libraries (or asks you to pick it);
   - detects Grinch's CheatMenu and offers to move its freecam key from F6
     (MW2-GTA's toggle) to F11, keeping a backup of its settings;
   - copies `MW2GTA.asi` into GTA and the MW2 runtime into `<GTA>\MW2GTA`
     (or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MW2GTA` when GTA is under Program Files);
   - optionally creates a desktop shortcut.

The installer **never deletes or changes save games** (GTA's are in
`Documents\GTA San Andreas User Files`; MW2's folder is only read). Files it
replaces are backed up to `<GTA>\MW2GTA-backup\<date>`.

To remove the mod, run **`Uninstall-MW2GTA.bat`**.

## Play

Start GTA San Andreas, load your game, and press **F6**. The first start
prepares MW2 assets and takes about a minute.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| F6 | MW2 mode on/off |
| WASD, Shift, Space | Move, sprint (hold Shift while aiming to steady a scope), jump |
| C / Ctrl | Crouch / prone |
| Left / right mouse | Fire / aim (with akimbo: right gun / left gun) |
| R | Reload |
| 2 | Next weapon |
| V | Melee |
| E | Use (e.g. pick up a thrown knife) |
| G / H | Lethal equipment / tactical equipment |
| F | Get into a nearby vehicle (MW2 mode returns when you get out) |
| F8 | Weapon and equipment menu (arrows to choose, Enter to equip) |
| F9 | Refill ammo |
| F7 | Options: FOV, help text, infinite ammo, health regeneration, MW2 resolution |

**MW2 resolution** (F7): "Match GTA" renders MW2 at GTA's aspect ratio (up to
1280x720); fixed sizes are also available. Changing it restarts the MW2 runtime.

## Known limitations

- GTA missions are not specifically supported: missions that require a
  particular GTA weapon or GTA-only actions (climbing, swimming) may not work in
  MW2 mode. Press F6 to switch back to GTA controls at any time.
- Water, ladders and moving platforms are not adapted to MW2 movement.
- Flashbangs make GTA NPCs freeze in place; GTA has no blinded state.
- Killstreaks, MW2 radar contacts and scoreboard are not integrated with GTA.
- Occasional short MW2 hitches can still happen.

## Troubleshooting

- **The camera jumps to a frozen spot when entering a vehicle (or "player
  teleported" appears).** Grinch's CheatMenu also uses F6, for its freecam,
  and Enter teleports the player while that freecam is on. Let the installer
  move the freecam key, or in CheatMenu open Menu > Hotkeys and rebind
  "Toggle freecam" to another key.
- **Nothing happens on F6.** Check that an ASI loader is installed and that
  `MW2GTA.log` appears in the GTA folder after starting the game.

## Building from source

The repository has two halves:

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `bridge/` | Native GTA SA plugin (`MW2GTA.asi`), C++ against plugin-sdk |
| `iw4l/` | Modified IW4L runtime (Rust) |
| `installer/` | Release installer and uninstaller |

Prerequisites: Visual Studio Build Tools with C++ (x86), a built
[plugin-sdk](https://github.com/DK22Pac/plugin-sdk) for GTA SA, and Rust
(rustup; the toolchain is pinned by `iw4l/rust-toolchain.toml`).

```powershell
$env:PLUGIN_SDK_DIR = 'C:\dev\plugin-sdk'
bridge\Build-ASI.cmd                     # -> bridge\build\MW2GTA.asi
cd iw4l
$env:CARGO_PROFILE_D

# ฟังแป๊บ — เกมทายเพลงไทย (MVP)

เกมแนว Songless สำหรับเพลงไทย ฟังท่อนสั้น 0.5 วินาที ทายผิดหรือกดข้ามจะได้ฟังยาวขึ้น
(0.5 → 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 วินาที) รวม 6 ครั้ง

## เริ่มต้น

ต้องใช้ Node.js 18.18 ขึ้นไป (แนะนำ 20 ตาม `.nvmrc`)

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
```

ต้องต่ออินเทอร์เน็ต เพราะเสียงตัวอย่างโหลดจาก iTunes ตอนเล่น

## คำสั่งที่ใช้บ่อย

| คำสั่ง              | ทำอะไร                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | รันเซิร์ฟเวอร์สำหรับพัฒนา  |
| `npm run build`     | build สำหรับ production    |
| `npm run lint`      | ตรวจโค้ดด้วย ESLint        |
| `npm run typecheck` | ตรวจ type ด้วย TypeScript  |
| `npm test`          | รัน unit test (Vitest)     |
| `npm run format`    | จัดรูปแบบโค้ดด้วย Prettier |

ก่อน push ควรผ่าน `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test`

## โครงสร้างโปรเจกต์

```
src/
├── app/                    # Next.js App Router: layout, หน้าแรก, global CSS
│   ├── layout.tsx
│   ├── page.tsx
│   └── globals.css         # design tokens (สี ฟอนต์ ขอบมน) + ค่าเริ่มต้นของ element
├── components/
│   ├── game/               # ทุกอย่างบนหน้าเกม ไฟล์ละหนึ่ง component + CSS Module ของตัวเอง
│   │   ├── Game.tsx        # ตัวประกอบหน้าจอ: ต่อ state, เสียง และ component ย่อยเข้าด้วยกัน
│   │   ├── GameHeader.tsx  # โลโก้ เลขเกม ปุ่มวิธีเล่น
│   │   ├── CategoryTabs.tsx
│   │   ├── ModeToggle.tsx  # เพลงประจำวัน / สุ่มเล่น
│   │   ├── GuessList.tsx   # 6 แถวคำตอบ พร้อมสีผลทาย
│   │   ├── Player.tsx      # แถบเวลาและปุ่มเล่น
│   │   ├── GuessInput.tsx  # ช่องค้นหาเพลง + ปุ่มข้าม
│   │   ├── ResultCard.tsx  # เฉลย แชร์ผล สถิติ
│   │   └── HelpDialog.tsx
│   ├── monetization/       # ตำแหน่งโฆษณาและการ์ดสมาชิก (ตัวอย่าง ยังไม่ต่อระบบจริง)
│   └── ui/                 # ชิ้นส่วนทั่วไป เช่น footer
├── hooks/                  # React hooks ที่แยก logic ออกจาก UI
│   ├── useGame.ts          # state ของรอบเกม: คำตอบ การทาย การบันทึก สถิติ
│   ├── usePreview.ts       # ดึง URL เสียงจาก iTunes
│   ├── useAudioClip.ts     # เล่นเสียง N วินาทีแรกแล้วหยุดเอง
│   └── useFirstVisit.ts    # เปิดวิธีเล่นครั้งแรกที่เข้าเว็บ
├── lib/                    # TypeScript ล้วน ไม่ผูกกับ React ทดสอบได้ง่าย
│   ├── types.ts            # type หลักของโปรเจกต์
│   ├── constants.ts        # ค่าคงที่ เช่น ความยาวท่อน หมวดเพลง วันเริ่มเกม
│   ├── songs.ts            # โหลดคลังเพลงและชื่อศิลปินภาษาไทย
│   ├── search.ts           # ค้นหาเพลงจากชื่อเพลงหรือศิลปิน
│   ├── daily.ts            # คำนวณเลขวันตามเวลาไทย และเลือกเพลงประจำวัน
│   ├── scoring.ts          # ตรวจคำตอบ ความยาวที่ปลดล็อก ข้อความแชร์
│   ├── itunes.ts           # เรียก iTunes Lookup API
│   ├── storage.ts          # อ่าน/เขียน localStorage แบบไม่ throw
│   ├── format.ts           # จัดรูปแบบเวลาและเปอร์เซ็นต์
│   └── *.test.ts           # unit test อยู่ข้างไฟล์ที่ทดสอบ
└── data/
    ├── songs.json          # คลังเพลง: [iTunes trackId, ชื่อเพลง, ศิลปิน, หมวด, ปี]
    └── artists.json        # ชื่อศิลปินภาษาไทยสำหรับช่องค้นหา
scripts/
└── fetch_itunes.py         # ดึงรายชื่อเพลงของศิลปินจาก iTunes เป็น CSV เพื่อคัดเพิ่ม
```

### หลักการแบ่งไฟล์

- **`lib/`** เป็น logic ล้วน ไม่ import React จึงเขียน unit test ได้ตรงๆ
- **`hooks/`** เป็นตัวเชื่อม logic กับ React state และ side effect (เสียง, network, localStorage)
- **`components/`** แสดงผลอย่างเดียว รับข้อมูลผ่าน props แต่ละไฟล์มี `.module.css` ของตัวเอง
- สี ฟอนต์ และขนาดขอบมนกำหนดเป็น CSS variable ไว้ที่ `globals.css` ที่เดียว

## เพิ่มเพลง

1. รัน `python scripts/fetch_itunes.py "ชื่อศิลปิน"` เพื่อดึงรายการเพลงเป็น CSV
2. คัดเพลงที่คนรู้จัก แล้วเพิ่มลง `src/data/songs.json` ในรูปแบบ `[trackId, "ชื่อเพลง", "ศิลปิน", "หมวด", "ปี"]`
   หมวดใช้ได้: `pop`, `rock`, `luk`, `hiphop`
3. ถ้าเป็นศิลปินใหม่ เพิ่มชื่อภาษาไทยใน `src/data/artists.json`
4. รัน `npm test` เพื่อเช็คว่าไม่มีอะไรพัง

## เรื่องเสียงและลิขสิทธิ์

เว็บเก็บแค่ `trackId` แล้วเรียก `https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=th` ตอนเล่น
เพื่อเอา URL ตัวอย่างเสียง 30 วินาทีของ Apple มาเล่นโดยตรง ไม่ได้ดาวน์โหลดหรือเก็บไฟล์เพลงไว้เอง
และมีลิงก์ "ฟังเต็มเพลงบน Apple Music" ในหน้าเฉลย

เดโมนี้ใช้ทดสอบว่าคนอยากเล่นไหมเท่านั้น ก่อนใส่โฆษณาหรือเก็บค่าสมาชิกจริง ต้องตรวจเงื่อนไขการใช้งานของ Apple
และขอสิทธิ์จากค่ายเพลงหรือหน่วยงานจัดเก็บลิขสิทธิ์ และควรปรึกษาทนายด้านทรัพย์สินทางปัญญา

## Deploy

ต่อ repo นี้กับ Vercel แล้วกด Deploy ได้เลย ไม่ต้องตั้งค่าเพิ่ม (Hobby plan ใช้ได้เฉพาะงานที่ไม่ใช่เชิงพาณิชย์)

## ขั้นต่อไป

1. ย้าย `songs.json` ไปเป็นตาราง `songs` ใน Supabase (Postgres) และทำหน้าแอดมินเพิ่มหรือแก้เพลง
2. ล็อกอินด้วย Supabase Auth และเก็บสถิติบนเซิร์ฟเวอร์แทน localStorage
3. ตรวจคำตอบผ่าน API route ฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์ เพื่อไม่ให้โกงได้ก่อนทำ leaderboard
4. ใส่ Umami หรือ GA4 วัดจำนวนผู้เล่นรายวันและอัตรากลับมาเล่นซ้ำ
5. เมื่อได้สิทธิ์เสียงแล้ว ค่อยเก็บคลิปบน Cloudflare R2 และเลือกจุดเริ่มท่อนเองได้
6. ต่อ AdSense และระบบสมาชิก (Stripe หรือ Opn Payments ที่รองรับ PromptPay)

rachelmedvedev/shuk-game.readme:
# Name Your Price! — a haggling simulator in Machane Yehuda

A browser game set in Jerusalem's Machane Yehuda market. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no server.

**Play:** https://rachelmedvedev.github.io/shuk-game/

It's Friday morning and you have to do the Shabbat shopping before the market closes at 2 PM. Every game is a new market: a random shopping list (must-haves, nice-to-haves, only-if-cheap), a random budget, and random shops. The shops are real Machane Yehuda businesses (Halva Kingdom, Marzipan Bakery, Basher Fromagerie, Levi Brothers Falafel...) plus generic produce, spice and flower stalls. Each shop has its own drawn interior, and its vendor has:

- **one of 12 personalities**, each with hidden stats (pride, patience, flattery, humor, soft heart, greed, chattiness) and a quirk: the gossip's phone keeps ringing, the football fan's radio scores goals, the mystic sees omens, the grandmother slips you gifts, the businessperson only cares about numbers, and so on.
- **a mood of the day**: just became a grandparent, fought with the next stall, overstocked, slow day...
- **a randomized SVG look**, dressed for the job (baker's hat, butcher's apron...), with a face that reacts to their mood.

You haggle with 13 tactics in three groups (talk, haggle, tricks), including a slider for your own offer. Vendors answer from a bank of about 1,000 prewritten lines and, if your browser supports it, read them aloud. At the end, your Shabbat table is rated 1–5 stars, for what you bought plus the money you saved.

Business names are real; the characters, prices and dialogue are fictional and just for fun.

## Files

- `index.html`, `style.css`: screens, scenes, animations
- `js/data.js`: businesses, items, archetype stats, tactics, narration
- `js/archetypes/*.js`: dialogue for each of the 12 personalities
- `js/engine.js`: haggling rules, quirks, market generation and scoring (pure functions, runs in Node too)
- `js/art.js`: SVG vendors, shop interiors per business type, stall facades
- `js/game.js`: UI, sound, voices, game flow

The original Hebrew version is tagged `hebrew-v2`.

## Credits

Market ambience: ["Ballarò market ambience"](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Italia_Palermo_mercato-Ballaro_20161225_122421.ogg) by Marie Flutre, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).

Built with Claude Code for the "Build Something Live in 1 Hour" lab.

# Arena

C++23 ve [raylib](https://www.raylib.com) ile yazılan, Vampire Survivors tarzı bir arena survival oyunu. Asıl amaç oyun değil: aynı oyunu her aşamada farklı bir **programming paradigm** ile yeniden şekillendirip CS321'de işlenen trade-off'ları **ölçerek** öğrenmek.

Her aşamada tek metric değişmez: **frame time (ms)**. Bir değişikliğin iyi olup olmadığına "daha temiz görünüyor" diye değil, aynı koşullarda ölçülmüş before/after ile karar verilir.

## Kurulum

Gerekenler: CMake 3.25+, C++23 destekli bir derleyici (Clang 17+, GCC 13+ veya MSVC 2022), Git. raylib ilk configure sırasında otomatik indirilir; ayrıca kurmana gerek yok.

**Qt Creator:** File → Open File or Project → `CMakeLists.txt` → Configure Project → Run.

**Terminal:**

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
./build/arena
```

Linux'ta raylib şu paketleri ister: `libgl1-mesa-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libxcursor-dev libxinerama-dev libasound2-dev`. macOS ve Windows'ta ek paket gerekmez.

**Kontroller:** WASD veya ok tuşları ile hareket, ESC ile çıkış.

## Yol haritası

Her aşama ayrı bir git tag'i (`stage-0`, `stage-1`...) ile kapanır; böylece aşamalar arasında `git diff` alıp ne değiştiğini görebilirsin.

| Aşama | Paradigm / konu | Oyunda eklenen | Ölçülecek soru |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 ✅ | Procedural | Game loop, oyuncu hareketi, delta time | 60 FPS'te frame time kaç ms? |
| 1 | Procedural | Düşmanlar oyuncuya yürür, çarpışma, can, skor | Kaç düşmanda frame time 16,6 ms'yi aşar? |
| 2 | OOP | `Entity` base class, `virtual update()/draw()`, düşman türleri | Aşama 1'e göre aynı düşman sayısında fark ne? |
| 3 | Generics | `ObjectPool<T>`; silahlar `virtual` yerine `std::variant` + `std::visit` | Runtime vs compile-time dispatch farkı |
| 4 | Functional | Pure `update(state, input) -> state`, `std::ranges`, seed'li deterministic replay | Aynı seed iki kez aynı oyunu üretiyor mu? |
| 5 | Data-oriented / ECS | 5.000+ düşman, AoS → SoA | Aşama 2'deki OOP tasarımına göre kaç kat hızlı? |
| 6 | Agent-driven code | Claude refactor eder; clang-tidy + benchmark gate script'i kabul veya ret verir | Gate hangi değişikliği reddetti, neden? |
| 7 | Optimizasyon | `constexpr` tablolar, `-O2`/`-O3`, LTO | Her bayrak frame time'ı ne kadar değiştirdi? |

Teslim haftalarında (CS321 Phase 1: 23-27 Kasım, Phase 2: 21-25 Aralık) proje dondurulur.

## Aşama 1 görevi

`src/main.cpp` içinde, sınıf kullanmadan (henüz procedural aşamadayız):

1. Düşmanları bir `std::vector<Vector2>` içinde tut; her saniye ekranın kenarından yeni bir düşman doğsun.
2. Her düşman her frame oyuncuya doğru yürüsün (oyuncu hareketindeki normalize mantığını yeniden kullan).
3. Düşman oyuncuya değerse can azalsın; can bitince "Game Over" yazısı çıksın.
4. Ekranın köşesine düşman sayısını yaz.
5. Bonus: doğma hızını artırıp frame time'ın 16,6 ms'yi geçtiği düşman sayısını not et. Bu sayı Aşama 2 ve 5'te karşılaştırma noktamız olacak.

## Ölçüm notları

Ölçümleri buraya ekle: tarih, aşama, düşman sayısı, build tipi (Debug/Release), ortalama frame time.

| Tarih | Aşama | Düşman | Build | Frame time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | |

# Jazda! Polish Streets

A 2.5D pixel-art street-skating racer through Warsaw, Rzeszów, Gdańsk and Wrocław. It is one HTML file: no build step, no server, no paid libraries. All the art and music is generated in code.

## Play it on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new repository (for example `jazda`) and upload `index.html`, `README.md` and `.nojekyll`.
2. Go to **Settings → Pages**. Under **Source**, choose **Deploy from a branch**, then pick **main** and **/(root)**, and click **Save**.
3. After a minute or two the game is live at `https://<your-username>.github.io/jazda/`.

To play it on your own computer, open `index.html` in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Optional asset files only load when the game is served over HTTP (GitHub Pages, or `python3 -m http.server` in this folder).

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard (remappable in Options) | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change lane | ← → or A D | Swipe left or right |
| Jump (ollie) | Space, ↑ or W | Swipe up |
| Manual (on the ground) | ↓ or S, hold | Swipe down and hold |
| Flip trick (in the air) | K; add ← → ↑ ↓ for other flips | Tap |
| Grab trick (in the air) | L, hold, and release before landing | GRAB button |
| Boost | Shift | BOOST button |
| Shoot paint | F | Tap, or the FIRE button |
| Balance on a rail | ← → | Swipe left or right |
| Pause | Esc or P | II button |

## Features

- **Two modes:** Race (you against 3 AI rivals, about 2 minutes) and Score Run (90 seconds).
- **Four cities**, each with its own landmarks, colours, music and a day/night cycle. Weather can be clear, rain or snow.
- **Three difficulties** (Easy, Hard, Expert). They change top speed, obstacle density, rival skill and aggression, the rail catch window, balance drift and the score multiplier.
- **Moves:** grinds with a balance meter, flip and grab tricks, manuals, combos, a boost meter, kicker ramps and boost pads.
- **Paint shot:** unlock it in the skill tree or pick up paint crates. Rivals on Hard and Expert shoot back, but always flash a red "!" first.
- **Progression:** XP levels, stars, skill points, a 5 × 3 skill tree, 5 boards, outfits, decals, trails and victory poses.
- **Collectibles:** 20 hidden items, 5 per city (mermaid badges, golden pączki, seagulls and gnomes).
- **Saving:** auto-saves to `localStorage` with a versioned format, plus JSON export and import.
- **Accessibility:** colourblind mode (shapes and outlines, not only colour), three text sizes, reduced motion, subtitles for every voice line, remappable keys and full keyboard menus.
- **Performance:** Auto quality drops to Medium or Low when the frame rate falls, then steps back up.

## Optional assets

Every asset is optional. To replace generated art or music, add an `assets` folder and an `assets/manifest.json`, for example:

```json
{
  "chars": { "stary": { "back": "chars/stary_back.png", "front": "chars/stary_front.png" } },
  "music": { "warsaw": ["music/warsaw.ogg", "music/warsaw.mp3"] },
  "vo": { "stary": { "go": "vo/stary_go.ogg" } },
  "bg": { "gdansk": { "far": "bg/gdansk_far.png" } }
}
```

- **Back-view sheets** (`<id>_back.png`): 384 × 512 px, frames of 48 × 64, 8 columns × 8 rows. The rows are ride, push, crouch, air, flip, grab, grind and bail.
- **Front sheets** (`<id>_front.png`): 576 × 256 px, frames of 96 × 128. The rows are idle and victory.
- **Music:** a seamless loop of 60–180 s, in OGG plus MP3.
- **Voice lines:** short mono clips named `go`, `trick`, `crash`, `hit`, `win` and `lose`.
- **Backgrounds** (`<city>_sky.png`, `_far.png`, `_near.png`): 800 × 225 px.

Character ids are `stary`, `stara`, `kuba` and `ola`. City ids are `warsaw`, `rzeszow`, `gdansk` and `wroclaw`. The full asset list, with naming rules, is in the design pack.

## Code layout (inside `index.html`)

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| CORE | Constants, maths, seeded RNG, game data (difficulties, cities, characters, boards, cosmetics, skills, tricks) |
| SAVE / INPUT | Versioned save with migration, export and import; remappable keyboard, touch swipes and buttons |
| ART | Pixel font, palettes, characters (back and front views), props, buildings, skylines |
| TRACK | Seeded road layout, city zones, scenery, obstacle patterns with a guaranteed free path, rails, pickups |
| SKATER | Shared physics for the player and the AI: lanes, jumps, flips, grabs, manuals, grinds, boost, crashes |
| GAME | Race flow, rival AI, collisions, pickups, paint pellets, positions, rewards |
| RENDER | Pseudo-3D road, parallax, sprites with hill clipping, lights, particles, weather, motion blur, colour split, vignette |
| AUDIO | Web Audio music sequencer per city, synthesized sound effects, rolling and grind loops, voice lines |
| UI / MAIN | Menus, HUD, pause and results screens; game loop and adaptive quality |

## Roadmap

- **Next:** Kraków and Poznań, a daily seeded challenge, a ghost of your best run.
- **Then:** online leaderboards, ghost races with friends, track share codes, live races for 2 to 4 players (these need a small backend).
- **Later:** seasonal events (Christmas markets, Juwenalia, a Baltic summer), a track editor.

## Credits

Game design and direction by Dasz. Code, pixel art and music were generated by Claude. Fonts: Pixelify Sans and Barlow Semi Condensed (SIL Open Font License). Every shop and brand in the game is invented.

crafter-games/shizuku-web.readme:
# shizuku-web

A browser reimplementation of Leaf's MAX engine that plays the PC-98 visual
novel **Shizuku** (雫, Leaf, 1996) in Spanish, from the player's own disks.

No game data is in this repository, and none is ever hosted. Players load
their own five floppy images; they stay in the browser. A pre-commit hook and
CI reject disk images and anything decoded from them.

```sh
pnpm install
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
pnpm decode      # decode the disks in ../pc98/fixtures/private/shizuku into out/
pnpm test
```

See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design and the file formats.

## Deployment

shizuku.crafter.games is built by the Dockerfile in the private
`crafter-games/shizuku-es` repo (Dokploy, from its `main`): it clones this
repo, adds the translation and serves `packages/web/dist` with
`deploy/nginx.conf`. Pushing here does not redeploy by itself; redeploy the
Dokploy app (or push to shizuku-es).

## Credits

- File formats and scenario bytecode: XLVNS by Go Watanabe (BSD), ported to TypeScript.
- PC-98 specifics cross-checked against Her-Saki's English patch tools (used as documentation).
- FM music: the PMD driver and YM2608 emulator of 98fmplayer by Takamichi Horikawa (BSD-2-Clause), built to WebAssembly in `packages/pmd` (see its LICENSE).

venson01/mama-put-rush.readme:
# Mama Put Rush

A lunch-rush time-management game set in a Lagos buka. Customers sit on the bench with an order chit; dish their plate from the pots and serve them before their patience runs out. Built for [start.ng](https://start.ng).

![Mama Put Rush](public/cover.png)

## How to play

1. Read the order chit above each customer.
2. Tap the pots to dish it: one item from the pot, one meat or fish, and a side if they asked for one.
3. Tap the customer to serve. Fast service earns bigger tips, and correct plates in a row build a streak bonus.

Pots run out: tap an empty pot to cook more. From Day 4 you can hire an assistant, Tobi, for ₦8,000 a day: Tobi dishes whole orders and serves them for you. Five walkouts and the shop closes for the day. Meet the day's sales target to open the next day, with new food on the menu and hungrier customers.

Keyboard: `1`–`4` serve a seat, `Backspace` throws the plate, `P` pauses.

## start.ng

- The game has no player character, so it shows a start.ng **profile card** (face, character name, `@account`) above the signboard. Guests see start.ng's guest look and a **Sign in** button.
- A **leaderboard** ranks runs by days cleared, then naira earned (`public/startng.json`). Signed-in players save their run at the end of every day; the board shows on the start and day-end cards.
- All start.ng calls go through the hidden connect page and only run on `*.start.ng`. Played anywhere else, the game works without a player.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run test     # engine unit tests (Vitest)
npm run build    # typecheck, then build to dist/
npm run cover    # re-render public/cover.png with headless Edge/Chrome
```

`dist/` is committed on purpose: start.ng serves the built game and never runs a build. The source `index.html` lives in `src/` so the repo root has no unbuilt page. Rebuild and commit `dist/` with every change.

- `src/game/`: pure game logic (menu, balance, customers, engine), no DOM or audio. Randomness is injected so tests are deterministic.
- `src/components/`: React UI, with food and customer art as inline SVG.
- `src/startng/`: the start.ng connect-page client.
- `reference/mama-put-rush.html`: the original single-file prototype, the source of truth for rules, balance, art and copy.

# Nông dân lúa nước – prototype

Prototype web cho game mô phỏng nông dân thuê 5 công ruộng lúa nước, xoay xở tiền bạc qua các vụ và tránh vòng xoáy nợ. Thiết kế và luật chơi: xem `CLAUDE.md` và `docs/`.

## Chạy khi phát triển

```
npm install
npm run dev            # mở http://localhost:5173
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run validate-data
npm run sim -- --bot all --runs 1000
```

Trong game, phím `` ` `` mở bảng debug (state ẩn, nhảy ngày, xuất/nhập file lưu).
Trang dev: `?preview` (các mẩu giấy), `?preview=scene&day=40` (cảnh trên một lượt chơi thật của bot).

## Build để đăng itch.io

```
npm run build
```

Kết quả nằm trong `dist/` (`index.html` + `assets/`). Mọi đường dẫn là tương đối (`base: "./"` trong `vite.config.ts`), nên chạy được khi đặt trong thư mục con bất kỳ.

1. Nén **nội dung** của `dist/` thành một file zip (`index.html` phải nằm ở gốc file zip, không nằm trong thư mục `dist/`).
2. Trên itch.io: tạo project, *Kind of project* = **HTML**, tải file zip lên, đánh dấu **This file will be played in the browser**.
3. Kích thước khung gợi ý: 1200 × 720, bật **Mobile friendly** và **Fullscreen button**.

Thử trên máy trước khi tải lên:

```
npm run preview        # phục vụ dist/ tại http://localhost:4173
```

Ghi chú:
- Font (Be Vietnam Pro, Patrick Hand) tải từ Google Fonts; không có mạng thì dùng font dự phòng của máy.
- Game tự lưu cuối mỗi ngày vào `localStorage` của trình duyệt. Chỉ giữ ván đang chơi: bắt đầu ván mới là ghi đè ván cũ. Xóa dữ liệu trang web là mất bản lưu.
- File lưu có thêm dữ liệu playtest (số lần tua, bậc nợ cao nhất, thời điểm dừng chơi…). Người chơi thử có thể xuất file lưu từ bảng debug để gửi lại.

# Door Duty Contractors

A crowd-science tycoon/puzzle game. You run a small firm fitting entrances on the High Street: revolving doors, swing and sliding doors, and later the ticket gates at the station. Every client is a puzzle. Design the frontage, test it in a 40-second rush hour full of simulated people, and sign it off if the client is happy. Fitted clients pay maintenance every month; spend it on research, staff and bigger premises, and the town opens up around you.

**Play:** the GitHub Pages build of this repo (one self-contained page, works offline once loaded).

## Develop

No dependencies to install. You need Node 20+ (and Python 3 with Playwright for the browser bot).

```
npm run dev     # then open http://localhost:8080/src/shell.html
npm test
npm run build   # dist/index.html
```

See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for the architecture, house rules and how to add a building, and [docs/game-loop.html](docs/game-loop.html) for the design.

utkarsh3mehta/cabo.readme:
# Cabo Online

A browser-based, real-time multiplayer version of the **Cabo** memory card
game. Play remotely with friends in private rooms (code or invitation link),
or solo against easy bots. No accounts, no installation.

> Unofficial fan implementation. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the
> publisher. All artwork and text are original.

## Features

- Private rooms for 2–5 participants (bots count toward the limit), joined by
  a 6-character code or an invitation link.
- Solo games against 1–4 easy bots.
- Full game (to 100 points, the default) and quick game (best of three rounds).
- The current publisher's standard rules: choice cards (Peek, Spy, Swap),
  2–4-card matching with the failed-match procedure, Cabo calls with final
  turns, +5 failed-call penalty, tie rules, Shooting the Moon, one-time
  100 → 50 reset, draw-pile reshuffling. See
  [docs/RULES_SPECIFICATION.md](docs/RULES_SPECIFICATION.md).
- A server-authoritative engine. Every client and bot only ever receives a
  per-player projection of the state, so hidden cards never reach a browser
  that is not entitled to them.
- Reconnection after refreshes and network drops. Host transfer. The host can
  hand a disconnected player's seat to a bot.
- A responsive, keyboard-accessible UI for phones and desktops, with no
  animations or sounds.
- Docker and Caddy deployment with automatic HTTPS.

## Repository layout

```
apps/server            Node.js server: Fastify HTTP API, Socket.IO, rooms, sessions, bots runner
apps/web               React + Vite client
packages/shared        Card inventory, schemas, protocol and view types (Zod-free entry: /client)
packages/game-engine   Pure rules engine (no I/O): transitions, scoring, player views, invariants
packages/bots          Easy bot strategy; depends only on @cabo/shared, never on engine internals
e2e                    Playwright browser tests
deploy/Caddyfile       Reverse proxy and TLS
docs/                  Rules specification, architecture, implementation plan, deployment guide
```

## Local development

Requirements: Node.js 22.12+ (24 recommended) and pnpm through Corepack.

```sh
corepack enable          # provides the pinned pnpm version
pnpm install
pnpm dev                 # server on :3000 (tsx watch) + Vite on :5173
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. To try multiplayer on one machine, use a second
browser profile or a private window for each extra player, because sessions
are stored per browser.

In development `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` is not required, and WebSocket origin checks
are disabled (the server logs a warning).

## Tests

```sh
pnpm typecheck           # strict TypeScript in every package
pnpm test                # unit + integration tests (Vitest)
pnpm exec playwright install chromium   # once, for browser tests
pnpm test:e2e            # builds, starts the production server, runs Playwright (desktop + mobile)
pnpm test:all            # all of the above
```

What they cover:

- **Engine** (`packages/game-engine/test`): deck integrity, deal, inspection,
  every action, abilities, matching, Cabo and final turns, reshuffle, scoring
  fixtures and boundaries, quick and full endings, illegal transitions, and
  property-based random playouts checking card accounting and that no view
  leaks hidden cards.
- **Bots** (`packages/bots/test`): complete bot-only games with legal moves
  only, memory accuracy, and a structural check that bot code cannot import
  the engine.
- **Server** (`apps/server/test`): real Socket.IO clients against a running
  server. Covers rooms, auth, host rules, sanitised snapshots, private
  delivery of peeks, spies and draws, wrong-player and malformed commands,
  duplicates, concurrency, stale versions, complete human and bot games
  verified against the pure scorer, reconnects, host transfer, bot takeover,
  TTL cleanup, rate limits and static serving.
- **Browser** (`e2e/`): create, join by code, join by link, start, inspect,
  synchronised move, tampered-client rejection, solo quick and full games with
  score checks, refresh recovery, bot takeover, and a 360 px mobile layout.

To run the browser tests against an already running deployment, set
`E2E_BASE_URL=https://your-host`. Note that the production rate limits will
throttle the full suite.

## Production build without Docker

```sh
pnpm build
NODE_ENV=production PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://cabo.example.com PORT=3000 pnpm start
```

The server serves the built client from `apps/web/dist`. Put it behind an
HTTPS reverse proxy that supports WebSockets.

## Docker / VPS deployment (summary)

```sh
cp .env.example .env     # set DOMAIN, PUBLIC_ORIGIN, ACME_EMAIL
docker compose up -d --build
```

This starts the app container (not exposed) behind Caddy on ports 80/443.
Caddy obtains a Let's Encrypt certificate automatically and proxies
WebSockets. The full guide, covering DNS, firewall, TLS, updates, logs,
configuration and troubleshooting, is in
[docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).

**Restart behaviour:** game state is in memory only, so restarting or
updating the server ends every active game.

## Known limitations

- **Deck inventory verification.** The per-value counts (two 0s, four each of
  1–12, two 13s) and the 7–8 Peek / 9–10 Spy / 11–12 Swap mapping are
  corroborated by several independent sources, but the current publisher does
  not print them in published text. They should be checked against a physical
  2025 deck ([RULES_SPECIFICATION §13](docs/RULES_SPECIFICATION.md)). A
  correction is a one-file change in `packages/shared/src/cards.ts`.
- **Interpreted rules.** Quick-game scoring ("best of 3 rounds"), tie-breaks
  in final standings (shared win), the next starter when a round has several
  winners, and where the drawn card goes after a successful match are
  documented interpretations, not publisher text.
- **Single process, in memory.** No persistence, no horizontal scaling, and
  games end on restart. Abuse protection is limited to rate limits,
  connection caps, vali

starMinK/deephold.readme:
# 딥홀드

던전을 파밍하고, 내 던전을 짓고, 친구가 도전하는 2.5D 도트 액션 (TypeScript + Phaser 3).
규칙·수치의 기준은 「딥홀드 기획서」.

## 실행

Node.js 가 있으면 바로 실행된다 (미리 빌드된 `dist/` 포함).

```
node tools/serve.mjs dist
```

브라우저에서 http://localhost:8080 을 연다. 끄려면 터미널에서 Ctrl+C.

## 조작 (M2)

| 키 | 동작 |
| --- | --- |
| WASD / 방향키 | 이동 |
| J | 공격 (누르고 있으면 계속 벤다). 베면서 걸을 수 있다(70% 속도) |
| K | 구르기 (약 52px, 앞 0.3초 무적). 공격과 동시에는 못 한다 |
| L | 누르고 있는 동안 바라보는 방향 고정 |
| E | 계단·포탈 이용, 상자 열기, 촛대 불 붙이기, 기름 샘 퍼 올리기 (계단·포탈은 층 목표를 끝내야 열린다) |
| J (레버 앞) | 레버는 검으로 베어서 당긴다 |
| Q | 회복약 |
| Tab | 누르고 있는 동안 지도 표시 (게임은 멈추지 않음) |
| Enter | 사망 후 새 원정 |
| F2 | 새 시드로 다시 시작 (개발용) |
| F3 | 충돌 원·시드·틱 표시 (개발용) |

주소 뒤에 `?seed=7` 을 붙이면 같은 던전이 나온다. (예: http://localhost:8080/?seed=7)
`&depth=5` 를 더 붙이면 그 층부터 시작한다. (예: http://localhost:8080/?seed=7&depth=5)

데스크톱 앱(Mac·Windows)으로 실행·설치 파일 만들기는 `docs/설치_방법.md`, 친구 서버 연결은 `docs/서버_연결.md` 를 본다.

코드를 고쳐서 다시 빌드하려면 먼저 한 번 `npm install` 이 필요하다.

| 명령 | 하는 일 |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | `dist/` 에 게임을 새로 만든다 |
| `npm start` | `dist/` 를 8080 포트로 띄운다 |
| `npm run dev` | 코드를 고치면 자동으로 다시 빌드 (브라우저 새로고침하면 반영) |
| `npm run typecheck` | 타입 검사 |
| `npm test` | 테스트 실행 |

## 폴더

| 폴더 | 내용 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/` | **게임 규칙** (이동·충돌·전투·몬스터·던전 생성). 화면 코드를 쓰지 않는 순수 TypeScript. 나중에 서버가 같은 코드로 리플레이를 검증한다 |
| `src/core/config/balance.ts` | 확률·시간·비용 같은 **밸런스 수치를 모아 둔 곳** |
| `src/game/` | Phaser 화면 코드 (장면, 에셋 불러오기) |
| `assets/` | 아트 대화방이 준 에셋. `manifest.json` 의 이름·크기·기준점만 믿고 불러온다. 이 폴더는 통째로 교체해도 된다 |
| `vendor/phaser.min.js` | Phaser 3 (npm 대신 파일로 넣어 둠) |
| `tests/` | 테스트 (같은 시드 = 같은 결과, core 가 화면 코드를 안 쓰는지, 에셋이 manifest 와 맞는지) |
| `tools/` | 빌드·서버 스크립트 |

## 지키는 약속

- 규칙은 60Hz 고정 틱으로만 진행한다. 난수는 시드 기반 `Rng` 만 쓴다 (`Math.random`·현재 시각 금지 — 테스트가 검사).
- 에셋 파일 이름은 바꾸지 않는다. 아직 없는 에셋은 같은 크기의 단색 임시 도형으로 대신한다.

nomeata/hydro.readme:
# Hydro

A slow, cozy water-management sandbox in the browser.

Rain falls, rivers wander, groundwater rises and sinks. You shape the land
with trenches, dikes, reservoirs and (eventually) pumps and turbines, but you
only ever *plan*. Little people walk over and build it, and then decide for
themselves where to farm, fish, graze and settle.

**Play:** https://hydro.nomeata.de/ (desktop and phone)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Overview](https://hydro.nomeata.de/screenshots/overview.png) | ![Close-up](https://hydro.nomeata.de/screenshots/closeup.png) |

<sub>Screenshots are rendered by CI from the deployed build.</sub>

## Status

Early development. See [the roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md).

## Controls

| | Mouse | Touch |
|---|---|---|
| Pan | drag | one finger (Look tool) / two fingers |
| Zoom | wheel | pinch |
| Rotate | right-drag | two-finger twist |
| Draw plan | left-drag with a tool | one finger with a tool |

URL options: `?seed=123` picks a world, `?size=512` a bigger map,
`?stats=1` shows performance numbers.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run check      # typecheck + unit tests
npm run e2e        # Playwright browser tests
npm run bench      # simulation kernel benchmark
npm run preview-world -- 1 2 3   # worldgen preview PNGs in out/preview
```

Design and architecture: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md),
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md).

## Credits & license

Code: Apache-2.0. 3D models: [Kenney](https://kenney.nl) (CC0), see
[CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

# English Quest

**[🇬🇧 English](#english) · [🇷🇺 Русский](#русский)**

▶️ **Play: https://rasulovnazim-design.github.io/English-Quest/**

---

## English

English Quest is a free web game for learning English. It is for native Russian speakers. It starts from zero (A0) and goes up to everyday conversation (A2). All menus, instructions and explanations are in Russian. Everything you learn is in English, with Russian translations, and uses British spelling and a British voice by default. You can switch to American in Settings.

- **Map in four stages**: First Words → Me and My World → Everyday Life → Out and About, plus a final conversation at the end. Each stage unlocks once the previous one is complete. Within a stage, you can do the categories in any order.
- **Short lessons** of about 5 minutes. They go from recognising words to producing them yourself:
  - matching words to pictures or Russian
  - listening and choosing
  - flashcards in both directions
  - filling gaps
  - building sentences from word tiles
  - dictation
  - speaking (checked by the browser's speech recognition)
  - translating from Russian
- **Conversation boss** at the end of every category: a role play with a character, in three rounds — choose the reply, build it from tiles, then type or say it freely. Answers about yourself (name, age, country, city, job) are accepted in any correct form, so *I'm 34*, *I am 34 years old* and *34* all count.
- **XP, levels, daily goal and streak.** Ranks go from Beginner (Новичок) to Explorer (Исследователь), Traveller (Путешественник), Speaker (Собеседник) and Conversationalist (Мастер общения).
- **Review (Повторение)** with spaced repetition: words come back after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 60 days. Words you get wrong come back sooner.
- **Phrasebook** for every category, plus a searchable master phrasebook. Each entry has the Russian translation, IPA and audio. Every phrasebook page can be printed or saved as a PDF.
- **Typical Mistakes** cards in Russian for each category: articles, the *th* sound, *w* vs *v*, *ship* vs *sheep*, false friends and more.
- Works **offline**, installs to the home screen, has light and dark themes, and has no account or server. Progress is saved in your browser, and you can export or import it as a file.

### Install it on your phone

- **iPhone (Safari):** open the link → tap **Share** (the square with an arrow) → **Add to Home Screen**.
- **Android (Chrome):** open the link → menu **⋮** → **Install app** (or **Add to Home screen**).
- **Laptop (Chrome / Edge):** click the install icon in the address bar.

After the first visit, the game works without an internet connection. Speech recognition needs a connection in Chrome, and Firefox doesn't support it. When it isn't available, the speaking exercises turn into typing exercises.

### Run it locally

You need Node.js 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # development server: http://localhost:5173/English-Quest/
npm test             # unit tests (answer checker, personal answers, review scheduling, content files)
npm run build        # production build in dist/
npm run e2e          # Playwright tests on iPhone, Android and laptop screen sizes (local build)
BASE_URL=https://rasulovnazim-design.github.io/English-Quest/ npm run e2e   # the same tests against the live site
```

Every push to `main` runs the unit tests, deploys to GitHub Pages and then runs the Playwright tests against the live site (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`).

### Add or correct content

All learning content is kept apart from the code:

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Words, phrases, translations, IPA, lessons, grammar, typical mistakes, boss dialogue | `src/data/categories/<id>.json` |
| Stages and the order of tiles on the map | `src/data/stages.json` |
| Countries, nationalities and languages accepted in answers | `src/data/countries.json` |
| Final conversation | `src/data/final-boss.json` |
| All Russian interface text | `src/locale/ru.json` |

**To add a category:**

1. Copy `src/data/categories/greetings.json` to a new file, such as `food.json`, and change the `id` to `"food"`.
2. Make sure the id is listed in `src/data/stages.json`. Until a data file exists, the tile shows as "Скоро" (coming soon).
3. Fill in the file:
   - `words` (15–25) and `phrases` (8–12): `en`, `ru`, `ipa`. Optional fields:
     - `emoji`
     - `us`: the American variant
     - `alt`: other accepted answers
     - `note`: a short note in Russian
   - `grammar`: a short explanation in Russian, an optional table and examples.
   - `mistakes`: the Typical Mistakes card.
   - `lessons` (3–5): each lesson lists the `items` it introduces and its `steps`.
     - Automatic steps: `"intro"`, `"match"`, `"listen"`, `"meaning"`, `"flash-en"`, `"flash-ru"`, `"dictation"`, `"speak"`, `"grammar"`.
     - Hand-written steps: `{"type": "gap"}`, `{"type": "tiles"}`, `{"type": "translate"}`, `{"type": "choose"}`, `{"type": "dictation"}`.
   - `boss`: a conversation graph of `nodes`. Each node has the character's line (`npc`, `ru`) and an optional `reply`:
     - `answers` are the correct replies. Each has a `say` text and optional `accept` variants, `patterns` for personal answers and `next` for branching.
     - `wrong` are the wrong options shown in round 1.
     - `hint` and `why` are explanations in Russian.
4. Run `npm test`. The content tests check the counts, the ids, the lesson items and the boss graph. They also check that every correct boss reply is accepted and every wrong option is rejected.

**Personal-answer patterns** (in `patterns`): `[a|b]` means one of the alternatives, a `?` after a group makes it optional, and `{slot}` captures the learner's own detail. The slots are `name`, `age`, `country`, `city`, `job`, `nationality`, `language`, `number`, `letters` and `any`. For example, `"[i am]? {age} [years old]?"` accepts *I'm 34*, *I am 34 years old* and *34*. Contractions, capital letters and punctuation are ignored automatically.

---

MihailKKostov/NintendoFamGameExchange.readme:
# 🎮 Family Game Exchange

A website for sharing Nintendo games between family and friends. It runs on GitHub Pages with a Firebase backend. Anyone can sign in, **create a family** and **invite people by email**. Each family has its own private library of everyone's games, and tracks who lent what to whom.

- **Families**
  - Sign in with Google or an emailed sign-in link.
  - Create a family with a name, icon and colour, or join one you were invited to. You can belong to several families and switch between them in the top bar.
  - **Roles:** owner, admins and members. Admins invite people by email (or share an invite link), promote or demote members, and remove people. Owners can delete the family.
- **Profiles:** account name, nickname, a photo or an icon on a colour, status message, Switch friend code and email preferences.
- **Add games three ways:**
  - **eShop search** with autocomplete over the real Nintendo eShop catalog. The official eShop icon and details are filled in automatically: publisher, developer, release date, genres, player count, local/online/co-op multiplayer, play modes and rating.
  - **Scan a screenshot or photo** (console home screen, game list, shelf of cases) with the OpenAI API. This is optional, and **each person uses their own API key, stored only in their own browser** (details below).
  - **Manual entry** for anything that isn't in the eShop.
- **Browse and filter** the family library. Filters cover name, genre, platform, publisher, developer, release year, player count, multiplayer, local, online, co-op, owner, availability and format.
- **Borrowing:**
  - **Request to borrow** marks the game *pending* and notifies the owner in the app and by email. The email has **Accept / Decline / Reply** buttons that open the request.
  - **Owner actions:** the owner can accept with an optional due date, decline, or lend a game directly without a request.
  - **Loans page:** tabs for incoming and outgoing requests, games you've **lent out**, games you've **borrowed**, and history.
  - **Per-loan activity:** each loan has a timeline with comments, due-date changes and "mark as returned".
- **Everything updates live** in every open browser.
- **Nintendo-inspired UI:**
  - Joy-Con colours, a dock of round buttons, the pulsing cyan selection frame, and a tile row with the title floating above the selected game.
  - Console-style dialogs and Basic White / Basic Black themes.
  - Small synthesized menu sounds you can turn off.
  - Fully responsive.

> Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with Nintendo. Game names, icons and details come from Nintendo's public eShop catalog.

---

## Try it locally (demo mode)

On your own computer, without a Firebase config, `npm run dev` runs the app in **demo mode**: sample families stored only in your browser, sign in as a sample person (or any email) and switch people from the banner to test lending.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

The published site never shows demo data: without a usable Firebase config the GitHub workflow stops with an error, and a build made without one shows a "setup needed" page. (To deliberately publish the demo, set a repository variable `DEMO` = `true`.)

---

## How it works

```
GitHub Pages (static React app)
   ├── Nintendo eShop catalog (public search index) ── autocomplete, icons, game details
   ├── OpenAI API (optional, called straight from the browser with YOUR key) ── screenshot scanning
   └── Firebase (your project, Blaze plan)
         ├── Authentication ... Google + passwordless email links
         ├── Firestore ......... families, members, games, libraries, loans, comments, notifications
         ├── Storage ........... profile pictures
         └── Cloud Functions ... every rule-bound action (create family, invite, join, request,
                                 accept, lend, return, comment…) + notification/invite emails
```

**Privacy and security**

- **Families are isolated.** Firestore security rules only let you read a family you are a member of. Everything that changes state goes through Cloud Functions, which check who is allowed to do what: only the owner of a game can accept a request, only admins can invite, and so on. Browsers can only edit their own game copy's notes, format and lendable flag, and mark their own notifications as read.
- **Invites are tied to an email address.** An invite can only be read or accepted by someone signed in with that exact, verified email address, or seen by the family's admins.
- **Removing someone cuts their access immediately.** Their games leave the library and their open requests are cancelled. Loan history is kept.
- **OpenAI keys never leave the person's device.** Each person pastes their own key in *Settings → Screenshot scanning*. It is saved only in that browser's local storage and sent only to `api.openai.com` when that person scans. It is never sent to Firebase, the Cloud Functions or other family members. OpenAI bills that person's own account; a scan typically costs a fraction of a cent. Removing the key (or clearing site data) deletes it.
- **Fast reopening keeps a copy on the device.** So the app opens instantly, each browser keeps the app's files (a service worker) and a copy of what you last saw in your current family: profile, families, games, copies and loans. Firebase's own offline cache already stores the same data there. The copy is replaced by live data as soon as your sign-in is confirmed, and deleted when you sign out or your sign-in is no longer valid. A new release is picked up in the background and used the next time the app opens.

---

## Go live: setup guide

You'll need a Firebase project on the **Blaze** (pay-as-you-go) plan. Cloud Functions and Storage require it. Family-sized usage stays within the free quotas.

### 1. Firebase project

1. In the [Firebase console](https://console.firebase.google.com), open your project or create one, and make sure it is on **Blaze**.

laboratorio-cmd/tronwell-game-zone.desc: TRONWELL KIDS GAME ZONE: retro space arcade for English practice (ages 10-16)
laboratorio-cmd/tronwell-game-zone.readme:
# TRONWELL KIDS GAME ZONE

A retro space arcade for English practice (students aged 10–16). Four short games (1–3 minutes each) share one content model, one scoring system and one progress profile:

| Game | Genre | Practises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Grammar Blaster** | Space shooter | Verb forms, auxiliaries, negatives, questions, tense choice |
| **Word Jumper** | Side-scrolling platformer | Vocabulary, word groups, spelling, picture words |
| **Tense Racer** | Lane racer with pit stops | Tense choice from context, word order |
| **English Detective** | Point-and-click mystery | Reading for detail, inference, dialogue |

It is a companion to the **Tronwell Kids Practice Zone** (`../tronwell_kids/index.html`, published at `laboratorio-cmd.github.io/tronwell-kids/`). That portal is a single static HTML file with no accounts or server, so the Game Zone is a separate static app meant to be published on the same GitHub Pages domain (`laboratorio-cmd.github.io/tronwell-game-zone/`). Both apps then share the browser storage of that domain.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm test             # unit + content tests (Vitest)
npm run typecheck    # TypeScript strict mode
npm run validate:content
npm run build        # production build in dist/
npm run preview      # serve dist/ locally
```

Node 20+ is required (developed with Node 24).

## Student level

The games never invent a level and never treat arcade scores as a CEFR assessment. The level is resolved in this order (`src/services/level.ts`):

1. **Teacher link:** `?level=rocket` (any Practice Zone level id: `tiny`, `moon`, `rocket`, `planet`, `comet`, `galaxy`) or `?level=A2` (a CEFR code). It is remembered on the device.
2. **Practice Zone placement test:** the portal saves the result in `localStorage` key `twk2_level`. Because both sites live on `laboratorio-cmd.github.io`, the Game Zone reads it directly.
3. **Level chosen in Game Zone settings.** A newer placement test in the portal takes over again.
4. If nothing is known, the student is asked which Tronwell Kids level they are in.

Portal level → content band: Tiny Stars A0 · Moon Walkers A1 · Rocket Riders A1 · Planet Explorers A2 · Comet Chasers B1 · Galaxy Masters B2.

## Architecture

```
src/
  app/                 App shell, hash router (works as static files), AppContext (services)
  components/          PixelSprite, Modal
  features/
    lobby/             Arcade lobby with four cabinets + pilot card
    play/              PlayScreen (lifecycle), HUD, start/pause/results/error overlays, touch controls
    progress/          Student progress page
    settings/          Sound, music, motion, level
    level/             First-run level question (only when no level is known)
  games/
    registry.ts        The four GameDefinitions
    shared/            BaseScene, createGame, audio (Web Audio synth), input, store/channel, types
      pixel/           assets.ts (asset table, no Phaser), manifest.ts (loading), art.ts (original pixel art)
    grammar-blaster/   definition.ts + BlasterScene.ts
    word-jumper/       definition.ts + JumperScene.ts + levelGen.ts + spelling.ts
    tense-racer/       definition.ts + RacerScene.ts + PitStopPanel.tsx
    english-detective/ definition.ts + DetectiveScene.ts + DetectivePanel.tsx + caseMachine.ts
  education/
    types.ts           Content schema (CEFR levels, skill categories, item kinds, detective cases)
    content/           Content banks: one file per game and level
    questionEngine.ts  Selection, shuffling, answer checking, recent-content rotation
    validation/        Validator + tests over the whole bank
  services/
    progress/          ScoreKeeper, rewards (XP/coins/ranks), achievements, ProgressService, repository, stats
    level.ts, settings.ts, storage.ts
```

**React** renders menus, HUD, prompts, feedback, results and the two game panels (pit stop, case notebook). **Phaser 3** renders gameplay. They talk through a `GameBridge` (`src/games/shared/types.ts`): the scene writes HUD state into small external stores (no React re-render per frame), records answers through the shared `ScoreKeeper`, and calls `bridge.finish()` once. `PlayScreen` turns that into a `GameResult`, validates it and saves it with `ProgressService`.

Every game implements the same `GameDefinition` contract: metadata, `buildSession(level)` (content selection), `loadScene()` (lazy, so Phaser only downloads when a game starts) and an optional React panel.

Lifecycle: `intro → loading → playing ⇄ paused → results` (or `error`). Esc/P pauses, leaving the tab pauses, restart and quit destroy the Phaser instance, so a game never runs twice.

## Content

`src/education/content/<game>/<level>.ts`, all marked `status: 'draft'` (sample content written for the MVP, **not yet reviewed by a Tronwell teacher**; set `status: 'reviewed'` after review).

| Bank | A0 | A1 | A2 | B1 | B2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grammar Blaster (gap-fill) | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Word Jumper (15 word groups + 15 spellings) | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Tense Racer (18 gates + 12 word-order) | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| English Detective (cases) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |

450 challenge items + 10 complete cases (each with 4–5 questions, an accusation and a proof question). British spelling, Tronwell crew characters, no textbook names.

To add content, copy an item in the right file and run `npm run validate:content`. The validator rejects: missing fields, ids that don't match the file's game/level, invalid answer indexes, duplicate ids or questions, ambiguous option lists, feedback that only repeats the answer, word-order alternatives that aren't permutations, spelling clues that contain the word, and detective cases that cannot be completed (a question requiring hidden evidence before it is revealed, evidence that is never revealed…). At runtime invalid items are skipped, never served.

deathangel4290/Loony.readme:
# Loony Wheels

A 2D physics hill-driving game for iOS. Drive as far as you can across six worlds (including a low-gravity moon), flip for coins, manage fuel, upgrade seven very different vehicles and chase your best distance.

Everything is original: the vehicles, terrain, sprites, music and sound are all generated in code, so there are no third-party art or audio assets.

## Highlights

- **Real 2D rigid-body physics** (planck.js / Box2D): wheel-joint suspension with progressive bump stops, motor and brake torque, traction, weight transfer, and arcade air control.
- **Forgiving by design.** A pedal held from the ground through a jump levels the car for landing; a fresh press in the air spins it (gas = forward, brake = backward). There's also anti-flip assist on big wheelies, and props can never trap the car.
- **Seeded procedural terrain** built from hand-designed pieces (hills, kickers, gaps, bridges, lava pits, rooftops, ice). Every non-ramp segment is slope-checked, so there's always a way forward. Difficulty ramps with distance.
- **Tricks and combos**: flips (double, triple…), big air, long jumps, perfect landings, close calls and wheelies, with a combo multiplier. A perfect landing also fires a short speed boost in your equipped boost effect.
- **Daily Challenge**: one seeded course per day, the same for every attempt. It has a rotating world, a loaner car, a distance goal and a once-a-day reward, and you race a ghost replay of your best attempt.
- **Progression**: coins, gems, upgrade tokens, XP and levels, 6 upgrade stats × 10 levels per vehicle, 41 cosmetics, rotating missions, 24 trophies and a 7-day daily reward.
- **Game feel**: interpolated 120 Hz physics, look-ahead camera that frames your landing, trauma-based shake, slow-motion crashes, particles, floating trick text, coins that fly to the HUD, a driver whose head bobs with the car, and haptics.
- **Audio** made entirely with WebAudio: a layered engine whose pitch follows RPM, tire, skid and wind layers, about 25 synthesized sound effects, and a generative soundtrack per world.
- **Offline-first**, with a checksummed save and a backup slot. Corrupted fields are repaired one at a time instead of wiping the save.

## Tech

| | |
|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript (strict) |
| Rendering | Canvas 2D (procedural art baked into sprites; cached `Path2D` terrain) |
| Physics | [planck.js](https://github.com/piqnt/planck.js) |
| UI | DOM overlay (safe-area aware, landscape) |
| Build | Vite |
| Native shell | Capacitor 8 (iOS project in `ios/`, Swift Package Manager, no CocoaPods) |
| Tests | Vitest (unit + headless physics), Playwright (smoke and visual) |

Why this stack: it works on iOS through Capacitor and on the web unchanged. Android is one command away (`npx cap add android`). The game logic also runs headlessly, so physics and balance are tested by simulation.

## Play in the browser (GitHub Pages)

Every push to the default branch runs `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, which typechecks, runs the tests, builds the release game and publishes it to **https://deathangel4290.github.io/Loony/**.

- In **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**, set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**. Until then, GitHub also publishes the raw source on every push. The workflow waits for that build and deploys afterwards, so the game still wins.
- On iPhone, open the page in Safari and choose **Share → Add to Home Screen** to play full-screen. A service worker caches the game, so it also works offline after the first load.

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173 (debug tools enabled)
npm test             # unit + physics regression tests
npm run build        # release build -> dist/
```

### iOS

Requires macOS with Xcode 15+.

```bash
npm run ios:sync     # build the web app and copy it into the iOS project
npm run ios:open     # open in Xcode, choose a team, run on a device
```

The iOS app is landscape-only and full-screen with the status bar hidden. It uses the Taptic Engine through `@capacitor/haptics` and native key-value storage through `@capacitor/preferences`. The deployment target is iOS 15; a `roundRect` polyfill covers older WebKit.

### Android (optional)

```bash
npm i -D @capacitor/android && npx cap add android && npx cap sync android
```

## Project structure

```
src/
  App.ts                 app root: main loop, scene switching, pause, lifecycle
  core/                  math, seeded RNG, event bus, pools, polyfills
  data/                  all content and tuning (data-driven)
    vehicles.ts            7 vehicles: physics, trait, engine sound
    upgrades.ts            upgrade stats, costs, effect curves
    worlds.ts              5 worlds: palette, terrain mix, decor, music
    missions.ts achievements.ts cosmetics.ts rewards.ts config.ts
  game/                  gameplay (no DOM; runs headless)
    GameSession.ts         one run: physics world, scoring, collectibles ("LevelManager")
    VehiclePhysics.ts      wheel joints, motors, bump stops, air control, traits
    PlayerController.ts    fuel, damage, crash/end rules
    TerrainGenerator.ts    seeded piece-based terrain + coins/fuel/props/decor
    TerrainManager.ts      streams collision chunks and props around the camera
    TrickSystem.ts         flips, air, wheelies, landings, combos
    CameraController.ts    follow / look-ahead / zoom / shake
    Tutorial.ts            first-run teaching state machine
    Autopilot.ts           bot driver (menu attract mode, balance tests)
    GameView.ts            binds a session to rendering, FX, audio, haptics, HUD state
  render/                Canvas renderers: background, terrain, vehicle art, sprites, particles
  systems/               save, settings, currency, progression, upgrades, garage,
                         worlds, missions, achievements, daily rewards, audio, music,
                         haptics, input, services container
  ui/                    UIManager, screens (menu,

sgilson7/pots.desc: Protection of the Spheres: a browser game that plays like DotA Allstars, with heroes of its own. Arcade missions against computer players and 5v5 online with rollback netcode.
sgilson7/pots.readme:
# Protection of the Spheres

A browser game that plays like the Warcraft III map Defense of the Ancients (DotA Allstars, version 6.72/6.73), with heroes, items and art of its own. Two sides of five heroes push three lanes of creeps toward the other side's Sphere; the side whose Sphere breaks loses.

Play it at <https://sgilson7.github.io/pots/>.

- **Arcade:** ten missions that teach the game, from last-hitting alone in one lane to a full five against five, and a custom match where the size of each side and the skill of each side's computer players are set apart.
- **Online:** up to ten players by room code, with rollback netcode and rejoining a match after a dropped connection. Empty seats are played by the computer.

Ten heroes, each carrying the abilities and numbers of a DotA hero under an original name and look: Ironvow (after Sven), Rime (Crystal Maiden), Cinder (Lina), Thistle (Drow Ranger), Gristle (Pudge), Tectus (Earthshaker), Kestrel (Juggernaut), Hexwright (Lion), Longwick (Sniper) and Tempest (Zeus).

## How to play

Right-click the ground to walk, and an enemy to attack it. Q, W, E and R use abilities; a targeted ability waits for a click. Press O, then an ability key, to learn it. B opens the shop, Tab the score, Space centres the camera on your hero, A then a click attack-moves. Gold comes only from the killing blow, so land the last hit on enemy creeps, and deny your own below half health.

## What the game copies from DotA

Every number the game copies has a source in `notes/LITERATURE.md`: archived pages of playdota.com (IceFrog's site, captured at 6.72/6.73), IceFrog's changelogs from 6.48 to 6.79c, and player threads. The rules include DotA's attack-type and armor-type table, the armor formula, dice-rolled damage, pseudo-random bashes and crits, attack points and backswing, last hits and denies, the gold and experience formulas, creep waves and upgrades, mega creeps, neutral camps that refill on the minute, runes, the boss and its shield, the tower invulnerability chain, backdoor protection and the glyph, day and night, trees that block sight and paths, and high ground. Where the game simplifies, `SECOND-ORDER.md` says so, row by row.

## How it is built

A [Builder](https://github.com/sgilson7/builder-setting) project. A Rust core holds every rule and performs no input or output; a WebAssembly shim moves values and decides nothing; the page draws what the core returns.

| Path | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/core` | the match (`world.rs`, `combat.rs`, `orders.rs`, `lanes.rs`, `ability.rs`, `item.rs`, `ai.rs`), the screens and HUD (`game.rs`, `ui.rs`), the 3D scene (`scene.rs`, `models.rs`), online play (`online.rs`) |
| `crates/shim` | the `wasm-bindgen` functions the page calls |
| `web/` | the page: WebGL renderer, the view model's DOM, input, the online transport in `web/net/` |
| `data/` | every number and word: units, abilities, items, map, behavior trees, models, strings |
| `tools/` | generators for the data (`unitgen.py`, `abilitygen.py`, `itemgen.py`, `mapgen.py`, `modelgen.py`), the TikZ icon pipeline, screenshots |
| `tests/browser/` | the browser check; `tests/online/` the online smoke test and the five-runner test |

```bash
./scripts/setup.sh              # once: Python venv with Playwright and three browsers
cargo test --workspace          # every rule, in seconds
./scripts/build.sh              # release WebAssembly build into dist/
python3 scripts/serve.py        # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
./scripts/check.sh              # everything, before publishing
.venv/bin/python tests/online/runners.py runs/out 10   # five browsers play ten minutes online
```

Online play introduces browsers through public Nostr relays this project does not run, then connects them directly. Nothing loads from another site until a player hosts or joins.

Miiiiiiiid/blacksmith.readme:
# Blacksmith Prototype

대장장이 성장 시뮬레이션 RPG의 프로토타입이에요. 목표는 "무기를 만들어 팔고, 능력이 자라고, 마왕군을 버티거나 진다"를 30일 동안 해보고 재밌는지 확인하는 거예요.

## 구조

| 폴더 | 내용 |
| --- | --- |
| `Core/` | 게임 규칙 전부. 엔진과 무관한 순수 C#이라 Unity로 옮겨도 그대로 쓴다. |
| `Core.Tests/` | Core 테스트 (xUnit) |
| `godot/` | Godot 4 프로젝트. 화면과 입력만 맡는다. |
| `godot/data/` | 재료와 품목 정의 (JSON). 코드 수정 없이 품목을 늘릴 수 있다. |

밸런스 숫자(하루 행동 수, 퇴보 비율, 침공 주기 등)는 `Core/GameRules.cs` 한 곳에 모여 있어요.

## 실행

1. [Godot 4.7 .NET 버전](https://godotengine.org/download)과 .NET 8 SDK를 설치해요.
2. Godot에서 `godot/project.godot`을 열고 실행(F5)해요.

테스트: 저장소 루트에서 `dotnet test`

## 지금 되는 것

- 하루 4행동 턴제, 하루 마치기
- 채집(무학 성장), 구매(화술 성장, 화술이 높으면 할인), 제작(품목별 능력치 성장), 판매(화술 성장), 왕국군 납품(명성 +)
- 능력치 3쌍: 한쪽 +1이면 반대쪽 -0.6
- 7일마다 마왕군 침공. 납품한 방어력 / (방어력 + 위협) 확률로 방어. 결과는 시드로 고정돼서 세이브-로드로 바꿀 수 없음
- 무기 제작 미니게임: 가열 → 망치질 5번 → 담금질. 움직이는 표시를 초록 구간에서 멈추면 되고, 힘이 높을수록 구간이 넓어짐. 스페이스나 버튼으로 조작
- 같은 품목을 3번 직접 만들면 자동 제작 가능 (최고 품질의 80%)
- 30일 버티면 승리, 침공을 못 막으면 게임오버
- 행동할 때마다 자동 저장 (`user://save.json`)

## 아직 임시인 것

- 도구와 장신구도 아직 무기와 같은 미니게임을 씀
- 화면은 버튼만 있는 임시 UI

## 안드로이드로 내보낼 때

내보내기 설정의 "리소스 외 파일 필터"에 `*.json`을 넣어야 `data/` 파일이 포함돼요.

# OpenAPI_SE_Lab

Software Engineering lab work for **Problem Statement #41: OpenAPI Mock Server Generator**.

**Author:** Akshansh Agrawal  
**SRN:** PES2UG24CS045

## Problem Statement

An OpenAPI Mock Server Generator reads an existing OpenAPI 3.0 spec and turns it into a working fake API, so developers and testers don't have to wait for a real backend before they start working.

The system:

- Parses and validates an uploaded OpenAPI 3.0 spec (YAML or JSON) and rejects broken files with a line-numbered error.
- Generates mock HTTP endpoints for every path in the spec.
- Returns randomized responses that still match the schema's types and required fields.
- Lets the developer set a minimum and maximum response delay per endpoint to simulate real network conditions.
- Runs inside a CI/CD pipeline, giving test suites a stable target when the real backend is incomplete or down.

Its main users are API Developers and QA Engineers. A CI/CD Pipeline, a System Administrator and a DevOps Engineer are supporting actors.

## Labs

| Lab | Topic | Summary | Deliverables |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Lab 1](Lab1/) | Requirements Engineering & UML Use Case Modelling | Identifies the five actors, lists the functional and non-functional requirements (FR-001 to FR-005, NFR-001 and NFR-002), describes six use cases in detail, and draws the UML use case diagram. | [Requirements & Use Case report](Lab1/Requirements_and_UseCase/) |
| [Lab 2](Lab2/) | Agile Backlog Creation & Sprint Simulation | Builds a prioritized, story-pointed product backlog, runs it across two simulated sprints with boards and a burndown chart, and reflects on how accurate the estimates were and how much the team could deliver. | [Backlog, sprints & reflection report](Lab2/Agile_Backlog_and_Sprint/) |
| [Lab 3](Lab3/) | Component Modelling & Architectural Pattern Selection | Models the system as a three-layer architecture (Presentation, Business, Data) in a UML component diagram, and explains why a layered pattern was chosen, including its security and performance benefits. | [Component diagram](Lab3/Component_Diagram/), [Written justification](Lab3/Written_Justification/) |
| [Lab 4](Lab4/) | VibeCoding | Uses an AI coding assistant to fix and extend a Pygame Fruit Ninja game: reliable fast-swipe slicing, a Game Over screen, replay at Easy/Medium/Hard, and sound effects. | [Videos](Lab4/Videos/), [Code](Lab4/Code/) |

## Repository Structure

```
OpenAPI_SE_Lab/
├── Lab1/
│   └── Requirements_and_UseCase/
│       └── PES2UG24CS045_Lab1_SE.pdf
├── Lab2/
│   └── Agile_Backlog_and_Sprint/
│       └── PES2UG24CS045_Lab2_SE.pdf
├── Lab3/
│   ├── Component_Diagram/
│   │   └── PES2UG24CS045_SE_Lab3_Diagram.pdf
│   └── Written_Justification/
│       └── PES2UG24CS045_SE_Lab3_Justification.pdf
├── Lab4/
│   ├── Videos/
│   │   ├── Before_fix_Fruit_Ninja.mp4
│   │   └── After_fix_Fruit_Ninja.mp4
│   └── Code/
│       ├── main.py
│       ├── requirements.txt
│       └── game/
│           ├── fruit.py
│           ├── game_engine.py
│           └── sounds.py

└── README.md
```

Each lab folder has its own README with more detail.

# Roadster Pursuit

A *Split/Second: Velocity*-style escape game in the browser. You drive the 2nd-generation Tesla Roadster
and use its **suction fans** and **cold-gas thrusters** to survive scripted disasters and police roadblocks.

Live at **https://game.konstantinrichter.de**

## Run locally

```sh
python3 server/leaderboard.py --port 8000 --static . --db leaderboard.sqlite
# open http://localhost:8000  (game + leaderboard API)
```

Three.js (r160) loads from jsDelivr. There is no build step, and the server uses only the Python standard library.

## Controls

- **A / D or ← →**: steer. Speed is automatic and rises over time.
- **Space**: thrust jump. Hold it to fly while pressure lasts.
- **Shift**: suction (grip, ride tunnel walls, survive blasts).
- P pauses, M mutes. Touch buttons appear on phones.

## Events

Police pursuits, a falling radio tower, roadblocks, tanker blasts, missing bridge sections, tunnel cave-ins, overpass collapses,
a **head-over loop** (the highway does a full barrel roll; hold suction or fall off),
and a police chopper that drops mines. When the chopper swoops low, thrust-fly into it to bring it down.
Over distance, the standard speed rises (about 134 mph up to about 220 mph), events come closer together,
and more cops and traffic appear. The rear thrusters fire once, for the 0–60-in-0.81 s launch.
The pressure and suction tanks are small, so use them wisely. You have 3 lives (hearts).

## Leaderboard & deployment

- `server/leaderboard.py`: `GET /api/leaderboard`, `POST /api/scores`, SQLite table `scores`,
  best run per nickname, an 8 s cooldown per IP, and basic plausibility checks.
- On the VPS: nginx serves `/var/www/roadster-pursuit` and proxies `/api/` to the systemd unit
  `roadster-leaderboard` (127.0.0.1:3010). The database is `~/roadster-data/leaderboard.sqlite`.
- Deploy with `./deploy/deploy.sh` (rsync + systemd + nginx; TLS via certbot).

## Based on the Oct 15, 2026 reveal

- Fan-based suction of up to 2 G. The reveal showed the car driving up an inverted ramp and holding itself upside down.
- SpaceX-developed cold-gas thrusters fed by ultra-high-pressure air tanks. They did kickflips, flipped over other cars and landed.
- Trims: Performance (<1.6 s 0–60), Thrust (rear thrusters, <0.9 s), Rocket (perimeter thrusters, <0.59 s, 230+ mph).
- 0–60 in 0.81 s shown on the reveal stream.
- "Ano White" paint, a visor-style tinted canopy, a full-width light bar, and active wings in Track Mode.

This is a fan-made game, not affiliated with Tesla or SpaceX.

## Code map

- `src/track.js`: streamed road and tunnel geometry, plus the `(s, u, h)` to world transform.
- `src/car.js`: Roadster physics (thrust, hover, suction wall-ride).
- `src/events.js`: event director and obstacles.
- `src/police.js`, `src/traffic.js`: AI.
- `src/models.js`, `src/city.js`, `src/fx.js`: visuals. The Roadster body and canopy are lofted from keyframed cross-sections.
- `src/audio.js`: WebAudio synth sounds.
- `src/hud.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/leaderboard.js`: UI and leaderboard client.
- `src/main.js`: game loop.

IntelligentRebel/constellations.readme:
# Constellations *English · [Français](README.fr.md)* A turn-based 4X space strategy game, **freely inspired by Stars!** (Jeff Johnson & Jeff McBride, 1995). It runs entirely in the browser, offline, with nothing to install. **[▶ Play it in your browser](https://intelligentrebel.github.io/constellations/)**, or download it to play offline (see [Play](#play)). **Version 0.3.9.13** (early version: the numbering restarts at 0.x until the game is considered complete). ![The galaxy map in the middle of a game: a spiral arm crossed by dark clouds, the borders of rival empires, fleets on their way, and on the right the panel of the capital, with its sector governor and its culture.](docs/screenshots/en/map.png) ## Why this game Constellations started as a personal project: to live again a 1990s game I loved, Stars!, without what has aged badly. Stars! had remarkable depth (race design, ship design, a real economy, fuel, minefields, battle plans) behind a Windows 3.1 interface: dozens of small windows, orders given one dialog at a time, numbers you had to work out by hand, and limits that only came from the computers of the time. So Constellations keeps the rules of Stars! as its foundation, gives them a modern interface with a great deal of quality of life, and adds many new mechanics inspired by Stellaris and other 4X games, along with plain common sense. All the names are its own (hulls, components, races, technologies): it is a tribute, not a copy. It was created with the help of **Claude Opus 5.5** (Anthropic). ## Screenshots

A fleet sent across the empire: speed, duration and fuel of each leg, refuelling at friendly shipyards on the way.
Ship design: the hull's slots, the characteristics, the combat role, a combat simulator and a comparison with an enemy design.

Research: progress in each field, the budget, and the exclusive doctrines (the other path closes for good).
Diplomacy with the computers: war and peace, agreements, what each empire thinks of you, the latest news.

The Empire page: discoveries and relics, the cost of distance to the capital, sector governors.
The colony planner: every analysed world ranked by habitability, with its minerals and a button to send an ark.

A battle replayed phase by phase, with the losses of each side.
A story in three acts, each of which changes the rules of the game.
## Play - **Online**: [intelligentrebel.github.io/constellations](https://intelligentrebel.github.io/constellations/), nothing to install. - **Offline**: download the repository (green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**), unzip it and open `index.html` in a web browser. No server, no installation, no internet connection needed. - The online and offline copies keep their saves apart (each in its own browser storage): to move a game from one to the other, "Export" it, then "Import" it. - The game picks the language of your browser; if that language is not supported, it starts in English. You can change it on the welcome screen or in the "⋯" menu. Languages: English, 简体中文, Deutsch, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Français, 日本語, 한국어, Polski, Italiano. - New to the game? **✦ Tutorial**, on the welcome screen, teaches it step by step in a real game: the essentials first (about twenty minutes), then optional chapters on everything else. - Games are saved automatically in the browser (up to eight). "Export" writes a file you can import again; Chrome and Edge can also keep backup files of the last turns in a folder you choose. ## For purists: close to the original **New game, Game tab: "Experience close to Stars!"** switches every Constellations rule off at once: square galaxy, no new mechanics, fleets identified as soon as they are seen, wormholes crossable from the start, production templates that do not chain, victory no earlier than after 50 years. The formulas are those of Stars! (from its decompiled help and the open-source craig-stars project, checked against the original game under Windows 3.11). The interface improvements stay: you play the Stars! rules with the comfort of a modern game. Each new rule can also be switched on or off one by one.

## What differs from Stars! ### Interface and quality of life - A single modern screen: map, tabs (colonies, colony and mining planners, fleets, empire, design, research, diplomacy, reports, guide), a side panel for the selection, and keyboard shortcuts for everything. - Every report is clickable: the name of a planet, a fleet or a battle opens it. Reports are sorted by importance and routine builds are summed up in one line a year. - Tooltips explain every technology, component and figure; every table can be sorted; undo (Ctrl+Z) for orders. - One-click missions: send a scout, an ark or a miner, or build one that leaves by itself once ready. - Routes: fuel gauge with the forecast, speed and duration of each leg, legs crossed without stopping, warnings when fuel runs short, at overwarp or through a known minefield (slowing down only inside the field), engine graphs. - Interception in one click with a standing pursuit, refue
