ztorage/slop-commander.readme:
# Slop Commander (Godot 4, macOS)

A from-scratch, affectionately named remake of Origin Systems' *Strike Commander* (1993) in Godot 4, with
upscaled textures and modern rendering.

**This repository contains no original game code or assets.** To play you need your own copy of the
Strike Commander CD. The included tools read your disc and convert its data locally; the
converted files are gitignored and are never part of an exported build.

## Attribution

This work has been made possible, in large part, thanks to [Remi Leonard](https://remileonard.github.io/), and [Fabien Sanglard](https://fabiensanglard.net/), specifically their work on [libRealSpace](https://github.com/remileonard/libRealSpace), which was used as reference for Claude when deciphering some of the file formats and data structures.

## Setup

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python tools/extract.py /path/to/StrikeCommander.cue   # .cue, .img/.bin, .iso or a mounted CD folder
godot --path godot
```

Music is rendered from the original General MIDI scores with [FluidSynth](https://www.fluidsynth.org)
(`brew install fluid-synth`) and a General MIDI SoundFont: put one at `soundfonts/default.sf2` (for
example [GeneralUser GS](https://www.schristiancollins.com/generaluser)) or set `SC_SOUNDFONT`. Without
it the game runs without music. Engine sound is muffled to 50% by default (`ENGINE_LEVEL` in
`godot/scripts/audio.gd`).

### Graphics: original sprites or upscaled

The extractor always keeps the original art exactly as it is on the disc (320x200, 256 colours)
and, by default, also writes a 4x upscaled copy of every sprite, screen and texture to
`gamedata/hd/`. In the game, **F11** on the menus (or the switch in the developer menu, F12)
chooses between them; the choice is saved. The original sprites are drawn with hard pixel edges;
anything that has no upscaled copy falls back to its original. `SC_GRAPHICS=original` or
`=upscaled` overrides the setting for one run.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/extract.py --skip-disc --no-upscale    # originals only (smaller, quicker)
```

#### Optional: AI upscaling

The art is dithered 256-colour pixel art. With `--ai` the upscaled copy is made by local AI
models (de-dithering, then 4x) instead of the default pixel-art scaler:

```sh
.venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements-ai.txt
.venv/bin/python tools/extract.py --skip-disc --ai
```

It runs on your machine (Apple Silicon GPU, CUDA, or slowly on the CPU); nothing is uploaded. On
an M1 Pro the first run takes about an hour, and results are cached so later runs are quick.
The two models are downloaded on first use from their authors' release pages into
`~/Library/Caches/sc-remake` (`$SC_CACHE` to change) and checked by SHA-256:
[1x-DitherDeleterV3-Smooth](https://openmodeldb.info/models/1x-DitherDeleterV3-Smooth) (WTFPL) and
[4x-UltraSharpV2](https://openmodeldb.info/models/4x-UltraSharpV2) by Kim2091 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0,
for non-commercial use). Overlay frames (mouths, blinks, heads, animated sprites) are upscaled
over the picture beneath them, so they line up when the game draws them. 3D model and terrain
textures always use the pixel-art scaler.

`extract.py` writes:

| Folder        | Contents                                         | In git? |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `extracted/`  | raw files copied/unpacked from your disc         | no      |
| `gamedata/`   | converted assets the game loads at runtime       | no      |
| `gamedata/hd/`| upscaled copies of the art (unless `--no-upscale`)| no      |

The game looks for `gamedata/` in `$SC_GAMEDATA`, then the app's user-data folder
(`~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/Slop Commander/gamedata`), then next to
the `godot/` project. Without it, the game shows instructions and does not start.

## Controls (follows the original reference card)

| Key | Action | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arrows | stick (pitch/roll) | `,` `.` | rudder |
| `1`–`5` | military power 20–100% | `6`–`0` | afterburner 20–100% |
| `+` `-` | throttle up/down (into afterburner) | L | landing gear |
| B | wheel brakes / air brake | Ctrl+E | eject |
| Space | fire selected weapon | W | next weapon |
| G | guns (dogfight) mode | T / Shift+T / Ctrl+T | target farther / closer / none |
| `;` | chaff | `'` | flare |
| F1 | cockpit | F2 | chase camera |
| F3 / F4 / F5 | look left / right / back | F6 | external (orbit, mouse-drag) |
| Z (or F1 again) | cockpit zoomed onto the HUD | Y | padlock: track the target |
| Right-drag | free look in the cockpit | F9 | automatic victim camera on/off |
| F10 | weapon camera (again: back) | A | autopilot: take-off / jump to nav point / landing |
| `[` `]` | cycle views | D | right MFD: weapons / damage |
| Ctrl+I | cockpit art on/off | Ctrl+R / Shift+R | restart / restart airborne |
| N | navigation map | Shift+Tab / Tab (hold) | time compression 1×/2×/4× / 6× |
| Esc | menu | | |

The victim camera cuts to the target as your missile or bomb arrives and cuts back a few
seconds later; a crippled aircraft is followed down until it hits the ground. In the air, the
autopilot shows one fly-by and the jet emerges at the next nav point (or short of it when
enemies are in the way); the music only changes for enemies and the mission's end.

Gamepads: left stick flies, triggers are throttle, A fires, X next weapon, Y target, B decoys.

## Layout

- `tools/` — disc reader, archive/format decoders, asset converters (Python)
- `docs/FORMATS.md` — reverse-engineered file format notes
- `godot/` — the game project

## Known Issues

1. The game engine is janky:
    - Weapons are implemented poorly
    - Controls are all over the place
    - Camera angles are a lot to be desired
    - Objectives aren't programmed well in many missions
    - Autopilot half-functional (e.g., auto-landing misses the runway, but somehow survives)
    - AA vulcan is not implemented (target trailing

mikmcelroy1/takeanumberdotgov.readme:
# Please Take a Number

A timed game of deliberately bad government web pages. Plain HTML and JavaScript, no build step.

Live at https://takeanumberdotgov.com (once deployed). Hosted as a Cloudflare Worker; the scoreboard is a Cloudflare D1 database. Every push to `main` on GitHub rebuilds and updates the live site.

## Folders

- `public/` is the website itself: everything in it is published.
- `src/index.js` is the Worker: it sends `/api/scores` to the scoreboard (`src/scores.js`) and serves everything else from `public/`.
- `schema.sql` creates the scoreboard table. `wrangler.toml` holds the Cloudflare settings.

## Run it locally

With the scoreboard (needs Node; run `npm install` once, then `npm run db:local` once to create the local table):

```bash
npm run dev
```

Then open http://localhost:8788. Scores go into a local copy of the database in `.wrangler/`, not the real one.

Without the scoreboard (just Python):

```bash
python3 serve.py 8731
```

Then open http://localhost:8731. The leaderboard falls back to a list kept in your browser. `serve.py` also tells the browser not to keep old copies of files, so edits show up on a normal reload.

## Scoreboard rules

`src/scores.js` only saves a score if the initials are 3 capital letters, the time is between 20 seconds and 2 hours, and the level list is a real run (4 different levels, Before You Begin first). Each visitor can post 5 scores a minute. IP addresses are only stored in scrambled form, for that limit. Times are measured in the player's browser, so these checks stop junk, not a determined cheater. If you change `RANDOM_LEVELS`, change `PAGES_PER_RUN` in the scoreboard script to match.

## How a run works

Every run plays **Before You Begin** first, then 3 levels picked at random from all the others, in random order (4 pages in total). The number of random levels is `RANDOM_LEVELS` in `public/js/game.js`.

## Levels

Each level has a permanent short name. The number is its place in the load order in `public/index.html`.

| # | Name | Title | File |
|---|------|-------|------|
| 1 | `intro` | Before You Begin (always first) | `public/js/levels/intro.js` |
| 2 | `pin` | Property Lookup | `public/js/levels/pin.js` |
| 3 | `human` | Are You Human? | `public/js/levels/captcha.js` |
| 4 | `address` | Mailing Address | `public/js/levels/address.js` |
| 5 | `sticker` | City Vehicle Sticker | `public/js/levels/sticker.js` |

## Leaderboard link

The footer's **Fastest Times** link opens the top 10 in a pop-up box over the current page. During a run the clock keeps going while it is open. https://takeanumberdotgov.com/#fastest-times opens the box directly, for sharing.

## Testing one level

Add `?level=` to the address to play only the levels you name, in that order. These runs are marked "practice" and their times are not saved to the leaderboard.

- http://localhost:8731/?level=address plays only the Mailing Address level.
- http://localhost:8731/?level=4 does the same, by number.
- http://localhost:8731/?level=pin,sticker plays Property Lookup, then City Vehicle Sticker.

## Adding a level

1. Create `public/js/levels/<name>.js` with `Game.register({ id: '<name>', title, crumbs, render(page, done) { ... } })`. Call `done()` when the player finishes the level.
2. Add a `<script>` line for it in `public/index.html`, after the other levels, so the existing numbers do not change.
3. Add a row to the table above.

The new level is then in the random pool automatically.

## Analytics

Events go to the Mixpanel project **take-a-number** (id 4074309). The browser loads Mixpanel's library from `public/js/vendor/` and sends events to `/mp/...` on this site, which `src/index.js` forwards to Mixpanel, so ad blockers don't drop them. Events are only sent from takeanumberdotgov.com (`LIVE_HOST` in `public/js/analytics.js`), so a copy of this code running anywhere else sends nothing. To test on localhost, add `?track=1` to the address; those events are tagged `env = local`, live ones `env = live`. Nothing the player types is ever sent.

Every event carries Mixpanel's automatic details (browser, device, city and country, the page address, and any `utm_` tags such as `utm_medium=share`), plus `traffic_source` (Shared score link, Social, Search, Other campaign, Direct or Other website) and `referring_site`, worked out once per page load by `trafficSource()` in `public/js/analytics.js`. Many social apps hide the referring site, so when posting the game on social media, use a link like `https://takeanumberdotgov.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social`. Events during a run also carry `level`, `page_number`, `practice` and `seconds_on_page`.

| Event | Sent when | Extra details |
|---|---|---|
| Page Viewed | Any page appears: the start screen, each level, the finish screen | `page` (`start`, a level name, or `finish`), `page_title`; on level pages also `level`, `page_number` |
| Run Started | "Take a Number" is pressed, or a `?level=` test link opens | `levels` (in order), `practice` |
| Page Completed | A page is accepted | where the player is (see above) |
| Mistake Made | The player gets something wrong (table below) | `code`, `reason`, plus details per level |
| Run Finished | The last page is accepted | `total_seconds`, `levels`, `seconds_<level>` for each level |
| Run Abandoned | Restart is pressed during a run | where the player was |
| Standards PDF Closed | The address level's PDF is closed | `furthest_page`, `reached_suffix_table` |
| Initials Submitted | The Board of Ethics review ends | `approved`, `reason` if denied |
| Share Clicked | Share Score is pressed | `method` (`copy` or `share menu`), `completed` |
| Leaderboard Viewed | The footer's Fastest Times link is pressed, or someone opens takeanumberdotgov.com/#fastest-times | `from` (`footer` or `link`), `in_run`, and where the player was if in a run |

### Mistakes

`code` is what the page shows the player (some levels show none). `reason` is a plain description the player never se

leesyashin/Acai.readme:
# Açaí Fever

Ein Zeitmanagement-Spiel im Stil von *Cooking Fever* für den Browser: Du arbeitest in einem modernen
Açaí-Café. Deine Gäste bestellen Bowls – serviert in durchsichtigen Plastikbechern, in denen man die
Schichten sieht – und später Smoothies; du stellst sie per **Drag & Drop** unter Zeitdruck zusammen. Gebaut für **Tablets im Querformat**, spielbar auch mit
Maus am PC und (verkleinert) auf dem Handy. Deutsch und Englisch, Soundeffekte und Musik
werden synthetisch erzeugt – es gibt keine Bild- oder Audiodateien.

Reines HTML/CSS/JavaScript (ES-Module), kein Framework, keine Laufzeit-Abhängigkeiten.
Die verbindliche Spezifikation steht in [`docs/DESIGN.md`](docs/DESIGN.md).

## So wird gespielt

**Steuerung:** Alles läuft über Ziehen und Loslassen – mit dem Finger oder der Maus. Gültige Ziele
leuchten auf, während du etwas ziehst. Lässt du an einer falschen Stelle los, fliegt das Teil zurück
und ein kurzer Hinweis erklärt, warum.

1. **Basis mixen:** Zieh eine gefrorene Packung (Açaí, später Pitaya oder Blaue Spirulina) aus der
   Gefriertruhe in einen leeren Mixer. Nach ein paar Sekunden ist die Basis fertig.
2. **Bowl hinstellen:** Zieh eine leere Bowl (einen durchsichtigen Becher) vom Stapel auf einen freien
   Platz. Ohne Becher geht nichts hinein – am besten stellst du ihn hin, während der Mixer noch läuft.
3. **Bowl füllen:** Zieh den fertigen Mixer auf die leere Bowl. Eine Mischung reicht für zwei Bowls
   (mit dem großen Mixkrug für drei).
4. **Belegen:** Zieh Früchte & Crunch und danach Toppings & Soßen aus der Kühlschiene auf die Bowl.
5. **Servieren:** Zieh die fertige Bowl auf den Gast. Stimmt sie genau mit der Bestellung überein,
   wird bezahlt – plus Trinkgeld, je geduldiger der Gast noch war. Der Platz ist danach frei für den
   nächsten Becher.

**Die Schichten-Regel:** Eine Bowl wird immer in derselben Reihenfolge gebaut:
**Basis → Früchte & Crunch → Toppings & Soßen**. Innerhalb einer Schicht ist die Reihenfolge egal.
Eine Frucht auf einem Topping, ein Topping vor der ersten Frucht, eine Zutat ohne Basis, doppelte Zutaten oder mehr als sechs Zutaten
werden abgelehnt.

**Mixer läuft über:** Ab Level 3 wartet ein fertiger Mixer nicht ewig. Lässt du ihn zu lange stehen,
fängt er an überzulaufen (rot, wackelt) – dann schnell ausgießen! Danach ist die Basis verdorben und
der Mixer muss in den **Mülleimer** gezogen werden. Falsche Bowls (samt Becher) und Smoothies kommen ebenfalls in den Müll.

**Smoothies:** Ab Level 7 bestellen manche Gäste zusätzlich einen Smoothie. Zieh eine passende Frucht
(Banane, Erdbeere, Blaubeere, Mango, Kiwi) in die Smoothie-Maschine, warte kurz und zieh den fertigen
Becher auf den Gast.

**Herzen:** Jeder Gast hat eine Geduldsanzeige. Läuft sie ab, geht er ohne zu bezahlen und du verlierst
ein **Herz**. Bei 0 Herzen ist das Level verloren. Ab Level 12 (vier Plätze) hast du vier statt drei Herzen.

**Sterne:** Jedes der 20 Kampagnen-Level hat ein Zeitlimit und drei Geldziele. Erreichst du das erste Ziel,
ist das Level geschafft (1 Stern), für 2 und 3 Sterne brauchst du mehr. Bei Ladenschluss kommen keine
neuen Gäste mehr – wer schon wartet, wird noch bedient. Verdiente Münzen behältst du auch bei einer Niederlage.

**Laden:** Mit deinen Münzen kaufst du im Shop neue Zutaten (am Anfang hast du nur Açaí, Banane, Granola
und Honig – insgesamt gibt es 16), bessere Qualität (mehr Münzen pro Zutat), Küchen-Upgrades
(schnellerer Mixer, großer Mixkrug, zweiter Mixer, mehr Bowl-Plätze, Doppel-Smoothie) und Deko,
die Gäste geduldiger macht.

**Endlos-Modus:** Nach Level 10 wird der Endlos-Modus freigeschaltet: kein Zeitlimit, alle 30 Sekunden
wird es schwerer (mehr Plätze, mehr Gäste, größere Bestellungen). Gespielt wird, bis alle Herzen weg sind
oder du im Pausenmenü die Schicht beendest – deine Münzen und dein Highscore werden gespeichert.

Fortschritt, Sprache und Ton-Einstellungen werden im Browser gespeichert (`localStorage`).

## Lokal starten

Voraussetzung: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22 oder neuer.

```bash
npm install          # nur für Build und Tests nötig (esbuild, Playwright)
npm start            # Entwicklungsserver ohne Cache → http://localhost:8080
```

ES-Module funktionieren nicht über `file://` – zum Entwickeln also immer `npm start` verwenden.
Zum Testen auf einem Tablet im selben WLAN: `node tools/serve.mjs 8080 . --host 0.0.0.0` und auf dem Tablet
`http://<IP-des-Rechners>:8080` öffnen.

Ohne Server spielen: `npm run build` ausführen und danach **`dist/acai-fever.html`** direkt im Browser
öffnen (Doppelklick) – diese eine Datei enthält das komplette Spiel.

## Befehle

| Befehl | Was passiert |
|---|---|
| `npm start` | Statischer Server (`tools/serve.mjs`) auf Port 8080, ohne Caching. Anderer Port: `node tools/serve.mjs 3000` |
| `npm test` | Unit-Tests mit `node --test` (Engine, Bestellungen, Daten, Speicherstand, Übersetzungen, Audio, Grafik, Balancing); `node --test tests/` geht auch |
| `npm run build` | Bündelt alles mit esbuild zu `dist/acai-fever.html` (eigenständig, läuft per `file://`) und `dist/artifact.html` (gleicher Inhalt ohne `<html>/<head>/<body>`-Hülle, zum Veröffentlichen als Claude-Artifact) |
| `npm run e2e` | Führt alle Playwright-Skripte `tests/e2e/*.e2e.mjs` nacheinander aus (Chromium, headless, Server auf Port 8090 bzw. `E2E_PORT`). Filter: `npm run e2e -- playthrough` |

`tools/build.mjs` versteht außerdem `--entry <datei>`, `--outdir <ordner>` und `--root <ordner>`.
E2E-Skripte legen Screenshots in `$E2E_OUT_DIR` ab (Standard: Temp-Ordner), nie im Repository.
`playthrough.e2e.mjs` spielt Level 1 komplett mit echten Maus-Drags durch (inkl. Tutorial, Shop-Kauf, Level 2),
dann mit Touch auf 1024×768, testet den Endlos-Modus und die englische Oberfläche, prüft, dass ein

nicht gegenseitig überschreiben. `build.e2e.mjs` baut das

deloy4/graveyard-gridiron.readme:
# Graveyard Gridiron

A football game against a field full of zombies, played in the browser. Pick a play, snap
the ball, throw to one of three receivers, and run it to the far end zone before the
60-second clock runs out. The clock only runs while a play is live, and you get four downs
to make ten yards.

The running game follows the rules of an old Java applet from the late 1990s. The code,
art and sound here are all new.

## Controls

Before the snap, the up and down arrows pick a play and Space snaps the ball. After the
snap, the arrow keys (or I J K L) move, and A, S and D throw to the receiver with that
letter while you're still behind the line of scrimmage. If a zombie is touching the
receiver when the ball arrives, the pass is incomplete. A touchdown is worth 7 points, and running into a ghost is worth 2, though it leaves a tombstone in its place. M mutes the sound. On a
touchscreen, buttons for all of these appear under the field.

## Running it

Open `index.html` in a browser. There is no build step.

MohitOrange/finger-ninja.readme:
# 🥷 Finger Ninja — AR Fruit Slicer

A browser game where **your webcam is the controller**. The game reads your hands in real time (Google MediaPipe), and your **index fingertip becomes a blade**. Slice the fruit, dodge the bombs.

## How to play

1. Click **Turn on camera** and allow camera access.
2. **Player-ready check** — the game waits until it sees:
   - ✅ camera on  ✅ AI tracking loaded  ✅ your **hand** (no face needed)
3. Hold your fingertip on the glowing **START** ring to begin.
4. Swipe your index finger fast through fruit to slice it.

| Rule | |
|---|---|
| 🍉 Slice fruit | +1 to +3 points per fruit |
| ⚡ Combo | 3+ fruits in one swipe = bonus points |
| ❤️ Lives | Miss 3 fruits → game over |
| 💣 Bomb | Touch one → **instant game over** |
| ⏸ Auto-pause | Game pauses if no hand is seen for 3 seconds, resumes when you raise it |

Both hands work as blades. A mouse (click + drag) also works for testing.

## Run it locally

Cameras only work on `https://` or `http://localhost`, so don't open `index.html` by double-clicking — serve it:

```bash
# Python
python -m http.server 8000
# or Node
npx serve .
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000> in Chrome or Edge.

## Publish with GitHub Pages

Repo → **Settings → Pages** → Source: `Deploy from a branch` → `main` / `root` → Save.
Your game will be live at `https://<your-username>.github.io/finger-ninja/`.

## Project structure

```
finger-ninja/
├── index.html        # screens: intro, player-ready check, HUD, game over
├── css/style.css     # visuals & HUD
└── js/
    ├── game.js       # game loop, spawning, slicing, scoring, rendering
    ├── tracker.js    # camera + MediaPipe hand tracking
    └── audio.js      # synthesized sound effects (no audio files)
```

## Tech

- [MediaPipe Tasks Vision](https://developers.google.com/mediapipe/solutions/vision/hand_landmarker) — `HandLandmarker` (21 points per hand, up to 2 hands)
- HTML5 Canvas 2D for rendering, Web Audio API for sound
- No build step, no dependencies to install

## Privacy

All tracking runs locally in your browser. No video is recorded or sent anywhere.

asdkfkosafj/SDT-Godot.readme:
# SDT-Godot

A port of the Flash game *SDT* to the Godot engine (4.7). It aims to stay faithful to the original while being
easier to extend (mods, new features) and running much faster than the Flash version.

**Adult content (18+).** The game is sexually explicit.

The game's art, sounds and fonts are included, already converted from the original `SDT.swf` into
`game/assets/sdt/`, so the original game is not needed to play. They belong to the original game's author and are
not covered by this repository's license. If you are a rights holder and want them removed, please open an issue.

## Layout

- `game/`: the Godot project.
  - `game/flash/`: a small Flash runtime (display list, timelines, filters, text, SharedObject; an ActionScript
    interpreter for mod scripts).
  - `game/src/`: the game, ported class by class from the original ActionScript (same class and method names).
  - `game/scenes/main.gd`: entry point, plus the scripted test harness options.
- `native/`: source of the C++ GDExtension for hot paths (see [native/README.md](native/README.md)).
- `game/assets/sdt/`: the converted game assets (shapes, sounds, fonts, timelines in `library.json`).
- `game/bin/`: the native extension, prebuilt for Windows (debug and release DLLs).
- `tools/swfconv/`: converts `SDT.swf` into the asset library (only needed to regenerate `game/assets/sdt/`).
- `tools/porting/`: one-off scripts used while porting the ActionScript (kept for reference).
- `Mods/`: created on first run in the repository root (next to `run_debug.bat`; next to the executable in an
  exported build), with `Clothing`, `Hair`, `Backgrounds`, `Characters`, `Dialogue` and `Plugins` folders.
  Vanilla SDT `.swf` mods placed there show up in the in-game pickers.

## Running

1. Install [Godot 4.7.2](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/4.7.2-stable/) (the standard version, not .NET).
2. Tell `run_debug.bat` where Godot is, in one of these ways:
   - create `run_debug.local.bat` next to it containing
     `set GODOT=C:\path\to\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe` (the console version shows the log), or
   - set the `GODOT` environment variable to that path, or
   - copy or rename the Godot executable to `godot.exe` in a folder on PATH.
3. Run `run_debug.bat`. The first run imports the assets once (a few minutes), then the game starts.

You can also open `game/` in the Godot editor and press F5.

The ready-to-run setup is for **Windows** (the launcher and the prebuilt native extension). On Linux or macOS, run
`godot --headless --path game --import` once, then `godot --path game`. There is no prebuilt native extension for
those systems yet: Godot reports the missing library and the game uses its slower GDScript code instead.

## Regenerating the assets (optional)

Only needed to rebuild `game/assets/sdt/` from an original `SDT.swf`. Requirements: Python 3 with `pillow` and
`numpy`, Java and [JPEXS FFDec](https://github.com/jindrapetrik/jpexs-decompiler).

```
python tools/swfconv/convert.py original/SDT.swf game/assets/sdt --scale 2 [--ffdec path/to/ffdec.jar]
python tools/swfconv/fix_hitmasks.py original/SDT.swf game/assets/sdt
python tools/swfconv/supersample.py original/SDT.swf game/assets/sdt
```

The native extension can be rebuilt from source too, see `native/README.md`. Without it the game falls back to
slower GDScript code.

## Testing

`game/scenes/main.gd` documents the command-line options for scripted runs (`--eval`, `--driver`, `--shot`,
`--frames`, `--deterministic`, ...). Always pass `--save-dir=<folder>` to test runs so they don't overwrite your
own save. Example:

```
godot --headless --path game -- --save-dir=/tmp/sdt-test --driver=res://debug/stress_costumes.gd
```

`tools/regress.sh` runs the regression tests (Git Bash or any POSIX shell, with `GODOT` set). It plays fixed
scenarios headless (menu, idle, grab and stroking, costume changes, every character, cumming) with sound and timers
following game time, so runs repeat exactly. It compares dumps of the display list and character state with the
references in `tests/golden/`. It runs without mods and with a throwaway save. Options:
- `--update` accepts the current output as the new reference; check `git diff tests/golden` first;
- `--stress` adds the costume stress test and reports memory per round;
- `--mods=<folder>` load-tests every `.swf` mod in a folder.

An intended change to the game's behaviour shows up as a difference: review it, then run `--update`.

`tools/check_all.sh` parse-checks every script. It reports "Identifier not found: Flash / g" for autoloads, which
can be ignored.

## Contributing

Code contributions are licensed under the MIT license (see `LICENSE`).

maevlyn/gate-fixer.desc: 3D logic-gate puzzle game for teaching Grade 12 students (three.js)
maevlyn/gate-fixer.readme:
# Gate Fixer

A browser game for teaching logic gates to Grade 12 students. Each level shows a circuit with one or more missing gates and a target truth table. Students choose gates for the empty slots, then test the circuit: it runs every input combination while 3D signals travel through the wires, and each row of the truth table is marked right or wrong.

Built with [three.js](https://threejs.org/) (r128, loaded from cdnjs). No build step.

## Levels

1. Ignition interlock (AND)
2. Two doorbells (OR)
3. Staircase light (XOR)
4. Seatbelt warning (NAND)
5. Through an inverter (choose the gate before a NOT)
6. Sprinkler control (three inputs)
7. Enabled parity check (two missing gates)
8. Half adder (two outputs: sum and carry)

Stars reward getting a level right on the first test. Progress is saved in the browser's local storage.

## Run it

Open `index.html` through any static web server, for example:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then visit http://localhost:8000. It also works as-is on GitHub Pages.

## Controls

- Click a dashed slot in the 3D view (or a slot button) to select it.
- Pick a gate from the palette, or press keys `1` to `6`.
- **Test all inputs** checks the circuit against the target truth table.
- The **Gate reference** panel lists every gate's truth table and rule.

## Files

- `index.html`: the game and its levels
- `gates3d.js`: shared three.js kit (gate shapes, switches, lamps, wires, circuit evaluation and signal animation)
- `shared.css`: layout and styles

6up-b/bluff-lab.desc: Does memory make AI agents better or more exploitable? A bluffing-game lab with ground truth.
6up-b/bluff-lab.readme:
# Bluff Lab

A controlled experiment in how AI agents learn through persistent memory without retraining, and in whether
that memory makes them more capable or more exploitable.

The testbed is a 3-player bluffing card game with ground truth. Every challenge reveals the cards, so we always
know who lied. Our agent, **the Profiler**, keeps a typed, time-aware memory of each opponent: a base bluff rate,
plus hypotheses written as machine-checkable predicates. Between games, a frozen Claude model proposes those
hypotheses, and later reveals score them (provisional → confirmed → refuted or superseded). Only confirmed lines
affect decisions, and lines without evidence get weight 0. Every decision is recorded, and you can replay any of
them under a different memory.

- **Mind Inspector:** the recorded decision variables for any decision: card math, the memory line used and its
  evidence, p(bluff), EV and the action.
- **Memory Surgery:** the same recorded state under `full` / `as_of:N` / `minus:<aspect>` / `false_memory` /
  `transplant` memory. Decision level uses `/replay`. Outcome level uses `/branch`: games 11–20 on the same
  seeds with learning frozen.
- **The Long Con:** a sleeper opponent is honest for 5–8 games, then defects. We measure rounds to detection,
  the bluffs it gets through, and the trust curve.
- **Strategy Forge:** memory is compiled into a Python strategy, checked by a static gate, and run as
  untrusted code in a network-blocked Daytona sandbox.

`SPEC.md` is the full specification. `NOTES.md` covers the pitch and framing. `INTERFACES.md` describes the
module seams.

## Quick start (local, no cloud)

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
# one 20-game world, stub reflection (no network) → runs/local/telltale-profiler-s7/
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli local --table telltale --agent profiler --seed 7
# re-run one recorded decision under different memories
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli replay telltale-profiler-s7 <decision seq> --variants full,as_of:0,false_memory
# outcome-level surgery: restore game 10, play 11–20 on the same seeds with memory erased
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli branch telltale-profiler-s7 --from-game 10 --variant as_of:0
# metrics with bootstrap CIs → runs/local/results.json + summary.md
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli analyze --run local
```

Tables are `telltale`, `longcon`, `falsealarm` and `telltale_overt`. Agents are `counter`, `bayes`,
`bayes_discount`, `logreg_bow`, `profiler_amnesic`, `profiler` and `profiler_blind`. Real Claude reflection
uses `--llm`.

## The Show (presentation app)

A static page that replays one real recorded world through a presenter-paced cue file. There is no build step,
and it works offline.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli pick-demo --run local     # or --run r01 → show/bundle/
cd show && python -m http.server 8000                                  # open http://localhost:8000/?hud
```

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Space / → / PageDown | next cue |
| ← / PageUp | previous cue |
| R | reset |
| H | presenter HUD |
| F | fullscreen |

`?cue=N` jumps to a cue.

`pick-demo` chooses the world and the Surgery Reveal decision by a fixed rule (SPEC §13), never by hand. It
writes every bundle file from real event logs and real `replay_decision` outputs, and records the choice in
`show/bundle/PROVENANCE.md`. Panels whose data doesn't exist render "awaiting data", and cues whose files are
missing are skipped.

## Cloud run (Daytona)

```bash
# create settings.env with the keys listed below (gitignored; never commit it)
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli spike                  # PASS/FAIL table for every integration
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli provision --boxes 2 --cpu 4 --mem 8
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli run --matrix matrix.yaml --run r01
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli reflect --run r01      # orchestrator-side Claude + SurrealDB loop
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli ablate --run r01
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli collect --run r01 && .venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli analyze --run r01
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.cli pick-demo --run r01
.venv/bin/python -m blab.orchestrator.pick --devpost --run r01   # DEVPOST.md → DEVPOST.filled.md from results.json
```

`run --local-only` runs the same matrix in-process (ProcessPoolExecutor) without Daytona.

Environment variables (in `settings.env`):

- `DAYTONA_API_KEY`
- AWS Bedrock credentials or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- `ARIZE_SPACE_ID`, `ARIZE_API_KEY`
- `SPECTRON_API_KEY`, `SPECTRON_URL`, `SPECTRON_CONTEXT_ID` (SurrealDB Agent Memory)
- `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`
- `BLAB_KEY`

Every integration degrades to a no-op or SKIP when its keys are missing.

## Architecture

```
orchestrator (laptop, `blab` CLI) ── provision · run · reflect · ablate · forge · voice · collect · analyze · pick
   │  reflect: box ⇄ orchestrator ⇄ SurrealDB Agent Memory ⇄ Claude (Opus 5.5 via Bedrock)
   │  tracing: Arize AX · voice: ElevenLabs
   ▼  HTTPS preview URL + token
Daytona world boxes: worldd (FastAPI :8000), K worlds each → events.jsonl, ckpt/gNN.json, memory/<seat>.json
Daytona forge box (ephemeral, network_block_all): forge_eval runs the engine in the parent process and the
   untrusted policy in a child process
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `blab/engine.py` | rules, features, card math, snapshot/restore |
| `blab/events.py` | the frozen event contract between Lab and Show |
| `blab/hypotheses.py` | predicate DSL evaluator (never `eval`), grid posteriors, scoring, supersession, drift |
| `blab/agents/` | scripted opponents; `counter`, `bayes`, `logreg_bow`, `profiler*` |
| `blab/world.py`, `blab/replay.py` | world runner, checkpoints, `/replay`, `/branch` |
| `blab/worldd.py` | box server |
| `blab/orchestrator/` | integrations, `analyze.py` (metrics), `pick.py` (Show bundle

bar371/my-spiel.readme:
# SPIEL '26 Planner 🎲

A small planner for our crew (Sjoerd, Annemieke, Bar and Naomi) at **SPIEL Essen 2026**
(Messe Essen, Thu 22 – Sun 25 October 2026).

- **My day**: a time grid of your day: demo sessions you've joined (fixed times 🔒) and booth visits you've planned. Drag a visit by its ⠿ grip to move it, or by its bottom edge to change its length (15-minute steps, mouse or touch). Clashes are outlined in red, and **Fix clashes** moves overlapping visits to the next free time.
- **Games**: every game we're tracking with publisher, hall/booth, players, play time, price, description, a link, and its session times. Tap a game to join a demo session, **plan a booth visit** (any game, no demo needed: pick a day, start and length; it suggests your next free slot), add it to your buy list, or write notes.
- **Favorites**: tap ☆ on any game to mark one you like, even if you won't plan it. **★ Favorites** filters the list, and the Crew tab shows the crew's favorites, most-liked first.
- **Crew**: *Who's going where*: day by day, every demo session and booth visit anyone has planned, with everyone's meeples and a 🤝 badge when you're going together. Updates live once crew sync is on.
- **Budget**: set your budget, mark games must-have or maybe, tick them off when bought, and see what's left.
- **More**: switch player, share your plan, back up or restore, and install instructions.

It's a single static page (HTML, CSS and plain JS, with no build step) that works offline once loaded.

## Running it

- **Locally:** open `index.html` in a browser, or run `python3 -m http.server` and visit http://localhost:8000.
- **Online:** every push to `main` deploys to GitHub Pages through `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
  One-time setup: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**.
  The site is then at `https://bar371.github.io/my-spiel/`.

## Installing on iPhone / iPad

1. Open the GitHub Pages URL in **Safari**.
2. Tap **Share → Add to Home Screen**.

It launches full-screen with its own icon, like an app, and keeps working offline.
No App Store or Xcode needed.

## Where data lives

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Members, fair days, the shared game list | `data/spiel-data.js` (edit and push to `main` to update everyone) |
| Your sessions, booth visits, buy list, budget, notes, games added in the app | the phone's `localStorage`, mirrored to the crew's live database when crew sync is on |

## Live crew sync (Firebase, one-time setup, about 5 minutes)

So everyone sees who's going to which session, the app syncs through a free
[Firebase Realtime Database](https://firebase.google.com/docs/database). There's no server to run.

1. Go to <https://console.firebase.google.com>, choose **Create a project** (any name, e.g. `spiel26-crew`), and switch Google Analytics off.
2. In the project, open **Build → Realtime Database → Create Database**. Pick **Belgium (europe-west1)** and **Start in locked mode**.
3. Open the **Rules** tab, replace everything with the rules below, and click **Publish**:

   ```json
   {
     "rules": {
       "crews": {
         "$crew": {
           ".read": "$crew.length >= 10",
           ".write": "$crew.length >= 10"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

4. Copy the database URL from the **Data** tab (it looks like `https://spiel26-crew-default-rtdb.europe-west1.firebasedatabase.app`)
   and put it in `data/sync-config.js` as `databaseURL`. Push to `main`.
5. In the app: **More → Live crew sync → Start a crew**, then send the invite link to the others.
   Opening the link joins the crew. A crew code can also be pasted under **More**.

Notes:
- The crew code is a random 12-character key that only travels in the invite link. Anyone with the link can see and edit the crew's plans, so share it only with the crew.
  The database can't be listed, so nobody can find your crew without the code.
- Each phone keeps working offline and catches up when it's back online. When two phones change the same thing, the newer change wins.
- Before crew sync is set up, **Share my plan** still sends your plan as a one-off link.

### Adding a game to the shared list

Add an entry to `games` in `data/spiel-data.js`:

```js
{
  id: "my-game",                 // unique, never reuse
  name: "My Game",
  publisher: "Some Publisher",
  hall: "3", booth: "3-B210",
  players: "2–4", duration: "60 min",
  price: 45,
  url: "https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/…",
  description: "…",
  sessions: [
    { id: "my-game-1", day: "2026-10-23", start: "11:00", end: "12:00", location: "Table 4", note: "" }
  ]
}
```

The shared list holds the BoardGameGeek SPIEL 2026 preview (boardgamegeek.com/geekpreviewv2/93; about 770 games
with a hall or booth, with price and player count where the publisher gave them; listings without any hall or booth
are left out as they're probably not at the fair; `bgg` is the BoardGameGeek id) plus 33 games compiled
from preview articles (marked `preview: true`, each linking to its source).
Demo times are unpublished, so add them with **Edit game** in the app (shared with the crew when sync is on) or in this file.

To refresh the BGG games, run the **Import BGG SPIEL preview** workflow (Actions tab), or locally
`node tools/import-bgg-preview.js`. It keeps the preview games, only filling their empty fields from BGG.

Every game has `tags` for the type filter in the Games tab (Engine building, Deck building, Worker placement,
PvP / conflict, Co-op, Trick-taking, Party, Solo, Quick, …; the chip order is `SPIEL_SEED.tags`). The importer
derives them from BGG's mechanics, categories and subdomains, falls back to keywords in the description for
games BGG hasn't classified, and adds hand-picked ones from `MANUAL_TAGS` in `tools/import-bgg-preview.js`.
Selecting several tags shows games that have all of them. Two extra chips come first: **📰 Preview** (the preview-article games) and **🎲 Demo slot** (games with at least one demo session, including ones added in the app). Tags can

DarkendSun/PSP-Homebrew-Store.readme:
# PSP Homebrew Store

A homebrew store that runs on a PSP with CFW, for a few friends. It shows a **signed catalogue** of free
homebrew from the Internet Archive's
[PlayStation Portable Library: Homebrews](https://archive.org/details/psp-homebrew-library), downloads apps
through a small **relay** (a Cloudflare Worker), checks each download, and installs it to
`PSP/GAME/<folder>/`.

> These are third-party homebrew files, made by many different people. You use them at your own risk.
> The store never touches `PSP/GAME/UPDATE`, and it only deletes folders it installed itself.

**Status: tested in the PPSSPP emulator, not yet on a real PSP.** GitHub Actions builds the app, and every
build of `main` is published as the [nightly prerelease](https://github.com/DarkendSun/PSP-Homebrew-Store/releases/tag/nightly)
(`EBOOT.PBP`, a ready `HBSTORE.zip`, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`). See "Tested" below for what has been checked.

```
app/        PSP app (C, pspdev): EBOOT.PBP
generator/  catalogue builder + ed25519 signer (Python, no extra packages)
relay/      Cloudflare Worker: serves the signed catalogue and passes through listed archive.org files
```

## How it fits together

1. **Generator** (your PC): lists the archive.org collection and GitHub releases of open-source PSP
   homebrew. It keeps entries whose `.zip` contains an `EBOOT.PBP` app, drops anything in the
   `not-working-psp` item, and writes `relay/public/catalogue.txt`, signed with your ed25519 key
   (`catalogue.sig`).
2. **Relay** (Cloudflare): the PSP can't do modern HTTPS, so it talks **plain HTTP** to the relay. The relay
   serves the catalogue, and fetches from `https://archive.org` or GitHub only files that are **listed in
   the catalogue**. It isn't an open proxy: anything else gets a 404.
3. **App** (PSP): it accepts a catalogue only if its signature matches the public key built into the app.
   It checks every download's SHA-1 against the catalogue before unpacking, and its own updates against a
   SHA-512.

## 1. Catalogue generator

```
py -3 generator/hbgen.py keygen       # once: makes the key + app/src/pubkey.h (already done on this PC)
py -3 generator/hbgen.py build        # whole collection
py -3 generator/hbgen.py build --limit 40   # quick test
py -3 generator/hbgen.py verify
```

- **The private key** is `%USERPROFILE%\.psp-hbstore\signing.key`, outside the repo and gitignored. Back it
  up somewhere private. Lose it and you'd have to ship a new app build with a new key. `keygen` refuses to
  overwrite it.
- **The first full build** checks about 4,170 entries with 1 to 2 polite requests each (1 s apart, cached in
  `generator/cache/`), so it takes a couple of hours. Later builds only ask about new entries. A test run of
  40 entries kept 37.
- **Only `.zip` versions are used**, because the app unpacks zip but not 7z. If an entry has several zips, it
  prefers the newest-looking one (not under "Old versions").
- **GitHub releases** (`generator/github_source.py`): candidates come from the
  [PSP-Archive](https://github.com/PSP-Archive) organisation, the `psp-homebrew` topic and
  `generator/github_repos.txt`. A repo is listed only if:
  - GitHub reports an open-source license (MIT, BSD, GPL, LGPL, Apache, MPL, Unlicense and so on).
  - It isn't CFW, flasher or firmware tooling.
  - Its latest release has a `.zip` asset with an `EBOOT.PBP` app. The generator downloads the zip once to
    look inside and to take its SHA-1.

  The source, author, license and repo link are recorded, and shown on the app's details screen. If a GitHub
  app is also in the archive.org library, the GitHub release is kept and the archive.org copy dropped. API
  answers are cached for a day. Unauthenticated GitHub allows 60 API calls an hour; for more, set
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` in your shell for that run (read-only, never put it in a file in the repo). Add
  `--no-github` to skip this source.
- **Catalogue format** (`catalogue.txt`, UTF-8, ASCII text fields):
  `PSPHBS 2 <generated> <app version> <app size> <app sha512>` on the first line, then one line per entry:
  `E <id> <title> <kind> <date> <zip file> <size> <sha1> <prefix>NAME|... <description> <source> <author>
  <license> <link>`, tab-separated. GitHub entries have ids `gh:<owner>/<repo>` and files `<tag>/<asset>`.
  The signature covers the exact bytes.

## 2. Relay (a new, separate Cloudflare Worker)

`relay/` is its own Worker, **`psp-homebrew-relay`**, separate from anything else on your Cloudflare
account.

- `GET /catalogue.txt`, `/catalogue.sig`, `/app/EBOOT.PBP`: published files from `relay/public/`.
- `GET /dl/<id>/<file>`: streams `https://archive.org/download/<id>/<file>`, or for `gh:` entries
  `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`, only when that pair is in the
  catalogue.
  - Redirects are followed only within archive.org, or within github.com, `objects.githubusercontent.com`
    and `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`.
  - It retries once if the source has a hiccup.
- **Rate limit:** 60 requests a minute per IP, using Cloudflare's rate-limit binding.
- **No login or token:** anyone with the address can read the catalogue and fetch the listed files. The
  allow-list and the rate limit stop it being used for anything else.

Run it locally (tested):

```
cd relay
npm install
npx wrangler dev --ip 0.0.0.0 --port 8787
```

Then point the app (or `curl`) at `http://<this PC's LAN IP>:8787`.

**Deploying is your call.** Nothing has been deployed or changed on Cloudflare. When you want it:

```
cd relay
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy
```

Each `deploy` publishes whatever is in `relay/public/`, so run the generator
first.

**Plain HTTP:** `workers.dev` answers plain `http://` as well as `https://` and doesn't redirect, so
`http://psp-homebrew-relay.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev` works with **no settings changes**. That's the
recommended address. (Browsers force HTTPS on `.dev` because of HSTS preloading, but the PSP's network
stack doesn't, which i

Louzada-git/Dungeon-Crawler.readme:
# Dungepm — As Cisternas

Dungeon crawler de sobrevivência com cara de PlayStation 1, feito na Godot 4.7.

Você desce pelas cisternas com uma mochila, um pouco de comida e uma arma. Cada expedição gera um labirinto novo. Explore as salas, cuide da fome, do fôlego e dos ferimentos, troque o que achar com o mercador e derrote o capataz de cada andar para abrir a descida. Se o aventureiro morrer, ele não volta: o próximo começa do zero, mas lembra o mapa que você já explorou.

![Uma sala do 1º andar, na câmera isométrica](revisao/terceira/04-mesmo-lugar-isometrica.png)

## Baixar e jogar

Não precisa instalar nada: o jogo inteiro vai dentro do executável.

| Sistema | Download | Como abrir |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (64 bits) | [Dungepm-windows.zip](https://github.com/Louzada-git/Dungeon-Crawler/raw/main/downloads/Dungepm-windows.zip) (47 MB) | Extraia (botão direito → **Extrair tudo**) e abra `Dungepm.exe`. Se o Windows avisar que o programa não é conhecido, clique em **Mais informações → Executar assim mesmo**. |
| Linux (64 bits) | [Dungepm-linux.tar.xz](https://github.com/Louzada-git/Dungeon-Crawler/raw/main/downloads/Dungepm-linux.tar.xz) (29 MB) | Extraia e abra `linux/Dungepm.x86_64`. Se não abrir com dois cliques: `chmod +x Dungepm.x86_64` e `./Dungepm.x86_64`. |

Precisa de placa de vídeo com OpenGL 3.3. O jogo é em português. Os créditos e as licenças vão junto nos dois pacotes.

## O que tem no jogo

**Labirinto**
- Gerado por semente a cada expedição. O 1º andar tem 10 salas, e cada andar seguinte é maior (20, 40, 60…).
- Salas de combate, de suprimentos, de tesouro, covis com o carcereiro (elite) e a câmara do capataz, que guarda a descida.
- Um mercador na entrada de cada andar compra e vende com vinténs. O estoque muda de andar para andar.
- Baús abertos e monstros mortos continuam assim quando você volta a um andar. Alguns baús são trancados e precisam de gazua.

**Sobrevivência**
- Fome, fôlego, carga da mochila e ferimentos que sangram até você tratar com bandagens ou unguento.
- O abrigo do 1º andar é o único lugar seguro: lá você descansa e salva.
- 77 itens: comida, bebida que devolve fôlego, curativos, armaduras leves e pesadas, gazuas, chave-mestra, mapa do andar e tesouros para vender.

**Combate**
- 31 armas, cada uma com seu jeito: espadas, sabre e alfanje cortam, lanças, pique, alabarda e tridente estocam em linha, maças, marretas e martelos esmagam (e furam armadura), machados e lâminas serrilhadas fazem sangrar, adagas matam quem não te viu, e arcos, bestas e funda atiram munição que dá para recolher (flechas de osso, de ponta larga, virotes pesados…).
- O golpe acerta quem a arma encosta: cada arma tem uma hitbox do tamanho do modelo que segue a animação, e o alcance mostrado é o da lâmina. Os monstros acertam com a garra e se jogam no golpe; recuar no preparo escapa.
- Arma pesada bate forte e demora para golpear de novo: cada kg da arma soma 0,1 s de espera.
- Guarda com o botão direito, esquiva, corrida, andar agachado e ataque furtivo.
- Cinco tipos de monstro: afogado, carniçal (rápido), inchado (resistente), carcereiro de elite e o capataz do andar, com pancada em área e fúria na metade da vida.

**Personagem**
- No começo você distribui 25 pontos entre Força, Vigor, Agilidade e Destreza e escolhe a arma inicial (ou começa de punhos).
- Proficiências que sobem com o uso, no estilo de Oblivion, em três grupos: Combate, Furtividade e Sobrevivência. Os ramos dão talentos a partir do nível 5.
- Habilidades com objetos encaixados: cada objeto muda a habilidade (Lâmina afiada faz sangrar, Braço longo estica a lâmina, Golpe duplo acerta duas vezes…), e a ordem dos objetos importa. As teclas das habilidades são você quem escolhe.
- Barra rápida de 1 a 9 com qualquer item.

**Visual**
- Filtro PSX: imagem em pixels grandes, cores reduzidas, texturas sem suavizar e vértices que tremem, como no PS1. Pode desligar.
- Câmera isométrica ou em terceira pessoa, à sua escolha.
- Sangue, faíscas, poeira, fumaça e tochas com chama animada.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Terceira pessoa, com um monstro à frente](revisao/terceira/02-sala-com-monstro.png) | ![O capataz e o anel da pancada em área](revisao/labirinto/03-chefe-golpe-em-area.png) |
| Câmera em terceira pessoa | O capataz avisa a pancada em área com um anel vermelho |
| ![A hitbox da espada ao longo do golpe](revisao/hitbox/01-sword-lado.png) | ![A janela da loja do mercador](revisao/loja/02-loja.png) |
| A hitbox da espada ao longo do golpe (em verde, a posição do impacto) | A loja do mercador |
| ![Janela de habilidades, com objetos e teclas](revisao/barra/02-teclas-das-habilidades.png) | ![Barra rápida com vários itens](revisao/barra/01-barra-rapida.png) |
| Habilidades: objetos, prévia e teclas | Barra rápida de 1 a 9 |

## Controles

| Ação | Controle |
|---|---|
| Mover | WASD ou setas |
| Atacar | Botão esquerdo |
| Mirar / guarda | Segurar botão direito |
| Correr | Shift |
| Esquivar | Espaço |
| Andar agachado | C |
| Interagir / abrir baú / arrombar / loja | E |
| Inventário | I ou Tab |
| Mapa explorado | M |
| Condição física | H |
| Barra rápida (qualquer item) | 1 a 9 |
| Proficiências | P |
| Habilidades: montar e trocar teclas | T |
| Habilidades: usar | Q, R, F, G (ou as que você escolher) |
| Câmera isométrica ou terceira pessoa | Esc → Câmera |
| Aproximar / afastar câmera | Roda do mouse |
| Terceira pessoa: soltar o cursor | Segurar Alt |
| Pausar | Esc |
| Salvar no abrigo | F5 |

## Primeiros passos

1. Monte o aventureiro: distribua os pontos e escolha a arma.
2. No abrigo, pegue o que precisar dos baús e veja o que o mercador vende. Comida e bandagens ocupam a barra rápida desde o começo.
3. Explore o andar. Chegue agachado (C) em monstros que ainda não te viram para um ataque furtivo.
4. Chegue perto o bastante para a arma encostar, e recue quando o monstro preparar a garra. Sem fôlego, você não esquiva nem segura a guarda.
5. O capataz fica na sala mais distante. Derrote-o para abrir a descida.

lieroliu/taiwanese-simulator.readme:
# 台灣人生模擬（暫名）

以台灣為舞台的人生模擬網頁遊戲。玩家選擇一個**出生世代**，被隨機分配身分、家庭與出生地，從出生走到人生終點。重點不在數值，而在**角色每個階段的心境與遇到的處境**。

靈感來源：[1 in 8 Billion（80億分之1）](https://1in8b.life/)。原作比較的是「出生在哪個國家」，本作比較的是「出生在台灣的哪個年代、成為什麼樣的人」。

## 核心概念

- **五個出生世代**：五、六、七、八、九年級（民國年級，1961–2010）。戰後的經歷透過父母那一代呈現
- **身分軸會隨世代改變**：早期世代的人生差異主要來自族群與性別；後期世代則越來越取決於家庭所得與城鄉
- **統計決定發生什麼，文字呈現怎麼感受**：壽命、死因、升學率、所得等由公開統計抽樣；心境文字預先撰寫並經人工審稿
- **同一刻出生的其他人**：沿用原作設計，讓同世代、不同身分的角色並行，看見彼此人生的分岔

## 怎麼玩

線上版：<https://lieroliu.github.io/taiwanese-simulator/>（`main` 更新後自動部署）。也可以直接用瀏覽器打開 [index.html](index.html)。整個遊戲是一個單一 HTML 檔，不需要伺服器。輸入出生年（1961–2010），遊戲會依當年統計抽出出生地、性別、族群和家境，然後一個月一個月往下算，有事發生才停下來。

## 檔案結構

| 路徑 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| [index.html](index.html) | 可玩的原型，所有程式、資料和文字都內嵌在這一個檔案裡 |
| [data/stats/](data/stats/) | 官方統計資料（戶政、主計總處、衛福部、教育部等），來源見 [sources.md](data/stats/sources.md) |
| [content/](content/) | 文字內容：歷史事件的個性版本、0–6 歲事件、交往過程、族群專屬事件與共同事件的族群版本。格式見 [FORMAT.md](content/FORMAT.md) |
| [tools/build.py](tools/build.py) | 把 `data/stats/` 和 `content/` 重新嵌進 `index.html` |
| [tests/](tests/) | 用 Playwright 跑大量人生的自動檢查 |
| [docs/](docs/) | 設計文件與歷史事件清單 |

## 修改流程

1. 改 `content/*.json` 或 `data/stats/*.json`
2. `python3 tools/build.py`
3. 跑測試（需要 Playwright，`PW` 可指定 playwright 模組路徑）：
   - `node tests/smoke.js`：跑 1500 個人生，不能有錯誤
   - `node tests/consistency.js index.html 400`：抓年紀、父母、婚姻、孩子的前後矛盾，並輸出政治參與分布
   - `node tests/repetition.js`：同縣市、不同地區、不同族群（含新住民子女）的日記重複率
   - `node tests/cohort.js`：各世代的升學、結婚、生育、買房比例
   - `node tests/money.js`：各世代 30／45／65 歲的存款中位數
   - `node tests/share.js`：跑幾個人生到結局，檢查分享圖能產生 1080×1920 的圖
   - `node tests/testmode.js`：檢查測試模式（網址加 `?test=1`）能指定出生縣市、族群、性別和家境
   - `node tests/eras.js`：同樣家境、同樣個性的人，生在不同年級的差距（學歷、買房、存款、後悔的事）
   - `node tests/fun_content.js`：檢查好笑小事、差點死掉、死因場景和高風險選擇的內容格式
   - `node tests/fun.js`：跑很多人生，看好笑小事的比例、差點死掉的次數、高風險選擇出現和被選的次數，以及平均壽命
   - `node tests/classes.js`：國中能力分班（升學班、普通班、放牛班）在各年代、各家境的比例
   - `node tests/repeats.js`：同一生裡同一句話、同一個問題重複出現的次數
   - `node tests/age_rules.js`：未滿 16 歲不騎機車，16–17 歲偷騎會照當年的取締寫出有沒有被抓；未成年抽菸喝酒照當年法規
   - `node tests/kin_content.js`：親戚建議內容檢查；`node tests/kin.js`：每個人都有親戚的建議、填志願衝突怎麼選、轉系和重考的結果
   - `node tests/sats.js`：結尾「你滿意的事」，每個成年角色至少一件，各種來源出現的次數
   - `node tests/pop_content.js`：流行物年表內容檢查；`node tests/pop.js`：每一生的流行物日記、童年幾則、結尾「你那一屆的童年」
   - `node tests/house.js`：買房的頭期、房貸本息攤還、銀行審核；各年代北北與其他地區的房貸負擔和買房比例
   - `node tests/partners.js`：各年代認識對象的管道、兩個人選一個、個性合不合、住公婆家的比例、三十年婚姻裡另一半外遇的比例（目標一成到一成五）
   - `node tests/scenarios.js index.html 60`：特殊背景（最早最晚年次、原住民、離島、單親、隔代教養、務農與公教、新住民子女、受難者家屬、隨機亂選）各跑一批人生，抓前後矛盾、季節錯、職業錯、被守門員剪成半句的日記，以及各選項出現的年紀與狀態

MenuuTUX/jojo-hftf-native.readme:
# JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heritage for the Future, native port

A native macOS build of the PlayStation version of *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure* (Capcom, 1999, US release SLUS-01060).

The game is a static recompilation on [psxrecomp](https://github.com/RetroPortingToolKit/psxrecomp). On top of it, the game's own code is being replaced with native C, one function at a time. Each replacement has been compared against the original on thousands of captured game states before it is allowed to run.

Built with LLM agents (Claude Code and Codex), directed and reviewed by a human.

## Status

- The 1v1 fight engine (shared fight code, the main loop, scheduling, hit tests, animation) runs natively: 918 functions, checked against 97,634 captured states with no mismatches.
- All 22 selectable characters, the 4 encounter-only bosses (as the second player), all 33 stages, VS and training mode and their select screens have native code. 3,573 of those 7,188 functions are verified so far. The others still run as recompiled MIPS until a test route reaches them.
- Story and Arcade mode run on the recompiled code.
- macOS on Apple Silicon is the only tested platform.

## Building

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). You need your own copy of the game disc.

## Layout

```
CMakeLists.txt     build (psxrecomp project)
game.toml          game configuration for the runtime
generated/         the recompiled game code (psxrecomp output)
src/game/          native game code: generated from the decompilation (gen_*.c) and hand-written (manual/)
src/hybrid/        glue between the runtime and the native code
src/platform/      platform layer (files, CD streaming, audio)
src/shell/         macOS app (Swift, Metal)
assets/disc/       files extracted from the disc (see NOTICE.md)
assets/xa/         streamed audio extracted from the disc
psxrecomp/         the recompiler and runtime (git submodule)
patches/           local changes to psxrecomp, applied by setup.sh
docs/              architecture and file format notes
disc/              where your disc image goes
```

## How it works

[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains the recompilation, how native functions replace recompiled ones, and how they are checked. The tools that generate and verify the native code (decompiler scripts, the C generator, the capture and replay harness) and the full phase reports are in the development repository, jojo-hftf-native-tools.

## Legal

Not affiliated with Capcom or with the psxrecomp authors. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

recompiled game code in generated/, files extracted from the disc in
assets/ (see NOTICE.md), psxrecomp as a pinned submodule with local
hooks in patches/. The development tools and phase reports are in
jojo-hftf-native-tools.

Aashishgtbit/roadster-liftoff.desc: Fan-made, physics-simulated 3D take on the Tesla Roadster flying-car unveiling. Watch or fly the ramp hang and lineup jump, or race a random night course. TypeScript, three.js, Vite.
Aashishgtbit/roadster-liftoff.readme:
# Roadster Liftoff

A fan-made, physics-simulated 3D take on the Tesla Roadster unveiling of October 15, 2026. Watch the ramp hang
and the lineup jump the way they happened on the night, fly them yourself, or race a random night course. Every
move is computed by a rigid-body simulation running in your browser, and the sound is synthesised live from the
same numbers.

[![Test, build and deploy](https://github.com/Aashishgtbit/roadster-liftoff/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Aashishgtbit/roadster-liftoff/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)

**[Play it in your browser →](https://aashishgtbit.github.io/roadster-liftoff/)**

![The lineup jump: the car rolls upside down over a row of parked vehicles at night](docs/lineup-jump.webp)

> **Fan project.** Not affiliated with or endorsed by Tesla or SpaceX. The car is a fan-made model built from
> Tesla's public launch photos and videos, not official design data, and the repo contains no Tesla images or
> logos. Masses, thrusts and other physics values are estimates. Tesla, Roadster, Cybertruck, Cybercab and Semi
> are trademarks of Tesla, Inc.

## What's in it

| | Watch | Play |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lineup jump** | The car spools its floor jets, lifts off, rolls 360° over two sedans, a Semi cab, a Cybertruck and a Cybercab, and glides down to land at about 2 m/s. | Lift off before the first car, roll in the air, and land on your wheels past the last one. The parked vehicles are solid. |
| **Ramp hang** | Suction fans hold the car on a curved wall past vertical. It pauses upside down 12 m up, tips off the end, rolls 180° about its length and lands facing back. | Climb the wall, let go of the gas to hang upside down, drive off the end, flip, and land on your wheels. |
| **Drive it** | | A new random 330 m course every run: bust crate stacks at 45 km/h or more, fly over walls on the jets or launch off kicker ramps, collect fuel, flip for points. Three wall crashes wreck the car. |

While you play, a speedometer, fuel gauge, altimeter, attitude dial and a map of the ten nozzles show what the car
is doing; a scoreboard tracks points as you earn them; banners, screen flashes and confetti mark each success or
crash; and the camera looks ahead along your path. Best scores are kept in your browser.

![Playing Drive it: speedometer and fuel at the top, scoreboard on the right, every control along the bottom](docs/playing.webp)

The second page, `about.html`, is the story of the night: what the car did, the spec sheet as announced, a 0–60
drag strip at real speed, the trims, what is still unproven, the timeline, and the coverage.

![The story page](docs/story.webp)

## Controls

| Key | Touch | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `W` `↑` | ↑ | Gas (up the wall on the ramp) |
| `S` `↓` | ↓ | Brake, then reverse. In the air: glide down to a soft landing on the jets |
| `A` `D` `←` `→` | ‹ › | Steer: front wheels on the ground, nose jets in the air |
| `Space` | jets | Floor jets: climb to a hover and hold it |
| `Q` `E` | ⟲ ⟳ | Roll in the air. Let go past halfway and the car finishes the flip |
| `Shift` | boost | Rear jets |
| `R` | | Put the car back on its wheels |
| `V` | | Camera view: Auto, Chase or Side |
| `C` | | Free look: drag to orbit the car |
| `P` · `M` · `F` | | Pause · sound · full screen |
| `Enter` · `Esc` | | Start the run again · close the results card |

On screen, **Play it / Watch demo** switches a stunt between flying it yourself and watching the flight computer,
and **Wing** cycles the Track Mode aero (Road, High-Downforce, Low-Drag), which changes the downforce.

## Run it locally

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 20 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Aashishgtbit/roadster-liftoff.git
cd roadster-liftoff
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the address Vite prints (usually http://localhost:5173).

| Script | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Dev server with hot reload |
| `npm test` | Headless checks of every stunt, the game physics and the course generator (Vitest) |
| `npm run typecheck` | Strict TypeScript over the app, the tests and the config |
| `npm run build` | Type-check, then build the static site into `dist/` |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the built site |

## How it works

The simulation steps at a fixed 240 Hz, independent of the frame rate:

- **Rigid body.** A 1,900 kg car with its own inertia for roll, pitch and yaw, integrated with semi-implicit
  Euler and Euler's equations for the spin.
- **Suspension and tyres.** Each wheel casts a ray to the ground, a box top, a kicker ramp or the curved wall, and
  rides its own spring, damper and bump stop. Tyre forces stay inside a friction circle (μ 1.15).
- **Ten cold-gas nozzles.** Four under the floor, four in the diffuser, two in the nose. Each pushes from its own
  position with about 40 ms of valve lag, so firing one side harder turns the car.
- **Suction fans** pull the floor toward the wall with up to 1.6 times the car's weight.
- **Aero.** Drag, plus downforce that depends on the wing mode.
- **Collisions.** Hull points push out of the ground, the ramp and obstacles; a solid hit removes the speed into
  the obstacle at once, so nothing tunnels through a wall.
- **Flight computer.** The demos are scripted as phases (spool, lift, roll, glide, touchdown…) using roll
  profiles, a quaternion attitude controller, heading hold and a glide-path landing. When you play, the same
  thrusters take your controls, with a hover height hold and a stability assist.

Sound is Web Audio, generated from the simulation state: motor whine from wheel speed, tyre roar, jet hiss and
roar from total thrust, a pop as each valve opens, fan whine, and a landing thump scaled by the touchdown speed.

## Project structure

```
index.html            the game: full-window 3D stage
about.html            the story page
src/
  main.ts             app entry: loads the scene, warms up the first frame, runs the render loop
  config.ts           shared c

HarrisonZeng/grapple-game.readme:
# 钩锁突袭 · Grapple Raid

A first-person browser game built around a Pathfinder-style grappling hook (Apex Legends). Swing, slide and shoot through five modes. It is one self-contained HTML file using Three.js, so there is nothing to install.

**Play:** https://harrisonzeng.github.io/grapple-game/ (desktop browser with a mouse and keyboard)

## Modes

- **钩锁突袭** (Grapple Raid): arena FPS with dual hooks, an EVA-8 shotgun and a G7 scout with a 2x scope. G7 headshots one-shot.
- **巨人狩猎** (Titan Hunt): Attack on Titan style. Swing around a big city and cut titan napes with blades, or use the crossbow to make them kneel. A Colossal titan boss shows up every third wave.
- **空岛突袭** (Sky Islands): floating islands over a void. Falling costs 20 HP and respawns you on the last island.
- **熔岩闯关** (Lava Run): a Ghostrunner-style 840 m obstacle course over lava with 6 checkpoints. Any kill refreshes your hooks, double jump and glide.
- **城市摆荡** (City Swing): free roam across the city map.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Mouse | Look |
| WASD | Move (auto sprint), steer while hooked |
| Q / E | Left / right grappling hook |
| Space or mouse wheel | Jump; in the air, double jump then a 1 s glide |
| C | Slide |
| Left mouse | Shoot / slash |
| Right mouse | Aim down sights |
| 1 / 2 | Switch weapon |
| R | Reload |
| X | Toggle double jump |

Click the game to lock the mouse; press Esc to release it.

## Run locally

Open `index.html` in a browser. Three.js loads from the jsDelivr CDN, so you need an internet connection.

# N-Back

A Dual N-Back working memory trainer that runs in the browser and is built for phones first.

**Play:** https://martinvojneski.github.io/nback/

## How to play

Every few seconds a square lights up on a 3×3 grid and a letter is spoken.

- Tap **Position** when the square is in the same spot as **N** turns ago.
- Tap **Sound** when the letter is the same as **N** turns ago.
- Both can match on the same turn; tap both.

Score 80% or more to move up a level, under 50% to drop one. Score is `hits / (hits + misses + wrong taps)`.

Modes: Position only, Sound only, or Dual (both). Settings let you change the speed (2–3.5 s per turn), switch spoken letters for tones, and turn off instant feedback or auto-levelling. Sessions are saved on your device.

Keyboard: `A` = Position, `L` = Sound, `Esc` = pause, `Space` = start.

## iPhone

Open the link in Safari, tap **Share → Add to Home Screen**, and it launches full screen like an app and works offline. If you hear nothing, turn up the volume or flip the silent switch off, or pick **Tones** under Settings.

## Run locally

It's plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step:

```bash
python -m http.server 8765
```

Then open http://localhost:8765.

# 蜂巢兵棋 · Hexwar

一个两人对战的六边形格子策略游戏，以及一个从零开始、靠自我对弈训练出来的 AI「宗师」。

- **在线试玩**：<https://pphy96826-coder.github.io/hexwar/>（第 36 代网络，随训练自动更新）（Chrome / Edge / Safari 18+，宗师需要浏览器支持 WebGPU）
- **游戏**：单个 HTML 文件，下载后用浏览器打开 `hexwar.html`（或 `index.html`）也能玩，不需要安装任何东西。
- **AI**：AlphaZero 式训练（神经网络 + 蒙特卡洛树搜索 + 自我对弈），网络在浏览器里用 WebGPU 运行，你思考时它也在后台思考。
- 讲解视频：[`video/hexwar_explainer.mp4`](video/hexwar_explainer.mp4)（规则 + AI 是怎么训练出来的）

## 规则速览

| | |
|---|---|
| 目标 | 打掉对方大本营（20 血）。双方同时归零时，场上单位总费用高的一方获胜 |
| 费用 | 每回合 +3/+4/+5 费（第 1–3 / 4–7 / 8 回合起），占领矿桥每回合额外 +1，上限 10 |
| 部署 | 只能放在与「连通区域」相邻的空格：从本方大本营出发、经由本方单位相连的格子。大本营周围 2 格内永远可以部署 |
| 先后手 | 先手方先部署，后手方看到后再部署；先手每回合轮换 |
| 结算 | 双方都结束部署后**同时**结算：一个单位受到的伤害 = 所有覆盖它的敌方单位伤害之和，≥ 血量就阵亡，可以同归于尽 |
| 克制 | 突击 → 远程 → 重装 → 突击，克制方伤害 +1；护甲减伤，穿透无视护甲 |
| 大本营 | 每回合对相邻敌人造成 2 点伤害；每损失 5 血获得 2 费（怒气） |
| 孤立 | 与大本营断开的单位攻击 −1，也不能当落脚点 |
| 决战 | 第 15 回合起所有单位攻击 +1 |

23 个兵种：民兵、剑士、骑兵（突进）、刺客（潜行）、狂战士（血怒）、盾兵、长枪兵、荆棘卫（反伤）、守护者（护甲光环）、攻城锤（只打大本营）、弓手、弩手（穿透直射）、游侠（破甲标记）、投石车（攻城×2）、火药桶（殉爆）、工兵（架桥筑路）、旗手（前哨）、骷髅兵（重生）、战鼓手、牧师、法师、伞兵（空降）、巨龙（飞行、唯一）。所有射程都朝向敌方大本营。

地形：森林（血+1，挡直射）、高地（远程攻击+1）、河流（只有工兵和巨龙能站）、矿桥（+1 费）、岩石（不可进入）。

地图：河谷、高原、峡谷三张固定地图，以及「随机生成」：每局一张新的中心对称地图，双方地形完全一样。

## 电脑难度

| 难度 | 做法 |
|---|---|
| 简单 / 普通 / 困难 | 手写规则 + 局面评估（评估权重用自我对弈调参） |
| 大师 | 在「整回合部署方案」上做蒙特卡洛树搜索，每步约 4 秒 |
| **宗师** | 神经网络 + 逐个部署的 PUCT 树搜索；局面判断一半来自网络、一半来自大师的威胁计算；用对手思考时间预先搜索 |

## AI 是怎么训练出来的

完整代码在 [`train/az/`](train/az)。

1. **规则就是模拟器**：训练直接加载 `hexwar.html` 里的游戏脚本（`train/engine.js`），保证训练和真实对局用的是同一套规则；`simEndRound` 与真实游戏逐回合比对一致（`consistency_test.js`）。
2. **局面编码**（`game.js`）：87 个特征平面（地形、双方各兵种、血量/攻击/护甲、覆盖范围、可部署格、费用、回合……），棋盘总是转到「当前行动方在下方」，所以一个网络同时会玩先手和后手。
3. **网络**（`model.py`）：全卷积残差网络（64 通道 × 6 层，约 52 万参数），对任何大小的地图都适用。输出：每个(兵种, 格子)的部署概率、结束回合的概率、胜率估计。
4. **搜索**（`mcts.js`）：每一步动作是「放一个兵」或「结束回合」，用 PUCT 搜索选择。
5. **自我对弈循环**（`train.py` + `selfplay.js`）：
   - 先模仿手写 AI 的 640 局，得到一个起点；
   - 每代：自我对弈 384 局（随机地图占多数，让它学会读地形而不是背地图）＋ 与大师对战 96 局 ＋ 与脚本进攻者对战 64 局；
   - 训练 1200 步；新版本与当前最强版本对打 40 局，胜率 ≥ 55% 才替换；
   - 每 3 代与手写大师打 48 局，衡量真实进步。
6. **从真人对局中学习**：在本地页面与宗师对战的每一局都会自动存成训练数据（`server.py`），每一批训练都混入玩家对局的局面。
7. **浏览器里的宗师**（`train/az/web/`）：
   - `nn.js`：WebGPU 计算着色器实现的网络推理（结果与 PyTorch 一致到 1e-5）；
   - `mctsweb.js`：批量 + 虚拟损失的树搜索，4 个 Web Worker 并行；
   - 思考时间利用：玩家部署时，AI 按「玩家现在就结束回合」的局面提前搜索；
   - `threat.js`：专门识别「铺一串工兵、把攻城锤送到大本营背后」的威胁——这是人类玩家反复击败 AI 的打法。

### 训练进展（只用网络、不混入手写评估，每步搜索 200 个局面，对手为手写大师）

| 代数 | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 15 | 18 | 21 | 24 | 27 | 30 | 33 | 36 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 胜率 | 33% | 50% | 33% | 27% | 43% | 49% | 42% | 62% | 60% | 79% | 82% | **94%** |

第 21 代之后加入了：持续训练候选网络、与大师/脚本进攻者的对局、玩家对局数据、胜率目标与搜索估计的混合。宗师实战配置（网络 + 手写威胁评估）对大师 24:0。

## 自己训练

需要 Node.js 18+、Python 3.10+、PyTorch（Apple 芯片用 MPS，NVIDIA 用 CUDA）。

```bash
python3 train/az/train.py                 # 开始或继续训练（检查点和日志在 train/az/out/）
python3 train/az/server.py 8765           # 本地服务器：http://localhost:8765/hexwar.html 会自动加载最新网络并回传对局
train/az/run_forever.sh                   # 崩溃后自动重启训练
touch train/az/out/STOP                   # 当前一代结束后停止
python3 train/az/web/build.py hexwar_base.html models/net_best.bin hexwar.html   # 把网络打包进游戏页面
```

`models/` 里是当前最强的网络（第 36 代）：`best.pt`（PyTorch）和 `net_best.bin`（浏览器用）。

# Silkiu Magnatai Fantasy Analytics App

Silkiu Magnatai Fantasy Analytics App: live EuroLeague stats with custom Fantasy Points. Results, live games with box scores, upcoming fixtures, season leaders, every player's game log, history against any opponent over past seasons, and standings.

blackworm86/eftaios.readme:
# EFTAIOS Companion

Web companion for the physical board game *Escape from the Aliens in Outer Space* (Black Edition maps: Galilei, Fermi, Galvani). Cards are **not** included: you keep using the real deck. The app replaces the paper map and pencil:

- hex map with pan / pinch-zoom, reachable sectors highlighted (Human 1, Alien 2, fed Alien 3, Adrenaline 2)
- your private route with turn numbers, 39-turn counter
- exact wording to announce (noise, silence, attack, hatch), item and attack helpers
- shared-table notes: announcements heard, hatch status, Spotlight range warning
- Basic, Advanced and Infection rule sets; map editor / import / export; offline (PWA)

Run: `python3 -m http.server` in this folder and open http://localhost:8000.

Map format (`maps/maps.json`): `rows_data` is 14 strings of 23 characters (row 01..14, columns A..W): `.` dangerous, `s` secure, `x` empty space, `H` human, `A` alien, `1`-`4` hatches.

## Playing

1. **Host** taps *Host a table*, picks map and rules, and shares the code, QR or link.
2. **Players** join, then each draws a Character card from the physical deck and picks Human or Alien in the app (never shared with anyone).
3. When everybody is *Ready* the host taps *Start game*; a random first player is announced.

**Turns:** the host arranges the order of play in the lobby; only the player whose turn it is can act, and everyone else sees whose turn it is. Eliminated or escaped players are skipped, and the host can skip an absent player.

**Digital cards (full online):** pick *Digital cards* when creating the table. The host device deals the 8 Character cards and shuffles the 25 Sector, 12 Item and 6 Escape Hatch cards, tracks the draw and discard piles and reshuffles the discards when a pile runs out. Items, Spotlights and attacks are resolved automatically (Defense is played for you, Spotlight positions are revealed, attacks after movement). Positions and routes stay on each device; the host must keep the app open while playing.

**Pass and play:** *Pass and play (one device)* on the start screen lets 2–8 players share one phone or tablet with digital cards. After each turn a hand-over screen hides everything until the next player taps their name; roles, routes and items stay private per player.

**Map markers:** each player has a colour; the border shows the faction you suspect (black = you, yellow = undecided, blue = Human, red = Alien). Your bluffs (noise announced away from where you really are) appear as semi-transparent markers in your colour with the turn number. Tap a player on the map strip to see only their timeline.

Offline or without Firebase, *Play without a table* works on a single device.

Tests: serve the folder on port 8123 and run `node tests/lobby.test.js`, `tests/turns.test.js`, `tests/online.test.js`, `tests/online2.test.js`, `tests/hot.test.js`, `tests/markers.test.js`, `tests/overlap.test.js`, `tests/undo.test.js` and `tests/close.test.js` (uses an in-memory Firebase stand-in, `tests/fake-firebase.js`).

## Deploy: GitHub Pages + Firebase

**GitHub Pages**: *Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions*. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes on every push.

**Firebase** (Realtime Database): enable *Authentication → Anonymous*, create the database, put the web config in `firebase-config.js`, publish `database.rules.json` (Realtime Database → Rules), and add `<user>.github.io` under *Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains*. The rules must be re-published whenever `database.rules.json` changes.

jrmorgan18/word-quest.desc: Word Quest — a vocabulary adventure game for kids
jrmorgan18/word-quest.readme:
# Word Quest — Brooks's Vocabulary Adventure

A tablet-friendly vocabulary game for a strong first-grade reader. Brooks explores three new words each week through six activity types, takes a weekly quiz and a next-day Memory Check, earns original stickers, and decorates Dinosaur Island, Space Explorer, and Pixel Arcade scenes.

The app is a static web app/PWA. There's no backend, no accounts, no ads, and no external AI or paid services.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173 (add --host to open it from a tablet on your Wi-Fi)
npm test             # 72 unit tests (Vitest)
npx playwright install chromium webkit   # one-time
npm run test:e2e     # 14 browser tests: Android tablet (Chromium) + iPad (WebKit)
npm run build        # static site in dist/
npm run preview      # serve dist/ locally
```

## Deploying

`npm run build` produces a fully static `dist/` folder that uses relative paths and hash routing. You can upload it to any static host (Netlify drop, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, a NAS) with no server configuration.

HTTPS is required for offline/PWA install (localhost is exempt).

**On the iPad:** open the site in Safari → Share → **Add to Home Screen**. After the first load, the game works offline.

## How the learning loop works

1. **Discover**: each word has a discovery card with a mystery clue, a meaning reveal, a second example in a different setting, a thinking question about the illustration, a word family, and a discussion prompt.
2. **Practice**: Choose the Meaning, Complete the Story, Word Detective (meaning from context, correct usage, what a character meant), Word Connections (synonym matching, "persistent vs. stubborn" nuance sorting, same/opposite sorting, word families), and Creative Challenge (self-confirmed, never graded).
3. **Weekly quiz** unlocks after all 3 words are discovered and each word has 2 *different* practice games (Creative is a bonus and doesn't count).
   - 9 questions, 3 per word, mixed formats, at least one application question per word.
   - Answer positions are randomized.
   - Pass: ≥8/9 and ≥2/3 per word. This awards the 3 word stickers and a weekly achievement.
4. **Memory Check** opens 20 hours later: 6 new questions, 2 per word. Pass: ≥5/6 and ≥1 per word. This masters the week, awards the giant week sticker, and unlocks the next week.
5. **Missed quiz**: supportive feedback per word, a targeted Quick Refresher for only the missed words, and a fresh question variation next time. Nothing is ever taken away.
6. **Spaced review (Memory Mission)**: mastered words come back after 1 → 3 → 7 → 14 → 30 days.
   - A miss shows a refresher, steps the word back, and makes it due tomorrow.
   - Words with more misses are prioritized.
   - Mastery and stickers are never removed.

Quiz content (application scenarios, situations, later example sentences, synonym/antonym and definition questions) is kept **separate** from practice content, and quiz retakes prefer never-seen questions. All thresholds and intervals are configurable defaults in the parent dashboard, not research-mandated cutoffs.

Sessions are designed to be short. After about 4 activities or a quiz, Home suggests a natural stopping point. There are no timers, streaks, or leaderboards.

## Grown-ups dashboard

Tap **🔒 Grown-ups**. This is a family gate to keep little fingers out, **not** security.

- **Set a PIN** (Settings → Grown-ups PIN, 4–8 digits). Once set, the gate asks for it, and 3 wrong tries pause entry for 30 seconds. The PIN is saved as a salted hash, not plain digits.
- **No PIN yet:** the gate asks a two-digit × two-digit multiplication question, and the dashboard reminds you to set a PIN.
- **Forgot the PIN?** The gate's link asks a three-digit × two-digit problem that removes the PIN. Progress is never affected.

- **Overview**: current week, words due for review, words needing attention, Memory Check timing, and storage status.
- **Weeks & Words**: per-word status, practice done, struggle score, review date, and every quiz attempt with per-word scores. From here you can:
  - mark a word or week complete
  - unlock or relock weeks
  - open a Memory Check now
  - reset a week's quizzes (history is kept and marked "reset"; stickers are kept)
- **Curriculum**:
  - edit any word's definition, examples, synonyms, prompts, etc.
  - add or replace words
  - add weeks beyond 10
  - Edited words are flagged and protected from future built-in content updates; learning history is never touched.
- **Settings**: name, sound, read-aloud and speed, animations (follow device / calm / full), mastery thresholds, and review intervals.
- **Backup**: export progress + curriculum (or curriculum only) as JSON, import with confirmation, and reset everything (double confirmation).

## Persistence and backups

- All state is one versioned JSON document in **IndexedDB** (falls back to `localStorage` if IndexedDB is unavailable). Saves are debounced and flushed when the tab is hidden or closed.
- **Progress is stored per browser, per device.** Two tablets do **not** sync. To move progress, use Backup → *Export* on one device and *Import* on the other.
- Safari can evict data for websites that haven't been used for a while. Installing to the Home Screen avoids this, and the dashboard can request persistent storage. Exporting a backup occasionally is still wise.
- **Schema migrations** (`src/engine/migrations.ts`): saved documents carry `schemaVersion` and are upgraded step by step on load or import, then normalized.
- **Curriculum migrations**: when `CURRICULUM_VERSION` is bumped, new words and weeks are merged in and unedited words are refreshed. Parent-edited words, week word lists, and all progress are preserved.

## Historical progress (Weeks 1–2)

On first launch, Weeks 1 and 2 are marked complete with source **parent-confirmed**:

- No quiz scores or dates are invented (`masteredAt: null`, no attempts).
- Their 6 word stickers and 2 weekly stickers are g
