jeffcampbell/Pumpkin-Carving-Party-Game.desc: Carve 3D jack-o-lanterns in the browser, share them, and play a timed carving party game
jeffcampbell/Pumpkin-Carving-Party-Game.readme:
# 🎃 Pumpkin Carving Party Game

Carve a 3D jack-o-lantern in the browser, light it with any candle color, set it
in a spooky scene, and share it with a link. Or get up to 8 friends into a room,
carve the same prompt against the clock, and vote for the best one.

The app calls itself **Pumpkin Patch** in its header.

![Carving during a party game round](docs/images/game-carving.jpg)

## Features

- **Real carving tools:** saw, drill, shape cutters (eyes, grins, stars, bats and
  more), an etcher that shaves the skin so it glows (pass over it again to go
  deeper, until you break through), and a patch tool to undo mistakes locally.
- **Physics-ish pieces:** anything you cut loose falls out and lands on the table.
  Undo rewinds it back into place.
- **Candle light that behaves like a candle:** light escapes only through what you
  carved, so the face is projected onto the scene around it.
- **Six scenes:** kitchen table, witch's cottage, graveyard, pumpkin patch, front
  porch and a plain studio. They're all drawn in code, so there are no image assets.
- **Save and share without accounts:** each pumpkin gets a short link with a
  preview image. Only the browser that made it can edit it, and anyone else gets
  a remix.
- **Party game:** room codes, easy-to-carve prompts ("A lazy cat") from a category
  the host picks (animals, jobs, moods, monsters, food, things, random, or the
  host's own custom list), configurable carving time (default 2 minutes) and
  votes per player (default 3), anonymous voting, results, and rematches.
- **Stats page:** `/stats` (the 👻 in the menu) shows pumpkins carved, visitors,
  parties and votes, with a 30-night candle chart, favorite scenes and candle
  colors. Visitors are counted without cookies.

![The six scenes](docs/images/scenes.jpg)

## Quick start

Requires Node 20 or later (20.6+ for `--env-file`).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000 (API, game server and Vite hot reload)
npm test         # unit and integration tests
```

Without a `DATABASE_URL`, saved pumpkins are kept in memory and lost on restart,
which is fine for trying it out. To use Postgres locally, copy `.env.example` to
`.env`, fill it in, and run `node --env-file=.env server/index.js --dev`.

## Documentation

| Doc | What's in it |
|-----|--------------|
| [How to play](docs/how-to-play.md) | Carving tools, shortcuts, saving and sharing, running a party game |
| [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | How carving, rendering, falling pieces and scenes work; data model; REST and WebSocket APIs |
| [Deploying](docs/deploying.md) | Supabase and Railway setup, environment variables, health checks, scaling notes |

## Stack

One small Node process does everything, which keeps hosting cheap:

- **Client:** vanilla JavaScript and [Three.js](https://threejs.org), bundled by
  Vite (about 175 KB gzipped).
- **Server:** Express 5 for the REST API and static files, plus `ws` for game rooms.
- **Database:** Postgres on Supabase through the plain `pg` driver. There's one
  table, and the server creates or migrates it on startup.

```
server/
  index.js         HTTP server, link-preview tags for /p/:id, Vite middleware in dev
  stats.js         counters and visitor counting for /stats
  pumpkins.js      REST API for saved pumpkins
  store.js         Postgres store, or in-memory when DATABASE_URL is unset
  validate.js      payload checks shared by the API and the game
  game/rooms.js    room state machine (lobby → carving → voting → results)
  game/socket.js   WebSocket transport at /ws
  game/prompts.js  prompt word lists and picking
shared/            scene and prompt-category lists used by client and server
src/
  pumpkin/         geometry, shaders, carving mask, tools, falling pieces, scenes
  ui/workbench.js  carving UI shared by solo mode and the game
  pages/           editor (/, /edit/:id), viewer (/p/:id), /mine, /game, /stats
  game/client.js   WebSocket client with automatic reconnect
db/schema.sql      table definition (applied automatically)
railway.json       Railway build and deploy settings
.github/workflows/ keep-awake ping for the free Supabase project
test/              node:test suites
docs/              documentation and screenshots
```

## Deploying

It runs on Railway (app) and Supabase (database) for about $5 a month.
[`railway.json`](railway.json) holds the deploy settings: build, health check
at `/healthz`, app sleeping when idle, and resource caps. A GitHub Action
([`keep-awake.yml`](.github/workflows/keep-awake.yml)) pings the app every 3
days so the free Supabase project isn't paused. See
[docs/deploying.md](docs/deploying.md) for the full setup.

derikatwork/f4mm-linux.readme:
# BETH Mod Manager

A mod manager for Bethesda games (Fallout 4, Skyrim Special Edition, Fallout: New
Vegas, Fallout 3, Oblivion, Starfield, Skyrim LE) installed through **Lutris/Wine**
on Linux. You pick an archive you downloaded from Nexus Mods with "Manual
Download"; the app works out which game it is for and where its files belong,
and (from phase 2 on) installs it by linking files into the game folder, so the
game folder can always be returned to vanilla.

## Status

The project is built in phases:

| Phase | What | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Game discovery, placement rules, tests, read-only CLI | **done** |
| 2 | Staging, deploy/undeploy with symlinks, manifest, CLI | next |
| 3 | Desktop GUI (PySide6) | |
| 4 | FOMOD installer, plugins.txt management | |

**Phase 1 never changes your game folders.** Every command in this phase only reads.

## Install (Ubuntu and Ubuntu-based: Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin, ...)

### 1. System packages

You need Python 3.11 or newer and the `7z` program.

Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux Mint 22 / Pop!_OS 24.04 and newer (Python 3.12 included):

```bash
sudo add-apt-repository multiverse     # 7zip-rar lives here; harmless if already enabled
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3-venv git 7zip 7zip-rar
```

Ubuntu 22.04 / Linux Mint 21 / Pop!_OS 22.04 ship Python 3.10, so also install 3.11:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-venv git p7zip-full p7zip-rar
```

(`7zip-rar` / `p7zip-rar` add `.rar` support. `.zip` and `.7z` work without them.)

Check with `python3 --version` (or `python3.11 --version`) and `7z | head -2`.

### 2. The app

```bash
git clone https://github.com/derikatwork/f4mm-linux.git
cd f4mm-linux
python3 -m venv .venv            # on 22.04-based systems: python3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'
```

Run it with `.venv/bin/bethmm ...`, or make it available everywhere:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
ln -s "$PWD/.venv/bin/bethmm" ~/.local/bin/bethmm   # ~/.local/bin is on PATH on Ubuntu after re-login
```

## Using phase 1

### Find your games

```bash
bethmm games            # uses the cached result after the first run
bethmm games --rescan   # search again
```

Games are found by:

* scanning `~/Games` (Lutris's default install folder) for `Fallout4.exe`,
  `SkyrimSE.exe`, `TESV.exe`, `FalloutNV.exe`, `Fallout3.exe`, `Oblivion.exe` and
  `Starfield.exe`;
* reading Lutris's own records — `~/.local/share/lutris/games/*.yml`,
  `~/.config/lutris/games/*.yml`, `~/.local/share/lutris/pga.db`, and the same
  files of the **Flatpak** Lutris under `~/.var/app/net.lutris.Lutris/` — so games
  installed elsewhere are found too.

For each game it shows the game folder, Data folder, Wine prefix, Wine user, the
`plugins.txt` location inside the prefix (GOG Skyrim SE uses
`AppData/Local/Skyrim Special Edition GOG`), and the store it detected.

If something is wrong or missing, set it by hand:

```bash
bethmm override fallout4 --root "~/Games/fallout-4/drive_c/GOG Games/Fallout 4 GOTY"
bethmm override fallout4 --prefix ~/Games/fallout-4
bethmm override skyrimse --ignore          # hide a game
bethmm override fallout4 --clear           # back to automatic
bethmm config --games-dir /mnt/games       # scan a different Lutris folder
```

### See where a mod would go

```bash
bethmm analyze ~/Downloads/"Some Mod-1234-1-2-1700000000.7z"
bethmm analyze ~/Downloads/SomeMod.zip --game fallout4   # check against a specific game
bethmm analyze ~/Downloads/SomeMod.zip --json
```

This extracts the archive to a temporary folder inside
`~/.local/share/beth-mod-manager/tmp`, then prints:

* the mod name, version and Nexus mod ID taken from the file name;
* which game it is for, how sure it is, and why (plugin masters, script extender
  loader names, ...);
* which rule placed it (Data folder / Data content / game-root content / FOMOD /
  unknown) and how confident that is;
* every file's destination **in your real game folder**, with case matched to the
  folders that already exist (a mod's `Textures/` goes into your existing
  `textures/`), and which files would replace vanilla files;
* files that won't be installed (readmes, screenshots, script extender source code).

The temporary extraction is deleted afterwards.

When the layout isn't recognised (or the archive is a FOMOD installer), the mod's
files are shown as a tree together with the folders that look installable. Preview
your own choice of root folder and target — still without changing anything:

```bash
bethmm analyze SomeMod.7z --root "00 Core" --root "01 Optional" --target data
bethmm analyze SomeMod.7z --target game     # detected root, but into the game folder
```

`--root` can be given several times (later ones win where files overlap);
`--target` is `data` (the Data folder) or `game` (next to the game's `.exe`).
Without `--target`, each root's place is detected on its own.

### Look inside a plugin

```bash
bethmm plugin-info SomeMod.esp
```

Prints the plugin's masters, header version and the game it was made for.

## Where things are kept

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Settings | `~/.config/beth-mod-manager/settings.json` |
| Game discovery cache | `~/.local/share/beth-mod-manager/games.json` |
| Log of every file operation (settings/cache writes, extractions, temp folders) | `~/.local/share/beth-mod-manager/logs/bethmm.log` |
| Staged mods (phase 2) | `~/.local/share/beth-mod-manager/mods/<game>/<mod>/` |
| Backups of replaced vanilla files (phase 2) | `~/.local/share/beth-mod-manager/backups/<game>/` |

## Running the tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest
```

The tests build fake game folders, fake Lutris configs and fake mod layouts in
temporary directories; they never touch your real home folder or games.

## How mods are placed

The rules live in `bethmm/placement.py` and are applied in order:

1. **Wrapper folders** — a single unrecognised top-level folder such as
   `CoolMod v1.2/` is stepped into (repeatedly). Loose readmes next to it are ignored.
2. **FO

# Ayvago

Retro aksiyon, casual ve bulmaca oyunlarını tek çatı altında toplayan web oyun platformu — [ayvago.com](https://ayvago.com).

## Durum

**Faz 0 — Hazırlık.** Monorepo iskeleti, CI, Firebase güvenlik kuralı tabanı ve oyun manifest şeması hazır.
Yol haritası: [`docs/plan/yol-haritasi.md`](docs/plan/yol-haritasi.md) · Oyun import planı: [`docs/plan/oyun-import-plani.md`](docs/plan/oyun-import-plani.md) · Faz 0 kontrol listesi: [`docs/setup/faz-0.md`](docs/setup/faz-0.md)

## Yapı

```
apps/web            Next.js platform uygulaması (Vercel)
packages/shared     Ortak tipler ve zod şemaları (ayvago.json oyun manifesti)
firebase/           Firebase yapılandırması ve güvenlik kuralları
docs/               Yol haritası, ADR'ler, kurulum kontrol listeleri
```

## Geliştirme

Gereksinimler: Node 22, pnpm 10 (`corepack enable`).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # http://localhost:3000
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

Ortam değişkenleri için `apps/web/.env.example` dosyasını `apps/web/.env.local` olarak kopyalayın. Gerçek anahtarlar asla commit edilmez.

## Deploy

Vercel projesinde **Root Directory** = `apps/web`. Firebase kuralları `firebase/` klasöründen `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,database,storage` ile yayınlanır.

# Stargame – Sternen-Legespiel

Ein Legespiel für eine Person im Browser: Sieben farbige Sternteile (3–4 Sterne je Teil) werden in eine Form mit 26 Plätzen (Reihen zu 7/6/7/6) gelegt, bis kein Platz mehr frei ist.

## Spielen

`index.html` im Browser öffnen – es gibt keine weiteren Dateien oder Abhängigkeiten.

## Schwierigkeitsstufen

| Stufe   | Vorgabe                                          |
|---------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Starter | 4 Teile liegen fest, 3 sind zu legen             |
| Junior  | 3 Teile liegen fest, 4 sind zu legen             |
| Expert  | 2 Teile liegen fest, 5 sind zu legen             |
| Wizard  | nur 3 farbige Einzelsterne, alle 7 Teile legen   |

Jedes Rätsel wird zufällig erzeugt und hat genau eine Lösung. Teile lassen sich wie im echten Spiel nur drehen, nicht spiegeln.

## Bedienung

- Teil aufs Brett ziehen – es rastet ein, wo es passt; vom Brett wegziehen legt es zurück.
- Antippen wählt ein Teil aus, nochmal antippen dreht es (oder Taste `R`, Mausrad beim Ziehen).
- **Tipp** legt ein richtiges Teil, **Lösung** zeigt alles, **Zurücklegen** räumt das Brett ab.

# tictactoe-lab

running an epic through task-flow with two models: one builds a task, the other
reviews it.

## Запуск

Игра для двух человек за одним терминалом: X ходит первым, ход — номер
клетки 1–9 и Enter.

```bash
python3 -m tictactoe
```

## Тесты

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

hermes98761234/browser-arcade.desc: Free browser game platform — 3000 games you can play instantly, no login
hermes98761234/browser-arcade.readme:
# Browser Arcade

A free browser game platform with **3000 games** you can play instantly — arcade classics, puzzles, strategy, racing, sports, music toys and hand-written interactive stories. No registration, no login, no downloads, no tracking: everything runs on a static GitHub Pages site and your scores stay in your browser.

**▶ Play now: https://hermes98761234.github.io/browser-arcade/**

[![Deploy](https://github.com/hermes98761234/browser-arcade/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hermes98761234/browser-arcade/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)

![Browser Arcade catalog](docs/screenshot.png)

## Features

- **3000-game catalog** with 50 games per page, live search and filters: genre, visual style, gameplay type, era (year the genre was born), 2D/3D, players, controls, difficulty and the 120 themed collections.
- **Canvas preview image** for every game, drawn from the game's own engine and theme.
- **Story games** with hand-written branching plots and multiple endings.
- Favorites, recently played and personal best scores (stored locally).
- Keyboard, mouse and touch controls with an on-screen gamepad on phones; local two-player modes.
- English and Ukrainian interface, dark and light themes, fullscreen play.

## Game engines

46 engines, each with variants picked from the game's own description:

| Group | Engines |
|---|---|
| Arcade & action | snake, brick breaker, shoot 'em up / bullet hell, twin-stick & .io arenas, dodge & catch, one-button flyer & lunar lander, reflex & timing, endless runner, platformer (procedural levels), fighting, paddle sports |
| 3D | three.js flight, raycaster mazes & dungeons, pseudo-3D racing |
| Puzzle | match-3, sliding & pipe puzzles, memory & spot-the-difference, minesweeper / nonogram / sudoku / akari / binairo, 2048 & merge, Lights Out / Flood-It / lasers, mazes & flow lines, sokoban, falling blocks & polyomino packing, stacking, ball sort, chain reaction, escape rooms |
| Strategy & sim | tower defense, Galcon-style conquest, turn-based tactics & auto-battler, idle tycoon / farming / trading, Reigns-style decision cards, Oregon-Trail-style journeys, roguelike dungeons |
| Cards & board | solitaire, blackjack, video poker, deck-builder, lane battler; chess (alpha-beta AI), checkers, reversi, connect four, go, mancala, gomoku… |
| Words & learning | wordle, crossword, hangman, ciphers, spelling hive, word search, typing shooter, quizzes (math, geography, science, languages, trivia), Lightbot-style programming |
| Creative & music | drawing with symmetry, falling sand, generative art, pixel art, step sequencer, piano, theremin, procedurally composed rhythm game |
| Stories | 10 hand-written branching stories (40–60 scenes, 5–7 endings each) |

Every engine works with keyboard, mouse and touch, and adapts to portrait phone screens.

## How it works

The game list lives in [`data/games.md`](data/games.md): 3000 one-line game designs in 120 collections. `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` parses it into `src/data/raw.json`, and `src/lib/catalog.ts` classifies every entry — from its name, description and build notes — into one of the gameplay **engines** in `src/engines/games/`, a visual **theme** (palette + sprite set), a genre and a set of variant flags (`gravity`, `boss`, `dark`, `versus`, …). Each game runs its engine with its own theme, flags and random seed, so games that share mechanics still look and play differently. Engines are lazy-loaded, so the catalog stays fast.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm test         # catalog, classifier and i18n tests
npm run build    # static site in dist/
```

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

kapilsid/KemEveryDay.readme:
# Kemistri Everyday

Standalone Android app for EdBetter with application ID `uk.edbetter.kemdaily`.

The application intentionally runs in portrait orientation. Its board, discovery tray, daily cards, and one-handed controls are designed around a consistent portrait play area.

## Run in Android Studio

1. Open the **`KemistriEveryday` folder itself** in Android Studio (not the parent `StudioProjects` folder).
2. Allow the Gradle sync to finish. The project uses Android Gradle Plugin 8.9.3, Gradle 8.11.1, JDK 17, and compile SDK 36.
3. In **Settings › Build, Execution, Deployment › Build Tools › Gradle**, select Android Studio's embedded JDK 17 if no Gradle JDK is selected.
4. Open **Tools › Device Manager** and start an API 36 phone. On this development machine, `Medium_Phone_API_36` is ready to use.
5. Select the shared **Kemistri Everyday** run configuration and press Run. Android Studio will build, install, and open the default activity.

The `.run` directory provides three shared configurations:

- **Kemistri Everyday** — install and launch the app on the selected device.
- **Unit Tests** — run the pure Kotlin chemistry and game tests.
- **Emulator Smoke Test** — launch the app instrumentation test on the selected emulator.

If Android Studio asks for the SDK location, create `local.properties` containing your own SDK path:

```properties
sdk.dir=/path/to/Android/sdk
```

`local.properties` is intentionally excluded from source control because it is machine-specific.

## Command line

Open this directory in Android Studio, or run:

```bash
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug
```

The debug APK is written to `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`.

To start the configured API 36 emulator, run all JVM and instrumented smoke tests, and leave the app open:

```bash
./scripts/emulator-smoke-test.sh
```

Pass a different installed AVD name as the first argument when required:

```bash
./scripts/emulator-smoke-test.sh Pixel_9
```

## Implemented MVP

- Pure Kotlin chemistry engine with nested formula parsing and order-independent composition matching.
- Versioned offline library of 127 known substances, two-to-three-sentence notes, all 118 element symbols, explicit isomer ambiguity, and no composition-to-structure overclaiming.
- Deterministic 5×5 Molecule Hunt engine: eight-direction paths, swipe or tap selection, backtracking, scoring, repeats, streaks, gravity, caps, hints, and shuffle recovery.
- Standard 10-in-20 mission and reproducible UTC daily seed.
- Compose home, hunt, discovery reveal, completion/result, daily, interactive Everyday Chemistry, pending-review, and settings screens.
- Science Uncovered: one resumable three-life run per UTC day, drawn from 25 mysteries across scientists, elements, scientific places, discoveries, and instruments. A letter reveals every matching position, correct solutions preserve every life and add up to 100 points to the cumulative run score, while incorrect letters and skips cost a life. The final score locks when the lives are exhausted; the device retains the daily state and personal best for a future server-enforced online leaderboard.
- Science Leaders provides today's live/final score, anonymous Firebase identity, editable public nickname, worldwide daily ranking and device-local fallback. Server-enforced one-score-per-day setup and deployment are documented in `docs/FIREBASE_LEADERBOARD.md`.
- Element a Day covers the full 118-element periodic table with a deterministic daily selection, atomic data, table position, uses, and a short explanatory story.
- Discoveries belong to the current hunt and reset with a new game; there is no persistent collection.
- Device-local active-game restore, pending-review counts, and settings.
- Daily Board history and streak calendar: best result per UTC board date, current and best streaks, a Monday-first month calendar, and stale saved Daily games discarded at the UTC rollover.
- Accessibility descriptions, numbered selections, 48dp controls, live chemical symbols, and reduced-motion preference.
- Google AdMob interstitials with the UMP consent prompt, shown only when a finished board is left (at most one every three minutes), never during a hunt. Pending formulas never leave the device.

The catalogue model, gameplay/reference split, scientific caveats and source conventions are documented in `docs/CHEMISTRY_LIBRARY.md`.

## Google Play release

Release builds are shrunk with R8 and signed from an untracked `keystore.properties` (copy `keystore.properties.example`). Store listing text, the 512px icon, the feature graphic and phone screenshots are in `app/src/main/playstore/`, the privacy policy is `docs/privacy-policy.html`, and `docs/PLAY_RELEASE.md` has the step-by-step Play Console answers.

## Production gates

The brief is retained at `docs/DEVELOPMENT_SPEC.md`. Before store release:

- Replace the lightweight preferences repository with the specified Room schema and add migrations.
- Expand expert-reviewed chemistry/content provenance and localisation resources.
- Prove 10-discovery mission reachability over 10,000+ complete simulated sessions. Current generation guarantees a playable initial board and recovers dead boards, but does not claim the stronger full-mission mathematical guarantee.
- Add consent-compliant monetisation, analytics adapters, audio, and the optional special-lattice mode.
- Review and export the generated icon source into final adaptive production artwork and complete the illustration/audio inventory.

## Visual asset

The generated 1024px mascot source is `app/src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/kemistri_everyday_icon_source.png`. The launcher currently uses a small deterministic vector foreground for adaptive-icon safety.

The approved 1024px branded home/splash artwork is `app/src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/kemistri_everyday_brand.png`. Its embedded wordmark is used at display size, while the text-free mascot remains the adaptive launcher treatment so the icon stays legible

Olusive/firefly-dash.readme:
# Firefly Dash

A one-tap pixel-art phone game: flutter a firefly through ten glowing worlds, collect sparks, and spend them on power-ups.

Installable web app (PWA): open the hosted link on your phone, then **Add to Home Screen** (iPhone: Safari → Share; Android: Chrome → ⋮ → Install app). Runs full-screen and works offline after the first visit.

after a spark, the next 3-6 pillars stay empty (Spark Storm shortens it,

# Meridian Daily

A daily geography game. Each day brings ten prompts, three in calm seas (easy), four in choppy waters (medium) and three in stormy seas (hard), such as "Name a country that borders Germany" or "Name a strait". Any correct answer counts, and rarer answers earn more leagues. Your ship sails Columbus's 1492 route from Palos to La Navidad as you score.

Everything is in `index.html`: no build step, no dependencies.

## Hosting

This repository is served by GitHub Pages from the `main` branch root. Pushing to `main` updates the site.

## Scoring on this site

Rarity is scored against a built-in estimate of how often people give each answer. Your progress, streak and stats are saved in your browser.

The version hosted on claude.ai also pools every player's answers to measure real rarity. That needs a shared database; to add one here, connect a backend such as Supabase and replace the `connect()` and `savePicks()` functions in `index.html`.

# Koníčci

Dětská hra pro Android (6–11 let) o péči o koníčky a procházkách barevným světem.

- Herní návrh a plán: [docs/herni-navrh.md](docs/herni-navrh.md)

## Spuštění

1. Stáhni [Godot 4.4](https://godotengine.org/download) (standardní verze, ne .NET).
2. V Godotu otevři `project.godot` a stiskni F5.

Zatím je ve hře:

- **Stáj:** krmení, voda, mrkev, česání, úklid koblížků; až 4 koníci, každý se svým jménem a barvou.
- **Zahrádka:** z uklizeného hnoje vyrostou mrkve.
- **Album objevů, obchůdek s ozdobami a nastavení pro rodiče.**
- **Mapa světa:** louka s potůčkem, březový lesík, rybníček a Kouzelný les (další místa se odemykají procházkami).
- **Procházka shora:** dítě koníka vede (jde vedle něj s vodítkem) nebo na něm jede, sbírá jablka, kytičky a podkovy a potkává zvířátka.
- **Objevy:** keříky s překvapením, ukryté poklady, úkoly, déšť s duhou, světlušky, Kouzelný les s jednorožcem.
- **Zvuky a hudba:** zatím syntetizované skriptem `tools/make_sounds.py`.

Grafika je zatím jen zástupná, kreslená kódem.

## Instalace do tabletu

Po každém nahrání změn GitHub sám sestaví instalační soubor:

1. Na GitHubu otevři záložku **Actions**, vyber poslední běh „Sestavení APK“.
2. Dole v části **Artifacts** stáhni `konicci-apk` (je to zip, uvnitř je `konicci.apk`).
3. Soubor přenes do tabletu a otevři ho. Android se zeptá na povolení instalace z neznámých zdrojů, to je potřeba povolit.

Aktualizace se instaluje stejně, uložená hra zůstane zachována.

## Test

```
godot --headless --script res://tests/smoke_test.gd
```

srmrpapitas/Terror-game-.readme:
# Última Compra

Un juego de terror cooperativo para 1 a 4 amigos: entráis de noche en un supermercado cerrado, tenéis que llenar la cesta con la lista de la compra y salir por las cajas antes de que el monstruo os atrape. Se juega en el navegador, en PC y en móvil.

## Cómo jugar

1. Uno crea la partida y comparte el enlace (o el código de 4 letras).
2. Los demás entran con el enlace o escriben el código y pulsan **Unirse**.
3. El anfitrión pulsa **Empezar**.

| Acción | PC | Móvil |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moverse | WASD | Joystick izquierdo |
| Mirar | Ratón (clic para capturarlo) | Deslizar en la mitad derecha |
| Correr | Shift | Botón Correr, o joystick al borde |
| Agacharse | C | Botón Agachar |
| Linterna | F | Botón Linterna |
| Coger producto | E | Botón Coger (aparece al estar cerca) |

**El monstruo:** no ve en la oscuridad: te oye si te mueves con el carrito y ve tu linterna si le apuntas con ella (si apunta a otro lado, solo de muy cerca) (corriendo 16 m, andando 7 m, agachado 3 m) y ve la luz de tu linterna. Si te quedas totalmente quieto no te ataca, aunque lo tengas delante... pero cada 15 segundos o así se te escapa una tos que se oye a 8 m. Agachado y sin moverte te confundes con las estanterías: no te ve ni te ataca y la tos se ahoga. De espaldas no se entera de que pasas a su lado, y cuando te ve tarda casi un segundo en lanzarse (ruge y se gira): si corres en ese momento, puedes escapar. Corre más que tú, pero cada 5 segundos de persecución se para y gira 360° buscando objetivos: es el momento de esconderse tras una estantería o quedarse quieto. Si doblas una esquina y deja de verte, va a donde te vio por última vez y desde ahí solo te sigue por el oído, más despacio. Cuantos más productos de la lista os lleváis, más se enfada: corre más, oye más lejos y persigue más rato. Si te atrapa, susto y pasas a ser fantasma hasta la siguiente ronda.

## La Cena (segundo juego)

En la sala, el anfitrión elige **Supermercado** o **La Cena**. En La Cena estáis sentados a la mesa, unos enfrente de otros, con un plato de guisantes cada uno. En la cabecera, el monstruo lee el periódico. Mientras lee, carga guisantes en el tenedor (**Cargar**, o mantenerlo pulsado) y cómetelos (**Comer**). Cuando hace ruido con el periódico es que lo va a bajar: si al bajarlo te ve comiendo o con el tenedor cargado, te dispara (**Soltar** devuelve los guisantes al plato). A veces solo pasa la página. Ojo: cada pinchazo en el plato y cada bocado hacen ruido, y el ruido le hace bajar antes el periódico (y que un amago acabe en bajada de verdad). Los demás siguen hasta limpiar el plato, y al final hay clasificación: primero quien termina antes, y después los eliminados según cuánto aguantaron.

| Acción | PC | Móvil |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cargar un guisante | Clic o Espacio (mantener para varios) | Botón Cargar |
| Comer | E | Botón Comer |
| Soltar | Q | Botón Soltar |
| Mirar | Arrastrar | Arrastrar |

Los tiempos del centinela están en `DINNER` en `shared/constants.js`.

## Ejecutarlo

Necesita Node.js 18 o superior. Antes de empezar, copia el monstruo de Mixamo en `public/models/` (instrucciones en [public/models/LEEME.md](public/models/LEEME.md)); sin él se usa una figura provisional.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000 (modo desarrollo)
```

Para jugar con amigos en la misma red, abrid `http://<IP-de-tu-PC>:3000`. Para producción:

```bash
npm run build
npm start          # sirve dist/ y el servidor multijugador en el puerto $PORT (3000 por defecto)
```

Se puede desplegar tal cual en cualquier servicio que ejecute Node y permita WebSocket (Render, Railway, Fly.io...).

## Publicar en Cloudflare

En Cloudflare el juego corre como un Worker (`worker/index.js`): cada sala es un Durable Object con la misma lógica que `server/game.js`, y los archivos del juego salen de `dist/`.

1. En el panel de Cloudflare, **Workers & Pages → Create application → GitHub**, elige este repositorio y despliega. El nombre del Worker tiene que ser `terror-game` (el de `wrangler.toml`). Cada push a `main` vuelve a publicar.
2. Sube el monstruo y sus animaciones (los de `public/models/LEEME.md`) al bucket de R2 `ultima-compra-models`, en la raíz y con los mismos nombres. El Worker los sirve desde ahí.

Para probar la versión de Cloudflare en local: `npx wrangler dev`.

```bash
npm test           # pruebas del servidor: salas, productos y la IA del monstruo
```

## Estructura

| Carpeta | Qué hay |
| --- | --- |
| `shared/` | Mapa del supermercado y ajustes de juego, compartidos por cliente y servidor |
| `server/` | Servidor HTTP + WebSocket, salas y la IA del monstruo (el servidor es el árbitro) |
| `src/` | Cliente Three.js: mundo, jugador, controles táctiles, sonido y el susto |
| `public/models/` | Donde va el monstruo de Mixamo (no se sube al repo) |

Los ajustes de velocidad, ruido, visión y tiempos del monstruo están en `shared/constants.js`.

# Couchfin

[![Made with Slint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slint-ui/slint/master/logo/MadeWithSlint-logo-whitebg.png)](https://slint.dev)

A controller-first [Jellyfin](https://jellyfin.org) client for Bazzite/SteamOS
and Steam Big Picture, written in Rust with libmpv for playback and Slint for
the UI.

Couchfin is in early development. The roadmap for the first milestone is in
[docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md), and contributor conventions are in
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

## Development setup

Bazzite's root filesystem is immutable, so development happens inside the
Couchfin dev container, entered through Distrobox. Podman and Distrobox come
preinstalled on Bazzite. The container shares your home directory, display,
GPU and controllers, and CI builds and tests in the same image. See
[docs/dev-environment.md](docs/dev-environment.md) for what the image contains
and how to update it.

1. Create the box and enter it. The image is public, so no registry login is
   needed:

   ```sh
   distrobox create --name couchfin-dev --image ghcr.io/nkahlor/couchfin-dev:latest
   distrobox enter couchfin-dev
   ```

2. Check that every tool and library is present, then build and run:

   ```sh
   check-devenv
   cargo run
   ```

   This opens Couchfin fullscreen. The first time, type your server's
   address (for example `jellyfin.lan:8096`), then sign in. Home shows the
   server's name and version, who is signed in, and a carousel of
   placeholder title cards. Next time it skips straight to Home while the
   sign-in still works.

   Tab or the Up and Down arrows move between controls, Left and Right
   slide the carousel one card at a time (and move the cursor in a text
   field), Enter presses or selects, and Escape goes back.
   Escape on the address screen or on Home quits. A controller works too:
   the D-pad and left stick act as the arrows, A as Enter and B as Escape,
   through the same code ([decision 011](docs/decisions/011-home-row.md)),
   and the app falls back to the keyboard alone if SDL can't start. Logs go to
   stderr; set `RUST_LOG=debug` for more. They never include passwords or
   tokens. To diagnose input, run with `RUST_LOG=couchfin=debug`: it logs every
   controller and navigation-key event with a timestamp, and any duplicate
   it drops because Steam typed the same key ([decision 013](docs/decisions/013-steam-desktop-layout-dedupe.md)).

To try changes to the Containerfile before they're merged, build the image
locally:

```sh
podman build -t localhost/couchfin-dev -f .devcontainer/Containerfile .devcontainer
distrobox create --name couchfin-dev-local --image localhost/couchfin-dev
```

## Workspace

| Crate | Owns |
|---|---|
| [`couchfin-api`](crates/couchfin-api) | Typed Jellyfin HTTP client: auth, items, images, playback reporting |
| [`couchfin-core`](crates/couchfin-core) | App state, navigation stack, settings, image cache |
| [`couchfin-gamepad`](crates/couchfin-gamepad) | Game controllers via SDL3, mapped to one `Input` enum (the keyboard is handled in `couchfin-ui`) |
| [`couchfin-player`](crates/couchfin-player) | libmpv wrapper: load, play/pause, seek, tracks, position events |
| [`couchfin-ui`](crates/couchfin-ui) | Slint screens and components; focus handling |
| [`app`](app) | The `couchfin` binary: wires everything together, window, main loop |

`couchfin-api`, `couchfin-gamepad` and `couchfin-player` never depend on each
other or on the UI, and `couchfin-core` depends only on `couchfin-api`.
`app/tests/workspace_layout.rs` enforces this, so a forbidden dependency fails
`cargo test`.

The Rust toolchain is pinned in [rust-toolchain.toml](rust-toolchain.toml).

### Checking a real Jellyfin server

`couchfin-api` has a small example that checks a server, logs in and calls
`/Users/Me`, so you can try the client against your own server without the
UI. If the address redirects (for example a proxy sending
`http://` to `https://`), it prints the address the server really answers on
and uses that from then on. It asks for the password without echoing it and
never prints it or the token:

```sh
cargo run -p couchfin-api --example probe -- http://jellyfin.lan:8096 alice
```

Afterwards, the server's Dashboard > Devices lists "Couchfin". Each run uses a
new device ID unless `COUCHFIN_DEVICE_ID` is set to one it printed before. See
[decision 006](docs/decisions/006-api-client-design.md) for how the client is
built.

### Checking a controller

`couchfin-gamepad` has an example that prints every input from every
connected controller (Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, Menu) and logs
each connect and disconnect with the pad's name and type, so you can check a
pad without the app. Ctrl+C quits:

```sh
cargo run -p couchfin-gamepad --example gamepads
```

The D-pad and left stick repeat while held (after 400 ms, then every 60 ms).
Buttons go by position: the bottom face button selects and the right one goes
back, on every pad. Under Steam Input only Steam's virtual pad should show
up, not the physical one as well. See
[decision 012](docs/decisions/012-gamepad-mapping-and-thread.md).

### Where Couchfin keeps its data

`couchfin-core` stores the session, so a restart skips the login while the
token still works:

- `~/.config/couchfin/settings.toml` (or under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) holds the
  device ID, the server's address and the last username. It holds no
  secrets. The device ID is created on the first run and kept, so the
  server's Dashboard > Devices lists one "Couchfin".
- The access token goes in the system keyring (the Secret Service: KWallet
  or GNOME Keyring). If there is no keyring, which is common in Game Mode or
  in a container, or it doesn't answer within 3 seconds, the token goes in
  `~/.config/couchfin/tokens.toml` instead. Only you can read that file
  (mode 0600).

Sign out on Home forgets the token. To log out by hand, delete the keyring
entry for the service "Couchfin" and `tokens.toml`. See
[decision 007](docs/decisions/007-session-persistence.md).

Yashgurav002/hearsay.desc: NPCs that remember what you did, and gossip about it. A 3D game + NPC memory engine on a FalkorDB graph (Graph Hacks 2026).
Yashgurav002/hearsay.readme:
# Hearsay: *Everyone's talking about you.* **A memory engine that lets game characters remember what you did, gossip about it, and explain exactly who told whom, built on a [FalkorDB](https://www.falkordb.com/) graph.** It's playable here as a small 3D village. The same engine is a baseline for NPC memory in any open-world or story game. ### ▶ Play it live: **https://hearsay-six.vercel.app** · Repo: https://github.com/Yashgurav002/hearsay **Hackathon:** Graph Hacks: Context for AI Agents (WeMakeDevs × FalkorDB) **Tracks:** Track 02 — **Agent Memory and Coordination** (primary) · Track 01 — **Agents That Act on Connected Data** **Docs:** [How to play](docs/HOW_TO_PLAY.md) · [Reading the graph (every chart in the UI explained)](docs/READING_THE_GRAPH.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Measured results](docs/results.md) · [Decisions](DECISIONS.md) ![Third-person 3D: the inn crowd at dusk, mood rings at their feet](docs/screenshots/3d-inn.png) ## Why this is a baseline for NPC memory in any game The village is a demo. The reusable part is the engine underneath: **a graph that stores what every character saw, what they've heard, from whom, and how sure they are, and spreads it realistically.** Any game where characters should react to the player's reputation can sit on top of it, whether that's a GTA-style city, a Witcher-style fantasy world, a western, or a small social sim. ### What games usually do today, and what the graph adds | Typical approach | Its limit | With a Hearsay-style graph | |---|---|---| | One **reputation / honour meter** per player or region | Everyone "knows" at once; nobody knows *why* | Each character has their **own** belief, with a confidence and a **source** | | **Witnesses** report a crime and a bounty appears | Instant and global, then it resets | News travels **person to person, along trust**, and takes time to reach the next town | | Scripted barks ("I heard about you…") | The same line everywhere, unrelated to what really happened | Lines come from the character's actual belief, and stories **exaggerate** as they're retold | | Reputation fixed by waiting or paying a fine | No gameplay in repairing it | You repair it by **convincing the right people**, which is a puzzle over the social network | | Debugging "why does this NPC hate me?" | Hard to trace | One query returns the exact chain: *Ilsa ← Bertha ← Tomas (saw it)* | The graph does work a single number or a list can't: - a **variable-length path** gives provenance (who told whom); - **trust edges** decide who hears what; - **PageRank**, **communities** and **shortest paths** tell the game (or the player) who matters and how a story will travel. ### What it could look like in an open world (design sketches) - **Crime city (GTA-style):** a shop clerk sees a robbery and tells their cousin, who runs with a gang. The gang now prices you differently, while the police only hear the version that reached an informant, three hops and two exaggerations later. A *fixer* character uses shortest-path to plant a cover story. - **Fantasy RPG (Witcher-style):** you kill a monster outside a village. The innkeeper turns it into "slew a griffin bare-handed", a travelling bard carries it to the next town, and a sceptical alderman (needs two sources) still doesn't believe it. Ask "Why?" and he names the bard. - **Western / honour system:** a stranger sees you help a rancher. The sheriff, who trusts the rancher, softens toward you before you've met. A bounty hunter who trusts nobody ignores it. - **Detective or social games:** tracing a rumour back to its source *is* the gameplay: the provenance query is the mechanic. ### How a game would plug it in ```mermaid flowchart LR G["Game engine
(Unity · Unreal · Godot · web)"] -- "event happened here,
these NPCs are here,
advance time" --> H["Hearsay engine
(FastAPI + Cypher queries)"] H -- "NPC believes X about you (conf 0.6),
opinion −0.5 → rule fires,
here's why: A ← B ← C" --> G H <--> F[("FalkorDB
one graph per save / region")] ``` - **Small contract:** the game sends *events* and *who is where*, and gets back *beliefs*, *opinions*, triggered *rules* and *explanations*. It's HTTP, so it works from any engine. - **Content is data, not code:** characters, schedules, trust, behaviour rules and the "how stories get worse" ladders all live in [`backend/seed/village.json`](backend/seed/village.json) and `Rule` nodes. A designer can add "the blacksmith refuses to sell below −0.5" without touching code. - **The AI is optional:** decisions come from the graph. A language model (or none) only words the lines, so characters can't invent knowledge (0 / 50 in the grounding test). ### Is it fast enough? Measured on a laptop ([docs/results.md](docs/results.md)): reading a character's beliefs and opinion takes **~1 ms (p95 2.3 ms)**, flat from 10 to **500 separate worlds** in one FalkorDB instance, and a full hour of village gossip takes ~15 ms. That's cheap enough to run per character, per interaction. **Honest scope:** this prototype has 6 characters in one village. For a GTA-sized world you would: - simulate gossip in full only near the player and in story-relevant groups (a "level of detail" for gossip); - split the world into region graphs that travelling characters carry stories between; - batch each tick's updates into a few large queries. The model and the queries stay the same. [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §11](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#11-using-the-engine-in-another-game) has the details. ## The demo: one stolen apple Every villager's memories, beliefs and relationships live in the graph. Villagers who see you act remember it. When villagers meet, rumours travel along their trust relationships and get worse with every retelling. Villagers who never saw you act on what they've *heard*, and when you ask **"Why?"**, they show you who told whom. > Steal an apple. Only Old Tomas sees it. That evening at the inn, Tomas and Pip tell Bertha,

LuckyMonkey/luckymonkey-game.desc: 🐵 On-call in the jungle: a Bevy/WebAssembly game about keeping a make-believe network alive. Trace problems to their origin, delegate to a crew of five, run real commands, read the verdict.
LuckyMonkey/luckymonkey-game.readme:
# 🐵 Lucky Monkey: On-Call in the Jungle **A browser game about keeping a make-believe jungle network alive through one on-call shift.** Routers are temples, firewalls are vine gates, the database lives in a lake, and the outages are real ones in costume. [![Play in your browser](https://img.shields.io/badge/▶_play-go.fridge.run%2Fluckymonkey-22c55e?style=for-the-badge)](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey) [![Training shift](https://img.shields.io/badge/🎓_start-training_shift-f59e0b?style=for-the-badge)](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey#shift) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-2024-b7410e?logo=rust&logoColor=white) ![Bevy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bevy-0.20-232326?logo=bevy&logoColor=white) ![WebAssembly](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebAssembly-WebGL2-654ff0?logo=webassembly&logoColor=white) ![Data driven](https://img.shields.io/badge/rules-live_JSON-0ea5e9) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/sim_tests-14_passing-22c55e) ![Faults](https://img.shields.io/badge/fault_types-18-ef4444) ![Nodes](https://img.shields.io/badge/nodes-33_on_11_islands-84cc16) ![The archipelago: floating islands, one river from void to void, rope links between islands](docs/img/oncall-overview.png)
> *It is 09:00. You are on call. A stampede of bison is about to hit the Banana > Cache, a worm is reaching across the vines, and the certificate on the Auth > Gate expires in fifty seconds. The Watchtower can see some of it coming. Not > all of it.* --- ## 📚 Contents - [🎮 How to play](#-how-to-play) - [🧠 What it teaches](#-what-it-teaches) - [⚙️ How the game code works](#️-how-the-game-code-works) - [🛠️ Build and run it yourself](#️-build-and-run-it-yourself) - [✏️ Change the game without recompiling](#️-change-the-game-without-recompiling) - [📖 Documentation](#-documentation) - [🙏 Credits and licences](#-credits-and-licences) --- ## 🎮 How to play ![An incident: the big red Time to Loss timer, red rope links to the troubled node, the crew and the shared network log](docs/img/oncall-red-links.png) You run a small crew through an 8-minute shift (09:00 → 17:00 on the game clock). Things break. You read the symptoms, send someone, pick the response, and race the **⏳ Time to Loss**. ### 1. Learn the network first. Nothing breaks until you start. | Key | Mode | | |---|---|---| | **T** | 🗺️ **Tour** | Island by island through all 28 nodes: what each one *is*, its lore, what it links to, and how many services lose their path if it goes down | | **P** | 🧪 **Practice** | One problem at a time, timers ×3, nothing spreads, no game over | | **B** | 📖 **Field guide** | Every concept you've met, with the example where you met it | ![Tour mode](docs/img/oncall-tour.png) ### 2. Delegate to your crew | | | Faster at | Can't | |---|---|---|---| | 🐵 | **Mango** the monkey | good at everything | | | 🦜 | **Pip** the parrot | diagnosis | heavy work | | 🦥 | **Moss** the sloth | maintenance: certs, patches, canaries | | | 🐸 | **Fern** the tree frog | hardware: cables, vents, power | | | 🐘 | **Tusk** the elephant | heavy work: rollbacks, hotfixes, replicas | | Pick a response and a crew member **runs it straight away**, in about 2.5 s. They still travel to the node on the map, but nothing waits for them. Each runs one thing at a time, so the whole crew can work five problems at once. ### 3. Find the origin, not the symptoms ![DNS left alone: two neighbours already failing because of it, each pointing back to the origin](docs/img/oncall-spread.png) Every problem **starts somewhere for a reason** (*"A botnet of a million bison found the Banana Cache on the open internet"*) and, left alone, **spreads along its links** as its timer runs down. - 🟡 **Warning**: nothing is broken yet. Prevent it (renew the cert, canary the deploy) for bonus points. - 🔴 **Incident**: the origin. It's degraded and counting down; at 0 it goes **down**. - 📉 **Symptom**: a neighbour suffering from it. Nothing to fix there: **O** jumps to the origin, and fixing the origin clears every symptom at once. - 🐛 **Worms** are contagious: they infect neighbours for real. - 🩶 **Unreachable**: fine, but cut off because the only path runs through a down node. ### 4. Run the command, read the verdict ![Four responses to the same DDoS: two wrong, one that buys time, one that fixes it](docs/img/oncall-terminal.png) Pick one of four responses. The terminal types the real command, streams its output, runs a health check, and then says **✅ CORRECT**, **🩹 PARTLY** (it bought time) or **❌ NOT THE FIX**, with the reason. Not sure? 🍌 **H** spends a banana on a hint, or 🔍 **I** diagnoses every option. ![Diagnosed: every option labelled with what it would do](docs/img/oncall-diagnosed.png) ### 5. Keep the SLA **Network health** is the network right now. **Shift SLA** is its average over the shift, and you need **95%** to pass and unlock the next level. At the end you get your score, ✅ what went right, ⚠️ what went wrong (with specifics such as *"メインルーター Router went down when its Time to Loss ran out, cutting off 27 other service(s)"*), and your shift history. ![End of shift](docs/img/oncall-gameover.png) ### ⌨️ Keys `Enter` start · `Space` most urgent · `Tab` cycle problems · `1-4` respond · `I` diagnose · `H` 🍌 hint · `O` go to the origin · `Z X C V N` pick a crew member · `G` send · arrows hop nodes · `Q/E` islands · `WASD`/drag pan · wheel/pinch zoom · `F` follow 📱 On a phone: drag, pinch, tap a node, tap a response. Off-screen nodes become **pins on the screen edge**. Tap one to fly there. ▶ **Jump straight into a situation:** [DDoS on the Banana Cache](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey#node=banana-sector&incident=ddos&zoom=1.2) · [a deploy that migrated the database](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey#node=main-router&incident=migration) · [a certificate about to expire](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey#node=auth-gate&forecast=cert&zoom=1.3) · [DNS down](https://go.fridge.run/luckymonkey#node=dns-shrine&incident=dns

prachetpoddar/blind-auction-figgie.readme:
# Blind Auction Figgie

A four-player variant of [Figgie](https://www.figgie.com), the card game about trading under uncertainty, in which players can **pay for information** before each trading window. Every player sees who bought what and at what price, but only the buyer sees the cards. The question the game asks is when information is priced right, and what buying it gives away.

This repository holds the playable game, the simulators that test its rules with the game's own bot code, every result, and a five-page write-up ([`Blind_Auction_Figgie.pdf`](Blind_Auction_Figgie.pdf)).

## Play

**[Play it here](https://prachetpoddar.github.io/blind-auction-figgie/)** against three bots. The game is a single HTML page, [`docs/index.html`](docs/index.html), served by GitHub Pages. Saved games, the rating and the leaderboard need the page's original hosting and switch themselves off here; the game, the bots and the data desk all work.

## The rules in brief

- Standard Figgie deck and payout: 40 cards (one suit of 12, one of 8, two of 10), a pot of 200 from 50-chip antes, 10 per goal-suit card and the rest of the pot to the largest holder of the goal suit.
- Four trading windows of 60 seconds. Any trade cancels all of your resting quotes.
- Before each window a **data desk** sells, by sealed-bid auction with a house reserve: a **Peek** (one random card from a random opponent), a **Scan** (five cards from an opponent you pick), an **X-ray** (an opponent's whole hand, kept current through the trade tape) and a **Tracker** (a live grid of every player's buys and sells). Winners pay the clearing price. All payments go to the house.

## Results

Final rules, seeded simulation, mixed tables of four bots drawn from five styles, about 8,000 rounds per style (95% intervals):

| Style | Net chips per round | Rounds finished top | Paid for data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Info-hungry | +1.5 ± 1.3 | 35% | 21.1 |
| Equilibrium | −2.0 ± 1.2 | 28% | 9.8 |
| Bluffer | −3.1 ± 1.2 | 27% | 9.9 |
| Cautious | −5.1 ± 1.1 | 19% | 0.0 |
| Naive | −43.9 ± 1.5 | 16% | 11.6 |

At the same tables, Info-hungry beats Equilibrium by +4.2 ± 2.3 chips a round, and Equilibrium beats Cautious, which never buys, by +3.9 ± 2.1. Buying information pays, but nobody can buy a large edge.

Under the original rules, which auctioned a yes/no answer about the deck, Info-hungry led every table at +8.5 ± 1.2 a round. One answer carried as much as seeing about 18 more cards. The write-up explains how the design got from there to here, including the controls that overturned early results and a bug that an independent review found in the simulator.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` | The game: `logic.js` (deck model, Bayesian bots, game flow), `desk.js` (the data desk), `ui.js` and `ui.css` (interface), `page.html` (markup), `build.py` (assembles everything into one page), `tools/` (texture and card-back generators) |
| `docs/index.html` | The built game, ready for GitHub Pages |
| `sim/` | Headless simulators that load the game's bot code (`sim_auction.js` for the old rules, `sim_desk.js` for the desk), the seeded runner `run_series.py`, `check_reproduction.py`, `infovalue.js` and `legacy/` (the code as it was for the earlier rule sets) |
| `results/` | `results.json` (rules v3 to V18), `results_v19.json` (final rules), `infovalue.txt` |
| `tests/` | `test_reveal.js` (regression test for the peek bug) and `test_desk.py` (a full round in a headless browser) |
| `writeup/` | `build.js` and `chart.py`, which build the PDF from the results files |
| `DESIGN.md` | The design log for every version |

## Reproduce

Needs Node 18 or later and Python 3. The browser test also needs Playwright with Chromium.

```bash
python3 sim/check_reproduction.py v19_final mixed     # reruns one stored cell (about 3 minutes) and compares
SERIES=v19 OUT=results_v19.json python3 sim/run_series.py   # final rules, about 25 minutes on 2 cores
python3 sim/run_series.py                              # rules v3 to V18
node sim/infovalue.js                                  # information value table
node tests/test_reveal.js                              # passes on the current code
DESK_SRC=../sim/legacy/desk_v18.js node tests/test_reveal.js   # fails on the V18 code, as it should
python3 tests/test_desk.py 1440 900 dk                 # one full round in a headless browser
python3 src/build.py                                   # rebuild docs/index.html from src/
node writeup/build.js Blind_Auction_Figgie.docx        # rebuild the write-up (needs the docx package)
```

Every run is seeded, so the same command gives the same numbers.

## How this was built

I designed the game, its rules and the experiments, and made the design calls at each stage. Much of the code was written with Claude, an AI assistant, working from my direction.

## Licence

MIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

# Crownmere

A 3D medieval kingdom game that runs in the browser (Three.js, no build step). Build a village into a kingdom, and outlast rival kingdoms, alone or with up to 3 friends.

- **Multiplayer:** one player hosts and shares a five-letter room code; friends join with it. The host's browser runs the game, so keep that tab open.
- **Showcases:** [a City at its height](https://c0s1nlarry10.github.io/crownmere/#city) · [sandbox](https://c0s1nlarry10.github.io/crownmere/#demo)

Uses [Three.js](https://threejs.org) (MIT) and [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com) (MIT), and the fonts IM Fell English and Alegreya Sans (SIL Open Font License), loaded from their public CDNs.

ZippyParakeet097/commonwealth-survey.readme:
# Commonwealth Survey

The Fallout 4 map warped onto real eastern Massachusetts, so you can measure the Commonwealth in true miles.

The game squeezes Boston and its suburbs into a few square miles. This tool puts every game location back on the real ground: real landmarks sit where they really are (Diamond City on Fenway Park, the Castle on Fort Independence), and fictional places are placed by stretching the game map to fit them. It is built for lore writers, modders and anyone who wants a realistic sense of how big the Commonwealth is, and how far the Sole Survivor walked looking for Shaun.

## What it does

- **Scale grid.** Even squares over the game map, sized ¼ mi to 10 mi (or ½ km to 20 km), or sized to the zoom automatically. Columns are lettered and rows numbered from the northwest corner, so every place has a grid reference like `G6` that you can cite in your own writing.
- **Measure.** Click out any route to get its straight-line length and walking time. Points snap to nearby places.
- **The Sole Survivor's search.** One click traces the main quest from Vault 111 to the Courser at Greenetech Genetics: ten legs, about 93 miles as the crow flies.
- **Every location.** 258 marked map locations and 151 unmarked ones, each with its real latitude and longitude, real town, the real site it stands on where there is one, and how its position was worked out.
- **Real coordinates anywhere.** Hover for latitude, longitude and grid square; click empty ground to drop a pin with links to OpenStreetMap and Google Maps.
- **The Glowing Sea.** The in-game Sea warped onto real ground, plus a theory of how far it runs past the map's edge, worked out from fallout drift, October winds and real terrain. Both nuclear craters are drawn at their estimated true size.
- **Nuka-World, theorized.** The park is off the game map, so it gets its own figure: southern New England with the survey sheet, the game map and the fan-favoured site, Six Flags New England in Agawam, about 66 miles west-southwest of the transit center. The fastest real drive there, 82 miles by the Mass Pike, is drawn on it. The figure and the place card give the reasoning and sources.
- **Places on real ground:** site plans of Diamond City, the Castle, Fort Strong and Hangman's Alley, drawn from OpenStreetMap at true scale.
- **On a Pip-Boy.** The survey runs on the Pip-Boy 3000 from Fallout 3 and New Vegas. Its casing frames the screen: the rad gauge (which reads the selected place, so the Glowing Sea pegs it), the badge, the model plate, the tuning knob and the brass thumbwheel. SURVEY, SITES, DATA, MAP and SEA are the lamp buttons under the screen, in Fallout 4's slot order, and the open one is lit. On the glass, as in the games, a bracketed title bar runs across the top with readouts and the clock, the prompts sit under it, and the sub-tabs run along the foot with the open one boxed. The map marks places with squares, as New Vegas does: filled where the position comes from a real site or the game's clues, hollow where it is estimated. Settlements carry a Minutemen pennant, downtown Boston folds into one counted marker until you zoom in, and routes are dotted like a quest path. Pick the colour under Settings from the four the games offer: green (the Fallout 3 default), amber (the New Vegas default), blue or white. On a phone the casing folds away and the lamp buttons stay along the bottom.
- **Or a field survey kit.** A second look: an Army Map Service sheet on khaki paper, with stencilled headings, a typewritten index card for each place and your own routes, pins and selections in red grease pencil. Choose it under Settings; by default the page uses it in light mode and the Pip-Boy in dark mode.
- Miles or kilometres, and links that open on a place: `…/#place=Diamond%20City`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Everything works from the keyboard, and the keys follow the game where it has one. Press `?` for the full list.

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `1`–`5` | Survey, Sites, Data, Map, Sea |
| `M`, `J` | Map, Data (as in Fallout 4) |
| `A` `D` | Previous or next sub-tab |
| `W` `S` or `↑` `↓` | Move up or down a list; `E` or `Enter` shows the highlighted row on the map |
| On the map: arrows or `W` `A` `S` `D`, `+` `−` | Move the crosshair, zoom |
| On the map: `E`, `Enter` or `Space` | Select the place under the crosshair, drop a pin, or add a measuring point |

The letter and number shortcuts can be turned off under Settings (WCAG 2.1.4), and never fire while you type in a field. Tab, the arrow keys, Enter and Esc always work.

The page aims at WCAG 2.2 AA. Every Pip-Boy shade is a mix of the chosen colour with black, and `npm run check` verifies that each text and control colour pair meets AA contrast for every tint, for the tab labels on the Pip-Boy's casing and for the field kit. With one colour on screen, map layers are told apart by line style and texture rather than hue: wetlands by marsh tufts, the Glowing Sea by a hatched band inside its edge, Brotherhood of Steel places by the Brotherhood's emblem and its ground (Logan Airport) by cross-hatching inside a double border, the game map's edge by a dash-dot line. Selections and changes are announced to screen readers. Scanlines and glow, or the field kit's paper grain, can be switched off; the scanlines also switch off by themselves when your system asks for more contrast. The Pip-Boy's power-on and screen flicker don't play when your system asks for reduced motion.

## Run it

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 18 or newer; there is nothing else to install.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ZippyParakeet097/commonwealth-survey.git
cd commonwealth-survey
npm start          # then open http://localhost:8080
```

Or build the single-file version, `npm run build`, and open `dist/commonwealth-survey.html`. It is the whole tool in one file: it opens straight from disk, works offline (the web fonts fall back to system fonts) and can be shared on its own.

# ألعاب الشلة 🎲

ألعاب جماعية تنلعب من الجوال: المضيف يفتح غرفة على شاشة (لابتوب أو تلفزيون)، والكل يمسح الباركود ويدخل ويجاوب من جواله.

**العب الحين:** https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com

فيها ست ألعاب: «عقلية القطيع» 🐄 و«تحدي الوقت» ⏱️ و«سين جيم» ❓ و«حروف» 🔤 و«برا السالفة» 🤫 و«مافيا» 🎭. المضيف يختار اللعبة من لوبي الغرفة، ويقدر يبدّل بينهم بين كل لعبة والثانية بدون ما أحد يطلع من الغرفة.

الصفحة الرئيسية فيها بطاقة كبيرة لكل لعبة، وكل لعبة لها صفحتها الخاصة بألوانها وشكلها: طريقة اللعب، وعيّنة منها، وزر «أنشئ غرفة». الروابط: [`/herd`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/herd) و[`/time`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/time) و[`/seen`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/seen) و[`/letters`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/letters) و[`/outsider`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/outsider) و[`/mafia`](https://herd-game-hf2y.onrender.com/mafia). ونفس الألوان تكمل داخل اللعبة، على شاشة المضيف والجوالات (`data-theme` في `style.css`).

## اللعبة الأولى: «عقلية القطيع» 🐄

مستوحاة من لعبة الحفلات المشهورة **Herd Mentality**.

- يطلع سؤال للكل، مثل «اذكر لون من ألوان قوس قزح» أو «شاي ولا قهوة؟».
- قبل ما يرسل جوابه، كل لاعب يختار رقم من **1 إلى 15** يراهن فيه. كل رقم يستخدمه **مرة وحدة بس** في اللعبة، والرقم ينحرق سواء فاز أو خسر.
- الفايز ياخذ نقاط الرقم اللي راهن فيه، والخسران يروح عليه رقمه.
- اللي ما يجاوب على السؤال قبل الكشف ينحرق **أقل رقم باقي عنده**.

### الأطوار
| الطور | الهدف | مين يفوز |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🐄 **مع القطيع** | جاوب نفس جواب الأغلبية | أكبر مجموعة جاوبت نفس الجواب. لو تعادلت أكبر مجموعتين أو أكثر، الكل يفوز. والجواب اللي ما قاله إلا شخص واحد ما يفوز. |
| 🦄 **عكس القطيع** | جاوب جواب صحيح ما أحد غيرك يقوله | كل واحد جوابه ما تكرر. لو اثنين أو أكثر قالوا نفس الجواب، يخسرون كلهم. |

### فئات الأسئلة
بنك الأسئلة فيه 1296 سؤال مقسومة 11 فئة و42 قسم (كل قسم فيه 20 سؤال أو أكثر لـ«مع القطيع» و10 أو أكثر لـ«عكس القطيع»). المضيف يختار فئة كاملة، أو يفتح «الأقسام» ويختار قسم معيّن (مثلاً «الدوري الإسباني» بس، أو «الإمام المهدي (عج)» بس)، أو يخلط بينهم. اللعبة تسحب من الفئات المختارة بالتساوي، وبعدين بالتساوي بين الأقسام داخل كل فئة. كل قسم فيه أسئلة للطورين: أسئلة «عكس القطيع» أجوبتها محدودة (مثل «يوم من أيام الأسبوع») عشان الانفراد بالجواب يحتاج تفكير.

| الفئة | الأقسام | مع القطيع | عكس القطيع |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🍔 أكل وشرب | أكلات سعودية وشعبية، حلويات، مشروبات وقهوة، مطاعم ووجبات سريعة، فواكه وخضار | 104 | 50 |
| ☕ حياة يومية | عادات وروتين، جوال وتطبيقات، مدرسة وشغل، عائلة وناس، جسم وصحة | 106 | 50 |
| 🏠 أشياء وأماكن | البيت، أماكن عامة، أجهزة وأدوات، سيارات ومواصلات | 81 | 40 |
| 🇸🇦 السعودية والخليج | مدن ومناطق، عادات ومناسبات، دول الخليج | 61 | 31 |
| 🌍 جغرافيا ومعلومات | دول وعواصم، فضاء وطبيعة، تاريخ واختراعات | 60 | 31 |
| 🐪 حيوانات | حيوانات، طيور وحشرات، بحر | 60 | 30 |
| ⚽ رياضة | الدوري السعودي، الدوري الإسباني، الدوري الإنجليزي، كرة القدم العالمية، رياضات عامة | 100 | 53 |
| 🎬 ترفيه | كرتون، مسلسلات وأفلام، ألعاب فيديو وجوال، ألعاب شعبية وطاولة | 80 | 40 |
| 🤔 آراء واختيارات | هذا ولا ذاك، أفضل وأحلى، لو… | 62 | 32 |
| 🔤 أرقام وحروف وألوان | أرقام وأوقات، حروف وأسماء، ألوان | 60 | 34 |
| 🕌 دينية | الإمام الحسين (ع) وكربلاء، الإمام المهدي (عج)، الإمام علي والزهراء (ع)، عام: القرآن والأنبياء والعبادات | 81 | 50 |
| **المجموع** | | **855** | **441** |

الأسئلة الدينية على المذهب الشيعي.

### مراجعة الأجوبة
- الأجوبة المتشابهة تنجمع تلقائياً (`أحمر` = `الأحمر` = `احمر`).
- المضيف يقدر **يدمج** جوابين بنفس المعنى (مثلاً `بحر` و`شاطئ`).
- ويقدر **يرفض** أي جواب غلط فما يفوز صاحبه. هذا مهم في «عكس القطيع» عشان ما أحد يكتب أي كلام عشان ينفرد.
- لو محتار، يضغط **«🗳️ تصويت»** على الجواب: كل اللاعبين إلا اللي كتبوه يصوّتون من جوالاتهم (يُقبل / ينرفض). النتيجة ما تطلع إلا لما يخلص التصويت، والأغلبية تقرر. لو تعادل، المضيف يقرر.
- كل دمج أو رفض أو نتيجة تصويت يقدر يتراجع عنها قبل ما يعتمد النتيجة.

### شاشة المضيف
- باركود ورقم غرفة من 4 أرقام، وقائمة اللاعبين (ويقدر يطرد أحد).
- الإعدادات: طور اللعبة، عدد الأسئلة (3–15)، المؤقت، مصدر الأسئلة (بنك جاهز، أو أسئلة يكتبها المضيف، أو الاثنين)، والفئات والأقسام.
- يشوف مين جاوب بدون ما يشوف الأجوبة، وبعدها يكشف ويدمج ويرفض أو يطلب تصويت، ويعتمد النتيجة.
- لو المضيف يبي يلعب معهم، يمسح الباركود بجواله مثل الباقين.

## اللعبة الثانية: «تحدي الوقت» ⏱️

فريقين وساعتين وصور من 50 فئة. تشتغل مثل **ساعة الشطرنج**: كل فريق عنده وقته، والفريق اللي يخلص وقته يخسر الجولة.

- اللاعبين ينقسمون **🔴 الأحمر** و**🔵 الأزرق** تلقائياً أول ما يدخلون. المضيف ينقل أي لاعب بضغطة على اسمه، أو يوزّعهم عشوائي.
- **كل جولة شخص ضد شخص:** يلعب واحد من كل فريق بالدور، عشان الكل يلعب (الترتيب عشوائي أول مرة). وهو بس اللي يجاوب، وفريقه ما يساعده 🤫. المضيف يشوف الاثنين قبل الجولة، ويقدر يبدّل أي واحد منهم بلاعب ثاني من فريقه لين يبدأ الوقت، واللي انبدّل يجي دوره الجولة الجاية. وأسماؤهم تطلع على الساعتين وفي الجوالات.
- كل جولة المضيف **يدوّر العجلة** فتختار الفئة. العجلة تدور على شاشة المضيف وفي كل الجوالات، والفئة ما تتكرر لين تخلص الفئات المختارة.
- تطلع صورة، واللي عليه الدور يقول وش هي بصوت عالي. **المضيف هو الحكم**، والجواب يطلع عنده بس:
  - **✅ صح:** يوقف وقته ويبدأ وقت اللاعب الثاني على صورة جديدة.
  - **⏭️ تخطي:** صورة جديدة ووقته يبقى شغّال، ومن الإعدادات ممكن ينخصم 3 أو 5 ثواني زيادة.
  - **⏸️ إيقاف** لو صار نقاش (الصورة تتغطى في الجوالات)، و**↩︎ تراجع** يلغي آخر ضغطة ويرجّع الوقت مثل ما كان.
  - **🚫 استبعد الصورة:** لو الصورة غلط أو تفضح الجواب، تتبدل بدون ما ينخصم وقت، وما تطلع مرة ثانية في الألعاب اللي تستضيفها من نفس الجهاز.
- لو خلصت صور الفئة قبل الوقت، يفوز اللي باقي له وقت أكثر.
- بعد كل جولة يطلع ملخص فيه كل الصور وأجوبتها.
- أول فريق يكسب عدد الجولات المحدد (جولة إلى 5) يفوز. الفرق تتناوب على بداية الجولات.
- الإعدادات: وقت كل فريق (30 أو 45 أو 60 أو 90 ثانية)، عدد الجولات، خصم التخطي، والفئات.
- اختصارات الكيبورد للمضيف: **مسافة** = صح، **S** = تخطي، **P** = إيقاف/كمّل، **Z** = تراجع، **X** = استبعد.
- لو شاشة المضيف قدام الكل، يضغط على الجواب عشان يخفيه.
- كل الأجهزة تحمّل الصور الجاية أول ما توقف العجلة، عشان الوقت ما يروح على التحميل.

# TalenttreeIncremental

An incremental RPG where the talent tree is the whole game world. Skills, crafting, combat, dungeons and a home base sit as connected clusters of nodes on a large map that grows as you play.

How far the project has come is in [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md). AI agents (Codex, Claude and others) follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), and Claude Code also reads [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

## Getting started

Requires Node.js 22 or newer. Nothing needs to be installed.

```bash
npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:5173/prototype/. To see the whole map, open http://localhost:5173/prototype/?load=all. That is a demo game where every cluster is open, and it is saved separately, so your normal game is not touched.

The game is saved in the browser. The Developer button gives higher game speed, resources and levels for testing, plus a reset.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `npm start` | Starts the prototype at http://localhost:5173/prototype/ |
| `npm test` | Runs the game engine tests |
| `npm run simulate` | Lets a bot play the prototype and measures when the milestones are reached |
| `npm run check:assets` | Checks the theme's image files against the manifest |
| `npm run asset-list` | Regenerates the asset list from the manifest |
| `npm run check` | Runs both the tests and the asset check |

## Documents

- [Game concept and decisions](docs/game-concept.md): separates the user's decisions, the user's possible extensions and the agents' proposals
- [Node list](docs/prototype-nodes.md): every node in the prototype with requirements, prices and effects
- [Balance](docs/balance.md): milestone times from the balance simulator (generated)
- [Idea history](docs/idea-history.md): the user's creative messages, verbatim
- [Asset list](docs/asset-list.md): generated from [asset-manifest.json](themes/asset-manifest.json) and [the starchart theme.json](themes/starchart/theme.json)
- [The first eight style sketches](konceptbilleder/OVERSIGT.md) and [their prompts](konceptbilleder/billedprompts.md)

## Folders

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `prototype/` | The playable prototype in plain JavaScript with no build step |
| `themes/` | The asset manifest and one folder per theme. The starchart theme is complete |
| `tools/` | Server, asset check, asset list generator and balance simulator |
| `tests/` | Automated tests of the game engine |
| `docs/` | Concept, node list, idea history, balance and asset list |
| `kilder/` | Codex's deliveries per round: originals, prompts, scripts and contact sheets |
| `grafik/` | Graphic explorations: test batch 01, style samples and pixel moodboards |
| `konceptbilleder/` | The first eight style sketches |

`kilder/`, `grafik/` and `konceptbilleder/` are Codex's archives. They keep their Danish names for now and will be renamed together with Codex later.

# StudyRPG

A pixel-art study timer (Pomodoro-style) where every finished study session is a battle won. Earn XP to level up your hero, gold for gear, and command an idle army that raids demon keeps while you study.

**Play:** https://daneviser.github.io/StudyRPG/

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Documentation

- [Game features](docs/GAME_FEATURES.md): everything the game can do, with all numbers.
- [Technical guide](docs/TECHNICAL.md): architecture, save format, how to extend it, and the plan for backend saves and login.

Progress is stored in the browser's `localStorage`; use **Config → Export / Import** to back it up.

nadocodes/DeadCoach.desc: Deadlock post-match coach: role-based grades vs your lobby, build coaching and an in-game style item browser.
nadocodes/DeadCoach.readme:
# Deadlock Macro & Itemization Coach

## DeadCoach website (`docs/`)

A static site, hosted on GitHub Pages, that anyone can use: type an account ID
(or open `…/?id=<account_id>`) and it loads matches live from
[deadlock-api.com](https://deadlock-api.com) in the browser, with no server and no syncing.

- Ranked / Standard / Street Brawl tabs, each game graded S–D against its lobby
  for the role actually played (detected from the build, healing and hero type).
- Coach's note three ways: **Quick coach** (free, built from meta win rates for that
  enemy lineup), **Claude via claude.ai** (copy the request, paste Claude's reply
  back to see it visualised), or **Claude via your own API key** (stored only in
  that browser).
- In-game style item browser highlighting your build and the coach's build.

Publish: push this repo to GitHub, then Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch →
`main` / `/docs`. Run locally with `python -m http.server 8766 --directory docs`.
After a game patch, run `python build_item_catalog.py` to refresh item and hero data.

## Original local Flask app

A local web dashboard: pick one of your recent matches, and it pulls your
build + the current meta stats for that hero/matchup from the community
[Deadlock API](https://deadlock-api.com), then asks Claude to write you a
short coaching note on what you bought and why it did or didn't work.

This is **Phase 1** (post-match coaching). It's deliberately not a live
in-match overlay yet — see "Phase 2" below for why, and what to do once
you're happy with the coaching quality here.

## 1. Get an Anthropic API key

1. Go to https://console.anthropic.com and sign up / log in.
2. Create an API key under **API Keys**.
3. You'll be billed per request (this app's calls are small — a few cents
   at most per coaching note). Free trial credit is usually available for
   new accounts.

## 2. Install and run

```bash
cd deadlock-coach
pip install -r requirements.txt

# macOS/Linux:
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-...your-key-here...
# Windows (cmd):
set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-...your-key-here...
# Windows (PowerShell):
$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-api03-...your-key-here..."

python app.py
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5000** in your browser.

Without an API key set, the app still runs and shows you the raw match +
meta data it *would* have sent to Claude — useful for checking the plumbing
works before you spend any API credit.

## 3. Find your account_id

The Deadlock API uses your 32-bit Steam account ID, not your SteamID64 or
Steam vanity name. If you have your SteamID64 (a long number starting with
`7656119...`), subtract `76561197960265728` to get your account_id. Several
community tools linked from the [deadlock-api.com docs](https://api.deadlock-api.com/docs)
can also do this conversion from a Steam profile URL directly.

## If something 404s

`deadlock-api.com` is an independent community project, not run by Valve or
Anthropic, and endpoint paths can change as they develop it. `app.py` has a
block of constants and small `dl_get(...)` calls near the top clearly
documenting which endpoints it expects:

- `GET /v1/players/{account_id}/match-history`
- `GET /v1/matches/{match_id}`
- `GET /v1/analytics/item-stats`
- `GET /v1/analytics/hero-build-stats/{hero_id}`
- `GET /v1/assets/heroes`
- `GET /v1/assets/items`

If you get a 502 error mentioning one of these, open
https://api.deadlock-api.com/docs, find the current name/shape for that
endpoint, and update the corresponding function in `app.py` — the rest of
the app doesn't need to change.

## What the coaching note actually uses

For the match you click:
- **Your build** — the items you bought, pulled from the match detail
- **The matchup** — your hero vs. the specific enemy heroes you faced
- **Live meta stats** — item win rates *for your hero specifically against
  that enemy composition*, not just generic hero win rates
- **Aggregate build stats** — what item/skill orders tend to win with your
  hero across many matches

Claude is prompted to structure feedback as: what you did well, the single
biggest itemization miss (not a laundry list), what the data suggests
instead and why, and — only when the match data supports it — one macro
note about timing or rotations.

## Phase 2 — live in-match assist

Once you're happy with the coaching quality here, the natural next step is
a near-real-time version using `live.deadlock-api.com`'s event stream
(built for betting platforms, paid API key, ~60-90s delay inherited from
Valve's spectate feed). That's a bigger lift — a background listener,
a buffer of recent game-state events, and a way to surface a suggestion
without breaking your flow mid-fight — happy to help build that next.
