AbrahamCain/glassbox.desc: A game for exploring the inside of a vision-language model: climb its layers, cast interventions, bet on the outcome.
AbrahamCain/glassbox.readme:
# Glassbox

[![ci](https://github.com/AbrahamCain/glassbox/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AbrahamCain/glassbox/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A game for building intuition about what happens inside a vision-language model.
You climb a tower where each floor is one transformer block, cast "spells" that
rewrite the model's internal state, **bet on what will happen first**, and see what
the model actually does. Your prediction hit rate is the real score.

**[▶ Watch the 72-second demo, with sound](docs/glassbox-demo.mp4)**: climbing the tower, a
quest, and finding the floor where the model hands the answer from the picture to the text.

[![screenshot](docs/screenshot.png)](docs/glassbox-demo.mp4)

## How it fits together

```
Godot 4 client (godot/)  <-- WebSocket JSON -->  Python backend (backend/)
  tower, HUD, quests,                              model adapter -> hook engine
  XP / predictions                                 (PyTorch forward hooks)
```

- **Adapters** (`backend/glassbox/adapters/`) map an architecture onto a common schema:
  residual blocks, unembedding, tokens tagged image/text/special. A new model means
  one new adapter; the game doesn't change.
- **Engine** (`backend/glassbox/engine.py`): captures the residual stream after every
  block and applies the tools:
  - **ablate** ("Erase" in-game): replace cells with the same-kind mean, or zero
  - **patch** ("Transplant"): copy cells from another loaded scene (same prompt → same layout)
  - **steer** ("Push"): add `scale * (r(to) - r(from))` at a floor
- **Outcomes** players bet on: `nothing` (<5 pt change in p(clean answer)),
  `nudge` (5–30), `shove` (>30, answer kept), `flip` (answer changes).

## Running it (Windows)

```powershell
# backend, once
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\make_scenes.py

# every session
.\run.ps1                      # SmolVLM-256M on GPU (~0.7 GiB VRAM)
.\run.ps1 -Model tiny          # random tiny model, for client development
```

Then open `godot/project.godot` in Godot 4.7 and press F5.

Checks:
- `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests` checks the engine with no download.
- `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\smoke.py` checks the real model.
- `godot --path godot -- --autotest` plays the tutorial and quest 1, checks unlocking and
  cell picking (including board view), and saves screenshots.
- `godot --path godot --write-movie recordings/demo.avi --fixed-fps 30 -- --demo` records a
  captioned 72 s tour with sound (Movie Maker mode; convert to MP4 with ffmpeg).

## Playing

The first launch starts a **guided tutorial** (replay it from Help). After that:

- **Confidence meter** (left of the tower): for each floor, how sure the model would be of
  its answer if it stopped there. After a spell, orange bars show the floor's confidence in
  the model's *new* answer. Click a row to go to that floor; hover for details.
- **Tools**: **Erase** (replace cells with an average cell or zeros), **Transplant** (copy
  cells from a second run on another picture), **Push** (add the direction between two
  words). Tools unlock as you reach the quests that teach them, and only the current
  tool's settings are shown.
- **Quests** unlock one after another. Help has a switch to unlock everything.
- **Hover** any cell for what it is and how active/changed it is. **B** gives a top-down
  board view (floors above are hidden) for precise selection.
- **H** opens the help sheet with every key and term.

## Controls

W/S climb floors (or click the meter) · click/drag select cells (Shift adds) · A all picture
cells · T all text cells · X clear · Enter add selection to spell · 1/2/3 Erase/Transplant/Push ·
Tab activity/ripple colours · B board view · I picture on/off · M mute · H help ·
right-drag orbit · middle-drag pan · wheel zoom

## Sound

All audio is synthesised at startup in `godot/scripts/audio.gd`: no audio files. Two
sounds carry information:

- **Floor tone**: when you change floors, a glass note plays whose pitch is p(clean answer)
  at that floor, read by the logit lens (A minor pentatonic, low = unsure, high = sure).
  Climbing the tower, you hear the answer form.
- **Ripple sweep**: after a cast, one ping per floor rising up the tower, louder where
  the spell changed the model's state more.

The rest is feedback: select/add/cast sounds, an outcome sting (nothing/nudge/shove/flip),
a verdict on your bet, a quest fanfare, and a looping ambient drone that rises as you
climb. Volume, Music and M (mute) are saved with your progress. To audition or tweak
the sounds outside the game:
`godot --headless --path godot -s res://tools/export_sounds.gd` writes them all as WAVs.

## Verified findings on SmolVLM-256M (the quests are built on these)

- Patching all 64 image cells from a blue-circle run flips "Red"→"Blue" on floors 0–22,
  and fails from 23 up.
- Patching **only the last position** fails on floors 0–22 and works from 23 up.
  Floors 22→23 are where colour moves from image tokens to the answer position.
- Mean-ablating every image cell never removes "Red", because the mean is still reddish.
  Zero ablation does remove it, but pushes the model off-distribution.
- Steering ` red`→` blue` on image cells at floor 10, strength 4, gives "blue" but then
  repeats it ("blue blue blue…"). Steering only the last position mostly breaks the model.

## Security

Every push and pull request runs tests, security tests, SAST (Bandit, Semgrep), a dependency
audit (pip-audit), and a full-history secret scan (Gitleaks). See [`security/README.md`](security/README.md)
for the gates, the threat model, and the tuning decisions.

## Roadmap toward big MoE models

1. ✅ Small VLM (SmolVLM-256M): patch board, tower, logit lens, 3 tools, quests
2. Attention lines view; per-head ablation
3. Small MoE (e.g. OLMoE-1B-

Riyazkhan53/Zen-Play.readme:
# Zen-Play

Multiplayer board and card games for **Android, iOS, iPad and the web**, built with Expo.

| Game | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 🎲 Ludo (2–4) | ✅ Playable |
| 🐍 Snakes & Ladders (2–6) | ✅ Playable |
| ♟️ Chess (2) | ✅ Playable |
| 🎯 Carrom (2, or 4 in teams) | ✅ Playable |
| 🃏 UNO (2–8) | ✅ Playable |
| ♠️ Rummy — 13-card Indian (2–6): Points, Pool 101/201/custom, Best of 3/5, 7 rounds with hidden joker | ✅ Playable |

## Ways to play

- **On this device** — pass the phone or tablet around, add computer players. Works fully offline.
- **Online** — create a room and share the 5-letter code or invite link. Friends join from anywhere.
- **Nearby Wi-Fi** — no internet needed. One phone hosts and shows a QR code; others on the same Wi-Fi
  (or the host's hotspot) scan it or type the address. *Android/iOS app only — browsers can't open
  local network sockets.*

You can mix all three: people sharing one phone can join an online or Wi-Fi room together, and the
host can fill empty seats with computer players. If someone drops mid-game, they rejoin and get their
seat back; the host can also hand their seat to a computer player.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run server          # online server on ws://localhost:8787 (in one terminal)
npm start               # Expo dev server; press w for web
```

Wi-Fi play uses a native module (`react-native-tcp-socket`), so it does **not** work in Expo Go.
Use a development build:

```bash
npx eas-cli@latest build --profile development --platform android   # or ios
```

Point the app at a deployed server with `EXPO_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL=wss://your-server` (already set for
the `preview` and `production` EAS profiles in `eas.json`).

## Checks

```bash
npm test          # game rules, room host, online server end-to-end
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

## Deploy

`render.yaml` defines the online server (`zen-play-server`) and the static web app (`zen-play`).
Update the server URL in `render.yaml` and `eas.json` if your Render service gets a different name.

## How it fits together

```
src/games/      Rules engines (pure TypeScript, no UI): ludo/, snakes/, registry.ts
src/net/        Multiplayer: room-host.ts (authoritative room), protocol.ts, session.ts (app state),
                connection.ts (same-device + WebSocket), lan.native.ts (Wi-Fi TCP host/join)
server/         Online server: WebSocket rooms keyed by code, reusing the same RoomHost
src/app/        Screens: home, game/[id] (choose mode), room (lobby), play, scan, join (deep links)
src/components/ Boards, dice and shared UI
tests/          node:test suites run with tsx
```

Every game runs through one `RoomHost`: on the server for online rooms, on the host phone for Wi-Fi,
and inside the app for same-device play. It validates each move with the game engine, runs computer
players and broadcasts state, so all three modes behave identically.

lendegroote/kabooze.readme:
# KABOOZE

Een gemeen Vlaams drinkspel voor aan tafel, met een verborgen bom. 2 tot 8 spelers, 1 gsm, geen build (gewone HTML/CSS/JS). Groen CRT-scherm in een dun pixel-Game Boy-kader.

Speel: https://lendegroote.github.io/kabooze/

Water telt mee. Ken je limiet.

## Spelverloop

1. TITEL: START, HOE SPEEL JE.
2. SPELERS: naam + selfie (camera met live groene dither, of fotokiezer als de camera niet lukt).
3. GEHEIMEN (per speler, in het geheim, de gsm gaat rond): duid iemand aan bij een vraag, biecht 1 ding (overslaan mag) en neem 1 foto met een willekeurige opdracht (overslaan mag). Geheimen en foto's blijven alleen in de localStorage van dit toestel.
4. RONDES in willekeurige volgorde, elk ongeveer 5 beurten: WIE ZEI DIT, WIE ZOU HET EERST, HETE PATAT, DIT OF DAT, IK HEB NOG NOOIT, WIE HEEFT DIT GEBIECHT, WIENS FOTO IS DIT. Fout raden = 1 drinken + 3 seconden geblokkeerd, juist raden = die persoon drinkt 2 (of 1) en krijgt de gsm.
5. DE BOM: 1 verborgen lont (30 tot 120 s), met een mm:ss-aftelling bovenaan (rood en knipperend in de laatste 10 s). De lont staat stil terwijl iemand typt, foto's neemt of in het geheim stemt, en loopt bij het doorgeven en raden. Bij KABOOM draait de houder van de gsm aan het ROULETTE-wiel (alleen voor jezelf, 4% kans op TRAKTEER EEN RONDE).
6. Na alle rondes: nog een ronde of stoppen (tabel met slokken).

## Bediening

Alles is aanraken. Op laptop mag het toetsenbord: pijltjes + X (bevestigen), Z (terug), Enter (menu), Shift (geluid). Het menu (bovenaan) heeft DOORGAAN, SPEL HERSTARTEN, OPNIEUW BEGINNEN (wist spelers, antwoorden en foto's na bevestiging; staat ook op het titelscherm), TERUG NAAR START, GELUID, MUZIEK, INHOUD en VOLLEDIG SCHERM (op iPhone: zet de pagina op je startscherm, dan start hij volledig scherm via manifest.json).

## Inhoud

`data/content.json` is de bron (stabiele ids, Vlaams, HOOFDLETTERS). `js/content-fallback.js` is een gegenereerde kopie. Aanpassen: `python3 scripts/build-content.py`. `content.html` (menu, INHOUD) toont alles, met zoeken en VERWIJDER/ONGEDAAN per item. Verwijderde ids staan in localStorage `kabooze_removed`; KOPIEER VERWIJDERDE LIJST om ze definitief uit de repo te schrappen.

## Lokaal draaien

```
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Camera werkt alleen via https of localhost (GitHub Pages is https).

## Bestanden

```
index.html, style.css          app-shell, CRT + Game Boy-kader, bureau-achtergrond
js/app.js                      alle schermen, bom, roulette, camera, rondes
js/data.js                     laadt content (fetch + inline fallback), verwijderde ids
js/content-fallback.js         gegenereerd uit data/content.json
js/audio.js                    Web Audio effecten + oorspronkelijke chiptune
js/avatar.js, js/font.js       selfie en foto naar groene dither, 5x7 bitmaplettertype
content.html, js/content.js    inhoudslijst met zoeken en verwijderen
manifest.json, assets/         web app manifest, icoontjes, lettertype
```

Het scherm blijft altijd staand (ook als je de gsm kantelt), het scherm gaat niet in slaapstand tijdens een spel, en bij een herlaad pak je de lopende ronde weer op.

# Mister Mole

Demo: https://billylz.github.io/r3f-mister-mole/

1980'lerin klasik maden oyunlarından esinlenen, React Three Fiber ile yazılmış 3B bir maden oyunu. Grafikler, sesler ve mağaralar bu projeye özgüdür; hiçbir oyundan varlık kopyalanmamıştır. ![Mister Mole](docs/mister-mole.png) ## Sürümler Ana menüden üç görünüm arasında seçim yapılır; seçim tarayıcıda hatırlanır. Oyun kuralları ve mağaralar tüm sürümlerde aynıdır. - **Sürüm 1 · Klasik:** aydınlık mağara, blok toprak, madenci karakter. - **Sürüm 2 · Modern** (`src/v2/`): karanlık mağara. Işığı köstebeğin gölge düşüren kafa lambası, elmaslar, ateşböcekleri ve patlamalar verir. Ayrıca: - birbirine kaynayan organik toprak, bazalt sütunlar, pırlanta kesimli yanardöner elmaslar; - havada süzülen toz zerreleri, patlamada şok dalgası ve kısa ağır çekim; - düşen nesnelerde esneme-sıkışma, ileriye bakan kamera, telefonda titreşim; - elmas ilerleme halkası ve süre azalınca kırmızı nabız atan ekran kenarları. ![Mister Mole Sürüm 2](docs/mister-mole-v2.png) - **Sürüm 3 · Oyuncak tuğla** (`src/v3/`): aydınlık mor sahne ve canlı renkli, düğmeli plastik tuğlalar. Ayrıca: - kayalar düğmeli gri toplar, çerçeve mor karolar; toplanacak elmaslar yerine kubbe başlı küçük robotlar var (kafaları sağa sola bakar); - sabit duvarlar uçları yuvarlak, delikli tek parça kirişler; - oyuncu 2,5 saniye durursa çıkış noktasından halka halka yayılan yumuşak bir dalga başlar: her tuğla bütün olarak Z ekseninde ileri geri gider, sabit duvarlar ve çerçeve yerinde kalır (hareket edince söner); - açılan çıkış beyaz oklu kırmızı bir karo; - kazılan tuğla kendi renginde parçalara, patlamalar rengarenk tuğla parçalarına ayrılır; - karakter, kara kasklı, pelerinli ve kırmızı enerji kılıçlı oyuncak figür **Kara Lord**. Robota ulaşınca kılıcını savurur: sıfırdan sentezlenen kılıç sesi, beyaz çekirdekli kırmızı ışıma ve çevreye saçılan kırmızı ışık. ![Mister Mole Sürüm 3](docs/mister-mole-v3.png) ## Özellikler - **Motor** (`src/engine.ts`): render'dan bağımsız, deterministik TypeScript. Klasik maden oyunlarındaki gibi ızgara her tick'te yukarıdan aşağıya, soldan sağa taranır. Taşlar ve elmaslar düşer, yuvarlak nesnelerin üstünden yuvarlanır. Ateşböcekleri sol duvarı, kelebekler sağ duvarı takip eder. Ayrıca amip, sihirli duvar, 3×3 patlamalar, taş itme ve "yerinde kazma" vardır. - **Mağaralar** (`src/levels.ts`): klasik oyunlardaki gibi tohumlu rastgele dolgu üzerine çizim komutlarıyla üretilen 6 mağara. - **Görünüm**: instanced mesh'ler, iki tick arasında yumuşak hareket, gölgeler, bloom, parçacıklar, kafa lambalı madenci, kamera takibi ve sarsıntı. Sesler Web Audio ile sentezlenir. Dokunmatik ekranlar için yön tuşları vardır. ## Kontroller | Tuş | İşlev | | --- | --- | | Ok tuşları / WASD | Hareket | | Shift + yön | Yerinden kıpırdamadan kaz veya al | | Esc | Sıkışınca mağarayı baştan al (bir can gider). Telefonda üstteki ↺ düğmesi | | P | Duraklat | | V | Genel görünüm | | M | Ses aç/kapat | | Fare tekerleği | Yakınlaştır/uzaklaştır | ## Çalıştırma ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 npm test # oyun kuralları ve mağara kontrolleri npm run build ``` Testler (`scripts/check-game.ts`) düşme, yuvarlanma, ezilme, toplama, itme, düşman hareketi, kelebek elmasları, sihirli duvar, amip ve süre kurallarını kontrol eder. Her mağara için de gerekli elmas sayısına ulaşılabildiğini, düşmanların kendiliğinden ölmediğini ve rastgele oynanışta çökme olmadığını doğrular. ## Demo yayını (GitHub Pages) `.github/workflows/pages.yml` her push'ta testleri çalıştırır ve projeyi derler. Varsayılan dala yapılan push'larda `dist/` klasörünü GitHub Pages'e yayınlar. Bunun için **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions** seçilmelidir.

commits.msg:
Redesign the lightsaber sound

The previous sawtooth-through-resonant-filter sound with a high crackle
was harsh. The new one is a low sine hum (92 Hz plus harmonics and a
slightly detuned partner for a gentle beat) through soft saturation,
with a Doppler-like pitch rise and fall and a swell in volume during the
swing, over a soft low band of air noise. No high crackle.

The sound graph can now be built in any audio context, so it can also
be rendered to a file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

- New synthesized saber sound: detuned sawtooth hum with vibrato, a
  rising and falling filter sweep, a band-passed whoosh and a short crackle
- The blade gets a white-hot core inside an additive red halo and outer
  glow; on a strike the glow flares and the saber light brightens
- The sword arm swings down in a fast arc, red sparks fly at the robot

tarikhokka/GameJam2026TOOADEVS.readme:
# İmza

**CIVIL GAME JAM 2026** · Tema: *Afete Hazırlık ve Farkındalık* · Takım: **TOOADEVS**

Bir şehrin yapı denetim mühendisisin. Her sabah masana yeni bina projeleri geliyor: başvuru dosyası, laboratuvar raporu ve bazen de masaya "unutulmuş" bir zarf. İmzanı attığın her bina şehirde yükseliyor. Ve her gece bir deprem olabilir.

Ertesi sabah gazete, imzanın neye mal olduğunu yazıyor.

## Kurulum

1. `Imza.zip` dosyasını bir klasöre çıkar.
2. `Imza.exe`'yi çalıştır.

Windows 10/11, 64 bit. Kurulum gerekmez. Oyun 1920×1080 tam ekran açılır.

## Kontroller

| Eylem | Kontrol |
|---|---|
| Tüm etkileşimler | Fare (sol tık) |
| Menü | Esc |

## Nasıl oynanır

- **Masa:** Her projede belgedeki değerleri yönetmelikteki en düşük değerle karşılaştır. Değeri yetmeyen bina güvenli değildir.
- **Belgeleri karşılaştır:** Başvuru dosyası ile laboratuvar raporu aynı parseli, aynı tarihi ve aynı mühendisin imzasını taşımalı. Rapordaki kaşe, raporun başlığındaki laboratuvara ait olmalı ve o laboratuvar akredite listede bulunmalı. Tutmayan bir ayrıntı sahte belge işaretidir.
- **El Kitabı:** Kuralları, yönetmelikteki alt sınırları ve akredite laboratuvarların listesini masadaki **El Kitabı** butonuyla istediğin an açabilirsin. İlk gün masaya oturduğunda kısa bir anlatım seni karşılar.
- **Ek test:** Şüphelendiğin projede ücretli ek test iste; gerçek değerler ortaya çıkar.
- **Zarf:** Bazı müteahhitler rüşvet teklif eder. Rüşvet teklif edilen her proje kurallara aykırıdır.
- **Kabadayı:** Bazı müteahhitler "hayır" cevabını sevmez. Reddedersen ofisinin camı kırılabilir; tamiri sana kalır.
- **Gün sonu:** Afet olursa gazete, onayladığın binaların akıbetini yazar. Olmazsa günün özetini görürsün.
- **Ödeme:** Her gün kira ve kredi ödenir. Kasada yetmeyen gider borca yazılır; borç çok büyürse ofis kapanır.

Oyun 10 gün sürer. Dört farklı son var; hangisini göreceğin, attığın imzalara bağlı.

## Jüri için kısayollar

10 günü baştan sona oynamadan bütün sonları görebilmeniz için oyun sırasında:

| Tuş | Etkisi |
|---|---|
| F9 | Son güne atlar (o günün sonunda son belirlenir) |
| F10 | O gecenin sonunda afet kesin olur |

## Ekip

| Kişi | Rol |
|---|---|
| Ahmet İlman | Oyun mantığı (Core), veri, entegrasyon, build |
| Oğuzhan Yurt | Masa ekranı (belgeler, kararlar, ses ve kaşe) |
| Onur Kabadayılar | Akış ekranları (gazete, gün özeti, ödeme, sonlar, ana menü) |
| Tarık Hokkaömeroğlu | Görsel ve ses, içerik metinleri (müteahhitler, gazete manşetleri, sonlar), asset ve yapay zekâ kaydı |

## Hazır asset ve yapay zekâ kullanımı

Kullanılan bütün hazır asset'ler (lisanslarıyla) ve yapay zekâ kullanımı [`CREDITS_AND_AI.md`](CREDITS_AND_AI.md) dosyasında listelenir. Atıf gerektiren asset'ler oyun içinde ana menü → **Emeği Geçenler** ekranında da gösterilir.

## Hassasiyet notu

Oyundaki bütün kişi, bina, mahalle ve şirket adları kurgusaldır. Gerçek bir afete ya da kişiye atıf yoktur. Oyun, depremden etkilenen insanları değil, yapıları denetleyenlerin sorumluluğunu konu alır.

## Teknik

- Kaynak kod: https://github.com/tarikhokka/GameJam2026TOOADEVS
- Unity **6000.6.4f1**, 2D (URP), uGUI + TextMeshPro, Input System.
- Kod klasörleri: `Assets/_Project/Scripts/` (`Core`, `Desk`, `Flow`).
- Geliştirici notları: `memory.md` (ortak kararlar), `AHMET.md`, `OGUZHAN.md`, `ONUR.md`.
- Testler: Unity → Window → General → Test Runner → EditMode.

# Hospital Escape

A browser game for iPhone (and any other browser). Your shift ended at 17:00. Get out of the hospital before anyone hands you more work.

## Hospital Escape 3D (`index.html` + `js/`)

A satirical first-person stealth game in Three.js (r128, loaded from cdnjs). German UI. A thoroughly cost-cut hospital in seven sections: Innere (5B), Orthopädie, Radiologie, Dermatologie, Keller, Notaufnahme, Parkhaus P2. The full design is in [`GAME_DESIGN.md`](GAME_DESIGN.md).

- **Start:** a short story scene in the doctors' room (typewriter text, camera pan, pager beeps), then the whiteboard briefing where you pick up to three side missions, then "Mission verstanden" and you play.
- **Stealth instead of a chase:** everyone has a floating triangle. White = unaware, yellow = suspicious and looking at you, red = coming over to talk, green = friendly. Awareness builds up gradually and depends on distance, view cone, light and how you move (standing, sneaking, walking, running). Running makes noise, the flashlight gives you away in the dark.
- **Sneak:** pull the left stick only slightly, or toggle SCHLEICHEN (C).
- **Safe rooms:** on-call room, ward kitchen, store room. Nobody follows you in, and the sofa restores energy and nerves once.
- **One conversation per person:** whoever catches you gets one dialogue (quiz, yes/no, bets, family satisfaction survey) and then leaves for good.
- **People are articulated 3D figures** (legs, knees, arms, elbows, faces, hair, glasses, coats, props) with walk animations. No emoji heads.
- **Side missions:** Bewerbungsmappe, Pünktlich, Dienstfrei, Phantom, Held:in der Nacht, Glow-up.
- **Job offers / endings:** Pharma, Dermatologie (Praxis Dr. Glatt), Beratung, Startup, Gesundheitsamt, Kreuzfahrt, or back on Monday. The end screen shows your duty roster for next month.
- **Also:** creepy dark corridors, flickering lamps, thunderstorm at the windows, shadow figures, the ghost Dr. Ewig in the cellar, MRT pulling metal items, CPR mini-game, phone calls, lab papers on the floor, inventory, compass, waypoint, floor route dots and minimap.
- **Difficulty:** "Entspannt" (default) or "Dienstalltag".
- **Controls:** phone: left stick walk (light = sneak), right side look (joystick or swipe), SCHLEICHEN / RENNEN, yellow button to use, tap LAMPE to switch the flashlight. Keyboard: WASD, mouse (click to capture) or arrows/Q, C sneak, Shift sprint, E action, F flashlight, 1–6 inventory, J/N calls, Tab missions, M mission plan, P pause.

Code layout (plain `<script>` files sharing one global scope, no build step): `js/data.js` (levels, story, dialogue data), `js/world.js` (renderer, textures, 3D people), `js/level.js` (level construction), `js/game.js` (run state, HUD, items, audio), `js/dialog.js` (conversations), `js/play.js` (input, stealth AI, hazards, events), `js/flow.js` (story, briefing, endings, rendering, boot).

## Classic 2D (`classic.html`)

The original top-down version in English.

## Play

Open `index.html` in a browser; there is no build step. On iPhone, host the folder (for example with GitHub Pages), open it in Safari, then Share → Add to Home Screen to play full screen.

csinva/board-game-web.readme:
# Board Game Web

**Live site:** https://csinva.io/board-game-web/

One illustrated page per board game, with every rule needed to play, plus tools to find similar games.

- **`index.html`**: every game, filterable by players, length and family.
- **`game.html?g=<id>`**: the game's page (see below). Prints on one landscape page.
- **`map.html`**: games linked by hand-curated "plays like" pairs (hover a line for why), grouped by family, or on a chart of any two traits. Heavy games are ringed.
- **`deepdive.html`** ("Explore games by their traits"): every game scored 0–100 on 11 traits, plotted on any two, plus a player-type profile with recommendations (`?picks=catan,codenames,…` is shareable).

## A game page

Most important first. Rules, in the order you need them:

1. **What it is**: an annotated illustration of the table.
2. **How you win.**
3. **How it ends.**
4. **Your turn**: a chain (do every step), a fork (choose one) or simultaneous play, with an animated walkthrough of a real turn.
5. **How the game flows**: the whole game as a timeline (setup → rounds/phases → end-of-round events → end).
6. **Scoring**: every way to earn points.
7. Setup, a quick-reference table, key terms, and rules people miss. Heavy games add collapsible extended details.

Then **Strategy** (the key decision, first-game tips, where points usually come from) and **Is it for you?** (a feel profile and similar games).

Components appear as icons inline (`{wood}` in the data), drawn the same as in the illustrations. If you know a closely related game, an "Already know…" bar explains only what differs.

## Adding a game

1. Add `js/games/<id>.js` following [`SCHEMA.md`](SCHEMA.md) (copy `js/games/catan.js`).
2. Add the id to `GAME_IDS` in `js/core.js`.
3. Add its trait scores to `js/deepdive-data.js`, and any genuine "plays like" pairs to `js/kin.js` (with a bridge in `js/bridges/` if knowing one teaches the other).
4. Run `tools/validate.sh <id>` (macOS JavaScriptCore; no build step, no dependencies). `walk-preview.html?g=<id>` shows all walkthrough slides at once.

The site is plain static HTML/JS. Serve locally with `python3 -m http.server`.

gabrielflorianoo/Vic3-Inspired.readme:
# Iron & Society

A performance-first historical grand-strategy game (Godot 4.3, Compatibility renderer, GDScript).
**Current state: playable vertical slice.** Main menu, province-based nation pick, then a monthly/weekly
simulation of population, a market economy, politics, technology, diplomacy/war and AI countries,
with save/load. Fictional 1836-style world of 14 countries and 205 provinces.

| Menu | Nation pick |
|---|---|
| ![Main menu](docs/screenshots/menu.jpg) | ![Nation pick](docs/screenshots/pick.jpg) |
| ![Market](docs/screenshots/game_market.jpg) | ![Politics](docs/screenshots/game_politics.jpg) |

## Requirements
- Godot **4.3-stable** (standard build, not .NET). Uses the `gl_compatibility` renderer (OpenGL 3.3), which fits the target GPU class (Radeon R7 350).

## Run
```sh
godot --path .                       # main menu: New Game / Continue / Load Game / Settings / Quit
godot --path . -- --benchmark        # scripted map benchmark, prints results and quits
godot --path . -- --low              # disables ocean animation + vignette
```
Or open `project.godot` in the editor and press F5.

**New Game**: click any province, then *Play as ...*: you rule the country that owns it. The game starts paused
(press Space). **Continue** loads the newest save (autosave is monthly by default; Settings changes this).

### Controls
| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| LMB | select province (opens the province card) |
| drag LMB/RMB/MMB, WASD / arrows | pan |
| wheel | zoom to cursor |
| `Space` | pause / resume |
| `1`-`5` | speed 1 (1 day/s), 2 (3), 3 (8), 4 (20), 5 (maximum) |
| `+` / `-` | faster / slower |
| `F5` / `F6` / `F7` | map mode: Political / Terrain / Provinces |
| `L` | toggle labels |
| `F3` | cycle performance overlay (off / compact / detailed) |
| `F9` | map benchmark |
| `Esc` | close dialog / clear selection / pause menu |

Top-bar tabs: Overview (budget, taxes), Market, Buildings (queue construction), Population, Politics (laws, interest groups),
Technology (pick research), Diplomacy (relations, alliances, trade, claims, war and peace), Military, Events.

### Dev / CI arguments (after `--`)
`--autostart=N` skip menu and pick, play country N - `--continue` load the newest save - `--newgame` go straight to nation pick -
`--tab=overview|market|buildings|population|politics|technology|diplomacy|military|events` - `--speed=0..5` -
`--run-days=N` simulate N days before the first frame - `--pause-menu` - `--open=settings|load` (menu) -
`--select=P` select province - `--view=x,y,zoom` - `--mode=0..2` - `--shot=path.png [--shot-delay=s]` save a screenshot and quit -
`--monkey=SECONDS` UI fuzzer (random tabs and buttons while running) - `--benchmark` - `--low`.

## Tests
```sh
sh tests/run_all.sh                                           # both suites below; exit code 0 = pass
godot --headless --path . --script res://tests/run_tests.gd      # world, sim core, economy, population, saves
godot --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_strategy.gd  # politics, tech, diplomacy, war, AI, determinism + save
godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/sim_benchmark.gd  # 5-year sim: per-subsystem tick cost, save size
```
Always wrap headless runs in `timeout` (a script error can leave Godot hanging), e.g. `timeout 400 godot --headless ...`.
Rendered run under Xvfb:
`timeout 90 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x720x24" godot --path . --audio-driver Dummy --rendering-driver opengl3 -- --autostart=3 --run-days=365 --tab=market --shot=/tmp/a.png`

## Regenerate the world
The map is baked offline, so no generation happens at runtime:
```sh
godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/generate_world.gd [-- --seed=1836 --provinces=220 --size=2048]
```
Output goes to `data/generated/` (terrain + province-ID images as compressed `.res`, plus `world.json`).

## Export
`export_presets.cfg` defines **Windows Desktop** and **Linux** presets (the `include_filter` packs
`data/scenario/*.json` and `data/generated/*.json`, which are not Godot resources). Install the 4.3 export templates, then:
```sh
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Windows Desktop" build/windows/IronAndSociety.exe
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Linux" build/linux/IronAndSociety.x86_64
```
Saves go to `user://saves/` (`~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/Iron & Society/saves/` on Linux).

## Layout
```
project.godot            engine config (Compatibility renderer, 1280x720, autoload Session)
scenes/main_menu.tscn    main scene -> src/ui/main_menu.gd
scenes/game.tscn         game scene -> src/main.gd (map + HUD + controller)
docs/GAMEPLAY_SPEC.md    module contracts (simulation, AI, UI); docs/DEVLOG.md decisions + measurements
src/game/                session.gd (autoload: scene flow, new/load/save), game_controller.gd (speed, time-sliced
                         stepping), settings.gd, monkey.gd (dev UI fuzzer)
src/sim/                 game_state.gd (calendar, module wiring, events), population.gd, economy.gd, politics.gd,
                         technology.gd, diplomacy.gd, military.gd, ai.gd, save_system.gd, sim_util.gd
src/ui/                  main_menu.gd, nation_pick.gd, game_hud.gd (top bar, tabs, toasts), ui_kit.gd, settings_screen.gd,
                         perf_overlay.gd, panels/*.gd (one per tab, pause menu, save/load dialog, province card)
src/world/               biome.gd, id_codec.gd, world_generator.gd (offline), world_data.gd (runtime tables)
src/map/                 map_view.gd + map.gdshader (whole map = 1 quad), map_camera.gd, map_overlay.gd
src/benchmark/           map_benchmark.gd
tools/                   generate_world.gd, sim_benchmark.gd
tests/                   run_tests.gd, test_strategy.gd, run_all.sh (+ fake_state/fake_pops helpers)
data/scenario/           countries, goods, buildings, laws, interest groups, techs (JSON)
data/generated/          baked map assets
TODO.md                  prioritised backlog
```

MarioArchives/ui-mocks.readme:
# UI mocks

Phone-first UI mocks for [Quest-Game](https://github.com/MarioArchives/Quest-Game): try a screen in your hand before it
is built into the game. Each mock is a plain front-end page with made-up data, no Firebase and no backend.

## Mocks

| Mock | Game | What to try |
|---|---|---|
| [Booking desk](https://marioarchives.github.io/ui-mocks/#/booking) (`#/booking`) | Mystery Pub Crawl | What a new player sees after signing in with Google: fill in your particulars on a manila booking sheet, then press and hold the livescan glass to have your "prints" taken (nothing is read; it only looks the part). Ends on your booked file, waiting for the GM. Android phones buzz along; iPhones don't support vibration from a web page. |

## On your phone

- **Published:** every push to `main` builds and publishes to GitHub Pages (see `.github/workflows/pages.yml`), at
  `https://marioarchives.github.io/ui-mocks/`. One-off setup: Settings › Pages › Source = "GitHub Actions".
- **From this machine, same Wi-Fi:** `npm run phone` starts the dev server on your network and prints a QR code. Scan
  it and edits hot-reload on the phone as you save.
- **Add to Home Screen** opens the mocks full screen, without the browser bars, which is closest to how the game feels.

## Commands

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `npm run phone` | Dev server on your network, plus a QR code to open it on a phone. |
| `npm run dev` | Dev server on http://localhost:5180 (also on your network). |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript, silent on success. |
| `npm run build` | Static build in `dist/`; works from any host or sub-path (relative base, hash routing). |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the build on :5181. |

Node 24 (`.nvmrc`). With nvm: `export PATH=~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.1/bin:$PATH`.

## Adding a mock

1. Make a folder `src/mocks/<id>/` whose default export is a full-screen component, with its own CSS.
2. Add it to `MOCKS` in `src/mocks/index.ts` (id, title, one-line blurb, game, backdrop colour).
3. It gets a row on the list and its own link, `#/<id>`. A small "‹ Mocks" pill in the top right leads back.

For a game's look, import its theme from `src/themes/` (`mystery.css` copies the mystery pack's tokens and fonts from
Quest-Game's `src/packs/mystery/theme.css`; keep them in step when the game's change). Use 16px or larger type in
inputs, or iPhones zoom in when you tap them.

alternatefact/eko-rising.readme:
# Eko Rising

Build Lagos from scratch. Start as a farmer and his wife by the lagoon, grow a
yam farm into a compound, a town, a port city and a modern metropolis, and decide
how the history of Nigeria goes: trade with the Portuguese or send them away,
stand up to Benin and the British, and unite the peoples of the land into
**The New Nigeria**.

An original game by [alternatefact Studios](https://alternatefactstudios.com/).
Play it at **https://alternatefactstudios.com/games/eko-rising/**.

## How it plays

Strangers arrive when your people are fed and happy. They wait at the campfire
(or the town square once there is a palace) until you build them a home, then
move in and work wherever they are needed: woodcutters, yam and cassava farmers,
garri makers, hunters, fishermen, palm oil pressers, miners and smiths.

The settlement grows through five ages: farmstead, compound, town, port city and
metropolis. Moving up an age needs people, money and a number of neighbouring
kingdoms conquered or paying tribute. Money comes from taxes, the market, trade
agreements with other kingdoms and merchant ships at the port, and pays for
buildings, upgrades, trained soldiers and hired fighters.

Along the way you meet the Awori, Egun, Egba, Ijebu and the Edo war camp, and
can befriend, trade with, subjugate or conquer each of them. Benin, the
Portuguese, the Atlantic trade, the French and the British arrive as your
progress brings them, and each asks for a choice. The chapter ends when every
people is united, the foreign question is settled, and The New Nigeria is
proclaimed.

## Run it

It is plain ES modules with no build step. Serve the folder with any static
server and open it in a browser:

```bash
npm start            # serves on http://localhost:8080
```

The game draws in 3D with three.js (bundled in `js/vendor/`) and falls back to
a hand-drawn 2D view where WebGL is not available. Players can switch between
them from the in-game menu.

## Code

```
index.html    the page; css/game.css styles it
js/main.js    boots the game, the loop, saving and the renderer
js/sim/       the simulation, with no DOM: economy, citizens, military, factions, trade, events
js/world/     terrain types, map generator, A* pathfinding
js/data/      buildings, units, resources, ages, names, the art catalogue
js/regions/   one file per state; lagos.js is chapter one
js/render3d/  3D cartoon view: ground.js land and water, flora.js trees and grass,
              models.js buildings, people.js people and soldiers
js/render/    2D canvas renderer, hand-drawn sprites, minimap
js/ui/        HUD, panels, story pop-ups, mouse/touch/keyboard input, settings
art/          painted story art, portraits, age pictures, and ground, plant and building textures
brand/        studio logo and favicon
tests/        headless simulation tests and a scripted player
```

The art in `art/` was made with Higgsfield and is listed in `js/data/art.js`;
anything missing from that list falls back to emoji art or textures drawn in
code.

To open another state, copy `js/regions/lagos.js` (terrain template, peoples,
places to explore, events, goals), register it in `js/regions/index.js`, and
give its entry in `STATES` a region id.

## Tests

The tests run the simulation headless, including a scripted player that plays
through the ages. They need Node 20 or newer and nothing else:

```bash
npm test
```

They also run on every push.

## Publishing on the studio site

The live game is a copy of this folder at
`frontend/public/games/eko-rising/` in the `Alternatefact-site` repository.
To release a new version, copy everything except `tests/`, `package.json`,
`README.md` and `.github/` into that folder and deploy the site.

## Ownership

© 2026 alternatefact Studios. All rights reserved. Eko Rising, its story, art
and code are the property of alternatefact Studios.

three.js is © its authors and used under the MIT License; see
`js/vendor/three.LICENSE`.

# Mountain Mogul

Build a ski resort on an untouched mountain: clear trees, cut trails, run chairlifts,
and keep thousands of skiers happy through a full winter of weather.

**Play:** https://mtmogul.com/

## How it's put together

- `index.html` is the whole game (three.js for the 3D mountain).
- `vendor/` holds the libraries it loads: three.js r128 and supabase-js 2.110.0.
- Online features (accounts, cloud saves, leaderboards, visiting other resorts) use
  [Supabase](https://supabase.com). `supabase/schema.sql` creates the one table they need.
- The page is served by GitHub Pages straight from the `main` branch.

## Setting up Supabase (one time)

1. SQL Editor → New query → paste `supabase/schema.sql` → Run.
2. Authentication → Sign In / Providers → turn on **Allow anonymous sign-ins**
   (players start as guests, no sign-up needed). Email should already be on.
3. Authentication → URL Configuration → set **Site URL** to
   `https://mtmogul.com/` and add the same address under
   **Redirect URLs**, so email sign-in links come back to the game.

The publishable key in `index.html` is meant to be public. Never put the secret or
`service_role` key in this repository.

quzopl/anyps5-converter.desc: One-click GUI/CLI converter for AnyPS5: turn a decrypted PS5 game dump into a native Windows, Linux or macOS program
quzopl/anyps5-converter.readme:
# AnyPS5 Converter

One-click front end for [AnyPS5](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5): point it at a PS5 game dump and get a native Windows, Linux or macOS program.

![AnyPS5 Converter window](docs/screenshot.png)

AnyPS5 is not an emulator. Its relinker rewrites a PS5 executable into a native program that runs against reimplemented system libraries. Converting a game by hand takes several steps: unwrap every SELF container, find the module folders, pick the right relinker flags for your CPU, download the matching libraries and lay out `libs/` and `app0/`. This tool does all of that for you.

## Features

- **GUI and command line**: a single Python file, standard library only.
- **Cross-platform**: runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, and builds for Windows, Linux or macOS targets.
- **CPU selection**: detects your CPU and picks the right mode:
  - AMD: native, no flags.
  - Intel: `--to-intel`.
  - Apple Silicon: `--to-rosetta`.
  - You can override the detected mode.
- **Automatic SELF unwrapping**: `eboot.bin`, `sce_module/`, Unity `Media/Plugins` and `Media/Modules`, and any other folder with modules. Encrypted files are detected and reported.
- **Automatic downloads**: fetches the relinker and system libraries from the AnyPS5 GitHub release (latest or a chosen version) and caches them.
- **No 25 GB copies**: on the same OS, `app0/` is built from hard links and junctions/symlinks to the original files. Choose copy mode to move the game to another machine or OS.
- **Patches (game updates)**: select a decrypted patch folder and it is layered on top of the base game. Patch files override base files, everything else is linked from the base dump, and nothing is copied or modified.
- **Safe rebuilds**: converting again into the same folder rebuilds the program and keeps save data (`_sd`, `data`) and the shader cache.

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+ (on Linux the GUI needs `python3-tk`)
- A **decrypted** PS5 game dump: the folder with `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/`, `sce_module/`, …
- To run the converted game: an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, FMA, F16C, BMI1/2, LZCNT and MOVBE, and a Vulkan GPU.

## Usage

### GUI

- **Windows**: double-click `AnyPS5-Converter.bat`.
- **Linux/macOS**: run `./anyps5-converter.sh`.

Select the game folder (or `eboot.bin`), adjust the options if needed and click **Convert**.

### Command line

```sh
python anyps5_converter.py <game folder | eboot.bin> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--patch DIR` | Decrypted game update (patch) folder to layer on top of the base game |
| `-o, --output DIR` | Output folder (default `<game folder>_<os>`) |
| `--os windows\|linux\|macos` | Target OS (default: this computer) |
| `--cpu auto\|amd\|intel\|rosetta` | Target CPU: `amd` keeps the code as is, `intel` adds `--to-intel`, `rosetta` is for Apple Silicon (macOS only) |
| `--version vX.Y.Z` | AnyPS5 release (default: latest) |
| `--link-mode auto\|link\|copy` | Game files in `app0/`: links (no extra disk space) or a full copy. `auto` links when the target OS is this OS and copies otherwise |
| `--run` | Launch the game after conversion |
| `--windows-gui` | Windows program without a console window (output goes to `anyps5.log`) |
| `--include-executables`, `--executable PATH` | Extra game executables started with `sceSystemServiceLoadExec` |
| `--relinker FILE`, `--libs DIR` | Custom relinker / libraries (required for macOS, see below) |
| `--extra ARG` | Extra argument passed to the relinker (repeatable) |
| `--force`, `--keep-stage`, `-v` | Write into a non-empty folder, keep the unwrapped ELF files, verbose log |

Examples:

```sh
python anyps5_converter.py D:\PS5\PPSA12345                        # Windows build for this PC
python anyps5_converter.py D:\PS5\PPSA12345 --os linux -o E:\game  # Linux build (files copied)
python anyps5_converter.py ~/games/PPSA12345 --cpu amd --run
python anyps5_converter.py D:\PS5\PPSA12345 --patch D:\PS5\PPSA12345-patch   # base game + update
```

## Patches and DLC

**Patches** are supported. AnyPS5 only reads the game from `app0`, so the update has to be merged with the base game. Select the patch folder in the **Patch** field (or pass `--patch`) and the tool does the merge for you:

- Files in the patch replace the same files in the base game. This includes `eboot.bin`, `sce_module/`, plugins and `sce_sys/param.json`.
- Files only in the base game or only in the patch are both kept.
- The patch must be a **decrypted** dump, like the base game. Many dumpers can also dump base + patch already merged; in that case just select that folder as the game.
- The tool checks that the patch's `titleId` matches the game (override with `--force`) and logs both versions (`contentVersion`).

**DLC (add-on content)** is not supported yet. AnyPS5's `libSceAppContent` currently reports no add-on content for every entitlement, so games cannot mount or see DLC ([libSceAppContent debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/debt/libSceAppContent.md)).

## Output layout

```text
<output>/
  Game.exe | Game.elf | Game   converted program
  libs/                         AnyPS5 system libraries
  app0/                         game files + converted modules (*.guest.prx)
```

Start the program from its folder. On Linux, if you get a `/dev/udmabuf` error, add your user to the `kvm` group.

## How it works

1. Layers the patch (if any) over the base game, then finds `eboot.bin` and every folder with `.prx`/`.sprx` modules. `sce_sys/` and `fakelib/` are skipped because AnyPS5 provides those libraries.
2. Unwraps SELF/fSELF containers into clean ELF files with [`unwrap_self.py`](unwrap_self.py) from AnyPS5.
3. Downloads `relinker` and `prx-<os>` for the chosen release into `cache/`.
4. Builds `app0/`, then runs the relinker with `--windows`/`--macos`, `--to-intel`/`--to-rosetta` and one `--module-dir` per module folder.
5. Copies `libs/` and writes `.anyps5-converter.json`, which later rebuilds use.

## Limitations

- **Encrypted dumps are refu

RedNoos/topo-heli.readme:
# Topo Heli

A browser topography game: fly a helicopter over a map and find as many cities as you can before time runs out.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # static site in dist/
```

## How it plays

- Arrow keys / WASD to fly. On touch screens, drag anywhere to get a virtual joystick.
- Fly within range of the city and a flashing dot appears; fly over it to score.
- You start with 3:00. Every 10 cities: +1:00 and the next level. Each level adds smaller towns
  to the pool and the dot appears later (smaller reveal radius).
- `N` skips a city (−10 s), `P`/`Esc` pauses, `M` toggles sound.

**Mountains, rivers & lakes** (Serbia; rivers only for the Netherlands; switch on the start screen): physical features are mixed in
with the cities. Lakes and mountains are found by flying over them. Rivers are found by *following*
them: the bar fills with the length of river you have flown along (40 km, or 60% of a short river);
simply crossing a river covers only ~8 km. Best scores are kept per map and mode.

**Languages:** English, Dutch, Serbian Latin and Serbian Cyrillic (flag menu on the start screen;
the default follows the browser's language list, falling back to English). UI text
lives in [src/i18n.ts](src/i18n.ts); Serbian is written once in Latin script and transliterated to
Cyrillic. Place names: Serbia uses its (Serbian Latin) names, Europe has Serbian and Dutch names in
`src/maps/europe/names.sr.json` / `names.nl.json`, Dutch town names are kept as-is.

Tuning lives in [src/config.ts](src/config.ts).

**Provinces** (Netherlands): pick a province in the list under the map buttons to play only that
province: its map, its places (capital always in level 1) and, where there are any, its rivers.

## Adding a map

1. Add an entry to `MAPS` in [scripts/build-map.mjs](scripts/build-map.mjs): the Natural Earth
   country codes that form the playable area, a bounding box, and how to group the internal
   borders.
2. Run `npm run build:map -- <id>`. This downloads Natural Earth data into `.cache/` and writes
   `src/maps/<id>/geo.json`.
   Optional settings there: `projection` (equal-area, for large regions), `colorCountries`
   (a colour per country with clear borders) and `merge` (draw a territory as part of a country).
3. Add `src/maps/<id>/cities.json`: `{ name, lat, lon, pop, level? }`. Population decides which
   cities appear at which level; `level` puts a city in play from that level regardless of size
   (used for capitals).
4. Register the map in [src/maps/index.ts](src/maps/index.ts) (`viewKm` sets the zoom level:
   larger regions want a larger value).

## Physical features

Dutch places and provinces: the curated list is [data/netherlands-cities.json](data/netherlands-cities.json);
`npm run build:places` adds municipality seats (OpenStreetMap) and villages of 2,000+ inhabitants
(GeoNames) and writes the per-province lists. In the whole-country map the added places only come
up from level 6. Build order after changing map data: `build:map` → `build:places` → `build:physical`.
Province definitions: [scripts/provinces.mjs](scripts/provinces.mjs).



`npm run build:physical` queries OpenStreetMap (Overpass API) for the rivers, lakes and peaks
listed in [scripts/build-physical.mjs](scripts/build-physical.mjs) and writes
`src/maps/<id>/physical.json`. Each feature has a `level` that decides when it can be asked.

## Credits

Inspired by *Topografie Nederland* (Radarsoft, Commodore 64, 1984), whose helicopter game had
the same idea: fly to a named place before time runs out; it appears as a pulsing dot once you
are close.

## Data

- Borders, rivers and lakes: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) (public domain).
  The Europe map uses the internationally recognised borders (Natural Earth's German point of
  view), with Kosovo drawn as part of Serbia on every map.

Catherine1708/lol-esports-prediction.desc: Predicting pro League of Legends matches with Elo team ratings and champion draft features (2020-2025)
Catherine1708/lol-esports-prediction.readme:
# Pro League of Legends: Team Ratings & Draft Win Prediction

How well can we predict who wins a professional League of Legends game, and
does the champion draft add anything beyond how strong the two teams are?
This project uses 65,894 pro games from 2020–2025. It builds an Elo rating
system for every team, turns each side's champion picks into draft features,
and compares models that use team strength, the draft, or both. Every feature
uses only games played before the one being predicted, and all results are
for the unseen 2025 season.

**Headline finding: team strength does almost all the predicting.** Team
ratings pick the winner in 65.7% of 2025 first-division games, against 52.8%
for always picking the blue side. Adding the champion draft lowers log loss by
only 0.002 (95% interval −0.001 to 0.005) and does not change accuracy.

**[View the results page →](https://catherine1708.github.io/lol-esports-prediction/)**

**Tech stack:** Python · DuckDB (SQL) · pandas · scikit-learn · matplotlib ·
pytest · static HTML/CSS/JS with Chart.js on GitHub Pages

---

## Results at a glance

| Model (2025 test, 2,611 first-division games) | Log loss | Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Always blue side | 0.692 | 52.8% |
| Better season win rate so far | 0.653 | 62.9% |
| Draft only (logistic regression) | 0.689 | 54.0% |
| Plain Elo | 0.633 | 64.4% |
| Refined Elo | 0.616 | 65.6% |
| Rating only (logistic regression) | 0.617 | 65.7% |
| **Rating + draft (logistic regression)** | **0.614** | **65.6%** |

Lower log loss is better.

- **Team strength is what predicts results.** In the combined model, rating
  difference outweighs the strongest draft feature by about 6 to 1.
- **The draft signal is real but small.** Draft features are almost
  uncorrelated with team strength (r = 0.04), but on their own they barely
  beat a coin flip.
- **Cross-region information matters.** Letting MSI and Worlds results adjust
  whole regions raised accuracy on 2025 international games from 58.5% to
  64.8%.
- **A more flexible model does not help.** Gradient boosting is no better than
  logistic regression.

Full write-ups:
[rating system design and results](reports/ratings.md) ·
[draft findings and limitations](reports/findings.md)

## How it works

1. **Data pipeline** ([`ingest.py`](src/lolpred/ingest.py),
   [`sql/01_games.sql`](sql/01_games.sql)). Loads the yearly CSVs into
   DuckDB and reshapes them to one row per game: date, league, patch, both
   teams, the winner, and each side's picks by role and bans.
2. **Team ratings** ([`ratings.py`](src/lolpred/ratings.py),
   [`rating_eval.py`](src/lolpred/rating_eval.py)). Elo, updated after
   every game in date order. Refinements add a blue-side advantage,
   regression toward the league average between seasons, league-average
   starting ratings for new teams, and a cross-league adjustment. Each is
   tuned on 2024.
3. **Draft features** ([`features.py`](src/lolpred/features.py),
   [`sql/02_draft_features.sql`](sql/02_draft_features.sql)). For each pick,
   the champion's earlier win rate and pick count, overall and on the current
   patch window, smoothed toward 50%. These are summarised per side as
   blue-minus-red differences.
4. **Models** ([`models.py`](src/lolpred/models.py),
   [`model_eval.py`](src/lolpred/model_eval.py)). Logistic regression and
   gradient boosting on rating only, draft only, and both. They train on
   2021–2023, are tuned on 2024 and tested on 2025, with a bootstrap interval
   for the draft's added value.
5. **Results page** ([`export.py`](src/lolpred/export.py), [`docs/`](docs/)).
   Small summary files and a static page.

**No look-ahead.** Ratings, champion statistics and baselines use only
earlier games, and train, validation and test splits are by time. Automated
tests check this by changing a past result or removing future games and
confirming that earlier predictions do not move.

## Data

Match data comes from **[Oracle's Elixir](https://oracleselixir.com/)** by Tim
Sevenhuysen, which publishes free yearly CSVs of professional LoL games. All
credit for collecting and maintaining the data goes to Oracle's Elixir. The
raw data is not redistributed in this repository.

| Year | Games | Leagues | Partial data | Blue-side win rate |
|------|------:|--------:|-------------:|-------------------:|
| 2020 |  9,740 | 52 |  1.4% | 52.7% |
| 2021 | 12,291 | 60 |  9.6% | 52.7% |
| 2022 | 12,519 | 55 | 15.1% | 52.5% |
| 2023 | 11,097 | 52 | 15.6% | 53.3% |
| 2024 | 10,203 | 53 | 13.6% | 53.1% |
| 2025 | 10,044 | 45 |  8.2% | 53.3% |
| **Total** | **65,894** | **102** | | **52.9%** |

All leagues feed the ratings and champion statistics. Predictions are scored
only on first-division games: LCK, LPL, LEC, LCS/CBLOL/LLA (the LTA from
2025), PCS/VCS/LJL (the LCP from 2025), MSI and Worlds.

Cleaning decisions:

- **Partial games are kept.** Oracle's Elixir marks some games as `partial`
  (missing some in-game stats). Much of the LPL and LDL is partial, but picks
  and results are present, which is all this project needs.
- **15 of 65,909 games (0.02%) are dropped:** 2 have no recorded winner, 12
  list the same team on both sides (a source error in minor leagues), and 1
  has an unidentified team. Dropped games are kept in a `games_dropped` table
  with the reason.
- **Teams are identified by Oracle's Elixir `teamid`**, so rebrands don't
  create new teams. Where `teamid` is missing (about 900 games, mostly LJL), it
  is recovered from the team name when that name maps to exactly one id.
- **`date` is used for time ordering, not `year`.** The `year` column is a
  season label: some qualifiers played in late 2025 are labelled 2026.
- **Bans are missing for about 2,600 games**, mostly LDL. Picks are complete.

## Reproduce

Requires Python 3.11+. Works on macOS, Linux and Windows.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Catherine1708/lol-esports-prediction.git
cd lol-esports-prediction
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment:

- macOS / L

rachelmakesfunprojects/omegas-shawarma.readme:
# Omega's Shawarma

A first-person browser game set in a late-night shawarma shop on King St W, Toronto.

**Play it:** https://rachelmakesfunprojects.github.io/omegas-shawarma/

You've got the keys and the boss is stuck at Costco. Open up the shop, layer the meat on the spits, bake the pita, and fill the sauces and topping bar. Then build every wrap by hand for a full day of customers: Bay Street suits, the broccoli-haired mandem, silk merchants with a camel parked on Spadina, date night, and Dave from the night shift. At closing, clean up everything (watch for raccoons).

## How to play

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| W A S D | Walk (Shift to hustle) |
| Mouse | Look |
| Click or E | Use / pick up / add |
| R | Roll the wrap |
| Q | Toss the wrap |
| P or Esc | Pause |
| M | Mute |

On a phone, your left thumb walks, your right thumb looks, and you tap things to use them.

**Making a wrap:** grab a pita from the warmer, carry it to the spits and shave the meat, set it down on the board, add the toppings and sauces, press R to roll it, then hand it to the customer. Click a bin twice for extra.

## The music

Everything you hear is synthesized live in the browser with the Web Audio API. There are no audio files. The track is a Hijaz-scale club tune over a darbuka rhythm, with a synthesized woman's voice singing a Ya Leil-style vocal that comes and goes. You can hear it on its own at [vocal-mix.html](https://rachelmakesfunprojects.github.io/omegas-shawarma/vocal-mix.html).

## Tech

- Single-file HTML. 3D uses [three.js](https://threejs.org/) r128, loaded from cdnjs.
- Every texture, sign and ingredient is drawn in code. There are no image assets.
- Fonts: Lalezar, Reem Kufi, Rubik, Courier Prime and Permanent Marker, from Google Fonts.

To run it locally, open `index.html` in a browser, or serve the folder:

```bash
python3 -m http.server
```

*Omega's is a made-up shop, loosely inspired by the late-night shawarma spots on King Street.*

# videogame

Cookie eats cookies: a tiny 2D game built with Python and [pygame-ce](https://pyga.me/).
Move a hungry cookie around, eat the small cookies, and grow.

## Setup

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate videogame
```

## Run

```bash
videogame            # or: python -m videogame.main
```

The game opens with a short love note (with floating hearts and baby seals); tap or press
any key to continue.

Pick a mode from the menu (tap or click it, or use Up/Down + Enter, or press 1/2):

- **Classic**: eat cookies at your own pace. Touch a small cookie to eat it and grow;
  burnt (dark) cookies shrink you.
- **Challenge**: 20 seconds to eat as many as you can, with burnt cookies too, while
  big angry cookies chase you (one slow, one fast); if one catches you, the round ends.

Controls:
- **Keyboard**: arrow keys / WASD to move, Esc to go back to the menu (or quit from the menu).
- **Touch or mouse**: touch and hold (or click and hold) and the cookie moves toward your finger.
  Tap a mode to start it, and use the on-screen Menu / Play again buttons.

## Browser version

The game also runs in a web browser via [pygbag](https://github.com/pygame-web/pygbag),
which `src/main.py` is the entry point for.

```bash
cd src
python -m pygbag --title "Cookie eats cookies" .   # serves it at http://localhost:8000
python -m pygbag --build --title "Cookie eats cookies" .   # just build into src/build/web
```

Pushing to `main` rebuilds it and publishes it to GitHub Pages
(`.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml`). The page needs a click before the game starts (browsers block audio and focus until then).

## Layout

- `src/main.py`: entry point for the browser build
- `src/videogame/main.py`: game loop, menu, and rounds
- `src/videogame/entities.py`: player, cookies, and chasers
- `src/videogame/settings.py`: window size, colors, speeds, challenge tuning
- `assets/`: images, sounds, fonts

# LSWTSS Level Exporter — version 0.1.0 (first release, early preview)

Exports maps from **LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga** (PC) into Blender `.blend` files: the placed meshes, rebuilt materials with their textures packed inside the file, the map's sky and its authored lights. It reads your own installed copy of the game; **no game files are included** with this tool.

## What you need

- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).
- LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga installed on PC (Steam is detected automatically; any copy works if you browse to its folder — the one containing `GAME.DAT`).
- **Blender**, free from [blender.org](https://www.blender.org/download/). Tested with Blender 5.2; 4.2 or newer is required.
- Disk space: the first export unpacks game files into a cache (several GB, grows as you export more maps). A finished map is typically 100 MB – 1 GB.

You do **not** need Python or .NET installed.

## How to use it

1. Unzip the folder anywhere and run **`LSWTSS Level Exporter.exe`**.
2. Check the **Game folder** and **Blender** paths (filled in automatically when found).
3. Choose an **Output folder** (default `Documents\LSWTSS Exports`).
4. Click **Load level list**. The first time this indexes the game archives and takes a few minutes.
5. Pick a map (type in **Search** to filter, e.g. `kachirho` or `federal`) and click **Export selected level**.
6. Wait. Small maps take a few minutes; big hub planets can take 15–30 minutes and need plenty of RAM (16 GB+ recommended for the largest).
7. Open the `.blend` from the output folder. Use **Material Preview** to look around; render with **Cycles** for the game-like lighting.

Windows SmartScreen may warn that the app is unrecognised (it is not code-signed). Choose **More info → Run anyway** only if you got this copy from a source you trust.

## What gets exported

- Static map geometry: models, GSC objects (LEGO builds and props), painted foliage, terrain, projected decals, glow strips/panels, streamed hub puzzle props (initial state).
- Per-placement detail: material overrides and painted vertex colours.
- Materials translated from the game's own shader graphs (all 6,103 game materials compile; ~84% match the game shaders exactly, the rest approximate a few effects — see below).
- HDR sky as the World background, and the game's placed lights.
- Editor helpers, collision and shadow-only meshes are hidden.

Each `.blend` contains two text blocks (Blender's Text Editor): **Level Export Report.json** and **Material Translation Report.json**, listing anything that was skipped or approximated.

## Known limitations (version 0.1.0)

- **Not exported yet:** characters/NPCs, particle effects (fire, smoke, sparks), water surfaces, sand/snow/mud weathering on props, destructible/alternate states.
- **Approximated:** wind sway (rest pose), close-up parallax (within ~4 m), soft fog edges, screen-space glass distortion, leaf translucency, live in-game screens (TVs/terminals show black).
- Only a handful of maps have been checked visually so far; other maps may show problems. Please report them with the map name and a screenshot.
- Lighting is the game's placed lights and sky rendered by Cycles, not the game's baked lightmaps, so it can differ from the game.

## Credits and licences

- Game archive reading uses the BrickVault TTGames DAT reader (C#), built into `ArchiveReader.exe`.
- Oodle decompression uses `oo2core_8_win64.dll` **from your own game installation**; it is not distributed with this tool.
- Built with Python, Pillow, NumPy and PyInstaller.
- LEGO, Star Wars and The Skywalker Saga are trademarks of their respective owners. This is an unofficial fan tool, not affiliated with or endorsed by TT Games, LEGO, Lucasfilm or Warner Bros.

## Download

Get the ready-to-run Windows build from the [Releases page](../../releases): download `LSWTSS_Level_Exporter_v0.1.0_win64.zip`, unzip, and run `LSWTSS Level Exporter.exe`.

## Building from source

- `exporter_app.py` — the desktop app (Tkinter). `exporter_app.py --prepare …` runs the data stage.
- `prepare_level.py` — reads the game archives, decodes scenes, models, GSC objects, terrain, foliage, decals and materials, and writes the build manifests.
- `build_blend.py` + `lib/lswtss_native_lod0/` — runs inside Blender to assemble the scene and compile the materials.
- The archive reader (`ArchiveReader.exe`, BrickVault-based, .NET 10 self-contained) is not part of this source tree; it ships inside the release zip.

Packaged with PyInstaller (`--windowed`, adding `build_blend.py`, `lib/`, `light_schema.json`, `prepare_level.py` and `ArchiveReader.exe` as data).

MagicMiikka/TowerDefense.readme:
# Tower Defense prototype

A compact-grid mazing roguelite where the enemy evolves to counter your build.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Packages/com.tdgame.core/` | **Game logic, no Unity dependencies** (asmdef `TD.Core`, `noEngineReferences`). Grid, pathing, towers, enemies, waves, Essence, the adaptation engine, bots. |
| `Assets/_Project/Scripts/` | **Greybox view** (asmdef `TD.Game`). Draws the sim with coloured shapes, handles mouse and touch, IMGUI HUD. Throwaway. |
| `Tools/TD.Core.Tests/` | Tests for the core, runnable outside Unity. |
| `Tools/TD.Sim/` | Headless balance sim: bots play the run across many seeds. |

## Play the greybox

Open the project and press Play in any scene. A `Prototype Game` object creates itself.

- **1–5**: Wall, Bolt, Flame, Venom, Sell. **Click or tap** a tile to use the tool.
- **Space**: send the next wave (the first is manual; after that waves also come on a timer and can overlap). Sending early pays bonus Essence.
- **F**: speed x1/x2/x4. **P**: pause.

The left panel shows the swarm's learning meter, the incoming adaptation with its reason and weakness,
and (Debug) the counter scores it is weighing.

## Run tests and the balance sim (needs the .NET 8 SDK)

```
cd Tools/TD.Core.Tests && dotnet run -c Release
cd Tools/TD.Sim && dotnet run -c Release -- 50 --log
```

## Rules of the codebase

- Game rules live in `TD.Core` only. The view reads state and drains `SiteSim.Events`; it never decides anything.
- All tuning numbers are in `Balance` (`Runtime/Model/Defs.cs`).
- Layouts are ASCII (`.` ground, `#` rock, `S` spawn, `E` exit). Y grows downward; the view draws tile (x, y) at world (x, -y).
- Determinism: all randomness goes through the `Rng` class, seeded from the run.

tooltonix/strays.readme:
# Strays

A tiny browser game with a speed slider: a stray cat jumps over cardboard boxes.
Built as a hands-on example for the blog post "REA und ‚Software is done': Was
KI-Reverse-Engineering wirklich kann" (in German) on [promptandpixel.dev](https://promptandpixel.dev/).

## What it is about

[REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) ("Reverse Engineer Anything") was used to examine the
speed rule of the Chrome dino game, in the browser build of
[wayou/t-rex-runner](https://github.com/wayou/t-rex-runner) (Chromium code, BSD license).
This game was then built following the **clean-room principle**:

1. Analysis and measurement: [`PROTOCOL.md`](PROTOCOL.md)
2. The rule in our own words, without code: [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md)
3. Rebuild based only on the specification: `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`

Only the rule is borrowed: start at 6, +0.001 per simulation step without a collision, at most
13. Graphics, jump, collision and code are original designs. Unlike the original, the
simulation runs on a fixed 60 Hz tick, so the acceleration does not depend on the refresh rate.

## Run it

No dependencies, no build. Start any static server in this folder, e.g.:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000/>. Jump with Space, arrow up, click or tap.

## Test

`test/test-game.mjs` checks the behaviour with Playwright (increase per second, freeze on
collision, restart at 6, cap at 13) and saves screenshots:

```bash
npm i playwright-core
python3 -m http.server 8766 &
CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chromium node test/test-game.mjs screenshots
```

## Origin and licenses

- Own code, graphics and texts in this repository: MIT license, see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).
- Speed rule from the T-Rex game of the Chromium project, © The Chromium Authors, BSD license;
  analysed in wayou/t-rex-runner (BSD-3-Clause).
- REA: MIT license.

deborahantunes/encaixe-perfeito.desc: Encaixe Molecular VR - educational molecular docking game for Meta Quest (WebXR) and the browser
deborahantunes/encaixe-perfeito.readme:
# Encaixe Molecular VR

**Play:** https://deborahantunes.github.io/encaixe-perfeito/
**Event mode (visitor queue, 3 stages):** https://deborahantunes.github.io/encaixe-perfeito/?evento=3

An educational WebXR game about how medicines work. Grab molecules with your hands and dock them into the
pocket of real proteins to see strong and weak fits, blocking, activation and selectivity. It runs on
**Meta Quest** (VR or mixed reality, with controllers or hand tracking) and in any browser (mouse or touch).
The game is available in Portuguese (pt-BR), English and Spanish.

- **Real proteins:** molecular surfaces generated from PDB structures: trypsin (1BJU), thrombin (1PPB) and the
  β2-adrenergic receptor (2RH1). Their pockets are simplified into three cavities that mirror real features
  (for example, Asp189 at the bottom of the trypsin/thrombin S1 pocket).
- **Fictional molecules:** every ligand is invented. The game does not show or recommend any real medicine.

## How to play on Meta Quest

1. Open the link above in the Quest browser.
2. Tap **Enter Virtual Reality** (or **Mixed Reality**).
3. Point and pull the trigger (or pinch with your fingers) to grab a molecule, turn your wrist to rotate it,
   and release it close to the protein pocket.

After one online visit the game is stored on the device and also works **offline**.

## Event mode (visitor queue)

Designed for science fairs and open-house events with many visitors:

- The headset waits on a **"Ready for the next player!"** panel with a big **START** button.
- Each visitor plays the stages in a row, with no menu. The next stage starts automatically after each win.
- At the end, the panel shows **Congratulations!**, the total time, the time per stage and the best time of the
  day. Then it is immediately ready for the next person.
- Staff choose how many stages each visitor plays: **1 stage** (Stage 1), **2 stages** (Stages 1–2) or
  **3 stages** (full game). Choose on the start screen, on the "Staff" row of the in-headset panel, or with the
  URL: `?evento=1`, `?evento=2`, `?evento=3` (`?evento=0` turns it off). The choice is saved on the device.
- The language is chosen on the start screen (Português / English / Español); the whole game follows it.
- The clock counts playing time only (not the 5 s pause between stages). "Restart" does not reset it.
- "End game" returns to the next-player screen. After 3 minutes with no interaction, the game returns there
  automatically. The result stays on screen for 90 s.
- "Free mode" returns to the regular menu (tutorial, stages and free lab).

## Analytics

Visits are measured with Google Analytics 4 (property **EncaixePerfeito**, measurement ID `G-85PTRY5D21`).
The tag is loaded only on the published site (`deborahantunes.github.io`), never in local development.
Besides page views, the game sends a few custom events:

| Event | Parameters |
| --- | --- |
| `play_start` | `mode` (`vr`, `mixed_reality`, `browser`), `event_phases` |
| `level_complete` | `level`, `event_mode`, `xr` |
| `event_run_start` | `phases` |
| `event_run_complete` | `phases`, `total_seconds`, `day_record` |

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev                              # development server
pnpm test                             # docking rules, translations and event-mode tests (vitest)
pnpm run manus:build-source           # production build in dist/ (with offline service worker)
node scripts/smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:3000/   # end-to-end browser test
python3 scripts/proteins/build.py     # regenerate public/proteins/*.glb and src/game/proteins.json
```

Every push to `main` is built and published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.

### Code map

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/game/data.ts` | Molecules, protein targets and stages |
| `src/game/rules.ts` | Docking rules (size + chemistry scoring) |
| `src/core/analytics.ts` | Google Analytics loader and custom events |
| `src/game/event.ts` | Event mode settings, timing and best time of the day |
| `src/game/game.ts` | Scene, menus, stages and animations |
| `src/game/models.ts` | Protein surfaces and 3D molecules |
| `src/core/pointers.ts` | Controllers, hands and mouse |
| `src/i18n/*.json` | English and Spanish translations (Portuguese text is the key) |

## Credits

Developed by **NUBBICS** — Núcleo de Bioinformática e Biologia Computacional em Saúde.

John-ODell/freeciv-macos27.readme:
# freeciv-macos27

Getting [Freeciv](https://www.freeciv.org/) running well on macOS 27 (Apple Silicon), then improving it.

Freeciv is the GPL empire-building game inspired by Civilization I/II. This repo holds
the macOS 27 port work: notes, build scripts, exported patches against upstream, and
packaging. It does not contain Freeciv itself, Civ2 code, or any Civ2 assets.

## Layout

| Path | What it is | In git? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refs/` | Shallow clones of the upstream repos (`freeciv`, `freeciv-S3_2`, `freeciv-web`, `freeciv-environments`, `freeciv-website`). Read-only reference. | No |
| `port/` | Working fork of Freeciv where fixes are made and built. Its own git repo. | No |
| `patches/` | Patches exported from `port/` with `git format-patch`, one per concern, upstreamable. | Yes |
| `scripts/` | `build.sh` (configure+build+install), `test.sh` (autogame + save/load probe), `bundle.sh` + `fix-dylibs.py` (self-contained .app with a compiled `launcher.c` and the `collect-licenses.py` notices), `sign-app.sh` (ad-hoc or Developer ID, hardened runtime), `dmg.sh` (DMG, optional notarization), and the probe helpers used for the evidence. | Yes |
| `notes/` | Findings: project map, reproduction logs, REA analysis of prebuilt apps, root cause, plan, backlog, install log, Civ4/5 planning menu (`civ45-planning.md`), the proposal for the port, civ45 and civ54 as two or three games (`game-directions.md`), and the Freeciv45 build plan (`freeciv45-plan.md`, research in `freeciv45/`). | Yes |
| `downloads/` | Prebuilt macOS apps and tarballs used for diagnosis. | No |
| `inbox/` | Notes between this desk and other Claude desks (rules in `inbox/README.md`). Local only. | No |

## Download (macOS 27, Apple Silicon)

Releases: https://github.com/John-ODell/freeciv-macos27/releases. Each release has `Freeciv-<version>-arm64.dmg`,
its `.sha256`, and `freeciv-<version>-src.tar.gz`, the exact source the DMG was built from (upstream S3_2 plus
`patches/`). The app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized, so the first launch of a downloaded copy is refused by
Gatekeeper. Either open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway after the refusal, or run:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Freeciv.app
```

# Нефритовый стержень

Кликер с ритмом: води платком по стержню вверх и вниз. Если держать ровный темп, монеты капают. Если темп падает, бусины сгорают. Темп выше предельного не засчитывается. За монеты в Лавке продаются улучшения и украшения. По мазкам растёт ранг: 80 рангов на 10 ступенях.

Фон — старый плакат в сепии: солнце с лучами и звездой, дворец, заводы, колосья, падающие золотые звёзды. Ещё фонари, мудрые цитаты и музыка: три трека играют по кругу.

## Файлы

| Файл | Что это |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | разметка, вид и логика страницы |
| `rules.js` | темп, ранги и цены Лавки |
| `audio/` | музыка: три трека в AAC (`.m4a`) |

## Онлайн-режим

Страница может работать с сервером игры: тогда монеты и прогресс хранятся там, а Лавка покупает за серверный баланс. Адрес сервера задаётся параметром ссылки и в коде страницы не записан. Без него игра работает сама и хранит прогресс в браузере (`localStorage`).

## Приватность

- Шрифты подгружаются с Google Fonts.
- В браузере сохраняются только прогресс игры без сервера и настройка звука, в `localStorage`.
