ddjess/bits-fetch.readme:
# 🦴 Bits Fetch

A tiny 8-bit fetch game that sends **traces, logs, custom metrics and RUM** to Datadog.
Hold to charge, let go to throw, and Bits (a good white dog with a purple collar) runs out, jumps over things, and brings the bone back. Usually.

![Bits jumping mid-fetch](docs/screenshots/jump.png)

Each throw is **one distributed trace across five Python services**. The trace starts when the bone leaves your hand and ends when Bits returns it, so trace duration matches what you see on screen.

| Hold to charge | Bringing it back | Good dog! |
|---|---|---|
| ![Power meter and aim preview](docs/screenshots/charge.png) | ![Bits carrying the bone home](docs/screenshots/return.png) | ![Good dog speech bubble](docs/screenshots/good-dog.png) |

```
Browser (RUM + Session Replay)
   │  POST /throw  (streams each phase back as it happens)
   ▼
thrower-api ──► terrain-service   where did it land? grass / mud (slow) / pond
     │
     ├──────► dog-service ──► jump-service   random 0–3 jumps per run, one span each
     │
     └──────► bone-service ──► terrain-service   dig it out (retries once)
```

| Signal | What gets sent |
|---|---|
| **Traces** | `bone.fetch` root, `bone.flight`, `dog.run`, `dog.jump`, `bone.dig` retries, `bone.deliver` |
| **Logs** | `fetch!` on throw, `good dog!` on return, `bad dog...` on failure. JSON, trace-correlated |
| **Metrics** | `dog.bone.thrown`, `dog.bone.returned` (DogStatsD counts, tagged `dog_name`, `throw_distance`, `terrain`) |
| **RUM** | Sessions, Session Replay, custom actions `throw_bone`, `bone_returned`, `fetch_failed`, linked to backend traces |

### Built-in failures (about 15% of throws)

| Failure | Rate | What you'll see |
|---|---|---|
| 🐿️ Squirrel | 6% | Error span on `dog-service`, Bits runs off-screen, the bone is never returned |
| 🫧 Bone lost in the pond | 6% | `terrain-service` 503 → `bone-service` retries once, then gives up |
| 💥 bone-service crash | 3% | Unhandled `KeyError` with a stack trace in Error Tracking |
| 🐢 Muddy terrain | 10% | Not an error: a slow `terrain.scan` and a slower run, so p95 latency spikes |

You can change every rate in `.env`. Turn them up before a demo.

## Setup

**You need:** [Colima](https://github.com/abiosoft/colima) (or Docker Desktop) with `docker compose`, a Datadog API key, and a Browser RUM app.

1. **Create a RUM app** in Datadog: *Digital Experience → RUM → New Application*. Choose **Manual Setup**, name it `bits-fetch`, and pick **JavaScript**. Copy the **Application ID** and **Client Token**.
2. **Configure:**
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```
   Fill in `DD_API_KEY`, `DD_RUM_APPLICATION_ID` and `DD_RUM_CLIENT_TOKEN`. `.env` is git-ignored.
3. **Run:**
   ```bash
   colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```
4. Open **http://localhost:8080** and throw the bone.

Stop everything with `docker compose down`.

## Import the dashboard and monitor

![Bits Fetch dashboard in Datadog](docs/screenshots/dashboard.png)

- **Dashboard:** *Dashboards → New Dashboard → ⚙ (settings) → Import dashboard JSON*, then paste [`datadog/dashboard.json`](datadog/dashboard.json).
- **Monitor:** *Monitors → New Monitor → Import from JSON*, then paste [`datadog/monitor.json`](datadog/monitor.json). It alerts when fewer than 70% of thrown bones come back in a 15-minute window (normal is about 85%). Add your own `@notification` handle to the message.

## A 5-minute walkthrough

1. Turn on **Auto-Fetch** so data keeps flowing while you click around.
2. **APM → Service Map:** five services, with `thrower-api` in the middle.
3. **APM → Traces**, `service:thrower-api`: open one. The flame graph mirrors the animation, with each jump as its own span. Find a trace with an error and see where it broke.
4. Inside the trace, open the **Logs** tab: `fetch!` and `good dog!` carry the same trace ID.
5. **Error Tracking:** the `KeyError: 'bone-2'` crash, grouped, with its stack trace.
6. **Metrics → Explorer:** `dog.bone.thrown` vs. `dog.bone.returned`, split by `throw_distance` or `terrain`.
7. **RUM → Sessions:** replay your session and watch Bits run, then jump from a `/throw` resource to its backend trace.

## Notes

- Everything runs in containers, including the Datadog Agent, so the only thing to install is Colima.
- DogStatsD submits counts as a rate per flush interval. Use `.as_count()` in queries (the dashboard and monitor already do) to get bone totals.
- `env:sandbox` and `version:1.0.0` are set in `docker-compose.yml` (unified service tagging).
- **Port 8080 already in use?** Change `"8080:5000"` in `docker-compose.yml`.
- **Nothing in Datadog?** Run `docker compose exec datadog-agent agent status` and check the APM, Logs and DogStatsD sections.

Bits is an original pixel character made for this project.

# Đại Việt Hiệp Khách

Game nhập vai hành động lấy bối cảnh lịch sử Việt Nam, chạy thẳng trên trình duyệt và iPhone. Có 6 môn phái, 6 chương từ Văn Lang đến Đống Đa, đánh quái nhặt đồ, rèn trang bị, thú cưỡi và một thành chính có tường bao để nghỉ chân.

**Chơi ngay:** mở `index.html` (hoặc trang GitHub Pages của repo).

## Có gì trong game
- **Bí kíp:** mỗi lần lên cấp chọn 1 trong 3 bí kíp (24 loại, mỗi loại 5 cấp). Hai bí kíp hợp nhau cùng đạt cấp 3 thì ghép thành Tuyệt kỹ (7 loại).
- **Đồ Huyền Thoại:** 14 món mang tên tích sử Việt, mỗi món có hiệu ứng riêng. Có cơ chế bảo đảm: chơi hết game thường nhặt được 3–6 món.
- **Ép đồ rủi ro kiểu MU:** từ +10 thất bại có thể vỡ đồ, Bùa Bảo Hộ giữ được đồ.
- **Boss ba giai đoạn:** mỗi boss có chiêu báo trước và một cơ chế cần đứng đúng chỗ (dụ vào bãi cọc Bạch Đằng, nấp Hốc Đá, phá Hỏa Đàn…).
- **Ngũ Hành tương khắc:** giữa môn phái và quái, đánh vào hệ bị khắc mạnh hơn 25%.
- **Thành chính:** tường bao, hồ sen, 7 nhà có chức năng.

## Điều khiển
- **Điện thoại:** kéo ở nửa trái màn hình để di chuyển, nút đỏ để đánh, ba nút kỹ năng bên cạnh.
- **Bàn phím:** WASD di chuyển, J đánh, K / L / I kỹ năng, E nói chuyện với NPC, B túi đồ, R lò rèn, C chợ, T kỹ năng, Q nhiệm vụ, M bản đồ, V thú cưỡi, Esc cài đặt.

## Cấu trúc
| Đường dẫn | Nội dung |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Bản game đã ghép, một file duy nhất |
| `src/` | Mã nguồn chia theo phần: dữ liệu, thế giới, nhân vật, thành chính, vật phẩm, quái, vòng lặp game, hiệu ứng, giao diện. Mô-đun mở rộng `perks.js`, `legend.js`, `boss2.js` cắm vào qua điểm nối `HK` trong `core.js` |
| `build.sh` | Ghép `src/` thành `dist/dai-viet-hiep-khach.html` |
| `styles/` | Trang so sánh 10 phong cách vẽ (`dist/phong-cach-ve.html`) |
| `t/` | Kiểm thử Playwright: giao diện, bàn phím, bot tự chơi, đo hiệu năng |

## Dựng lại
```bash
bash build.sh   # tạo dist/ và cập nhật index.html (bản đứng riêng có đủ khung trang)
```

## Kiểm thử
```bash
cd t && npm install @fontsource/be-vietnam-pro @fontsource/yeseva-one gsap@3.12.5 three@0.128.0
pip install playwright
python3 ui_test.py   # 69 bước trên iPhone, iPhone SE, màn ngang, máy tính
python3 keys.py      # phím tắt và chuột
python3 bot.py kiem 18   # bot tự chơi 18 phút giả lập
```

## Móc cho ứng dụng iPhone (WebView)
- `window.DVHK.pause()`, `window.DVHK.resume()`, `window.DVHK.getState()`
- Game gửi sự kiện qua `webkit.messageHandlers.dvhk` (lên cấp, qua chương).

# CryoSat

Cryogenics and orbital infrastructure for [Mekanism](https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism).

Liquefy air into cryogenic coolants, run superconducting power networks that have to stay cold,
and fuel rockets that put asteroid miners, utility satellites and orbital weapons into orbit.

* Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge
* Requires Mekanism 10.7.19 or newer (Mekanism Generators optional)

## Development

```
./gradlew build          # compile and package
./gradlew runClient      # launch a dev client with Mekanism and Generators
./gradlew runServer      # headless dev server
./gradlew runGameTestServer  # run game tests headless, exits with failure if any test fails
./gradlew runData        # data generation into src/generated/resources
```

Textures follow [docs/texture-style-guide.md](docs/texture-style-guide.md) and are generated by
scripts in `tools/textures/`.

## License

MIT. Mekanism is MIT licensed by Aidan C. Brady and contributors.

FunPixelNest/funpixelnest-mgp.readme:
# FunPixelNest MGP — Multi Gaming Platform

One app, many skill games, 5-player tournaments. Android, iOS and Web from a single
Kotlin Multiplatform codebase, with the games themselves built in Unity.

> **Status:** app shell (phase 1). Lobby, tournaments, leaderboards and wallet work
> end-to-end against an in-memory backend. Unity games and the real server come next.

## How it fits together

```
┌──────────────────────────── composeApp (Kotlin Multiplatform) ────────────────────────────┐
│  Shared Compose UI: lobby · game detail · tournaments · leaderboard · wallet · profile     │
│  domain/   Tournament, Pool, ranking + 50/30/20 prizes                                     │
│  data/     PlatformRepository  ←  FakePlatformRepository today, Nakama next                │
│  game/     GameLauncher        ←  the one seam to Unity                                    │
└───────────────┬───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
          androidMain                   iosMain                     wasmJsMain
       MainActivity (APK)        MainViewController → iosApp     ComposeViewport (browser)
     + Unity as a Library        + UnityFramework (later)        + Unity WebGL (later)
```

## Tournament rules (implemented in `domain/Leaderboard.kt`)

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Players per pool | 5, all get the **same seed** (identical board/deal) |
| Timeout | **None** — a pool stays open until all 5 have submitted |
| Prizes | 1st **50%**, 2nd **30%**, 3rd gets the **remaining 20%** (absorbs rounding) |
| Platform fee | Configurable per tournament (`platformFeePercent`), taken before prizes. Sample data uses 10% as a placeholder |
| Tie-breakers | Higher score → shorter duration → earlier submission (so ties can't happen) |
| Quit mid-game | Counts as score 0 (entry is already paid) |
| One ticket = one submission | Enforced in the repository; must be enforced on the server too |

The app only *displays* rankings. In production the **server** ranks pools and pays prizes.

## Project layout

```
composeApp/
  src/commonMain/kotlin/com/funpixelnest/mgp/
    App.kt                    root composable + navigation wiring
    domain/                   models, Leaderboard (ranking + payouts)
    data/                     PlatformRepository, FakePlatformRepository, SampleCatalog
    game/GameLauncher.kt      interface Unity will implement on each platform
    ui/                       theme, navigator, components, screens/
  src/commonTest/             LeaderboardTest (prize split, tie-breakers)
  src/androidMain/            MainActivity, manifest
  src/iosMain/                MainViewController (called from Swift)
  src/wasmJsMain/             main.kt, index.html
iosApp/                       SwiftUI host + XcodeGen spec (project.yml)
.github/workflows/build.yml   CI: tests, Android APK, Web, iOS framework
```

## Running it

**Requirements:** JDK 17+, Android Studio (latest stable) with the Kotlin Multiplatform plugin.
iOS additionally needs a Mac with Xcode 16+.

### Android
Open the project folder in Android Studio and run the **composeApp** configuration, or:
```bash
./gradlew :composeApp:assembleDebug
```

### Web
```bash
./gradlew :composeApp:wasmJsBrowserDevelopmentRun
```
Opens the app in your browser (needs a WasmGC-capable browser: current Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).

### iOS (on a Mac)
```bash
brew install xcodegen
cd iosApp && xcodegen generate
open iosApp.xcodeproj
```
Set your team under *Signing & Capabilities* and run. The Xcode build calls Gradle to compile the shared Kotlin framework automatically.

### Tests
```bash
./gradlew :composeApp:testDebugUnitTest
```

## App navigation

Bottom bar: **Rewards · Store · Games · Featured · Profile** (Games is the home tab, in the center).

| Tab | What's there |
|---|---|
| Rewards | 7-day login streak, free coins from videos (3/day), missions with coin rewards |
| Store | Coin packs (demo mode: added free, real billing comes later) |
| Games | All games with category filter |
| Featured | Hero banner, new games, big prize events (join directly) |
| Profile | Stats, balance, my tournaments, coin history |

Tapping the coin balance in the top bar opens the Store.

## Trying the demo flow

1. **Games** tab → pick a game → **Join** a tournament (you start with 1,000 coins).
2. The placeholder game screen shows exactly what Unity will receive (game id, seed, ticket). Tap **Finish & submit demo score**.
3. Watch the 5-player leaderboard fill in. Other players are **simulated "Demo" players** — this exists only in `FakePlatformRepository` for UI development. The real backend never adds bots.
4. When all 5 finish, ranks lock and the top 3 are paid into the wallet.

## Roadmap

- [x] **Phase 1 — App shell:** KMP project, shared UI, tournaments, leaderboard, wallet (in-memory)
- [ ] **Phase 2 — Unity integration:** decide per platform (Unity as a Library vs WebGL), implement `GameLauncher`, port games to a common launch/score interface
- [ ] **Phase 3 — Backend:** Nakama server (pools, seeds, tickets, ranking, payouts), auth, real-time leaderboard updates
- [ ] **Phase 4 — Product:** free practice mode, Addressables game downloads, push notifications, analytics, admin panel
- [ ] **Phase 5 — Real money:** legal review, payments/KYC, geofencing (separate workstream)

## Conventions

- Package / bundle ID: `com.funpixelnest.mgp`
- Game ids (`SampleCatalog`) are the contract with Unity: the Unity project must use the same ids.
- "Flappy Bird" is listed as **Flap Dash** (the original name is trademarked).

dinocode00/epic-racer.readme:
# Epic Racer

A free, home-built couch-multiplayer kart racer. Race movie vehicles (Pod Racer, Batmobile,
Nazgûl rider) through movie scenes on a TV, using iPhones or Xbox controllers as pads.

See [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) for the full design, and [docs/screens](docs/screens) for
renders from the latest build.

## Play it

### At home with phones (the full setup)

You need [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org) on the computer that drives the TV. Then, in a
terminal:

```sh
corepack enable     # once: provides pnpm
git clone https://github.com/dinocode00/epic-racer.git
cd epic-racer
git checkout claude/keen-curie-e7kh6o
pnpm install
pnpm start          # builds, starts the server, prints a URL + QR code
```

1. On the computer, open `http://localhost:4000` and go fullscreen (F11). Mirror or cast
   that screen to the TV (HDMI, AirPlay, Chromecast tab cast…).
2. Each player scans the QR code with their iPhone (same Wi-Fi), types a name and picks a
   ride. Xbox controllers join with **A**, the keyboard with **Enter** / **Space**.
3. When everyone is **Ready** the race starts. 2 players split the screen top/bottom,
   3-4 players get quarters.

If phones can't reach the URL, check they're on the same Wi-Fi and that the computer's
firewall allows Node on port 4000.

### Couch mode (no server)

Any static copy of `apps/game/dist` (e.g. the hosted build) runs without the server: the
lobby switches to **couch mode** for the keyboard (up to two players) and Xbox controllers.
Phones need the home setup above.

## Controls

| Action                     | Keyboard (solo) | Keyboard P1 / P2 (shared) | Xbox controller    | Phone                 |
| -------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------- |
| Join / ready               | Enter           | Enter / Space             | A                  | READY                 |
| Change ride (lobby)        | ← →             | ← → / A D                 | Stick / D-pad      | Tap a ride            |
| Change track (lobby)       | T               | T                         | LB / RB            | ◀ ▶                   |
| Steer                      | ← → or A D      | ← → / A D                 | Left stick / D-pad | Drag on the left half |
| Accelerate                 | ↑ or W          | ↑ / W                     | RT                 | GAS                   |
| Brake / reverse            | ↓ or S          | ↓ / S                     | LT                 | BRAKE                 |
| Drift (hold while turning) | Space / Shift   | Right Shift / Left Shift  | A / RB             | DRIFT                 |
| Look back                  | C               | , / C                     | Y                  | —                     |
| Leave (lobby)              | Backspace       | Backspace / Q             | B                  | —                     |
| Toggle Retro look          | F2              | F2                        | —                  | —                     |

Drift tip: hold drift through a corner; the sparks go blue → orange → purple, and letting
go fires a mini-turbo. Press GAS when the countdown shows **1** (not earlier) for a start
boost.

## Developer URL options

`?players=1..4` · `?demo=1` (autopilot) · `?t=20` (skip ahead) · `?look=retro` ·
`?vehicles=pod,bat,nazgul,mach5` · `?scene=showroom` · `?fixed=1` (deterministic frames)

## Layout

```
apps/game        Three.js host: renders to the TV, runs the race
apps/controller  Phone controller page
apps/server      Local server: serves pages, relays phone input, QR code
packages/sim     Pure, deterministic race simulation (unit tested)
packages/shared  Protocol and data types
```

# אפליקציית ערב פוקר: תשתית (שלב 1)

המסמך הזה מכסה את מה שנבנה עד עכשיו: מסד הנתונים, ההרשאות, מנוע החישובים, והוראות ההתקנה. ממשק המשתמש (Expo) הוא השלב הבא.

## מה יש בתיקייה

| קובץ | מה הוא עושה |
|---|---|
| `supabase/migrations/20261003000000_init.sql` | כל מסד הנתונים: 9 טבלאות, הגנות שלמות נתונים, RLS, Views לסיכומים ולליגה, ופונקציות להצטרפות לקבוצה, לאישור חברים ולסגירת ערב |
| `src/core/settle.ts` | מנוע החישובים: יתרות, המרת צ'יפים לשקלים, איזון יחסי, מינימום העברות, חלוקת קופה במזומן, ופרסי טורניר |
| `src/core/settle.test.ts` | 10 בדיקות, כולל ערב הדוגמה ו-2,000 ערבים אקראיים |
| `supabase/tests/` | 36 בדיקות של מסד הנתונים על Postgres אמיתי: הרשאות, ניסיונות עקיפה וסגירת ערב |

## מה המערכת אוכפת (נבדק)

| כלל | איך |
|---|---|
| רק הבנקאי מזין | RLS: צופה שמנסה להכניס כסף נחסם |
| את העבר לא משנים | אין UPDATE ואין DELETE ביומן. טעות מתוקנת ב-reversal, והטעות נשארת מתועדת |
| ערב סגור קפוא | אחרי `close_game` אין שום שינוי |
| סגירה רק כשמאוזן | הקופה חייבת להיות שווה לסך היציאות, וההתחשבנות חייבת להתאים ליומן שקל בשקל |
| מקסימום ריבאיים | נאכף בשרת |
| צ'יפים לשקלים | השרת מחשב בעצמו ודוחה סכום שלא תואם את מספר הצ'יפים |
| קבוצות סגורות | זר לא רואה קבוצה, שחקנים, משחקים או פרופילים |
| שידור חוזר ללא כפילות | אותו אירוע שנשלח פעמיים מהטלפון נרשם פעם אחת |

## התקנות שלך (פעם אחת)

| # | מה | איפה | זמן |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Node.js LTS (22 ומעלה) | nodejs.org | 5 דק׳ |
| 2 | Git, וריפו פרטי ב-GitHub | github.com | 5 דק׳ |
| 3 | חשבון Supabase ופרויקט חדש, אזור **Frankfurt (eu-central-1)** | supabase.com | 5 דק׳ |
| 4 | Supabase CLI: `npm i -g supabase` | טרמינל | 2 דק׳ |
| 5 | חשבון Expo (לשלב הבא) | expo.dev | 2 דק׳ |
| 6 | בטלפון אנדרואיד: אפליקציית **Expo Go** (לפיתוח) | Google Play | 2 דק׳ |

## העלאת מסד הנתונים ל-Supabase

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref <PROJECT_REF>      # מופיע ב-Settings > General
supabase db push                               # מריץ את קובץ ה-migration
```

לבדוק אחרי ההעלאה, ב-Table Editor:
- 9 טבלאות קיימות, ובכולן מופיע "RLS enabled".
- ב-Database > Publications, הפרסום `supabase_realtime` כולל את games, game_players, ledger_entries ו-settlements.

## כניסה עם Google

1. ב-Google Cloud Console: פרויקט חדש, OAuth consent screen, ואז Credentials > OAuth Client ID מסוג Web application.
2. ב-Authorized redirect URI להדביק את הכתובת ש-Supabase מציג ב-Authentication > Providers > Google.
3. ב-Supabase: להפעיל את Google ולהדביק Client ID ו-Client Secret.
4. ב-Authentication > URL Configuration: להוסיף את כתובות האפליקציה. נגדיר אותן בשלב הבא.

## מפתחות: מה נכנס לאפליקציה ומה לא

| מפתח | איפה |
|---|---|
| Project URL ו-anon key | באפליקציה. הם גלויים בכוונה, וההגנה היא ה-RLS |
| service_role key | **אף פעם לא באפליקציה.** רק ב-GitHub Secrets, לגיבוי |
| Database password | במנהל סיסמאות |

## להריץ את הבדיקות בעצמך

```bash
node --experimental-strip-types --test src/core/settle.test.ts   # מנוע החישובים
./run_db_tests.sh                                                # מסד הנתונים (דורש Postgres מקומי)
```

## הרצת האפליקציה (שלב 2)

| # | פעולה |
|---|---|
| 1 | לחלץ את ה-zip לתיקייה, למשל `C:\dev\poker-app` |
| 2 | ב-PowerShell: `cd C:\dev\poker-app` ואז `npm install` (כ-2 דק׳) |
| 3 | `npx expo start` |
| 4 | בטלפון אנדרואיד: לפתוח **Expo Go** ולסרוק את ה-QR שמופיע בטרמינל. הטלפון והמחשב באותה רשת Wi-Fi |
| 5 | בדפדפן במחשב: ללחוץ `w` בטרמינל, ונפתחת גרסת הדפדפן |

הקובץ `.env.local` כבר מכיל את כתובת הפרויקט והמפתח הציבורי.

## מה עובד בגרסה 0.1

| מסך | מה אפשר לעשות |
|---|---|
| כניסה | הרשמה והתחברות עם מייל וסיסמה |
| בית | ערבים פתוחים, הקבוצות שלי, קבוצה חדשה, הצטרפות עם קוד |
| קבוצה | טבלת ליגה, היסטוריה, שחקנים, אורחים, קוד הזמנה, אישור ממתינים (כולל "זה שחקן שכבר קיים") |
| ערב חדש | כניסה, צ׳יפים לכניסה, מצב התחשבנות, ריבאיים, בנקאי, בחירת שחקנים |
| שולחן | קופה חיה, הדגשת "אני", מחוון חיבור, אירוע אחרון, ריבאי מהיר, ביטול, שחקן מאוחר |
| ספירה | מקלדת צ׳יפים עם המרה לשקלים, התקדמות מול הקופה, ספירה מחדש |
| סיכום | איזון יחסי, פודיום זהב/כסף/ארד, זיקוקים פעם אחת, העברות או חלוקת קופה, שיתוף |

מסך נדלק נשאר דולק אצל הבנקאי, וכל הזנה נשמרת קודם בטלפון ונשלחת לשרת ברקע.

## עוד לא בגרסה הזו

כניסה עם Google, טורניר, Push, התקנת APK, ואתר לאייפון. אלה השלבים הבאים.

nathan6609/roadster-launch.readme:
# Roadster Launch

A browser stunt game built with three.js: launch up a reverse-C ramp, come off it upside down, roll upright and jet-land, then hop the line-up. Or switch to rocket mode and fly to Mars. Solo or online with other players, with a paint shop and a global leaderboard.

**Play:** https://roadsterarena.dev/ (free, no install, no login; keyboard or touch)

Made by [@nathangu76](https://x.com/nathangu76).

## Run it locally

The models load with `fetch()`, so serve the folder instead of opening the file directly:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

then open http://localhost:8000/

## What's inside

- `index.html`: the whole game (physics, rendering, volumetric smoke, synthesised audio, UI). three.js 0.160 is loaded from jsDelivr.
- `models/`: meshopt-compressed glTF models (car, line-up vehicles, pilot).
- `voice.js`, `smoke.js`: the finale voice clip and a fallback smoke atlas.
- `ai.js`: recorded runs that AI drivers replay when an online room is quiet.

Online play (rooms, leaderboard, paint jobs) talks to a small Cloudflare Worker at `api.roadsterarena.dev`.

## License

The code and the original assets in this repository (the procedural scene, the synthesised music and sound, the original pilot character) are released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

This is an unofficial fan-made project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Tesla or any other car maker. "Tesla" and "Roadster" are trademarks of their respective owners, and the vehicle designs belong to them; the MIT License grants no rights to any trademark, logo or vehicle design.

# mision_sobris

Misión Sobris: a tiny 2D cookie game built with Python and [pygame-ce](https://pyga.me/).
Each nephew/niece picks their own cookie character, then moves it around to eat the small
cookies and grow. The in-game text is in Spanish.

## Setup

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate mision_sobris
```

## Run

```bash
mision_sobris        # or: python -m mision_sobris.main
```

First pick a character (Juani, Lucha, Male, or Juli; they're defined in `CHARACTERS` in
`settings.py`), then pick a mode from the menu (tap or click it, or use Up/Down + Enter, or press 1/2):

- **Classic**: eat cookies at your own pace. Touch a small cookie to eat it and grow;
  burnt (dark) cookies shrink you.
- **Challenge**: 20 seconds to eat as many as you can, with burnt cookies too, while
  big angry cookies chase you (one slow, one fast); if one catches you, the round ends.

Controls:
- **Keyboard**: arrow keys / WASD to move, Esc to go back to the menu (or quit from the menu).
- **Touch or mouse**: touch and hold (or click and hold) and the cookie moves toward your finger.
  Tap a mode to start it, and use the on-screen Menu / Play again buttons.

## Browser version

The game also runs in a web browser via [pygbag](https://github.com/pygame-web/pygbag),
which `src/main.py` is the entry point for.

```bash
cd src
python -m pygbag --title "Misión Sobris" .   # serves it at http://localhost:8000
python -m pygbag --build --title "Misión Sobris" .   # just build into src/build/web
```

Pushing to `main` rebuilds it and publishes it to GitHub Pages
(`.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml`). The page needs a click before the game starts (browsers block audio and focus until then).

## Layout

- `src/main.py`: entry point for the browser build
- `src/mision_sobris/main.py`: game loop, menu, and rounds
- `src/mision_sobris/entities.py`: player, cookies, and chasers
- `src/mision_sobris/settings.py`: window size, colors, speeds, challenge tuning
- `assets/`: images, sounds, fonts

# Music Memory

A memory match game played by ear. Flip two tiles, each plays a short Spotify snippet, and pair the ones that sound the same.

Built with **Vue 3 + Vite** (v2 refactor of the original vanilla JS version).

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://127.0.0.1:5173
npm test         # unit tests for the game logic
npm run build    # static site in dist/
```

Spotify only accepts loopback IPs for http redirect URIs, so open the dev server at
`http://127.0.0.1:5173` (not `localhost`). Add `http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback` to your
Spotify app's redirect URIs next to the production one.

Deploy `dist/` to any static host. `dist/callback/index.html` forwards Spotify's
`?code=…` to the app root, so no SPA rewrite rules are needed.

## Structure

```
src/
  data/tracks.js           track catalogue (uri, snippet start/duration, tags)
  lib/game.js              pure game logic: filtering, deck building, scoring (unit-tested)
  lib/spotify.js           PKCE auth, token refresh, Web API client
  lib/players.js           player names and colours
  lib/storage.js           safe localStorage/sessionStorage wrapper
  store.js                 persisted settings + toast notices
  composables/useSpotify.js  connection phase, profile, devices, snippet playback
  composables/useGame.js     game state machine, turns, persistence
  components/              TopNav, DeviceMenu, SetupGuide, GameBoard, MemoryCard,
                           SettingsModal, TagSelect, WinModal, BaseModal, AppToast
public/callback/index.html OAuth redirect target
tests/game.test.js
```

## Adding tracks

Add a line to `src/data/tracks.js`:

```js
t('<spotify track id>', startMs, durationMs, 'Artist', 'Title', ['90s', 'house']),
```

Tags are picked up automatically by the include/exclude filters.

nathanlr29/Comptatycoon.readme:
# ComptaTycoon

Jeu de gestion Idle/Tycoon, mobile-first : faites grandir votre cabinet d'expertise comptable sur une carte 2D.
Site statique (TypeScript, Vite, Phaser 3), publié sur GitHub Pages, sans backend.

> En développement. L'avancement est suivi dans [`PROGRESS.md`](PROGRESS.md), les règles du jeu dans [`docs/GDD.md`](docs/GDD.md).

## Démarrer

Prérequis : Node.js 22.12 ou plus récent.

```bash
npm install        # installer les dépendances
npm run dev        # serveur local (http://localhost:5173)
npm test           # tests Vitest
npm run build      # version de production dans dist/
npm run preview    # servir dist/ localement
npm run check      # typage + tests + build (à faire passer avant chaque commit)
```

Pour reproduire le build de GitHub Pages en local :

```bash
VITE_BASE=/Comptatycoon/ npm run build
VITE_BASE=/Comptatycoon/ npm run preview   # puis ouvrir http://localhost:4173/Comptatycoon/
```

## Sauvegarde

La partie est enregistrée **dans ce navigateur, sur cet appareil** (`localStorage`) : toutes les 15 s, après chaque achat et quand vous quittez la page. Jusqu'à 5 cabinets par appareil, choisis sur l'écran d'accueil.

- Sur iPhone, Safari peut effacer les données d'un site que vous n'avez pas ouvert depuis 7 jours.
- Le jeu ajouté à l'écran d'accueil a un stockage **séparé** de Safari : ce sont deux parties différentes.
- Pour changer d'appareil ou garder une copie : Paramètres › **Exporter** (texte à copier), puis **Importer** sur l'autre appareil (écran d'accueil ou Paramètres).

## Déploiement GitHub Pages

Le workflow [`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy.yml) vérifie le typage, lance les tests et construit le jeu à chaque pull request.
À chaque push sur `main`, il publie en plus le dossier `dist/` sur GitHub Pages, sous `https://<utilisateur>.github.io/<dépôt>/`.

À faire une seule fois : **Settings › Pages › Build and deployment › Source : GitHub Actions**.

Vérifier : onglet **Actions**, le workflow « Déploiement GitHub Pages » doit être vert ; l'adresse du site apparaît dans le job `deploy`.

## Développement avec Claude Code

Le travail est découpé en étapes dans [`docs/prompts/`](docs/prompts/). Le contexte permanent est dans [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).
Une session = une étape : `Exécute docs/prompts/0N-….md`.

NChandrasekharR/sikku-kolam-tetris.readme:
# Sikku Kolam Tetris

A Tetris where every block is a sikku kolam loop. Each side of a block's
loop checks one neighbour: an empty side curves back around the pulli
(dot), a filled side runs out at 45° and crosses the neighbour's line.
Stack the pieces and they weave into one rice-flour pattern. Every move
plays a note from Raga Mohanam.

**Play it: https://kolam-tetris.vercel.app**

| Folder | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`site/`](site) | The game. Static files, no build step. This is what deploys. |
| [`video/`](video) | Remotion project for the gameplay video, the thread diagram and the link-preview card. |

## Deploy (Vercel)

Import the repo and set **Root Directory** to `site`, framework preset
**Other**, no build command. Or from a checkout: `cd site && npx vercel --prod`.

Link previews (Open Graph and X card tags in `site/index.html`) point at
`https://kolam-tetris.vercel.app`. If the domain changes, update the
`canonical`, `og:url`, `og:image` and `twitter:image` URLs to match.

## Controls

Keyboard: arrows or WASD to move and rotate, Space to hard drop, C or Shift
to hold, P to pause. G ghost, T weave mode, I ink, B background, M sound.

Touch: tap to rotate, swipe to move, drag down to soft drop, flick down to
hard drop, flick up (or tap the HOLD piece) to hold.

fallensignalstudios/SovereignEngine.readme:
# Sovereign Engine (research build, First Ignition)

A separate, independent research engine: native editor, renderer, runtime and tools in C++20 on a
single Vulkan 1.3 backend. It is not an Unreal plugin and depends on no Unreal code. Private research;
no licence has been chosen (ADR-009).

Status: **G0 + G1 implemented against the owner's First Ignition contracts; G1 not complete:
physical-GPU qualification is blocked** on the build host (no physical GPU; every rendering result
here is software-rendered). Read `docs/reports/G0_G1_REPORT.md` for exactly what was verified and how,
by validation-matrix ID.

## Quick start

```
# Headless: core, scene, commands, CLI, tests. No display, SDL or Vulkan needed.
cmake --preset dev-headless
cmake --build --preset dev-headless
ctest --preset dev-headless

# Graphics: editor, runtime, Vulkan rendering tests.
scripts/build_dxc_from_source.sh          # Linux, once per host (ADR-015)
cmake --preset dev-vulkan
cmake --build --preset dev-vulkan
ctest --preset dev-vulkan

# On a machine with a physical GPU: refuses software Vulkan devices.
ctest --preset gpu-qualify
```

Prerequisites: CMake >= 3.25, Ninja, GCC 13+ / Clang 17+ / MSVC 19.38+, git, Python 3; for
`dev-vulkan` a Vulkan 1.3 driver, the Vulkan loader, `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`, and on Linux the
X11 development headers listed in `dependencies.lock.json`. All third-party code is fetched by CMake at
the pinned revisions in `dependencies.lock.json`; afterwards builds work offline.

## Try it

```
B=build/dev-headless/bin
$B/sovereign-cli --version
$B/sovereign-cli scene validate --scene content/authoring/first_light.scene.json
$B/sovereign-cli scene apply --scene content/authoring/first_light.scene.json \
                             --commands examples/place_banner.command_batch.json   # dry run: changes nothing

V=build/dev-vulkan/bin
$V/sovereign-editor  --scene content/authoring/first_light.scene.json
$V/sovereign-runtime --scene content/authoring/first_light.scene.json
$V/sovereign-runtime --scene content/authoring/first_light.scene.json --no-vsync --perf-report perf.json
```

To commit an edit, copy the example batch, give it a new `idempotency_key` and `request_id`, set
`"dry_run": false`, and apply it. Re-sending the same batch replays the recorded result; changing its
content under the same key is rejected; an outdated `base_revision` is rejected with conflict details.
While the editor has a scene open, CLI writes to it are refused (exit 3).

## Map

- `AGENTS.md`: rules for agents (the owner's, verbatim); `docs/DEVELOPING.md`: repository guide.
- `docs/packet/`: the First Ignition packet as supplied; `schemas/`, `examples/` are verbatim copies.
- `docs/architecture/`: conventions, command protocol and durability, logging/errors, modules.
- `docs/decisions/`: ADRs.
- `docs/VALIDATION_MATRIX.md`: what G0/G1 must prove; `docs/reports/`: what was proven, and
  `docs/reports/GPU_TEST_PROCEDURE.md` for the physical-GPU run.
- `third_party_notices/`: upstream licences of the pinned dependencies.

ondrik/quantum-arcade.desc: An attempt of a Quantum version of PacMan
ondrik/quantum-arcade.readme:
# Quantum Arcade

Classic computer games rebuilt around quantum mechanics: superposition, phase flips, entanglement, measurement and tunneling, each turned into a game mechanic. Every game is a static page with no build step: plain HTML, CSS and canvas JavaScript.

**Play:** <https://ondrik.github.io/quantum-arcade/>

| Game | Folder | Quantum twist |
|---|---|---|
| **Quak-Man** | [`quak-man/`](quak-man/) | Pac-Man: superposed mirrored copies, Z gates that flip ghosts to edible `|−⟩`, entangled ghost pairs, Schrödinger's Clyde, EPR portals, tunneling |
| **Quetris** | [`quetris/`](quetris/) | Tetris: pieces superposed over two shapes that collapse on contact, `|−⟩` antimatter that annihilates blocks, entangled piece pairs, tunneling |
| **MineQueeper** | [`minequeeper/`](minequeeper/) | Minesweeper: numbers are expectation values, superposed and entangled mines, anti-mines that count −1, a measurement tool |

Each game's page lists its full rules and controls in a side panel.

## Run locally

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000   # then open http://localhost:8000
```

## Layout

- `index.html` is the arcade landing page.
- Each game lives in its own folder (`index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`, `favicon.svg`) and links back to the arcade.
- To add a game, create a new folder and add a card for it to `index.html`.

## Deploying

GitHub Pages serves the repository root from `master` (**Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch**, then `master` and `/ (root)`). `.nojekyll` turns off Jekyll processing.

JohnnyNero/daily-grind.readme:
# Daily Grind (working title)

A café sim for phones. You set up the café, staff it with characters you made up or recognise from work, and watch it run. Inspired by RimWorld's emergent drama and the Sims' everyday autonomy; drawn in the "Pawn" style.

The full design and the decisions behind it are in [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md).

## Run it

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # serves on your network; open the printed address on your phone
```

Other scripts:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | Runs the simulation and stress tests (headless, no browser, about 5 seconds) |
| `npx vite-node test/soak.ts 6 30 4` | Long soak: 6 seeds × 30 days per venue with 4 random manager actions an hour, saving and reloading every 6 hours, checking every invariant |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript checks |
| `npm run build` | Builds a static site into `dist/` that works from any folder |

Add `?seed=123` to the URL to skip the start screen and open a fresh café from that seed (it ignores the saved one).

## Play online

Every push to `main` is tested, built and deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:
https://johnnynero.github.io/daily-grind/

## Install on your phone

Open the site, then use your browser's *Add to Home Screen* (Share → Add to Home Screen on iPhone; the menu → Install app on Android). It then opens full screen and works offline.

## Starting a game

The start screen offers **Continue** (your saved place), **New game** and **Import save**. A new game asks what you're opening, then shows your starting team in the **character creator**: tap someone to change their name, skin, hair and up to three traits with a live preview, or use *New face* for a random person, *Add someone* (up to 8), *Remove* and *Shuffle everyone*. *Open the doors* starts day one.

## Venues

There are two so far: **the café** (mornings, flat whites, cake) and **the pub** (evenings, pints, crisps, quiz night, stag dos). To switch, open the venue panel's **Save** tab and tap *New game*. Or add `?venue=pub` to the address to skip straight in. Venues live in `src/sim/venues.ts`, so adding one is mostly data.

## How it plays

You run the place; your staff decide what to do. The puzzle is keeping it running as it gets busier, and the people are both the problem and the reward.

- **Fame and stars.** Happy customers spread the word, walkouts, queues out the door and bad reviews undo it, and it fades a little each night. Fame brings more customers; fame times reputation gives the 1–5 star rating in the top bar. A good café gets busier until the layout and the team are the limit.
- **Money.** Takings in; wages (each person's own, rising with skill and raises), ingredients (18% of the usual price of everything made), rent and business rates (which rise with the value of your fit-out), repairs and services out. People pay up to 8% more per star without minding. In the red you pay overdraft fees, wages go out late below £250 overdrawn, and below £500 the bank stops lending for furniture and building work. Nothing ends the game; recovering takes days.
- **Skill and passions.** Skill sets speed (0.4× to 1.6×) and quality, grows slowly with practice, and much faster in what someone loves (an orange dot on the Jobs grid). Switching between kinds of work costs a little settling-in time, so specialists win.
- **Machines** wear with every drink: worn ones make worse drinks and break down more. A service (£60, Place tab) makes them new; a bodge repair doesn't.
- **Stress and days off.** Shifts, rushes, low mood and long days build stress; time off eases it. Past 60 it shows in mood, past 85 people are burnt out and sometimes off sick with it. Everyone has a day off a week (set them in the shift editor); the top bar shows the weekday.
- **Rushes** are announced 15–30 minutes ahead and grow with fame. Coach parties in the café, stag dos in the pub.

## Controls

- Drag to pan, pinch (or scroll wheel) to zoom; the corner button fits the café back on screen. Pause, 1×, 3×, 6× in the top bar; while nobody's working the clock skips ahead to the morning.
- **Alerts** under the top bar say what's wrong right now (nobody on the till, a rush coming, someone close to breaking, washing up piling up, in the red...). Tap one to jump to the person or panel.
- **Inbox**: big news and decisions (a raise request, a rival trying to poach someone, a friend thinking of following someone out). Decisions wait until closing time the next day, then take their first option.
- **Calls**: three direct orders for a crisis, each with a cost and a cooldown. *All hands* (20 minutes of nobody waiting at their post; a little stress), *Close the doors* (no arrivals for 20 minutes; a little fame), *Comp a round* (everyone waiting gets patience back; costs money, earns fame).
- Tap a person to see what they're doing: traits, mood and its biggest reasons, stress and needs; *Show more* adds every reason, how they feel about each colleague and what they want. Guests show their order and patience.
- Events pop up at the top; tap one to jump to that person. When the place shuts, the day's recap appears.
- **Staff** has four tabs. **Team**: today's numbers; each card has a **Station** and an **In a rush** station, *Shift* (hours and days off), *Break now*, *Send home*, *Edit* (name, looks, traits and catchphrases), *Live in* (once there's a staff flat) and *Lead* (one shift lead, +£1.50/h: a lead in good spirits steadies the team, one in a foul mood drags it down). **Jobs**: work priorities, and walking time per task (long walks mean the layout is costing you). **Hire**: applicants, with their passions and asking wage. **Log**.
- **Who does what:** staff stick to their station: when it's quiet they wait at their post, and only help elsewhere after about 8 in-game minutes with nothing to do, straight away if another area is in a rush (4+ queuing, 4+ drinks waiting, 3+ dirty tables, 8+ cups by the sink, 2+ spills) or nobody covers it, or

songadaymann/watertower.readme:
# Water Tower Smash

A Roblox game for little kids who love water towers. You start small in a new land with a water tower far off on the horizon. Bump into things to smash them and grow. Grow big enough to break through the walls into bigger areas, then knock down the water tower for a giant splash. Then jump through the rainbow ring to a brand new land.

**Live:** not published yet.

## How it plays

- **Smash to grow.** Walk into anything that sparkles. It pops, stars fly into you, and you get bigger. Things that are still too big just wobble and say "💪 Grow more!"
- **Three areas per land**, each bigger than the last, with a wall in between. You must be big enough to smash each wall.
- **The water tower** stands at the far end, visible from the start. The meter in the top-left is a little water tower that fills with water as you grow. When it's full, go knock the real one down: it falls, bursts, leaves a swimmable pond and a rainbow, and you get a trophy.
- **A new land every time.** Five biomes (Town, Farm, Snow, Beach, Candy), each laid out randomly, with five water tower styles: classic legged tank, candy-stripe, spheroid, hydropillar, and a Peachoid.
- No way to lose, no reading required. Banners are there for grown-ups to read aloud.

## Run it locally

You need [Roblox Studio](https://create.roblox.com/). The game world is built by scripts at runtime, so all the place needs is the code in `src/`.

**With [Rojo](https://rojo.space/)** (builds a fresh place file):

```bash
rojo build -o WaterTower.rbxl
```

Open `WaterTower.rbxl` in Studio and press Play.

**Without Rojo** (sync into a place you already have open):

```bash
python3 tools/dev-sync-server.py
```

Then paste `tools/studio-sync.luau` into Studio's command bar. It pulls every script from `src/` into the place, turning HttpEnabled on only for the fetch. In that place, also delete the default Baseplate and SpawnLocation, and set `Workspace.StreamingEnabled` to false so the faraway tower always loads.

## How it's built

Luau, laid out Rojo-style:

| Path | What's there |
| --- | --- |
| `src/shared/Config.luau` | Tuning: tier sizes, growth rate, speeds, sound IDs, music |
| `src/server/Land.luau` | Generates a land: zones, cliffs, walls, path, scattered stuff |
| `src/server/Items.luau` | Every smashable thing, built from primitive parts |
| `src/server/Towers.luau` | The water tower styles |
| `src/server/Biomes.luau` | What each biome looks like and what shows up in it |
| `src/server/Smash.luau` | Touch detection, growing, flinging debris, the tower fall and splash |
| `src/server/Main.server.luau` | Players, smooth scaling, the portal to the next land |
| `src/client/` | HUD, sparkles, camera zoom, effects, music, the far-away tower picture |

Easy things to change:

- **Town names** painted on the towers: `names` in `src/server/Biomes.luau`. Put your kid's name on one.
- **How fast you grow:** `Config.GROWTH` in `src/shared/Config.luau`.
- **Sound:** the 🔊 button in the top-right corner. Sound starts muted in Studio playtests and on in the real game.

## License

Code: [MIT](LICENSE). Sounds and music: see [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md).

Made by [Jonathan Mann](https://jonathanmann.net) (Song A Day).

technotrue-bit/trueaigaming.readme:
# TrueAIGaming

A free, public arcade of games built with AI. Every game listed here was made with AI tools and is free to play in the browser.

It's a static site: Vite + vanilla TypeScript, no backend, no accounts, no trackers, no third-party fonts or CDNs. One file, [`public/games.json`](public/games.json), drives the whole thing.

- **Home (`/`)**: a grid of game cards. Each card links straight to the game's live URL (new tab).
- **Play page (`/play.html?id=<game-id>`)**: embeds the game in an iframe, with a prominent "Open full screen in new tab" link for when embedding doesn't work well (mobile, fullscreen, games that block framing).

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm run dev      # local dev server
npm run build    # type-check + production build to dist/
npm run preview  # serve dist/ locally
```

## Add a game

1. **Add one entry to `public/games.json`:**

   ```json
   {
     "id": "my-game",
     "name": "My Game",
     "description": "One sentence about the game",
     "playUrl": "https://my-game.vercel.app",
     "thumbnail": "/thumbs/my-game.png",
     "status": "live",
     "repo": "https://github.com/you/my-game"
   }
   ```

   | Field         | Notes                                                                                            |
   | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   | `id`          | Unique, URL-safe slug. Used in `play.html?id=…`.                                                 |
   | `name`        | Display name.                                                                                    |
   | `description` | Short one-liner shown on the card.                                                               |
   | `playUrl`     | Live game URL. **Must be `https://`**; entries with other schemes are ignored.                   |
   | `thumbnail`   | Path under `public/`, starting with `/`. Must be local (the CSP only allows same-origin images).  |
   | `status`      | e.g. `live` (green badge) or `beta` (yellow badge); anything else gets a neutral badge.          |
   | `repo`        | Optional source link (`https://`).                                                               |

2. **Add a thumbnail** at `public/thumbs/<id>.png`, 1280×720 (16:9). To capture a real screenshot of the live game with Playwright:

   ```sh
   npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
   node scripts/thumb.mjs https://my-game.vercel.app public/thumbs/my-game.png
   ```

   The script loads the page at 1280×720, waits ~8 seconds for the game to render, then saves the PNG. With no arguments it re-captures Super Star Party.

3. **If the game is NOT hosted on `*.vercel.app`**, add its origin to `frame-src` in the `Content-Security-Policy` header in [`vercel.json`](vercel.json). Otherwise the play page's iframe will be blocked:

   ```
   frame-src https://super-star-party.vercel.app https://*.vercel.app https://my-game.example.com;
   ```

   The game's own site must also allow being framed (no `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or restrictive `frame-ancestors`). If it doesn't, the card's main Play button still works, because it opens the game in a new tab.

4. Run `npm run build`, then commit and push.

## Deploy

The site is hosted on Vercel and auto-deploys from git:

- **Push to `main`** → Vercel runs `npm run build` and deploys `dist/` to production.
- Pushes to other branches and PRs get preview deployments.

[`vercel.json`](vercel.json) sets the framework (Vite) and applies security headers to every route:

- a strict Content-Security-Policy: scripts, styles, and images come from the site itself only, iframes only from allowed game origins, and the site itself can't be framed
- `X-Content-Type-Options`
- `Referrer-Policy`
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
- a minimal `Permissions-Policy`
- HSTS

wilheim77/willysGate.readme:
# willysGate

Motor de RPG táctico isométrico por turnos para navegador, con estética retro, y los juegos construidos sobre él.

| Juego | Reglas | Estado | Jugar |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Intereses**: fantasía oscura y deudas en el pueblo minero de Hondonegra | 5e simplificado (SRD 5.1) | Fase 1: esqueleto técnico | https://wilheim77.github.io/willysGate/intereses/ |

## Requisitos

Node 22 o superior.

## Uso

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run dev
```

Abre http://localhost:5173. Para arrancar otro juego, usa `GAME=<id> npm run dev`.

| Comando | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Servidor de desarrollo (por defecto, `GAME=intereses`) |
| `npm test` | Tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run check` | Typecheck de todas las capas y tests. Hay que pasarlo antes de cada commit. |
| `npm run coverage` | Cobertura de `engine/` y `rulesets/` |
| `npm run build:all` | Construye todos los juegos en `dist/<juego>/` y la portada en `dist/index.html` |
| `npm run art` | Regenera el arte de cada preset (`content/<juego>/art/<preset>/`) a partir de `art-src/` y el generador LPC |
| `npm run gen:logic-tiles` | Regenera el tileset lógico que usa Tiled |

## Controles

- **Ratón:** clic en una casilla para moverte, arrastrar para desplazar la cámara y rueda para el zoom. Al pasar por encima se ve la ruta.
- **Táctil:** toca una casilla para moverte, arrastra para desplazar la cámara y pellizca para el zoom. Pellizcar o arrastrar nunca mueve al personaje.
- **Comparar arte:** añade `?arte=0x72` o `?arte=lpc` a la URL.

## Despliegue

Cada push a `main` ejecuta `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, que pasa el typecheck y los tests, construye todos los juegos y publica en GitHub Pages. Para lanzarlo a mano: pestaña *Actions* → *Test and deploy* → *Run workflow*.

## Documentación

| Documento | Contenido |
|---|---|
| [docs/PROGRESS.md](docs/PROGRESS.md) | Estado actual y siguiente paso. Es lo primero que hay que leer al retomar. |
| [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) | Arquitectura (motor, rulesets y contenido) y decisiones |
| [docs/NEW_GAME.md](docs/NEW_GAME.md) | Cómo crear un juego nuevo sobre el motor |
| [docs/STORY.md](docs/STORY.md) | Historia aprobada de *Intereses* |
| [docs/BRIEF.md](docs/BRIEF.md) | Encargo original |
| [docs/ART_OPTIONS.md](docs/ART_OPTIONS.md) | Catálogo de packs de arte y comparativa |
| [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md) | Créditos y licencias (código MIT; arte derivado de LPC CC-BY-SA 3.0) |
| [TODO-ART.md](TODO-ART.md) | Placeholders pendientes |

SeardnaSchmid/patient-gamer-games-rank.readme:
# Patient Gamers Rank

A static page that ranks patient games: games out for at least a year and finished (not Early Access, not live service), so the hype is over, the patches are in and the price has dropped. Two scores answer the patient gamer's two questions, and the cards show the numbers behind them (reviews now, change since launch, price and discount, distance to the all-time low):

- **Worth the wait**: is the game good and finished today? Quality from the last 6 months of Steam reviews, how reviews moved since the launch quarter (was it fixed?), out a year and not Early Access or live service, Metascore.
- **Buy now**: is today the moment? Discount off the list price, distance to the all-time low, and, once 30 days are tracked, whether the price is below what the game usually costs.

Two other lenses sit beside them, not in the focus:

- **Gamer Dad**: does it fit a busy schedule? Short main story, quality, Steam Deck, controller, cloud saves, "Save Anytime".
- **Multiplayer** (online games only): is the community still there? Players, review activity now vs. half a year ago, quality, recent developer announcements.

The rules and weights are in `score.js` and on the page under "How the scores work". You can filter by genre, owned, price, deal (on sale, at the all-time low), length, and patient games vs. all games.

**My games**: the ✓ button on a cover marks a game as owned. The marks live in your browser's local storage (`pgr.status.v1`), with no account, and drive the "My games" filter (all, not owned, owned). The filters are stored in the URL hash, so you can share a link to a filtered ranking. Click a score to see how it was calculated.

## Data

Every value a score uses is fetched, not typed in. `scripts/fetch.mjs` takes every Steam game with at least 1,000 reviews and 75 % positive (from [SteamSpy](https://steamspy.com/api.php)) and builds `games.json` from:

| Value | Source |
|---|---|
| Release date, Metascore, controller support, Steam Cloud, "Save Anytime", free-to-play/in-app purchases, Early Access, single-player/online co-op/PvP/MMO | Steam store API (`appdetails`) |
| % positive reviews, Steam price and list price, peak players yesterday | SteamSpy |
| % positive at launch and in the last 6 months, review activity (refreshed monthly) | Steam review histogram |
| Date of the last developer announcement (refreshed monthly) | Steam news API |
| Steam Deck Verified / Playable | Steam Deck compatibility report |
| Best current price across stores, all-time low (USD) | [CheapShark API](https://apidocs.cheapshark.com/) |
| Genre tags (top 4, minus mood tags like "Indie") | SteamSpy |
| Main-story hours | HowLongToBeat (unofficial site API, may break) |

A source that fails keeps the game's previous value. The scoring rules are in `score.js`.

### Daily data releases

`games.json` is not in the repo. Every day at 05:00 UTC the workflow downloads the latest data release, fetches every game fresh on top of it (about 3.5 hours; it stops after 5 hours and keeps the rest from the previous day), appends today's values to `history.json`, publishes both as a release named `data-YYYY-MM-DD` and deploys the site with them.

`history.json` carries over from release to release, so every release holds the whole history. Per game it stores one row for every day on which the price, all-time low, Steam %, Metascore or Deck rating changed (with the review count of that day):

```json
{"fields":["day","price","lowest","steamPct","metascore","deck","steamReviews"],"games":{
 "620":[["2026-10-16",9.99,0.99,99,95,"verified",412000]]
}}
``` Pushes deploy the latest release's data without fetching.

To fetch and release outside the daily schedule:

```sh
gh workflow run deploy.yml -f fetch=true
```

## Local development

```sh
gh release download --pattern '*.json' --clobber      # latest data and history
python3 -m http.server 8000                          # then open http://localhost:8000
node --test
LIMIT=50 node scripts/fetch.mjs                      # fetch details for up to 50 games
```

There is no build step and there are no dependencies.

## Publishing

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which runs the tests and publishes the repo root (plus the latest `games.json`) on GitHub Pages. Set **Settings → Pages → Source** to **GitHub Actions** once.

divyachandana/Inference-Rally.readme:
# Inference Rally

> On-device AI models race taxis through a 3D maze. Every turn is a decision; every second is compute.

ExecuTorch Hackathon — Compute Track (Copilot+ PC, Snapdragon X Elite).
Each racer is the same (or a different) model on a different compute unit — **NPU vs GPU vs CPU**.
At every junction the model is asked *left, right or straight?* and its car **waits while it thinks**,
so faster on-device inference visibly wins.

See **[docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)** for the plan and architecture, and
**[docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md](docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md)** for coding rules.

## Demo video

[![Inference Rally demo video: click to watch on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/c1g9Ugve1Pw/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/c1g9Ugve1Pw)

▶️ **[Watch the demo on YouTube](https://youtu.be/c1g9Ugve1Pw)**

## Screenshots

![DEMO mode: simulated NPU vs GPU vs CPU racing through the maze, with the live map and standings](docs/images/demo-race.png)

| PLAY mode: you vs Llama-3.2-1B on the GPU | Race results |
|---|---|
| ![PLAY mode race](docs/images/play-race.png) | ![Results screen](docs/images/results.png) |

## Two modes

| Mode | Racers | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **DEMO** (default) | Simulated NPU vs GPU vs CPU — realistic speeds and mistakes | nothing |
| **PLAY** | **DC (you, arrow keys)** vs **Llama-3.2-1B on the M1 GPU** (real, via llama.cpp) vs a simulated racer | llama.cpp running |

Switch with **G** (or the MODE button). Lineups live in `racers.yaml` (`demo`, `play`, `snapdragon`).

## Quick start (Mac)

```bash
# 1. Python game server (once)
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# 2. Frontend (once)
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..

# 3. Run server (:8000) + UI (:5173)
./scripts/dev.sh
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> and press **Enter**.

### PLAY mode: real model on your Mac

```bash
brew install llama.cpp            # once
./scripts/start_models_mac.sh     # second terminal; first run downloads the model (~0.8 GB)
```

Then press **G** in the game (MODE: PLAY) and **Enter**. If the model isn't running, its car shows
"MODEL OFFLINE" and keeps going with fallback moves.

In PLAY mode the overview map is locked until you finish — like the models, you only know where the
exit is (follow the green beam).

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | Start / rematch (same maze) |
| N | New random maze |
| G | Switch DEMO / PLAY |
| ← ↑ → | Drive at a junction (PLAY): left / straight / right |
| ↓ | U-turn (PLAY) |
| M | Sound on/off |
| P | Retro pixels on/off |
| 1 / 2 / 3 | Focus one racer full screen |
| 0 / Esc | Back to split screen |

## Layout

- `src/inference_rally/` – Python game server
  - `maze.py` seeded maze + A* · `race.py` race engine · `deciders.py` racers' brains: simulated, real model (OpenAI-compatible), human
  - `prompts.py` junction prompt + reply parsing · `metrics.py` TTFT / tokens/sec timing
  - `models.py` typed config + event schema · `server.py` Starlette + Server-Sent Events
- `frontend/` – Three.js split-screen game (Vite)
  - `world/` maze, scenery, procedural pixel textures · `cars/` car model, driving, option arrows
  - `render/` split-screen viewports, overview map · `hud/` HUD, leaderboard, overlays · `audio/` chiptune synth
- `racers.yaml` – race settings and racer profiles (`demo`, `play`, `snapdragon`)
- `tests/` – pytest suite (game logic runs offline with simulated racers)
- `models/` – exported `.pte` / `.gguf` models (git-ignored)
- `scripts/` – `dev.sh` runs server + UI · `start_models_mac.sh` runs llama.cpp for PLAY mode
- `docs/` – plan, architecture, coding standards

## Demo build (single process)

```bash
cd frontend && npm run build && cd ..
python -m inference_rally.server   # serves the built UI at http://localhost:8000
```

## Checks

```bash
ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src && pytest
```

storrence88/snack-hole.readme:
# Snack Hole

A 3D hole game that runs in the browser. Slide a hole around a wooden floor covered in snacks. Anything smaller than the hole falls in. Eat enough and the hole grows, so you can swallow cupcakes, burgers, layer cakes and a giant donut.

## Controls

- **Phone or tablet:** drag anywhere on the screen.
- **Computer:** move the mouse and the hole follows it. You can also use the arrow keys or WASD.

Clear 80% of the snacks to finish a level. Each new level has a bigger board.

## How it's built

The whole game is one `index.html` file. It uses [three.js](https://threejs.org/) 0.160.0 from jsDelivr for rendering, plus a small custom physics loop for stacking and falling. There's no build step, so any static host can serve it (GitHub Pages, Vercel, Netlify).

To run it locally, serve the folder with any static server, for example `npx serve .`, and open the printed URL.

rkachniarz/SuperRollies.readme:
# Super Rollies

A d20 roll-off game. Pick up your die, throw it, roll higher than your opponent.
Lose a round and you lose a heart; lose three and the match is over.

Real rigid-body physics, a proper twenty-sided die with the numbers etched onto
its faces in the standard (non-spindown) layout, and a throw driven by an actual
drag-and-release gesture that works the same with a mouse or a finger.

## Running it

It's a static site with no build step — but it does need to be served over HTTP,
because browsers refuse to load ES modules from `file://`. Opening `index.html`
by double-clicking it will show a blank page.

```bash
npm install     # only needed for the dev server and the artifact build
npm run dev     # http://localhost:8000
```

Any static server works just as well (`python -m http.server`, the VS Code Live
Server extension, etc.).

## Publishing

The repository root *is* the deployable site. For GitHub Pages: push, then in
Settings → Pages pick your branch and the `/` root folder. `index.html`,
`styles.css` and `src/` are all that's served; three.js and cannon-es come from
a CDN at runtime.

## Layout

```
index.html    the page: markup, and the import map pinning three.js / cannon-es
styles.css    all styling - HUD, hearts, menu, result card
src/
  config.js   every tunable number and colour, in one place
  d20.js      the icosahedron, and which number goes on which face
  dice.js     building a die: faceted body, etched numbers, physics shape
  arena.js    the tray - renderer, camera, lights, walls, physics world
  input.js    grab / drag / release, and telling a throw from a fumble
  hud.js      hearts, the message card, the menu
  game.js     match flow: rounds, hearts lost, win and lose
  main.js     wires it together and runs the frame loop
tools/
  build-artifact.mjs   bundles everything into one file (see below)
```

Start with `main.js` — it's short, and it names every piece in the order they're
created.

## The single-file build

`npm run build` writes `dist/artifact.html`, the whole game inlined into one
page. That exists only for publishing to claude.ai as an artifact, which takes a
single file. Nothing about running or deploying the site needs it.

## A few things worth knowing before changing them

Several details here look arbitrary but are load-bearing — each one is commented
at the point it matters:

- **Face numbering is computed, not hard-coded.** Opposite faces summing to 21 is
  derived from the geometry itself, so it can't silently disagree with the mesh.
- **The number decals' orientation basis must stay right-handed.** Building it
  the other way round produces a mirror, which a quaternion cannot represent —
  the numbers then render at wrong angles or vanish entirely.
- **A throw is judged by distance dragged, not speed.** Speed came from
  timestamps a couple of pointer events apart and was badly unreliable whenever
  the browser was briefly busy.
- **The die is confined to what's actually on screen.** The camera's field of
  view is vertical, so a narrow phone screen sees less of the tray's width — and
  a die resting off screen can't be tapped, which would strand the match.
- **Camera near/far is deliberately tight**, to keep depth-buffer precision where
  the etched numbers need it.

# AutoSWF Vector Animation

**Turn your finished drawings into AdventureQuest Worlds items — without Adobe Animate.**

AutoSWF is a Windows desktop app for AQW item artists. You draw a cel-shaded item in Clip Studio
Paint, as usual. AutoSWF opens the file with its layers and does the rest: it converts the art into clean
vector shapes that look hand-made in Animate, finds the parts with AI (eyes, hair locks, ears,
accessories), animates them Flash-style (blinking eyes, swaying hair, light cloth physics), wires AQW's
color customization, shows the item on the AQW body, and exports a SWF ready for the game.

> **Status: early development.** Phase 1 (helms and morph helms) is being built. Done so far: the SWF engine
> (AQW-valid helm export) and the preview of a helm on the AQW male and female bodies.

## Why

Making an AQW item today means drawing it, then redrawing every line as vector art in Adobe Animate and
animating it by hand. That second step is slow, and Adobe discontinued Animate on March 1, 2026.
AutoSWF replaces it.

## Planned features — Phase 1: helms

- **Open your files directly:** Clip Studio Paint `.clip` and `.psd`, keeping your layers by painting
  pass (line art, flat colors, shadow, occlusion shadow, details, light).
- **Vectorization like hand-made Animate art:** brush-like line art with varying width, flat color
  regions without gaps, cel shading as separate shapes, few nodes.
- **AI part detection:** eyes, hair locks, ears, horns, accessories, back hair. You confirm or fix
  everything with a click.
- **Flash-style animation presets:** Blink (same pattern as AQW's own eyes), Sway with spring physics,
  Twitch and Pulse, all editable on a 24 fps timeline.
- **AQW color custom built in:** hair follows the player's Hair color, skin follows Skin, irises follow
  Eye, and other areas can follow Base, Trim or Accessory. Shadow and light layers become the game's
  Dark, Darker and Light tones.
- **Preview on the AQW body:** male and female, playing the game's own animations, with any player
  colors.
- **Export:** normal helms and morph helms (a whole new head with its own face), optional back hair,
  optional male/female variants. Every file is checked against the AQW format before it is saved.

## Roadmap

| Phase | Items |
|---|---|
| 1 | Helms and morph helms *(in progress)* |
| 2 | Armors (all 11 body parts, male and female) |
| 3 | Capes and weapons, plus **AI FX from a text prompt** (e.g. "electric energy running from the guard to the blade tip") |
| 4 | Pets |
| Later | Native Procreate, Krita, Illustrator, Animate and SWF importers |

Phase 1 is built in six steps: SWF engine → preview window → import and vectorization → parts and
color custom → animation presets → the full app (`.exe`).

## For developers

Requirements: Windows 10/11, Python 3.12 or newer.

```bash
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest
```

Documentation:

- Design: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-autoswf-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-autoswf-design.md)
  — includes the AQW item format, verified against live game files.
- Implementation plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/` (the plan in progress lives on its feature branch until it is
  merged)

### Try it

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python -m autoswf download-aqw
.venv/Scripts/python -m autoswf demo-helm cache/demo.swf
.venv/Scripts/python -m autoswf preview cache/demo.swf
```

`download-aqw` fetches the current AQW game client and one armor (for the preview body) from AQW's public server.
AQW files are only downloaded when you ask, stay on your computer (in `cache/`), and are never committed or shared.
Other commands: `inspect FILE` describes a SWF, `render FILE --class NAME --out OUT.png` renders one class, and
`fidelity` compares the renderer with JPEXS FFDec on official items.

## Disclaimer

AutoSWF is an independent fan-made tool. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Artix Entertainment.
AdventureQuest Worlds and all of its art belong to Artix Entertainment. This repository contains no AQW
game files: the app only downloads reference files from AQW's public servers on the user's own computer,
for preview, and never redistributes them.

JE2950/Escaperoom4.readme:
# Urbs Sepulta

A first-person Latin mystery for Common Entrance Level 1. Two levels:

1. **The Buried City.** A Roman city under Vesuvius lives the same day over and over. Find who will put out Vulcan's fire.
2. **The Rubicon.** Caesar's camp, the night of 10 January 49 BC. Find who will steal the eagle of the Thirteenth Legion.

Each level has five people with three Latin tasks each: 15 questions per level. The questions come from *Prep School Latin* by R. C. Bass (CC BY-NC-SA).

## Playing it

The game is hosted on GitHub Pages. Open the Pages address for this repository.

To test on your own computer you need a small local web server, because browsers block the game's scripts when you double-click `index.html`. Either:

- open the folder in VS Code and use the **Live Server** extension, or
- run `python3 -m http.server` in this folder, then visit `http://localhost:8000`.

## How the files fit together

```
index.html                 the page: screens, panels and buttons
css/style.css              all the styling
js/boot.js                 loads Three.js, the photo textures, then the scripts below in order
js/data/latin-bank.js      the Latin sentences, grammar tables and question builder
js/engine/                 renderer, textures and materials, lights and fire, buildings, people
js/levels/sepulta/         Level 1: ground, world, people and dialogue
js/levels/rubicon.js       Level 2: the camp, people and dialogue
js/game/                   state, audio, HUD, dialogue, Latin tasks, journal, time loop, player, setup screen
js/game/levels.js          the list of levels and the text that changes between them
js/main.js                 the main loop and start-up
assets/textures/           photo textures (stone, plaster, marble, wood, roof tiles, bronze)
assets/portraits/          portraits shown in the dialogue panel, named after each character's id
vendor/three/              a local copy of Three.js 0.160, so school networks that block CDNs still work
```

The scripts are ordinary (non-module) scripts loaded one after another, so they share one global scope. Load order matters: it is the list in `js/boot.js`.

## Adding a level

1. Write `js/levels/<name>.js` with a build function, five people (`PEOPLE`), their dialogue (`D`), and ground functions. `js/levels/rubicon.js` is the model to copy.
2. Add the file to the `SCRIPTS` list in `js/boot.js`, before `js/game/levels.js`.
3. Register it in `LEVELS` in `js/game/levels.js` and add a button with `data-level="3"` to the title screen in `index.html`.

## Backups

Before every push, the version that is live gets saved as a branch named `backup/<date>-<label>`. To go back to one, check out that branch, or open it on GitHub and copy its files over `main`.

## Credits

- Latin sentences: *Prep School Latin*, R. C. Bass, CC BY-NC-SA.
- [Three.js](https://threejs.org), MIT licence (see `vendor/three/LICENSE`).
- Fonts: Cinzel and EB Garamond from Google Fonts.

deloy4/jetpack-christmas.desc: Browser rebuild of Jetpack Christmas Special (1993 DOS) with new art and sound
deloy4/jetpack-christmas.readme:
# Jetpack Christmas Special

A browser rebuild of Jetpack Christmas Special, the 1993 DOS game by Adam Pedersen that Software
Creations gave away as freeware. Play it at https://deloy4.github.io/jetpack-christmas/

All ten original levels are here, and the rules come from reading the original program: walking
and jetpack speeds, gravity, fuel, ladders, ice, sludge, conveyors, the Phase Shifter's dig and
regrow times, all eight monsters, buttons, barriers, teleporters, the pop-up pickups, scoring and
lives. The art and sound are new. Every tile and sprite is drawn with canvas paths, keeping the
original's layout and colours.

## Controls

The arrows walk and climb, Alt or Z fires the jetpack, and Ctrl, Enter or X runs the Phase
Shifter, which tunnels through brick but not grey stone. Hold Down while flying to keep your
height, and press Down on a button or teleporter to use it. Esc loses this Santa when you're
stuck, + and − change the game speed, P pauses and M turns the sound off. On a touchscreen,
buttons appear under the game. The original's hidden keys still work: hold Tab and 2, then press
L for an extra life, F for a full tank, I for a shield or S to skip the level.

## How it runs

The game runs at 31.6 frames a second, which is what level 1 measured in the original running
in DOSBox. Positions use the original's units (1/32 of a pixel), and the screen draws between
frames so movement stays smooth.

- `index.html`, the page.
- `game.js`, the game: the frame loop in the original's order, the monsters, and the screens around play.
- `art.js`, all the drawing.
- `levels.js`, the ten levels decoded from the original `JETLEV.DAT`.
- `shapes.js`, the rounded corners and stone edges of each brick tile, read from the original sprite sheet.
- `preview.html`, a still view of one level's art (`preview.html?level=3&monsters=1`).

There is no build step; open `index.html` in a browser.

Differences from the original: one player only, no level editor or demo, and the frame rate is
the same on every level (the original speeds up on levels with many monsters). High scores are
kept in your browser. The status bar adds a gift count.

your best score is kept on the phone.

chopki/test-game.readme:
# Hold the Hall

A 3D browser tower-defence / survival game. Raiders pour in from the edges of the map to tear down your
**Town Hall**. Ring it with **castle walls**, raise **archer towers**, **cannon towers**, **magic spires** and
**catapults**, and survive as many waves as you can against goblins, orcs and trolls.

| Desktop | Phone (Pixel 7) |
| ------- | --------------- |
| ![Desktop, High preset](docs/screenshots/showcase-desktop-high.jpg) | ![Phone, High preset](docs/screenshots/showcase-phone-high.jpg) |

Map 8 (`?seed=8`) on the default High preset.

Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) and [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/). Plain JavaScript (ES modules), no assets: every model
is built from primitives in code.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
```

| Script            | What it does                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `npm run dev`     | Dev server with hot reload                       |
| `npm run build`   | Production build into `dist/` (static, relative paths) |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally               |
| `npm test`        | Run the headless simulation tests (Vitest), incl. a check that the pre-baked sprites are current |
| `npm run bake`    | Re-bake the battlefield sprites into `public/sprites/` and `public/sprites-hd/` (run after changing models or textures) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Vital browser tests (`@smoke`, ~3 min, desktop + phone) |
| `npm run test:e2e:full` | Full browser regression suite (~4 min)      |
| `npm run test:all` | Unit tests + vital browser tests                |
| `npm run test:full` | Unit tests + full browser suite                |

Requires Node 18+.

## Play in the browser (GitHub Pages)

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs the unit tests and builds on every push, then publishes the default branch to
GitHub Pages. The browser tests are a separate, manual workflow: **Actions → "Browser tests (manual)" → Run workflow**, choosing
the `smoke` (vital) or `full` suite.
One-time setup: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**. Then push (or run the
workflow from the Actions tab). The game is served at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`.

GitHub Pages needs a **public** repository on a free GitHub plan; private repos need GitHub Pro, Team or Enterprise.
The build in `dist/` is plain static files (relative paths), so it also works on any static host such as Netlify,
Vercel or Cloudflare Pages.

## How to play

- Enemies spawn in the **dirt border** around the map and march toward the Town Hall.
- You get a build phase before each wave (60s before the first wave, 30s after that). The banner at the top tells you
  what's coming next and from which direction. Press **Space** to start early.
- **Walls don't make enemies give up, they make them choose.** Enemies take the cheapest route to the Town Hall: they walk
  around a short wall, but if the way round is too long (or the Hall is fully enclosed) they smash through. Damaged walls
  are weaker spots and attract attackers. Funnel enemies past your towers, and layer your walls.
- Kills and cleared waves earn gold. Selling a building refunds half its cost, scaled by its remaining HP.
- The Town Hall fires arrows of its own, but it won't hold out alone for long. If it falls, the game is over.

### Controls

| Input                    | Action                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `1` – `5`                | Castle Wall / Archer Tower / Cannon Tower / Magic Spire / Catapult |
| Left click               | Place building · select building           |
| Left drag (wall mode)    | Plan a wall line (straight or L), shows cost; release to build. Drag onto a tower to join it |
| `X`                      | Sell mode                                  |
| Right click / `Esc`      | Cancel build mode / deselect (placing a tower also ends it; wall mode stays on) |
| Right drag               | Pan camera (the iso view is fixed, like the art reference) |
| Middle drag / `WASD` / arrows | Pan camera                            |
| Mouse wheel              | Zoom                                       |
| `Space`                  | Start next wave now                        |
| `P` / `F`                | Pause / cycle speed (1×, 2×, 3×)           |
| `H`                      | Help                                       |

**On phones and tablets:** tap a build button, then tap or drag on the map to position the building. The map stays
still while you do; drag to the edge of the screen to scroll it. Lift your finger and tap **✓** to build or **✕** to
cancel. You can drag the building again before confirming. Building a tower ends placement mode (pick it again
to place another); wall mode stays on so you can draw several lines. Walls work the same way: drag out a line, adjust either
end, then ✓. Dragging a wall end over a tower snaps it onto the tower's side. With no build mode
selected, one finger pans; pinch with two fingers to zoom. Graphics settings are automatically lighter on touch
devices.

## Graphics settings

Open **⚙** in the top bar. The game pauses while the menu is open.

| Preset | Render scale | Anti-aliasing | Frame-rate cap | Scenery and ground detail |
| ------ | ------------ | ------------- | -------------- | ------------------------- |
| Low | Auto | off | 30 fps | low |
| Medium | Auto | off | 60 fps | medium |
| High (always used at startup) | 150% | on | unlimited | high |

**Auto** render scale adjusts itself (50%–150%, capped at the screen's pixel density) to hold the frame-rate
cap: it drops as soon as frames slow down and creeps back up after a few smooth seconds. Shadows are baked into
the sprites, so they cost nothing extra.
The FPS counter also shows the current render scale.

The menu's **Map** row shows the current map number and has a **New map** bu
