sgilson7/mage-tower-battle.readme:
# Mage Tower Battle

You are the new archmage of a mage college. The last one was fired, and on his way out he pulled every book off the library shelves. Read what he left on the floor to learn spell pieces, join them into spells at the laboratory, interview applicants, and teach your students by drawing each spell's glyphs at the podium. Then watch: every tower is attacked at once, and your students cast what you taught them, as well as you taught it.

**Play it:** https://sgilson7.github.io/mage-tower-battle/

## Playing

- Walk with WASD or the arrow keys. Stand at a station to use it; E does its main thing and Esc cancels.
- A day is a few minutes of preparation and then a battle you watch. Walking, reading, interviewing and teaching all take time, so the order you visit stations in matters.
- Spells read left to right: modifiers change the next payload, and a trigger starts the rest of the spell when the payload hits, dies or ends. A strong spell with a short cooldown costs much more mana.
- Teaching one student forgives a shaky line; a whole class needs a careful one. How well you draw is how well they learn.
- Spells that start with Invade send summons at a rival. Yours show in their invasion book at once; your students' only when the battle starts.
- Damage to your tower lowers your score, and nothing raises it. The highest score after the last day wins.
- Modes: versus three computer rivals (the Spellcrafter, the Mass Teacher, the Attack Mage and the Balanced Archmage), a short practice day, and four trials with Bronze, Silver, Gold and Archmage medals. Online play for four is planned for the next update.

## How it is built

The game is a [Builder](https://github.com/sgilson7/builder-setting) project. Every rule lives in a Rust core with no input or output, no floats and no clocks: battles, spells, the room, the mini-games' scoring, the bots, the drawing lists and even the chip sounds. A WebAssembly shim moves values to the page and decides nothing, and the page draws what the core returns. Tests read the repository's own source and fail if a rule leaks out of the core.

The design, the plan and the record of every decision made along the way are in `BRIEF.md`, `PLAN.md`, `SECOND-ORDER.md`, `DECISIONS.md` and `HANDOFF.md`.

## Build, test and serve

```bash
./scripts/setup.sh              # once: Python venv with Playwright and three browsers
cargo test --workspace          # the core, boundary, copy and storage tests
./scripts/build.sh              # release WebAssembly build into dist/
python3 scripts/serve.py        # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
./scripts/check.sh              # everything, before publishing
python3 scripts/break_tests.py  # each row of tests/breaks.json must make its test fail
./scripts/count-tests.sh        # the test count to quote in a document
```

Probes, outside the check: `tools/probe_wasm.py` (physics in the browser), `crates/core/tests/physics_probe.rs` and `crates/core/tests/balance_probe.rs` (run with `--ignored --nocapture`).

Needs Rust (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`), `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.127 and Python 3.

## Layout

| Path | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/core` | every rule: `battle.rs`, `prep.rs`, `spell.rs`, `game.rs`, `bot.rs`, the physics in `body.rs` and `ragdoll.rs`, drawing in `scene.rs`, `look.rs` and `render.rs`, chip sounds in `sound.rs`; `session.rs` is the door the shim calls |
| `crates/shim` | the `wasm-bindgen` functions the page calls; each is one call into the core |
| `web/` | the page: `app.js`, the WebGL renderer `gl.js`, the overlay `render2d.js`, panels `ui.js`, `keys.js`, `sound.js`, and `store.js`, the only file that touches browser storage |
| `data/` | every word (`strings.json`), the content and balance (`content.json`), models, palette, sounds, controls and shaders |
| `GLOSSARY.md`, `TONE.md` | what each term means; how every string is written |
| `tests/browser/` | the browser check and the practice day it plays |

## Licence

MIT. See `LICENSE` and `LICENSES.md`.

ekarbe/world-drive.readme:
# World Drive 🚗

An endless, procedurally generated voxel driving game that runs in the browser.
Cruise through cities, villages, forests and fields, collect coins, pull stunts,
deliver cargo, and spend your earnings on new cars, upgrades and paint jobs.

**Play:** https://ekarbe.github.io/world-drive/

## Features

- **Endless world**: 64 m chunks are streamed in around you with level of detail. Each save has its own fixed world seed.
- **Simcade driving**: a custom raycast-suspension vehicle model with tyre slip, drifting, jumps and air control.
- **Ways to earn coins**: coin pickups, near misses with traffic, drifts, big air off ramps, and delivery missions between depots.
- **Shops**:
  - 🚗 Car dealers: 7 cars, from the Pixel Hatch to the Apex Hyper.
  - 🔧 Tuning shops: engine, tyres, brakes and suspension, 5 levels each.
  - 🎨 Paint shops: paint, rims, racing stripes, underglow and spoilers.
- **AI traffic**: cars follow lanes and turn at intersections.
- **Audio**: synthesized engine and effects plus generative lo-fi music, with no audio files to download.
- **Controls**: keyboard, gamepad and touch.
- **Saving**: autosaves to `localStorage`.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Gamepad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accelerate / brake & reverse | W / S or ↑ / ↓ | RT / LT |
| Steer | A / D or ← / → | Left stick |
| Handbrake | Space | X / RB |
| Enter shop | E / Enter | B |
| Camera | C | Y |
| Map | M | Back |
| Reset car | R | LB |
| Menu | Esc | Start |
| Horn / music toggle | H / N | |

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # local dev server
npm test         # unit tests (world generation & physics)
npm run build    # production build into dist/
```

Pushing to `main` builds, tests and deploys the game to GitHub Pages (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`).
In the repository settings, set **Pages → Source** to **GitHub Actions**.

See [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) for the architecture and the roadmap.

# Wipeout Soup

> **Fork of [NJH-1001/Wipeout2K97XL](https://github.com/NJH-1001/Wipeout2K97XL).**
> All credit for the recompilation project goes to its author. This fork adds
> experiments on top:
> - ultrawide aspect choices in the widescreen mod;
> - a **Scene Depth (ReShade)** mod that gives the game a real depth buffer
>   for ReShade, built on a full-PGXP build of the game. See
>   [docs/soup/scene-depth-reshade.md](docs/soup/scene-depth-reshade.md);
> - framework fixes that let the retail SCPH-1001 BIOS boot (see
>   [docs/upstream/psxrecomp-scph1001-issue.md](docs/upstream/psxrecomp-scph1001-issue.md)).
>
> Framework changes live in `patches/psxrecomp-soup.patch`, applied after
> upstream's `patches/psxrecomp.patch`.
> The rest of this README is upstream's. Report problems with the fork's
> changes here, not upstream.

# Wipeout XL Recompiled — Wipeout2K97XL

An unofficial PSXRecomp compatibility project for **Wipeout XL (USA), SCUS-94351**.
Windows 10/11, 64-bit Intel or AMD. OpenBIOS and SDL3.

[Download setup kits](https://github.com/NJH-1001/Wipeout2K97XL/releases/latest) ·
[Report a problem](https://github.com/NJH-1001/Wipeout2K97XL/issues)

## Download and setup

The public artifact is `wipeoutxl-0.1.0-windows-x64.zip`, a **setup kit**, not a
prebuilt copy of the game. Supply your legally obtained USA Redump-style CUE
and all **12 BIN tracks**. Other regions and revisions are not supported.

1. Extract the entire setup ZIP into a writable folder.
2. Install Python 3.11 or newer. Allow disk space for your disc and a local build.
3. Run `Wipeout2K97XL.exe`, keep OpenBIOS selected and select your CUE.
4. Choose **Generate & rebuild**. The wizard can obtain its supported CMake,
   Ninja and Clang toolchain; game code is generated and compiled locally.
5. Reopen the setup executable after compilation. It forwards to the local
   playable build. Keep the kit together and back up your saves before updates.

No disc images, extracted game executable, generated game code, retail BIOS,
memory cards, captures or analysis databases are distributed. Windows setup
binaries are unsigned. [Experimental Linux and macOS previews](https://github.com/NJH-1001/Wipeout2K97XL/releases/tag/v0.1.0-native-preview)
are available for Linux x64 and Intel/Apple Silicon Macs. **Gameplay unverified.** See
[native platform status and setup](docs/native-platforms.md).

### Supported data track

- Boot executable: `SCUS_943.51`
- Track 01 size: `86045568` bytes
- MD5: `bee4ab5e4835235ccf6f16bc8caea5e6`
- SHA-1: `5694008c30fa9896d17afdd6281e4bebb9f63953`

## Controls

Connect a controller before launching; Player 1 automatically selects a
recognized gamepad. Select Keyboard in the launcher to use keyboard controls.
The emulated pad is locked to NeGcon mode. Xbox and the wired PowerA Advantage
Switch 2 controller have been physically tested. Other Switch, PS4 and PS5
models use SDL3 mappings but have not been physically tested here.

The **NeGcon enhanced dual sticks** mod starts with this customizable preset:

![NeGcon enhanced dual sticks: steering, pitch, air-brakes, weapon and acceleration](docs/images/negcon-dual-sticks.png)

[Open the full-size controller diagram](docs/images/negcon-dual-sticks.png).

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left stick horizontal | Analog steering |
| Right stick vertical | Pitch |
| Right stick left / right | Right / left air-brake (reversed) |
| L1 / R1 or LB / RB | Left / right air-brake |
| Right trigger | Analog acceleration, when hardware supports it |
| Bottom face button | Full acceleration / menu select |
| Left trigger or left face button | Fire equipped weapon |
| Right face button | Discard weapon (NeGcon A) |
| Top face button | Change view / menu back (NeGcon B) |
| D-pad | Menu navigation and original directional controls |
| Start / Plus / Options / Menu | Start / pause |

Open **Mods** before launching to change stick assignments, brake direction,
brake buttons, trigger assignments and face-button acceleration. Select
**Recommended dual sticks** to restore the preset's behavior, or **Custom** to
use your saved individual choices. **Use input.ini bindings** or disabling this
mod returns to the editable input file. Right-stick steering and braking can
share an axis; disable stick brakes if that is unwanted. Pitch and air-brakes
are digital, matching the game's decoded inputs; steering and throttle are analog.
Changes apply on the next launch. Keyboard and other button bindings remain
editable in `keybinds.ini` and `input.ini`; rebuilds preserve existing files.

Keyboard: WASD/arrows for directions, Space/X for acceleration, Q/E for
left/right air-brakes, Enter for Start and Backspace for Select. See
[controller details](docs/controllers.md) for other button assignments.

## Display mods

- **16:9 Widescreen:** wider 3D view with centered menus and extended loading
  backgrounds. OpenGL required.
- **Extended Draw Distance:** extends road, scenery and billboard visibility.
- **Extended Enemy Ship Distance:** extends ship meshes and exhaust; enable
  Extended Draw Distance as well.
- **CRT Display:** JVC and Sony Trinitron inspired effects. These approximate
  the appearance of MiSTer presets; they are not exact FPGA filter ports.

Visual mods are off by default and can be enabled on the Mods page. The default
renderer is OpenGL with 4x internal resolution and 4:3 presentation. Distance
mods remain experimental: user playtests accepted their results, but exhaustive
track, camera and clipping coverage is not complete. Netplay is not enabled.

## Verification and reporting

See [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md) for tested behavior and remaining release
gates. Report OS, CPU/GPU, controller and connection, renderer, enabled mods and
reproduction steps. Do not upload copyrighted game data or private captures.

See [PUBLICATION.md](PUBLICATION.md) for pa

lauPhilip/au-btech-open-door.desc: Interactive, team-based learning of threat modelling in the browser, built on the CyPro method from Aarhus University.
lauPhilip/au-btech-open-door.readme:
# Open Door

**Walk the office, spot the risks: an open-source classroom game for interactive learning of threat modelling.**

Open Door is a browser game for teams of three to five students. Each team walks through a top-down office of a fictional company, talks to the people who work there, and leaves sticky notes wherever something could go wrong. Then a scenario plays out — the webshop goes down on Black Friday, malware arrives on a USB stick, a fake invoice lands in accounting — and the class compares which team saw it coming.

Behind the play sits the CyPro method from the [Digital Business Development toolbox](https://dbd.au.dk/p/toolbox) at Aarhus University: context establishment, system modelling, assets, threat identification and threat analysis. Students practise the method first and learn its names in the debrief. The game is being designed for the MSc in Engineering, Technology-Based Business Development, at Aarhus University in Herning, and runs in any browser on the university network (eduroam) without accounts or logins.

> **Status:** milestone M2 – Playable is in progress. A class can join, hear the story and walk the office together; close-ups, sticky notes and the day of the incident come next. The eduroam classroom test is planned for later. See [next steps](docs/dev-notes/next-steps.md).

## What is in this repository

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`docs/concept-book/`](docs/concept-book/index.html) | The concept book: target group, journey, core loop, UX rules, design system, assets, mockups, teacher kit and architecture — 15 boards in one HTML page |
| [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md) | The development roadmap, from repository setup to version 1 |
| [`docs/backlog.md`](docs/backlog.md) | 45 work items in four milestones; [`scripts/`](scripts/) turns them into GitHub issues |
| [`scenarios/`](scenarios/) | Game content as text files: the first scenario, *Nordknit · Black Friday*, and the file format’s schema |
| [`docs/scenario-format.md`](docs/scenario-format.md) | How to write a new scenario, with no coding needed |
| [`docs/testing/`](docs/testing/) | Test plans, starting with the M1 classroom test on eduroam |
| `app/`, `room/`, `shared/` | The code: browser app, Cloudflare Worker with live rooms, and shared message format |
| [`docs/decisions/`](docs/decisions/) | Short records of the main decisions and why they were made |
| [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) | An index of all documentation |

To read the concept book, open `docs/concept-book/index.html` in a browser, or visit the published version once GitHub Pages is turned on: `https://lauphilip.github.io/au-btech-open-door/`.

## Run it

Open Door is written in TypeScript. The app is built with Svelte and Vite, and the live session rooms run on Cloudflare Workers with Durable Objects through PartyServer. You need [Node.js 22](https://nodejs.org) or newer.

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

This builds the app and starts two local servers: the rooms on port 8787 and the app on port 5173. Other devices on the same network can join through your computer’s address on port 5173.

| Address | Who uses it |
|---|---|
| `/teacher` | The teacher: create a session, then start the story and the walk |
| `/screen/CODE` | The projector: QR code and teams, then the story, then the live office map |
| `/` or `/j/CODE` | Students: type the code (or scan the QR code), pick a name, a face and a team |
| `/network-test` | The hello room from milestone M1; add `?view=projector` for its projector view |

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Runs the app and the rooms locally |
| `npm run scenarios` | Checks the scenario files and turns them into code for the game |
| `npm run check` | Type-checks all three parts |
| `npm test` | Runs the unit tests |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Plays a whole session in real browser pages with Playwright (run `npm run build` and `npx playwright install chromium` first) |
| `npm run build` | Builds the app into `app/dist` |
| `npm run deploy` | Builds and deploys everything to Cloudflare (run `npx wrangler login` once first) |
| `node scripts/simulate-class.mjs` | Simulates a class of 40 players joining the network-test room |
| `node scripts/simulate-class.mjs --mode game` | Simulates a whole game session: a teacher, a projector and 25 students who join, sit down and walk |

The code is split into three parts: `shared/` holds the message format and game rules used everywhere, `room/` is the Cloudflare Worker that serves the app and hosts the rooms, and `app/` is what students and teachers see in the browser.

## How a class plays

| Step | Time | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Join | 3 min | Students scan a QR code, choose a nickname and a face, and join a team |
| The story | 3 min | A short illustrated story from the company’s CEO sets the goal |
| Walk and spot | 25 min | Teams explore the office, open close-ups of people and things, and write sticky notes |
| The day happens | 25 min | The scenario unfolds; teams follow clues room to room and make a final call |
| Talk it through | 30 min | The projector compares all teams, and the CyPro terms are revealed |
| Take it home | — | Each team downloads its notes as a filled-in CyPro threat table |

## Licence

Open Door is open source under two licences. The **code** is released under the [MIT licence](LICENSE). The **content** — scenarios, texts, illustrations and the concept book — is released under [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0](LICENSE-CONTENT.md), because it builds on CyPro material published under the same licence. See [decision 0002](docs/decisions/0002-licensing.md) for the reasoning.

## Credits

The learning content builds on the CyPro project, “Cybersecure manufacturing in Denmark”, by Aarhus University, the Alexandra Institute, DAMRC, UGLA Insights and FORCE Technology, funded by the Danish Industry Foundation. remathes/DragonLantern.readme:
# Dragon's Lantern

A Dragon's Dogma style belt lantern for **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered (5.0)**.

![Dragon's Lantern](docs/thumbnail.jpg)

- Hangs on Geralt's left hip (or right hip, back, front-left) while equipped in a Pockets slot. Optionally always on the belt.
- **Auto light**: lights when you put it in a Pockets (quick) slot, goes out when you take it out. It can also light only at night, or be manual only.
- Use it from the quick slot to light or douse it by hand. It never goes into his hand.
- Burns **Lantern Oil**. One flask lasts 8 game hours by default, and carried flasks refill it automatically.
- Swimming or diving **puts it out**. You relight it yourself.
- Hidden in cutscenes and dialogue. Swings as he walks, runs and rolls.
- Innkeepers and shopkeepers sell the lantern and oil.
- Everything can be adjusted under Options > Mods > Dragon's Lantern.
- Text in all 17 languages the game supports.

## Get the mod

- **Steam Workshop:** https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3821132676
- **Nexus Mods:** https://www.nexusmods.com/witcher3/mods/14479
- **Mod.io:** coming soon

Requires The Witcher 3 Remastered (game version 5.0 or later). Then buy the
Belt Lantern from an innkeeper or shopkeeper and put it in a Pockets slot.

## Reporting bugs

Please report bugs here on GitHub, wherever you got the mod:
**[Open a bug report](https://github.com/remathes/DragonLantern/issues/new/choose)**

The form asks for your game version, where you got the mod and what other mods
you use. If you can, open the debug console and run `ddlstatus`, then paste what
it shows. That usually pinpoints the problem.

## Learning from this mod

The whole REDkit project is here, so you can see how a script-driven mod for
the Remaster is put together:

- `workspace/scripts/local/dragonsLantern.ws`: the gameplay script. It uses
  REDkit's annotations (`@wrapMethod`, `@addMethod`, `@addField`), so no vanilla
  script is replaced and it combines well with other mods.
- `docs/REDKIT_ASSET_GUIDE.md`: how the lantern entity was made from a vanilla
  model in REDkit's Entity Editor.
- `docs/PROVENANCE.md`: which vanilla script or data file each part follows.
- `src/strings/`: translations kept in one Python file and written into
  REDkit's string database by a small script.

## Layout

```
dragonslantern.w3edit                REDkit project
workspace/                           what REDkit sees (shown as "virtualdepot")
  mods/dragons_lantern/ddl_lantern.w2ent   lantern entity (from vanilla lantern_dwarf_01)
  gameplay/items[_plus]/def_item_dragons_lantern.xml
  gameplay/gui_new/icons/inventory/ddl/    inventory icons
  scripts/local/dragonsLantern.ws
src/                                 source copies, kept in sync with workspace/
  scripts/dragonsLantern.ws          all gameplay logic
  items/def_item_dragons_lantern.xml lantern + oil item definitions
  menu/modDragonsLantern.xml         mod settings menu (goes in the game's bin\config)
  icons/                             icon PNGs
  strings/translations.py            all text, 17 languages
  strings/apply_strings.py           writes translations.py into the project string database
LocalEditorStringDataBaseW3_UTF8_mod.db   REDkit string database
docs/                                guides, provenance, changelog, store texts
```

## Building

You need The Witcher 3 Remastered and the free REDkit (Steam, GOG or Epic).

1. Open `dragonslantern.w3edit` in REDkit.
2. Script changes: edit `workspace\scripts\local\dragonsLantern.ws` and copy it to `src\`.
   REDkit compiles scripts on startup, so restart it after editing.
3. Text changes: edit `src\strings\translations.py`, close REDkit, run
   `python -I src\strings\apply_strings.py`, then Publish > Cook Mod Strings.
4. Publish > Save and publish mod project, with **Install** ticked.
5. Copy `src\menu\modDragonsLantern.xml` to the game's
   `bin\config\r4game\user_config_matrix\pc\`.

## Console commands

Commands that take values need parentheses and commas, e.g. `ddlpos(0, 2, 0)`.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ddlgive` | Adds a Belt Lantern and 3 oil flasks |
| `ddltoggle` | Lights or douses the lantern |
| `ddlstatus` | Shows owned / spawned / lit / oil remaining |
| `ddlglow(brightness, radius)` | Sets the light (0 keeps a value); saved to the mod menu |
| `ddlpos(forward, up, out)` | Nudges placement in cm, on top of the default |
| `ddlrot(pitch, yaw, roll)` | Rotates the carrier in degrees |
| `ddlbody(pitch, yaw, roll)` | Rotates the lantern body about its own axes |
| `ddltune` / `ddlreset` | Show / clear the nudges |

## Consoles

It's unknown whether Mod.io mods on PS5/Xbox may ship scripts. This mod relies
entirely on scripts, so it targets PC.

## License

Original work in this repository is MIT licensed. The Witcher 3 game content it
builds on belongs to CD PROJEKT RED and is used under the REDkit EULA and Fan
Content Guidelines. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). This is a free fan project, not
affiliated with CD PROJEKT RED.

MikeWeaver-dev/niagara-or-bust.desc: Niagara or Bust! A browser ragdoll game about surviving the Horseshoe Falls.
MikeWeaver-dev/niagara-or-bust.readme:
# 🌊 Niagara or Bust!

A cartoon ragdoll game in the spirit of Happy Wheels: try to survive going over the **Horseshoe Falls**. It runs in the browser on Chrome, both desktop and mobile.

Start on the bank, pick your spot, jump in, paddle and dodge while the current drags you to the brink. Then go 188 feet straight down. Survive and you earn lumens. Don't survive and you earn lumens *and* a gore bonus.

## How to play

| | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| Walk on the bank / steer | ◀ ▶ or A / D | drag on the left half of the screen |
| Paddle faster / slower | ▲ ▼ or W / S | drag up / down |
| Jump in / ability / mini-game | Space (or Enter / E / Shift) | big button on the right |
| Pause | Esc / P | ❚❚ button |

* **Lanes matter.** The middle of the river is the **Green Channel**: fastest current, but deep water at the bottom (+12%). The edges are slower but end in **rocks** (-10%).
* **Your live survival odds** are always on screen. Damage lowers them, and so does a wrecked vessel (then you're swimming). Going faster helps you clear the rocks at the base.
* **The drop is physics.** Each vessel has its own mini-game, then the dice roll on your final odds.

## Vessels (unlock in order)

| Vessel | Base | River ability | Drop mini-game |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absolutely Nothing | 14% | PANIC! (swim faster) | Pencil-dive ring timing |
| Life Jacket | 22% | BOB (hop) | Tuck ring timing |
| Surfboard | 22% | OLLIE (+ SHRED lumens in rapids) | **Surf down the face of the falls**, keep your balance |
| Oak Barrel | 34% | BRACE (-75% damage) | Brace ring timing |
| Kayak | 30% | ROLL (invulnerable) | Tilt the nose into the green, then BOOF |
| Canoe (+ Gary) | 33% | POWER STROKE (dash) | "Hold on, Gary!" ring timing |
| Hamster Ball | 42% | BOUNCE (jump) | Curl-up ring timing |
| Jet Ski + Parachute | 34% | TURBO (smash logs) | **Deploy the chute** in the green altitude zone |
| The Golden Goose | **100%** | FLAP (fly) + lays golden eggs | Glide down like royalty (flap to float, steer anywhere) |

The Golden Goose unlocks last, after *everything* else, and you always survive with it.

## Characters

* **Annie Edson Taylor** (1901): the first person to survive in a barrel, on her 63rd birthday. Her cat tags along.
* **Lil' Timmy**, age 7: cartoon physics protect him. Bonks and a ghost instead of gore (the only character without it).
* **Kacey the Rainbow Giraffe**: four legs, a very long neck, and rainbow glitter gore.
* **Bobby Leach** (1911): steel barrel. Later died after slipping on an orange peel. Watch the beach.
* **Jean Lussier** (1928): rode a giant rubber ball with 32 inner tubes.

## Economy

* Every attempt pays **lumens**: river pickups, skill bonuses, a survival bonus, and a gore bonus for messy deaths.
* Each unlock gives **+15% lumen earnings** (ramping), so later unlocks come faster.
* **Settings → Economy → TEST** (the default) makes everything cheap for testing. **NORMAL** is 6x prices.

## Cheats (all available from the start)

The cheat menu has 19 toggles: **Salmon Mode** (swim upstream and never go over... until a bear eats you in the most disgusting nature documentary ever made), Try Everything, God Mode, Always Die, Gore Galore, Explosive Impact, Explosive Diarrhea, Big Head, Tiny Mode, Moon Gravity, Bullet Time, Noodle Limbs, Disco Falls, Super Paddle, Invincible Hull, Rock Party, Lazy River, Skip to the Edge, Lumen Rain. There are also quick buttons for +500 / +5000 lumens, Unlock Everything and Reset, plus a **GO!** button on the Shop and Cheats screens that jumps straight into a run.

Secret codes: `SALMON`, `IDDQD`, `GOD`, `BLOODBATH`, `KABOOM`, `POOP`, `BIGHEAD`, `DISCO`, `MOON`, `MONEY`, `LUMENS`, `GOOSE`, `UNLOCKALL`, `HONK`.

## Gore

The gore setting can be **OFF / ON / MAX** (MAX is the default). Adults get streaking blood, spurting arteries, torn stumps with bone and marrow, chunks of meat, organs and intestines, blood on the rocks, in the water and splattered across the screen. Kacey bleeds rainbow glitter. Every now and then a death is **explosive diarrhea** instead. OFF turns every death into cartoon bonks and ghosts, so it's kid friendly.

Knocked out in the river? You come to after 5 seconds.

## Tech

* Vite + React 18 + React Router 6 (basename `/game`).
* All game rendering is hand-drawn vector art on a 2D `<canvas>`, so there are no image assets.
* A custom Verlet physics engine runs the ragdolls, with breakable joints for the gore.
* The whole soundtrack and every sound effect are **synthesized live with the Web Audio API**. There are no audio files.
* Progress is saved in `localStorage`, per device.

```
src/
  audio/      audio.js (synth SFX engine), music.js (sequencer + 7 original songs)
  data/       characters, vessels, cheats, death/survival messages
  game/       Game.js loop, river.js (bank + river + salmon), drop.js (the falls),
              physics.js, ragdoll.js, fx.js particles, *Art.js renderers, hud.js, input.js
  components/ React screens: Title, Play (loadout/game/results), Shop, Cheats, Settings, HowTo
```

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # dev server (also on your LAN)
npm run play    # production build + LAN server at http://<your-ip>:5173/game/
```

See **[DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md)** for publishing it at `yourdomain.com/game` on Firebase Hosting.

*Going over Niagara Falls is illegal and extremely dangerous. This is a cartoon. Stay on the bank and buy a hot dog.*

# Archmere Volleyball

Buildless mobile-first static website. Serve `dist/` with a static HTTP server.

Data is a reviewed snapshot, not an automatic Google Sheets feed. `players.json` was read from the native Google Sheet on October 16, 2026 and includes Patreece Spence's corrected 2011 graduation year. `prepare.py` prepares source data and verifies every career subtotal. It needs the sibling `archmere_record_book/normalized.json` archive in the original workspace; the deployed `dist/data.json` is self-contained.

The two unverified Lillian Guzevich Smyrna assists remain excluded. Blank statistics remain null; zero is retained. Player source-row counts are not games played.

All routes use URL fragments so player/game/filter links can be shared without server rewrites. Website data is read-only. Update `dist/data.json`, validate totals and republish to change the public records.

Branding: standalone Auks logo supplied by Archmere's BSN Sports school store: https://cache.bsnsports.com/comp/sls/get/43/3488?f=jpg&sid=3488&ts=1638206562. Displayed in full without cropping.

Player-page update: game logs now show verified opponent logos from the MaxPreps Delaware school directory. Exact name mappings, asset URLs and source pages are retained in dist/opponents.json. Schools without a verified image use initials. Marks are current identity references, not historical-season certifications.

Logo coverage update: all 34 opponents now have school marks. Added official sports-site references and full-mark display windows for Padua, Ursuline, Delmarva Christian and Campus Community; replaced low-resolution thumbnails with original assets. Opponent logos appear in the shared game cards on Games, Home and season pages, as well as player logs. Exact per-school sources and display bounds are in dist/opponents.json.

## Hosting and automatic updates

The site is published from this repository to GitHub Pages at https://auksvb.com.

- `.github/workflows/update-from-source.yml` runs every 3 hours (hourly in the evening after matches). It runs `scripts/sync-source.mjs`, which reads the official schedule (https://www.aukssports.com/page9857) and each result page by column headings, reconciles `currentSchedule`, and imports results through the safe merge in `scripts/update-results.mjs`. Only verified changes are committed; the site is then republished.
- Anything it will not guess (unknown names, changed columns, score mismatches, a new school year) is listed in a **Results need review** issue. A failed run opens an **Updater failing** issue and leaves the last good data live; it closes itself after the next successful run.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` publishes `dist/` after the checks pass, on every push that changes the site or data.
- Tests: `node scripts/test-sync-source.mjs` (saved official pages in `scripts/fixtures/`) and `node scripts/test-update-results.mjs`.
- Run an update by hand: Actions → Update from official source → Run workflow, or locally `node scripts/sync-source.mjs` (dry run) then `--apply`.
- Each new school year needs the reviewed roster added to `dist/data.json` before results import; the updater opens a review issue when the official schedule switches years.

clayvanderburg/geometry-survivor.desc: Vectra // Survivor — Geometric twin-stick roguelite with Crab Drill-Claw asteroid excavation, reactive warp grid, synthwave audio & Live Tuning Studio
clayvanderburg/geometry-survivor.readme:
# VEXOLITH // SURVIVOR

A browser-based geometric twin-stick roguelite & asteroid-excavation survival game inspired by *Geometry Wars*, *Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor*, and *Vampire Survivors*.

## Quick Start (Local Dev Server)

```powershell
npm start
```
- **Play Game**: `http://127.0.0.1:8096`
- **Standalone Live Tuning & Dev Sandbox Studio**: `http://127.0.0.1:8096/tuner.html` (or press **`[T]`** in-game to toggle the slide-over Tuner Drawer).

---

## Core Mechanics & Features

1. **Geometric Crab Ship with Twin Rotary Drill-Claws (`drawCrabShip` in `js/main.js`)**
   - Wide hexagonal armored crab carapace with 6 scuttling side legs.
   - **Twin Front Rotary Drill-Claws**: Orient automatically toward your movement direction (or snap onto the asteroid rock face you are boring into), clamping inward, spinning helical drill threads, vibrating, and spraying grinding sparks.
   - **360° Independent Plasma Turret**: Rotates toward your aim cursor (`p.angle`) independently of your crab hull.
   - **Strict Mining Separation**: Weapons, missiles, orbitals, singularities, and Supernova bombs **never** mine asteroids—bullets spark off rocks as solid cover. **Only your Crab Ship's front Drill-Claws** can carve tunnels through asteroid clusters.

2. **10x Scrolling Sector (`4200 x 4200`) & Destructible Asteroid Clusters (`js/asteroids.js`, `js/grid.js`)**
   - 38 dense asteroid formations physically block and funnel enemy swarms until you carve escape tunnels through them.
   - Shattering rocks unearths hidden veins: **Gold Geom Veins** (5x Golden XP/Multiplier Geoms + rare buried Relic Chest roll), **Shield Crystal Veins** (`+25 Shield HP`), and **Deep Core Veins** (`+1 ❖ Void Core`).
   - Bottom-right **Tactical Sector Radar Minimap** displays asteroid clusters, rich ore veins, enemies, bosses, and Relic Supply Caches.
   - Camera-culled **Hooke's-Law Spring-Mass Warping Neon Grid** (`js/grid.js`) ripples from explosions and funnels into gravity wells at 60+ FPS.

3. **Emergent Swarm Archetypes (`js/enemies.js`)**
   - **Boid Swarmers** (Magenta Diamonds): Flock using separation, alignment, cohesion, and swirl.
   - **Weavers** (Emerald Darts): Sense incoming player fire and dodge perpendicular to bullet trajectories.
   - **Pinwheels** (Violet Rotating Squares) & **Splitters** (Golden Hexagons that fracture into 3 fast mini-triangles).
   - **Vortexes** (Crimson Singularities, internal type `blackhole`): Funnel the grid, swirl enemies, pickups and sparks inward, bend passing shots, and tug your ship. The tug is capped below your thrust (`js/gravity.js`), so holding away always escapes. Strengths live in the tuner's *Gravity Wells & Singularities* group.
   - **Prismatic Dreadnought Bosses**: Spawn every 3 waves and drop a guaranteed Super Relic Supply Cache. Each one is a staged event: a `bossWarningTime` (default 3 s) warning with a hazard strip countdown, klaxon, music drop, red screen frame, radar ring and off-screen arrow to the reserved spawn point; then an arrival shockwave and title card (e.g. `PRISMATIC DREADNOUGHT — WAVE 3 WARDEN`), a gold-crowned silhouette, and top-of-HUD health bars (up to 3 stacked, `+N MORE` beyond). A kill triggers a fixed-tick hit-stop + half-speed slow-mo, gold flash and a reward banner. Sandbox `+Boss` runs the same event.

4. **Luck Stat, `+2`…`+5` Multi-Level Rolls & Relic Supply Cache Jackpots (`js/upgrades.js`, `js/main.js`)**
   - **Multi-Level Upgrades**: Level-up cards have a Luck-scaled chance to jump multiple levels at once (`10%` for `+2`, `3.5%` for `+3`, `1%` for `+4`, `0.25%` for `+5`, each × luck, never past the level cap). The jump size *is* the card's rarity.
   - **Relic Supply Caches**: Guaranteed drop from Bosses and very rare Luck-scaled drop from lesser enemies / Gold Veins. Opening a cache triggers the **Relic Supply Cache Jackpot Modal** (`1x` standard, or rare `2x`, `3x Triple Jackpot`, or `5x Penta-Core Mega Jackpot` free upgrades). Caches install through the same `applyUpgradeLevels` path as level-up picks, so they share one `player.upgradeLevels` state.
   - **Readable Cards (`js/upgrade-cards.js`)**: Every level-up and cache card shows an enlarged headline (e.g. `+2 PROJECTILES`), a short summary and exact **before → after** stats, computed by installing the upgrade (including its rolled level jump) on a copy of the player. Weapon formulas live in `js/weapon-scaling.js` so cards and gameplay can't drift. Rarity is the rolled level jump and sets the card color: `+1` common gray, `+2` uncommon green, `+3` rare blue, `+4` epic purple, `+5` legendary gold; evolutions are magenta. Cards, caches and HUD tags all use the same `LV n` wording.

5. **Interactive 132-BPM Synthwave Music & Procedural WebAudio (`js/audio.js`)**
   - Procedural WebAudio sequencer (dynamics compressor, punchy kick, dual-oscillator sawtooth + sub-square bassline, snare, hi-hats, detuned arpeggiator, and chord pads) that scales filter cutoff and layering with combat intensity.
   - **Hull-Hugging Shield Barrier** (`drawPlayerShield` in `js/ship-renderer.js`) wraps the crab's silhouette and is also the contact hitbox (`shieldTouches`). Its charged arc shows current shield %, thickness grows with max shield, color shifts blue → amber → critical red, and hits flash with a ripple. Hue, padding and thickness are tunable.

6. **Persistent Highscore Board & Void Armory Meta-Progression (`js/progression.js`)**
   - Custom **Pilot Callsign / Name Entry** on Title and Game Over screens.
   - Spend **Void Cores (❖)** harvested during runs on 6 permanent Armory upgrades persisted in `localStorage` (`vectra_survivor_save_v2`).

7. **Live Tuning & Dev Sandbox Studio (`tuner.html` + `js/config.js` + `[T]` Drawer)**
   - Exposes 47 live parameters across 6 categories (*Crab Ship & Drill-Claws*, *Weapons & Shield*, *Luck & Chests*, *Asteroids & Economy*, *Audio & Visual FX*, *Hit Feedback & Damage Numbers*) with real-time cross-tab sync via `BroadcastChannel` + `localStorage`.

GencSaracaydin/operation-long-shadow.readme:
# Operation Long Shadow

A Cold War first-person shooter for the browser, in the style of Call of Duty: Black Ops. It is built in Unity 6 (URP) and targets WebGL.

**October 1984, the fictional Republic of Sardahn.** You are Sergeant Nathan Calder, SUNDIAL-3, part of a four-man black-ops team sent into the market town of Zaroud at golden hour to recover a warlord's ledgers, film reels and a numbers-station codebook. The sun sets in the middle of the raid. Then the station starts reading numbers on your own squad's radio.

The mission is told as a flashback from an interrogation chair: about 14 minutes of play, with a helicopter insertion cold open, squadmates, radio chatter, mission title cards and a debrief.

> **Status: in development.** Assets and game systems are in place. Level assembly, cinematics and the first web build are in progress. There is no playable build yet.

## Controls

| Action | Input |
| --- | --- |
| Move / look | WASD / mouse |
| Fire / aim down sights | Left / right mouse button |
| Reload | R |
| Sprint | Left Shift (hold) |
| Jump / mantle | Space |
| Crouch / slide (while sprinting) | C |
| Frag grenade (hold to cook) | G |
| Knife | V |
| Interact | E |
| Switch weapon | 1 / 2, mouse wheel |
| Objectives | Tab |
| Pause | Esc |
| Skip cinematic | Hold Space for 1 s |

## Open the project

1. Install **Unity 6000.6.6f1** with the **Web Build Support** module.
2. Open this folder in Unity Hub. The first import takes a while.
3. Design docs are in [`Docs/`](Docs/): [`GDD.md`](Docs/GDD.md) for the mission, [`TECH_PLAN.md`](Docs/TECH_PLAN.md) for the architecture, and [`CINEMATIC_DIRECTION.md`](Docs/CINEMATIC_DIRECTION.md) for the camera and realism direction.
4. Builder menus live under **LongShadow/** in the editor menu bar. The web release build is **LongShadow/Build/Web Release**.

## How it was made

The game was built by Claude (Anthropic) agents driving the Unity Editor through Unity MCP.
- **Generated with [fal.ai](https://fal.ai):** 3D models (Tripo, Hunyuan 3D), images, sound effects, music and voice lines.
- **CC0 libraries:** textures, skies and props from Poly Haven and ambientCG.
- **Open-licence downloads:** characters and animation; see [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

The setting, factions, languages and scripts are fictional.

shreyasijonnala-creator/pokerGame.readme:
# Buy-In Board

A live $20 buy-in tracker for home poker games. Anyone can create a table and get a 5-character code. Players join with the code and their name. Only the host who created the table can add buy-ins, rename the table or end the game. Everyone at the table sees the totals update live.

There are no accounts. Each browser gets a random secret key that's saved in that browser, and the server uses it to tell who the host is. If you clear your site data, or open the page in a different browser, you won't be recognized as the host anymore.

## Run it on your computer

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. To test from a phone on the same Wi-Fi, use your computer's local IP address instead, for example `http://192.168.1.20:3000`.

## Put it on the web

The server is a single Node process (Node 18 or newer). Where it keeps tables:

- **With `DATABASE_URL` set**, tables are stored in that Postgres database. Use this on any host that wipes its disk on restart or redeploy, which includes Render's free plan.
- **Without it**, tables go in `data/tables.json` (or in `DATA_DIR` if you set it). That's fine on your own computer, but on a free host every table is lost whenever the server restarts.

### Render (free plan) with a free Neon database

1. Create a free database at [neon.tech](https://neon.tech). Copy its **connection string**, which looks like `postgresql://user:password@ep-something.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require`.
2. In Render, create a new **Web Service** from this GitHub repository.
3. Set the build command to `npm install` and the start command to `npm start`.
4. Under **Environment**, add `DATABASE_URL` and paste the connection string as its value.
5. Deploy. The log should say `tables saved to Postgres`.

The app creates its own database table the first time it runs. Render sets `PORT` for you.

Free Render servers go to sleep after about 15 minutes without visitors. The first visit afterwards takes up to a minute to wake the server, but tables aren't lost because they're in the database.

Other hosts that run a Node server and support WebSockets (Railway, Fly.io, a VPS) work the same way. Any Postgres database works, including Render's or Supabase's.

Run only one copy of the server, because each running copy keeps its own list of tables. A table is deleted 30 days after its last change.

## Files

- `server.js`: serves the page, stores the tables and enforces the host-only rules
- `public/index.html`: the page layout and styles
- `public/app.js`: the browser code that talks to the server

# 동물기록 복구작전 · 하루와 모리의 자연 탐험 (0.4.0)

초등 과학 ‘동물의 생활’ 학습 게임. 사람 탐험가 하루가 이미지 지도에 그려진 길을 따라 이동하고, 너구리 모리가 따라다니며 관찰과 기록을 돕는다. 다섯 장소마다 서로 다른 4개 활동을 진행한다.

## 실행

Node.js 20 이상, 외부 패키지 설치나 API 키 불필요.

```sh
npm start
npm run check
npm test
npm run build
npm run preview
```

개발 주소는 `http://127.0.0.1:4173/`. `npm run preview`는 `dist/` 배포본을 같은 기본 포트로 제공한다. 개발 서버가 열려 있으면 별도 포트를 지정한다. PowerShell 예: `$env:PORT='4174'; npm run preview`.

## 20개 탐구 활동

| 장 | 첫 탐구 | 다음 탐구 |
|---|---|---|
| 관찰의 숲 | 확대 렌즈로 개구리·게 6곳 관찰, 공통점·차이 비교 | 오리·토끼 6곳 관찰, 다른 특징 비교 |
| 분류의 정원 | 6종을 날개로 분류 → 이동 예상 → 기준 바꿔 비교 | 6종을 다리 네 개로 분류 → 새 기준과 비교 |
| 생태의 물가 | 3환경 발견, 움직임 재생·정지·장면 기록, 개구리 생활 연결 | 새 동물의 움직임 기록, 토끼 생활 연결 |
| 동물 찾기 안내소 | 부분 그림의 단서 수집→후보 줄이기→오리의 환경·생활 | 새 단서 수집→후보 줄이기→토끼의 환경·생활 |
| 발명의 공방 | 물갈퀴 관찰→오리발 설계→폭 변경·예상·두 시험 비교·설명 | 등딱지 또는 털을 활용한 발명→덮개 범위 또는 겹 변경·시험·설명 |

첫 발명은 물갈퀴를 이용한 오리발, 두 번째는 안전모 또는 방한 외투를 만든다. 같은 조건에서 한 부분만 바꾸고, 서로 다른 두 설정을 시험하여 비교한다. 예상이 틀렸다고 실패하지 않으며 관찰·예상·시험·비교·알게 된 점을 남겨야 한다. 시험은 정성적인 설명 모형이며 실제 물리 성능·안전성 측정이 아니다. 펜 스케치와 글의 내용은 자동 채점하지 않는다. 친구와 설명·질문·의견 교환을 함께 운영한다.

## 역할과 보상

- 하루: 학생을 대신하는 탐험가. 지도 길의 실제 경유점을 따라 이동한다.
- 모리: 하루를 따라가는 기록 보조원. 실제 수집 기록을 수첩과 도구에 보여 준다.
- 검증한 활동당 탐험 별 1개, 최대 20개. 반복 클릭이나 속도로 추가 점수를 얻지 않는다.
- 장소를 복구하면 관찰 렌즈·분류 나침반·서식지 수첩·특징 스캐너·발명가 배지를 받는다.
- 도구를 가방이나 활동 화면에서 꺼내 다음 탐구에 사용한다. 모은 동물 카드 7종과 두 발명이 최종 결과에 반영된다.

## 교육과정과 화면 검증

[4과02-01] 관찰·특징 분류, [4과02-02] 환경과 생김새·생활 관계, [4과02-03] 특징을 활용한 생활용품 설계·협력적 소통과 연결했다. 협력적 소통은 실제 교실 대화와 교사 관찰을 함께 확인한다. 상세 근거와 화면별 검증 범위는 [태블릿 탐구 QA](docs/reviews/TABLET-INQUIRY-QA-20261016.md)를 참고한다.

## 저장과 이전 기록

현재 브라우저 LocalStorage에 자동 저장한다. 주소·포트·브라우저가 다르면 기록도 분리된다. 학생 이름·학번을 수집하거나 기록을 서버로 보내지 않는다.

0.3 저장 형식과 기존 별·완료 기록은 유지하며 새 관찰·시험 필드만 추가한다. 기존 완료 기록을 취소하거나 새 활동을 했다고 가정하지 않는다.

0.2 버전 기록은 보관하고 확인 가능한 첫 관찰·분류·환경 탐구만 이관한다. 새로 늘어난 활동과 바뀐 4장은 직접 해야 한다. 이전에 열렸던 장소의 입장 권한을 유지한다. 전체를 처음부터 보려면 탐험 가방 → 탐험 기록 초기화에서 확인 후 시작한다.

통과한 동물 안내 카드와 발명은 별도 제출 기록으로 보관한다. 다시 탐험하며 초안을 바꿔도 미검증 초안으로 최종 결과가 덮어써지지 않는다. 시험과 설명을 다시 마치면 성공 기록이 갱신된다.

## 주요 파일

- `src/inquiry.js`: 비교 시험·움직임 장면·단서 기록의 정규화와 판정
- `src/inquiry-views.js`, `src/inquiry.css`: 설명 모형·비교 시험 화면과 태블릿 레이아웃
- `src/expedition.js`: 20활동 콘텐츠·판정·보상·저장 이관
- `src/adventure-app.js`: 실제 입력·화면 이동·저장·스케치·내보내기
- `src/mission-views.js`, `src/shell-views.js`: 활동·지도·보상·가방 화면
- `src/trail-map.js`: 이미지 지도에 맞춘 경유점과 하루·모리 이동
- `src/presentation.js`, `src/assets.js`: 2D 이미지 경계. 이후 3D 교체 위치
- `src/adventure.css`: 실제 로드하는 공통 디자인·반응형 스타일
- `assets/adventure/`: 새 이미지 7종의 PNG 원본·WebP
- `docs/ADVENTURE-PLAN-20261015.md`: 이번 활동·역할·보상 설계
- `docs/ADVENTURE-ASSET-PROMPTS.json`: 실제 생성 프롬프트
- `docs/reviews/ADVENTURE-QA-20261015.md`: 이번 검증 결과

`src/model.js`는 이전 저장 정규화와 발명 판정에도 사용한다. 기존 `app.js`, `hub.js`, `style.css`, `polish.css`는 이전 버전 보관용이며 현재 화면과 배포에서 로드하지 않는다. `tests/app.test.mjs`는 이전 버전 회귀, `tests/adventure-app.test.mjs`와 `tests/expedition.test.mjs`는 현재 버전 검증이다.

## 빌드와 전달

`npm run build`는 실행에 필요한 파일만 `dist/`에 복사하고 CSS 이미지 경로를 확인한다. 이전 빌드 매니페스트에 기록된 미사용 실행 파일만 정리하며 원본·사용자 파일을 삭제하지 않는다. PNG 원본·테스트·문서는 배포 ZIP에서 제외한다. 정적 호스팅에 `dist/`의 내용만 올린다.

외부 배포는 실행하지 않았다. 실제 교실 기기·학생 사용·교사 내용 검수는 별도 확인 사항이다. 외부 패키지나 웹폰트·학생 계정·실시간 3D·영상은 추가하지 않았다. 이미지 생성 고지와 제공 자료 출처는 설정과 `assets/CREDITS.md`에서 확인할 수 있다.

FlamingFury00/Cartoon-Hitster.readme:
# Sigle in Fila 🎵📼 **A Hitster-style party game made of Italian cartoon theme songs** ("sigle dei cartoni animati"), from *Ufo Robot* (1978) to the latest Cristina D'Avena and Giorgio Vanni themes. One phone, 2–6 players, no accounts: a song plays with its title hidden, you guess when it first aired in Italy and slot the card into your own timeline. First to 10 cards wins.

## Play | | | |---|---| | 📱 **Android** | Download [`SigleInFila.apk`](https://github.com/FlamingFury00/Cartoon-Hitster/releases/latest/download/SigleInFila.apk) on the phone and open it (allow installs from the browser the first time). New versions install over the old one and keep saved games and history. | | 🌐 **Browser** | — works on any phone; "Add to Home screen" installs it as an app (PWA, works offline except for the music). | Both are published automatically by GitHub Actions on every push to `main` (the web version needs GitHub Pages enabled once: *Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions*). ## How a turn works 1. **Pesca la sigla** — a random song you have not heard recently starts playing. Title, cartoon and singer stay hidden (a cassette with a live spectrum is all you see). 2. **Place it** — tap (or drag) the mystery card into a gap of your timeline: before, after or between the cards you already own. 3. **Challenge** (tokens on) — other players can spend a token to bet on a different gap. 4. **Gira la carta!** — drum roll, flip: year, cartoon, song and singer. Right place → you keep the card. Wrong → it is discarded, or stolen by the first challenger who was right. 5. **Bonus** — name both the cartoon and the singer to earn a token (tokens: skip a song for 1, challenge for 1, buy a card for 3). Modes: **Classica**, **Esperto** (you keep the card only if you also name the cartoon) and **Squadra** (co-op: one shared timeline, tokens are lives). Options: target 5–15 cards, equal turns, deck filters by decade, fame and genre (Cristina D'Avena, Giorgio Vanni, super robots, magical girls, sport, anime, western cartoons). The full rules are in the app (*Come si gioca*). ## The deck **251 hand-verified theme songs**, each pointing to the original recording (never covers, karaoke, duets or re-recordings). The year on a card is the **first Italian release or broadcast of that specific sigla**: shows with several themes (sequels, reruns with a new theme) get one card per theme, with a note on the card. How every year and recording was checked, plus the full list with sources: [`docs/DECK.md`](docs/DECK.md). The master sheet is [`deck/songs.csv`](deck/songs.csv) (opens in any spreadsheet). ## How the music works without any account - Songs play from the public **30-second previews** that Deezer and Spotify serve to everyone: the app asks the Deezer API (JSONP) for a fresh signed preview URL and falls back to the Spotify preview stored in the deck. Nothing is bundled in the app. - Previews are downloaded and decoded with the Web Audio API, so playback starts instantly, loops seamlessly and the next cards are preloaded during the reveal. - Every preview was measured offline (EBU R128 loudness, ffmpeg) and is played with its own gain correction, so a 1978 mono recording is as loud as a 2010 master. - "🎧 Ascolta tutta la sigla" opens the full song in the Spotify app; a settings switch can play every card in Spotify instead (the title is visible there, so it is a fallback only). ## Development Requirements: Node 22+, and for the APK a JDK 17+ and the Android SDK (platform 36). ```bash npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 npm run check # svelte-check (strict TypeScript) npm test # engine unit tests (Vitest) npm run test:e2e # Playwright end-to-end tests (music services are mocked) npm run build # production web build in dist/ npm run apk # Android APK in android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/ ``` Stack: Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite, a pure and fully tested rules engine (`src/lib/game/engine.ts`), Web Audio playback (`src/lib/audio/`), PWA via vite-plugin-pwa. The Android app (`android/`) is a small Kotlin WebView shell that serves the built web app from its assets through `WebViewAssetLoader`, adds haptics and keeps the screen on. ### Deck pipeline ```bash npm run deck:match # find Deezer / Spotify candidates for deck/songs.csv (review the report!) npm run deck:sources # Spotify preview URLs + store metadata -> deck/sources.json npm run deck:loudness # ffmpeg loudness and silence analysis -> deck/sources.json npm run deck:build # deck/songs.csv + deck/sources.json -> src/data/deck.json (verified rows only) npm run deck:validate # sanity checks (also run by CI) node tools/deck/report.mjs # regenerate docs/DECK.md ``` Node needs `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` behind an HTTP proxy. Spotify lookups drive the public web player with Playwright (no developer account needed). ### Signing APKs are signed with the side-load key committed in `android/sideload.jks`, so every build can update the previous one. It is not a secret: anyone could sign an APK with it. To use a private key instead, add the repository secrets `SIF_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `SIF_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `SIF_KEY_ALIAS` and `SIF_KEY_PASSWORD` (the release workflow picks them up; switching keys requires uninstalling the old app once). ## Notes A private, non-commercial game for family and friends, inspired by the *Hitster* card game. All songs belong to their rights holders; the app only plays the public previews provided by Deezer and Spotify.

retrospective-dev/KuOnPc.readme:
# Kuon decompilation

A matching decompilation of **Kuon** (FromSoftware, 2004, PlayStation 2), targeting the
PAL release **SLES-53411 v1.01**. The long-term goal is a native PC port.

This repo contains **no game code or data**. You need your own disc.

## Status

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | Rebuilds `SLES_534.11` byte-for-byte from source + disassembly |
| Compiler | Metrowerks CodeWarrior PS2 3.0.x, `-O4`, identified and verified |
| Game functions | 433 / 2,909 matched in C (14.9% of functions, 0.7% of code bytes: the trivial ones so far) |

Run `make progress` for current numbers.

### What's in the executable

| Region | Address | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| crt0 + SDK + runtime | `0x100000`-`0x12E4B0` | Sony PS2 SDK 2.8.0 (libgraph, libdma, libpad, libcdvd, libmc, libsdr, libipu, libvu0), Metrowerks MSL C runtime |
| **Game code** | `0x12E4B0`-`0x221410` | ~2,900 FromSoftware functions, ~970 KB |
| VU1 microcode | `0x221410`-`0x229920` | 25 VIF MPG uploads: the custom VU1 renderer |
| Kernel patch | `0x229920`-`0x22AE50` | SDK kernel-mode code |
| Data | `0x22AE50`-`0x25E300` | data / rodata / sdata |
| BSS | `0x25E300`-`0xA6AA00` | ~8 MB |

IOP modules loaded from disc include FromSoftware's own sound drivers (`fssd.irx`,
`fssdivag.irx`, `fssdsyth.irx`, `fsmfstrm.irx`). Movies are PSS. Textures are TM2 and `.tex`.

## Setup (Linux or WSL)

1. Copy `SLES_534.11` from your PAL disc into `original/`
   (sha1 `bd495fc0bb5b905b2459ac2441622d19c33bad42`).
2. `bash tools/setup.sh`

That installs MIPS binutils and splat, downloads `wibo` and the CodeWarrior compiler,
splits the executable, builds it, and checks it matches.

### GitHub Actions

`.github/workflows/build.yml` runs the same steps on every push and pull request
(and on demand from the Actions tab). The job fails if the rebuilt image doesn't match
retail. The linker map and `docs/functions.csv` are uploaded as the `kuon-map` artifact
(no executables: they're Sony/FromSoftware code), and the progress numbers show up in the
run summary.

CI needs the retail executable. It uses `original/SLES_534.11` if present, otherwise it
downloads it from the URL in the `KUON_ELF_URL` repository secret (a private link you control).

### Testing the output

`make` writes `build/SLES_534.11`: the rebuilt code inside the retail executable's ELF
headers. While the build matches, it is identical to the file on the disc.

- **PCSX2:** System → Start File, pick `build/SLES_534.11`. The game reads its data from the disc, so keep your Kuon ISO
  loaded: set it under Settings → Game List or System → Start Disc first.
- **Replace it in the ISO:** swap `SLES_534.11` in a copy of your ISO with an ISO editor
  (e.g. ImgBurn / UltraISO) and boot the ISO as usual.

## Working on it

```
source .venv/bin/activate                # once per shell
python3 tools/todo.py --bucket tiny      # easiest unmatched functions
python3 tools/diff.py func_0014A670      # compile + byte-diff one function
make                                     # full rebuild, must print OK
make progress
```

See `SPEC.md` for the project plan and `CLAUDE.md` for the matching rules and agent workflow.

## Layout

```
kuon.yaml            splat config (segments, compiler)
Makefile
include/common.h     shared types
src/game/            matched functions, one per file (linked into the build)
src/wip/             near-misses, not linked
tools/diff.py        per-function compile/link/byte-compare
tools/todo.py        work queue
tools/inventory.py   docs/functions.csv (size, float/VU0 use, string hints)
tools/split_game.py  per-function asm split
tools/gen_ld.py      linker script choosing C over asm per function
```

## Road to a PC port

1. Decompile game logic (integer code first, then FPU, then VU0 macro code).
2. Name things: recover structs for the big globals, module boundaries (`SfxMng.c` etc.).
3. Move data ownership from asm into C (strings, tables, floats).
4. Replace the platform layer: GS/VIF/VU1 rendering → modern renderer,
   libpad → SDL input, CD/IOP file I/O → filesystem, FromSoftware sound IRX → PC audio.
5. Build for x86-64 with a modern compiler once the code no longer depends on PS2 hardware.

martinvd/sc2-build-optimizer.readme:
# sc2-build-optimizer

Finds the fastest StarCraft II build order to reach a goal, for Zerg, Terran and Protoss.
The same binary runs as a desktop app or as a command-line tool.

## Usage

### Desktop app

```
cargo run --release
```

Run with no arguments to open the desktop app, built with [GPUI Kit](https://gpui-kit.com).

### Command line

```
cargo run --release -- 10 roaches
```

Pass a goal to run in the terminal instead. This prints the build as a table of start
times, supply and actions, plus the time the goal is done. Add `--timeline` for a chart of
when each action is in production. Run with `--help` for all options.

### Goals

Goals accept counts and common names, for example `"5 roaches"`, `"roach=8, ravager=2"`,
`"20 lings and ling speed"`, `"6 marines and stim"` or `"4 stalkers and blink"`. The units
in the goal set the race.

## How it works

A simulation steps through the game in 0.25s ticks. It models mining, supply, larva,
injects, MULEs, chrono boost and warp-ins. A search uses it to pick what to start next,
including workers, supply, gas and expansions.

Each build starts with 12 workers and 1 town hall. By default the search stays within
these limits, which you can change in the app's Model settings or with the CLI options:

- 1 expansion, with a 12 second worker walk to it
- 2 gas buildings
- 3 production structures of each type
- 2 queens and no macro hatcheries
- 1 million search states, about 1 GB of memory

Goals of 20 or more units can hit the state limit. You then get the best build found, and
the output marks it as not proven fastest.

The simulation does not model archons, motherships, macro command centers, scans, supply
drops, add-on swapping or proxy structures.

matt-moses/brow-guess.readme: # Brow Guess A party word game for phones: hold the phone to your forehead, let your friends describe the word, tilt down when you get it, tilt up to pass. **Play:** Scan the code with a phone camera to open the game. It's handy for passing around at a party. It is a static, installable web app (PWA) that works offline after the first visit. No accounts, no ads, no tracking. ## How to play 1. Open the link on your phone and pick a deck. 2. Allow motion access if your phone asks (iOS does). 3. Turn the phone sideways (landscape) and hold it on your forehead, screen facing your friends. Hold still until the countdown starts. 4. Your friends describe the word on screen without saying it. - **Tilt down** (screen toward the floor) when you guess it: correct. - **Tilt up** (screen toward the ceiling) to pass. - Bring the phone back to your forehead to get the next word. 5. When the 60-second timer runs out, hand the phone around to see the score and every word, then play again or choose another deck. Tip: on iPhone, use **Share → Add to Home Screen** for a fullscreen, offline-ready app. ## Local development Requires Node 22 (pinned in `.nvmrc`; `engines` allows >= 20). ```bash nvm use # or install Node 22 another way npm ci npm run dev # http://localhost:5173/ ``` To try it on a phone over your LAN, expose the dev server and open the printed network URL on the phone: ```bash npm run dev -- --host ``` ### Motion sensors need HTTPS on iOS iOS Safari only delivers `deviceorientation` events (and only shows the motion permission prompt) on a secure origin. A plain `http://192.168.x.x:5173` URL works on Android Chrome for some setups but not on iOS. Options: - **Self-signed HTTPS in Vite:** `npm i -D @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`, add `basicSsl()` to the `plugins` in `vite.config.ts` (locally, don't commit), then `npm run dev -- --host` and accept the certificate warning on the phone. - **A tunnel:** run `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173` or `ngrok http 5173` and open the HTTPS URL it prints. - **Production:** GitHub Pages is always HTTPS, so the deployed site works everywhere. ### Desktop simulator (`?sim`) Desktops have no orientation sensor. In dev mode only, open to load a simulator that pretends the phone is in landscape and streams orientation events: neutral by default, hold **Arrow Down** to tilt down (correct), hold **Arrow Up** to tilt up (pass). It is stripped from production builds. ## Scripts | Script | What it does | | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `npm run dev` | Vite dev server with hot reload (`-- --host` for LAN). | | `npm run build` | Production build to `dist/` (honours `BASE_PATH`). | | `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally. | | `npm run lint` | ESLint (type-aware typescript-eslint). | | `npm run format` | Prettier, rewrite files. | | `npm run format:check` | Prettier, check only. | | `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` over app, tests, e2e and configs. | | `npm test` | Vitest unit and jsdom flow tests, once. | | `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. | | `npm run coverage` | Vitest with V8 coverage (`coverage/`). | | `npm run test:e2e` | Playwright smoke and offline specs against `vite preview` (CI; see below). | | `npm run acceptance` | Runs the automatable PRD acceptance checks and prints a PASS/FAIL/PENDING table. | | `npm run verify` | The local gate: lint, format check, typecheck, purity check, brand check, tests, build, dist check. | | `npm run check:pure` | Ensures game logic in `src/game/` stays DOM-free. | | `npm run check:brand` | Fails if third-party trademarked names appear in the repo. | | `npm run check:dist` | Validates the build: base path, manifest fields, icons, service worker precache. | | `npm run gen:icons` | Rasterises the source artwork in `assets/` into `public/icons/`. | ## Testing - **Unit and flow tests (Vitest):** `npm test`. Game logic (tilt detection, normalization, round, shuffle) is pure and clock-injected; screens and the full game flow run in jsdom against fake device adapters. This is the main local loop. - **End-to-end (Playwright):** runs in CI only by default (browsers are heavy on small dev machines). `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` plays a full round with synthetic orientation events and a fake clock; `e2e/offline.spec.ts` checks that the app loads and starts a deck offline after one visit. PeterJohn89/rugby-league-experience.readme:
# The Rugby League Experience

A top-down, NRL-style rugby league game that runs in the browser, built with Three.js.
Designed and built by [Goodwin Studios](https://goodwinstudios.com.au).

## Project layout

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Landing page (screenshots, features, controls, Play button) |
| `play/index.html` | The game |
| `src/` | Game source. No external assets: models, stadium, crowd and audio are generated in code |
| `public/` | Copied as-is into the build: favicon, screenshots (`img/`), `landing.js`, security headers (`_headers`, `.htaccess`) |
| `tests/` | Automated tests (`npm test`) |
| `tuning/` | Gameplay tuning scripts that print match metrics (`npm run tune`) |

## Requirements

Node.js 22.12 or newer.

## Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:5181 for the landing page, or http://localhost:5181/play/ for the game.
In the dev server only, add `#dev` to the game URL (`/play/#dev`) to expose the `window.__rl`
test hooks. They are stripped from production builds.

## Build and deploy

```bash
npm run build
```

This creates `dist/`, a fully static site (no server code, no database, no API keys):

```
dist/
  index.html        landing page
  play/index.html   the game
  assets/           bundled JS and CSS (hashed file names)
  img/              screenshots
  landing.js, favicon.svg
  _headers          security headers for Netlify / Cloudflare Pages
  .htaccess         security headers for Apache / cPanel
```

Upload everything inside `dist/` (including the hidden `.htaccess`) to any static host.
All paths are relative, so it works at a domain root or in a sub-folder.

- **cPanel / FTP:** upload the contents of `dist/` into `public_html/` (or a sub-folder).
  Once SSL is set up, uncomment the HTTPS redirect at the bottom of `.htaccess`.
- **Netlify / Cloudflare Pages:** build command `npm run build`, publish directory `dist`.
  `_headers` is picked up automatically.
- **Vercel / GitHub Pages:** build command `npm run build`, output `dist`. These hosts ignore
  `_headers`, so add the same headers in the host's own config if you want them.

Check the production build locally before uploading (it serves with the same
Content-Security-Policy as the live site):

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

Then open http://localhost:5182.

Optional: for nicer link previews on social media, change `og:image` in `index.html` to the
full URL of `img/hero.jpg` once you know the final domain.

## Security

- The site is static: there is no backend, no login, no forms and no data sent anywhere.
- Saved preferences (settings, teams, key bindings) are stored in the player's own browser
  (`localStorage`) and validated on load: unknown keys and unexpected values are ignored.
- A strict Content-Security-Policy only allows scripts from the site itself and fonts from
  Google Fonts. Inline scripts are blocked.
- Test hooks and shader debugging are development-only and are not in the production bundle.
- `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. Run it again before each release.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| W A S D | Run (Shift to sprint) |
| < > | Pass left / right |
| Space | Tackle, fend, dive to score |
| K | Kick (hold for power, the kick type is picked for you) |
| 1-5 | Set plays in attack, defensive styles in defence |
| E | Switch defender |
| F / Q | Pressure / line rush |
| V | Slow motion (charged by run metres) |
| C | Change camera |
| Tab | Coach's Box (tactics, bench, match stats) |
| Esc | Pause |

All keys can be remapped in Settings.

## Tests

```bash
npm test        # rules engine, headless match simulations, practice drills
npm run tune    # slower gameplay metrics (ruck tackles, line breaks, draw and pass, support)
```

## Rules notes

Sets of six, play-the-ball with markers and the 10 metre line, six-agains, penalties
(goal, touch, tap), 40/20 and 20/40 kicks, goal-line dropouts, sin bins, conversions
taken in line with the try, golden point. Simplified: no video referee, scrums are
automatic and interchanges are limited to 8.

Club names and colours describe the teams only. Player names, crests and sponsors are
original placeholders and are not affiliated with or endorsed by the NRL or any club.

## Copyright

© Goodwin Studios. All rights reserved.

LK1248/Pawnbroker.readme:
# Pawnbroker

A chess variant where every piece except the King starts as a pawn. Every turn earns a point, and points buy promotions.

## Rules

- Both back rows start as pawns, apart from the Kings on e1 and e8.
- A capture earns 2 points, whatever was taken (en passant included). A turn without a capture earns 1 point, including a turn ended by a checking upgrade. Points arrive at the end of the turn, so they can be spent from the player's next turn.
- Before moving, a player may spend points to upgrade **one** piece per turn. The price is the difference in material value (Pawn 1, Knight 3, Bishop 3, Rook 5, Queen 9) plus a flat 2-point fee. For example, Pawn to Knight costs 4 and Pawn to Queen costs 10, while reaching a Queen in three steps costs 14. The fee rewards saving up for a big upgrade.
- Knights and Bishops can't be converted into each other. Kings and Queens can't be upgraded.
- If an upgrade gives check, the turn ends there with no move.
- No upgrades are allowed while your own King is in check: a check must be answered with a move. Banked points can't buy a way out of mate.
- An upgrade that doesn't give check is only allowed if you still have a legal move afterwards.
- Only pawns on the second row may move two squares. Reaching the far row promotes for free, as in standard chess.
- Castling needs an unmoved King and an unmoved Rook in the corner. A corner pawn upgraded to a Rook without moving counts as an unmoved Rook.
- A player in check with no legal move is checkmated. A player not in check with no legal move and no legal upgrade is stalemated.
- The other draw rules are standard: threefold repetition (point totals count as part of the position), the 50-move rule (upgrades reset the count) and insufficient material, which only applies to King against King because points keep coming in.

## Running it

`pawnbroker.html` is a single self-contained page. Open it in a browser, or serve the folder locally:

```bash
python -m http.server 8731
```

Then visit http://localhost:8731/pawnbroker.html.

Two players share one screen. The game state is saved in the browser's local storage.

## Code layout

The rules engine lives in the `<script id="engine">` block and doesn't touch the DOM. The UI script below it only calls `newGame`, `legalMoves`, `doMove`, `doUpgrade` and `upgradeOptions`. A computer opponent or remote play can reuse the engine as it is.

## Planned

- Computer opponent
- Remote two-player games

single capture. The fee makes saving up for a Rook or Queen the better
deal.

> **⚠️ WARNING FOR MAKERS & AI CODING ASSISTANTS:**  
> Even though this board is often marketed as a "Cheap Yellow Display" (CYD), **it is NOT the same as the classic 2.8" CYD (`ESP32-2432S028R`)**.  
> If you upload standard 2.8" CYD code to this board, **the screen will stay completely black** because the backlight is wired to **GPIO 27** (instead of GPIO 21) and the touch controller shares the **HSPI bus** rather than using a separate SPI port.

---

## 📸 Hardware Identification

Look at the silkscreen marking on the back of your PCB:
- Right between the ribbon cable connector and the ESP32-WROOM module, you will see a silkscreen box that reads: **`ESP32-035`**.
- This board is sold on AliExpress/Alibaba under names such as **TZT ESP32 3.5 Inch LCD**, **Sunton ESP32-3248S035R**, or **MSP3520**.

| Front Display (480x320) | Back PCB (`ESP32-035` Silkscreen) |
| :---: | :---: |
| ![Display Front](docs/images/esp32_035_display_front.png) | ![PCB Back](docs/images/esp32_035_pcb_back.png) |

---

## ⚡ Key Differences: 2.8" CYD vs. 3.5" ESP32-035

| Specification / Pin | Classic 2.8" CYD (`ESP32-2432S028R`) | 3.5" Board (**`ESP32-035` / `3248S035R`**) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Screen Resolution** | 320 × 240 (QVGA) | **480 × 320 (HVGA)** |
| **Display Controller** | ILI9341 / ST7789 | **ST7796** *(or ILI9488 on some panel batches)* |
| **Backlight Pin (BL)** | `GPIO 21` | **`GPIO 27` (Drives transistor Q2)** |
| **Touch Controller** | XPT2046 on separate VSPI (`25, 32, 39, 33`) | **XPT2046 on shared HSPI (`14, 12, 13, CS: 33, IRQ: 36`)** |
| **RGB LED** | Pins 4 (R), 16 (G), 17 (B) — Active LOW | **Pins 4 (R), 16 (G), 17 (B) — Active LOW** *(Identical)* |
| **Light Sensor (LDR)**| Analog ADC1 (`GPIO 34`) | **Analog ADC1 (`GPIO 34`)** *(Identical)* |
| **USB Interface** | Micro-USB (or dual Type-C on Rev 2) | **USB Type-C** (connected to CH340C serial chip) |

---

## 🛠️ Complete Pinout Reference Table

| Peripheral | Signal / Function | ESP32 GPIO Pin | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **TFT Display** | Backlight Control | **`GPIO 27`** | Active HIGH. Drives backlight driver transistor Q2 |
| | MOSI / SDI | **`GPIO 13`** | Hardware HSPI Data Out |
| | MISO / SDO | **`GPIO 12`** | Hardware HSPI Data In |
| | SCLK / SCK | **`GPIO 14`** | Hardware HSPI Clock |
| | Chip Select (CS)| **`GPIO 15`** | Dedicated LCD Chip Select (Active LOW) |
| | DC / RS | **`GPIO 2`** | Data / Command register select |
| | Reset (RST) | **`-1` / `EN`** | Connected to board system reset |
| **Touch (XPT2046)**| Chip Select (CS)| **`GPIO 33`** | Dedicated Touch Chip Select |
| | Interrupt (IRQ) | **`GPIO 36`** | Touch detect interrupt (`SENSOR_VP`) |
| | MOSI / MISO / CLK| **`13, 12, 14`** | Shares hardware HSPI bus with the display |
| **Onboard RGB LED**| Red Channel | **`GPIO 4`** | Active LOW (0 = ON, 1 = OFF) |
| | Green Channel | **`GPIO 16`** | Active LOW (0 = ON, 1 = OFF) |
| | Blue Channel | **`GPIO 17`** | Active LOW (0 = ON, 1 = OFF) |
| **Sensors & Audio**| LDR Light Sensor | **`GPIO 34`** | Ambient light CdS photoresistor (ADC1) |
| | Speaker | **`GPIO 26`** | Audio amplifier (NS4168 / FM8002A) |
| **MicroSD Slot** | TF SPI Bus | **`CS: 5, MOSI: 23, SCLK: 18, MISO: 19`** | Dedicated separate VSPI bus |

---

The root of this repository is dedicated solely to the **Physical Board Hardware Reference & Diagnostics Suite**. Every project and visual animation is isolated in its own self-contained sub-repository under `examples/` with dedicated source code, headers, and docs:

hudasol/meta-adaptive-parallax.desc: ADAPTIVE: PARALLAX — Autonomous Principal Engineering Build Directive
hudasol/meta-adaptive-parallax.readme:
# ADAPTIVE: PARALLAX

**See the pieces. Discover the impossible.**

A seated, hands-first spatial puzzle for Meta Quest, built with the Immersive
Web SDK (IWSDK, WebXR). Shards of light float within a seated reach (every shard within 0.62 m of
the eye). A fixed
aperture casts their images onto a plate in front of you. Move, turn and push
the shards through depth until, from that one point, their light fits an
amber outline, and a scattered sculpture becomes a single impossible form.

The second idea is in the name: *how* you pick up shards can adapt. Three
interaction profiles (Direct, Forgiving, Reach) change how hand input is
interpreted, never what counts as correct. If pinches keep narrowly missing,
the game may offer a different profile. You can accept it, undo it, decline
it, or switch suggestions off.

> Built as an entry for the Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026
> (Gaming track, New Experience division). This is an independent project;
> it is not affiliated with, reviewed or endorsed by Meta.

## Status at a glance

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Three complete puzzles, progression, reveal | Implemented; solved end to end with emulated hands |
| Direct, Forgiving, Reach profiles; adaptation prompts | Implemented; unit and emulator tested |
| World-space UI, onboarding, pause/resume, settings, persistence | Implemented; emulator tested |
| Unit tests | 157 passing (`npm test`) |
| Emulator end-to-end run | 40/40 checks passing (`npm run test:e2e`) |
| Independent review | All 18 findings resolved; see [docs/REVIEW-LOG.md](docs/REVIEW-LOG.md) |
| Production build | Builds (`npm run build`); CI green on GitHub |
| **Meta Quest hardware** | **Not yet tested on a headset.** Frame rate on Quest is unmeasured. |
| Public link (GitHub Pages) | Live at <https://hudasol.github.io/meta-adaptive-parallax/> (deployed 2026-10-17; verified loading in desktop Edge, not yet opened on a Quest) |

Full detail, including what is unverified: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## How to play

- **Seated, hands only.** Controllers also work (trigger to pinch) but are never needed.
- **Pinch** a shard with thumb and index finger to pick it up; open your fingers to let go.
- **Move your hand** to move the shard. **Turn your wrist** to turn it.
- Watch the **plate**, not your hands: cyan is the light your shards cast,
  amber is the outline asked for. Where they meet exactly, they fuse to white.
- Nearer shards cast bigger images. Release close to the right place and the
  shard glides into it.
- The first puzzle teaches one idea at a time. Later puzzles add overlap,
  occlusion and shards that must tilt through depth.
- **Menu** (left of the shards by default): pause, undo, hints, interaction
  and comfort settings, recenter, leave VR.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22.12+ (see `.nvmrc`); npm.
- For headset testing: a Meta Quest on the same network, or the built-in
  IWER emulator that the dev server injects into desktop Chromium browsers.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run dev:http
```

Opens on `http://localhost:8081` with the IWER WebXR emulator injected, so
you can enter VR and use emulated hands on a desktop. `localhost` counts as a
secure context, so WebXR works over plain HTTP here.

To try it on a Quest over Wi-Fi, use the HTTPS dev server and open its
network URL in the Quest Browser (accept the local certificate warning once):

```bash
npm run dev
```

> **Windows note.** IWSDK 1.0.1's dev server gives PowerShell 1.5 s to report
> its process start time. On machines where PowerShell starts slower, `npm run
> dev` fails with "Cannot establish this process birth identity". Run the
> opt-in, version-checked patch once after installing:
>
> ```bash
> npm run fix:iwsdk-process-probe
> ```
>
> It only raises that dev-tool timeout; the production build is unaffected.

## Test

```bash
npm test
```

Unit tests (Vitest, plain Node, no XR runtime): projection maths, puzzle
validity and solvability, validator tolerances (property tests with thousands
of random poses), the authoritative puzzle session, all three interaction
profiles, tracking-loss recovery, the adaptation engine, persistence and
corruption recovery, game flow, the reveal timeline, the stage anchor, and a
parser check on every UI panel.

```bash
npm run test:e2e
```

Emulator play-through. Needs `npm run dev:http` running and Microsoft Edge
(default) or Google Chrome (`npm run test:e2e -- --chrome`) installed.
It enters VR in the IWER emulator, presses every menu with a hand ray and
pinch, and solves all three puzzles by driving emulated articulated hands,
including a tracking loss mid-move. This proves logic and input flow, not
headset performance.

```bash
npm run check
```

Typecheck, unit tests and production build together.

```bash
npm run bench
```

Per-frame CPU cost of puzzle evaluation and projection on the machine that
runs it (not a Quest).

## Build and deploy

```bash
npm run build
```

Outputs a static site in `dist/` with relative paths, so it can be hosted
under any sub-path (GitHub Pages, Vercel, any static host).

GitHub Pages is enabled with GitHub Actions as the source. Publishing is
manual: run the **Deploy to GitHub Pages** workflow (Actions tab, or
`gh workflow run deploy-pages.yml`). Pushing to main does not redeploy. See
[docs/SUBMISSION.md](docs/SUBMISSION.md) for the full checklist.

## Project structure

```
src/
  domain/        Layer 3  Puzzle model, projection, constraints, validator, session, the three puzzles
  interaction/   Layer 2  Hand samples -> holds; pinch detection, targeting, profiles
  adaptation/    Layer 4  Evidence-based profile suggestions
  game/          Layer 5  Flow state machine, progression, reveal timeline, orchestration (GameApp)
  presentation/  Layer 6  Chamber, shard views, projection plate, guides, procedural audio
  ui/            Layer 7  UIKitML panel manager, UI controller, 2D landing page
  persistence/   Layer 8  Versioned local saves and in-progress
