feygon/SS2PsiAutocastMFD.readme:
# psi_autocast_mfd: an in-game psi macro MFD for System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster

**TLDR:** Press one key and an MFD opens over the game: every discipline with its duration, effect, overload value and cyber module cost, plus an editor that builds [psi_autocast](https://github.com/feygon/SS2PsiAutocast) macros and saves them to keys. Requires psi_autocast 1.2 or later.

**Step-by-step setup for both mods, and a troubleshooting table:** [SETUP_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/feygon/SS2PsiAutocast/blob/main/SETUP_GUIDE.md).

## What it shows

A scrolling table of all 35 disciplines, each with its icon, tier and name, and:

- **Duration** at your current PSI and at PSI 8.
- **Effect** at your current PSI and at PSI 8: damage, healing, stat bonus, chance or recharge.
- **Overload:** what an overload gives you, for the disciplines that benefit from one.
- **Cyber Mods:** "bought", or the cost, including every tier unlock still needed to reach it. Costs follow your difficulty.

The numbers are read from the running game, so they follow SCP if you use it.

## Building a macro

1. Pick a **macro key** at the top or bottom of the MFD.
2. Click a discipline, or its **+Overload** / **+Quick** button, to add a cast.
3. Add psi hypos, click a wait to change it, and choose a **Finish** weapon switch.
4. **Save**, close the MFD, and press the key.

T1–T5 jump to a tier.

## Install

1. Install and enable psi_autocast 1.2 or later.
2. Extract this zip into the **game folder**, the one with `SystemShock2Remastered.exe`. It adds `mods\psi_autocast_mfd.kpf`.
3. Choose **New Game → Mods**, add **psi_autocast_mfd** (keep psi_autocast), **Apply** and start. Once the first level loads, load your own save, then make a regular save.

## Set up the keys

Scripts can't bind keys while the game runs, so this happens once, with the game closed, in:
`%USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\Nightdive Studios\System Shock 2 Remastered\user.bnd`

Back it up first. Either run `setupPsiMfd.bat` from the GitHub repo (`extras/`), which binds free keys for you (and asks, key by key, about non-default keys whose command is also on another key), or add the lines yourself:

```
bind keypad_star "summon_obj PsiMfd"
bind keypad_minus "run user:/psi_macros\MacroKPMinus.cmd"
bind keypad_del "run user:/psi_macros\MacroKPDel.cmd"
```

- **The first line** opens and closes the MFD.
- **Each other line** is a macro key. Add one per key you want, changing the key and the file name together. The MFD finds these lines and offers those keys.

Optional: the mouse wheel scrolls the table when the mouse is over the open MFD, and switches weapons everywhere else. The setup script asks about this (y/n); by hand, replace the two `mouse_wheel` lines with:

```
bind mouse_wheel_up "summon_obj PsiMfdWheelUp"
bind mouse_wheel_down "summon_obj PsiMfdWheelDown"
```

In a save without psi_autocast_mfd enabled, the wheel then doesn't switch weapons. To undo, put back `bind mouse_wheel_up "cycle_weapon 1"` and `bind mouse_wheel_down "cycle_weapon -1"`.

## What it writes

Each macro is a small text file in `Saved Games\Nightdive Studios\System Shock 2 Remastered\psi_macros\`, one per key, in the format psi_autocast's Macro Builder writes. The MFD reads `user.bnd` and never changes it, and it doesn't touch the game folder.

## Uninstall

1. Remove the lines you added to `user.bnd`, with the game closed.
2. Delete `mods\psi_autocast_mfd.kpf`, and the `psi_macros` folder in your save folder if you no longer want the macros.

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`. Source and developer notes: https://github.com/feygon/SS2PsiAutocastMFD

pricilaModesto20/money-maze.readme:
# Money Maze: a live Q&A game for your talk

The audience scans a QR code, types their name and a question, and turns into a **piggy bank** running around the
**Money Maze** on the projector. Piggy banks collect coins and "pay off" the **FEES / DEBT / INFLATION** blocks.
Every question unlocks one of the dashboard fundamentals (Budget, Cash flow, Revenue, Expenses, KPIs, Forecast).
When you put someone's question on screen they get +150 bonus points, and everyone who asks gets a badge they can share on LinkedIn.

| Page | Who uses it | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Ask page | Audience phones (the QR code) | `/` |
| Projector screen | Laptop connected to the projector | `/screen` |
| Host panel | You or a helper (phone or 2nd laptop) | `/host?key=…` |

## 1. Customize it

Edit [config.js](config.js): your name, the talk title, your LinkedIn URL, the "You are…" options, the 6 fundamentals, and the point values.

## 2. Run it on your laptop

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

The terminal prints three links. The **host key** changes each time you start the server. To keep it the same,
start with `HOST_KEY=mysecret npm start` (Git Bash) or `$env:HOST_KEY="mysecret"; npm start` (PowerShell).

## 3. Make it reachable from the audience's phones

Phones have to be able to reach your server. Pick one option:

**A. Same Wi‑Fi (easiest, but test it at the venue).** The QR code uses your laptop's Wi‑Fi IP, for example `http://10.0.0.39:3000`.
Many college and conference networks block phone-to-laptop traffic, so try it from your own phone in the room.
Windows may ask to allow Node.js through the firewall. Allow it on **Private** networks.

**B. Free tunnel (works on any network).** Install [cloudflared](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/downloads/), then:

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000
```

Copy the `https://….trycloudflare.com` address it prints and restart the app with it:

```powershell
$env:PUBLIC_URL="https://your-tunnel.trycloudflare.com"; npm start
```

**C. Deploy it (most reliable).** Push this folder to GitHub and create a free **Web Service** on [Render](https://render.com)
(build command `npm install`, start command `npm start`, set the environment variable `HOST_KEY`). Render provides the
public URL automatically and the QR code uses it. Open the site a minute before your talk, because free services go to sleep when nobody is using them.

## 4. During the talk

1. On the projector laptop, open `/screen` and click **Fullscreen** (bottom right).
2. On your phone, or a helper's phone, open the host panel link. Click **Show on screen** on a question to display it.
   The asker gets +150 points, a gold ring around their piggy bank, and a "your question is on the big screen!" alert on their phone.
3. **Clear screen** puts the card away. **Hide** and **Delete** handle off-topic questions, and **Remove** takes a player out of the game.
4. **Reset everything** (host panel) wipes the board before your real session. Do this after testing!

Data is saved to `data/state.json`, so restarting the server keeps the game going.

## Safety built in
- Names are limited to 24 characters and questions to 280. A simple filter blocks common profanity.
- Each phone has to wait 15 seconds between questions.
- Questions **only** appear big on screen when you choose them. Names do appear in the maze automatically, so use **Remove** if someone enters a rude name the filter missed.

joshuaschaible/gameguide.readme:
# Game Guide

Share your game with a friend. They watch and draw; their marks show up on top of your game and fade after 4 seconds.

Standalone desktop app for Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon). No accounts, no game hooking: it captures a window or screen, like a screen share.

## Download

Get the latest from [Releases](../../releases/latest):

- **Windows:** `Game-Guide-Windows-v<version>.zip` → Extract All → run `Game Guide\Game Guide.exe` (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway).
- **Mac:** `Game-Guide-Mac-v<version>.zip` → open it, right-click `Game Guide.app` → Open.

After that the app updates itself: when a new release is out it shows **Update available**.

## How it works

- The player shares a game window or a screen and sends an invite link (or a 6-character code).
- Pairing goes through the free PeerJS service; video and drawings then flow directly between the two computers (WebRTC, encrypted), with a free relay as a fallback.
- Drawings appear in a transparent, click-through overlay on the player's game, only while marks are visible.
- Stalls, alt-tab, recreated game windows and dropped video recover automatically.

## Develop

```sh
npm run setup
npm start          # run from source
npm test           # two-app end-to-end test (local PeerJS server)
npm run package    # Mac arm64 + Windows x64 into dist/
```

The product name, link scheme, app ID and GitHub repo live in `app/brand.json`; change them there to rename.

## Releasing

Bump `version` in `app/package.json`, commit, then:

```sh
git tag v1.5.1 && git push --tags
```

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) builds both apps, signs the Mac app with the certificate in the `MAC_SIGN_CERT` / `MAC_SIGN_KEY` repo secrets (so macOS keeps its permissions across updates), and publishes the release. Installed copies pick it up within a couple of minutes. It can also be run by hand from the Actions tab.

The invite page (`site/join/`) is published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.

Plans for multiplayer and hosting: [docs/multiplayer-and-relay-plan.md](docs/multiplayer-and-relay-plan.md).

Harlock123/AVACastlesOfDrCreep.desc: AVA Castles of Dr. Creep: a puzzle-platformer of castle escapes after the 1984 C64 classic. Seven castles, a synthesised speaking welcome, two players. C# / .NET 10 / Avalonia.
Harlock123/AVACastlesOfDrCreep.readme:
# AVA Castles of Dr. Creep

[![Build](https://github.com/Harlock123/AVACastlesOfDrCreep/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Harlock123/AVACastlesOfDrCreep/actions/workflows/build.yml)

A puzzle-platform game in the style of Ed Hobbs's 1984 Commodore 64 classic **The Castles of Dr. Creep**,
built with .NET 10 and Avalonia UI. A voice welcomes you in, and then you have to find your way out. Each
castle is a set of single-screen rooms joined by doors, full of machines, traps and monsters. Nearly every
hazard has a control box somewhere in its room. Learn what each control does and you can turn the castle's
traps on its monsters. Play alone, or with two players at once.

## Features

- **Seven castles**, chosen from the title screen: the **Tutorial**, **Ravenmoor**, **Grimwald**,
  **Thornhallow**, **Mortlake**, **Wyrmgate** and **Blackspire**. They range from five easy rooms to six hard
  ones. Start at any castle; escaping one takes you into the next.
  - **Thornhallow** drops a mummy through a trapdoor and lures the monster into lightning. It ends in a vault
    with a three-way matter transmitter and a race against a force field.
  - **Wyrmgate** is a loop that brings you back into its first hall by another door. On the way you park a
    ray gun, stop a conveyor, and shoot a mummy on the floor below from a gun control on the floor above. At
    the end you leave the monster shut behind a force field.
- **Getting about:** walk the floors, climb ladders up and down, slide down poles. Go up at a door to go
  through it, and the matching door on the other side opens too. Walk off a ledge and you fall. More than a
  few squares is fatal.
- **The machines, and their controls:**
  - **Doorbells** open shut doors. **Coloured keys** open the locks of their colour.
  - **Trapdoors** open and shut from a lever. Anyone (or anything) on one when it opens drops through.
  - **Moving walkways** carry whoever stands on them. Their control stops them and sends them back the
    other way.
  - **Force fields** stop players and monsters alike. Their button drops a field for six seconds.
  - **Lightning machines** kill whatever walks into them. A switch turns each one on and off.
  - **Ray guns** slide up and down their rails, find your height, and fire across the room. From the
    gun's control it's yours to move and fire, and it won't fire on you.
  - **Matter transmitters**: the button picks a receiver by colour, and up sends you there.
- **The monsters:**
  - **Mummies** rise from their tombs when you touch the ankh, and walk their floor after you. They
    can't climb.
  - **The monster** stands in its coffin until you pass on the same floor. Then it follows you anywhere
    you can go, by ladder and pole too, though more slowly.
  - Both stop at force fields, and lightning, the ray guns and an open trapdoor finish them (500 each).
- **The map** (Tab, or Back on a gamepad) shows the rooms found so far, the doors between them, and where
  everyone is.
- **Two players** play at once with their own keys or gamepads. When they're in different rooms, the screen
  shows both rooms side by side. Each has three lives, and a lost life starts you again at the door you
  last came in by. The castle is escaped when everyone still in the game is out.
- **Times and points:** the clock runs from the moment you're in. Your **best time** for each castle is
  kept and shown on the title screen. Escaping scores 1,000 times the castle's number, plus a bonus for
  every second under the castle's target time.
- **The welcome:** *"Welcome, visitor... Come in... You will never leave!"*, spoken over a faint organ with a
  stone hall's echo, on the title screen and again at the door of each new game, before the music. The voice
  is synthesised from scratch the way the 8-bit machines talked: a buzz and a hiss shaped by formant filters
  (`tools/speech.py`), with the words written out as phonemes. No recording and no speech engine is involved.
- **The attract mode** walks the Tutorial castle by its way out.
- **Every castle is proved escapable.** Each castle file ends with its way out, step by step. The tests
  walk every castle by it, from the door in to the way out, without losing a life.

# Carmageddon for Android

Native Android build of **Carmageddon** and **Carmageddon Splat Pack** (1997), no emulation.
The game code is [dethrace](https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace), a reverse-engineered C
reimplementation of the original executable, running on SDL2 on the phone's CPU.

**This repository contains no game files.** You need your own copy of
[Carmageddon Max Pack from GOG](https://www.gog.com/game/carmageddon_max_pack); the build takes
the data from its installer. Do not share APKs built with it: they contain the game.

## What you get

- Two launcher icons, *Carmageddon* and *Carmageddon Splat Pack*, each starting its game directly.
- Everything on screen is the original game: intro and cutscenes, menus, fonts, the hand cursor.
  Menus are used by touch, as with the mouse.
- In races, touch buttons sit in the side bars left free by the 4:3 picture: steering, accelerate,
  brake/reverse, handbrake, pause, map, repair, camera and recovery. They are drawn at runtime from
  the game's own replay-panel buttons and icons, and they follow key remapping done in the game's
  options screen.
- Back button / gesture acts as ESC; a keyboard button in menus brings up the soft keyboard for names.
- The data is packed into the APK and unpacked once on first launch (about 20 s), behind the
  game's own loading screen.

## Building

Requirements: Android SDK with NDK 29 and CMake 3.31.6 (both from the SDK manager), JDK 17+,
Python 3, [innoextract](https://constexpr.org/innoextract/), and `bsdtar` (built into macOS;
`libarchive-tools` on Debian/Ubuntu).

```sh
git clone --recursive https://github.com/Vadim170/carmageddon-android.git
cd carmageddon-android

# 1. Game data from your GOG installer -> game-data/ (ignored by git)
tools/prepare-data.sh /path/to/setup_carmageddon_max_pack_1.0_gog_*.exe

# 2. APK with the game data inside
cd android
./gradlew assembleRelease
adb install app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

The APK is arm64-v8a only and signed with the local debug key.

### Faster iterations

`./gradlew assembleDebug -PnoGameData` leaves the data out of the APK (a few MB instead of ~290 MB).
Push the data once instead:

```sh
P=/sdcard/Android/data/com.dethrace.carmageddon/files/games
adb shell mkdir -p $P
adb push ../game-data/c1 ../game-data/sp $P/
```

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `android/` | Gradle project: launcher entry, first-run unpacking, SDL activity |
| `dethrace/` | Submodule: [dethrace fork](https://github.com/Vadim170/dethrace/tree/android), branch `android` — Android build, touch controls (`src/harness/platforms/sdl2_touch.c`) |
| `SDL2/` | Submodule: SDL 2.32.10, built from source with the game |
| `tools/prepare-data.sh` | Unpacks the installer and merges each game's CD image data with its installed files |
| `tools/make-resources.py` | Renders the unpacking screens and launcher icons from the game data at build time |

## Notes

- The GOG release keeps key maps and all cutscenes only on the CD images it mounts in DOSBox;
  `prepare-data.sh` takes them from there. `PATHS.TXT` is dropped so the game does not look for a CD drive.
- Rendering is the original software renderer.

## Legal

Carmageddon is the property of its owners (THQ Nordic); this project is not affiliated with or
endorsed by them. dethrace may only be used with assets from an owned copy of Carmageddon, and its
source is for non-commercial use only — see the dethrace repository for its terms.

Native Android build of Carmageddon and Splat Pack

Gradle project around dethrace (fork with Android support and touch
controls) and SDL2, plus tools that take the game data from your own
GOG Max Pack installer. No game files are included: the unpacking
screens and launcher icons are rendered from the game data at build time.

Jakedapro/Pokemon-Game.readme:
# PokeBrawl

A Pokemon battle game for Mac and Windows with **every Pokemon** (all 1,025 species plus regional forms, Megas and Primals), real moves and learnsets, and three modes:

| Mode | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Practice** | Turn-based battles vs a bot on **Easy / Normal / Hard / Insane** |
| **Showcase** | Huge auto-battles for content: *Gen 1 vs Gen 3*, *Fire vs Water*, *10 Legends vs 200*... Watch live or **record a vertical MP4** (720x1280, ready for TikTok / Reels / Shorts) |
| **PvP** | Play your friends online with just a room code. Comp teams with abilities, Tera, items, natures, EVs, Mega Stones, Showdown import/export |

Practice and PvP are **turn-based (Showdown-style)**: 6v6 singles with:
- team preview, switching and priority
- hazards (Stealth Rock, Spikes, Toxic Spikes), weather and screens
- U-turn/Volt Switch pivots, Protect, Substitute, Trick Room and more

Keys: **1-4** pick a move, **M** to Mega Evolve, **T** to Terastallize.

The real-time arena is used only for showcases.

## Install (one command)

### Mac

Open **Terminal** and paste:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jakedapro/Pokemon-Game/HEAD/install.sh | bash
```

Then type `pokebrawl` (or open **PokeBrawl** from `~/Applications`).

The installer:
- installs into `~/.pokebrawl`
- doesn't need Apple's Command Line Tools or git: if your Mac has no suitable Python, it downloads a private copy just for PokeBrawl
- installs the game engine (`pygame-ce`)
- installs `ffmpeg` with Homebrew for video recording, if you have Homebrew
- downloads the Pokedex and sprites once (about 20 MB)

### Windows 10 / 11

Open **PowerShell** (Start menu, type *PowerShell*) and paste:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jakedapro/Pokemon-Game/HEAD/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then double-click **PokeBrawl** on your Desktop (or in the Start menu), or type `pokebrawl` in a new window.

The Windows installer:
- installs into `%USERPROFILE%\.pokebrawl` with its own private copy of Python (nothing else on your PC changes)
- adds Desktop and Start menu shortcuts and a `pokebrawl` command
- installs `ffmpeg` with `winget` for video recording
- downloads the Pokedex and sprites once (about 20 MB)

### From a zip (no GitHub needed)

Got a `PokeBrawl.zip` from a friend? Unzip it first (don't run it from inside the zip), then:

- **Mac:** double-click `Install on Mac.command` (if macOS blocks it: right-click > Open > Open), or run
  `bash ~/Downloads/PokeBrawl/install.sh` in Terminal
- **Windows:** double-click `Install on Windows.bat` (if SmartScreen pops up: More info > Run anyway)

It installs (or updates) the game from that folder. Your save and progress are kept. To update later, get a newer zip
and do the same again.

### Updating

The game **updates itself**: it downloads new versions in the background while you're in the menu and installs
them the next time you open it (or hit *Update ready - Restart*). Turn it off in Settings. You can also run the
install command again, or `pokebrawl update`. Your friends install it the same way.

> The repo must be **public** for the one-liner to work for your friends (or add them as collaborators and have them `git clone` it).

## Playing with friends online

Open **PVP**, pick your team, and choose a connection:

- **Online room code (default, works anywhere):** press **HOST** to get a 5-letter code. Your friend types it and presses **JOIN**. No IP addresses or port forwarding needed. It runs through free public MQTT message servers and falls back to the next server if one is down. Set *List room publicly* and friends can just pick your room from **BROWSE OPEN ROOMS**.
- **Same Wi-Fi:** HOST, and your friend's JOIN screen finds you automatically.
- **Direct IP:** works with Tailscale IPs, or with port 7777 forwarded.
- **Relay server:** run `pokebrawl relay` on any server you own.

During the match:
- ping meter
- emotes (GG, LOL, EZ... also F1-F6)
- 60-second turn timer
- **Rematch** button

Every battle is saved as a replay and counted in your win/loss record against that friend.

The host runs the battle. Rules: Species Clause, Item Clause, one Mega and one Tera per team.

Room codes go over normal HTTPS (via the free ntfy.sh service), so they work even on school or work Wi-Fi that blocks games. If that's unavailable, the game falls back to public MQTT servers. Run `pokebrawl nettest` to see what works on your network.

## Showcases (content mode, owner only)

Showcase is hidden for everyone except the game's owner, who unlocks it on their computer with a secret code.

Pick a preset or build a custom matchup in the app:

- **Matchups:** any generation, Legendaries, fully evolved Pokemon, by BST, or any type
- **Team size:** All, 100, 50, 25, 10, 3 or 1
- **Toggles:** Megas, boss HP bars for legendaries, the trainer-catches-the-winner finale, speed

Then **Watch live** (Space = pause, +/- = speed) or **Record video**. Videos go to `~/Movies/PokeBrawl/`.

- **Auto-edit:** recordings are cut down to the *Video length* you pick (TikTok 60s by default). The intro,
  cutscenes, finishers and the catch play at normal speed; the long middle of the fight is fast-forwarded with
  a small `>> x6` tag. Pick *Full battle* to keep everything.
- **Battle royale:** set *Mode* to Royale (or pick a royale preset): every Pokemon for itself while a storm
  shrinks the arena. Royales with 60+ Pokemon go full screen in a wide arena while you watch; recordings stay
  vertical.
- **Gigantamax:** the 32 Pokemon with a Gigantamax form can Gigantamax (no plain Dynamax) - in showcases they
  grow huge with a red cloud crown, and in 1v1 battles it's a gimmick next to Mega and Tera: 3 turns, more HP,
  G-Max moves, no flinching. Mega Evolution and Gigantamax both have their own cutscenes.
- **Mewtwo:** when Mewtwo snaps it gets a rampage cutscene, says a line (spoken with the Mac's built-in voice,
  shown as subtitles) and a psychic shockwave wipes out everyone near it.

Fix FireRed graphics not downloading on Macs

errors on many Macs, so Adventure silently fell back to the drawn art. It now uses
the game's own downloader (system keychain, certifi, curl fallback). Also fixes
the tile set folder names for generic house interiors, and the title screen now
says when the graphics couldn't be downloaded.

paulofcmello/rea-chess.readme:
# REA Chess

A local, single-player take on chess.com's puzzles and bots. No accounts, no multiplayer.
Progress (puzzle rating, rush scores, bot records, daily streak) is kept in your browser's localStorage.

## Run

```sh
cd app
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # static site in app/dist
```

## Features

- **Puzzles (rated):** Elo-style rating that starts at 800, picks puzzles near your level, with hints (using one fails the puzzle), retry, solution, themes reveal and a recent-results strip.
- **Puzzle Rush:** 3 min / 5 min / Survival, 3 strikes, ramping difficulty, best scores.
- **Daily Puzzle:** the same puzzle for everyone on a given date, with a day streak.
- **Themes:** drill one tactic (mate in N, fork, pin, ...) at 5 difficulty levels, unrated.
- **Play Bots:** 13 bots from 250 to 3200 with personalities and chat, color choice, hints, takebacks, an optional eval bar, a result screen and game review.
- **Analysis:** Stockfish 19 eval bar, top 3 lines, move navigation (arrow keys), FEN/PGN import and export.
- **chess.com look and sound:** all 39 chess.com piece sets, 31 boards and 9 sound themes, plus animation speed, move highlights, legal-move dots and coordinates (Settings).
- **Puzzle page cloned 1:1 from chess.com:** same layout, Chess Sans font, animated coach (their Rive file), speech bubble, footer buttons, correct/incorrect badges and colors, two-step hint, puzzle sounds.
- **Board engine modelled on chess.com's:** 180 ms slides, capture fade-out, drag hover outline, click-again to deselect, right-click square marks and arrows (Shift/Ctrl/Alt colors, L-shaped knight arrows).

## How it was made

The UI and flows were reverse-engineered from chess.com's `/puzzles/rated` and `/play/computer` with
[REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) (`inspect-web-page`, `capture-web-screenshot`, `analyze-web-bundle`).
The evidence is in `.rea/`. The piece-set list comes from chess.com's own bundle (via REA).

- Puzzles: [Lichess puzzle database](https://database.lichess.org/#puzzles) (CC0), about 4,100 sampled. Run `app/scripts/build-puzzles.sh` to regenerate.
- Engine: [Stockfish.js 19](https://github.com/nmrugg/stockfish.js) lite single-threaded WASM (GPLv3, see `app/public/engine/COPYING.txt`).
- Pieces, boards and sounds: chess.com's, loaded at runtime from `images.chesscomfiles.com` (nothing is copied into this repo). They're chess.com's artwork, so keep this app for personal use and don't publish it with them.
- Bots above 1320 use Stockfish's `UCI_Elo`. Weaker bots sample from MultiPV lines with rating-scaled noise and occasional random moves.

Xenia Canary is an experimental fork of the Xenia emulator. For more information, see the [Xenia Canary wiki](https://github.com/xenia-canary/xenia-canary/wiki). Come Join the Xbox Emulation Hub Discord server for help, support and general dissusion: https://discord.gg/WCmxvvxHqu For developer chat join `#dev` but stay on topic. # Infinix

A game in the style of *The World's Hardest Game*, built to be harder.
You are the red square. Take every yellow coin, reach the green exit, and don't touch a blue circle.

Open `index.html` in any browser. It is a single file (the soundtrack is embedded) with no install or build step.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrows / WASD | Move |
| Shift (or Space) | Precise movement (30% speed) for pixel-perfect gaps |
| P / Esc | Pause |
| F | Show the formula with live values |
| V | Toggle AI vision (where enemies expect you to be + what they learned) |
| M | Sound on/off |

On touch screens, drag anywhere to move. A short drag moves slowly.

Progress (room, deaths and what the enemies have learned) is saved in the browser.

## Rooms

| # | Name | What's new |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Entrance | Classic up/down enemies |
| 2 | Lanes | Horizontal lanes and coins |
| 3 | Orbit | Rotating crosses and orbiters |
| 4 | Watchers | Rail enemies that slide to where you will cross |
| 5 | Crossfire | Rails from every side and a checkpoint |
| 6 | Hunted | Free hunters that predict your movement |
| 7 | Pack | Hunters that work together (chase, cut off, flank) |
| 8 | The Wall | A wall whose gap mirrors you |
| 9 | Memory | Sentries that guard the routes you used before |
| 10 | Infinix | A ring around the exit. Far away its gap runs from you; up close it turns steadily so you can get in |
| 11 | Graph | Enemies trace equations (Lissajous, roses, sine), drawn on the floor like a graphing calculator |
| 12 | Echo | Your own path, replayed a few seconds behind you |
| 13 | Looped | The left and right edges connect; lanes of enemies stream around forever |
| 14 | Undertow | Conveyor floors push you while a wall sweeps and hunters chase |
| 15 | Shockwave | Expanding rings with one gap, placed at the edge of where you can reach in time |
| 16 | Serpent | Hunters with bodies that get longer the more you die |
| 17 | Recursion | Three nested rings around the exit, turning in opposite directions |
| 18 | Hive | Seven hunters and sentries working together |
| 19 | Collapse | Two walls at once, a shockwave and your echo |
| 20 | Infinix ∞ | Looping edges, nested rings, a serpent, a hunter and your echo |

After room 20 the rooms loop forever (mirrored each loop). The level number keeps counting, so the game keeps getting harder.

## The difficulty formula

```
L = level, D = deaths, x = L + D
d   = 1 + 99 · (1 − 0.5^(x/50))            approaches 100, never reaches it
PpR = max(20 · 0.5^(d − 90), 1)            only once d ≥ 90
```

- `d` sets enemy speed, reaction time, how far ahead they predict you, and patrol speed.
- `PpR` is the gap the AI enemies must leave you: between two hunters, around safe zones and coins, and the opening in walls, rings and shockwaves. Before `d = 90` the gap is 20 px. After that it halves as `d` rises, down to 1 px. Once it is online, walls and rings hold still while you thread a gap, so 1 px gaps stay possible.
- Enemies learn from every death through a heat map of where you go and where you die. Hunters lean toward your habits, sentries guard your favourite routes, walls and shockwaves open where you go least. Learning stops when `PpR` reaches 1 px (`d ≈ 94.32`).
- AI enemies are always slower than you, and every gap is at least your size + 1 px, so a path always exists.

## Music

The soundtrack is the song embedded at the bottom of `index.html`. It loops forever on a bar line (124 beats at 136 BPM) with a 50 ms crossfade, so there is no gap or click at the loop point. To use a different song:

```
node tools/embed-song.js path/to/song.mp3 [secondsPerBeat beatsPerLoop]
```

Without the last two numbers the whole song loops.

## Testing that every room is beatable

`tools/` runs the real game code headlessly in Node and uses a search bot to find a complete winning run, which is then replayed on a fresh game to confirm it.

```
node tools/bot.js --room 15 --D 120          # one room at one death count
node tools/verify.js --rooms 1-20 --targets 60,88,max   # the whole matrix, 4 at a time
```

A target is the difficulty `d` to test at, or `max` for an endgame save (2000 deaths, `PpR` = 1 px).

# Zotac Lister

Desktop app (Electron) for selling Steal a Brainrot pets on Eldorado.gg.

- **Auto List**: import pets from your bases, generate listing images, post offers
- **Listings / Orders / Wallet / Reviews / Notifications / Chat**: Eldorado seller dashboard, refreshes itself
- **Auto Delivery**: reads the buyer's Roblox username from the order chat, launches the stock account and trades the pet in game, then reports to a Discord webhook (cancels the order if delivery fails)
- **Roblox Accounts**: stock accounts with cookies stored encrypted (Windows DPAPI via Electron safeStorage); browser login captures the cookie
- **Image Editor**: listing card templates; brainrot art from the SAB wiki, trait and mutation icons from the game
- **Video Proof**: records deliveries

In-game scripts are in `scanner/` (`zotac_scanner.lua` scans your base, `zotac_delivery.lua` is the delivery agent). The app fills in its local port and agent token when you copy them from the app.

## Run

```
npm install
npm start
```

Build the Windows installer:

```
npx electron-builder --win nsis
```

User data (accounts, settings, pets) lives in `%APPDATA%\Zotac Lister\zotac-data.json` and is only ever stored locally

jinxlover/osm2zomboid.desc: Turn any real place into a playable Project Zomboid (Build 42) map from OpenStreetMap data, built the way the game's own map is built. Free and open source (MIT).
jinxlover/osm2zomboid.readme:
# osm2zomboid

**Turn any real place into a playable Project Zomboid (Build 42) map, built the way the game's own map is built.**

osm2zomboid is a **free and open-source** project, released under the [MIT License](LICENSE): anyone may use it,
study it, change it and share it, including their changes. Contributions are welcome (see
[Contributing](#contributing)).

It reads a real area from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) (streets, buildings, land use, shops,
parks, car parks) and writes a ready-to-install map mod: terrain, roads with curbs and lane lines, sidewalks,
car parks with cars, lawns and driveways, and every building fully built: walls, shop fronts, doors, windows,
stairs, lifts, roofs, and rooms furnished like Knox County's. It writes the game's map files directly; no
TileZed or WorldEd is needed.

## Goals
* **One shot.** Point it at your town, your street or a big piece of your city, and get a map you can play
  straight away, without editing by hand.
* **Faithful to the real place.** Streets, blocks and buildings stand where they really are and at their real
  size (one square is one metre). A corner store mapped on a corner is a corner store on that corner.
* **Faithful to the game.** Everything looks and plays like vanilla Knox County, not like a generated map. Every
  rule (what goes in a room, how a shop is stocked, how full a room is, where furniture stands, how grimy a wall
  is, how a car park is laid out) is **measured from the vanilla map**, not guessed, and checked against it.
* **Anyone can use it.** No mapping tools to learn; a command (and later a simple window) and a place name.

## Status
Working and playable, under active development and playtesting. The included preset is downtown
**Austin, TX** around 6th Street (about 1 km x 0.75 km, 330+ buildings, towers up to 28 floors). Residential
neighbourhoods (houses, rows of townhomes, yards, driveways) are being tuned now. Known limits are listed at the
end. Please report anything that looks wrong in game, ideally with a screenshot and a rough location.

## Requirements
* Project Zomboid **Build 42**, installed (the tool reads your own copy of the game; see below)
* Python 3.10+ and `pip install -r requirements.txt` (pillow, numpy, scipy)
* An internet connection the first time you build a new area (OpenStreetMap's Overpass API)

## No game files are included
This repository contains **no Project Zomboid files**. On first run the tool reads the tile definitions and the
vanilla map **from your own installed copy of the game** and stores its measurements in `cache/` on your PC,
which is never published (see `.gitignore`). Generated maps go to `output/` and to your `Zomboid/mods` folder.

## Where the Austin map sits
South-east of Muldraugh. Drive south out of town on the highway to the cross junction (world x ~10560,
y ~11204, cell 41,43) and turn east. That road (15 squares wide, world rows 11197-11211) used to stop in the
forest at x = 12899; the mod continues it 156 squares to the west edge of Austin, where it becomes 6th Street.

* Map block: cells **51-54 x 42-44** (world x 13056-14079, y 10752-11519). All twelve were forest in vanilla.
* Connector: vanilla cell **50,43** is imported whole and only the strip of road is repainted. It is a copy of the
  vanilla road's own last squares, so the join cannot be seen. The cell keeps its vanilla `chunkdata` file.
* The map is turned ~18 degrees so that Austin's street grid runs along the tile axes (straight walls and streets
  instead of staircases). The top of the map therefore points about 18 degrees east of north.

## Quick start
1. Install Python 3.10+ and run once:  `pip install -r requirements.txt`
2. Double-click **run_austin.bat** (builds the mod and copies it to `%USERPROFILE%\Zomboid\mods\Austin6thStreet`).
   Takes about three minutes (a 1 km x 1 km residential area: about a minute and a half). The OpenStreetMap data for Austin is cached in `cache/`, so it works offline.
3. Start Project Zomboid -> Mods -> enable **Austin, TX - 6th Street** -> New Game. On the spawn screen pick
   **Austin, TX - 6th Street**; you start on a sidewalk downtown (world 13568, 11108 or one of four other spots).
4. Optional: **preview_austin.bat** renders `preview.png` (an isometric cutaway drawn with the game's own sprites;
   trees are drawn by the game from other sprites and do not show in previews).

## Make your own map
```
python survey.py 60 10 72 18 site.png
python generate.py --name MyTown --title "My Town" --lat 40.7484 --lon -73.9857 --cells 4x3 --cell0 66,13 --entry-y 0 --install
```
* `survey.py CX0 CY0 CX1 CY1 out.png` draws a block of vanilla cells with the cell grid and lists what each one
  holds. A map mod replaces every vanilla cell it covers, so pick cells marked `forest`. `generate.py` warns when
  the block you chose holds rooms, roads or rails.
* `--lat/--lon`  centre of the area. `--cells WxH` size in 256x256 cells (1 tile ~ 1 metre; 4x3 is ~1 km x 0.75 km).
* `--cell0 X,Y`  world cell of the map's north-west corner.
* `--rotate`     `auto` (default) turns the map so the street grid follows the tile axes when the area has a clear
  grid; `0` keeps north up; any other number forces that angle.
* `--background` what lies between mapped features: `auto` (paved lots downtown, lawns in suburbs, grass beyond),
  `grass` or `concrete`.
* `--zombies`    zombie density. `0.5` (default) is half the spread of downtown Louisville, `1` the full spread, `0` none.
* `--entry-y 0`  no connector. To join a vanilla road instead, give all four:
  * `--entry-y`      world y of the centre line of the vanilla road (Austin: 11204.5 for rows 11197-11211)
  * `--vanilla-end`  world x of the first square past the end of that road (Austin: 12900)
  * `--link-cell`    the vanilla cell that holds the road's end (Austin: 50,43); the connector runs east from it
    through every cell up to the map, importing each one and keeping its `chunkdata`
  * `--entry-road`   name o

Gstxxx/shadow-ledger.desc: Remake web de um tycoon de espionagem: agência privada, comércio global e operações
Gstxxx/shadow-ledger.readme:
# Shadow Ledger

**Jogue no navegador:** https://shadow-ledger-delta.vercel.app

Você é o Diretor de uma agência privada de inteligência. Voa o mundo com sua Frota de cargueiros, compra armas, informação e mercenários onde a guerra é barata e vende onde ela paga caro. Abre Estações, monta Equipes e decide até onde vai: um roubo de tecnologia aqui, um Golpe ali. Cada passo deixa rastro, e o mundo inteiro está ficando mais tenso.

Estratégia em tempo contínuo com pausa, para navegador e celular (jogado deitado). É um remake com identidade própria das mecânicas de *Guns Girls Lawyers Spies* (2006): todos os nomes, textos, arte e sons são novos.

## O jogo

- **Comércio com Saturação:** os preços de 55 países reais reagem à política (guerra, guerra civil, sanções) e às suas próprias vendas.
- **Estações:** de Célula a Base, geram renda, mostram preços e defendem a si mesmas.
- **Equipes:** Pessoal destacado que age em outro país enquanto você está longe.
- **Reputação e Exposição:** como cada governo te vê e quanta atenção você chamou. A Exposição gera Ameaças anunciadas: batidas, processos, ataques.
- **Combate em grade** jurídico, urbano, militar ou aéreo, com Prévia de chance de vitória e Tática.
- **Agências Rivais** que jogam pelas mesmas regras.
- **Tensão Global:** guerras e operações empurram o mundo para o abismo. No topo, abre-se o mercado mais lucrativo e mais perigoso do jogo. Se ninguém parar, vem a Crise Final, e todos perdem.

## Desenvolvimento

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

```bash
npm test
```

- Glossário do domínio: [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md)
- Decisões de arquitetura: [docs/adr/](docs/adr/)
- Roadmap: [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md)
- Deploy: [docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md)

Stack: Vite, React 18, TypeScript, zustand, d3-geo e world-atlas, GSAP, Web Audio. Toda a arte, a música e os efeitos são gerados por código.

# Minigames

Party games for one shared screen. Pass the phone or laptop around.
A static site, deployed to GitHub Pages and installable as an app (PWA, works offline).
Python + uv are only used to build and preview it.

## Run locally

```sh
uv run minigames                  # opens http://127.0.0.1:8765/
uv run minigames --host 0.0.0.0   # play from phones on your network
uv run minigames build            # only regenerate site/games.json
```

## Games

| Game | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [Second Shot](site/games/second-shot/) | Click twice exactly N seconds apart. Furthest off is out each round; an exact hit wins instantly. Keeps a GOAT record per target time. |

## Deploy to GitHub Pages

1. Push this repo to GitHub (branch `main`).
2. In the repo: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**.
3. Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/pages.yml` and publishes `site/`.

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the layout, conventions and how to add a game.

destrukter/Chameleon_app.readme:
# Chameleon

An Android take on the social-deduction party game *The Chameleon*: everybody knows the secret word except
the chameleon, who has to bluff a clue that blends in. The app adds what the 3–8 player box can't do:

- **More players**: 3–30 in the local game, 2–16 in multiplayer (two is allowed for testing; play with three or more).
- **More chameleons**: always fewer than half the table. Multiplayer has one voting round per chameleon.
- **Bigger boards**: three presets, Small 4×4 (like the original card), Medium 5×5 and Large 6×6.
- **502 topic cards**, each with 36 words (`core/src/main/resources/categories.txt`). Smaller boards use a
  random subset of a topic's words, so the same topic plays differently each time.
- **Topic packs**: the cards are sorted into 12 themed packs, which can be switched on and off before a game.
  The packs are Animals & Nature, Food & Drink, Places & Travel, Sports & Outdoors, Gaming, Movies, TV & Books,
  Fantasy, Myth & History, Science & Tech, Arts, Music & Fashion, Home & Everyday Life, Out and About, and
  Describe It ("Things that are red", "Things with wheels", …).

- **Custom boards**: design your own 4×4, 5×5 or 6×6 boards (menu → *Custom boards*) and sort them into your own
  categories. Each category is a topic pack that can be selected only for games of a size it has boards for. In
  multiplayer the host's boards are used, and the board drawn at the start is sent to every player.
- **Share boards**: export some or all categories as a `.json` file (save it, or share it straight to a messenger)
  and import files from friends. Imports merge: same boards are updated, name clashes get a number, and
  incomplete boards are skipped.

## Install

Download [`apk/chameleon.apk`](apk/chameleon.apk) to your phone and open it (allow installing from unknown
sources when asked). CI rebuilds and commits this file on every push.

## Local game (pass & play)

1. Type in everybody's names. The game counts them when you press *Start*. Pick the number of chameleons,
   the board size and the topic packs to play with (remembered for next time).
2. The topic card is shown. *Accept* it, or *Reshuffle* to draw a different topic.
3. Pass the phone around. Each player sees their name, taps *Show*, sees the secret word (or
   "You are the Chameleon!"), then taps *Hide & next*. There are no dice; the phone hands out the word directly.
4. After the last player, the board is shown together with a randomly chosen start player. Give your clues
   out loud and point at the chameleon. *Reveal* shows who it was and the secret word.
5. *Play again* returns to the player list with the same names, where you can add or remove players.
   You can also go back to the menu.

## Multiplayer

One phone hosts the lobby, and the game state lives on that phone. There is no game server: other phones
reach the host in one of two ways, and both can be used in the same lobby.

- **Direct (8-character code, e.g. `K7QM-2XRA`)**: for phones on the same Wi-Fi, connected to the host's mobile
  hotspot, or in the same VPN such as Tailscale or ZeroTier. The code encodes the host's IP address and port plus a
  checksum. Phones connect over TCP and no internet is needed. The lobby shows a separate code for each network
  the host is on (Wi-Fi and/or VPN).
- **Over the internet (12-character code, e.g. `E4KD-9QXM-27TB`)**: for friends anywhere. The host and players
  exchange the game messages through a free public MQTT broker (`broker.emqx.io`, falling back to
  `broker.hivemq.com` and `test.mosquitto.org`). The broker only forwards messages: they are end-to-end encrypted
  with AES-GCM using a key derived from the code, and the topic name is a hash of the code. This depends on those
  free public services being up.

- **Create lobby** asks whether the lobby is **public** or **private**. A private lobby can only be joined with its
  code. A public one also appears in **Browse public lobbies**, where anyone can join with one tap; the listing is
  a retained message on the relay broker, refreshed while the lobby is open and removed when it closes.
- Players type either code into the same field and choose a name; duplicate names are rejected.
- The host chooses the number of chameleons, the board size, the topic packs, and types in the time to give a word
  (10–300 s) and the voting time (15–600 s). Everyone else sees the settings live in the lobby.
- The game starts right away. Non-chameleons see the secret word highlighted on the board. The turn order is
  random, and each player has to type their word before their timer runs out (otherwise the turn is skipped).
- A chat stays open the whole time for discussion.
- After everybody has given a word, voting starts. There are as many voting rounds as chameleons. Each round
  accuses the player with the most votes (the start player breaks ties). An accused chameleon gets one guess
  at the secret word.
- The results show the secret word, every chameleon, whether they guessed right, and the scores, using the
  board game's scoring applied per chameleon. Then the host can play again or go back to the lobby, and
  anyone can leave.
- A player who drops out mid-round can rejoin with the same name.

## Project layout

| Module | What |
| --- | --- |
| `core` | Pure Kotlin/JVM: word list, game engine (host-authoritative state machine), JSON-lines protocol, lobby codes, TCP and MQTT-relay transports. Unit-tested, including real games over loopback sockets and through an in-process MQTT broker. |
| `app` | Android app in Jetpack Compose: menu, rules, local game screens, and multiplayer lobby/game/chat screens. |

## Building

```bash
./gradlew :core:test          # engine, protocol, networking and word-list tests
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug  # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

Requires JDK 17+ and the Android SDK (compileSdk 35, minSdk 26). The GitHub Actions workflow
(`.github/workflows/android.yml`) runs the tests and uploads debug and release

mswietlicki/steam-frame-dictation.readme:
# Steam Frame dictation Voice typing for the Valve Steam Frame. Hold a controller button, speak, let go, and your words are typed into the window you're looking at, in Firefox, on the desktop, or in any other flat app. Speech recognition runs on the headset itself (no cloud, no account), takes well under a second, and handles English, Polish and 23 other European languages without any language setting. It's built on [Voxtype](https://github.com/peteonrails/voxtype), the dictation tool [Omarchy](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy) uses, plus the glue the Frame needs: a way to type into gamescope windows, a SteamVR controller binding, and a desktop button. - No root, no `steamos-readonly disable`: everything lives in your home directory and survives SteamOS updates. - One command to install, one to remove. - **Game mode:** one click in the VR dashboard pauses dictation and gives its RAM (about 1 GB) to a heavy game. ## Install You need a shell on the Frame as the `steamos` user: - **In the headset:** open **Desktop** (dashboard → **+** → Launch Program → Desktop), then **Konsole** from the app menu. - **Or over SSH**, if you've set it up (for example with [Frame Control](https://github.com/saphid/frame-control)): `ssh steamos@`. Then run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mswietlicki/steam-frame-dictation/main/install.sh | bash ``` Or clone it and run the script (git is on the Frame): ```bash git clone https://github.com/mswietlicki/steam-frame-dictation.git cd steam-frame-dictation ./install.sh ``` The first install downloads about 700 MB: Voxtype (45 MB) and the speech model (640 MB). It takes a few minutes. Open the Desktop in the headset before you install if you want the mic icon pinned to its panel. You can also add it later with `./install.sh pin`. Run the same command again to update. Other commands: ```bash ./install.sh status # services, engine, last log lines ./install.sh pin # pin the mic icon to the desktop panel (desktop must be open) ./install.sh unpin # take it off the panel ./install.sh uninstall # remove (keeps the config and speech models) ./install.sh uninstall --purge # remove everything ``` (With the curl one-liner, add the command after `bash -s --`, e.g. `curl -fsSL …/install.sh | bash -s -- uninstall`.) ## Use it Put the headset on: the mic is muted while it's off your head. You hear a beep when recording starts and another when it stops, and the text appears right after. | How | What to do | |---|---| | **Controller** | Hold **right Y** (or **left D-pad up**), speak, let go. Or tap it to start, and tap again to stop. | | **Desktop panel** | Click the mic icon in the panel to start, and click again to stop. | | **App menu** | Search for **Dictate** on the desktop. | | **Shell** | `~/.local/bin/voxtype-toggle` starts or stops it. | The controller button works while the **dashboard is open** and on a window in **gamepad mode**. It doesn't work in **pointer mode** (see [Known issues](#known-issues)). ### Game mode The speech model stays loaded so dictation starts instantly, and that keeps about 1 GB of RAM busy. Before a heavy game, open the dashboard → **+** → Launch Program and click **Game mode: OFF**. It stops Voxtype and the button, plays Steam's switch sound and shows a banner with the free RAM. The entry then reads **Game mode: ON**. Click it again after the game; dictation is back a few seconds later. A reboot turns game mode off. From a shell: `voxtype-game-mode on|off|status`. With game mode off, a game still wins if RAM runs out: the kernel stops dictation first, and it stays stopped until you click Game mode twice (or run `voxtype-game-mode off`). ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR B["Right Y / left D-pad up"] -->|OpenVR action| W["vr-button.py
(voxtype-button.service)"] I["Panel icon / Dictate"] --> T[voxtype-toggle] W -->|voxtype record start / stop| V["Voxtype daemon
(voxtype.service)"] T --> V M[Headset mic] --> V V -->|"Parakeet, on the CPU"| V V -->|dotool commands| S["dotool stand-in"] S -->|"ASCII: XTest on gamescope :1"| F[Focused window] S -->|"other text: Klipper + Shift+Insert"| F ``` 1. **Voxtype** (`voxtype.service`, a user service) records from the headset mic and transcribes with NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6b v3 (int8, ONNX). It's pinned to the Frame's fast A720 cores and keeps the model loaded. 2. **Typing.** On the Frame, Voxtype's usual typing tools can't reach apps. ydotool and dotool make a uinput keyboard, and nothing in the headset's display stack reads one. wtype needs a Wayland protocol KWin doesn't offer. What does work is XTest on gamescope's app X display (`:1`), which goes to whatever window has focus. So `files/dotool`, a small stand-in for dotool, reads Voxtype's commands and types plain ASCII with [xdotool](https://github.com/jordansissel/xdotool) (taken from the Frame's own package repo). XTest drops any other character (ą, é, “”), so text with those goes onto the desktop clipboard through Klipper and gets pasted with Shift+Insert. Your clipboard is restored afterwards. 3. **The button.** `vr-button.py` is an OpenVR overlay app with a single action bound to right Y and left D-pad up, which SteamVR's laser pointer doesn't use. Hold means push-to-talk, and a quick tap toggles. On a window in gamepad mode Steam Input would grab the button, so while dictation is allowed the action set runs at an *overlay global* priority. That needs SteamVR's "Experimental overlay input overrides" setting, which the installer turns on. 4. **Not in games.** The button does nothing while a VR game is running or a Steam game window has focus (it reads gamescope's `GAMESCOPE_FOCUSED_WINDOW`), so Y stays the game's. When it backs off, it also drops the priority. 5. **Desktop.** The installer adds a `Dictate` launcher to the desktop's app menu and pins

# Danny Abbo’s very own Monikers that makes up for him forgetting it

A pass-the-phone web version of the party game [Monikers](https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/156546/monikers) (Alex Hague & Justin Vickers). Unofficial; all card text is original.

One deck, three rounds:

1. **Anything goes**: say anything except the name.
2. **One word**: exactly one word per card.
3. **Charades**: no words.

## Features
- **Multi-phone play:** the host taps *Host a game* and gets a 4-letter room code. Everyone else opens the site on their own phone, taps *Join a game* and types the code (or opens the invite link). Everyone drafts on their own phone at the same time. During a turn the clue-giver sees the card, their teammates see "Guess!", and the other team sees the card so they can keep it honest.
- **One-phone mode:** pass a single phone around, no internet needed
- Deck building by **draft** (each player secretly keeps favorites from a hand), **quick deal**, or **write your own** names (Celebrity style)
- 2 to 4 teams, 30/45/60/90 second turns, cards worth 1 to 4 points
- Skip, end-of-turn undo, "did they get it at the buzzer?" check, leftover-time carry-over
- Survives a reload or locked phone (comes back paused), keeps the screen awake during turns
- Installable to the home screen and works offline (PWA)

## How multi-phone works
The host's phone runs the game. Other phones connect to it directly (WebRTC) using [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com/) 1.5.5, which is bundled in `vendor/` (MIT license). The PeerJS free cloud server only introduces the phones to each other. There are no accounts and no database.

- The host's phone has to keep the page open for the whole game. If the host reloads, the room reopens with the same code and everyone reconnects.
- A player who reloads or whose phone sleeps rejoins automatically.
- Some strict networks block peer-to-peer connections. PeerJS falls back to its free relay server, but if a phone still can't connect, switching it from Wi-Fi to cellular (or the other way) usually helps.
- To test against your own PeerServer, add `?peer=host:port` to the URL.

## Play on your phones
It's a static site: `index.html` plus a manifest, service worker and icons. No build step.

**GitHub Pages:** repo Settings → Pages → Source "Deploy from a branch" → pick the branch and `/ (root)`. The game is then at `https://<user>.github.io/monikers/`. On iPhone, open it in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen.

**Locally:** `python3 -m http.server` and open `http://localhost:8000`.

<https://sudoshd.github.io/glimmer-nook/>.

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Landing page — App Store Connect *Marketing URL* |
| `support.html` | Common questions and contact — Connect *Support URL* (required) |
| `privacy.html` | Privacy policy — Connect *Privacy Policy URL* (required), and the link in the game's Settings › Privacy |

App Review opens the support and privacy URLs, so neither may 404.

## Editing

Plain HTML with one shared `style.css` (the game's daylight and evening colors). Check locally before
pushing:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000>.

## Contact address

Every page uses **glimmernook.app@gmail.com**, a dedicated account rather than a personal one — the
address here is indexed and permanent. To change it:

```bash
sed -i '' 's/glimmernook\.app@gmail\.com/new@example.com/g' *.html
grep -o 'mailto:[^"]*' *.html | sort -u    # confirm every page moved
```

Keep it matching the support contact in App Store Connect.

## Source

These pages live in the app's own repository under `Docs/Site/` and are copied here to publish. The
privacy policy there is also `Docs/AppStore/PRIVACY_POLICY.md`. Edit them there and copy across, or
edit here and copy back — but do not let them drift.

soltheman/cavestory-pocket.readme:
![doukutsu-rs](./res/sue_crab_banner_github.png)

A reimplementation of the Cave Story (Doukutsu Monogatari) engine with many quality-of-life
improvements. It lets you enjoy the 2004 indie classic like a modern game, with support for the
original freeware, Cave Story+, and Nintendo Switch data files.

[Join the Discord server](https://discord.gg/fbRsNNB)

[![CI](https://github.com/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master?preview)

- Get stable/beta builds from
  - [get.doukutsu.rs](https://get.doukutsu.rs)
  - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/releases)
  - [Flatpak](https://flathub.org/apps/io.github.doukutsu_rs.doukutsu-rs) (Linux only)

- Get nightly builds (has latest fixes and improvements) from
  - [get.doukutsu.rs](https://get.doukutsu.rs)
  - [nightly.link](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master?preview)

  Permalinks to latest builds from `master` branch:

  - [Windows (64-bit)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_windows-x64.zip)
  - [Windows (32-bit)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_windows-x32.zip)
  - [macOS (Intel, 64-bit, 10.14+)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_mac-x64.zip)
  - [macOS (Apple M1, 11.0+)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_mac-arm64.zip)
  - [Linux (64-bit)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_linux-x64.zip)
  - [Android (armv7/arm64/x86)](https://nightly.link/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/workflows/ci/master/doukutsu-rs_android.zip)

> [!NOTE]
> macOS note: If you get a `"doukutsu-rs" can't be opened` message, right-click doukutsu-rs.app and click open.

> [!NOTE]
> If you get issues with Epic Games Store version, scroll down for instructions.

#### Data files

In order to work doukutsu-rs needs to be paired with supported data files. This repository does not contain any data
files.

doukutsu-rs works fine with freeware data files or [NXEngine(-evo)](https://github.com/nxengine/nxengine-evo) or from a
supported copy of [Cave Story+](https://www.nicalis.com/games/cavestory+).

<details>
  <summary>How to set up data files on Android</summary>
  
  If your phone has an app called **"Files"**:

  1. Launch this app.
  2. Press **☰** on the top left corner.
  3. Tap on **"doukutsu-rs game data"**.
  4. Copy your game data files to the opened folder.


  If your phone does not have this app:
  
  1. Install the **"Material Files"** app from *Hai Zhang* and launch it([Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=me.zhanghai.android.files) | [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/me.zhanghai.android.files/) | [Github Releases](https://github.com/zhanghai/MaterialFiles/releases)).
  2. Press **☰** on the top left corner.
  3. Press **"+ Add storage"**.
  4. In the window that pops up, press **"External storage"**.
  5. Press **☰** on the top left corner.
  6. Tap on **"doukutsu-rs game data"**.
  7. Press the large blue button at the bottom labelled **"USE THIS FOLDER"**.
  8. Then click on **☰** in the top left corner again and open.
  9. Tap on **"files"** above **"+ Add storage"**.
  10. Copy your game data files to the opened folder.
</details>

#### Supported game editions and data file acquisition guides

**Freeware**

doukutsu-rs works out of the box when it's placed in the same directory as the original Doukutsu.exe executable. On the initial
startup, doukutsu-rs will automatically extract the additional resources that are embedded in the vanilla game into the `data`
directory. Until that is done, both doukutsu-rs and the vanilla executable have to exist in the directory.

<details>
<summary>Example root directory</summary>

![example root directory with doukutsu-rs and vanilla Cave Story](https://i.imgur.com/3dJ7WMB.png)

</details>

**Cave Story+**

doukutsu-rs can be used as drop-in replacement for `CaveStory+.exe` (instructions for Mac are in the "Steam release (Win/Mac/Linux)" section). No modifications to game files are needed.

**Remastered version (first released in 2017 on Switch)**

> [!NOTE]
> This version is **incompatible** with saves from the original version.
>
> Interchanging the save files may result in spawning in wrong locations, softlocks, graphical glitches, or other issues.

<details>
<summary>Steam (2026) - not yet supported</summary>

See https://github.com/doukutsu-rs/doukutsu-rs/issues/365 for status.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Nintendo Switch</summary>

Extract the `data` folder (contained in `romfs`) from your console using tool such as [nxdumptool](https://github.com/DarkMatterCore/nxdumptool).

**Important notes:**

- doukutsu-rs doesn't rely on the original ROM or executable, you just need the data files, go to `RomFS options` menu to just extract the files to SD card so you don't need to do any extra steps.
- Ensure you're dumping the files **with update included** (`Use update/DLC` option), as 1.0 isn't supported.

**Nintendo Switch homebrew port specific info**

If you're running the homebrew port (drshorizon.nro) on your Switch, you can avoid the dumping step, doukutsu-rs will
automatically detect and mount the data files if you run it over Cave Story+ in Title Override mode (hold `R` while starting CS+ and launch d-rs from hbmenu).

You can put your own data files in `/switch/doukutsu-rs/data` directory on SD Card, which will be overlayed over RomFS if
you run it in setup described above.

</details>

**Original version (first released in 2011 on Steam)** - expand for instructions

<details>
<summary>Steam release (Win/Mac/Linux)</summary>

The `data` folder is in the same place across all platforms.

FlorianDaunay/bee-factory.readme:
# Bee Factory

A cute gacha game about bees. Build hives that make honey, open country packs to recruit bees from around the world, and lead teams of up to six through a turn-based story (Brave Frontier style).

- **Design:** [docs/GAME_DESIGN.md](docs/GAME_DESIGN.md) covers the lore, the mascot (Pip), rarities, zones, synergies, combat, economy, audio and platforms.
- **Stack:** Vite + React 18 + TypeScript, Tailwind 3 with the token theme system (`src/themes`), zustand (saved in localStorage), vitest.
- **Art and music are generated in code:** bees and enemies are parametric SVG, and the music is a Web Audio sequencer that adapts to the fight. There are no asset files.

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm test           # engine, gacha, synergy, hive and balance tests
npm run build      # static site in dist/
```

## Layout

```
src/core/      pure game logic, no React (data, battle engine, gacha, hives, synergies, progression)
src/audio/     synthesized SFX + adaptive music
src/art/       SVG bees, enemies, hives, icons
src/store/     saved game state (zustand persist) and settings
src/features/  one folder per screen (hive, summon, bees, story, battle, arena, settings)
src/themes/    token-based theme system
```

## Android app

The Android app is the same web build packaged with [Capacitor](https://capacitorjs.com/) (`android/`, `capacitor.config.ts`).

- After changing the web code: `npm run build && npx cap sync android`.
- Icons and splash screens are generated from `assets/` with `npx capacitor-assets generate --android`.
- The app version comes from `package.json` (`0.2.2` → versionName `0.2.2`, versionCode `202`).
- Local build needs JDK 21 and the Android SDK: `cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease`. Release signing reads `android/keystore.properties` (never committed).

**CI** (`.github/workflows/android.yml`): every push to `main` builds an APK (artifact), and every **published** GitHub release gets a signed `bee-factory.apk` attached. That is the file the website offers to Android visitors. Release builds need four repository secrets: `BF_KEYSTORE_BASE64` (the keystore, base64), `BF_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `BF_KEY_ALIAS`, `BF_KEY_PASSWORD`. Keep the keystore safe: every update must be signed with the same key.

## Deploy

Pushing to `main` builds and deploys to GitHub Pages (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`). To turn it on: repository **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**.

alexleo97/mesbg-tabletop.readme:
# MESBG Tabletop

An unofficial virtual tabletop for the **Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game** that runs in any web browser, on a computer or a phone. You don't need an account, and nothing to install: start a game, send your opponent the link, and play.

Build your army in the [MESBG List Builder](https://v2024.mesbg-list-builder.com/), export it, and drop it onto the table.

> Unofficial fan project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Games Workshop or Middle-earth Enterprises. No official artwork or rules text is included; you need your own rules to play.

## What it does

- **Guided turns.** The turn guide at the bottom of the screen runs the game for you. It walks through setup (scenario, board, armies, deployment), then each turn's phases in order. It rolls off for priority (re-rolling first-turn ties and passing later ties to the player who didn't choose last time), says whose go it is in the Move and Shoot phases, finds every fight on the table, and checks Broken armies and the scenario's end at the end of the turn. You press one button to move on.
- **Tap a model to act.** Selecting a model shows its profile, wounds, Might, Will and Fate, plus the actions that fit the phase. In the Shoot phase, tap an enemy to aim: it shows the range and what you need to hit and wound, then one tap rolls the hit, any In the Way rolls and the wound together. In the Fight phase, models in base contact get a ⚔ marker that opens the fight. Courage tests show whether they passed.
- **Real-scale board.** The board is 48"×48" by default (or 72"×48" / 24"×24"), with a 1" grid. Bases are real sizes: 25mm infantry, 25×50mm cavalry, and 40mm/60mm monsters.
- **Two players in real time** over a room link, plus spectators. Moves, dice and phases sync instantly, and you reconnect automatically if the connection drops.
- **Built-in list builder.** Pick an army (all 106 army lists), add heroes and warriors, choose wargear and mounts, and see points as you go. Lists are saved in your browser. The data comes from the open-source [MESBG List Builder](https://github.com/mhollink/mesbg-list-builder-v2024) (see [src/data/README.md](src/data/README.md)).
- **Unit photos and stat cards.** Models show their unit's photo on the base, and selecting a model shows its profile: Mv, Fv, Sv, S, D, A, W, C, I, wargear and special rule names. Mounted heroes get a cavalry base and their mount's move. Photos load from the list builder's image host and can be turned off in the Table panel.
- **List import.** Upload the list builder's .json export (read exactly, with options and mounts), or paste a plain list like `12x Warrior of Minas Tirith`. Each army deploys in its own zone (player 1 at the bottom, player 2 at the top), so armies never spawn on top of each other.
- **Measuring the MESBG way**, base edge to base edge:
  - **Ruler tool:** shows base-to-base distance when you start or end on a model.
  - **Move and control zones:** a selected model shows its move distance and its 1" control zone.
  - **Drag feedback:** while you drag, it shows distance moved against the model's Move, and turns red if you go over.
- **Dice rolled on the server**, so nobody can fudge them. The shared log shows who rolled what, and counts successes against a target (e.g. 4+).
- **Turn tracker.** It shows the turn number and phase (Priority, Move, Shoot, Fight, End), plus who has priority and a priority roll.
- **Model cards.** Each model tracks wounds, Might/Will/Fate for heroes, facing and base size. A casualty pile is built in.
- **Terrain and starter boards.** Four original starter boards (River Crossing, Ruined City, Woodland Edge, Mountain Pass), laid out like tournament tables: each half mirrors the other so both sides deploy facing the same terrain, about a quarter to a third of the table is covered, and something in the middle blocks line of sight. One button places five Domination-style objective markers. Terrain is drawn with natural outlines and shadows on textured ground (grassland, plains, forest floor, mud, flagstones, snow, sand), and you can add, resize, rotate and lock woods, rocks, hills, buildings, ruins, walls, water, rivers, cliffs, fields and objectives.
- **Matched play scenarios.** Pick any of the 24 matched play scenarios (six pools of four) or roll for one with server dice. The app draws each side's deployment zone, places the fixed objective markers, summarises the special rules and how the game ends, and keeps a shared victory points tally with a VP score in the top bar. The summaries are our own shorthand; the Matched Play Guide has the full rules.
- **Rules quick reference.** The 📖 Rules tab rolls to wound from Strength and Defence (including 6+/4+ results, where the server rolls the second die), to hit, In the Way, Courage and Intelligence tests, and the Jump, Leap, Climb, Swim and Thrown Rider tables, and shows the result. It can fill in stats from the selected model, and has the wound chart, missile weapons, turn sequence and heroic actions in short form.
- **Fight helper.** Select models from both sides and roll the whole fight at once with their real stats: the duel (ties go to the higher Fight value, then a roll-off), then the winner's strikes against the model you choose, with trapped fighters taking double strikes. One tap takes the wounds off.
- **Magic.** Cast any of the 35 magical powers with the Will dice you choose, and the target can resist with its own Will. Will is taken off the selected hero automatically, and a short reference covers every power and how casting and resisting work.
- **Broken and game end checks.** An army is marked Broken once it has lost more than half its starting models. In the End phase the app applies the scenario's end condition: it ends the game at 25%, or asks for the D6 roll in scenarios that end on a 1-2 once an army is Broken, and shows the final score.
- **Undo.** The ↶ Undo button on the tool rail (or Ctrl+Z) takes back your own last change, such as a misplaced drag, without

Ryubara/coney.readme:
# Coney

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Coney is in early development and not playable yet. It contains none of the original game's files or code: you
> play it with your own copy of the game. Coney was restarted in October 2026 with a stricter clean-room process; the
> [clean-room page](docs/clean-room.md) explains how it works.

## What Coney is

Coney is an independent, open-source reimplementation of the engine of *The Warriors* (PS2, 2005), written in C++23
on SDL3 for Windows, Linux and macOS. The goals:

- **Faithful gameplay.** Every gameplay rule matches the original until the game is complete.
- **Two renderer modes.** Faithful, which keeps the PS2 look, and enhanced, which adds shadows, reflections and
  highlights over the original lighting.
- **A fixed 60 Hz simulation**, deterministic, with networked play built in (lockstep with rollback).
- **Your own install.** A launcher reads your PS2 or Xbox disc image once and builds a local install from it. The
  original mission scripts run from that install on Coney's Lua 4.0 VM.
- **Modding.** A Lua SDK for new missions, and tools for custom content.

Coney is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive.

## Progress

The clean-room tooling comes first: the page checks, the gates between the research and the engine, and the
isolated containers implementers work in. Engine work starts when that system is in place, one subsystem at a time.

Progress will be reported per subsystem as the share of the original's code covered by reimplemented functions that
passed their comparison, next to the share of research that passed the page gate. Both numbers are generated, never
typed in.

## Building and running

### Requirements

- Python 3.11 or later, for `coney-tools` (standard library only, nothing to install).
- The engine's requirements (a C++23 compiler, CMake) arrive with the engine. Implementers work in a container and
  need only Docker ([CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)).

### Clone

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Ryubara/coney.git
cd coney
```

### Build and test

There is no engine to build yet. To run the tool's tests:

```sh
cd python
python -I -B -m unittest discover -s tests
```

To run every check CI runs, the same way CI runs it ([Checks and CI](docs/ci.md)):

```sh
python -I python/coney-tools.py ci
```

### Run

Nothing to run yet. The launcher and installer come first: they take your disc image and set up a local install.

## Documentation

- [`python/README.md`](python/README.md): `coney-tools`, including the research page check.
- [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md): how agents work in this repository.
- [`docs/ci.md`](docs/ci.md): the checks CI runs, how to run them locally, and the pinned versions.
- The [documentation site](https://ryubara.github.io/coney/), with the clean-room page and the guides (online once
  the repository is public; `docs/` holds the same pages).

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: who may take which role, and what each role needs. Everyone follows
the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Report security problems as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) describes.

## Licence

Coney's code is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)).
[LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md) covers game data, the clean room, trademarks and the licences of documentation and
dependencies.
