Elko-Lemiso/fafo.desc: Party game for one TV and a room full of phones: whose photo, whose song, name that tune, famous faces, flags, maps
Elko-Lemiso/fafo.readme:
# fafo

A party game for one TV and a room full of phones. The laptop plugged into the TV shows the game, and
everyone plays on their phone. Friends join by scanning a QR code, and nobody needs an account.

Play it at **https://fafo.up.railway.app**: open **https://fafo.up.railway.app/tv** on the laptop connected to the TV.

## Rounds

Pick any mix in the TV lobby under **Rounds tonight**:

- **Whose photo:** everyone adds up to 5 photos from their phone (baby pictures work great). Each one
  pops up on the TV and everyone guesses whose it is. Every photo gets played.
- **Whose song:** everyone picks up to 3 songs on their phone. The TV plays a clip and everyone guesses who picked it.
- **Name that tune:** the TV plays a clip and phones pick the song or the artist. Choose from about 50 genres,
  decades and moods, or type any artist or playlist.
- **Famous faces:** a photo of a well-known person sharpens from a blur. Answer early to score more.
- **Flags** and **Maps:** name the country from its flag or its outline.
- **Imposter:** everyone gets the same secret word on their phone, except one person who gets a similar word
  (or no word, if you choose). Everyone says a one-word clue out loud in turn, talks it over, then votes. There's
  no clock: each step moves on when the players are ready. Spotting the imposter scores 500; an imposter who gets
  away scores 1,000. Needs at least 3 players.

A **Theme** ties the rounds together. Music makes the faces come from tonight's playlist, Africa keeps flags,
maps and faces African, and so on. **Length** sets how many quiz rounds each type gets.

Scoring: a right answer is 500 to 1,000 points, faster scores more. When someone guesses your photo or song
wrong, you get 250 points. The last round counts double. Votes stay anonymous: the TV only shows how many
people picked each answer. The game ends with a podium and a few awards.

## Run it on your laptop

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18 or newer.

```bash
cd server
npm install
npm start
```

`npm install` is only needed the first time. `npm start` prints something like:

```
  fafo is running.

  TV (this laptop):   http://localhost:3000/tv
  Phones join at:     http://192.168.1.23:3000/  (or scan the QR code on the TV)
```

1. Open the **TV** link in a browser on the laptop that's plugged into the TV. Click **Full screen**.
2. Everyone scans the QR code on the TV with their phone camera and types a name.
   If a phone can't scan, type the address shown under the QR code into its browser, then the room code.
3. The first player to join gets the **Start game** button on their phone. The laptop has one too, or press Enter.

Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop. Photos live only in the server's memory and are gone when it stops.
Flags, maps and fonts work without internet; music, famous faces and artist photos need it.

## If phones can't connect

- **macOS firewall:** the first time, macOS may ask whether `node` can accept incoming connections. Click Allow.
  If you missed it, go to System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options and allow `node`.
- **Guest or venue Wi-Fi:** these often block devices from reaching each other. Turn on your phone's hotspot,
  connect the laptop and the other phones to it, and restart `npm start` so it picks up the new address.
- **Wrong address in the QR code:** if the laptop has several networks, set the address yourself:
  `HOST_IP=192.168.1.23 npm start`. The startup message lists the other addresses it found.
- **Port in use:** the server tries 3000, then 3001 and onwards. To choose one: `PORT=8080 npm start`.

## Put it online (Railway)

The `server` folder is self-contained, so you can also host the game at a public address.
Then phones can join over mobile data, with no shared Wi-Fi needed.

- Deploy from `server/` with `railway up`. Railway runs `npm start`, and `.railwayignore` keeps `node_modules` out of the upload.
- Railway sets `PORT`, and the server listens on it.
- The QR code points at `PUBLIC_URL` when that's set, otherwise at `https://$RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`.
- On a public server, a phone only sees the room whose code it scanned or typed.
- Run a single replica only. Photos and live rooms live in that one server's memory, and a restart or redeploy clears them.

## How it works

- `server/server.js` is a small Express and Socket.IO server. It serves the page, relays live state between the
  TV and the phones, and keeps uploaded photos in memory.
- `server/public/index.html` is the whole game: the TV screen and the phone controller. The TV tab runs the game.
- `server/quiz.js` serves the country list, flags (flag-icons) and world map (world-atlas) for flag and map rounds.
- `server/music.js` finds songs, 30-second clips and artist photos through Deezer's free API, and real artist
  photos through Wikipedia.
- `server/data/faces.json` is the famous-faces list with Wikipedia photos. Rebuild it with `python3 server/data/build-faces.py server/data/faces.json`.
- `server/data/imposter.json` holds the word pairs for Imposter rounds.
- `whos-who.html` is the original Claude artifact version, kept for reference.

Photos of famous people come from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons under free licences; song clips and cover art come from Deezer.

tamsler/wigglefeast.desc: Wigglefeast: an offline snake-style .io game with AI worms, saves and install-as-app support.
tamsler/wigglefeast.readme:
# Wigglefeast

A single-player snake-style .io game you can play offline. Eat, grow, and outsmart AI worms; there's no server.

## Play

**Online:** https://tamsler.github.io/wigglefeast/

**Install it as an app** (works offline afterwards):
- Chrome / Edge (Mac, Windows, Linux): click the install icon in the address bar
- Safari on Mac: File → Add to Dock
- iPhone / iPad: Share → Add to Home Screen
- Android: Chrome menu → Install app

**Locally:** open `index.html` in a browser (double-click works, nothing to build). Offline/install support needs it served over http(s), e.g. `python3 -m http.server`.

- **Mouse**: steer toward the cursor
- **Hold click / Space / W / ↑**: boost (burns mass, drops food behind you)
- **A / D or ← / →**: keyboard steering
- **P / Esc**: pause
- **Touch**: drag to steer, add a second finger to boost

Run into another worm's body and you die. Make others run into yours and eat what they leave behind.
Head-on collisions are won by the bigger worm. The red ring is the arena edge.

Power-ups: 🧲 magnet · x2 / x5 food multiplier · ⚡ free boost + speed · 🔭 zoom out (16s each).

## Saving

Everything is saved automatically in the browser's `localStorage`, so there's nothing to do by hand:

- **The world** (every worm, food, power-ups, your current run) is saved every 10 seconds, whenever the tab is hidden, and when the tab is closed or reloaded. When you reopen the game you land on a paused "Welcome back" screen and can resume your run (with a 2-second shield) or end it.
- **Stats** (lifetime totals, best score per difficulty, top 10 runs, last 50 games) are saved whenever a run ends. Open them from **Stats & high scores** in the menu.
- **Export / Import** on the stats screen writes everything to a `.json` file and loads it back. Use it as a backup or to move to another browser/computer. Clearing your browser's site data erases the in-browser save.

Storage keys: `wormarena.world`, `wormarena.profile`, `wormarena.settings` (the prefix predates the rename and is kept so existing saves load).

## Files

- `engine.js`: simulation (worms, food, collisions, bot AI). No DOM, so it can run headless in Node.
- `main.js`: canvas rendering, camera, input, HUD and menus.
- `index.html`, `style.css`: page and UI.
- `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`, `icons/`: installable app + offline support and release versioning.

Bot count (5–60) and difficulty (easy/normal/hard) are set in the menu. The arena size scales with the bot count.

## Releasing

Merging to `main` deploys to GitHub Pages, but installed copies only pick up a release whose version changed:

1. Bump `VERSION` at the top of `sw.js` (e.g. `'1.1.0'` → `'1.2.0'`) in the same PR as the change. The **Version check** on the PR fails with "Bump VERSION in sw.js" if you change a game file without doing this. Changes to `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `openspec/`, `.github/` and `.claude/` don't need a bump.
2. Merge. The **Tag release** workflow tags the commit `v<VERSION>` and publishes a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/tamsler/wigglefeast/releases) with notes generated from the merged PRs (versions with a suffix like `1.2.0-beta.1` are marked pre-release). Players get the new release downloaded in the background and see an **Update available → Reload** banner (never mid-run). Ignoring it is fine; it takes over on the next launch.
3. Never reuse a version: the PR check rejects a version that already has a tag. To roll back, publish the old code under a **higher** version.

When a release adds a new file the game loads, add it to `FILES` in `sw.js` too, or it won't work offline.

You can run the checks locally: `.github/scripts/check-version.sh main` and `DRY_RUN=1 .github/scripts/release-tag.sh`.

## Planning

Work is tracked in GitHub Issues. Feature-sized changes are planned with [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec) under `openspec/` (`/opsx:propose`, `/opsx:apply`, `/opsx:archive` in Claude Code); `openspec/specs/` describes how the game currently behaves.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Thomas Amsler

emberian/intmat2.readme:
# Interior 2

**Evolving matter as one continuous field.** Every voxel carries recurrent
activity, deposited solid, nutrient, waste and light. Activity deposits solid out
of nutrient; solid changes who the activity can talk to, blocks transport and
shades what lies beneath; light turns waste back into nutrient. Mass is conserved.
A 184-number local rule, shared by every voxel, decides what grows. There are no
agents: a cell is whatever region the dynamics make.

[Design](DESIGN.md) · [Working here](AGENTS.md) · Predecessor: [intmat](https://github.com/emberian/intmat) (archive)

```sh
julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
julia --project=. test/runtests.jl                 # conservation, bounds, oracle
julia --project=env/metal -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'   # Apple GPU
```

```julia
using Intmat2, Metal
r = random_rule(8); p = Physics{Float32}()
w = World(MetalBackend(), r, (128,128,128))
w = Intmat2.light!(w, r, p)
for _ in 1:1000; w = step!(w, r, p); end
summarize(w)
```

natemiller39/DD-s.readme:
# Austin's Fantasy DD's

An online table game for up to 6 players. Each player has a wing-nut launcher on the rim of a round arena. It sweeps back and forth; tap to fire a harpoon arrow, lead your shot, and reel DD's home. DD's are worth 1, 2, 3 or 5 points, and power-ups give triple shot (5s) or no reload (4s).

## Play

- **Online:** one person taps *Create online game* and shares the 4-letter room code (or the link). Friends join from their own phones. The host can fill empty seats with CPU players.
- **On one device:** *Play on this device*, up to 6 seats, each Player / CPU / Off.

## How it's built

- `public/index.html`: the game client (menus, rendering, input).
- `public/sim.js`: the game rules, shared by the browser (local play) and the server (online play).
- `server.js`: serves `public/` and runs game rooms over WebSockets at `/ws`. The server owns the game state and sends snapshots 30 times a second.
- `minews.js`: a small built-in WebSocket implementation, so there are no npm dependencies.

Run locally with `npm start` (port 3000).

## Hosting

Render web service `austins-fantasy-dds-live` (Node, `npm start`). Pushing to `main` redeploys it. The older static site `austins-fantasy-dds` serves the same page and connects to the live server for online games.

# Offline Scout

Scouting for FIRST robotics that **works with zero internet**. Install it once, then scout
in airplane mode. Every tap is saved on the phone straight away.

Milestone 1: FTC **BIOBUZZ** (2026–27) match scouting. FRC comes next season. Games are
JSON config files, not code.

**Live app:** https://dhirhpatel-droid.github.io/offline-scout/

## Using it

1. Open the link once with internet, then **Add to Home Screen** (Safari: Share → Add to
   Home Screen; Chrome: ⋮ → Install app / Add to Home screen).
2. Open it from the home screen from then on, with or without internet.
3. Home → set the event and your name once → **Scout a match**.
4. Pre: match #, team #, alliance. Then Auto → Teleop → End → Post with the big buttons.
   Minus is undo. **Save match**, then **Scout match N+1** in one tap.

> On iPhone, the home-screen app and the Safari tab keep **separate** storage. Pick one
> (the home-screen app) and always use it.

## Running it on a computer

No install, no build step. You need Python 3 (already on Macs).

```bash
npm start            # = python3 scripts/serve.py → http://localhost:8000
npm test             # unit tests (scoring, configs, entries)
npm run test:offline # real offline test in headless Chrome
```

## How it fits together

```
index.html               the one page; js/app.js draws every screen into it
manifest.webmanifest     makes it installable (name, icons, colours, portrait)
sw.js                    service worker: caches every file → works offline
css/tokens.css           all colours, sizes, fonts (dark + light themes)
css/app.css              layout and components
fonts/                   Archivo, self-hosted so it works offline (OFL licence)
js/app.js                start-up: theme, service worker, #hash router
js/db.js                 IndexedDB: saved matches, the current draft, settings
js/config.js             loads + validates game configs, finds fields by role
js/scoring.js            estimated points from a config + values (pure function)
js/entries.js            creating entries, summaries, next-match carry-over
js/fields.js             turns a config field into a widget (counter, Yes/No…)
js/ui.js                 small helpers: h() element builder, icons, dialog
js/screens/*.js          home, match, saved, settings
configs/                 one JSON per game + index.json listing them
tests/                   node --test unit tests
scripts/                 dev server, offline test, icon generator
docs/data-format.md      config and entry formats
```

**Why no framework?** The app is small, it must load offline from a cache, and every
line should be explainable. A 20-line `h()` helper (`js/ui.js`) does the job a framework
would.

**Why a service worker?** A normal web page asks the server for its files every time; with
no internet that fails. `sw.js` saves every file on the first visit and answers from that
copy afterwards.

**Why IndexedDB?** It holds real objects and far more than `localStorage`, and it's what
installed web apps are meant to use. The match in progress is a *draft* saved on every
tap, so a dead battery or closed tab loses nothing.

## Shipping an update

Change files → bump `VERSION` in `sw.js` → commit and push. Phones pick up the new
version next time they open the app with internet, and use it from the launch after.
If you add a file, add it to `APP_FILES` in `sw.js` too.

## Adding a game

See [docs/data-format.md](docs/data-format.md).

# 67 Arcade

A little collection of games that installs to your phone's home screen (it's a Progressive Web App). Opening the app shows a home screen of games; tap one to play, and use the ← button to get back.

## Games

### Stacky (`stacky/`)

**How to play:** a block slides back and forth. Tap to drop it. Whatever hangs off the edge gets sliced off, so the tower gets narrower. Miss completely and it's game over. Line a block up perfectly to start a combo; after 3 perfects in a row, your blocks start growing back.

## Put it on your phone

1. In this repo on GitHub, go to **Settings → Pages**.
2. Under **Build and deployment**, set **Source** to *Deploy from a branch*, pick the branch, folder `/ (root)`, and **Save**.
3. Wait a minute, then open `https://<your-username>.github.io/mobile-stuff/` on your phone.
4. Add it to your home screen:
   - **iPhone (Safari):** Share button → **Add to Home Screen**
   - **Android (Chrome):** ⋮ menu → **Install app** / **Add to Home screen**

It opens full-screen like a regular app and works offline after the first load.

## Running it locally

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open http://localhost:8000.

## Adding a game

1. Put it in its own folder, e.g. `newgame/index.html`.
2. Add a tile for it in the grid in the top-level `index.html`.
3. Add its files to `FILES` in `sw.js` so it works offline.

## Updating

After changing any file, bump `CACHE` in `sw.js` (e.g. `arcade-v3`) so installed copies pick up the new version.

# Chess Castles

**Learn · Play · Conquer** — the website at [chesscastles.com](https://chesscastles.com).

Everything chess in one place (online play, puzzles, analysis, live games, tournaments, books, friends and
leaderboards), plus:

1. **FIDE-rated opponents**: computer opponents that play in the style of players at each FIDE rating, from 1000 to 2800.
2. **A 5.4 million game database** beside every review.
3. **An AI opening trainer** built from the moves players at your level really play.
4. **Game Insights** from your chess.com and Lichess games, with a weekly study plan.
5. **Chess Guru**, an AI coach in English, Hindi and Marathi.

Chess Castles is not affiliated with or endorsed by FIDE, Lichess or chess.com.

## Stack

- SvelteKit 2 and Svelte 5 (TypeScript, Vite), built as a single-page app and served by a Cloudflare Worker
  (`wrangler.jsonc`).
- Board: [chessground](https://github.com/lichess-org/chessground); rules: [chessops](https://github.com/niklasf/chessops).
- Engine: Stockfish 19 (WebAssembly, in a Web Worker; `static/engine/` is copied from the `stockfish` package on install).
- Human-like play: [Maia-3](https://github.com/CSSLab/maia3) with ONNX Runtime Web, in a Web Worker (`static/maia-worker.js`).
- Opening book and game database: shards served by separate Workers (`src/lib/book/book.ts`, `src/lib/games/gamesDb.ts`),
  built from over-the-board games from [CaissaBase](https://caissabase.co.uk).
- Accounts: sign-in with Lichess (OAuth with PKCE), exchanged for a Firebase login.
- Players, friends, plans, analytics and the admin page talk to Chess Castles' API worker (not in this repository).
- Lichess API for online play, broadcasts, arenas and puzzles.

## Run it

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run check      # types
npm test           # unit tests
npm run build      # static site in build/
```

Data files are not in this repository (they are built from public sources by the scripts in `scripts/`):
`static/data/` (FIDE rating lists, puzzles), `static/books/` (public-domain books), `static/maia/` (the Maia-3
model, from the [Maia Chess platform](https://github.com/CSSLab/maia-platform-frontend)) and `static/ort/`
(ONNX Runtime Web). Without them the matching features show nothing.

## Licence

Chess Castles' website is free software under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later**
([LICENSE](LICENSE)). It builds on:

- chessground and chessops (GPL-3.0-or-later), Stockfish (GPL-3.0), Maia-3 (AGPL-3.0), the Maia Chess platform
  worker (GPL-3.0), ONNX Runtime Web (MIT), Svelte and SvelteKit (MIT), Firebase (Apache-2.0);
- the cburnett chess pieces by Colin M.L. Burnett (GPL);
- Lichess's chess-openings names and puzzle database (CC0);
- public-domain books from Project Gutenberg and Wikisource.

The names and logos “Chess Castles” and the Chess Castles crest are not covered by the licence: please don't use them
for another site or app.

## Thank you

To [Lichess](https://lichess.org), the free and open-source chess server, for its open API
([support Lichess](https://lichess.org/patron)); to the Stockfish, Maia and CaissaBase teams; and to everyone who
builds free chess software.

# The hidden family trees in your blood

Slides for a short talk by Dr Jiadong Mao (University of Melbourne) at the prize-giving of the University of Melbourne School Mathematics Competition, 17 October 2026. The talk is for secondary-school students, teachers and parents.

The talk asks how we can work out the family tree of blood cells that nobody watched dividing. Inherited DNA "typos" act as clues, and maths helps turn those clues into explanations we can test.

## View the slides

**[View the slides online](https://jiadongm.github.io/UniMelbMathsCompetition2026_PrizeGiving/slides.html)**

Or download `slides.html` and open it in a browser. It is self-contained, so it works offline.

- Arrow keys or the space bar move between slides and reveal steps.
- Press `S` to open the speaker view with notes.
- Press `F` for full screen.

## Rebuild

You need [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and Python 3.

```bash
python3 scripts/make_figures.py   # redraw the SVG figures in figs/
quarto render slides.qmd          # rebuild slides.html
```

`scripts/check_slides.cjs` is an optional layout check. It needs Node.js, Playwright and Google Chrome. It saves a screenshot of every slide to `qa/` and reports any content that runs off a slide.

## Files

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `slides.qmd` | Slide source and speaker notes (Quarto reveal.js) |
| `styles.css` | Deck styling |
| `figs/` | Figures. The SVGs are drawn by `scripts/make_figures.py` |
| `scripts/` | Figure generator and layout check |
| `AGENTS.md` | Talk plan, plain-language rules and working notes |

## Outline

1. Who is your closest relative? A human family tree
2. Your blood also has a family tree
3. From one cell to a whole family: DNA typos as clues
4. Puzzle: who are the closest relatives?
5. How many family trees are possible?
6. What do we care about family trees? Younger and older blood
7. Why it matters
8. An evolutionary game: luck and fitness
9. Who to talk to: Melbourne Integrative Genomics

## Notes and sources

The diagrams and counts are simplified illustrations, not real data. The evolutionary-game chart shows 20 runs of a simple computer model with a fixed random seed.

- Mitchell et al., [Clonal dynamics of haematopoiesis across the human lifespan](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04786-y), *Nature* 2022
- Jaiswal et al., [Age-related clonal hematopoiesis associated with adverse outcomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25426837/), *New England Journal of Medicine* 2014
- Felsenstein, The number of evolutionary trees, *Systematic Zoology* 1978

accipiter117/Spice-Raiders.readme:
# Arrakis Wars

A turn-based desert strategy game for phones, inspired by Dune: Spice Wars. Three powers (House Atreides, House Harkonnen and the Fremen) fight over twenty regions of Arrakis for spice, villages and the Emperor's favour. You lead one; the computer runs the other two.

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules) with no build step, so it runs straight from GitHub Pages. Best played on a phone held sideways.

## Playing it
- **On GitHub Pages:** Settings, then Pages, then "Deploy from a branch" and pick the branch and `/ (root)`.
- **Locally:** run `python3 -m http.server` in this folder and open http://localhost:8000.
- The game saves itself after every move. "How to play" is on the title screen and in the in-game menu.

## How the code is laid out
- `js/data/` the map, factions, units, balance rules and art slots. Retune the game here.
- `js/engine/` the rules, with no screen code. `applyAction(state, action)` is the only way to change a game, and games are reproducible from their seed.
- `js/ai/` the computer players (rules-based, same actions as the player) and the AI-vs-AI simulator.
- `js/ui/` the browser interface.
- `test/` run with `npm test` (Node 18 or newer), including 200 AI-vs-AI games.
- `tools/` `npm run sim` prints win rates by faction; `npm run assets` refreshes the art list below.

## Balance (computer vs computer)
Over 900 games: Atreides about 26%, Harkonnen about 38%, Fremen about 34%; median game 42 turns. Check again with `npm run sim` after any change to `js/data/`.

## Art
Every image goes through a named slot in `js/data/assets.js`. To add or replace art, save the file into `assets/` with the name listed below; if it is missing, the game shows the fallback instead. Most current art is reused from the My Arrakis project.

commits.msg:
Replace browser confirm() pop-ups with an in-game dialog

Starting a new game over a save, and abandoning a game, used the
browser's confirm() pop-up. Some hosts (including the Claude artifact
viewer, used for a quick play link) silently answer "no" to it, which
would make both actions impossible. Both now use an in-game "Are you
sure?" dialog in the game's own style. Checked in Playwright: new game
over a save and abandon both work, and no native dialog appears.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

M4: how-to-play guide, save and continue polish, art list in README

How to play
- New guide (js/ui/howto.js) in collapsible sections: the goal, your turn,
  land and villages, spice/worms/tax, battles, the factions, tips.
- Every number in it is read from the data files, so it stays correct
  after retuning.
- Shown automatically before your first game (with a Start button), and
  available from the title screen and the in-game menu.

Save and continue
- Save format version bumped to 2: saves f

Art and styling from My Arrakis

Matthew asked to reuse the game art and visual style of his My Arrakis
project where possible. All reused art is his own (commissioned for My
Arrakis), resized for phone use; 436 KB in total.

Art now in /assets (all through js/data/assets.js slots):
- Title painting on the start screen and portrait prompt, victory
  painting on the win screen.
- Faction tokens as emblems and as trooper counters on the map (the stack
  count sits inside the token, like the board

M3 rules: Spice Wars style land, desert and faction balance

Matthew asked for 35 to 50 turn games and for empty spice fields and the
Fremen to work as they do in Dune: Spice Wars. Changes, all in data where
possible:

How land works now (as in Spice Wars)
- Every owned region defends itself. Spice fields and passes get a small
  garrison, so land is never free to walk into; it must be attacked.
- Deep desert cannot be owned by anyone. Harvesters can still be sent onto
  its spice from a neighbo

M2: playable phone UI (faction pick, map, panel, combat cards, end screens)

Adds the browser game on top of the M1 engine, laid out for a phone held
sideways.

- Start screen: pick Atreides, Harkonnen or Fremen; "Continue" appears when
  an autosave exists.
- Top bar: Solari, Spice, Manpower, Authority, Hegemony (with per-turn
  change), turn number and spice tax countdown.
- Map (70% width, SVG): terrain colours, owner tints, fog of war, villages,
  spice field dots, harvesters and unit stacks

M1: rules engine, data files, AI and tests (no UI yet)

Arrakis Wars v1 foundation, built as plain ES modules with no build step so
it can run straight from GitHub Pages later.

Data (js/data/), all tunable without touching rules:
- map.js: 20 hex-style regions (rock / sand / deep desert), villages, spice
  field values 0 to 3, neighbours and SVG outlines. Capitals at Arrakeen,
  Carthag and Sietch Tabr, plus a starting spice field for each faction.
- factions.js: Atreides (cheaper annexing, +1

mutaaf/openaero-dfw.desc: OpenAero DFW — real-world Dallas–Fort Worth flight sim in the browser, built and groomed by autonomous agents. Live at mutaafaziz.com/openaero
mutaaf/openaero-dfw.readme:
# OpenAero DFW

A 6-DOF flight simulator in the browser, flown over real satellite imagery of the
Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. Land a 737 on DFW 35C, take an F-16 past Reunion Tower, or
shoot the approach into Love Field in a Cessna. No install, no account.

**Play:** https://mutaafaziz.com/openaero/

## Built and run by agents

This repo is developed by three scheduled cloud agents (Claude Code routines), with CI as
the gate and Cloudflare deploying `main` on every merge:

| Agent | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Scout** | Plays the current build, researches real-world references, grooms `docs/backlog/` |
| **Builder** | Ships the top ready ticket test-first, merges on green CI, verifies production |
| **Keeper** | Dependencies, performance budget, refactoring, tuning the agents' own prompts |

Their instructions are versioned in [`agents/prompts/`](agents/prompts/). The operating
manual for agents and humans alike is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). What shipped is in
[`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](docs/CHANGELOG.md); what's next is in [`docs/backlog/`](docs/backlog/).

### Controlling the agents

- **Pause / steer:** edit [`agents/control.json`](agents/control.json) (GitHub web or
  mobile is fine). `"paused": true` stops all three; per-agent `enabled`, a free-text
  `focus` that outranks the agents' own ideas, and caps like `max_merges_per_day`.
- **Frequency:** each agent's schedule lives at https://claude.ai/code/routines.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR on GitHub; Cloudflare redeploys `main`.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173/openaero/
npm run check    # the gate CI runs: backlog validator, unit tests, build, e2e
```

Controls: W/S pitch, A/D roll, Q/E rudder, Shift/Ctrl throttle, G gear, F flaps,
B brakes, C camera, Z autopilot, M mouse-yoke.

Satellite imagery © Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Built with three.js and Vite.

and crosswinds need a crab. Fog density follows visibility, a cloud deck

jarvis-jhk/spacehog.desc: Operation Spacehog (Free Lunch Design, 2000) natively on Linux, Windows and the Steam Deck: a C port verified tick by tick against the original DOS game. Needs the freeware's original data.
jarvis-jhk/spacehog.readme:
# Operation Spacehog — native port

A native C port of **Operation Spacehog 1.01** (Free Lunch Design, 2000, DOS freeware) for
Linux and Windows, rebuilt from a decompilation of the original `SH.EXE`. It plays like
the original — same logic, timing, graphics and sound — with modern extras: a resizable
window, fullscreen, and gamepads for both players.

The game data is **not** included. You need the original freeware release
(`SPACEHOG.DAT`, `SHLEV.DAT`, `SHBGS.DAT`, `SHSND.DAT`), for example from the
[DOS Games Archive](https://www.dosgamesarchive.com/download/operation-spacehog):
unpack its zip anywhere.

What comes next (4 players, mods, leaderboards): [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Download

- **Warpzone launcher** ([warpzone.virtualtabletop.io](https://warpzone.virtualtabletop.io)):
  installs and updates the game, finds the original data in your Downloads folder and
  hands it to the game, and adds it to Steam (Steam Deck included).
- Or by hand from the [releases](https://github.com/jarvis-jhk/spacehog/releases):
  `spacehog-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (also for the Steam Deck) or
  `spacehog-windows-x86_64.zip`. Copy the four `.DAT` files into the `spacehog` folder
  next to the program, or point it at them with `--data`.

## Playing

    spacehog --data /path/to/spacehog

Options: `--fullscreen` (Alt+Enter toggles), `--scale N`, `--square-pixels` (no 4:3
correction), `--save-dir DIR` (where `SPACEHOG.SAV` goes; default: the data directory, or the per-user app data directory if that is read-only or the data came from the launcher), `--help` for the rest. The data directory is,
in this order: `--data`, `$SPACEHOG_DATA`, `$WARPZONE_DATA_GAME` (set by the Warpzone
launcher), the current directory, `data/`, the program's own directory. The
original command line switches (`/nosound`, `/r_scores`, `/r_keys`, ...) still work.

Music: the original FM music (Allegro's Adlib/OPL driver on an emulated OPL3, as with a
Sound Blaster) is the default. Optionally the music can be played through a General MIDI
SoundFont instead, as with a wavetable card: `--music gm` (uses the first `*.sf2` next to
the game data, e.g. the free GeneralUser GS) or `--soundfont FILE`. The same can be set
permanently in `spacehog.ini` in the save directory:

    music = gm
    soundfont = GeneralUser-GS.sf2

Controls are the original ones (configurable in the options menu). Gamepads: choose
"Gamepad" for a player in the options. With two pads connected both players can use one;
pads can be plugged in at any time. A = fire / select, B = buy power-up, X = special,
Y = Enter (e.g. confirm quitting), Start = pause (and Space in menus), Back = Esc.
High score names can be entered with the pad: up/down pick a letter, A types it,
B deletes, Y finishes. Everything works without a keyboard.

## Online co-op (Warpzone)

Two players on two machines play together over [Warpzone](https://warpzone.virtualtabletop.io)
rooms (direct connection with relay fallback, encrypted):

    spacehog --warpzone-host                 # player 1: opens a room, shows its code
    spacehog --warpzone-code K7QM3X          # player 2: joins with that code
    spacehog --warpzone-join ROOM            # ... or by room id (the launcher's "Join")
    spacehog warpzone://join/...             # ... or with an invite link

The host is player 1 and runs the menus (choose 2 players as usual); the guest plays
player 2 with its usual player-1 keys or its gamepad. The host's settings, controls and
high scores are used (the guest's own `SPACEHOG.SAV` stays untouched). `--warpzone-private`
opens an unlisted room (code or invite link only), `--net-delay N` sets the input delay
(frames of 1/70 s; by default it follows the ping). The Warpzone identity is the launcher's; on a machine without
one, add `--warpzone-name NAME` once.

Both machines run the same deterministic game in lockstep: every input is applied on both
at the same emulated time, so nothing but the input crosses the network. A checksum of the
whole game state is compared twice a second ("out of sync" would show if they ever
differed). If the partner leaves, the game goes on with the remaining player.
`--record FILE` on either side writes the session as an ordinary replay.

## Building

Needs CMake ≥ 3.20, a C11 compiler and SDL 3 (linked statically).

    cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/sdl3
    cmake --build build

Online co-op needs the Warpzone client library: `scripts/fetch-warpzone.sh linux DIR`
downloads the pinned libwarpzone release (checksum-verified) and prints its folder; pass
it as `-DWARPZONE_DIR=...`. Without it the game builds without online play.

Release archives are built by CI (`scripts/ci-build.sh`, on ubuntu-22.04 so the Linux
binary runs with glibc 2.35 or newer); `scripts/package.sh` builds them locally into `dist/`.
`tools/fetch.sh` and `tools/build-sdl3*.sh` set up a self-contained toolchain in `tools/`
(static SDL3 for Linux, llvm-mingw + SDL3 for Windows; toolchain file
`cmake/mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake`). Always `source tools/env.sh` first.

## How it was made / verification

- `re/`: reverse-engineering pipeline (UPX 0.40 unpacker, datafile extractor, Ghidra
  scripts with recovered symbols and types). See `PLAN.md` for the full story.
- `src/compat/`: the subset of Allegro 3.11 the game uses, on SDL3 (graphics, palette,
  timers on a virtual 1193181 Hz clock, keyboard/gamepads, sample mixer, Allegro's MIDI
  player driving an emulated OPL3).
- `src/game/`: the translated game code.
- `re/refemu/`: a differential tester. It runs the original DOS code in an emulator next to
  the port and compares the complete game state and every drawing/sound call at every game
  tick. Full playthroughs and randomized 1/2-player sessions match exactly.
- Input recording/replay (`--record`, `--replay`) is deterministic.
- Player input: the game reads every player's keys, pad and mouse only through
  `player_input(p)` (`src/game/pinput.c`); `--input-latch` samples it once per ti

cavemancompanyllc/trogly.desc: Talk to your RAID: Shadow Legends account in Claude Code. Fan project, not affiliated with Plarium.
cavemancompanyllc/trogly.readme:
# Trogly

Talk to your RAID: Shadow Legends account in [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

"What gear is on Thor Faehammer?" "Which of my Epics are fastest?" "How fast would Thor be with my spare Speed boots?" Trogly reads
your account from the running game (read-only; it never changes anything in game) and answers in conversation.

Trogly is a fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Plarium. RAID: Shadow Legends is a trademark of
Plarium Global Ltd.

## What you need

- Windows, with RAID installed and logged in on the same PC
- [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) on a Claude Pro or Max plan (no API key needed)
- Python 3.11 or newer
- The Trogly Agent (`Trogly.Agent.exe`), installed yourself. Keep it as new as the plugins: an older Agent answers
  newer requests with an error saying so

## Set up

1. Make an instance folder and copy `instance-template/` into it, for example `D:\Trogly`.
2. Install the MCP dependency: `python -m pip install "mcp>=1.28,<2.0.0"`.
3. In that folder, start Claude Code and run:

   ```text
   claude plugin marketplace add cavemancompanyllc/trogly
   claude plugin install trogly-core@trogly --scope project
   claude plugin install trogly-artifacts@trogly --scope project
   ```

4. Open RAID, then ask Trogly to refresh your account. The first time, Trogly asks where you installed
   `Trogly.Agent.exe` and remembers it.

## Plugins

| Plugin | What it adds |
| --- | --- |
| `trogly-core` | Account access (refresh, search champions and artifacts, one champion's gear and calculated stats, "what if they wore this" stats) and memory (goals, saved teams, saved gear loadouts, notes, and "what changed since..." history) |

| `trogly-artifacts` | Gear advice: "Which artifacts should I put on Thor? At least 200 speed, then max attack." Finds the best loadout from your own artifacts (vault and the champion's own gear by default; borrowing from other champions only if you allow it), with exact stats. Installs `trogly-core` too |

More are planned: champion and dungeon knowledge, dungeon teams, and arena teams.

## Privacy

Your account data, history, and plans stay in your instance folder (`data/`). Trogly sends nothing anywhere except your normal Claude
conversation.

## Known limits

- Champion stats are calculated by Trogly and not yet verified against the in-game screen.
- If you're logged in on your phone, the PC client gets signed out and its data stops updating.
- If Trogly's tools don't show up after you fix a setup problem, Claude Code may have cached the failure: remove the
  `plugin:trogly-core:trogly` entry from `~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json` and restart Claude Code.

AndreyBelyy/dunecraft-conquer.desc: Browser RTS mash-up of Command & Conquer, Dune 2000 and StarCraft: 9 factions, multiplayer, WebGL. Converters build the art from your own game copies; no game files included.
AndreyBelyy/dunecraft-conquer.readme:
# DuneCraft & Conquer

[![made with universal-modder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder/main/docs/media/made-with-dark.svg)](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder)

![GDI, Zerg and Protoss clash in front of a GDI base, with the real C&C sidebar](docs/screenshots/battle.jpg)

A browser real-time strategy game that mashes up the classics the owner has on disk:
**Command & Conquer** (Tiberian Dawn and Red Alert), **Dune 2000** and **StarCraft: Brood War**. Nine
factions, three from each game, fight over spice, Tiberium and minerals on Arrakis, in the browser,
against the computer or each other.

Built with the [universal-modder](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder) toolkit, following its
`mod-any-game` loop and the `mashup-mods` skill's "reimplement, then fuse" route. The game code is new;
every sprite and sound is **converted on your machine from your own copies of the games**. None of the
games' files are in this repository, and none may be published with it.


## Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Atreides base on Arrakis: a Harkonnen column comes over the dunes and a sandworm surfaces under it](docs/screenshots/dune.jpg) | ![Zerg defend their hive against a Terran push, with the real Zerg console](docs/screenshots/starcraft.jpg) |
| Dune 2000: the real sidebar, worm sign and a sandworm strike | StarCraft: the Zerg console with group wireframes |
| ![Three-way battle with the C&C sidebar](docs/screenshots/battle.jpg) | ![The title screen in Dune 2000 style](docs/screenshots/title.jpg) |
| Command & Conquer: GDI vs Zerg vs Protoss | Title screen in any of the four games' styles |

## What's in it
- **Nine factions**:
  - Command & Conquer: GDI, Nod, Soviets (Red Alert).
  - Dune 2000: Atreides, Harkonnen, Ordos.
  - StarCraft: Terran, Zerg, Protoss.

  Each has its own tech tree, harvesters, defences and special units (Tesla Coils, sonic tanks, stealth
  tanks, deviators, cloaked Dark Templar...). Ground, air and sea, with anti-air and detectors.
- **One economy**: harvesters gather spice (sand), Tiberium (rock; regrows, hurts infantry) and
  StarCraft mineral fields. Spice blooms burst out of the desert, a sandworm hunts on open sand, and
  sandstorms sweep across the map.
- **A Warcraft III-style neutral map**:
  - creep camps (feral Zerg, Fremen, C&C dinosaurs and visceroids, Red Alert's giant ants) that pay bounties and drop crates;
  - capturable neutral buildings: geysers, oil derricks, a healing Xel'Naga temple, a power generator, a Psi Disrupter, and a CHOAM mercenary starport that sells units from all nine factions;
  - veteran ranks for units that kill.
- **The games' own art, shown crisp**:
  - Sprites keep their original pixels. A "sharp pixel" shader keeps them crisp at any zoom, with only the pixel edges smoothed.
  - Dune 2000 uses the game's own 16-bit art.
  - Team colours come from each game's own remap ranges and are tinted on the GPU, so any player can be any colour.
  - No AI upscaling: we tried it, and it invented detail. An optional xBRZ "smoothed" atlas exists for comparison.
- **The games' own sounds**:
  - EVA for GDI and Nod, Red Alert's EVA and Russian voices for the Soviets, per-house voices for the Dune factions.
  - Every StarCraft unit speaks its own lines.
- **VFX**: explosions from all three games, scorch marks, smoke and fire on damaged buildings, dust trails,
  Tesla lightning, screen shake, sandstorm overlay, floating bounty text.
- **Multiplayer**:
  - A Node.js server runs the authoritative simulation at 15 ticks/s and sends each player only what their units can see; fog of war is enforced on the server.
  - The lobby has rooms, chat, AI seats, teams, colours, map style and size.
  - A dropped player can reconnect; an AI holds their seat meanwhile.
- **Offline skirmish**: the same simulation runs in a Web Worker in the page, so single-player needs no server.
- **Computer opponents**:
  - Four levels: easy, normal, hard, brutal.
  - Levels can be changed during an offline game from the Esc menu.
  - They creep camps, capture neutrals and hire mercenaries.
- **Balance and fair maps**:
  - Maps are rotationally symmetric.
  - Balance is measured with headless duels and AI-vs-AI round robins; see `game/docs/BALANCE.md`.
- **How to play** screen (title screen and F1 in game) and a starter checklist ("field orders").
- **Each game's own interface**: the real C&C / Red Alert sidebars, Dune 2000 sidebar and StarCraft consoles, the games' cursors, and a title screen in the style of any of the four games (arrows at the bottom to switch). Built from your own copies by `tools/assets/ui.py` (part of `tools/build_all.sh`).

## Quick start
You need Node.js 20+, Python 3.10+ with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and your own copies of the games
(a folder with the C&C First Decade disc image and StarCraft; Dune 2000 from an installed copy via `D2K_DIR`).

```bash
D2K_DIR=/path/to/Dune2000 sh tools/build_all.sh ../to_mode     # converts everything into private/ and builds the atlas and sounds
cd game && npm install && npm start  # then open http://localhost:8080
```
Friends on your network open `http://<your-ip>:8080` and pick **Multiplayer**. Without converted assets the
game still runs, with placeholder shapes. Each converter has its own notes and re-run commands in
`tools/<game>/NOTES.md`.

## Controls
| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Select | Left click, drag a box, Shift to add, double-click for all of a type on screen |
| Move / attack / harvest | Right click (on ground / enemy / resource) |
| Attack-move | A, then left click |
| Stop / deploy MCV | S / D |
| Load a transport | Select units and right click your transport (APC, Chinook, Hovercraft, Dropship, Shuttle, Overlord), or select the transport and right click a unit |
| Unload | Select the transport: D unloads where it stands, Ctrl+right click unloads at that spot (StarCraft: the Unload All button) |
| Carryall | Select it and right click a vehicle to lif

# Volleyball Freizeitliga München · Redesign

A from-scratch redesign of [volleyball-freizeit.de](https://www.volleyball-freizeit.de/), the Munich recreational volleyball league site (run on dieLiga). This is a front-end prototype with realistic mock data and a working mock login.

## Stack

- **Vite + React 19 + TypeScript**, `HashRouter`
- **three.js**: the hero volleyball, drawn entirely in a GLSL shader (six panels, three strips each, stitched seams), tilts toward the cursor and "spikes" on click
- **GSAP**: ball drop and spike, count-ups, celebration bursts
- **Framer Motion**: page transitions, shared-layout indicators (nav, tabs, league picker), animated table re-ordering, list enter/exit
- **Canvas 2D** backdrop: a sports hall at night (breathing ceiling lamps, drifting dust, a perspective court and swaying net, an occasional serve arcing across). Reacts to pointer and scroll, pauses when the tab is hidden, honours `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Fonts: Big Shoulders Display (scoreboard headings), Figtree (body), IBM Plex Mono (labels)

## Pages

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/` | Hero, live results ticker, this week's fixtures (filter by league), season stats, league pyramid (promotion/relegation), training teaser, community news |
| `/live` | Live ticker: scoreboard cards per running game (set columns, current set, serve, set/match ball, point-by-point feed), recently finished games, countdown for games about to start |
| `/tabellen/:liga` | All 15 leagues (1, 2A–B, 3A–C, 4A–D, 5A–E). Standings with promotion/relegation zones, points bars, form; schedule with upcoming/results/all and team filter; hovering a team highlights its games |
| `/mannschaften`, `/mannschaften/:id` | Searchable team grid with tilt cards; team page with rank, set ratio, hall time, contact, games |
| `/termine` | Tournaments with free spots and "Interesse melden", league dates |
| `/community` | Spielerbörse and forum |
| `/infos` | FAQ, documents, contact |
| `/login` | Mock login (`demo` / `volley`, or tap "Demo-Zugang einsetzen"), password reset view |
| `/mein-team` | Logged-in area for Spartak Au: next match countdown, next training RSVP, attendance rings, mini table; **Training** (RSVP per session with quorum of 6, attendance matrix and trend); **Ergebnisse** (enter set scores with validation and live table impact, request a home-game move); **Live** (count your home game point by point from a phone; only for people with the „Ergebnisse“ right; when decided, the result goes into the table); **Kader & Rechte** (grant/revoke rights) |

`⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` opens a search palette for teams, leagues and pages. Light, dark and system themes.

## Data

`src/data/season.ts` builds a deterministic season: Liga 1 uses the real team names from the 2026/27 table, all other teams are invented. Matches are a double round robin; games before "now" get rally-by-rally simulated results (best of three, winner 2 points, 1:2 loser 1 point). Login state, entered results and RSVPs are kept in `localStorage`.

## Live ticker

`src/live/` holds the live layer. A game is stored as its list of rallies; score, sets, serve and feed are derived (`engine.ts`), so undo is just dropping the last rally. `transport.ts` defines a `LiveTransport` interface; the demo implementation shares games between tabs with `localStorage` + `BroadcastChannel`. A real backend (websocket, Supabase realtime) implements the same interface and must enforce the „Ergebnisse“ right server-side. Three games from other leagues are simulated from a seed and a shared start time, so every tab shows the same score; they loop every 40 minutes.

## Backend

With `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` set (see `.env.example`), the site loads leagues, teams and games from Supabase, uses real accounts (sign-up, password reset, invite codes) and syncs the live ticker over Supabase realtime. Rights are enforced with row-level security. Without the keys it stays the demo above. Setup, rights and tests: [`supabase/README.md`](supabase/README.md).

## Scripts

```bash
npm install
npm run dev              # local dev server
npm run build            # type-check + production build to dist/
npm run build:artifact   # single-file build used for the hosted preview
npm run test:db          # migrations + seed + RLS tests on a throwaway Postgres
npm run db:seed          # regenerate supabase/seed.sql from src/data/season.ts
```

# Tesla Bird A Flappy-Bird-style pixel-art game: fly the Roadster through gaps between Starship rocket pillars. Built with vanilla JavaScript and a single ``, with no runtime dependencies and no framework. It grew out of my [vanilla Flappy Bird on CodePen][codepen-original]. The idea comes from the new Tesla Roadster's thruster-powered flight at its [unveiling on October 16, 2026][roadster-cnbc]. In the game, every boost fires smoke from the wheels, and the car tilts as it climbs and falls.

▶ Play in your browser

## Play Play online at in a desktop browser. To play offline, open `index.html` from a copy of this repository. No build step is needed: the built files are committed. See [Run locally](#run-locally) to serve it over HTTP or to change the code. ## Controls | Action | Mouse | Keyboard | | --- | --- | --- | | Start, then boost | Left click | Space, Arrow Up or W | | Restart after a crash | Click the play button | Space | | Switch theme | NIGHT / DAWN / DAY on the start screen | Tab to the switch, then Enter | The first click or Space on the start screen starts the run and counts as the first boost. ## How to play - Gravity pulls the car down. Each boost sends it up again. - Pass between the rocket pillars. Each pair you pass scores 1 point. - The run ends if the car touches a pillar's hull, the top of the screen or the bottom of the screen. The fins on the noses and engines are decoration, so they do not count as a hit. **Charge** replaces the medals of the original game: | Score | Charge | | ---: | ---: | | 0–9 | 0% | | 10–19 | 25% | | 20–29 | 50% | | 30–39 | 75% | | 40+ | 100% (FULL) | ## Telemetry During a run, a telemetry strip along the bottom of the screen shows the state of the flight. ![Telemetry strip during a run: mission clock T+00:00:26, run 07, progress timeline past 25%, score gauge at 16 points and altitude gauge at 182 m](docs/telemetry.png) | Item | Shows | | --- | --- | | Mission clock | Time alive in the current run, as `T+HH:MM:SS`. | | Run counter | `TESLA BIRD · RUN NN`. It counts every run you start. | | Progress timeline | Nodes for LIFTOFF, 25%, 50%, 75% and FULL (scores 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40). The red tick marks your current score. | | SCORE gauge | Points in this run. The arc fills as you get closer to the next charge level. | | ALTITUDE gauge | Height of the car above the bottom of the screen, in metres (1 game pixel = 1 m). | The game-over screen shows three gauges (CHARGE, SCORE and BEST), the full timeline with a red CRASH marker at your score, and the final mission clock. ## Themes | Theme | Background | How to get it | | --- | --- | --- | | `night` | Starbase at night | NIGHT on the start screen | | `dawn` | Starbase at dawn | DAWN on the start screen | | `day` | Starbase in daylight | DAY on the start screen | When you first open the game, it uses your browser's light or dark setting (light gives `day`, dark gives `night`). When you select an option on the switch, the game remembers that choice. A `?theme=` value in the URL overrides both. To add a theme, add an entry (background image, dim colour, dim opacity) to `THEMES` in [`config.js`](flappy-assets/script/config.js). ## Screen sizes The game uses a resolution of 640×360 game pixels. It draws them at 3× (1920×1080) with nearest-neighbour scaling, so the pixel art stays sharp. If the window is not 16:9, the playfield grows to fill it, so there are no black bars: - A taller window shows more sky above and below the gaps. - A wider window shows more pillars at the same time. The game is made for desktop browsers. It does not support touch input. ## Run locally You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 18 or later for the tests and the build. The game does not need Node.js to run. ```sh python3 -m http.server 4173 ``` Then open . Any static file server works. | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `npm test` | Runs the unit tests with the built-in `node --test` runner. | | `npm run build` | Bundles the scripts and the stylesheet into content-hashed files and updates the references in `index.html`. | | `npm run check` | Runs the tests, then the build. | If you change a file in `flappy-assets/script/` or `flappy-assets/style/`, run `npm run build`. `index.html` loads the built files, not the source files. ### URL parameters | Parameter | Effect | | --- | --- | | `?theme=night`, `dawn` or `day` | Uses this theme and ignores the saved choice. | | `?debug=true` | Shows the hitboxes. If the car hits a pillar, the run continues, but that pillar does not score. The best score is not saved. The top and bottom of the screen still end the run. The **Debug** checkbox in the top-left corner sets this parameter. | ## Configuration [`app.js`](flappy-assets/script/app.js) starts the game: ```js FlappyBird('container', { difficulty: 'normal', // easy | normal | hard theme: 'day' // optional; leave it out to use the saved or browser choice }); ``` ### Difficulty All values are in game pixels. | Level | Pillar spacing | Gap height | Largest change in gap position | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `easy` | 200 | 96 | 50 | | `normal` | 170 | 80 | 60 | | `hard` | 145 | 70 | 72 | Physics and the other tuning values (speed, gravity, boost strength, hitbox) are in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` in [`config.js`](flappy-assets/script/config.js). ## Project structure ```text index.html Page; loads the built bundle flappy-assets/ script/ app.js Entry point: reads URL parameters, starts the game flappy.js Game loop, canvas rendering, HUD, menus,

TheoLopez/Tesla-Roadster-.readme:
# Roadster: Thrust City

Simulador web en tercera persona: conduce un superdeportivo eléctrico con **paquete de propulsores** por una ciudad y salta sobre tráfico, arroyos, huecos y peatones. Seis niveles con dificultad creciente, de día, al atardecer y de noche.

> Juego de fans, sin afiliación oficial con ninguna marca.

## Jugar en local

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # servidor de desarrollo
npm run build    # genera dist/ listo para publicar
npm run preview  # sirve dist/
```

Funciona en cualquier navegador moderno con WebGL2. No hay archivos binarios: modelos, texturas, efectos de sonido y música se generan por código al cargar.

## Controles

| Acción | Teclado | Mando |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Acelerar | `W` / `↑` | RT |
| Frenar / reversa | `S` / `↓` | LT |
| Girar | `A` `D` / `←` `→` | Stick izquierdo |
| Saltar (mantener = flotar) | `Espacio` | A |
| Propulsor trasero (boost) | `Shift` | X / RB |
| Cambiar cámara | `C` | — |
| Volver al checkpoint | `R` | — |
| Silenciar | `M` | — |
| Pausa | `Esc` / `P` | Start |

En pantallas táctiles aparecen botones en pantalla.

## Mecánicas

- **Colores**: Blanco Perla (por defecto), Rojo Multicapa, Negro, Azul y Plata.
- **Aceleración real**: 0-100 km/h en ~1,9 s, 187 km/h de velocidad máxima y hasta ~280 km/h con el propulsor trasero.
- **Propulsores de gas frío**: `Espacio` lanza el coche; si lo mantienes en el aire, los propulsores de sustentación lo hacen flotar hasta ~5 m. Todo consume la barra de **PROPULSORES**, que se recarga sobre el asfalto y con las **celdas de energía**.
- **Obstáculos**: barreras, conos (se pueden derribar), huecos y socavones, arroyos con puentes caídos, trancones, tráfico en ambos sentidos y cruzado, camiones altos, peatones cruzando y desfiles. Tocar a un peatón o a un vehículo, o caer a un hueco, te devuelve al último checkpoint con +5 s.
- **Puntuación**: celdas recogidas, *saltos limpios* sobre obstáculos, bono de tiempo y penalización por choques. Hasta 3 estrellas por nivel; el progreso se guarda en el navegador.

## Niveles

1. **Primer Arranque** (día): tutorial de aceleración, saltos y huecos.
2. **Hora Pico** (día): trancones, contravía y tráfico cruzado.
3. **Cruce Peatonal** (atardecer): festival con peatones por todas partes.
4. **El Arroyo** (atardecer): puentes caídos y socavones.
5. **Neón Nocturno** (noche): todo junto bajo luces de neón.
6. **Paquete SpaceX** (noche con lluvia): la prueba final, con un río de 62 m.

## Tecnología

- [three.js](https://threejs.org/) con renderizado físico (PBR), sombras dinámicas, mapas de entorno, bloom (UnrealBloomPass) y MSAA.
- Carrocería esculpida a partir de un superelipsoide guiado por curvas de perfil; ciudad procedural por bloques con geometría fusionada por material, culling por tramos y props instanciados.
- Web Audio API: motor eléctrico (zumbido, silbido del inversor), ruido de llantas y viento, siseo de propulsores, golpes, salpicaduras, y una banda sonora *synthwave* procedural distinta para cada ambiente.
- Calidad gráfica ajustable (Ultra/Alta/Media/Baja) desde *Ajustes*.

## Estructura

```
index.html         interfaz (menú, HUD, pantallas)
src/main.js        bucle de juego, estados, cámara, HUD
src/car.js         modelo del Roadster y física
src/city.js        generación de la ciudad (vías, edificios, arroyos, huecos)
src/obstacles.js   tráfico, peatones, barreras, conos, celdas de energía
src/levels.js      definición y trazado de niveles
src/environment.js cielo, iluminación y temas (día/atardecer/noche)
src/audio.js       motor de audio y música procedural
src/textures.js    texturas procedurales en canvas
src/fx.js          partículas y lluvia
```

## Publicar

El juego es un sitio estático (`dist/`), así que sirve cualquier hosting estático.

**Firebase Hosting** (configurado en `firebase.json`):

```bash
npx firebase-tools login
npx firebase-tools use --add      # elige o crea tu proyecto de Firebase
npm run deploy:firebase           # compila y publica en https://<proyecto>.web.app
```

**GitHub Pages**: el workflow `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` publica `dist/` al hacer push a `main` (o manualmente). Activa *Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions* en el repositorio.

thesigns/Reliq.desc: A treasure-hunting game for your daily walks.
thesigns/Reliq.readme:
# Reliq

A treasure-hunting game for your daily walks. You set up a **Vault** where your walks usually start, then head out. When you are at least 100 m from the Vault, search the ground. Most of the time you dig up junk, sometimes an ancient coin. Missions send you on longer walks to find the symbols of a tomb's key and then the tomb itself, with a unique artifact inside. Everything you find rides home in your backpack, and storing it in the Vault is a moment of its own.

The map is a fictional, hand-inked parchment laid over real GPS coordinates. There are no streets on it, only mountains, forests and plains, plus the areas you have already searched.

Reliq is a plain website (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, WebGL2, Web Audio) that can be installed as a PWA. It ships in English and Polish.

## How it plays

- **Search for treasure.** Each search marks a searched area with a radius of about 100 m. Nearby areas merge smoothly, like metaballs, and fade away after 6 hours. You can only search again outside every searched area and outside the Vault.
- **Fair play.** Searching is blocked when you move faster than 10 km/h (averaged over 20 s) or when the GPS error exceeds 50 m.
- **Finds.** Junk 65%, coin 35%. Coins are common, uncommon, rare or legendary (75/20/4/1%). All twelve are real historical coins, from a Roman nummus to Brutus's EID MAR aureus, modelled as low-poly 3D coins. Junk, ten kinds of it, drops in as a 3D model too, and is thrown away.
- **The backpack and the Vault.** Coins and artifacts go into your backpack. Walk back into the Vault's ring and they are stored: the treasure chest opens, the coins rain into it one by one and the artifact sinks in last. Nothing in the backpack is ever lost.
- **Missions.** One at a time, from the easiest of eight tiers (wood to diamond) to the hardest; the tier sets the walking distances. There are 24 so far, three per tier. A notebook page shows an ink sketch of the artifact and its lore. Each mission has four stages, each a walk of a set straight-line distance from where that stage began: three walks for the symbols of the tomb's key, then a longer one to the tomb. You can do them all in one go or spread them over the 7-day limit. Open the tomb's three-ring gate on site, by guessing the order of the symbols, to win the artifact. The next mission starts once that artifact is in the Vault.
- **The fence.** Sell coins from the Vault for money. Artifacts of missions you lost or abandoned turn up at the fence 7 days later, for a price.
- **The Vault journal.** Four tabs: the notebook with the missions, the coins, the artifacts and the fence.

The full rules are in [`docs/reliq-gdd.md`](docs/reliq-gdd.md) and the missions in [`docs/lista-misji.md`](docs/lista-misji.md) (both in Polish).

## Status

Playable, and being tested on test walks with a phone. See [`docs/implementation-plan.md`](docs/implementation-plan.md) (in Polish).

| Stage | Scope | State |
|-------|-------|-------|
| E1 | Look-and-feel prototype | done |
| E2 | Game logic, tests, save game | done |
| E3 | Real GPS, smoothing, compass, simulator | done (device testing pending) |
| E4 | Full map renderer: camera, tap tooltips, region names, scale, caching | done |
| E5 | Game flows: onboarding, vault journal, settings | done |
| E6 | Polish: splash, "ready to search" bell, ink particles, optional generative music | done |
| E7 | PWA: icons, manifest, offline service worker, install prompt | done |
| E8 | Performance, robustness (WebGL context loss), i18n checks; device testing pending | in progress |
| E9 | Tomb gates with a three-ring key, low-poly 3D artifacts | done |
| E10 | Missions, the artifacts, the fence; then the game menu, low-poly coins, the backpack and the deposit scene, mission tiers with all 24 artifacts, 3D junk | done |

A fresh install opens on the game menu. *Begin* leads to a short introduction (a letter and four pages of rules, also under *About*), then you stamp your vault where you stand and start walking.

## Running locally

There is no build step and there are no dependencies. Serve the folder with the bundled dev server, which turns off browser caching so edits show up on reload:

```sh
node scripts/serve.mjs 8137
# or: npm run serve
```

Use this server rather than a generic one such as `python -m http.server`: browsers may cache ES modules from those, and a reload can then run stale code.

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8137/>. On a desktop the game shows in a phone-sized frame.

Geolocation only works in a secure context. On `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` the game uses the built-in **GPS simulator** by default. Anywhere else it uses the real GPS, which requires HTTPS.

### Simulator and debug panel

The debug panel (⚙ in the top bar, beside the menu button) is shown on localhost. Anywhere else, `?debug=1` turns it on and the choice is remembered; `?debug=0` turns it off again.

- **Movement:** WASD or the arrow keys walk, and Shift runs (which trips the speed limit). Double-click the map to walk to a spot, Ctrl/⌘ + double-click to teleport.
- **Map:** drag to pan, use the wheel or pinch to zoom; on touch, double-tap zooms in and a two-finger tap zooms out. Tap a tomb, the vault or a searched area for details.
- **GPS:** the panel switches between the simulator and real GPS. In simulator mode it also sets accuracy, walking speed-up (time warp) and realistic noise (drift and multipath jumps), and can cut the signal.
- **Game:**
  - force the next find, including a symbol of the key or the tomb, and move time forward by an hour;
  - bring a mission's time limit a day closer, add coins or money, put six coins in the backpack, or put lost artifacts on sale at once;
  - teleport to the tomb's gate or to the vault;
  - preview each artifact, switch the language, start a new game, load a ready-made demo world, or move the demo world to your current position.
- **Readout:** a live view of the fix, speed, filter and compass.

URL parameters:

- `?gps=sim` or `?gps=real` overrid

# joshuapatrickallen.com

Fan site tracking Josh Allen's stats and Bills franchise records.

## How the numbers stay current (free)
- `.github/workflows/update-data.yml` runs every hour on GitHub Actions and runs `scripts/update_data.py`.
- The script pulls free nflverse data (schedule, results, player and team stats, injury reports) and writes
  `allen-2026.json`, `matchup.json` and `nfl-ranks.json` to the **stats-data** branch.
- The pages read those files straight from GitHub, so data updates never trigger a Netlify deploy (no credits used).
  The copies in `data/` on main are only a fallback.
- After each Bills game, the Next game page switches to the following opponent on its own.

## Things to fill in by hand (no free feed)
`data/overrides.json`: TV network per game, and the all-time series record against an opponent
(through a given season; later games are added automatically). Without a series entry the page shows
the record since 1999.

# GRAVOFF

[![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/README-English-2f81f7)](README.md)
[![中文](https://img.shields.io/badge/README-%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-e5534b)](README.zh-CN.md)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Play online](https://img.shields.io/badge/Play-foudreai.com-3fb950)](https://foudreai.com)

**Gravity is optional. Landing isn't.**

A tiny browser game about a sports car with suction fans and cold-gas thrusters: drive upside down, fly over a row of cars, and land on the target. Plain JavaScript + Canvas, no build step, no dependencies.

## Play

- **Online:** https://foudreai.com (with a global leaderboard)
- **Locally:**

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/weijt606/gravoff.git
  cd gravoff
  npm start            # → http://localhost:8080
  ```

  No npm? `python3 -m http.server 8080 -d public`, or just open `public/index.html` in your browser.

The open-source version runs fully offline: best scores are saved in your browser, and the result commentary comes from a built-in line set. The hosted leaderboard backend is not part of this repository.

## Modes

| Mode | Goal |
|---|---|
| **Inverted Loop** | Keep the fans above the white line to stick to the loop, drive upside down, fly off the end, flip upright and land on the target |
| **Car Jump** | Take off at the TAKEOFF line (45–60 km/h works best), clear five cars, then use fan suction and brakes to stop on the target before the cliff |

S and SS grades need a midair jet barrel roll (G) plus a perfect landing.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| → / ← | Accelerate / brake (reverse thrust in the air) |
| ↑ / ↓ | Fan power |
| Space | Thrusters (hold) |
| F / G | Kickflip / jet barrel roll |
| R / P / M | Retry / pause / mute |

Touch screens get on-screen buttons. The interface follows your browser language (English / 中文).

## Project structure

```
public/          the whole game (open index.html)
  js/            physics, rendering, scoring, 8-bit music, i18n
tools/           local server and physics simulators (npm run sim:loop / sim:kick)
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). All code, graphics and music are original to this project.

GRAVOFF is an independent, non-commercial fan project. It is not affiliated with, authorised, sponsored or endorsed by any car, aerospace or technology company. The vehicles and physics are fictional – please don't try any of this in real life.

# Tunfcb — API

API Express + MongoDB de l'application mobile et du tableau de bord.

## Démarrer

```bash
cp .env.example .env      # puis renseigner les secrets
npm install
npm run dev               # http://localhost:4000/api/health
```

Au premier démarrage, l'API crée le super administrateur (`SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`),
les règles du jeu par défaut, 7 missions et 35 questions de quiz.

| Commande | Rôle |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Serveur avec rechargement |
| `npm run build && npm start` | Production |
| `npm run typecheck` | Vérification TypeScript |
| `npm run seed:demo` | Ajoute 40 supporters de démo avec 30 jours d'activité |
| `npm run seed:demo -- --clear` | Supprime toutes les données de démo |

## Organisation

`src/modules/<domaine>/` : modèle Mongoose, schémas Zod, service, contrôleur, routes.

- **auth** — inscription / connexion des supporters (JWT 30 j), parrainage
- **admins** — connexion au dashboard (JWT séparé), gestion des administrateurs
- **users** — profil mobile, gestion admin (recherche, suspension, ajustement de points…)
- **points** — grand livre : chaque gain/dépense est une transaction (`awardPoints`)
- **leaderboard** — classements jour / semaine / mois / année (somme des transactions) et général (XP)
- **games** — quiz du jour, roue, pronostics (synchro ESPN), pubs récompensées, bonus quotidien, missions
- **settings** — économie du jeu (niveaux, récompenses, roue…) modifiable depuis le dashboard
- **notifications**, **stats**

## Règles importantes

- **Solde** (BP dépensables) et **XP** (gains nets, détermine le niveau) sont distincts.
- Les « jours » (quiz, bonus, classements) suivent `APP_TIMEZONE` (Africa/Tunis).
- Les gains sont protégés contre le double clic par des mises à jour MongoDB atomiques.
- Les pronostics sont ouverts 21 jours avant le match, fermés au coup d'envoi et réglés
  automatiquement avec le score ESPN (`PREDICTIONS_SYNC_MINUTES`).
- Pubs récompensées : en production, brancher la vérification serveur AdMob (SSV).

# Marione

Il bot Discord che tiene vivo il server. Python 3.12 · discord.py · Postgres (schema `marione`) ·
OpenRouter. Tutti i dati vivono nel suo database: niente è salvato nei messaggi di Discord.

## Funzioni

| Funzione | Cosa fa |
|---|---|
| Economia | Marioncelli per messaggi e minuti in vocale, `/marione paga`, classifica. Il saldo è la somma di un registro che non si modifica mai (vista di controllo sempre vuota). |
| Ruoli ricchezza | 12 ruoli (da *Morto di fame* a *Divinità Spaghettara*) assegnati in base al saldo. Creati e gestiti solo da Marione. **Spenti di default**: li accende un admin. |
| Furto | `/marione deruba`: probabilità e multa calcolate in modo che tentare sia sempre in perdita; se ti beccano paghi la multa alla vittima. Un tentativo l'ora, il tempo è nel database. |
| Soundboard | Libreria di suoni condivisa: tutti aggiungono (sito o `/marione soundboard-add`) e suonano nella propria vocale; solo gli admin eliminano. |
| Musica | `/marione play <link o titolo>` (dal titolo prende il risultato più probabile), skip, stop, pause, queue; dal sito si cercano 10 risultati e si sceglie. YouTube via yt-dlp, con ripiego automatico su SoundCloud quando YouTube blocca il server (per YouTube vero: `YTDLP_COOKIES`). Musica ed effetti della soundboard suonano insieme (mixer). |
| Abitudini | Marione nota quando i membri sono online, in vocale, a cosa giocano, cosa ascoltano, quando scrivono e che canzoni chiedono; lo usa in chat (strumento `member_info`) e gli admin lo vedono nel "cervello". 90 giorni, cancellabile con `/marione forget`, funzione `habits` spegnibile. Online e giochi richiedono l'intent **Presence**. |
| Presenza in vocale | Marione entra appena qualcuno entra in vocale e resta finché non rimane solo. |
| Suoni d'entrata | Quando entri in vocale suona uno dei tuoi audio a caso. Li gestiscono solo gli admin (dal sito o con `/marione-admin entrance-*`). |
| Chat con l'AI | Risponde se chiamato o quando ha qualcosa da dire (OpenRouter). Vede cosa stai citando, chi è in vocale, il tuo ruolo e i movimenti recenti; ricorda i membri in modo strutturato; la conversazione sopravvive ai riavvii. Può regalare o multare monete con tetti rigidi. |
| Sito web | Login con Discord, in inglese, italiano o francese. Per tutti: saldo, classifica e movimenti (paginati), pagamenti, furto, soundboard con ricerca e filtri. Solo admin: suoni d'entrata di tutti i membri, "cervello di Marione" (prompt di sistema, appunti e ricordi su ogni membro, chat salvata per canale), funzioni, saldi, scelta del modello AI e costi. |
| Lingue | Inglese (predefinito), italiano, francese: sito, risposte del bot e nomi dei comandi Discord (tradotti in base alla lingua dell'app Discord). Ognuno sceglie con `/marione language` o dal sito; l'admin sceglie la lingua degli annunci pubblici. |

Comandi (nomi inglesi, mostrati in italiano/francese a chi ha Discord in quella lingua):
`/marione` balance, pay, rob, leaderboard, history, soundboard, soundboard-add, play, skip, stop,
pause, queue, language, forget ·
`/marione-admin` give, fine, set, undo, feature, status, server-language, entrance-add/list/remove,
soundboard-remove, import-old.

## Sviluppo

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
bash scripts/check.sh                 # ruff + mypy strict + pytest
.venv/bin/python -m marione.dev.preview   # il sito con dati d'esempio su http://127.0.0.1:8099
```

I test avviano un Postgres temporaneo (o usano `TEST_DATABASE_URL`). L'anteprima non tocca Discord:
usa un finto server e un Postgres temporaneo (servono i binari di PostgreSQL). L'LLM nei test è
sempre un finto LLM con copione.

## Configurazione

Vedi `.env.example`. Obbligatorie: `DISCORD_TOKEN`, `GUILD_ID`, `DATABASE_URL`. L'AI parte con
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`; il login del sito con `PUBLIC_URL`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`,
`DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `WEB_SESSION_SECRET`.

## Pubblicazione (Railway)

1. Servizio nello stesso progetto del Postgres, `DATABASE_URL` sulla rete privata; il `Dockerfile` e
   `railway.toml` sono pronti. Le migrazioni girano all'avvio (lock consultivo, una transazione per
   file) e `/health` risponde 200/503.
2. Discord Developer Portal → bot: attiva gli intent **Server Members**, **Message Content** e
   **Presence** (senza Presence il bot parte lo stesso, ma senza stato online e giochi).
   Permessi: Connect, Speak, Manage Roles (per i ruoli ricchezza), Send Messages.
3. Discord → OAuth2: aggiungi `https://<tuo-dominio>/auth/callback` ai redirect.
4. Il ruolo di Marione deve stare **sopra** i ruoli ricchezza nella lista dei ruoli del server.
5. Il sito e il bot sono lo stesso processo, sulla stessa porta.

Vedi `docs/DECISIONS.md` per le scelte di progetto e `docs/WEB_API.md` per il contratto del sito.

# Cash to Freedom (Dòng Tiền 3D)

A 3D board game about money: earn, spend, invest, and escape the Grind Mill.

- `web/dong-tien-3d.html` – the game (Vietnamese source, single file, Three.js r128).
- `tools/build_web.py` – builds `ios/CashToFreedom/www/{vi,en}.html`. The English build uses an international setting with prices in USD (2,500 VND = $1, so game balance is unchanged). Translations live in `tools/en/`, keyed to `tools/vn_phrases.txt`.
- `ios/` – iOS app (Swift + WKWebView, XcodeGen). Bundle id `com.cashtofreedom.app`.
- `android/` – Android WebView app.
- `docs/` – support and privacy pages (GitHub Pages).
- `sim/` – Node balance simulation.

## Shipping to the App Store (GitHub Actions, `.github/workflows/ios.yml`)

Every push compiles the app on a GitHub Mac. Add a tag to the commit message (or run the workflow by hand) to do more:

| Tag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `[testflight]` | Signs and uploads a build to App Store Connect / TestFlight |
| `[listing]` | Takes screenshots (vi + en) on a 6.9" iPhone simulator and uploads texts + screenshots from `ios/fastlane/metadata` |
| `[submit]` | Attaches the newest processed build and submits for App Review |

Secrets: `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `ASC_KEY_ID`, `ASC_ISSUER_ID`, `ASC_KEY_P8`.

After changing the game text, add the new phrases to `tools/en/` (the build lists any untranslated ones).
