rembednarczyk/PanBug.readme:
# PanBug

Gra do nauki testowania oprogramowania. Gracz przechodzi przez 24 zadania w ośmiu
małych aplikacjach. Każde zadanie zawiera celowo wstrzyknięty defekt: gracz porównuje
działanie aplikacji z wymaganiami z opisu, odtwarza defekt i zgłasza go z kategorią.

PanBug jest **stroną statyczną**: cała gra działa w przeglądarce (Blazor WebAssembly),
bez serwera aplikacji i bez bazy danych. Najlepszy wynik i historia ostatnich gier
zapisują się w `localStorage` przeglądarki.

## Zadania

Każda aplikacja ma trzy zadania. Zadania jednej aplikacji mają ten sam widok i ten sam
opis wymagań, a różnią się defektem. Są rozrzucone po grze i nigdy
nie stoją obok siebie, więc powtórzony opis nie zdradza od razu, że to ta sama aplikacja.
Na początku są zadania za 1 punkt, na końcu najtrudniejsze.

| Aplikacja | Zadania |
|---|---|
| Kino: wybór seansu, plan sali, bilety z ulgą wiekową | 1, 9, 18 |
| Automat paczkowy: nadanie paczki (wymiary, waga, telefon) i odbiór kodem | 2, 6, 13 |
| Kalkulator raty kredytu z harmonogramem spłaty | 7, 14, 20 |
| Planer urlopów z pulami dni na dwa lata | 3, 16, 22 |
| Logowanie z blokadą konta i resetem hasła | 5, 12, 19 |
| Lista zadań z terminami, filtrem zaległych i sortowaniem | 10, 15, 23 |
| Podział rachunku w restauracji z kodami rabatowymi | 4, 11, 21 |
| Formularz zamówienia z dostawą (walidacja i dostępność) | 8, 17, 24 |

Kategorie zgłoszenia (12) łączą techniki projektowania testów z sylabusa ISTQB
(wartości brzegowe, klasy równoważności, reguły biznesowe, przejścia stanów) z obszarami
jakości: obliczenia, daty, formaty, spójność danych, interfejs, bezpieczeństwo,
dostępność i niezawodność. Za zadanie można zdobyć od 1 do 4 punktów, łącznie 51.

Opis defektów i kroki ich odtworzenia są w kluczu dla prowadzącego, który nie jest
częścią repozytorium. Aplikacja zapisuje odtworzenie defektu dopiero wtedy, gdy defekt
pojawi się na ekranie.

## Architektura

| Projekt | Rola |
|---|---|
| `PanBug.Domain` | Czysta logika: 8 aplikacji po 3 zadania, `TaskManager`, `DefectCatalog` (punkty i kategorie), punktacja. Bez UI i bez zależności od platformy. |
| `PanBug.Web` | Interfejs Blazor WebAssembly: strony gry, 8 komponentów zadań (zadania jednej aplikacji dzielą widok), sesja gry z lokalną punktacją, magazyn wyników w `localStorage`. |

Każda aplikacja ma klasę bazową z poprawnym zachowaniem i sprawdzeniem, czy to, co widzi
gracz, łamie wymagania. Klasa zadania nadpisuje jedną metodę i w ten sposób wprowadza
defekt. Filtry wpisywanych znaków działają w JavaScripcie (`wwwroot/app.js`).

## Wygląd

Układ i komponenty pochodzą z systemu UI aplikacji PortfolioCogitator: karty z nagłówkami
opisanymi małymi wersalikami, liczby czcionką mono, ikony [Lucide](https://lucide.dev)
(licencja ISC). Kolory są z pierwotnej aplikacji PanBug: zielony akcent #23C87C, czarny pasek
górny, pomarańczowe punkty #E07710, czerwień błędów #C62828 i neutralne szarości. Style są
w jednym pliku `wwwroot/app.css` z tokenami kolorów, bez kroku budowania CSS.

Przełącznik w pasku górnym zmienia motyw jasny i ciemny. Bez zapisanego wyboru motyw
podąża za ustawieniem systemu. `wwwroot/theme-init.js` ustawia go przed pierwszym
malowaniem, więc strona nie miga jasnym tłem.

## Strona i podgląd linków

`index.html` ma metadane do udostępniania: Open Graph i Twitter z obrazkiem 1200×630
(`og-image.png`), adres kanoniczny, dane strukturalne JSON-LD (`WebApplication`), manifest
z ikonami (instalacja na telefonie) oraz `robots.txt` i `sitemap.xml`.

Podgląd linków wymaga adresów bezwzględnych. Pliki źródłowe zawierają adres GitHub Pages,
a `build-static.sh` podmienia go na `SITE_URL`. Workflow GitHub Pages ustawia `SITE_URL`
sam, na Render skrypt bierze `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL`. Przy własnej domenie ustaw `SITE_URL`
w zmiennych środowiskowych.

Obrazek OG i ikony PNG są generowane z `branding/og-image.html` i `branding/icon.html`:

```bash
node branding/render.cjs   # wymaga Node i pakietu playwright
```

## Uruchomienie lokalne

Wymagany .NET SDK 8.0.

```bash
dotnet run --project src/PanBug.Web
```

Zbudowanie wersji do publikacji (wynik w `publish/wwwroot`):

```bash
./build-static.sh
```

Skrypt sam doinstaluje .NET SDK 8, jeśli go nie ma.

## Wdrożenie na Render

Repozytorium zawiera Blueprint [`render.yaml`](render.yaml) dla strony statycznej:

1. Render Dashboard → **New** → **Blueprint** → wskaż to repozytorium.
2. Render uruchomi `./build-static.sh` (instaluje .NET SDK i publikuje aplikację)
   i opublikuje katalog `publish/wwwroot`.
3. Reguła przepisywania `/* → /index.html` obsługuje wejścia na adresy podstron
   (np. `/gra`, `/pomoc`); aplikacja i tak zaczyna od ekranu powitalnego.

Strona statyczna na Render nie usypia, więc nie ma czekania na rozruch serwera.
Pierwsze wejście pobiera ok. 7,5 MB (ok. 2,3 MB po kompresji brotli), kolejne
korzystają z pamięci podręcznej przeglądarki.

## Wdrożenie na GitHub Pages

Workflow [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](.github/workflows/pages.yml) przy każdym
pushu do `main` uruchamia testy, buduje stronę i publikuje ją na GitHub Pages.

Jednorazowa konfiguracja: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source:
GitHub Actions**. Przy ustawieniu „Deploy from a branch” GitHub Pages pokazuje
surowe pliki repozytorium (stronę z README), a nie aplikację.

Strona projektu działa pod adresem `https://<użytkownik>.github.io/<repozytorium>/`,
więc workflow ustawia `BASE_PATH=/<repozytorium>/`. Skrypt budujący dodaje też
`404.html` (wejścia na adresy podstron) i `.nojekyll` (Jekyll pomija katalog
`_framework`).

Każde uruchomienie aplikacji (pierwsze wejście, odświeżenie, link z zakładki) zaczyna się
od ekranu powitalnego, niezależnie od adresu. Stan gry żyje tylko w pamięci przeglądarki,
więc odświeżenie `/gra` nie miałoby czego pokazać. Odpowiada za to `start-at-home.js`
w `<head>`, który zmienia adres na bazowy, zanim Blazor go odczyta. Nowa gra startuje
wyłącznie przyciskiem na ekranie powitalnym lub ekranie wyniku.

Tę samą zawartość `publish/wwwroot` można opubl

danielbank/push-poker.readme:
# Push Poker

Push 4 meets poker. A web card game for 2–4 players sitting at the same table, each on their own phone or laptop. One player hosts the server, and everyone else joins from a shared URL. Every move shows up on every screen instantly.

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

```sh
npm install
npm start            # serves http://localhost:3000
ngrok http 3000      # in another terminal; share the https URL with the table
```

Everyone opens the URL, picks a name and a color (the name generates their [DiceBear critter](https://www.dicebear.com/styles/critters/) avatar), and takes a seat. Once two or more players are seated, anyone can press **Deal!**.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm start` | Runs the server and restarts it automatically if it ever stops. Resumes the saved table. |
| `npm run fresh` | Starts a brand-new table (clears players and win counts). |
| `npm run once` | Runs the server once, without the auto-restart loop. |
| `npm test` | Runs the rules and hand-ranking tests. |

Set `PORT` to change the port (default `3000`) and `STATE_FILE` to change where the table is saved (default `game-state.json`).

## How to play

### The deal

The whole deck is dealt into **4 rows of 13 cards**. Each player owns one row. With fewer than 4 players, the leftover rows are **neutral**: nobody plays them, but cards still pass through them.

Only **5 cards in each row are in play**, and those are the only ones anyone can see. The rest of the row sits out of play, in order, and wraps around like a loop.

Your goal is to have the best poker hand in your row when the game ends.

### Moves

On your turn you make exactly one move:

- **◀ ▶ Shift your row.** Your in-play cards slide one step left or right. A card leaves play at one end, and the next out-of-play card enters at the other. The row wraps, so you can always shift.
- **▲ ▼ Shift a column.** Pick one of the 5 columns. The in-play card in that column moves one row up or down through all 4 rows, wrapping from top to bottom. This is how cards change hands between players.
- **Pick up a hole card.** Tap a card in your row to take it as your hole card. It is hidden from the other players and safe from every shift. Choose whether the gap fills from the left or the right, so you still have 5 cards in play. You can hold one hole card at a time.
- **Put your hole card down.** Tap your hole card, tap a **+** to choose where it goes in your row, then choose which end card gets pushed out of play. If you put it at the very start or end of the row, the card at the other end is pushed out automatically, so your hole card can never go straight back out of play.
- **Knock.** Allowed once 5 full rounds are done (every player has moved 5 times). Knocking uses up your move. Then everyone, including you, gets one last move, and then the hands are compared.

### Reading the table

Every player's row is labelled with the best hand showing in their 5 in-play cards, and 👑 marks whoever is leading. Both are worked out from the cards on the table only, so they never give away a hole card. While you hold a hole card that improves your hand, your own row also shows your real hand next to a card-back icon. Only you can see that label.

### Keyboard shortcuts

On a computer you can play without the mouse:

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Move the cursor along your row: over your cards, or over the **+** markers while you hold a hole card |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Pick up the card under the cursor, or put your hole card down at the focused **+** |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Shift your row |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Shift the column under the cursor (its ▲ ▼ buttons light up) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> | Knock |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> / <kbd>Esc</kbd> | When asked which side fills the gap or which end gets pushed out: choose a side, or cancel |

### Showdown

Your hand is the **best 5 cards** from your 5 in-play cards plus your hole card, if you have one. Standard poker rankings apply, from high card up to straight flush, and an ace can play high or low in a straight. The best hand wins the game. Tied players each get a win.

Win counts carry over from game to game. The first player rotates each game, and new players can sit down between games.

## Dropped connections

The game is built to cope with closed laptops, sleeping phones, and flaky Wi‑Fi:

- **Your seat belongs to you, not to your connection.** If you drop, your seat is held and you show as offline. The page reconnects by itself when you come back.
- **Switching devices:** open the URL on the new device and tap your name under **Rejoin your seat**.
- **Server restarts:** the table is saved to `game-state.json` after every change. `npm start` restarts the server automatically if it stops, and the game picks up exactly where it left off.
- **Someone leaves for good:** other players can **Skip their move** while they are offline, or **Abandon game** (no winner). Offline players can be removed in the lobby.

## Testing on one machine

Each browser tab normally shares one seat. Add `?p=<anything>` to the URL to give a tab its own seat, for example `http://localhost:3000/?p=alice` and `http://localhost:3000/?p=bob`.

## Project layout

```
server.js         Express + Socket.IO server: seats, reconnection, persistence
lib/game.js       Game rules as pure state transitions, and per-player views
lib/hands.js      Poker hand evaluation
public/           The browser client (index.html, app.js, style.css)
test/             Rules and hand-ranking tests (node:test)
```

The server owns the game state and enforces every rule. Each player is sent only what they may see: the in-play cards and their own hole card. All hole cards are revealed at the showdown.

## Credits

- Card art from [deck-of-cards](https://deck-of-cards.js.org/) by Juha Lindstedt (MIT).
- Avatars from [DiceBear](https://www.dicebear.com/),

delectablegrapfruit/stickrpg.readme:
# Stick RPG Complete — browser recreation

A fan recreation of XGen Studios' 2005 Flash game **Stick RPG Complete** (v1.22) in plain
HTML5 canvas and JavaScript: the same city, buildings, prices, jobs, stats, minigames and endings,
running in any modern browser with no plugins, build step or dependencies.

> Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by XGen Studios. All code, art and
> sound here are original, drawn and synthesized in code. Game rules and numbers follow the
> original; dialogue and story text are paraphrased.

## Play

Open `index.html` in a browser (double-clicking the file works; no server needed).

| Key / mouse | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrow keys or WASD | walk (walk into a door to enter a building) |
| Shift (with skateboard) | skate, 2× speed |
| C (with a car) | get in / out of the car |
| I | inventory |
| Esc | stats / options on the street; LEAVE in a building; closes a panel |
| M | sound off / on (remembered) |
| F | full screen on / off |
| Mouse | menus, street people, HUD buttons |
| Tab / Enter | move the yellow focus box over buttons / press it (hold to repeat), as in Flash |
| Touch | on phones and tablets a thumb pad (and SKATE / CAR buttons) appears while walking; menus are tapped |

## What's in it

- The whole city of the 2nd Dimension with the original's map layout, walking limits, door
  positions, traffic, falling off the paper-thin edges, the day/night sky.
- Every building: home (apartment, penthouse, mansion, castle) with sleep, messages, TV, stocks
  and saving; McSticks; the convenience store (and robbing it); pawn shop; furniture store; bank
  with loans and real estate; New Lines Incorporated's job ladder; University of Stick; the bus
  depot's out-of-town commodity deals; Sticky's bar with bar fights and drunken darts; the
  Silver Lining Casino with slots, blackjack and roulette.
- Street people: the smokes kid, Homeless Harold, the dealer, and the car you can hotwire.
- Game lengths of 15, 40, 100 days or unlimited; elections; the end-of-game net worth and rank.
- One save slot (browser localStorage), like the original. Closing the page with unsaved progress asks first.

## Faithfulness

Mechanics follow the original's ActionScript: prices, formulas, random ranges, time costs and the
order of checks. The original's quirks are kept (for example, a defaulted bank loan is fatal, and
blackjack hands stop at four cards). The rules were checked state-by-state against the original running in the Ruffle Flash emulator
(hundreds of scripted scenarios and walking replays). A few outright bugs are fixed:

- A timed game always ends once its last day is over (the original could skip past the end
  when days advanced outside of sleeping).
- Roulette pays straight-up numbers at 36×, pays bets on 30 and 36, and 0/00 lose outside bets.

## Small departures for comfort

Rules, numbers and looks stay the original's; these only smooth the edges of playing it today:

- Motion is drawn smoothly between the 35 Hz ticks on 60-144 Hz screens everywhere (the city, sprites,
  the intro, the rooms' animations, every minigame), with eased in-betweens where the original
  jumped between drawings; everything renders at the screen's real resolution. OPTIMIZE (the 2005
  low-quality-while-walking switch) starts off.
- A refinement pass in the original's own vector style: text that runs a little wide with the real
  Arial Black is fitted to its panels, low-contrast labels get a rim, overlapping or clipped art is
  fixed, and sparse scenes (the intro, YOU DIED) get light shading and detail.
- Keyboard: Esc and I as above, M for sound, Tab focus wraps inside the game, Ctrl / Cmd shortcuts
  never reach it, WASD walks on any keyboard layout, held keys survive a panel or a door.
- A double-click presses only the button it began on, never the one that appears under the
  pointer after the first click (OK over LEAVE, the dealer's offer over his spot on the map).
- Refused actions play the error sound (the original sometimes ignored the click silently); AMOUNT
  boxes select their contents when focused; a bus deal says DEAL DONE!.
- Saves: damaged ones are repaired or ignored, a failed save says so, and leaving the page with
  unsaved progress asks first.
- Phones and tablets: a thumb pad while walking; the stage fits portrait screens.
- Sound pauses in a background tab and fades instead of clicking when cut.

## Development

```
js/core      engine, state, rules, UI widgets, audio
js/world     map geometry, walking rules, map art, sprites
js/scenes    city, building menus, title, intro, results
js/locations buildings and street dialogs
```

Harsh-Aaryan/RPG_Dev.readme:
# RepoRaid

**Defeat vulnerabilities. Level up security.**

RepoRaid is a low-poly multiplayer boss fight in which verified security fixes damage the boss. Strix finds weaknesses in a repository, Gemma 4 turns them into educational quests, GitHub records the work, and only fixes that pass a regression test deal damage.

Built for the *Best Use of Gemma 4* and *Best Open-Source AI Project* tracks.

> **Honesty labels.** In this build **Strix is mocked** (`worker/mock_strix.py`), and every finding it produces is shown as **Simulated Strix scan**. Gemma 4 and GitHub are real integrations that switch on when their keys are set. Until then the UI shows **Template** and **simulated issue** badges.

## Demo loop

```
Select demo repo → Import (simulated) Strix findings → Generate Gemma quests → 3D boss
→ Create safe GitHub issue → Run regression test on a proposed fix → Verified hit → Boss loses HP → Victory
```

1. **Start Battle** → *Replay simulated scan* → approve findings → *generate quests* → *Start battle*.
2. Open a quest. Ask the mentor for a hint, create the safe issue, and edit the vulnerable function in the **Patch forge**.
3. **Run regression test**. A failing fix does nothing. A passing fix returns a signed receipt, and the boss takes exactly that quest's damage, once.
4. Clear all four quests (800 HP) to reach the victory screen.

As host you can use *Load reference patch (host demo)* to keep a live demo short.

## Architecture

```
Browser (React + R3F) ──/api/*──▶ Netlify Functions ──▶ Gemini API (Gemma 4), GitHub API
        │                                   ▲
   localStorage (MVP)                       │ sanitized fixture
                                            │
                    Scanner worker (local, not Netlify): mock_strix.py | strix → parse_strix.py
                                            │
                                demo-vulnerable-repo/ (authorized target)
```

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Vite + React + TypeScript app: Tailwind v4, React Three Fiber, Motion, Zustand, React Router |
| `src/components/arena/` | Procedural low-poly boss, floating island, hit and shatter effects, 2D fallback when WebGL is missing |
| `shared/` | Code shared by the client and functions: game rules, quest schema (Zod), prompts, regression verifier |
| `netlify/functions/` | `generate-quest`, `mentor`, `verify-fix`, `create-github-issue`, `github-webhook`, `import-fixture`, `create-battle` |
| `worker/` | Mock Strix CLI, Strix → SafeFinding adapter, scan script, runtime fix verifier ([details](worker/README.md)) |
| `demo-vulnerable-repo/` | The only allowlisted target: 4 intentional bugs, each with a security test that fails until fixed |
| `fixtures/demo-findings.json` | Sanitized output of the last scan, committed so the demo never depends on a live scan |
| `supabase/migrations/` | Schema with RLS and derived HP, for the realtime multiplayer step |

### Game rules

| Severity | Damage | Boss cue |
|---|---:|---|
| Critical | 400 | Crimson aura, 9 spikes (Rootkit Wyrm) |
| High | 250 | Amber aura, 7 spikes (Cipher Golem) |
| Medium | 100 | Violet aura (Null Wisp) |
| Low | 50 | Cyan aura (Null Wisp) |

`maxHP = Σ damage`, `level = ceil(maxHP / 250)`, `size = min(1.75, 1 + 0.07·findings)`. HP is **derived** from verified quests and never decremented by events, so duplicate verifications can't double-count. When the host reopens a quest because its fix was invalidated, the HP comes back.

### Trust model

- `verify-fix` accepts **code, never a `verified` flag**. It runs deterministic regression checks and signs an HMAC receipt only when all of them pass. The client applies damage only with a receipt that matches the battle, quest and finding.
- Player code is **not executed** in Netlify Functions. The function uses static checks that mirror `demo-vulnerable-repo/test/security.test.js`. `shared/verifier.test.ts` proves that the static checks and the real `node --test` suite agree on both the vulnerable code and the reference fixes. `worker/verify_fix.py` runs the real tests (plus an optional re-scan) outside Netlify.
- `github-webhook` checks the HMAC signature and **never** awards damage. Closing an issue alone does nothing.
- Gemma gets only sanitized fields, wrapped as untrusted content. Its JSON output is validated with Zod and retried once, and the template is the fallback. Gemma teaches but never decides whether a fix counts.
- Issues contain no exploit material and are deduplicated by finding fingerprint.

### MVP limitations

- Battle state lives in `localStorage`. Tabs on the same device stay in sync; another device that joins by QR gets its own copy of the demo battle. Shared realtime HP needs Supabase (schema provided, client not wired).
- If `/api` is unreachable (e.g. `vite preview`), the app falls back to the same checks in the browser and labels receipts `local-offline` / `unsigned`.
- Without `HOST_TOKEN`, host-only functions are open. Set it in any shared deployment.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev            # Vite + Netlify Functions emulation on http://localhost:5173
npm test               # game rules + verifier (cross-checked against the real security tests)
npm run scan:mock      # re-run the simulated Strix scan → fixtures/demo-findings.json
```

Optional `.env` (see `.env.example`): `GEMINI_API_KEY` (Gemma 4 via the Gemini API, model `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`), `GITHUB_TOKEN` + `GITHUB_REPO` (fine-grained token for the demo repo, issues: write), `HOST_TOKEN`, `VERIFIER_SECRET`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Never prefix secrets with `VITE_`.

## Deploy to Netlify

Import the repo in Netlify. `netlify.toml` already sets build `npm run build`, publish `dist`, functions `netlify/functions`, the `/api/*` rewrite and the SPA fallback. Add the private env vars above, scoped to Functions. The scanner worker is **not** deployed to Netlify.

## Roadmap

Supabase Realtime battles · GitHub App per repository · webhook-driven PR verificatio

Mndum/gd-level-viewer.readme:
# GD Level Viewer

View and edit Geometry Dash level files in your browser, in the style of the in-game editor.

- Opens `.gdlvl` and `.gmd` level files (drop one on the page, or Menu → Open level).
- Draws the level with the real editor sprites. Don't have the game? [Get Geometry Dash on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/322170/Geometry_Dash/).
- Build / Edit / Delete bar: the Build tab lists the object types in the level, the Edit tab shows
  the selected object (position, rotation, scale, colour channels, z layer, groups).
- **Editing:** select objects (Shift-click for several), drag them in Move mode with grid snapping,
  nudge, rotate, flip, scale, duplicate, delete, and undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y).
- **Saving:** Menu → Save edited level downloads a *new* file in the same format. Your original is
  never changed. Edited levels have not been tested inside Geometry Dash itself, so keep your original.
- **Trigger timeline:** a bar under the view plays or scrubs through the level. Colour triggers apply as you scroll, like the editor; tick Preview for the rest. Colour, pulse, move, alpha, toggle, rotate, scale, spawn, camera (zoom, offset, rotation) and shader triggers take effect, with easing; the level's own background and ground pictures and colours are drawn. Hover or select a trigger to see what it does. Shader strength is approximate, and other trigger types are described but not simulated.
- **Playable cube:** the Play button in the timeline bar runs a cube through the level (hold Space, Up or the mouse to jump, Esc to stop). The movement follows the game's player physics; it covers the cube in classic mode, solid blocks, slopes, spikes, speed and gravity portals, and basic pads and orbs, and ignores other vehicles and moving objects.
- Shader gallery: ten named image effects applied to the view, with Save PNG.
- UHD sprites by default, HD selectable.
- The level's song plays from your own game folder (see below) and is dropped when you open another level.

## Using it

1. Open the page in Chrome or Edge.
2. Sprites load automatically. Optional: Menu -> **Use my own game folder instead...** to read them from your installed game
   (Chrome and Edge will not open folders under `Program Files`).
3. Open a level.

Everything happens in your browser. Your level and the game files are not uploaded anywhere.

## Songs

Newgrounds does not allow other sites to stream its audio, so this page never does. Instead:

- Geometry Dash saves every song it downloads as `<song id>.mp3` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GeometryDash`.
  Menu → Song → **Choose game save folder…** (once; the browser remembers it) and the page plays the
  level's song from there. The song is kept in memory only and dropped when you open another level.
- Or use **Load song file…** with any audio file.
- A small lookup service ([`worker/song-service.worker.js`](worker/song-service.worker.js), a Cloudflare
  Worker) is used only to show the song's name and artist, and the page links to the song's Newgrounds page.
  You can run your own copy and change the address in Menu → Song.
## What is and isn't in this repository

- `assets/` contains Geometry Dash's sprite sheets and fonts, included with RobTop Games' permission.
  No audio or shader code from the game is included.
- `index.html` includes a table that maps object IDs to sprite file names, which is how the page
  knows which sprite to draw for an object.
- The effect shader is original code.

## Disclaimer

Unofficial fan tool. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by RobTop Games.
Geometry Dash and its artwork are the property of RobTop Games.

## License

The code in this repository is MIT licensed (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). The licence covers this project's own code only; it grants no rights to Geometry Dash, its artwork, or anything else owned by RobTop Games.

dpt/ZXGame.readme:
# ZXGame

A portable front-end library for ZX Spectrum game ports written in C.

* `src/ZXSpectrum`: a virtual Spectrum (screen conversion, keyboard, Kempston,
  128K paging, AY, timing, and macros and helpers that emulate Z80
  instructions for code translated from a disassembly). It has no Z80 CPU
  emulation.
* `include/ZXGame/Game.h`: `zxgame_ops_t`, the vtable a game supplies.
* `hosts/`: front-ends for SDL3, headless, macOS, Windows and RISC OS. See
  `hosts/README.md` for the state of each.

Used by [The Great Escape in C](https://github.com/dpt/The-Great-Escape-in-C) and
[Chase H.Q. in C](https://github.com/dpt/ChaseHQ).

## Using it

```cmake
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(ZXGame
  GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/dpt/ZXGame
  GIT_TAG master)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(ZXGame)
target_link_libraries(MyGame PRIVATE ZXGameSDL3)   # or ZXGameHeadless
zxgame_sdl3_app(MyGame)
```

```c
int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
```

- `*_lspatch_manager.apk`: for use with the LSPatch manager app.
- `*_fontpatched.apk`: unpatched game with the font fix only.

kllloh/gnome-strike.desc: Gnomes vs Goblins: a blocky browser FPS in a destructible English back garden
kllloh/gnome-strike.readme:
# Gnomes vs Goblins

A blocky, Counter-Strike-style first-person shooter that runs in the browser. You and four bot
teammates fight five bots in a destructible English back garden, at garden-gnome scale.
Single player: no server needed. Built with TypeScript, Vite and Three.js.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # development server
# or
npm run build && npx vite preview
```

Open the address it prints (use `localhost`).

**Play without a server:** `npm run build` produces a single self-contained `dist/index.html`
(everything inlined), which you can open by double-clicking it or share as one file. Don't open the
*source* `index.html` in the project root as a file: browsers won't run the TypeScript source that way.

**Play online:** https://kllloh.github.io/gnome-strike/ (auto-deployed from `main`).

## Playing

- **Pick a side** (Gnomes or Goblins) and a **class** on the start screen. Switching restarts the match.
- Rounds: 10s buy time, then eliminate the other team. First to 8 round wins.
- **Controls:** WASD move, Space jump, Shift walk, mouse aim, click shoot, right-click scope (sniper),
  R reload, G frag, V smoke, B buy menu, M toggle voices, H toggle gore, 1 primary / 2 pistol / 3 chainsaw.
- **Buy menu (B, during buy time):** 1 SMG, 2 Shotgun, 3 Rifle, 4 Sniper, 5 Armor, 6 Frag, 7 Smoke,
  8 RPG, 9 Chainsaw.

### Classes

| Class | HP | Free weapon | Perk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assault | 100 | Rifle | 1 frag |
| Scout | 80 | SMG | fast, high jump, 1 smoke |
| Heavy | 140 | Shotgun | 50 armor, slow |
| Sniper | 85 | Sniper rifle | scoped shots, 1 smoke |
| Medic | 100 | SMG | regenerates and heals nearby allies |

### The garden

Most props, the low brick walls, the shed and the greenhouse can be shot or blown apart; the house and
boundary walls can't. Smoke blocks bots' sight, glass stops movement but not bullets, and everything
resets each round.

### Chaos

- **Hats:** shoot a hat off and it goes flying, with no damage to the owner. Hats also fly off when someone
  dies or sneezes.
- **Weapons for the unhinged:** RPG (rockets with a huge blast radius) and a chainsaw that gibs whatever it touches.
- **Gore:** blood sprays, splats on the ground, gibs, and corpses launched by explosions. Goblins bleed
  green. Press **H** to switch it off.
- **Pests:** spiders, beetles and wasps turn up during rounds and attack both teams. Late in a round the
  Spider Queen may show up.
- **Accidents:** goblins fart and gnomes sneeze now and then (and so do you, depending on your side). It
  gives your position away.
- **Voices:** uses the best English speech voices your system has (gnomes: British-style, goblins: low male).
  Windows/Edge "Natural" voices sound the best.

## Code map

- `src/main.ts` – game loop, rounds, economy, HUD, input
- `src/world.ts` – blocks, collision, raycasts, destructibles
- `src/map.ts` – the garden
- `src/bots.ts` – bot AI (cover, peeking, class behaviour)
- `src/nav.ts` – nav grid, A*, cover spots
- `src/critters.ts` – spiders, beetles, wasps
- `src/classes.ts`, `src/weapon.ts`, `src/grenades.ts`, `src/gnome.ts`, `src/player.ts`, `src/fx.ts`, `src/audio.ts`

Yumenyan/Codiram.readme:
# Codiram

GUI だけで実用的な Web アプリを作るための、自分専用の Web アプリ開発環境。

**データ → UI → ロジック → 外部連携 → 完成した Web アプリ** を、ブラウザ上の GUI で構築し、
最後は普通の HTML / CSS / JavaScript / JSON として Export できます(特定サービスへの依存なし)。

## 使い方

ビルド不要・依存ライブラリなしの静的アプリです。

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000   # または任意の静的サーバ
# → http://localhost:8000/ を開く
```

(ES Modules を使うため `file://` ではなく HTTP サーバ経由で開いてください。)

## ターゲット(Generator)

Codiram は **Generator** を選んで、同じビジュアルなロジックから別の実行環境向けの成果物を生成します。Core は各 Generator の中身を知らず、`defineGenerator()` で登録されたものをレジストリから使います。詳細は [docs/GENERATOR_SDK.md](docs/GENERATOR_SDK.md) / [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)。

| Generator | 生成物 | 画面 |
|---|---|---|
| 🌐 Web アプリ | HTML / CSS / JavaScript | Design / Data / Logic / Preview |
| 🖥 デスクトップ (Tauri) | Web アプリ + **Tauri 1.x プロジェクト**(ファイル選択・クリップボード・通知・ウィンドウ操作ブロック) | Design / Data / Logic / Preview |
| 🦀 Rust CLI | **Cargo プロジェクト**(std のみ。`cargo run` で実行) | Data / Logic / Output |
| 🐍 Python CLI | Python スクリプト(定義データのみで作られた Generator) | Data / Logic / Output |
| 🛠 自作 Generator | **Generator Builder** で言語ルールを入力して登録(コード不要)。Export / Scaffold / Import / プラグイン配布に対応 | Data / Logic / Output |

* New Project でターゲットとテンプレートを選択(Web テンプレートはデスクトップでも使えます)
* ブロックは対応 Generator と必要な Capability を持ち、現在のターゲットで使えるものだけがパレットに表示されます。非対応ブロックを使うと「Rust CLI は「ボタンがクリックされたとき」に対応していません」のように検証されます
* 右上のターゲットチップから Target Settings(Generator 情報・対応ブロック数も表示)、ターゲットの追加・切替ができます
* Export したプロジェクトは Codiram なしで開発・ビルドできる普通のプロジェクトです

**全 Generator:** Web / Static Web / HTML・CSS / Vite / デスクトップ(Tauri) / Rust CLI / Python / Node.js / JavaScript / TypeScript / Godot / VS Code 拡張 / Discord Bot / SQL / SQLite / JSON データパイプライン / REST API / Node サーバー / OS ブートローダー。Export 時に **GitHub Actions** のワークフローも追加できます。

**便利機能:** プロジェクト全体検索(Ctrl+Shift+F)・コマンドパレット(Ctrl+K)・Snippets(実装テンプレ。自作登録・共有可)・処理データ(AI が書いた JSON)の読み込み/書き出し・プレビューの変数モニター・Generator Library / AI Export(🧰 Tools)。JSON ファイルはウィンドウにドロップするだけで読み込めます。

> Minecraft Mod Generator(Modiram)は **一時停止中** です。コードは残してあり既存の Minecraft プロジェクトは開けますが、新規作成の選択肢には出ません。将来 Generator SDK 上の Generator として再開する予定です(MCreator など成熟したツールを当面は利用)。

### (保留中)Minecraft Mod の最初の成功ルート

1. New Project → **Minecraft Mod** → テンプレート *Hello Minecraft*(Mod ID を入力)
2. Logic: 「プレイヤーが参加したとき」→「メッセージを送る "Hello Minecraft!"」
3. Output で生成された Java を確認 → **Export** で ZIP を書き出し
4. 展開して `gradle wrapper --gradle-version 7.6.4` → `./gradlew build` → `build/libs/*.jar` を Fabric 1.19.2 の `mods` フォルダへ

対応ブロック(MVP): イベント(参加・ブロック右クリック/破壊/設置・アイテム使用)、アクション(メッセージ・アイテムを与える/取り上げる・ブロックを置く・テレポート・音)、条件(アイテム所持・スニーク)、値(プレイヤー名/座標・手持ち・イベントのブロック)、共通(変数・IF・繰り返し・待つ・関数・比較)。
実機ビルド・起動の確認状況と既知の制約は [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#4-minecraft--modiram-mvpphase-2) にあります。

## 画面

| 画面 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| **Design** | 左: Components(検索・カテゴリ折りたたみ・My Components)/ 中央: Canvas(ドラッグ配置・入れ子・リサイズ・複製・削除)/ 右: Properties |
| **Data** | データモデル(String/Number/Boolean/Date/Array/Object)、スプレッドシート風の行編集、アプリ変数 |
| **Logic** | Scratch/Blockly 型の縦ブロック(カテゴリごとに色・形・アイコン・ラベルで識別)。イベント/ページ単位でスクリプトを整理。Drag&Drop・複製・削除・コピー/貼り付け・複数選択・検索 |
| **Preview** | 生成した実アプリを iframe で実行(Edit → Run → Use → Stop → Edit)。エラーはブロック単位で表示しワンクリックで移動 |
| **Export** | `index.html / style.css / app.js / data/ / assets/ / README.md` を ZIP で書き出し |

* Undo / Redo(Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y)、履歴パネル、自動保存(localStorage、`✓ Saved` 表示)
* ライト/ダークテーマ、狭い画面ではサイドバーを折りたたみ
* **多言語UI**: トップバーの 🌐 から 日本語 / English を切替(選択は保存されます)。辞書は `js/i18n-dict.js`、ブロックは `J('日本語','English')` で定義するので、言語の追加は `LANGS` と辞書に列を足すだけです
* **フォント**: Project Settings でアプリ全体、Properties › Style › Font で部品ごとに指定。内蔵フォント(游ゴシック・明朝など)と Google Fonts(Noto Sans JP、M PLUS Rounded 1c、Zen Maru Gothic … 任意の Google Fonts 名も入力可)に対応。Export した `index.html` に必要な `<link>` が自動で入ります
* **アニメーション**: Properties › Animation で 登場(フェード・スライド・ズーム・バウンド・フリップ…)/ 繰り返し(パルス・ふわふわ・回転・点滅…)/ ホバー効果(拡大・浮き上がり・発光…)を設定、▶ で即プレビュー。Logic の Animation ブロックで再生・トゥイーン(滑らかに移動/拡大/回転/透明度)・停止・リセットも可能(`prefers-reduced-motion` を尊重)
* ショートカット: Ctrl+S 保存 / Ctrl+Z,Y Undo,Redo / Ctrl+C,V,D コピー,貼り付け,複製 / Delete 削除 / Ctrl+F 検索 / F5 実行
* データバインド: Text に `{変数}`、Input/Select/Checkbox → 変数、Table/List → モデル
* 条件・式: `count + 1`、`Input1`(入力値)、`item.name`(各行) などを入力可。式として解釈できない文字列はそのまま文字列として扱います

## 値ブロック(丸・六角形のブロック)

Scratch の「丸い値ブロック」「六角形の条件ブロック」と同じように、**式の入力欄にブロックをドラッグして入れ子にできます**(変数に代入しなくても直接値が使えます)。

* パレット上部の **すべて / 命令 / 値** で表示を切り替え。値ブロックは各カテゴリの下に並びます
* 「変数 ○ に … を入れる」形式のブロック(約100種)は、そのまま値ブロックとしても使えます(演算・文字列・配列・日時・正規表現…)
* 専用の値ブロック: 変数の値 / UI部品の値 / 比較 / かつ / または / 〜でない / 条件で値を選ぶ / データの行数・行の値 / 関数の結果 / スプライト座標・キー入力・衝突判定・マウス座標 …
* 六角形(⬡)は真偽値、丸(◯)は値。入力欄を選んでからパレットの値ブロックをクリックしても入ります。外すときは ✕

## ゲーム作成

* **Game カテゴリ**: Stage(自由配置のステージ)/ Sprite(絵文字・画像・図形)/ Canvas(描画)
* ステージ上は**ドラッグで自由配置**(矢印キーで1px、Shift+矢印で10px微調整)

ScottMorris/lieutenant-fizz-dos.desc: Lieutenant Fizz Episode 1 for DOS — a Rust port with VGA graphics and AdLib sound that runs in DOSBox, in a browser and on a 1.44 MB floppy.
ScottMorris/lieutenant-fizz-dos.readme:
# Lieutenant Fizz for DOS

*Lieutenant Fizz — Episode 1: The Cocoa Caper* for MS-DOS. The game's own Rust simulation, from [`liminal-hq/lieutenant-fizz`](https://github.com/liminal-hq/lieutenant-fizz), runs as a 32-bit DOS program in VGA mode 13h (320 × 200, 256 colours) with AdLib music and effects, or PC-speaker effects. It fits a 1.44 MB floppy, runs in DOSBox, and runs in a browser through js-dos. > **Status:** Episode 1 plays from the title through the overworld and every level, with boss dialogue, saves and options. The simulation matches the web build's exactly (800 checked state hashes). Still missing: the opening cinematic, the ending and credits, and the controls screen. Nothing has run on real hardware yet. [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md) has the full list, the measured speed and what has not been verified. ## Play it **In a browser:** [scottmorris.github.io/lieutenant-fizz-dos](https://scottmorris.github.io/lieutenant-fizz-dos/). Click Play (browsers need a click before they will make sound) and use the keyboard. `?opl=default` or `?opl=fast` in the address loads the game with another OPL (AdLib) emulator from js-dos, to compare the sound. To check the sound itself, choose Quit from the title and type `TONETEST` at the DOS prompt: it plays an A (440 Hz) on the AdLib and then on the PC speaker (Restart starts the game again). **In DOSBox:** unpack `dist/fizz-dos-demo.zip` (or build it, below) and run `dosbox --conf DOSBOX.CONF` in the folder. `FIZZ.EXE` starts at a system check in the manner of Keen's — the hardware it found, a speed test of the real renderer and the sound it will use (A AdLib for everything, M music on AdLib with effects on the speaker, P speaker only, O off) — and Enter continues to the title. | Key | Action | |---|---| | Arrows or WASD | Move (Up and Down also climb and look) | | Ctrl or Z | Jump | | Alt or X | Pogo stick | | Space or C | Fire | | Enter | Confirm: enter a level marker, dismiss a card | | Esc | Pause menu, and back in a menu | | Backspace | Back to the overworld map | | PgUp / PgDn | Previous or next level | | R, N, M, E | Restart the level; night mode; music on or off; effects on or off | The Options screen has music, effects, which chip plays the effects, **frame rate** (auto, 60 Hz or 30 Hz), **detail** (auto, high or low, which drops the backdrop layers on slow machines) and night. Options are kept in `FIZZ.CFG` and game saves in `AUTO.SAV` and `SLOT1.SAV` to `SLOT4.SAV`, all beside the game. `FIZZ.EXE [level|map]` starts in a level or on the map; `nopreview` skips the system check. ## Build it You need `bash`, `python3`, `zip`, `curl`, `git`, `gcc` with 32-bit libraries, `rustup` and [Bun](https://bun.sh). `tools/setup.sh` checks for them (it does not install system packages), installs the Rust pieces that `rust-toolchain.toml` lists, downloads DJGPP, DOSBox Staging and CWSDPMI into `vendor/` with checksums, and clones the main game next to this repository if it is not there (the exporters and the determinism check read it; the committed assets build the game without it). ```bash tools/setup.sh # prepare a fresh clone m2/build.sh # build the simulation for DOS and compare it with the web build: PASS: 800 checkpoints m4/build.sh --no-run # build the playable m4/c/fizz.exe tools/make-dist.sh # pack dist/fizz-dos-demo.zip tools/check.sh # everything the CI runs tools/clean.sh # remove build outputs when disk space is short (--all also removes vendor/) ``` `m2/build.sh` is the check that matters most: it runs 16 levels for 3000 ticks and compares 800 state hashes with the web build's wasm. `m5/bench` counts instructions per frame natively and checks a frame checksum for five scenes, so speed work can show the picture did not change. ## How it works The simulation never learns it is on DOS. A patched `no_std` copy of it (`m2/sim`, `m2/game`) is linked into a Rust runtime (`m2/dos-rt`) that draws, runs the menus and keeps the saves; a small C layer built with DJGPP (`m4/c`) sets the video mode, hooks the keyboard and timer interrupts and drives the sound chips. The x87's precision control is set to 53 bits so its results equal the web build's `f64`. Lighting is done with the palette: 16 colours at 14 brightness levels, chosen per 8 × 8 cell. [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) has the layers, the build pipeline and the rules that keep the simulation identical. | Folder | What it holds | |---|---| | `m0` | Native determinism harness: hashes the simulation's state, to compare with the web build | | `m2` | The simulation for DOS (`sim` and `game`: the main game's crates plus `patches/`), the DOS runtime (`dos-rt`) and the custom i486 target | | `m3` | Sprite export, the sprite census and the screenshot converter | | `m4` | The playable build: the C layer, the exporters and the sound converters | | `m5` | `bench`, the instruction counter and frame checksums | | `tools` | Setup, check, clean, fetch, run, pack and convert scripts, the DOSBox configuration | | `dist`, `site` | The demo folder, and the GitHub Pages page | | `docs` | Status, architecture and the milestone notes | | `attic` | Superseded code from the first milestones, not buil

imjarvissingh/Primer.readme:
# Primer

Primer is an early-stage, interest-personalized mathematics game for US children ages 6–9. It aims to turn a child's interest into a learning adventure while measuring mathematical understanding, not just engagement.

Two themed experiences share one curriculum and one learning engine:

- **Block Builder** — bridges, building blocks and a builder guide.
- **Space Construction** — a space station, modules and a space guide.

## Current stage

**Early development, with a draft demo.** The repository contains the planning documents, a deterministic curriculum/math/tutoring engine (`src/domain`), one guided subtraction mission in two themes (Block Builder _The Broken Bridge_ and Space Construction _The Space Station Mission_, 13 − 5), a short independent check, and an adult-facing synthetic evidence summary. The missions and check are **draft demonstrations**: its content and hints have not been reviewed by an educator, and it is not a tested learning product. There are no accounts, database or data collection, and no learning results exist.

## Try the demo

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # then open http://localhost:3000/block-builder
                     # or http://localhost:3000/space-construction
```

Tap the 5 blocks (or modules) to put them on the bridge (or station), pick how many are left in the pile (or supply), and press "Check my answer". The answer buttons unlock once exactly 5 are placed. Answers are scored by the server (`/api/practice/mission`), which keeps short-lived in-memory sessions, so the demo needs `next dev` or `next start` (not a static export) and runs as a single instance. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the client/server boundary and limitations.

### Look and feel (Phase 8A)

Primer has an original visual identity: a warm cream/navy/teal system, a wordmark, and two distinct worlds (a sunny bridge-building scene and a space-station scene) on the same mission engine. The independent check is deliberately plainer. It uses system fonts, inline SVG and CSS only, honours reduced-motion settings, and adds no dependencies or data collection.

### Independent check and demo summary

`/assessment` is a short independent check (four draft questions, no hints, no right-or-wrong feedback, skippable). When it ends, "Summary for a grown-up" opens `/demo-progress?session=...`, which shows what the server recorded for that check: counts, each question's outcome, skills sampled and where the data came from. It says plainly that mastery is not awarded and that the data is synthetic. Opening `/demo-progress` with no session shows only guidance. Both are unauthenticated, in-memory, single-instance demos; see [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

**Sessions and recovery.** Sessions live in server memory for 30 minutes after last use. Refreshing a page, restarting the server or waiting too long ends a session; the page then says so and offers a fresh start. It never resumes or rebuilds results from the browser. "Start over" always begins a new session. Hosted multi-instance deployments cannot rely on this in-memory store.

**Recording the demo:** follow [docs/DEMO-RUNBOOK.md](docs/DEMO-RUNBOOK.md).

## Getting started

Prerequisites: Node.js 20.9 or newer (developed on 24.16) and npm. Git is needed to clone.

```bash
npm install                      # install dependencies from package-lock.json
npx playwright install chromium  # one-time download for browser tests
npm run dev                      # development server at http://localhost:3000
```

| Command                | What it does                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `npm run build`        | Production build                                       |
| `npm start`            | Serve the production build (run `build` first)         |
| `npm run typecheck`    | TypeScript strict type check                           |
| `npm run lint`         | ESLint                                                 |
| `npm run format:check` | Check Prettier formatting (`npm run format` fixes it)  |
| `npm test`             | Unit tests (Vitest + React Testing Library)            |
| `npm run test:e2e`     | Production build, then Playwright Chromium smoke tests |
| `npm run validate`     | All of the above checks in sequence                    |

Continuous integration (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same checks on every push to `main` and on pull requests, plus a production-dependency audit and a gitleaks secret scan. There is no automatic deployment.

### Stack

Next.js 16.4.2 (App Router), React 19.3, TypeScript 5.9 (strict), Tailwind CSS 4.3, ESLint 9, Prettier 3.9, Vitest 5, React Testing Library, Playwright 1.64 (Chromium).

## Documentation

All planning documents live in [`docs/`](docs/00-INDEX.md):

| Document                                | Contents                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| [00-INDEX.md](docs/00-INDEX.md)         | Project overview and milestones                |
| [PRODUCT.md](docs/PRODUCT.md)           | MVP product requirements                       |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Planned technical architecture                 |
| [CURRICULUM.md](docs/CURRICULUM.md)     | Skills, assessment banks, tutoring states      |
| [SAFETY.md](docs/SAFETY.md)             | Child-safety and privacy release gates         |
| [DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md)       | Decisions made, open questions, deferred items |
| [EVALUATION.md](docs/EVALUATION.md)     | Hypotheses and pilot evaluation plan           |
| [TASKS.md](docs/TASKS.md)               | Solo-founder schedule                          |

## Safety-first approach

Primer is intended for children, so safety and privacy gate every release. Before any live child use, the plan requires COPPA-specific legal review, verified parental con

benjtharm41/coordinator-challenge.readme:
# Coordinator Challenge

A mobile-friendly NFL play-calling game. You are the coordinator: you call every play on offense and defense, and the computer coaches the other team using real tendencies.

Personal, non-commercial project. No NFL or team logos are used.

## Status

All five phases are built:

1. Simulation engine calibrated to real NFL averages (`docs/CALIBRATION.md`), plus exploit and sanity tests (`docs/EXPLOIT-TESTS.md`).
2. Animated field, drawn diagrams for every call, route and zone overlays, phone layout.
3. Real nflverse data (rosters, depth charts, injuries, ratings, tendencies) refreshed by a weekly GitHub Action (`docs/DATA.md`).
4. Situations mode (11 scenarios, `docs/SCENARIOS.md`), stats tracking, backup export/import, home-screen install and offline play.
5. Deployed to GitHub Pages.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | Downloads the tools the project needs (once). |
| `npm run dev` | Starts the game at http://localhost:5173 (and on your Wi-Fi network). |
| `npm test` | Runs every automated test. |
| `npm run calibrate` | Sims 1,000 computer-vs-computer games and compares to real NFL averages. Writes `docs/CALIBRATION.md`. |
| `npm run exploits` | Checks that no single repeated call wins and that results look sane. Writes `docs/EXPLOIT-TESTS.md`. |
| `npm run scenarios` | Checks that each Situation is winnable but not a sure thing. Writes `docs/SCENARIOS.md`. |
| `python3 pipeline/build_data.py` | Downloads fresh nflverse data and rebuilds the team files. |
| `npm run build` | Builds the site for hosting. |

## How a play is decided

1. **The matchup** of your call against the other coordinator's call (`src/engine/matchup.ts`): e.g. screens beat blitzes, four verticals struggle against Cover 4, runs do better against light boxes.
2. **Player ratings** (`src/engine/ratings.ts`).
3. **Controlled randomness** (`src/engine/resolve.ts`).

The engine decides the outcome first; any animation only shows it. The computer coordinators scout your recent calls and adjust, so spamming one play doesn't work.

## Data

League targets and tendencies come from [nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data) play-by-play (2025 season + 2026 to date). Scripts are in `pipeline/` (Python standard library only).

kavemankai/Kaijustomp.readme:
# Kaijustomp

Retro low-poly kaiju reverse auto-shooter for Godot 4 (mobile first). You are the kaiju. Tanks, mechs and helicopters converge on you, you auto-fire a bullet spiral, and you crush buildings by walking through them. Killed enemies drop G-cells. Collect them to level up and pick a mutation. When you die, spend banked G-cells on permanent upgrades in the lab.

The project has no binary assets. Meshes, the 256x256 texture atlas and all sound effects are generated in code at startup.

## Run

1. Install Godot 4.2 or newer (developed against 4.3).
2. Import `project.godot` and press F5.
3. Controls: WASD or arrows to move. Drag on the left half of a touch screen to move. Tap the right half for the Atomic Nova ring (5 second cooldown). On the level-up screen press 1, 2 or 3, or click a card. In the lab press Enter to start the next run. Mouse input emulates touch.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/core/SimulationManager.gd` | Flat-array pools for bullets, enemies, pickups and debris, drawn through `MultiMeshInstance3D`. Spatial hash collision. Three enemy types (tank, mech, flying helicopter), DEFCON escalation, G-cell pickups with magnet pull. Ground units ask the navmesh for a waypoint once every 16 frames. |
| `scripts/core/RetroMeshFactory.gd` | Vertex-coloured `ArrayMesh` builders for every model. UVs point into the shared atlas. |
| `scripts/core/RetroTextureAtlas.gd` | Generates the 256x256 pixel-art atlas (scales, windows, armour, plasma). |
| `scripts/core/RetroAudioBank.gd` | Synthesizes 22,050 Hz 16-bit sound effects and plays them from an 8-voice pool. |
| `scripts/core/ProgressionManager.gd` | G-cells, best score and lab ranks, saved to `user://kaiju_save.cfg`. |
| `scripts/core/SpatialHash3D.gd` | Uniform grid on the X/Z plane. |
| `scripts/world/DynamicCityManager.gd` | `GridMap` city with three building types, destruction, async navmesh rebake, reset on restart. |
| `scripts/player/KaijuPlayer.gd` | Movement, HP, XP and mutations, 10 degree FOV diorama camera, auto-fire, Atomic Nova, revive. |
| `scripts/ui/MutationAndLabUI.gd` | Level-up draft (pauses the game) and the post-run lab. |
| `scripts/ui/MobileTouchController.gd` | Virtual joystick and tap detection. |
| `shaders/ps1_retro_model.gdshader` | Vertex snapping, affine texture mapping, vertex lighting. |
| `shaders/ps1_postprocess.gdshader` | 15-bit colour, Bayer dithering, CRT curve and scanlines. |

## Settings that matter

The renderer is `gl_compatibility` for both desktop and mobile. ETC2/ASTC import is on. `run/max_fps` is 60. The navigation map cell size is 0.25, and the navmesh in `DynamicCityManager` has to match it or region updates are rejected. The first navmesh bake waits a process frame and a physics frame, because `GridMap` builds its colliders late.

G-cells are held in memory during a run. They are written to disk on death, on a lab purchase, when the app is paused and when the window closes.

## Known gaps

- Balance is untuned. In a 150 second run with the player circling and auto-picking mutations, the player took no damage at DEFCON 1 and killed about 4,700 enemies. Bullets travel about 48 units, so tanks die near their spawn ring before they reach you.
- Not profiled on a device. The simulation took 4.3 ms per frame headless on a desktop CPU. Pool sizes (2,500 bullets, 500 enemies per type bucket, 400 pickups, 400 debris) and about 31 `map_get_path` calls per frame are untested on phone hardware.
- Sound effects are checked only for building and playing without errors. Nobody has listened to them.
- `apex_pass_unlocked` doubles G-cell income but nothing sets it. The save file is a plain text `ConfigFile` that a player can edit.
- Bullets pass through buildings. Helicopters are hit by ground bullets because collision ignores height.

aviate15/chessweeper.readme:
# Chessweeper

Chess meets Minesweeper. Mines hide on the board, landing on a square reveals how many mines surround it, and pieces that step on a mine blow up. Kings have three lives. Numbers are public, flags are private, and every few turns (6 by default) without a capture the mines reshuffle. Online and local pass-and-play, in an old-school Windows Minesweeper look.

Status: playable. Local pass-and-play and online two-player games (lobby, invite links, reconnect) work; play with friends from your laptop via [`docs/PLAY_ONLINE.md`](docs/PLAY_ONLINE.md); Fly.io and Vercel config is kept in [`docs/DEPLOY.md`](docs/DEPLOY.md). Rules live in [`docs/GAME_DESIGN.md`](docs/GAME_DESIGN.md).

## Quickstart

Requires Node 24 (see `.nvmrc`) and pnpm.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm check   # format check, lint, typecheck, tests
pnpm --filter @chessweeper/web dev   # play local pass-and-play in the browser
```

## Playing

- A rules page opens on first load. Reopen it any time from **Help → Rules** or the **?** button.
- A revealed number counts the mines in the 8 neighbouring squares. Hover or focus a number to see what it counts and which landing revealed it. When a piece stands on a numbered square the number shows in a small corner badge.
- **Game → New game...** sets the reshuffle interval (default 6 turns) and mine density (default 30%) for the new game. Online, the creator picks them in the Create game dialog and both players see them.
- Right-click (or the flag button) places private flags. Sound and board flipping are toggles in the Game menu.

## Play online with friends

One command runs the server on your laptop and shares it through a free public tunnel (Cloudflare, or SSH-based fallbacks for networks that block it; no account, no cost): `pnpm play`. Steps and limits are in [`docs/PLAY_ONLINE.md`](docs/PLAY_ONLINE.md).

## Deploying (later)

Server on Fly.io, web on Vercel. Step-by-step commands, rollback and a post-deploy smoke check are in [`docs/DEPLOY.md`](docs/DEPLOY.md).

## Layout

- `packages/engine`: pure TypeScript rules engine (no DOM, network or clock).
- `packages/protocol`: wire protocol shared by server and client.
- `apps/server`: server-authoritative WebSocket game server.
- `apps/web`: browser client (Vite + React): local pass-and-play, retro pixel skin, sound and animations.
- `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md`: the rules (single source of truth). `docs/IDEAS.md`: parked ideas that are not in the current rules.

## License

MIT

goyalion17/breakout-game.readme:
# Breakout

A classic Breakout arcade game built with Python and the `turtle` module, as part of my 100 Days of Code journey (Day 87).

![Breakout gameplay](screenshot.png)

## Features

- Paddle controlled with the arrow keys; the ball bounces at different angles depending on where it hits the paddle
- 6 rows × 10 columns of colored bricks, with higher rows worth more points
- Score, lives (3) and a persistent high score saved to a file
- 3 levels, with the ball getting faster on each level and as the rally goes on
- Start / pause with the space bar
- Sound effects (macOS system sounds)

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `←` / `→` | Move the paddle |
| `Space` | Start / pause |

## Run it

Requires Python 3 with Tkinter (included in most Python installations).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/goyalion17/breakout-game.git
cd breakout-game
python3 main.py
```

Sound effects use `afplay` and work on macOS only; on other systems the game runs silently.

## Project structure

```
├── main.py        # screen setup, game loop, collisions, levels
├── paddle.py      # Paddle class
├── ball.py        # Ball class: movement, bounces, speed
├── bricks.py      # Brick and Bricks classes: wall layout and collision check
├── scoreboard.py  # score, lives, high score, on-screen messages
└── sounds.py      # sound effects helper
```

## What I learned

- Planning a project first: spec, checklist and flowchart before writing code
- Splitting a game into small classes with a single responsibility
- Collision detection with rectangles, including choosing the bounce axis by penetration depth
- Managing game state (running, paused, levels) in a `turtle` game loop

Aryan-1908/Dussehra-Event.readme:
# Ravan Dahan (Dussehra game)

Everyone plays at the same time on their own screen. A live leaderboard ranks players by fastest time to burn Ravan.
The host approves who gets in and can run an optional team show on a shared screen.

## Run on a server

Needs Docker. No domain or HTTPS is required: plain `http://<public-ip>` works.
Open the port (80, or 8000) in the server firewall / security group.

```bash
git clone <your-repo-url> ravan-dahan && cd ravan-dahan
docker build -t ravan-dahan .
docker run -d --name ravan-dahan --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 80:8000 -e HOST_KEY=choose-a-long-secret \
  -v ravan-data:/app/data ravan-dahan
```

If port 80 is taken, use `-p 8000:8000` and add `:8000` to the links below.

Without Docker: `pip install aiohttp==3.9.5 && HOST_KEY=choose-a-long-secret PORT=8000 python server.py`

## Links

- Players: `http://<public-ip>/`
- Host: `http://<public-ip>/?host=<HOST_KEY>` (keep private)

## How a game works

- Every player gets **one game of 5 minutes**; the clock starts when they press **Pick up the bow**.
- Finishing (burning Ravan) ranks by fastest time. Players who run out of time are ranked after the finishers, by most heads down.
- A refresh resumes the game in progress, and a finished player sees their result instead of a replay.
- To run a fresh round (for example after testing), the host presses **New round (clear leaderboard)**. Every browser then resets itself.

## Event day

1. Open the host link first and keep it open. The entry panel is at the bottom-left.
2. Share the players link. Each person types a name and waits.
3. Press **Approve all** (or approve one by one, or tick **Auto-approve everyone**).
4. Optional finale: **Start live show** for a team battle on a shared screen.

## Notes

- Run a single instance. State lives in memory and in `data/state.json`.
- Set `AUTO_APPROVE=1` to skip approval by default.
- Browsers show "Not secure" over plain HTTP. The game still works.
- Optional HTTPS: Caddy (`your-domain.com { reverse_proxy localhost:8000 }`) handles WebSockets automatically. With nginx add `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";`.
- Health check: `GET /healthz`.

blackworm86/silent-chat.readme:
# Silent Chat — companion app for *Alice Is Missing* (IT/EN)

Two ways to host it. **Path A is the default** (free, no credit card, works from a phone).

| | **A — GitHub Pages + Firebase** | **B — Cloudflare** |
|---|---|---|
| Cost | free, no card | free, no card |
| Who runs the game "server" | the **host's phone/browser** (keep the app open in front) | Cloudflare (always on) |
| Needs a computer | no | no (Workers Builds) / yes (CLI) |
| Offline Wi-Fi mode | via `npm run relay` | via `npm run relay` |

> The deployed site contains **no readable game text**: cards and posters are AES-GCM encrypted (`public/pack`) and open with your group passphrase. Chat messages travelling through Firebase are end-to-end encrypted with a key derived from the same passphrase + room code. The plaintext cards (`content/`, `assets/`) are never committed.

## Path A — GitHub Pages + Firebase

1. **GitHub**: a *public* repository (free GitHub Pages needs public; nothing readable is exposed). Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**. Every push to `main` rebuilds the site (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`).
2. **Firebase** (console.firebase.google.com, Google account, no card): create a project → *Realtime Database* → create (locked mode) → **Rules**: paste `firebase/database.rules.json` → Publish → register a *Web app* → copy the `firebaseConfig`.
3. Put the config in `public/config.json` (`transport: "firebase"`).
4. Encrypt your game data with a group passphrase: `PACK_PASSPHRASE="..." node tools/pack.mjs --out public/pack` (needs `content/` + `assets/` locally).
5. Open `https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/` → enter the passphrase → open `#/diag` and run **Connection test** → play.

How it works: the device that *creates* the room runs the game engine in its browser and talks to the others through a small encrypted message queue in Firebase. If the host's phone is closed or loses signal, everyone sees "waiting for the host"; when it returns (same device) the game resumes from the saved snapshot. Rooms delete themselves at the end of the game.

## Path B — Cloudflare (always-on server)

`npm install && npx wrangler login && PACK_PASSPHRASE="..." npm run deploy` (remove or rename `public/config.json` so the app uses WebSockets). See `wrangler.toml`.

## Playing

Host creates a game → friends scan the QR (or get the link through **Share invite**) → the host picks **Full Digital** or **Chat + Game Aids** and the sound source (**host's device** or **shared tablet**) under *Game settings* → follow the on-screen steps. Everything the rulebook asks for is on screen; the red **X** is always one tap away.

**Deleting a game:** the host can delete a game at any time from the menu (☰ → *Delete game*), or from *Your games* on the home screen. Everyone connected is told the game was deleted; the room, its chat and its voicemails are erased (Firebase, relay and Cloudflare alike).

The interface is designed for phones first; see `docs/UX-REVIEW.md` for the mobile usability review behind it.

## Without internet (local relay)
```bash
PACK_PASSPHRASE="..." npm run build && npm run relay      # prints http://192.168.x.x:8787 for phones on the same Wi-Fi/hotspot
```
YouTube is unavailable offline (manual clock; play the music from another device).

## Develop / test
```bash
npm test          # 47 tests: rules engine (240 random games), relay, Firebase-style transport, game deletion, encryption, UI
npm run typecheck
```
`src/shared` rules engine · `src/client` Preact app (`bus/` = Firebase transport) · `worker` Cloudflare · `relay` local server · `tools` · `docs/SPEC.md`.

## Honest status
Tested in a sandbox: rules engine, both transports (WebSocket relay + real Cloudflare runtime; Firebase transport on an in-memory bus that mimics Firebase), encryption, UI (simulated browser). **Not tested here:** the live Firebase service, real phones, live YouTube, microphones. Use `#/diag` and a two-phone playtest before game night.

# 👁️ 眼動控制遊戲集錦

純前端（無需後端、無需安裝）的眼動控制網頁，使用網路攝影機 + [MediaPipe Face Landmarker](https://ai.google.dev/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/face_landmarker)（含虹膜關鍵點與眨眼 blendshape）。影像只在瀏覽器本機處理。

| 頁面 | 說明 |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | 首頁／校正狀態 |
| `calibrate.html` | **眼動校正**：可調直徑圓球，定點模式（自動追加校正點、驗證誤差）或軌跡模式（圓球沿路徑移動，視線跟隨）；頂部有**校正誤差指示條**（白線＝球半徑），誤差進入球半徑內即完成並存檔 |
| `mouse.html` | **眼控滑鼠**：視線移動虛擬游標，眨左眼＝左鍵、眨右眼＝右鍵 |
| `race.html` | **眼控賽車**：偽 3D 公路，看左右控制車子，眨眼發射飛彈炸掉車輛／石頭／樹木 |

## 執行
相機需要 HTTPS 或 localhost：

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000   # 然後開啟 http://localhost:8000
```
建議使用 Chrome / Edge。首次載入需連網下載 MediaPipe 模型（jsDelivr + Google Storage CDN）。

**沒有鏡頭也能試**：任一頁網址加 `?mock`——滑鼠＝視線，`Z`/`X`/空白＝左眼/右眼/雙眼眨。

## 原理
- **特徵**：兩眼虹膜相對眼角/眼瞼的比例（水平/垂直）＋頭部偏轉/俯仰（由臉部變換矩陣）＋臉部位置與大小。
- **映射**：嶺迴歸（樣本夠多時加入二次項）把特徵對應到螢幕座標，One-Euro 濾波降低抖動，眨眼期間凍結視線。
- **眨眼**：用 `eyeBlinkLeft/Right` 分數＋遲滯；單眼閉合超過約 140 ms 且另一眼睜開才算「眨單眼」，自然眨眼（雙眼同時、很短）會被忽略。若左右相反，在校正/滑鼠頁勾選「左右眼對調」。
- **校正收斂**：定點模式用「加入此點前的模型」去預測新點得到真實驗證誤差，最近 8 點平均 ≤ 球半徑才通過；軌跡模式用近 5 秒滾動平均（含 130 ms 視線延遲補償）。

## 限制
- 瀏覽器無法控制作業系統的真實滑鼠；「眼控滑鼠」是頁面內的虛擬游標（可操作該頁的按鈕等元素）。
- 一般網路攝影機的眼動精度有限；球半徑設太小（< ~30 px）可能無法收斂，可加大直徑。校正後盡量不要大幅移動頭部。

## 測試
```bash
node tests/gaze.test.mjs
```

# 볼링 게임 카타

Uncle Bob의 [The Bowling Game Kata](http://www.butunclebob.com/ArticleS.UncleBob.TheBowlingGameKata)를 TDD(Red → Green → 코드 리뷰)로 진행한 Java 프로젝트입니다. `Game` 클래스의 `roll(int)`과 `score()`를 구현했고, 각 사이클은 `PLAN.md`의 테스트 하나씩을 기준으로 사람이 단계마다 승인하는 방식(`agentic-tdd`)으로 진행했습니다.

## 사이클별 진행

| # | 테스트 | Red | Green |
|---|--------|-----|-------|
| 1 | 거터 게임 → 0점 | 실패 확인 (`expected 0 but was -1`) | `score()`가 `0` 반환 |
| 2 | 전부 1핀 → 20점 | 실패 확인 (`expected 20 but was 0`) | `roll`이 핀 합산 |
| 3 | 스페어 보너스 → 16점 | 실패 확인 (`expected 16 but was 13`) | `rolls[]` 배열 + 프레임 순회, 스페어 분기 추가 |
| 4 | 스트라이크 보너스 → 24점 | 실패 확인 (`expected 24 but was 17`) | 스트라이크 분기 추가 (인덱스 1 전진) |
| 5 | 퍼펙트 게임 → 300점 | 처음부터 통과 | 구현 변경 없음 |
| 6 | 10프레임 스페어 → 17점 | 처음부터 통과 | 구현 변경 없음 |
| 7 | 10프레임 스트라이크 → 19점 | 처음부터 통과 | 구현 변경 없음 |
| 8 | 혼합 게임 → 167점 | 처음부터 통과 | 구현 변경 없음 |

5~8번은 4번의 스트라이크 구현이 이미 일반적인 형태여서 처음부터 통과했습니다. 이 네 테스트는 Red 실패를 직접 확인하지 못한 회귀 테스트입니다.

## 실행

Gradle 래퍼를 사용합니다 (Windows는 `gradlew.bat`).

```
./gradlew test
./gradlew test --tests "bowling.GameTest.mixedGame"
```

## 범위 밖

입력 검증(음수·11핀 이상·프레임 합 10 초과), 게임 종료 후 `roll` 거부, 미완성 게임의 점수 정책은 구현하지 않았습니다.

okayline/dungeon-items.readme:
# dungeon-items

The one item table every game reads: 4Dungeon, irl-dungeon, 88x31. Items are not copied between games; each game asks this table.

- **Database:** D1 `items-db` (id b39d9b77-fb44-4474-82b2-60252578f38a, region OC). Holds 98 items: 4Dungeon's 46 from `rules.js` (12 common, 12 uncommon, 12 rare, 6 mythic, 4 moon; ids 1-46) and 52 original-tier 88x31 buttons (36 common, 16 uncommon; ids 47-98).
- **Read API** (`src/worker.js`, GET only, public, CORS open so the itch.io page can call it):
  - `GET /api/items`: active items. `?source=4dungeon`, `?rarity=moon`, `?all=1` (include retired).
  - `GET /api/items/:id`: one item, retired ones too, so an old find always resolves.
- **Rules the database enforces:** items are never deleted (retire them with `retired = 1`); an item's id, source, source_key, rarity and created_at never change; ids only count up. A game stores an item by id.
- **Columns:** `source` + `source_key` say where it came from (`4dungeon` / `COMMON:3`; later `88x31` / design id; `irl-dungeon`). `alignment` (LAW/CHAOS/NEUTRAL) and `nature` (tech/spirit/both) are 4Dungeon's. `type` and `image` are for 88x31 buttons. `extra` is JSON for a game's own details (4Dungeon: `has_use`, `use_text`, `both_name`). The effect code for the three items with a use stays in 4Dungeon.

## Adding items
Write a `seed/*.json` list and run `node scripts/seed-sql.mjs seed/x.json`, then run the SQL on the live database. It is `INSERT OR IGNORE`: re-running adds nothing and never overwrites an edited item. `scripts/extract-4dungeon.mjs ../daily-dungeon/rules.js` rebuilds `seed/4dungeon.json` from 4Dungeon (it only reads rules.js).

## 88x31 buttons
`src/buttons.js` turns 88x31's public catalog (`GET https://88x31.app/api/designs`) into items: original tier, common or uncommon, uncapped, active, not hidden. Each keeps its name, type and picture address (`https://88x31.app/api/img?d=N`); no credit or license is stored. The table is a snapshot: refresh with `node scripts/sync-88x31.mjs` (run where 88x31.app is reachable; it fetches the API, or pass a saved copy) then `node scripts/seed-sql.mjs seed/88x31.json` and run the SQL. The first load (2026-10-15) used the same filter run against 88x31's database through the Cloudflare connector, since this session's shell cannot reach 88x31.app.

## The copy registry
Every numbered copy of an item, across all the games, and who holds it. Copy numbers count up per item from 1 with no gaps and are never reused, whichever game makes the copy (until now irl-dungeon counted its own).

- **Tables** (`migrations/002_registry.sql`, also in `schema.sql`): `copies` (item, copy number, the game and key that made it, the holder as game + that game's player id, how many times it has changed hands) and `ledger`, one SHA-256 hash chain of every birth and every move. A copy and its ledger entry are written in one D1 batch, so a copy is born or moved if and only if it is on the chain. Ledger records hold item, copy and game names only: never a player id or a key.
- **Rules the database enforces** (triggers): copies are never deleted; a copy's item, number and birth never change; a copy only changes hands, one move at a time; numbers never skip or repeat; a retired item makes no new copies; the ledger can't be edited or deleted.
- **Not public.** The read API above has no route for copies, and holders are never published. The registry is a Worker entrypoint (`src/rpc.js`, class `Registry`) that only a Worker with a service binding can call. The Worker's entry is `src/index.js` (the read API plus the entrypoint).
- **How a game uses it.** In its `wrangler.jsonc`: `"services": [{ "binding": "REGISTRY", "service": "dungeon-items", "entrypoint": "Registry" }]`. Then:
  - `await env.REGISTRY.birth({ itemId, game, playerId, key })` makes the next copy for that player: `{ itemId, copy, created }`, or `{ error }` (unknown or retired item, bad arguments, a key already used for another item). `key` is the game's own name for the moment (irl-dungeon: its find), so a retry returns the same copy with `created: false`.
  - `await env.REGISTRY.moveCopy({ itemId, copy, from: { game, playerId }, to: { game, playerId } })` hands a copy over: `{ ok: true, moves }` or `{ error }` (not the holder, no such copy, already theirs).
  - `await env.REGISTRY.heldBy(game, playerId)` lists what a player holds: `[{ itemId, copy, moves }]`. `await env.REGISTRY.verify()` checks the whole chain: `{ ok, count, head }`.
- **Limits.** The chain can't show that its newest entries were dropped; keep the `head` that `verify` returns somewhere else. A game names itself in each call and the entrypoint believes it. If more than eight writers race for the same head at the same instant, the last ones get "The registry is busy" and should try again.
- **Going live.** Run `migrations/002_registry.sql` on `items-db`, then deploy this Worker (so the `Registry` entrypoint exists), and only then deploy a game that binds it.

## Not done yet
- 4Dungeon doesn't read the table yet. A button that leaves 88x31's catalog isn't retired automatically.

p12342234/tqgames.readme:
# 商品消除 Match-3（Phaser 3 + GitHub Pages + LiveOps + GAS）

純靜態網頁遊戲：程式與資源由 **GitHub Pages** 託管，玩家進度存在 **Google 試算表（Apps Script）**，活動與商品資源透過 **LiveOps 設定檔 + Texture Atlas** 不改程式即可更新。

```
index.html                 入口（Phaser 由 CDN 載入）
config/game-config.json    ① 遊戲設定檔（Config）：盤面、GAS 網址、基礎商品、難度參數
config/liveops.json        ② LiveOps：活動、新商品/圖集、停用商品、難度補丁、單關熱修、維護模式
assets/atlas/*.png|json    ③ TexturePacker 輸出的 Texture Atlas（每個「包」一組）
art/<pack>/*.png           ④ 原始圖（TexturePacker 的輸入；目前是佔位圖）
src/levelgen.js            ⑤ 關卡生成：組合數 + 倒推法 + 難度曲線（純函式，瀏覽器/Node 共用）
src/match3.js              ⑥ 消除規則（找連線、重力、洗牌、可走步驗證）
src/scenes/*.js            Preload / Menu / Game 場景
src/profile.js             ⑦ Gamer Profile（本機 + GAS 同步，離線可玩）
gas/Code.gs                ⑧ Google Apps Script 後端
tools/                     simulate.mjs（機器人測難度）、pack.sh（TexturePacker）、make_placeholder_art.py
.github/workflows/pages.yml  push 到 main 自動部署
```

## 快速開始

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080      # 或 npm run serve；不能直接用 file:// 開
# 開 http://localhost:8080
node tools/simulate.mjs 20       # 機器人模擬各關勝率
```

## 1. 關卡設計：組合數 + 倒推法 + 無限關卡

第 `L` 關完全由 `hash(L, levelSalt, 商品數)` 決定（**同一關永遠相同**，不用存關卡資料，也能無限延伸）。

**組合數（Combinations）**
- 商品池 `N` 種（核心 6 + 活動商品），第 L 關用 `k = 4 + ⌊(L-1)/15⌋`（上限 7）種上場。
- 用 combinadic（組合數系統）把亂數索引轉成「第 idx 個 C(N,k) 子集」→ 本關上場商品。
- 同樣方式從 k 種裡挑 `m` 種當**過關目標**（`m = 1 + ⌊(L-1)/15⌋`，上限 3）。
- 目前 N=8、k=4 就有 C(8,4)=70 種商品組合 × C(4,m) 種目標組合 × 預埋位置的排列；**LiveOps 每多一種商品，組合空間就倍數成長**。

**倒推法（Backward Induction / Reverse Engineering）— 從「過關」往回推盤面**
1. 先決定終點：目標每種收集 `count` 個。
2. 往回推最少需要 `par = Σ⌈count/3⌉` 次 match-3。
3. 把其中最多 6 個「一步可完成」的解法**預埋進盤面**（4 種 2×3 圖樣＋轉置，共 8 種）：兩個目標已並排、第三個在斜角，交換一次即消。預埋時由上往下排序成 `level.solution`，所以此關**保證有解**，且已知最短路徑。
4. **時間限制** = 預期步數 × 每步秒數：預期步數 = `par × (1.2 + 0.12·(色數−4) + 0.1·(目標種類−1))`，每步秒數從 6.5 秒緩降到 5.5 秒，取整到 5 秒並限制在 45–240 秒。
5. 其餘格用 seeded RNG 填入且不產生現成三連，最後整盤驗證，失敗就換 attempt 重生。

**難度曲線**（皆在 `config.difficulty`，可由 LiveOps `difficultyPatch` 即時覆寫）

| 手段 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 商品種類 4→7 | 盤面更雜，連線機率下降 |
| 目標 1→3 種、數量 `9 + 2·L^0.6`（上限 54） | 需要更多有效消除 |
| 每步秒數 6.5→5.5、BOSS 時間 ×0.92 | 時間逐步變緊，但永遠給足思考空間 |
| 每 10 關 BOSS（目標×1.2、時間 −8%）＋下一關喘息（時間 +10%） | 鋸齒節奏，避免只有單調變難 |

> 難度有「漸近上限」而非無限疊加，否則後期會變成不可能；後期靠 BOSS 與組合變化維持新鮮感。

## 1.5 時間限制與「悠閒玩到 100 關」

**玩法**：每關有一條計時進度條（綠→黃→紅），時間歸零即失敗；沒有步數限制。
- **碰盤面才開始計時**：進關可以先看盤面，輕觸盤面才開跑。
- **動畫與連鎖結算期間不扣時間**：看特效不吃時間。
- **連鎖加時**：連鎖 ×2 加 1.5 秒、×3 加 3 秒、×4 以上加 4.5 秒（不超過該關上限）。
- **失敗輔助**：同一關每連續失敗一次，下次多給 15% 時間（最多 4 次，約 +60%），通關後歸零。失敗次數只存本機。
- **星星**依剩餘時間評定：≥40% 三星、≥15% 兩星。

**休閒度驗證**（`node tools/simulate.mjs`）：機器人不受限制地玩，量測需要幾步過關，再用「真人每步秒數」換算在時間內過關的比例。

| 每步秒數 | 第 1–50 關 | 第 60–100 關（BOSS 為最差情況） |
|---|---|---|
| 3 秒（俐落） | 100% | 100% |
| 4.5 秒（休閒） | 100% | 95–100% |
| 6 秒（慢慢想） | 100% | 80–95%，非 BOSS 關更高 |

另外有連鎖加時與失敗輔助當緩衝，所以一般玩家應能輕鬆走到 100 關。完整的 1–100 關設計表見 [`docs/levels-1-100.md`](docs/levels-1-100.md)（`node tools/level-table.mjs > docs/levels-1-100.md` 重新產生）。

注意：機器人是貪婪策略、不會思考，只能當相對指標；上線後請用 `LevelStats` 的真實勝率校準，必要時用 `difficultyPatch`（例如調 `secStart`/`secEnd`）或 `levelOverrides`（例如 `{"37":{"timeDelta":20}}`）即時調整。

## 2. LiveOps（不改程式碼就更新）

玩家每次開啟遊戲都會抓 `config/liveops.json`（以 `cacheMinutes` 分桶避開 CDN 舊快取，失敗則用上次快取），**只改 JSON 然後 push 就生效**：

| 欄位 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `events[]` | 活動（`start`/`end` 含時區，到期自動下架）；可帶 `scoreMultiplier`、`extraSeconds`（每關加秒數）、新 `packs`（圖集）、新 `tiles`（商品） |
| `disabledTiles` | 緊急下架有問題的商品 |
| `difficultyPatch` | 覆寫難度參數（例：`{"slackEnd":1.6}`） |
| `levelOverrides` | 單關熱修（例：`{"10":{"timeDelta":15}}`、`{"37":{"time":120}}`） |
| `maintenance` | 維護模式，`enabled:true` 時主選單鎖住開始鈕 |

新增活動商品流程：把圖放 `art/tiles-xxx/` → `bash tools/pack.sh tiles-xxx` → `liveops.json` 新增 event（含 `packs`/`tiles`）→ push。圖集更新時把該 pack 的 `version` +1（載入時以 `?v=` 破快取）。

注意：商品池改變會改變 `N`，活動期間的關卡內容會與平常不同（組合空間變大）；若需要「不論活動與否同一關都一樣」，可把 `levelSalt`/商品池鎖定在核心商品，只讓活動商品當裝飾關。

## 3. Texture Atlas（TexturePacker）

- `bash tools/pack.sh` 會把 `art/<pack>/` 每個資料夾打包成 `assets/atlas/<pack>.png|json`（`--format phaser` = JSON Hash）。
- 遊戲以 `this.load.atlas(key, png, json)` 載入，`config.tiles[].frame` 對應圖集內的影格名稱。
- 目前 `assets/atlas/` 內是 `tools/make_placeholder_art.py` 產生的**相容格式佔位圖**（沒有 TexturePacker 也能跑）；換成正式美術時覆蓋即可，程式不用改。

## 4. Gamer Profile（Google Apps Script + 試算表）

部署步驟：
1. 建立 Google 試算表 → 擴充功能 → Apps Script → 貼上 `gas/Code.gs` → 執行一次 `setup()`（會建立 `Profiles`、`Runs` 分頁並授權）。
2. 部署 → 新增部署作業 → **網頁應用程式**；執行身分「我」、存取權「任何人」→ 複製 `/exec` 網址。
3. 填入 `config/game-config.json` 的 `gas.url`，push。

運作方式：
- 玩家以匿名 `playerId`（UUID）+ 暱稱識別；進度先存 `localStorage`，離線也能玩，結算資料進 outbox，連線後補傳。
- `sync`：雲端與本機合併（每關最佳分數/星數取最大、關卡取最大）。`result`：每局寫入 `Runs`（關卡、勝敗、分數、步數、時間上限、已用時間、活動 ID）。
- 簡易防作弊：宣稱的關卡不得超過「已通關最高關 + 1」、分數上限、暱稱公式注入過濾、`LockService` 防並發寫入；異常資料在 `flag` 欄標記。
- `rebuildLevelStats()` 會把 `Runs` 彙整成 `LevelStats`（各關勝率、過關時平均剩餘秒數），可設定時間觸發器每日執行；拿來決定要調 `levelOverrides` 還是 `difficultyPatch` —— 這就是 LiveOps 的閉環。

限制：匿名 ID 存在瀏覽器，清除資料會失去進度。若要跨裝置綁定帳號，可加 Google 登入並在 GAS 以 `oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo` 驗證 ID token，改用 Google 帳號 sub 當 `playerId`。

## 5. 部署到 GitHub

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m "init"
git branch -M main && git remote add origin https://github.com/<你>/<repo>.git && git push -u origin main
```
Repo → Settings → Pages → Source 選 **GitHub Actions**。之後每次 push 會先跑關卡生成冒煙測試，再部署。
