bilbiall/SNL.readme:
﻿# Snakes & Liquor 🐍🥃

A party board game: roll the dice, dodge the snakes, and find out who takes the shot, picks a friend, states a fact or breaks a rule. Play on **one phone** (party mode) or **online** with a 5-letter room code — no accounts for players.

Built on Laravel 12. Forked from the Pesa Mine arcade engine; money, wagers and XP are gone, replaced by **cards**.

## What's in the box

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| Table engine (turns, cards, prompts, win) | `app/Services/GameEngine.php` |
| Game vocabulary (modes, tile kinds, powers, timings) | `config/snl.php` |
| Play screen | `resources/views/play.blade.php` + `public/js/snl-play.js` |
| Admin (**GameSet**) — boards, squares, cards | `/gameset` |
| Starter content | `database/seeders` (board, cards, admin) |
| Plan & decisions | `docs/BUILD-PLAN.md` |

## Modes

* **Drinks** 🥃 — 18+ only, with an age confirmation.
* **Family** 🎈 — zero alcohol.
* **Spicy** 🔥 — reserved (disabled).

Same board, same rules — only the card deck changes. Intensity (Chill / Normal / Wild) filters which cards can appear.

## Local setup

```bash
composer install
cp .env.example .env && php artisan key:generate
# create an empty database named snakesandliquor, then:
php artisan migrate --seed
npm install && npm run build
php artisan serve
```

The seeder creates an admin from `SNL_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SNL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env` — **change them before deploying.** Sign in at `/login`.

## How a square plays

| Square | What happens |
|---|---|
| **You do it / Pick a friend / Everyone / Duel / Swap / Rule** | A card for the table (the roller picks the target where it says so). |
| **True or false** | The game states a fact; the roller calls it. Right = pass. Wrong = a penalty (set per card: 1 or 2 units — a sip/shot, or a forfeit in Family mode). The answer never leaves the server until the reveal. |
| **Fact or bluff** | The roller says a fact out loud (true or invented). Anyone can *call bluff*. A neutral judge (or the table, in party mode) rules: proven → the caller pays; caught → the roller pays. Nobody calls → safe. |
| **Spotlight** | A creative prompt on a clock — a movie for the moment, a song, a hot take. Fail it and take the penalty. |
| **Mystery spin** | Spins into any of the above. |
| **Free square** | Calm by default — a breather or a hydration nudge. But about 4 in 10 landings now do something small and fun: a **Quickfire** 10-second challenge, a **Roll again** bonus turn, a free **Shield** gift, or a **Group game** everybody joins. Tune it in `config/snl.php` (`free_event_chance`, `free_events`) and write more lines in GameSet → Cards (kinds *Quickfire*, *Group game*, *Free gift*, *Roll again*). |
| **Love ladder** | A sweet moment — compliments, memories, toasts. No penalty. |

Intensity (**Chill / Normal / Spicy**) decides which cards can appear and how hard penalties bite.

## Keeping it fresh — content that grows

* **Cards** (GameSet → Cards) are tagged by kind, mode (Drinks, Family, or *All modes*) and intensity.
* **Templates**: card text can contain `{you}`, `{other}` (a random player) and any word-list slot such as `{scene}`, `{vibe}`, `{genre}`, `{hot_topic}`. One card — *"Recommend a movie for {scene}"* — reads differently every time.
* **Words** (GameSet → Words) hold the slot lists. Add hundreds; add brand-new slots just by naming them.
* Bulk-add both: one per line. True-or-false lines look like `T | statement | optional explanation`.

## Players, start zone and joining late

* **Start zone** (GameSet → Boards → *Start zone*): drag a green box over the area where players wait before their first roll (the START sign works well). They spread out inside it instead of stacking on square 1, then hop onto the board when they roll. Remove it to go back to square 1.
* **Add a player mid-game** (party mode): hamburger menu → *Add a player*. They take a seat at the start zone and play last in the order (up to 12 players).

## Boards

The game ships with **Neon Night** (80 squares, 5 ladders, 5 snakes) — `database/seeders/data/snl-night.php` holds its artwork path, how the 6 rows of squares sit on the image, every square type and the ladder/snake links. `php artisan db:seed --class=BoardSeeder` creates it (once) and makes it the only active board.

## Your own board art

1. GameSet → **Boards** → **New board**: upload the art and say how many squares it has.
2. Drag every numbered square onto its spot (desktop layout; the mobile-landscape tab is optional).
3. Set what each square does, then tick **Active**.

Positions are stored as a percentage of the image, so any artwork works.

## Deploying (cPanel)

* Point the domain at `public/`.
* `.env`: production DB, `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, and keep `SESSION_DRIVER=file` / `CACHE_STORE=file` (the file cache provides the per-room action lock).
* `php artisan migrate --force && php artisan db:seed --force` (first time), `npm run build` (locally, then upload `public/build`).
* Make `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` writable; `public/uploads/boards` receives board art.
* Cron: `* * * * * php /path/to/artisan schedule:run` (purges idle rooms nightly).

## Responsible play

Drinks mode is for adults. Every screen reminds players that any drink can be swapped for water and that they should never drive after drinking.

## Credits & licences

* **Hero avatars** — 12 original comic-style heroes drawn in code (`scripts/lib/heroes.mjs`). They are not based on any Marvel/DC/other character and use no third-party names or emblems.
* **Retro avatars** — the pixel-art character style from [DiceBear](https://www.dicebear.com/styles/pixel-art/) (CC0 / public domain). 16 looks × 7 skin shades are generated by `npm run avatars` (`scripts/build-avatars.mjs`) into `public/avatars/` and committed, so production needs no extra build.
* **Rookie avatars** — 12 original streetwear characters (headphones, bucket hats, hijab, locs, buns…) drawn in code (`scripts/lib/genz.mjs`).
* **Bar Crew avatars*

# Books Library

A catalogue of all the books in our house.

## Goals

- **Scan to add.** Scan a book's barcode (ISBN) with a phone camera and add it to the library, with title, author and cover filled in automatically.
- **Manual entry.** Some books have no ISBN (older books, local prints, gifts), so they can be added by hand with title, author and any other details.
- **Wishlist.** Keep a separate list of books we want but don't own yet, and move them into the library once bought.
- **Browse and search.** Find any book in the house quickly by title, author or where it's shelved.

## How it works

A static web app (no build step). Open it on your phone, then:

- **Scan** opens the camera and reads the ISBN barcode (native `BarcodeDetector`, with ZXing as a fallback). Details come from Open Library, then Google Books. You can also type an ISBN.
- **Works offline and installs to the home screen** (open the site, then use the browser menu: Add to Home Screen). Looking up a new ISBN still needs internet.
- **Lookup tries four sources at once** (Open Library x3, Google Books). Books none of them know open the form with the ISBN filled in.
- **Optional cloud sync** to a free Supabase project (see `docs/SYNC.md`) so the library survives a lost phone and works on several devices.
- **Add by hand** for books with no ISBN.
- **Shelf/room, reading status (unread/reading/read) and "lent to"**, with filters for each (including a "Lent out" filter).
- **Library / Wishlist** tabs, search, and a "Got it" button that moves a wishlist book into the library.
- Data is stored in the browser (`localStorage`) on that device. Use **Export backup / Import backup** to move or save it.

Camera access needs https (or localhost). Run locally with `python3 -m http.server`, or host it free on GitHub Pages: merge to `main`, then in the repo go to Settings > Pages and set Source to "GitHub Actions". The workflow in `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes it at `https://<user>.github.io/repo-books-library/`. (`netlify.toml` is also included for Netlify.)

## Using it

1. Open https://ayushthaosen-gif.github.io/repo-books-library/ on your phone and add it to the home screen.
2. **Scan** a book's barcode (the one with the ISBN on the back). Check the details, tap Save, and the scanner reopens for the next book. Untick "Keep scanning" to scan one at a time.
3. No barcode? Tap **Add by hand**, or type the ISBN in the scan window.
4. Put a book on the **Wishlist** by choosing that list when you add it; tap **Got it** when you buy it.
5. Sort by newest, title or author, and filter by shelf, reading status or lent out.
6. Turn on sync once (docs/SYNC.md) so the library is kept safe off the phone.

Holmes-Leighton/Pet-Part-Hunter.readme:
# Pet Part Hunter

Roblox game: hunt pet parts while a mythic creature chases you, escape with your haul, and build mix-and-match pets.

See [docs/GAME_DESIGN_SPEC.md](docs/GAME_DESIGN_SPEC.md) for the full design specification.

## Status (build order, spec section 10)

| Step | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Chase prototype (Common area, chaser, bag, escape) | Done |
| 2. Data layer and validation (profile, session lock, rate-limited remotes, analytics) | Done |
| 3. Speed pads, levels, rebirth | Done (Apex comes after launch tuning) |
| 4. Part pipeline: part table, inventory, merge, pet building, Part Index, crafting UI | Done for all 48 placeholder species (shared pet rig, meshes and animations come with the art pipeline) |
| 5. All six areas, chaser scaling, gamepass and rebirth gating | Done (area mazes, 48 species, per-area chaser speed, free route + pass early access; pass IDs in Config.Passes are 0 until you create the passes) |
| 6. Home building (plot, starter room, furniture shop, placement ghost, move/rotate/delete, visitors, pets wandering) | Done |
| 7. Economy: selling parts, bag upgrades, pet slots, passes, Robux products (coin packs, luck boost, insurance), receipt handling, purchase announcements, everyone sees everyone's pets | Done (pass and product IDs in Config are 0 until you create them on Roblox) |
| 8. Trading: two-sided window (lock, countdown, confirm), eligibility, cooldown, lopsided warning, atomic swap, backend trade log | Done |
| 9. Admin panel, events system, monitoring and anti-exploit, dashboard feed | Done |
| 10. Closed test on phones, tune from the monitoring data, launch | Next (needs real devices and players) |
## Running

- Pure-logic tests: `python tests/run_tests.py` (set `LUAU` and `LUAU_ANALYZE` to the luau tool paths if they are not on PATH).
- In Studio: `rojo serve`, then connect from the Rojo plugin. Studio has no DataStore access by default, so players get temporary,
  unsaved data (`DataPersistent` attribute is false). Enable API access in Game Settings to test saving.
- Studio playtest helpers: set the `DebugChaserSpeed` workspace attribute, or `player:SetAttribute("DebugAddCoins", n)` to test pad buying. Building a pet costs coins and selling parts arrives with the economy step, so use DebugAddCoins to try it. Also `player:SetAttribute("DebugGrantPass", "Area_Mythic")` unlocks a paid area, and `player:SetAttribute("DebugAddCoins", n)` adds coins (needed for the furniture shop until selling exists).
- Where things live: `src/Shared` is pure rules (tested), `src/Server` and `src/Client` connect them to Roblox.

## Trade log (backend)

Every trade window that ends is recorded: completed, cancelled, expired and failed. See `src/Server/TradeLogger.lua`.

- **DataStore** `Config.Backend.TradeStore`: one record per trade under `T<epoch>_<id>`, plus a per-player index `P<userId>` (their most recent trades).
  A completed trade is written **before** the items move. If the record cannot be saved the trade does not happen (Studio excepted).
- **Your own backend (optional):** set `Config.Backend.TradeLogUrl`, enable HttpService, and store the API key as a Roblox secret named `Config.Backend.SecretName`.
  Records are POSTed as JSON with retries in the background.
- **Server output:** one summary line per trade, a warning when flagged (`lopsided`, `volume_<userId>`).
- **Crash recovery (automatic):** a trade moves items between two profiles that are saved separately, so each profile carries a journal
  (`Shared/TradeRecovery`). Order: mark the trade pending in both and save, write the record (the commit point), swap, mark applied and save.
  When a profile loads with a pending trade the server reads the record: none, or a later `_f` record = the trade never happened, so the note
  is dropped; a completed record = the trade happened, so that player's side is applied now (if not already). It is idempotent, each player
  recovers independently, and the tests simulate a crash at every step. Until it is settled the player cannot start another trade.
- **Reading it:** `TradeLogger.history(userId)`, `TradeLogger.get(key)` and `TradeLogger.recent()` for the admin panel. The record shape is `Shared/TradeLog` (tested).

## Events, admin tools and monitoring (build step 9)

**Events** are data, not code (`Shared/Events`, `Server/EventStore`, `Server/EventService`). An admin creates one in the panel (presets for the spec's event types, or
paste a JSON record); it is validated, stored in a DataStore and picked up by every server (refresh timer plus MessagingService). One record can carry modifiers
(luck, coins, speed gain, chaser speed), exclusive parts, a whole event area (a new maze with its own chaser, built while the event runs), a community goal, or a
chaos effect. Event parts are registered before any profile loads and stay registered after the event ends, so saved event parts are never lost; events that have
exclusive parts can be stopped but not deleted. Event parts are non-tradable unless the event says otherwise.

**Admin** (`Shared/Admin`, `Server/AdminService`): set `Config.Admin.Owners / Admins / Mods` (user ids) and/or `GroupId` with `GroupRanks`. In Studio the tester is an owner
(`StudioIsOwner`, never on live servers). Every command is checked on the server (role, validated arguments, a written reason for destructive actions), is written to the
audit log **before** it runs (no record, no action), and denied attempts are logged. Players, coins and parts, kick/ban (reaches all servers), snapshots and rollback,
live tuning (chaser speed, respawn rate, trade switch, per-area chaser and open/closed), events, announcements, metrics and exploit flags. Inventory commands need the target online.
Rolling back keeps trade journals, purchase receipts and passes; anything else earned after the snapshot is undone (the audit log shows what).

# Tamtech WEM Crossword

Live multiplayer crossword (Node.js + WebSocket). 60 words from `words.json` (built from the Excel file), one puzzle per room, one player per team.

## Run locally
```
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
```

## Pages
| Who | URL | Login |
|---|---|---|
| Players | `/` | name + team + 6-digit room code |
| Game Master / Overseer | `/staff.html` | role dropdown + name + password |

Passwords / codes (override with env vars): Game Master `Five9` (`MASTER_PASSWORD`), Overseer `Five9OS` (`OVERSEER_PASSWORD`), terminating code `5959` (`TERMINATION_CODE`).

## Updating the words
```
python -I tools/build_words.py "<new file>.xlsx" words.json
```
Row 1 is skipped. B = word, C = clue, D/E/F = Overseer hints. Restart the server; new rooms use the new words (existing rooms keep theirs).

## Deploy to crossword.worldoftechdev.com
The app needs a host that keeps a Node process running (WebSockets), so static hosting will not work.

**Option A: Render / Railway / Fly (simplest).** Push this folder to a Git repo, create a Web Service (build `npm install`, start `npm start`), attach a persistent disk mounted at `/data` and set `DATA_DIR=/data`. Add `crossword.worldoftechdev.com` as a custom domain and create the CNAME record they show you at your DNS provider. HTTPS is automatic.

**Option B: your own VPS.**
```
docker build -t crossword . && docker run -d --restart=always -p 3000:3000 -v crossword-data:/data -e DATA_DIR=/data crossword
```
Point an `A` record for `crossword` at the server, then put Caddy in front for HTTPS and WebSocket support:
```
crossword.worldoftechdev.com {
    reverse_proxy localhost:3000
}
```

Room state is saved to `DATA_DIR/state.json`, so a restart does not lose active rooms. Run a single instance only (state is in memory).

## Tests
With the server on port 3111: `node tools/e2e.js`

vanyapoker/steam-tui.desc: Lightweight, fast TUI Steam client for Linux (Omarchy). Browse, install, update and launch games without the Steam client.
vanyapoker/steam-tui.readme:
# steam-tui

Lightweight, fast TUI Steam client for Linux (built for Omarchy). Browse, install, update and launch your library without the Steam client or its browser processes.

Early state: some games won't work without original steam client.

![steam-tui](assets/screenshot.png)

- Starts in ~2 ms and uses ~30 MB of memory.
- Install and update games (native and Proton), with pause and resume.
- Friends, live notifications, game changelogs.
- Steam Cloud saves, with a side-by-side local/cloud conflict picker.
- Games run on our own Steam backend, so no Steam process is needed.

![save conflict picker](assets/conflict.png)

## Installation

Built for Omarchy (Arch, x86_64). Windows games need Proton, and a Secret Service keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet) stores your login.

**Prebuilt (fastest):**

```sh
curl -L https://github.com/vanyapoker/steam-tui/releases/latest/download/steam-tui-x86_64-linux.tar.gz | tar -xz -C ~/.local
steam-tui login --account YOUR_STEAM_NAME   # first run only
steam-tui
```

Make sure `~/.local/bin` is in your `PATH`.

**From source** (needs Rust, CMake, make, Perl and a C++ compiler; the first build takes a few minutes):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vanyapoker/steam-tui && cd steam-tui
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` installs to `~/.local` without sudo. Use `PREFIX=/some/path ./install.sh` to change that.

## Hotkeys

Press `?` in the app for the full list.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / double-click | Launch the game |
| Ctrl+Enter | Launch through Valve's Steam client |
| i / u | Install / update |
| p / c | Pause / cancel the download |
| C | Steam Cloud sync |
| n / right-click | Changelog |
| a | Achievements of the selected game (s / S sort, f filter, r reload) |
| / | Filter |
| f | Pin a game |
| v | All / installed / not installed |
| 1-4, s, S | Sort by column, cycle sort, reverse |
| Tab | Switch pane |
| r | Refresh |
| b | Backend traffic |
| q | Quit |

## Steamworks coverage

| Works | Partial | Not yet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User, Utils, Apps, Friends (basics) | Matchmaking and lobbies | Publishing Workshop items |
| Game Coordinator relay | Networking sockets, P2P and relay | Inventory |
| Steam Cloud | Auth tickets | Input, Screenshots |
| Stats, achievements (with icons), leaderboards | Global stats | Friend avatars |
| Workshop: queries, subscriptions, downloads, votes, favorites | | |

Interface versions from SDK 0.99 to 1.65 are served, laid out from Valve's SDK headers: SteamClient 006-021 and 023 (not 022), and every version Valve's public headers ever shipped for User, Utils, Apps, Friends, Matchmaking, Servers, UserStats, Networking, RemoteStorage, Screenshots, HTTP, HTMLSurface, Controller, Inventory, UGC and Input. Where an old version's call has no matching implementation, the slot logs and returns zero. Stats, achievements and leaderboard scores are read from and written to your real Steam account, like the normal client. Workshop items you subscribe to are downloaded in the background into the game's library (`steamapps/workshop/content/<app>/<item>`, recorded in Valve's `appworkshop_<app>.acf`) while the game runs; subscribing, voting, favoriting and the other Workshop calls act on your real account. Publishing items (CreateItem, SubmitItemUpdate) is not supported and reports failure, and so are the voted-on user lists. Unsupported calls log and abort rather than pretend to work.

## Limitations

- VAC-secured games run through Valve's Steam client without its web helpers. It must be signed in to the same account, and costs about 200 MB extra. Enter picks this automatically.
- Online matchmaking and relay networking are unfinished.
- Linux only.

## Not implemented yet

Chat, game invites, publishing Workshop items, store and community pages, trading.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Vendored and third-party code keeps its own license, see [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md).


> Not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve; Steam and VAC are Valve trademarks. steam-tui signs in to your real Steam account through its own client, which Valve's terms may not allow. Use it at your own risk.

jdahlin/ootss-mac.desc: Run Order of the Sinking Star on Apple Silicon Macs: x86_64 PE loader with Win32 shims, D3D12 via Apple's D3DMetal
jdahlin/ootss-mac.readme:
# Order of the Sinking Star on macOS

Runs the Windows build of *Order of the Sinking Star* on Apple Silicon Macs without Wine.

![The game running on an M4 MacBook at ~49 fps](docs/screenshot.webp)

A small x86_64 loader maps `sinking_star.exe` into memory and implements the ~300 Windows functions it
imports on top of macOS: Cocoa for the window and input, CoreAudio for sound, and our own Direct3D 12 on
Metal for graphics. Everything runs under Rosetta 2.

## Requirements

- An Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later and Rosetta 2 (`softwareupdate --install-rosetta`)
- Xcode Command Line Tools
- Your own copy of the game: the Windows build from Steam (the folder containing `sinking_star.exe`)

## Build and run

```sh
make msc     # downloads Apple's Metal Shader Converter library (not bundled; checked against a pinned SHA-256)
make
make run GAME="$HOME/Games/Order of the Sinking Star"
```

`make run` launches the game from an app bundle (`make app` builds `build/Order of the Sinking Star.app`),
which declares it a game so macOS can apply Game Mode. The Dock shows the game's own icon, read from its
executable when it starts; `make app GAME=...` also saves it as the bundle's Finder icon. The icon is never
stored in this repository. The game starts fullscreen as a borderless window with
the Dock and menu bar hidden; `LOADER_WINDOWED=1` starts windowed. Only one copy can run at a time. Saves go
to `~/Library/Application Support/Order of the Sinking Star`.

## Graphics

The game's D3D12 and DXGI calls are implemented on Metal in `src/d3d12/`: command lists are recorded and
replayed into Metal encoders, descriptor heaps become Metal buffers of descriptors, and the game's DXIL
shaders are converted at run time by Apple's Metal Shader Converter against each pipeline's root signature.
The first launch converts all 257 shaders, which takes a few seconds; the results are cached in
`~/Library/Caches/ootss-mac/shaders` (keyed by the shader, its root signature and the converter build).
Delete that folder to force a fresh conversion. Nothing derived from the game is stored in this repository.

At 2940x1912 on an M4 it runs about 28 fps against about 21 fps through D3DMetal, and the frames match
except for anti-aliasing at edges.

Not implemented: `ExecuteIndirect` count buffers and per-command root constants, depth resolve, UAV counters,
typed buffer views, queries and timestamps.

### D3DMetal (fallback)

`LOADER_D3D=d3dmetal` uses Apple's D3DMetal instead. Download the Game Porting Toolkit from Apple, copy
`D3DMetal.framework` to `build/D3DMetal.framework` (or set `D3DMETAL_FRAMEWORK_PATH`), and
`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` it if macOS blocks it. Then `make d3dmetal` builds
[d3dmetal-native](https://github.com/utmapp/d3dmetal-native) (MIT), which hosts it; the loader opens it with
`dlopen` only when this backend is selected (`brew install meson ninja`).

## Options

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `LOADER_FPS=1` | Show fps and frame time in the window title |
| `LOADER_MUTE=1` | Play no sound (the game's audio clock keeps running) |
| `LOADER_WINDOWED=1` | Start windowed instead of fullscreen |
| `LOADER_RENDER_SCALE=0.5` | Render at a fraction of the screen resolution (0.1 to 1); the layer stretches it to fit. Faster, softer |
| `D3D12_PROFILE=1` | Log GPU time per pass and compute shader, averaged per frame |
| `LOADER_DISPLAY=native` | Report the real screen resolution to the game instead of the window size |
| `LOADER_TRACE=1` | Log Win32 calls (verbose) |
| `D3D12_LOG_GPU=1` | Log GPU time per frame |
| `D3D12_LOG_PRESENT=1` | Check that the back buffer is not black; `D3D12_DUMP_FRAME=file.ppm` saves a frame |
| `D3D12_MAX_PRESENTS=n` | Exit after n frames (bounded debug runs) |
| `D3D12_NO_PRESENT=1` | Never show frames (benchmarking) |
| `D3D12_VSYNC=1` | Sync presentation to the display (off by default for lower input latency; `DMN_VSYNC` for D3DMetal) |
| `D3D12_DUMP_SHADERS=dir` | Write every DXIL shader the game creates pipelines from (for study; do not commit) |
| `D3D12_LOG_PSO=1`, `D3D12_LOG_ROOTSIG=1` | Log pipeline states and root signature layouts |
| `MTL_HUD_ENABLED=1` | Apple's Metal performance HUD |

Turn off Low Power Mode when playing; it roughly halves the frame rate.

## Status

Playable with keyboard, mouse and sound. Not done: gamepads, Steam features (achievements, cloud
saves), the clipboard. Steam is stubbed as "running, offline".

## Layout

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/loader.c` | PE loader, import binding, TEB/TLS through `%gs`, crash reports, `main` |
| `src/win32.h` | The Windows types, structures and constants we use, size-checked against x64 Windows |
| `src/shim.h` | Shim registration (`SHIM(...)`), logging and shared declarations |
| `src/sync.c` | Threads, events, semaphores, waits, critical sections |
| `src/files.c` | Files, directory search, file mappings, console output |
| `src/kernel32.c` | Virtual memory, heaps, time, system information, modules |
| `src/crt.c` | Universal CRT and VCRUNTIME, including Windows `printf` and `setjmp` |
| `src/window.m` | Window, message queue and display metrics on Cocoa |
| `src/input.m` | Keyboard, mouse and Raw Input |
| `src/audio.c` | MMDevice/WASAPI on CoreAudio (for the game's Wwise) |
| `src/d3d.m` | Chooses the graphics backend (ours, or D3DMetal as a fallback) |
| `third_party/` | Vendored headers: Microsoft's DirectX-Headers (MIT) and Apple's Metal Shader Converter headers (Apache-2.0) |
| `src/d3d12/` | D3D12 and DXGI on Metal: `device.m`, `dxgi.m`, `queue.m`, `list.m` (recording), `replay.m` (Metal encoders), `resource.m`, `descriptor.m`, `rootsig.m`, `pipeline.m`, `shader.m` (converter and cache), `binding.m` (Apple's runtime header), `profile.m` |
| `resources/Info.plist` | Game Mode and app metadata, embedded in the executable and the app bundle |
| `src/misc.c` | Registry, COM, shell, dbghelp |
| `src/steam.c` | Steam, reported as running but offline |
| `src/strings.c` | UTF-16, pa

mattschiering/pitch-hitch-ditch.readme:
# Pitch, Hitch, or Ditch

Online version of the buyer-journey pitching game. Teams join from their own devices and see only their own cards. The host projects `host.html` for the room.

| Page | Who | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | Students | Join with a game code and team name; see your own cards, timer and results |
| `host.html` | Host / judges | Create the game, deal cards, run the 90-second timer, judge pitches |
| `local.html` | Anyone | Single-screen version with no backend (host enters team names, everyone shares one screen) |

## One-time setup

1. **Supabase project:** create one at supabase.com (free tier is fine).
2. **Enable anonymous sign-ins:** Authentication > Sign In / Providers > turn on **Anonymous Sign-Ins**. Students don't need accounts; this gives each device a private identity so their hand stays private.
3. **Create the tables:** open the SQL Editor, paste all of `supabase/schema.sql`, and run it.
4. **Add your keys:** Project Settings > API. Copy the **Project URL** and the **anon / public key** into `config.js`. (The anon key is meant to be public; the rules in `schema.sql` protect the data.)
5. **Publish on GitHub Pages:** push this folder to a GitHub repo, then Settings > Pages > deploy from the branch. Students use `https://<you>.github.io/<repo>/`; you use `.../host.html`.

## Running a game

1. Open `host.html`, click **Create Game**, and project it. A 5-letter code appears.
2. Students open the site, enter the code and a team name. Teams appear on the projector.
3. Click **Start Game**. Each team's cards appear on their own device when you click **Start Prep Timer** (90 seconds, all teams at once).
4. When time's up, teams pitch live one at a time. Click **Pass** or **Fail**.
5. Everyone draws new cards each round. A passed Journey stage is kept and never dealt again. A team finishes when it has all four.

**Keep the host tab open** for the whole game; it drives the timer and round flow. If it reloads, it resumes the same game, though the persona and product decks reshuffle.

## Customising

Edit `cards.js` to change personas, products, journey stages or `PREP_SECONDS`.

## How privacy works

Each team's cards live in the `hands` table. Row-level security lets only the owning device and the host read a hand, so other teams can't see it even from their browser tools.

darthreckoner/sensory-town.readme:
# Sensory Town

A cozy, touch-first **3D toy town** for iPad (and desktop browsers): dress up, drive around, build houses in a shared town, and visit the sensory workshop to squish squishies, stretch slime and crack wax-coated squishies. No scores, no timers, no fail states. Everything works **offline** once installed.

Built with Vite + TypeScript + Three.js. All models, textures and sounds are generated in code — no downloads, no network.

---

**Live (installable, works offline): https://darthreckoner.github.io/sensory-town/**

## Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the printed URL (e.g. `http://localhost:5173`). The dev server also listens on your LAN (`http://<your-pc-ip>:5173`) so you can try it on an iPad on the same Wi-Fi — but a LAN dev server **can't be installed with offline support** (that needs HTTPS, see below).

Handy test URLs: `?scene=wax`, `?scene=squishy`, `?scene=slime`, `?scene=town`, `?scene=build`, `?scene=dressup` jump straight to an activity.

## Build

```bash
npm run build      # type-checks, then writes the static site to dist/
npm run preview    # serves dist/ locally to sanity-check the production build
```

`npm run build` produces a fully static `dist/` folder: HTML, JS, icons, the web-app manifest and a service worker that precaches every file.

## Deploy (HTTPS is required for installing to the Home Screen)

### Option A — GitHub Pages (set up in this repo)

The workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds and publishes on every push to `main`.

1. Push the repo to GitHub.
2. In the repo: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**.
3. Push to `main` (or run the workflow manually from the **Actions** tab).
4. The site appears at `https://<your-user>.github.io/<repo-name>/`.

The workflow sets `BASE=/<repo-name>/` so all paths work under the project sub-folder.

### Option B — Netlify or Cloudflare Pages

Build command `npm run build`, publish directory `dist`, and set the environment variable `BASE=/` (root-hosted). Or drag-and-drop a locally built `dist/` (built with `BASE=/ npm run build`) onto Netlify Drop.

## Install on the iPad (one-time, needs Wi-Fi)

1. On each iPad open **Safari** (must be Safari) and go to the HTTPS URL.
2. Wait a few seconds on the first screen so the game can save itself for offline use.
3. Tap the **Share** button → **Add to Home Screen** → **Add**.
4. Launch **Sensory Town** from the Home Screen icon (it opens full-screen, landscape).
5. **Offline check:** turn on **Airplane Mode**, close the app (swipe it away), open it again from the Home Screen. It should load and play normally.

Saves live on the iPad (IndexedDB) and survive restarts. The game asks the browser to keep its storage persistent.

### Sound on iPad
- The game's sound starts after the first tap (the "Who is playing?" screen).
- **The iPad's silent / ring switch (or Control Center silent mode) can mute web-app sound.** If there's no sound, turn silent mode off and turn the volume up.
- Volumes are in the 🏠 menu → **Sound**. Music in the workshop is off by default (toggle there).

## Two iPads: sharing a town

There is no live sync (the game is offline-only). To swap towns:

1. On iPad A: 🏠 menu → **Share Town** → AirDrop it to iPad B (or save to Files).
2. On iPad B: save the file to Files, then 🏠 menu → **Get Town** → pick the file → confirm.

The file contains the whole shared town **and** every player profile (outfits, cars, creations). Importing replaces the town on that iPad.

## How to play (for grown-ups)

v3 plays like Fortnite with all the combat removed. Touch controls are on screen; PC keys are in brackets.

- **Lobby:** tap your player (✏️ renames, ＋ adds a player), then **PLAY**. LOCKER and STUDIO sit right above it.
- **Party bus:** tap **JUMP!** [Space], skydive, and the glider opens; land anywhere. "Skip" puts you at your ride.
- **On foot:**
  - left stick moves; drag the right side of the screen to look [WASD + mouse drag];
  - JUMP [Space];
  - sprint by pushing the stick fully or double-tapping it [Shift];
  - SLIDE while sprinting [Ctrl / X];
  - walk into ledges to climb them; swim in water;
  - fall from a height or hit a bouncy launch pad and the glider opens;
  - ziplines: walk to a post and tap **Zip!** [E / F].
- **Rides:** walk up to any parked ride and tap **Drive** [E / F]. The 🚗 button calls your favourite ride [C]. The sports car, pickup, golf cart, hoverboard, ice-cream truck and boat all handle differently.
- **Build anywhere:** 🔨 [B]. Pick wall / floor / ramp / roof [1–4] and wood / brick / metal [T]. Tap to place; hold and sweep to place a run.
  - **Edit** [G] cuts windows, doors and arches.
  - **Decor** [V] places furniture inside.
  - **Starter** stamps a cabin, a townhouse or a ramp park.
  - **Undo** [U], **Delete** [X].
- **Emotes:** 😀 [Q] opens the wheel. Each dance has its own tune; moving stops it.
- **Locker** (☰ → Locker): outfits (skins and styles), Custom (piece-by-piece styling plus Face), back bling, glider, contrail, emote wheel, ride paint. Locked items show how many 💎 charms they need.
- **Charms:** 64 are hidden all over the island (rooftops, landmarks, glide-only spots). They unlock Locker items with a reveal card. Nothing is ever lost or timed.
- **Studio:** walk into the Studio building or use ☰ → Studio. 🧸 Squishy, 🫧 Slime, 🕯️ Wax (pick, then coat, then crack).
- **☰ menu:** Island / Locker / Build / Studio / Audio / Island Swap (share or import between iPads) / Switch player.

## Debug

| Key | What |
|---|---|
| `` ` `` | Toggle the debug overlay (fps, scene, draw calls, key tuning) — iPad: **three-finger tap** |
| F1 | Reset the current station |
| F2 | Fill the town with test houses |
| F3 | Wax harden time = 0 |

All tunable numbers live in `src/tuning.ts`. Dev builds also expose `window.__selftest.run()` (bug repro suite) and `window.__telemetry` (event log, errors, render cost). Playtest protocol for the kids: `docs/KIDS_PLAYTEST.md`.

peterdk31/spellmerge.readme:
# Spellmerge

*Merge spells. Cause chaos. Together.* · *Every spell is a merge request.*

A 2D top-down roguelite about building deep, combinable spells, for 1–4 local co-op players. Assemble spells from a form, an element, modifiers and triggers (a trigger holds another spell), find relics that bend the rules, and fight through rooms with up to three friends on one screen, with nobody ever waiting for anybody.

**Play:** [in the browser](https://peterdk31.github.io/spellmerge/play/) · [today's nightly](https://peterdk31.github.io/spellmerge/nightly/) · [Windows and Linux downloads](https://github.com/peterdk31/spellmerge/releases)

**Status:** milestone M1, the core loop prototype. The infrastructure (M0) is in place, and the first playable loop is being built. See the [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md).

## Built by an AI, in the open

Claude, an AI by Anthropic, writes the code, reviews every pull request and ships a new build every day, all on GitHub's servers. The owner (@peterdk31) sets the vision in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) and controls the protected infrastructure. Every AI change is made by the **spellmerge-bot** account, so it's always visible as such, and every bot action is listed in the pinned **Daily log** issue.

Human contributors are welcome and credited: code, pixel art, music, sound and writing. Art, music and text can be submitted without git, through issue forms. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), or [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) if you use a coding agent.

## Free on the web forever

The web version and the daily desktop builds stay free; the Steam version (later) funds development. No ads, no microtransactions.

## License

Code: [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE). Assets: CC-BY-SA-4.0, unless a file says otherwise (see [REUSE.toml](REUSE.toml)). Contributors sign the [CLA](CLA.md). A copyright concern? Use the **Report a copyright concern** issue form; the asset is taken out of the next build while it's checked. GitHub's DMCA process also applies.

## For maintainers

- [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md): the full plan
- [docs/NEXT.md](docs/NEXT.md): what Claude works on next
- [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md): why things are the way they are
- `tools/check.sh`: the hard rules on your local changes; `ci/build/build.sh`: a full local build

dogannahmet/yilan-oyunu.readme:
# Yılan Oyunu

Tarayıcıda çalışan, düz HTML + CSS + JavaScript ile yazılmış basit bir Yılan (Snake) oyunu.
Kütüphane, sunucu veya veritabanı yok.

## Nasıl çalıştırılır?

`index.html` dosyasına çift tıklayın, tarayıcıda açılır.

## Nasıl oynanır?

Bilgisayarda klavyeyle, telefonda parmakla oynanır:

| | Bilgisayar | Telefon / tablet |
|---|---|---|
| Başlat / yeniden başlat | **Boşluk** | Ekrana **dokun** |
| Yön | **Ok tuşları** | Tahtada parmağı **kaydır** |
| Sesi aç/kapat | **M** | Sol alttaki **ses düğmesi** |

- **Başlangıç:** sayfa açılınca oyun bekler; sağ altta ipucu görünür ("Boşluk: başla" ya da "Dokun: başla").
- **Yön girdisi:** tam ters yöne dönülemez; hızlı basılan tuşlar/kaydırmalar sırayla işlenir. Kaydırma için parmak en az 30 piksel hareket etmelidir, daha küçük hareketler yok sayılır. Kaydırırken sayfa kaymaz.
- **Ses:** tüm sesleri (efektler ve müzik) açar/kapatır; tercih tarayıcıda saklanır. Bilgisayarda sol altta "M: sesi kapat" ipucu, dokunmatik cihazda küçük bir ses düğmesi görünür.
- **Ekran uyumu:** tahta telefon ekranına sığacak şekilde küçülür, en-boy oranı (kare) bozulmaz.
- **Yem:** yılan yemi yiyince uzar, skor 1 artar ve kısa bir ses çalar
- **Çarpışma:** duvara ya da kendine çarpınca oyun biter ve farklı bir ses çalar
- **Skor:** sol üstte, **en yüksek skor** sağ üstte gösterilir (yarı şeffaf, altındaki yılan/yem görünür)
- **En yüksek skor:** tarayıcıda (localStorage) saklanır, sayfa kapansa da kalır
- **Müzik:** oyun sürerken arka planda hafif gerilimli bir müzik çalar, oyun bitince susar
- **Sesler:** ses dosyası yok, tarayıcının Web Audio özelliğiyle üretilir. Tarayıcılar sesi ilk tuş basışından ya da dokunuştan sonra açar.

## Dosyalar

| Dosya | Görevi |
|-------|--------|
| `index.html` | Sayfa, `<canvas>`, viewport etiketi ve ses düğmesi |
| `style.css` | Görünüm, telefona sığan tahta, dokunmatik ses düğmesi |
| `game.js` | Oyun durumu (`state`), güncelleme (`update`), çizim (`draw`), klavye, dokunma, ses |
| `docs/` | Proje slaytı (PDF) |

## Kod yapısı (`game.js`)

- `state`: snake, direction, inputQueue, food, score, highScore, started, gameOver
- `update()`: durumu değiştirir (hareket, yem, çarpışma, skor). Çizim yapmaz.
- `draw()`: sadece çizer. Durumu değiştirmez.
- `handleKey()`: ok tuşları, boşluk ve M tuşunu yönetir.
- `queueDirection()`: klavye ve kaydırmanın ortak girişi; yönü kuyruğa ekler.
- `handleTouchStart/Move/End()`: kaydırmayı (30 px eşik) ve dokunarak başlatmayı yönetir.
- `startOrRestart()`: oyunu başlatır ya da bitmişse yeniden başlatır (boşluk ve dokunuş).
- `toggleMute()`: sesi aç/kapatır (M tuşu ve ses düğmesi).
- `resetGame()`: oyunu başa sarar, en yüksek skoru korur.
- `loop()`: her 100 ms'de güncelle -> çiz.
- `state.inputQueue`: basılan yönler burada bekler (en fazla 2); `update()` karede birini işler.
- `beep()`, `playEatSound()`, `playGameOverSound()`, `unlockAudio()`: sesler ve ses bağlamını uyandırma.
- `startMusic()`, `musicTick()`: arka plan müziği.

## Geliştirme geçmişi

Her özellik ayrı bir commit olarak eklendi:

1. Proje kurulumu (README, CLAUDE.md)
2. Boş canvas'lı iskelet
3. Yılanı çizme
4. Hareket ve oyun döngüsü
5. Klavye kontrolü
6. Yem
7. Çarpışma
8. Skor
9. En yüksek skor
10. Boşluk tuşuyla yeniden başlatma
11. Skor yazılarını yarı şeffaf yapma
12. Yem ve oyun sonu sesleri
13. Arka plan gerilim müziği

v1.1 (`v1.1-duzeltmeler` dalı):

14. Hata düzeltme: yön girdileri kuyruğa alındı
15. M tuşuyla sessize alma ve ekranda ipucu (v1.1)

v1.2 (`v1.2-baslangic` dalı):

16. Başlangıç ekranı: oyun boşluk tuşuyla başlar

v1.3 (`v1.3-dokunmatik` dalı, telefon desteği):

17. Kaydırma (swipe) kontrolü
18. Dokunarak başlatma
19. Ekran uyumu ve dokunmatik ses düğmesi

Tam liste için: `git log --oneline`

## Bilinen sınırlar

- Yılan kendi kuyruğunun bulunduğu kareye girerse de çarpmış sayılır.

# WAB 2.0 data set for New Recruit — pilot (4 armies)

Built from your **Armies of Antiquity v2.0 .docx** (army lists) and the **WAB 2nd Edition rulebook PDF** (weapons, armour, psychology and formation rules). Layout follows the example Warhammer Armies Project repo: one game system (`.gst`) plus one catalogue (`.cat`) per army.

## Files
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Warhammer_Ancient_Battles_2.gst` | Game system: profile types, 11 missile weapons, 11 hand-to-hand weapons, 6 armour types, 8 shield/barding entries, 43 special rules, categories, and one force entry per army (variant) carrying the AoA2 composition percentages |
| `Early_Imperial_Roman.cat` | AoA2 list 44 (21 units). Early and Later Army are separate force entries |
| `Gallic.cat` | AoA2 list 12 (8 units) |
| `Parthian.cat` | AoA2 list 32 (7 units) |
| `Medieval_English.cat` | AoA2 list 92 (14 units, includes Gascon allies and the Cannon) |
| `extraction_review.txt` | For every unit: the rules, weapons and "+N pts" options the script detected. **Review this.** |
| `tools/` | The build and lint scripts, so the remaining 97 lists can be generated the same way |

## How to use
1. Choose the force entry matching the army (e.g. "Gallic", or "Early Imperial Roman - Later Army 110 AD to 193 AD"). Its percentages are enforced against the roster points limit.
2. Add units from the matching catalogue.

## Checks done
- All files are well-formed XML, 1,142 ids unique, all 346 links resolve (run `python3 tools/lint_wab2.py .`).
- Stats and points were parsed straight from the .docx tables.
- Rulebook reference data (weapons, armour, 23 rules) was transcribed from the printed Reference pages (book pp.205-212), not from OCR.

## Not yet verified
- **Not loaded in New Recruit yet.** The structure copies the example repo, but I couldn't test it here. If anything fails to load, send me the error.
- **Equipment options are auto-extracted** from the printed "(+N)" text. Labels can read oddly, and options that exclude each other (e.g. horse vs warhorse vs chariot) are not enforced. Notes as printed are on every unit under "Equipment and options (as printed in AoA2)".
- **Unit sizes are not enforced.** AoA2 gives no minimum, so troop units have min 1 model.
- **Not enforced:** "one machine per 800/1200 points" artillery limits, "0-1" limits across different units (the King and General can both be taken), and allied contingents from other lists. Allies are described in each list's "List Notes" rule only.
- **Troop-type rules are not defined as rules:** Light Infantry, Light Cavalry, Skirmishers, Open Order, Camelry, Riding Horses. Their text is still shown in the notes. AoA2's War wagons and Wagon tabor are not included.

## Source quirks to check against the book
- Gallic Standard Bearer is printed at 103 pts against the Chieftain's 90. Copied as printed.
- Parthian Horse Archers are "Nomad Horsemen"; AoA2 defines "Nomad Cavalry". Linked to Nomad Cavalry on the assumption it's a typo.
- Parthian standard bearer text reads "as a hand weapon" (likely "has").
- Medieval English "Hobilars" and similar entries' options were detected from sentence text; check the Irish Horse upgrade.

## Added: rulebook army lists (book pp.172-189)
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Roman_Army_List.cat` | 15 units: Army General, Army Standard Bearer, Legate, Tribune, 3 Legionary types, 3 Auxiliary types, Scorpio, Ballista, Tormenta, Marines, Camelry. Force entry "Roman Army List": Characters max 25%, Legionaries min 25%, Auxiliaries max 75%, Special Units max 25% |
| `Barbarian_Army_List.cat` | 12 units: Warlord, Battle Standard, Shaman, Chieftain, Warriors, Fanatic Warriors, Chariots, Noble Cavalry, Light Cavalry, Skirmishers, Mountain Tribesmen, Warhounds. Force entry "Barbarian Army List": Characters max 33%, Warriors min 33%, Cavalry and Chariots max 33%, Supporting Infantry max 33% |

Troop stats and points were transcribed by hand from the page images. Warhorse stats, the tribal variants (Gauls, Germans, Dacians, Ancient Britons, p.189) and the Roman allies rule are text only in each list's "List Notes" and are not enforced. Troop units have a 5-model minimum. Options are not mutually exclusive. Re-run with `python3 tools/rb_build.py .` after build_wab2.py.

## Source status
- **Official:** `Roman_Army_List.cat`, `Barbarian_Army_List.cat` (WAB 2nd Edition rulebook) and all rulebook reference data in the .gst.

# NHL game predictor

Give it two teams (or your own stats) and it predicts the winner, the win probability, the expected
score, and the probability of every scoreline. It's trained on real NHL results from 2018-19 onward
(about 9,900 games) and tested by predicting games it had never seen.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

python -m hockey_predictor predict --home COL --away BOS          # two NHL teams
python -m hockey_predictor slate                                  # every game today (live schedule)
python -m hockey_predictor teams                                  # current Elo / form for all teams

# plug in your own stats for either side (anything you leave out defaults to the team's current
# numbers, or league average for a made-up team)
python -m hockey_predictor predict --home A --away B \
    --home-elo 1560 --home-gf 3.5 --home-ga 2.6 --home-sf 32 --home-sa 27 --home-pts 0.66 --away-rest 1

python -m hockey_predictor update       # download newly finished games into data/games.csv
python -m hockey_predictor backtest     # re-run the accuracy test
pytest                                  # unit tests
```

Stats you can override per team: `elo`, `gf` / `ga` (goals for / against per game), `sf` / `sa`
(shots on goal for / against per game), `pts` (points %), `rest` (days since last game, 1 = back-to-back).
Rolling numbers are over the team's last 20 games.

## How it works

1. **Ratings.** Walking through games in date order, each game gets features computed only from games
   before it: Elo (with margin-of-victory), last-20-game goals/shots for and against, points %, rest days.
2. **Linear regression for goals.** Two ridge regressions predict each team's expected goals in 60 minutes.
3. **Every possible score.** Those expected goals drive a Poisson model over every scoreline (0-0 to 14-14),
   with the tie probability calibrated to hockey's real rate. Ties go to OT/shootout. This gives win,
   overtime, over/under and win-by-2 probabilities.
4. **Logistic regression** predicts the winner directly from the same ratings.
5. **Headline prediction** = 50/50 blend of 3 and 4.

## How accurate is it? (walk-forward test, 5,246 games, 2022-23 to 2025-26)

Every prediction used only games played before it; models were retrained monthly. Full tables in
[`results/backtest.md`](results/backtest.md).

| model | accuracy | log loss |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Always pick the home team | 53.8% | 0.690 |
| Team with better record | 56.3% | 0.689 |
| Elo only | 57.8% | 0.670 |
| **Blend (headline)** | **58.2%** | **0.665** |

Accuracy goes up as the model's confidence goes up, and the stated probabilities are close to reality:

| model says at least | share of games | actually right |
|:--|--:|--:|
| 55% | 70% | 62.1% |
| 60% | 45% | 66.0% |
| 65% | 25% | 69.5% |
| 70% | 12% | 76.3% |

**Honest limits.** Hockey is the most random of the major sports; one bounce decides a lot of games, so
~58% overall is in line with good public models, and no stats model gets close to "always right". The
number to trust is the probability, not the pick: when it says 70%+ it has been right about 3 times in 4.
The model doesn't know about injuries, goalies in the lineup, trades, or playoff series, which are the
main things that could still improve it. Accuracy varied by season (61%, 60%, 59%, 53%); 2025-26 was a
high-parity season (25% of games went past regulation). Differences under 1-2 points between models are noise.

Don't use this for anything where losing money matters: sportsbooks' lines already contain this
information and more.

## Layout

- `hockey_predictor/data.py` - NHL API download + cache (`data/games.csv`)
- `hockey_predictor/features.py` - Elo and rolling-form features (no look-ahead)
- `hockey_predictor/models.py` - ridge goals model, Poisson score simulation, logistic model, blend
- `hockey_predictor/backtest.py` - walk-forward test and report
- `hockey_predictor/predict.py`, `cli.py` - prediction API and command line

# cascade-game-shared

Публічні сторінки застосунків: лендинг Cascade та спільні блоки.

```
index.html          лендинг Cascade
assets/             стилі, скрипти, шрифти (Inter, JetBrains Mono, ліцензії OFL поруч), зображення
shared/             блоки, спільні для лендингів усіх застосунків (див. shared/README.md)
```

Це статичний сайт без збірки. Локально:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000   # http://localhost:8000
```

## Публікація

*Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → `main` / `/ (root)`.* Адреса: `https://witchdoctor90.github.io/cascade-game-shared/`. Усі шляхи відносні, тож сайт працює і з підкаталогу, і з власним доменом. Якщо адреса інша, поправте `og:image` в `index.html`: для превʼю в соцмережах потрібен абсолютний URL.

## Що всередині

- **Демо гри** (`assets/js/cascade.js`): палітри, скіни блоків, очки й комбо-віхи взято з застосунку. Поки ніхто не торкається поля, грає бот; клік, торкання, стрілки й пробіл переймають керування.
- **Повзунок комбо**: блок номер N за хід дає 10 × N очок, рівні банерів збігаються з грою.
- **Теми та скіни**: перемикають усю сторінку й гру нагорі; вибір, мова й тема зберігаються в `localStorage`.
- **Мови**: українська й англійська, за замовчуванням з мови браузера. Тексти в `assets/js/site.js`, статична українська версія є в `index.html` (для пошуковиків і для запуску без JS).
- **`<play-badge>`**: плашка «Скоро в Google Play» зі `shared/`. Коли застосунок вийде, додайте їй `live` і `href` (див. `shared/README.md`).

Сторінка поважає `prefers-reduced-motion`: бот і анімації вимикаються, гра чекає на вас.

## Новий застосунок

Створіть `notes/index.html`, підключіть `../shared/play-badge.js` і задайте плашці власну тему через CSS-змінні `--pb-*`. Структура, текст і поведінка плашки лишаться тими самими.

zvillanue/gamenight.readme:
# Game Night

A small private web app for organising game nights with friends.

- Login first; accounts collect only **name, username, password, and how you know Zack**
- Countdown to the next game night, with Going / Can't make it
- Home page shows who's coming, grouped by affiliation (hover a group to see names)
- Members suggest games (players range, type, genre, info, photo, "I have it") and food
- Everyone votes on games and food for the upcoming night; top 5 shown, search for the rest
- Game cards turn **yellow** when attendance is a little over the max players and **red** when it's well over
- Admin panel (the first account to register): game nights, affiliation options, members, password resets

Stack: Flask, SQLite, Gunicorn, Redis (rate limits), behind Caddy. Same conventions as `obsidian-store`.

## Develop

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
FLASK_DEBUG=1 .venv/bin/flask --app wsgi run
.venv/bin/pytest
```

## Security notes

- Passwords hashed with scrypt; changing one signs out every other session
- CSRF tokens on every form; strict CSP (no inline script/style); `HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite` cookies
- Login and registration rate-limited; generic login errors; constant-ish timing for unknown usernames
- Optional `INVITE_CODE` so only people you give it to can register
- Uploaded photos are validated, re-encoded to JPEG (strips EXIF/GPS), renamed randomly, and only served to logged-in members
- Members can delete their own account and data; deleted members' suggestions stay, without their name
- Nightly integrity-checked backups (`deploy/backup.sh`)

Deployment: see [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md).

pesuuu/Last-Frontier-V1.readme:
# Last Frontier

Open **LAST FRONTIER.html**. This is the only main playable release and runs offline with Three.js, game code and four music tracks embedded.

The LAST FRONTIER.html Downloads file supplied on October 8 is the authoritative gameplay baseline. All of its gameplay scripts and HTML/CSS are preserved; its soundtrack has been refreshed from the current music folder. Editable sources match this corrected version, including its weapon, dealer, backpack, survivor tactics, appearance mirror, combat feedback and day/night implementations.

## Title screen

js/title.js adds a minimal, letterboxed title screen that loops eleven in-engine vignettes that build from calm to intense (first light in the hall, the dealer at his stall, survivors in the living room; zombies in the yard, hammering the boards, a pistol in the dining room, a blade on the front lawn; a bat on the landing, bandit raiders, a shotgun or rifle in the back field; a full-auto last stand beside two survivors), shuffled within each act. The clips are purely visual: no game logic, spawns or audio run, and everything they touch (time of day, lights, held weapon, particles, decals, camera) is restored when NEW GAME is chosen, so the run starts normally in its random spawn room. Add ?notitle to the URL to skip it; dev mode (?dev=1) skips it unless ?title=1 is also set.

## Difficulty

NEW GAME opens a picker: **Easy, Normal, Hard, Nightmare**. The choice is remembered for next time, shown in the HUD, and can be forced with `?diff=easy|normal|hard|nightmare`. js/difficulty.js holds one table of multipliers and the few hooks that apply it; Normal is all 1s and plays exactly like the game did before.

Per level it changes: undead health, head and limb toughness, speed, damage and attack rate; horde size, how many are alive at once, spawn rate and the breather between waves; HP restored when a wave is beaten; scrap, material and ammo gained; dealer prices; melee weapon wear per hit; damage taken by the player and by survivors; panic build-up; barricade damage; and bandit raid chance, size and health. Fractional rewards use stochastic rounding, so "−40% scrap" averages out correctly instead of rounding every kill to the same number. The title screen always runs on Normal; the chosen level is applied when the run begins. Tested by tests/difficulty.cjs.

## Zombies

js/zombies.js builds and animates every zombie. The six gameplay parts (head, torso, both arms, both legs) keep their health, hit regions and dismemberment rules. Each now carries blocky visual segments: neck, jaw, pelvis, elbow/forearm, wrist/hand, knee/shin and ankle/foot. Ray hits on a segment resolve to its part, so a forearm hit is still an arm hit, a foot hit is a shin hit, and so on. Everything is still vertex-coloured boxes drawn through the shared actor instance batch.

- **Appearance.** Built from parts at spawn: skin tone with an infection tint, build, top (tee, long sleeve, hoodie, jacket, flannel, hi-vis/work, tank, polo, office shirt and tie, sweater), pants or shorts, shoes or a missing shoe, hair or cap, and glowing or milky eyes. Damage comes in three severity levels (some zombies are nearly clean): bites, torn sleeves and pant legs, exposed ribs, face tears, a missing eye, blood stains and handprints, gunshot holes and decay patches. Sprinters are fresher, fatties bloated, crawlers rotten and legless.
- **Movement.** Each normal zombie picks a walking style at spawn and keeps it: shamble, limp, aggressive, dragging leg, stiff or sway. Sprinters sprint, fatties use a heavy swaying gait, and crawlers drag themselves prone on thigh stumps. Injuries change the gait live. A damaged leg limps, and a badly hurt leg drags and slows the zombie slightly. With one leg it hops, and with no legs it crawls. A ruined arm hangs, and a damaged head lolls.
- **Attacks.** Attacks are chosen by range, arm health and zombie type: left/right scratch, double grab, grab-and-swipe, lunge, bite (jaw opens, head drives in) and low grab. Crawlers swipe and bite from the floor, and barricade attacks pound the boards. The wind-up is driven by the existing attack timer, so damage still lands at exactly the same moment. Lunges and bites are kept from pushing the head through the camera.
- **Hit reactions and staggers.** Hit reactions follow the region struck and the push direction. Melee hits are bigger, and bat hits whip the head and shoulders round. The existing knock/stagger timers now play one of five staggers (recoil, side stumble, twist, knee dip, loss of balance), and knockdowns sit the zombie down or drop it to its knees.
- **Deaths.** rgInit/rag are replaced by directional procedural deaths that use force direction, hit location and damage type. Possible deaths: headshot snap or crumple, falling backwards from the front, pitching forward from behind, falling sideways, collapsing toward a destroyed leg, a blunt stumble-and-spin, a katana slash that follows the swing, a fattie dropping to its knees, a crawler flattening out, and a slump when a wall is behind the body. Corpses settle into varied poses (face down/up, side, twisted, knees, slumped). Corpse lifetime and cleanup are unchanged.
- **Gore.** Gore follows the damage type: bullet wounds, long directional slash cuts, blunt bruises, chop gashes and stab punctures. Severing cuts at the segment that was hit (shoulder or elbow, hip or knee), leaves a stump with bone, and drops the piece as a separate falling fragment.

## Katana and Bat

js/melee-arcs.js gives both weapons alternating left-to-right / right-to-left swings. The first swing after a pause is always left-to-right.

- **Katana.** Broad, flat slicing arcs. A normal hit opens a directional cut (the cut reverses with the swing) and does not take the limb off. Separation needs a finishing stroke: a lethal hit has about a 50% chance (40% for legs), a second slash through an already cut limb always separates it, and there is a small chance on any hit. huuuda-aus/deathwalker.readme:
# Deathwalker

A browser remake, inspired by **Walker** (DMA Design / Psygnosis, Amiga, 1993): a bipedal mech advances right to left through a ruined city, aiming with the mouse and walking with the keyboard, while infantry fire back from the streets and the buildings.

Built with **TypeScript**, **Three.js** and **Vite**. All art is procedural placeholder geometry; nothing is taken from the original game.

> Status: playable prototype (milestones M1–M3 plus scene/camera work). See [Roadmap](#roadmap).

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev       # dev server with hot reload
npm run build     # type-check + production build into dist/
npm run preview   # serve the production build
```

Needs a browser with WebGL2.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| **A / D** or **← / →** | Walk left / right along the street |
| **W / S** or **↑ / ↓** | Walk away from / toward the camera (depth lane) |
| **Mouse** | Aim the reticle |
| **Hold mouse button** | Fire both guns |
| **Q** | Toggle post-processing (bloom, motion blur, vignette, haze) |
| **H** | Toggle the volumetric haze only |
| **R** | Restart after game over |

The mech never turns around: its body always faces left. Only the cockpit and its two rigid guns rotate, and only within the forward hemisphere, so you cannot shoot behind you. The guns overheat; release to cool down, and a full overheat locks them out until they cool.

## Gameplay

- The camera is on rails. A level is a list of **scenes**, each one or more screens wide, with a spawn budget and a kill goal. The camera will not advance until the goal is met; then the scroll unlocks and you walk on to the next scene.
- Enemies arrive in waves. Most spawn **inside the buildings**, walk to a ledge and shoot from there; the rest walk in from off-screen. Soldiers on the street steer around rubble and only fire when they have a clear line of fire.
- **Buildings are destructible ruins** built from floor slabs, pillars, walls, glazing and stairwells. A load-path solver collapses whatever loses its support, and shooting out the base of a building brings the whole thing down, crushing everyone inside. A collapsed building spawns no more enemies.
- **Rubble is physical and persistent.** It piles up, blocks soldiers and bullets, is kicked aside by the mech's legs, and slows the mech down when it is dense.
- Your shield is your health; you have three lives.

## How the shooting works

Bullets are not projectiles. Each shot is an instant ray cast from the camera through the reticle into the 2.5D world (enemies, walls, rubble, ground), and the guns' effect appears where it lands. The two guns fire alternately, and the heat level widens the spread slightly. Rubble on the line between a gun and its target stops the shot, for both you and the enemy.

## Project layout

```
src/
  main.ts       game loop, input wiring, spawning waves, HUD
  level.ts      scene list, on-rails camera, kill-gate state machine
  mech.ts       procedural mech, IK legs, cockpit aiming, rubble colliders
  weapon.ts     hitscan guns, heat, jitter
  targeting.ts  ray casts against enemies / walls / ground
  enemies.ts    soldiers: steering, line of fire, ledges, corpses
  building.ts   destructible buildings, ruin generation, collapse solver
  world.ts      sky, ground, parallax city, chunk streaming
  debris.ts     rubble physics (sleeping bodies, spatial hash), dust
  fx.ts         pixel sparks, blood bursts, muzzle flash
  post.ts       post-processing: volumetric haze, bloom, depth-aware motion blur, tone map
  sky.ts        night sky shader: clouds, stars, horizon glow
  wind.ts       shared wind (gusts); drives the haze drift and the litter
  litter.ts     scarce leaves and papers blown along by the wind
  fire.ts       burning oil barrels in the ground-floor bays, fire light pool, shared flame textures
  water.ts      puddles on the ground and the splashes the mech's feet make in them
  rain.ts       GPU drizzle: wind-slanted drops and splashes that land on roofs and the mech
  haze.ts       low-res raymarched volumetric haze pass
  ground.ts     procedural rubble/dirt ground texture + normal map
  input.ts      keyboard and mouse
```

Handy tuning knobs:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `src/level.ts` | `LEVEL` (scene widths, kill goals, spawn budgets), `SCREEN_W` |
| `src/main.ts` | `WALK_SPEED`, `MAX_ALIVE`, wave size and interval |
| `src/weapon.ts` | fire rate, heat per shot, cooling, spread |
| `src/mech.ts` | `MECH_SCALE`, gait (`STEP`, `LIFT`, `STANCE`), collider radii |
| `src/building.ts` | `CELL` size, member hit points, `SPAN`, `BEARING_MIN` |
| `src/debris.ts` | sleep thresholds, chunk cap, blocking sizes |
| `src/post.ts` | exposure, bloom, motion-blur shutter, haze density/colour/steps |
| `src/wind.ts`, `src/litter.ts` | wind strength and gusts, amount of flying litter |

## Roadmap

Done: scrolling scene and parallax city, mech with decoupled aiming, hitscan guns with heat, infantry, destructible buildings with collapse physics, persistent rubble, post-processing, on-rails scenes with kill gates.

Next (M4): more enemy types (tanks, planes with paratroopers, grenade throwers), HUD polish, a complete first level (Berlin 1944), radio-chatter audio. Later: the remaining stages (Los Angeles 2019, Middle East, 2420), bosses, lock-on missiles, difficulty modes, and more variety in what the player faces.

## Credits and legal

*Walker* is the work of DMA Design and Psygnosis; this project is an unofficial, non-commercial homage and contains none of the original's assets, code or music.

vita-port-lab/vita-builds.desc: PlayStation Vita homebrew ports, written with an AI assistant and tested on a real Vita
vita-port-lab/vita-builds.readme:
# Vita Port Lab **Native ports for a 2011 handheld that still has plenty of life. Written entirely by AI.** *Every line of code and every document in this repository was written by [Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/claude), Anthropic's AI model. It is fully vibecoded, and the headline numbers were measured on a real PS Vita.*
--- The PS Vita has a 960×544 screen, three CPU cores you can use, a GPU that still surprises people, and a library that stopped growing years ago. Games from the PSP, GameCube, Wii and Game Boy Advance eras sit in drawers while the Vita sits in another drawer. Emulators are the usual answer, and on a 444 MHz handheld they are the wrong ceiling. An emulator spends most of the Vita's budget pretending to be another machine. **This lab builds the games natively**: the original code is recompiled ahead of time to ARM, or rebuilt from a community decompilation, and all of the CPU is left for the game. ![Infected on a real PS Vita: average fps in mission 1, 16.6 in the morning, 25.2 after a leaner renderer, 31.6 with three cores working in parallel](docs/img/infected-fps.svg) *One title, one mission, one day, measured on a console. [The full story is here.](docs/case-study-30-fps.md)* ## Why this exists 1. **The Vita deserves its back catalogue, at full speed.** Not "it boots", not 12 fps on a good day. Playable, smooth, at the screen's native resolution. 2. **Nobody writes down what the Vita actually does.** The things that wreck a port (a kernel that checks stack bounds, a C++ runtime that quietly stops being multi-threaded, system calls that cost four microseconds each) are scattered across forum threads or not written down at all. This lab finds them the hard way and publishes them as [field notes](docs/vita-lessons.md) and [patches](patches/vitagl/). 3. **It tests what AI can do on real hardware.** Not a demo in a sandbox: cross-compiling with VitaSDK, installing a build on a real console over Wi-Fi, reading the logs, finding the bottleneck, fixing it, and doing it again. ## Built entirely by Claude Every recompiler, renderer, build script, measurement harness, patch and document here was written by Claude. It is fully vibecoded. A human sets the goals, plays the games and says "that feels wrong". Claude does everything else: reads decompiled code, writes the tools, builds, deploys to the console, reads the logs, and iterates. Nobody reviews every line by hand, so the lab leans on measurement instead of trust: - **Real-console numbers.** The headline performance figures come from a Vita, not an emulator. Emulators run the Vita's code on a much faster CPU: one earlier build showed 25–37 fps in an emulator and measured 6–12 fps on the console. Where a figure is a projection (an instruction count on an emulated Vita CPU), it says so. - **Oracles.** Each optimisation runs the old and the new code on the same input, in the same process, and compares. Millions of draws, zero differences, or it does not ship. - **Plain statements of what is not verified.** If a claim has not been run on a console, the documents say so. Expect rough edges. This is experimental software made by an experiment. ## Highlights - **Infected (PSP, 2005) plays natively on a real Vita.** Mission 1 runs from start to finish at 960×544, twice the PSP's resolution in each direction, with a 2,625-texture HD pack, at a 30 fps cap synced to the display, so there is no tearing. - **16.6 → 31.6 fps in one day**, uncapped. The slowest 1 % of frames went from 7 fps to 15 fps. - **Shaders about 10× cheaper.** The fragment programs the first version generated ran 110–190 GPU instructions per pixel. Specialised for the Vita's GPU they run 5–25. - **A "three-thread" renderer that was secretly running on one thread.** The static C++ runtime on VitaSDK does not enable threading unless you ask. [Found, explained and fixed.](docs/vita-lessons.md#2-your-static-c-runtime-is-probably-not-thread-safe) - **Far fewer hitches when something new appears.** Each new HD texture used to stall the GPU thread for 10–15 ms. A [vitaGL patch](patches/vitagl/) removed that stall, and a background loader took the card reads off the render path. - **A Game Boy Advance emulator at 59.94 fps with every extra on**: smooth upscaling, wide view, GBA colours and frame blending, with no audio underruns. A GPU upscaler was built, measured at 31–33 ms a frame, and switched off by default on the evidence. - **A Wii-era renderer front end 34 % cheaper** (6.20 M → 4.11 M instructions per frame on a game's title screen, counted on an emulated Vita CPU), with bit-identical output and every step checked by an in-process oracle. ## The projects | Project | Game | How | Where it stands (16 Oct 2026) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Infected** | PSP (2005) | The PSP's code recompiled to native ARM on a [PortableKit](https://github.com/TeamGDB/PortableKit) runtime, rendered through vitaGL | Mission 1 plays start to finish on a real Vita at a 30 fps cap. Other missions have not been tried on the console. | | **Super Mario Galaxy** | Wii | Built from a community decompilation, with a GX-level renderer on vitaGL | Title, file select, the opening and the castle plaza run on a real Vita. Performance work is in progress. | | **Mario Strikers Charged** | Wii | Built from a community decompilation, natively | Whole matches play on a PC build and in an emulated Vita. It has not run natively on a real Vita yet. | | **VitAdhoc** | GBA / GB / GBC | A Vita version of the GBAdhoc emulator with link play | 59.94 fps in the tested game with every extra on. Source and a BIOS-free build are staged for this repo. | ## What is in this repo | Path | What | | --- | --- | | [`docs/vita-lessons.md`](docs/vita-lessons.md) | Field notes: the traps found on real hardware, with the fixes | | [`docs/case-study-30-fps.md`](docs/case-study-30-fps.md) | Where one Vita frame goes, and how a mission went from 16.6 to 31.6 fps | | [`patche

Misterio77/jagex-auth.desc: Small browser-based Jagex account authentication helper for existing RuneScape clients
Misterio77/jagex-auth.readme:
# jagex-auth

A small, unofficial Jagex-account authentication helper for existing RuneScape
clients. Uses your normal browser, then starts a compatible client with the
`JX_SESSION_ID`, `JX_CHARACTER_ID`, and `JX_DISPLAY_NAME` environment variables.
It does not download/update clients or fix RS3's GTK2/OpenSSL dependencies.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the server-validation trust boundary and
callback lifetime details. It is not affiliated with Jagex.

## Usage

With the `rshub` desktop URL handler registered to Jagex Auth URL Handler:

```sh
jagex-auth authorize
jagex-auth launch -- runelite
jagex-auth launch -- hdos
jagex-auth launch -- runescape
```

Authorize opens your browser and prompts for a character if needed. Characters
without a display name are skipped; set a character name first if none are named.
If browser callback delivery does not work, paste the successful-login URL into the terminal
running `authorize`. Treat that URL as a secret; it is echoed like any other
terminal input. Installing the desktop file does
not necessarily register it as the default handler; check your desktop's URL
associations. Do not replace an existing handler without considering its users.
Raw ID tokens are not accepted: paste the complete successful-login URL so its
state can be checked. Run one authorization at a time (there is no locking;
the last one to finish wins). The wait times out after five minutes. Ctrl-C
cancels the attempt.

`launch` never prompts or opens a browser. It requires existing credentials;
if absent or invalid it asks you to run `authorize`. An expired/revoked game
session may instead be rejected by the game: authorize again. There is no
automatic session refresh or local check that a saved session is still valid.
Arguments following the command are passed through literally. `launch` replaces
itself with the client, preserving signal and exit-status behavior.

ID tokens are not signature-verified locally. The helper only checks that the
response is bound to its own request (state and nonce), then relies on Jagex's
HTTPS session exchange and character listing to establish authentication before
saving a login.

For direct Python use (Python 3.10+ on Linux; standard library only), run from
the source directory:

```sh
python3 -m jagex_auth authorize
python3 -m jagex_auth launch -- runelite
```

Browser callback integration additionally requires installing an appropriate
`.desktop` handler for `jagex-auth handle-url %u`. The Nix package supplies one.

## Nix

Run directly from GitHub:

```sh
nix run github:Misterio77/jagex-auth -- --help
nix run github:Misterio77/jagex-auth -- authorize
```

Or from a checkout:

```sh
nix run . -- --help
nix run . -- authorize
nix build .
./result/bin/jagex-auth --help
# Optional installation, including the desktop handler:
nix profile add .
```

The flake exposes `packages.<system>.{default,jagex-auth}` for `x86_64-linux`
and `aarch64-linux`. The package's `wrapLaunch` function wraps an
existing client. Add this input to your flake:

```nix
{
  inputs.jagex-auth = {
    url = "github:Misterio77/jagex-auth";
    inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
  };
}
```

A Home Manager module can then use:

```nix
{inputs, pkgs, ...}: let
  jagexAuth = inputs.jagex-auth.packages.${pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.system}.default;
in {
  home.packages = [
    jagexAuth
    (jagexAuth.wrapLaunch pkgs.runelite)
  ];
}
```

Following `nixpkgs` shares its revision, not your package configuration.
`pkgs.callPackage /path/to/jagex-auth {}` also works without using this flake.

The returned package preserves the client's desktop files and wraps its main
executable with `jagex-auth launch -- <original-executable>`. Authentication is
runtime-only; credentials never become Nix inputs or store contents. In-game
login was verified with the RuneLite 2.8.0 launcher, HDOS launcher 8, and RS3
2.2.12 package on 2026-10-16. This does not guarantee that other versions or
systems satisfy each client's runtime dependencies.

## Storage

Credentials live in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/jagex-auth/credentials.json`, defaulting to
`~/.local/share/jagex-auth/credentials.json`. The file holds the three `JX_*`
fields; unknown keys are ignored. The directory is private (`0700`); credential files are
created private (`0600`) and replaced atomically. Unsafe credential file types,
symlinks, files owned by another user, and group/world permissions are rejected.

Only the JSON format is supported; there is no legacy detection or migration.
Run `jagex-auth authorize` to create credentials. Do not paste credentials into
bug reports. On impermanent systems, persist the data directory if you want
sessions to survive a reboot.

Credentials are ordinary data, never shell code. They are passed to clients
through the environment, not command arguments. This is not protection from
processes running as your user (which may also read your files or environment).
Keep the account, browser profile, and machine secure. Logging out of this tool
is not yet implemented; deleting local files does not revoke a server session.

## Offline checks

```sh
# -S disables site packages, demonstrating that tests need only the stdlib:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -S -m unittest discover -s tests -v
# Build the package (including Python tests) and fake-client wrapper check:
nix flake check
# Optional development environment and formatter:
nix develop
nix fmt ./flake.nix ./default.nix ./tests/wrapper.nix
```

Tests use synthetic credentials and temporary directories, block unexpected
network/browser calls, and exercise process launching without starting a game.
Never use real credentials in fixtures.

## License and provenance

[MIT](LICENSE), Copyright (c) 2026 Gabriel Fontes.

Originally developed in [Foundry](https://github.com/Misterio77/Foundry).
