JorSanders/bomber-chess.desc: Bomberman on a chess board: the bombs are chess pieces and blow up the squares they attack.
JorSanders/bomber-chess.readme:
# Bomber-Chess

Bomberman on a chess board. You are a king, the bombs are chess pieces, and each one blows up exactly the squares it attacks. I wanted a small real time game to try peer to peer play on phones, and dropping a knight as a bomb was too funny an idea to leave alone. This is the first playable prototype: two players on one keyboard, or against a simple bot. Phone to phone play is the plan, not something that exists yet.

Live (once published): https://bomber-chess.jor.dev/

## Rules

1. You are a king. You walk up, down, left or right at about three squares a second, smoothly rather than square by square, and the game treats you as standing on whichever square your centre is on. In the open you can turn wherever you are. When something is in the way while you are off a lane, you get nudged sideways into the nearest open lane, the way Bomberman helps you around corners. No diagonals, kings walk through each other.
2. Drop a piece on the square you stand on. Two and a half seconds later it goes off and hits every square that piece attacks in chess: a rook sweeps its file and rank, a bishop its diagonals, a queen both, a knight jumps to its eight squares, a pawn hits the two diagonal squares ahead of it (ahead is up the board for white, down for black). Rubble, other pieces and kings stop sliding pieces, and that blocking square still gets hit. The square the piece stands on blows up too, so you cannot hide on top of your own piece.
3. A king on a hit square is captured and loses. If both kings go in the same tick it is a draw. Blasts linger for a moment, so walking into one also kills you.
4. A fused piece caught in a blast goes off immediately, so chains happen.
5. There is one drop button and it drops the active piece, shown as a badge on your king. After a drop the active piece moves on to the next best piece you hold, in the order queen, rook, bishop, knight, pawn, wrapping around from pawn back to your best piece. Pieces coming back or picked up never change the active piece, so what you are about to drop never swaps under you. You start with a knight active. Pawns never run out. Every other piece is out of your hands while it is fused and comes back to your inventory the moment it goes off, so a queen is one blast at a time, not one blast ever. There is no limit on how many pieces you can have fused, only that you cannot drop on a square that already holds one.
6. The board starts with about 45 percent rubble, except around the two corners where the kings start (white at a1, black at h8). Blowing up rubble has a 50 percent chance of uncovering a piece: a knight most often, then a bishop, then a rook, rarely a queen, and never more than one queen per game. Walk over it to pick it up. Pieces lying on the ground survive later blasts, so nothing you uncover gets lost.
7. Each player starts with one knight besides the endless pawns.
8. Nothing warns you where a fused piece will hit. You read the piece and its lines yourself, the way you read a bomb's range in Bomberman. Blasts are flames that linger for a moment.
9. The round lasts two minutes, then it is a draw.

I have only tuned the fuse, the walking speed and the rubble density by feel on my own machine. None of it is balanced yet.

## Modes

- **Versus bot**: you are white, black is a bot. It steps out of danger, walks to a square from which its next piece hits your king and drops it there, digs through rubble that is in the way, and picks up pieces lying around. It is beatable without being cheap: it thinks once per square, needs half a second to react to a piece you drop, never ignores danger it knows about, and takes only half of its kill chances. It does not foresee chain reactions and always runs for the nearest safe square, so trapping it between two blasts or with a chain is how you win. Those numbers are at the top of `src/bot.js`. This is the default on touch screens.
- **Two players, one keyboard**: both kings are human. This is the default when a mouse or trackpad is detected.

## Controls

- White: WASD to move. Space drops your best piece.
- Black: arrow keys to move, Enter drops your best piece.
- Touch: the d-pad under the board moves white and the pink button in its middle drops. A small badge on each king shows the piece that drops next, each player block says it in words, the inventory outlines it, and on touch the drop button shows its glyph. The d-pad is hidden on desktop. I have only tried it with a mouse and a phone sized browser window so far, not on a real phone.

## How the game loop works

The simulation in `src/game.js` runs at a fixed 20 ticks per second and is deterministic: a seed sets up the rubble and every later random choice (which rubble hides a piece, which piece) comes from the same seeded generator. Kings walk in whole steps of a sixth of a square, one step per tick, so positions stay integers. Every tick takes one input per player, a held direction and whether to drop. Nothing else goes in. The page just feeds it keyboard, touch or bot inputs.

That shape is on purpose. For peer to peer play the idea is lockstep: both phones run the same simulation from the same seed and only exchange inputs per tick, so no game state ever has to cross the wire and neither side can fudge it. The networking is not built yet.

## Run locally

ES modules need an HTTP server, so `file://` will not work.

```sh
npm run serve
```

Then open http://localhost:6768.

Dev URL parameters: `?seed=<number>` replays a specific board for the first game, `?mode=bot|two` picks the opponent. New game keeps the mode and picks a fresh seed, and the address bar always shows the current seed so you can copy it.

## Files

```
index.html             the page
style.css              styles on top of the brand tokens, board colors and piece glyphs are content
src/main.js            wiring: game loop, inputs, rendering, settings
src/game.js            the deterministic simulation
src/chess.js           board helpers and the at

openvectro/vectro.desc: Free, open-source interactive vector animation editor. Exports .riv, so it plays on the existing free runtimes for web, Flutter, iOS and Android.
openvectro/vectro.readme: # Vectro Free, open-source interactive vector animation: layers, vectors, timelines and state machines, for every platform. Vectro exports `.riv` files, so what you make plays on the existing free runtimes for web, Flutter, iOS and Android. Not affiliated with Rive. "Rive" is their trademark; Vectro reads and writes the format they publish. ## Status Early, but it works end to end. Draw rectangles and ellipses or import SVG paths, key position, size, rotation, scale, opacity, corner radius and colour on a timeline with easing, play it back, and export `.riv`. Rive's own web runtime plays the export the same way the editor shows it (checked frame by frame). State machines work in the core (`vectro-doc`): inputs, layers, states, number-driven blends, transitions with exit times and random choice, pointer listeners and events. Two files prove it in Rive's runtime: a loading bar and a tiny whack-a-mole game, drawn with gradients, strokes and Rive's feather (soft shadows and glows). The editor has a **State machines** tab: inputs, layers, a node graph (drag a state's port onto another state to add a transition), conditions, exit times, blends, random weights, and pointer listeners on shapes. **Preview** plays a machine with Rive's own runtime and gives every input a control. ``` cargo run --release -p vectro-doc --example loading_bar -- tests/web/loading-bar.riv cargo run --release -p vectro-doc --example whack -- tests/web/whack.riv # then serve tests/web and open interactive.html?file=whack.riv&sm=Game ``` ## Run the editor ``` cd editor npm install npm run wasm # builds the Rust core for the browser (needs wasm-pack) npm run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5173 ``` Tools: V select, R rectangle, E ellipse, P pen, N edit points (or double-click a path). Shift-click or drag a box to select several; ⌘G group, ⇧⌘G ungroup, ⌘D duplicate, arrows nudge (shift for 10), ⌘A select all. Pen: click for corners, drag for curves, click the first point to close, Enter or double-click to finish. Points: drag points and handles, Alt-drag a point to pull handles out, Alt on a handle breaks the pair, double-click the outline to add a point, ⌫ removes one. View: ⌘-wheel or pinch zooms, wheel pans, space-drag pans, ⌘0 fits. Space plays, ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z undo / redo. ## Tools ``` cargo run --release --bin vectro -- import-svg logo.svg > logo.vectro.json cargo run --release --bin vectro -- export logo.vectro.json logo.riv cargo run --release --bin riv-dump -- path/to/file.riv cargo run --release --bin riv-roundtrip -- path/to/*.riv cargo test ``` ## Layout - `crates/vectro-riv` reads and writes `.riv`; `riv-dump`, `riv-roundtrip` - `crates/vectro-doc` the document, playback maths and `.riv` export - `crates/vectro-wasm` the core compiled for the browser - `editor/` the web editor (Svelte), with a preview that uses Rive's own runtime - `data/rive-keys.json` type and property table from Rive's MIT runtime - `docs/format.md` what the format holds, confirmed on real files MIT licence. ## Brand `brand/` holds the mark and wordmark as SVG, icon and favicon renders, the GitHub banner, and the logo animated with Vectro itself (`brand/vectro-logo.vectro.json`, built by `examples/logo.rs`). `python3 brand/build.py` regenerates the renders. The wordmark is Inter Tight (OFL, in `brand/fonts`).

# React + Vite

This template provides a minimal setup to get React working in Vite with HMR and some Oxlint rules.

Currently, two official plugins are available:

- [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react) uses [Oxc](https://oxc.rs)
- [@vitejs/plugin-react-swc](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react-swc) uses [SWC](https://swc.rs/)

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend using TypeScript with type-aware lint rules enabled. Check out the [TS template](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/main/packages/create-vite/template-react-ts) for information on how to integrate TypeScript and Oxlint's TypeScript related rules in your project.

Kaux-Studios/KEDO.readme:
# KEDO — Kaux Enriched Data Object

Lenguaje y toolchain propios de Kaux Studios para definir contenido de juego enriquecido: objetos declarativos con herencia de valores, importación, mixins y componentes; expresiones; funciones y triggers que compilan a un IR determinista con continuaciones guardables; referencias a assets de cualquier clase. Independiente del motor. El primer cliente es Project Patriark, un juego de Kaux Studios (repositorio privado).

Estado: **alpha** (16/10/2026). Spec v0.1 aceptada; lexer, parser, formateador, resolver (capas, mezcla, borrado, procedencia, validación, hash), esquema como dato (`kedo_type`…) con `kedo schema`, compilador de hooks y funciones a IR, VM de registros con frames guardables, KEDO Pack binario (`kedo build`) y CLI completa, benchmarks, servidor MCP y skills, addon de Godot y el mini-juego `samples/outpost`. Desde el 16/10/2026: decimales de punto fijo, mapas con claves libres, restricciones de esquema (tamaño de listas, largo y valores de textos), advertencias de mezcla y orden de declaración ([ADR-0008](spec/adr/0008-decimales-de-punto-fijo.md) a [ADR-0010](spec/adr/0010-diagnosticos-de-mezcla-y-orden-de-declaracion.md)). Patriark compila todo su contenido con KEDO desde su propio repositorio. Pendientes: [backlog](https://github.com/Kaux-Studios/KEDO/issues).

## Principios (en orden)

1. **Rendimiento** antes que facilidad de uso. Lexer sobre spans, AST compacto, resolución incremental, VM sin asignaciones por instrucción, serialización por source generators, cero reflexión, compatible con NativeAOT y trimming.
2. **Facilidad de uso**: sintaxis pequeña y explícita, una sola forma de hacer cada cosa, diagnósticos con código, posición y sugerencia de arreglo, formateador canónico.
3. **Escalable**: decenas de miles de objetos, módulos, compilación incremental por archivo, catálogos inmutables.
4. **Flexible**: tipos, componentes, hooks y validadores se registran por extensión sin tocar el núcleo. Varios juegos sobre el mismo núcleo.
5. **Determinista y guardable**: valores enteros, azar y reloj inyectados por el host, frames de ejecución serializables, efectos idempotentes.
6. **Pensado para agentes de IA**: CLI con salida JSON, servidor MCP sobre el mismo núcleo, skills y ejemplos dorados desde el inicio.

Detalle en [spec/KEDO-00-Principios-y-Alcance.md](spec/KEDO-00-Principios-y-Alcance.md).

## Versionado

SemVer. **1.x nunca rompe**: gramática, AST serializado, IR, frames y API pública solo crecen; lo obsoleto avisa y sigue funcionando. Un cambio incompatible es 2.0 y trae `kedo migrate`. Patriark depende de `[1.0, 2.0)`: debe funcionar con 1.9.99. Ver [ADR-0001](spec/adr/0001-versionado-semver.md).

## Estructura

```
spec/            especificación del lenguaje, principios, ADR
src/Kedo.Core    valores, diagnósticos, lector del pack, VM determinista, host  (net8.0, AOT, superficie mínima)
src/Kedo.Compiler lexer, parser, AST, resolver, formateador, esquema, escritor del pack  (net8.0, AOT)
src/Kedo.Cli     herramienta `kedo`: parse | check | resolve | explain | compile | build | schema | fmt (todo con --json)
addons/kedo      addon de Godot (GDScript, sin cargar el ensamblado del juego): biblioteca de objetos, editor con resaltado, check/fmt vía CLI, diagnósticos con salto, cambios pendientes y borradores
tests/           golden corpus + xUnit + tests GDScript headless
samples/         mini-juego de muestra, distinto de Patriark, para probar que el núcleo es genérico
docs/research    investigación (origen y anexos A, B, D–I); docs/plans planes por bloque
```

## Comandos

```powershell
dotnet restore --locked-mode
dotnet build Kedo.sln -c Release
dotnet test tests/Kedo.Tests/Kedo.Tests.csproj
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- version
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- check spec/ejemplos            # parse + resolve + validate (modo permisivo)
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- resolve spec/ejemplos          # catálogo resuelto
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- explain spec/ejemplos event:road.sentinel.depot "options[risk].check.difficulty"
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- fmt spec/ejemplos --check
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- check --schema=spec/ejemplos/schema spec/ejemplos   # con esquema cerrado
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- compile --schema=spec/ejemplos/schema spec/ejemplos # IR de hooks y funciones
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- build --schema=spec/ejemplos/schema spec/ejemplos --out=patriark.kpk
dotnet run --project src/Kedo.Cli -- schema spec/ejemplos/schema --json              # JSON Schema para formularios y agentes
```

## Addon de Godot

`addons/kedo` es un plugin de pantalla principal escrito en GDScript que habla con la CLI (`Editor Settings > kedo/command`, `kedo/content_paths`, `kedo/schema_paths`): lista los objetos del catálogo por tipo con filtro, abre el archivo en un `CodeEdit` con resaltado KEDO, ejecuta Check y Format, muestra diagnósticos con salto a línea, integra los cambios pendientes en el diálogo de cierre del editor, guarda borradores en `user://` y bloquea Play si el contenido tiene errores. Los formularios generados desde el esquema quedan para una entrega posterior. Tests headless: `tools/godot-test.ps1 -GodotPath <godot 4.6>`.

## Herramientas para agentes de IA

aditk3/drinking-games-claude.readme:
# Drinking Games for 4

A local, browsable library of drinking games that work with exactly four people. No backend, no accounts, no runtime requests to anything but `localhost`.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the URL Vite prints (normally http://localhost:5173). The dev server also runs the room server for the multi-phone games, so everything works locally with no account.

To let phones on your wifi join a room while you develop, run `npm run dev -- --host` and share the network address Vite prints instead of localhost.

`npm run build` writes the site to `dist/client/` and the Worker to `dist/drinking_games/`; `npm run preview` serves the built output through the Workers runtime.

## Built-in games

The `/play` section has games built into the site, replacing apps that no longer exist:

- **Drink Roulette** (`/play/roulette`): one phone, a spinnable wheel.
- **Drinkopoly** (`/play/board`): one phone, a 24-square board game.
- **Party Room** (`/play/room`): everyone on their own phone, joined by a 4-letter code. Prompts (most likely to, never have I ever, would you rather, dares, truths, rules) and mini-games (reaction, tap race, hold steady, quick math). The host picks Spicy or Tame.

Content lives in `shared/content.ts`. Game logic for the room is in `shared/game.ts` and runs on the server; the client only renders state.

## Deploying

Live at https://drinking-games.drinking-games.workers.dev (library and all three built-in games).

The site and the room server deploy together as one Cloudflare Worker (free plan is enough; rooms use Durable Objects with SQLite storage, which the free plan includes).

```bash
npx wrangler login
npm run deploy
```

The first command opens a browser to authorize wrangler against your Cloudflare account. The second builds and deploys; wrangler prints the public `*.workers.dev` URL. Re-run `npm run deploy` after any change.

## Where the data lives

- `drinking-games.md` is the seed. It is only read by the parser.
- `src/data/games.json` is the source of truth the app renders.
- `src/data/types.ts` documents every field.

Each game has the seed fields (`id`, `name`, `category`, `subcategory`, `needs`, `vibe`, `style[]`, `howToPlay`, `tip`) plus research fields (`setup[]`, `rules[]`, `drinkTriggers[]`, `variations[]`, `watchOut`, `duration`, `playerSweetSpot`, `links[]`, `notes`, `source`).

`source` is `"seed"` for games that came from the markdown and `"added"` for games found during research. Added games are flagged in the UI and can be filtered with "Added by research" so you can review them. Links carry `verified: "fetched"` when the URL was actually loaded and checked, or `"unverified"` when it was not.

## Adding games to the markdown

Add the entry to `drinking-games.md` in the same shape as the others, then:

```bash
npm run parse
```

The parser rewrites the seed fields for every game from the markdown and keeps every other field already present in `games.json`. Games that exist only in the JSON (`source: "added"`) are kept and stay next to the rest of their subcategory. Renaming a game in the markdown changes its id, so its enrichment will be orphaned; rename the `id` in the JSON too if you do that.

## Merging more research

`scripts/merge-enrichment.ts` takes JSON files shaped like `[{ "id": "...", "rules": [...], ... }]` and merges them into `games.json` without touching seed fields. Objects with an unknown id are appended as new games with `source: "added"`.

```bash
npm run merge-enrichment path/to/file.json
```

ha7rock/blade2-mobile.readme:
# Blade II Mobile — 把 Switch 版《Blade II: The Return of Evil》搬到 iOS / macOS

这是对 [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)（把 Switch 版《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》原生跑在 iPhone 上的开源兼容层）的**方法论拆解**，以及把同一套方法**举一反三**用到本地另一款 Switch 游戏（Blade II，UE4 4.17）上的工程。
`dm/` 是 d2r-mobile 的 `dm/` 目录原样拷贝（MIT，见 `LICENSE.d2r-mobile`）加上 Blade 的改动；改动都能用 `git log -p` 看到。

状态（2026-10-15）：**Mac 宿主能进关卡正常游玩并出声；iOS 壳（`dm/ios/blade`）能为 iphoneos 编出完整 App，待真机验证**；细节见文末「现状与下一步」。
游戏内容（程序、资源、改写产物）一律不进仓库。

---

## 一、d2r-mobile 的核心思想

一句话：**不模拟 CPU，不翻译指令——Switch 和 iPhone 都是 AArch64，游戏程序本身可以原样执行；只把它对 Horizon 操作系统的依赖换成一个小宿主。**

它和模拟器（Ryujinx / yuzu）的根本区别：

| | 模拟器 | d2r-mobile |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 解释 / JIT 翻译每条指令 | 原生执行，一字节不动（除几类不能执行的指令） |
| 内核 | 完整模拟 Horizon 内核 | 只把 SVC 换成宿主函数（线程 = pthread，内存 = mmap） |
| 系统服务 | 模拟 IPC 服务进程 | 在 **SDK 函数接口处**按名字接管（HLE_FORCE） |
| 图形 | 模拟 Maxwell GPU | 在 **NVN API 层**接管，录制命令、Metal 回放 |
| 着色器 | 运行时翻译 | 离线翻译（Maxwell 机器码 → SPIR-V → MSL → metallib） |
| iOS JIT | 需要（iOS 不允许） | 不需要：改写在离线做，代码段作为已签名段编进 App |

### 1. 程序改写（`dm/tools/patch_nso.py`）

AArch64 上只有四类东西在苹果内核下不能原样跑，改写器用线性扫描找到它们，每处换成一条 `b` 跳进映像后面的「补丁区」，补丁块做完等价动作再跳回：

| 原指令 | 为什么不能跑 | 换成 |
|---|---|---|
| `x18` 的读写 | 苹果内核把 x18 当平台寄存器随时清零 | 读写线程槽 K18（`tpidrro_el0` + 键页里的键号×8 = pthread TSD 槽） |
| `mrs/msr tpidr_el0`、`mrs tpidrro_el0` | 游戏用它找 TLS / Horizon 线程区；苹果内核另有用途 | 读写线程槽 KTLS / KTLR |
| `svc #n` | 没有 Horizon 内核 | 跳「宿主门」（`entry.S` 的 `dm_gate`），按返回点查表得知是哪号 SVC |
| `mrs cntpct_el0` | 没有 19.2 MHz 系统计数器 | 也走宿主门，宿主换算 |

关键设计：
- **键页**：补丁块不写死 TSD 键号，而是从映像末尾一页只读「键页」里取，装载器填入实际键号——运行时零代码改写，iOS 才能把代码段原样签名。
- **窗口**：`ldxr/stxr` 独占访问序列里的 x18 不能单条替换（会破坏独占监视器），整段作为窗口一起改写。
- **跳转表 `br x18`**：目标必须离线枚举，补丁块按索引落到「落地垫」再恢复借用的寄存器。
- **剪口（CUTS）/ 观测门（OBS）/ 参数位（PARAMS）**：按 NSO 构建号登记的、有意的语义改动（离线补丁、宿主回调、分辨率参数），每条带原字节断言。
- **验证**：`dm/verify/equiv.py` 用 Unicorn 对每个改写点做「原指令 vs 补丁块」随机状态等价试验；`structck.py` 用独立反汇编器核对结构。

### 2. 装载与启动（`dm/host/loader.c`、`main.c`）

宿主扮演 rtld：映射 `main` 与 `sdk` 两个 NSO 的改写映像，建线程槽、登记门、做 ELF 重定位（RELATIVE / ABS64 / GLOB_DAT / JUMP_SLOT），按名字解析导入；然后**照抄 `nn::init::Start` 的真实次序**初始化 SDK 运行时（`_init_libc0 → nnosInitialize → _init_libc1 → nninitInitializeSdkModule → nninitStartup → _init_libc2 → 各模块 DT_INIT`），最后进 `nnMain`。每个游戏线程 = 一个宿主 pthread，跑在 SDK 给的客体栈上。

### 3. 三层接管（`dm/host/hle*.c`）

| 层 | 做法 |
|---|---|
| 内核 SVC | `hle_svc.c`（地址空间 / 堆 / 查询）、`hle_thread.c`（线程、锁、条件变量、地址仲裁、事件——按 Atmosphère mesosphère 的语义） |
| C 库 | `hle_table.c`：调用约定一致、无结构布局依赖的函数直通苹果 libc |
| 系统服务 | `HLE_FORCE("<改编名>", 理由, ...)`：SDK 里走 IPC 的服务客户端（fs / hid / audio / oe / account / nifm / vi …）在 SDK 接口处整个替换，`nn::os` 原样运行。表里有、没人引用的条目装载即报错——清单必须精确 |

没实现的导入接「记名桩」：被调到打一行 `UNIMPL 名字` 返回 0。

### 4. 图形（`dm/gfx`）

`main` 只导入一个 `nvnBootstrapLoader`，宿主接管它，之后游戏按名字取的 523 个 NVN 函数全部指向宿主：有 CPU 可见结果的按语义实现，只改 GPU 状态的录成命令、提交时用 Metal 回放。内存池 = 零拷贝 `MTLBuffer`（GPU 地址 = CPU 地址，只支持统一内存）。贴图从 Tegra block-linear 布局反 swizzle。着色器离线翻译：Ryujinx 的翻译器（C#）出 SPIR-V → spirv-cross 出 MSL → `xcrun metal` 编译；运行时按控制段 sha256 查库。

### 5. iOS 壳（`dm/ios`）

改写映像用 `gen_embed.py` 变成汇编内嵌进可执行文件（原 text 与补丁区是 `__TEXT` 的节、可写部分是独立段），装载器 `vm_remap` 回原相对布局——不复制代码、不改页权限。触屏层画在原版 UI 之上，命中由宿主按游戏面板树作答。

---

## 二、Blade II 的分析（本地 XCI）

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 游戏 | Blade II: The Return of Evil，title `01009cc00e224000`，更新 v131072 |
| 引擎 | **Unreal Engine 4.17** + PhysX 3.4（`++UE4+Release-4.17`、`D:\ProXTest\extra\Blade2toNS\...` 构建路径） |
| SDK | NintendoSDK 7.4（本体 6.5.2） |
| 模块 | `main` 48 MB（text 70 MB / rodata 37 MB / data 5 MB / bss 24 MB，解压后 131 MB）、`sdk` 13 MB、`subsdk0` 7 MB（任天堂 movie 库 + android 缓冲队列 + mkvparser） |
| 资源 | RomFS 4.1 GB：`BladeII/Content/Paks/*.pak`（两个 1.9 GB）+ 559 MB mp4 过场 |
| NVN | 取址 512 个函数，**静态调用 181 个**；其中 **37 个 D2R 从未调用**（`nvnCommandBufferDrawElements`、`BindTexture`、`BindVertexBuffer`、`SetViewport`、`nvnBuffer*`、`nvnQueueAcquireTexture`、`FenceSync`…），d2r 图形层没有实现 |

---

## 三、为了 Blade II 改了什么（举一反三的部分）

### 改写器（`dm/tools/patch_nso.py`）

直接拿 d2r 的改写器跑 Blade 的三个模块：`sdk` 一次通过；`subsdk0` 和 `main` 撞上三个 D2R 二进制里没有的情况，逐个补上：

1. **第二种跳转表写法**（UE4 / 较新 clang）：`adrp xB; add xB; ldrsw xT,[xB,xI,lsl #2]; add x18,xT,xB; br x18`，表项是 32 位相对偏移，到 `br` 时槽里已是绝对目标。新增 `site_br_abs`：离线按守门的 `cmp wI,#K` 读出 K+1 个目标，补丁块把槽值与每个目标比对后落到对应尾块恢复寄存器再跳。`sites.tsv` 以 `JA` 行登记。
2. **`blr x18`**（函数指针在 x18 里）：新增 `site_blr`。调用点上 x16/x17 本就可破坏（AAPCS64 IP0/IP1），直接借用。
3. **`ldr x18, <literal>`**：新增 `site_ldr_lit`。
4. **映像超过 128 MB**：`b` 的射程是 ±128 MB，补丁区再接在映像后面就够不着。改成**两遍发射**（第一遍只量长度），映像太大时把补丁区放到映像**前面**（`PATCH_OFF < 0`，产物文件 = 补丁区 + 映像），装载器把映像基址放在补丁区之后（`loader.c`，`patch_off` 改为有符号）。小模块布局不变，`sdk` 的产物逐字节与原改写器相同。

### 宿主（`dm/host`）

- `Makefile.blade`：只编通用部分（装载 / SVC / 服务接管 / 图形层），不带任何 `dm_*.c` 暗黑功能文件、`diag.c`、`touch_mac.c`。
- `blade_stubs.c`：通用文件里残留的 100 个 D2R 功能钩子的中性实现（过滤器原样放行、查询答「没有」、D2R 剪口才会到的宿主调用一律中止）。清单由 `tools/host_trial_build.sh` 的链接缺符号列表得出。
- `hle_blade.c`：Blade 多用到的 SDK 接口——movie 媒体信息、hid 六轴 / 握持 / 手柄支持小程序、oe、time 时区规则、swkbd 配置、vi 缩放、web / err / pctl / diag，**音频渲染器**（在 SDK 接口层按 voice 混音：PcmInt16 / DSP-ADPCM 解码、线性插值重采样、音量 × 混音矩阵（含 BufferMixer 路由）叠成立体声，CoreAudio 出声或静音接收端按实时消耗；波形缓冲播完归还、已播样本数如实；`DM_AUDIO=1` 出声，`DM_AUDIO_OUT_DUMP=<文件>` 转储混音结果），联网一组一律「不可用」。
- `hle_hid.c`：Joy-Con 双持 / 左 / 右三种样式答「没接」；`hle_fs.c`：`DeleteDirectory`、`CommitSaveData`、`GetDirectoryEntryCount`。
- `tools/extract_game.sh`：按本游戏的 title / 版本从 XCI 取文件（prod.keys 里格式不对的行先过滤）。

# Pung

Hong Kong mahjong you can actually play: against three opponents, or with friends around one table, in the browser, with nothing to install. 碰 (pung) is the call for claiming a discard to complete a set.

Live: https://francisphan.github.io/pung/

Pung is the sibling of [Sparrow](https://francisphan.github.io/sparrow/), which teaches the game from the first tile. Sparrow explains; Pung deals.

## The game

- **A full table.** 144 tiles, four seats, flowers set aside and replaced, a wall that runs down to the last tile. The dealer keeps the deal after a win or a drawn hand; the round wind turns after four dealerships. Play one East round or all four.
- **Every call.** Chow from the player before you, pung and kong from anyone, concealed and added kongs with a replacement draw, robbing a kong, self-drawn wins and wins on a discard. Priority is win, then pung or kong, then chow.
- **Hong Kong scoring.** Faan for all chows, all pungs, mixed and pure one suit, dragon and wind pungs, self-draw, a concealed hand, flowers, win on the kong, the last tile and robbing the kong, plus the limit hands: big and little three dragons, big and little four winds, all honours, all terminals, thirteen orphans, nine gates, four kongs, heavenly and earthly hands. A three-faan minimum by default (or one, or none), a thirteen-faan limit, points on the half-spicy-up table, and half payment from the two players who did not throw the winning tile.
- **Opponents that play fair.** Mei, Bo and Ling see only what a player at the table sees: their own rack, the open melds, the discards and the flowers. They judge a discard by how many tiles still bring the hand closer, and they only open a hand when it can still reach the minimum.
- **Friends at the table.** Host a table, share its four-letter code or link, and everyone picks a seat. Any seat left empty gets one of the bots when the host deals. The host's browser runs the table; the others connect to it directly, with nothing to install or deploy. A player who drops out keeps their seat and comes back to it; after twenty seconds away a bot moves for them until they return. See *Playing with friends*.
- **A table log.** Every deal, flower, discard, claim and win, with the tile shown, from your point of view: "Bo discarded Five of characters", "Ling pung on Bo's White dragon", "You win by self-draw". It sits beside the table on a wide screen and under your rack on a narrow one, scrolls back through earlier hands, and can be hidden.
- **The tiles you know.** Faces are the classic designs found on most sets, by Cangjie6 on Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0, see `CREDITS.md`), served as one optimised SVG sprite.
- **Soft sounds from the table.** A low wooden knock when a tile is set down, a lighter one when you pick one up, two or three for a claim, a muffled rummage as each hand is dealt, and a run of pieces when a winning hand is laid out. They are cut from CC0 recordings of chess pieces on a board (see `CREDITS.md`), kept quiet and low, and served from this site as MP3 files totalling under 200 KB, played through audio elements so they work on an iPad even with the ringer muted. "Sound off" in the masthead mutes them and the choice is remembered.
- **Pick up where you left off.** A solo game is saved in the browser after every move. An online table is remembered too: reload the page and you are back in your seat, and a host's reload brings the whole table back.

## Controls

Tap a tile to pick it up, tap it again to discard. When a discard suits your hand the table offers the claims you are allowed, with Pass beside them; a self-drawn win and any kong appear as buttons on your turn. Arrow keys move along the rack, Enter picks and discards, Escape puts a tile back.

Designed for an iPad held either way, and it works on a phone or a desktop.

## Playing with friends

Nothing to set up: the host's browser runs the table. The site on GitHub Pages is static, and the game, the bots and every player's view live in the host's page; friends' browsers connect to it directly over WebRTC. A public signalling service (PeerJS's) makes the introduction, which is how a four-letter code finds the right browser; after that no game data passes through anyone else.

- **Host.** In the lobby, give your name and tap *Host a table*. You get a code such as `QBAP` and a link (`…/pung/?join=QBAP`). You sit at East, which deals first. Keep the page open and in the foreground while you play: if it closes, the table closes for everyone (you are asked first when friends are at it). Reloading the page is fine; the table comes back from a copy kept in the browser and the others reconnect to it.
- **Join.** Friends enter the code, or open the link, and take the next open seat. Tapping another seat moves there; the host can put a bot on any open seat, or take one off, before dealing.
- **Deal.** The host chooses the rules and taps *Deal*. Open seats get bots. Only the host deals the next hand; everyone else sees the result card until then. When the game ends the host can play again at the same table with the same seats.
- **Dropping out.** A guest who closes the tab, loses the network or whose iPad goes to sleep keeps their seat. Come back to the same page and you rejoin; opening the table in a second window moves you to that window. After twenty seconds away a bot plays your turns and claims until you return. *Leave table* gives your hand to a bot for the rest of the game, or opens the seat if the game has not started. Someone arriving with the code during a game takes over a bot's seat.
- **Fairness.** Each guest's browser is sent only what its seat may see: its own rack, the open melds, the discards, and how many tiles the others and the wall still hold. The host's browser holds the whole table, so the host could in principle read the code's memory; among friends that is the same trust as handling the physical wall.
- **If a browser cannot connect.** Most home and office networks connect directly

A masthead

Pung: playable Hong Kong mahjong against three opponents

A sibling to Sparrow that deals instead of explaining. The engine in
src/engine is a pure reducer over a serialisable table state: dealing
with flower replacement, draws, discards, claim windows with win > pung
or kong > chow priority, concealed and added kongs with robbing, wins by
self-draw or discard, half-spicy-up settlement and dealer rotation over
one or four rounds. Scoring covers the common Hong Kong patterns and the
limit hands;

educlopez/diorama.readme:
Diorama

A Claude Code skill that builds small animated 3D worlds for the web.
Isometric scenes made of blocks and soft shadows, with little trucks, forklifts and people that keep their own time. A hero for a landing page, a card for your docs, or a mini figure for an empty state. Five themes, from pastel toy to a hairline drawing, all of them yours to tune.

 

examples/town.js, a hero. Cars, a bus and a tram keep the streets busy, the crane turns, the fountain splashes, the lights cycle.

--- Ask Claude for a 3D illustration and Diorama has it build a place: a yard, a street corner, a rack, a letterbox on a post. Every object is a handful of boxes and cylinders standing on a rounded base, seen from an isometric camera and lit by one warm sun with soft shadows. Two or three things keep their own time (a truck on a lap, a forklift shuttle, a flag), one thing answers the pointer, and the camera tilts a few degrees toward the mouse. The default look is an isometric camera, matte blocks, one warm sun with soft shadows and a few accents, built into a skill with themes, so the same scene file can be a pastel toy town, a cream editorial figure, a monochrome with one accent, a hairline drawing, or a night scene with the lamps on.

One figure file, five themes: toy, soft, mono, line, night. The gallery switches them live.

## Quick start ```sh npx skills add educlopez/diorama -g ``` Then, in Claude Code: ```text /diorama a hero illustration for our logistics landing page: a warehouse yard with trucks docking and forklifts moving pallets /diorama an empty state for the inbox when there are no messages, small and cute /diorama a card-sized scene for the docs explaining how the build queue works ``` Claude offers two or three concepts, builds the one you choose, checks it in a headless browser, and hands you one HTML file. ## Gallery | | | |---|---| | | | | **`island`** · a hero. The boat circles and ties up at the pier, the lamp turns, gulls cross, the waves breathe. | **`farm`** · a hero. The tractor laps the fields and stops at the barn, the windmill turns, the sheep graze. | | | | | **`warehouse`** · a hero. A truck does a lap and docks, a forklift carries pallets to the racks, a worker walks the aisle. | **`cafe`** · a card in `soft`. The barista pulls shots, a customer comes for a cup, the cat flicks its tail. | | | | | **`launchpad`** · a card, in `night`. The rocket waits under floodlights and every so often the arm swings back and it lifts off. | **`server`** · a card, in `mono` with a teal accent. The racks blink in their own rhythms, the fan turns; hover a rack and all its lights come on. | | |

RashidIsmayilzada/chess-match-analyzer.readme:
# chess-analyzer

A local, single-user web app that imports a chess.com user's games and produces a
chess.com-style Game Review: per-move classification (Brilliant, Great, Best, Excellent, Good,
Book, Inaccuracy, Mistake, Miss, Blunder), accuracy, estimated rating, opening name, eval graph
and key moments. Everything runs on your machine: Stockfish 19 does the analysis, SQLite stores
games and cached positions.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is the contract between the packages (types, classification rules, HTTP
API, database schema, UI routes). Read it before changing anything shared.

## Layout

```
packages/core     @chess-analyzer/core    pure logic: UCI engine wrapper, PGN parsing, openings
                                          book, classifier, game analysis orchestration
packages/server   @chess-analyzer/server  Fastify 5 API, SQLite (Drizzle), chess.com importer,
                                          analysis queue, SSE progress events
packages/web      @chess-analyzer/web     Vite + React 19 UI (chessground board, recharts graph)
engines/          Stockfish binary (downloaded by scripts/setup-engine.sh, git-ignored)
data/openings/    Lichess chess-openings dataset (ECO, name, moves)
data/fixtures/    sample PGNs and a chess.com archive used by tests
scripts/          setup-engine.sh, smoke.sh (+ smoke.mjs), calibrate.mjs
```

## Setup

Requirements: Node 22+, npm 10+, Linux x86-64 (for the bundled Stockfish download; any UCI
engine works if you point `enginePath` at it).

```sh
npm install                 # installs all workspaces (better-sqlite3 builds a native module)
scripts/setup-engine.sh     # downloads Stockfish 19 into engines/stockfish
npm run build -w packages/core   # server and web import core's compiled types from dist/
```

## Development

```sh
npm run dev        # server on http://localhost:3001 + Vite on http://localhost:5173
npm run dev:server # just the API (tsx watch)
npm run dev:web    # just the UI (proxies /api to :3001)
```

Open http://localhost:5173, enter a chess.com username on the Import page, then analyse games
from the Games page. Analysis progress streams over `/api/events`.

Server environment variables: `PORT` (3001), `HOST`, `DB_PATH` (`data/chess-analyzer.db`),
`ENGINE_PATH` (overrides the stored engine path), `LOG_LEVEL`.

## Build and run in production mode

```sh
npm run build                     # core -> server -> web
node packages/server/dist/index.js
```

The server serves `packages/web/dist` with an SPA fallback when it exists, so the whole app is
on http://localhost:3001.

## Tests

```sh
npm run typecheck   # tsc for all three packages
npm test            # vitest: core (engine tests use the real Stockfish binary) + server
```

Per package: `npx vitest run src/classify` from `packages/core`, etc.

## Smoke test (real engine, real chess.com API)

```sh
scripts/smoke.sh [username]        # default user: xseven123
```

Builds core and server, starts the server on a scratch database (`data/smoke.db`), imports the
user's three latest games, analyses the first at depth 12, verifies the resulting
`GameAnalysis` (move count, classifications, book moves, opening, accuracies, ratings, key
moments, no NaN/null), checks `/api/openings?q=london` and `/api/health`, and confirms that a
repeat analysis is served from the position cache in well under a second. The server log goes
to `data/smoke-server.log`. Environment: `PORT`, `SMOKE_DB`, `SMOKE_LOG`, `SMOKE_DEPTH`.

## Tuning classification thresholds

Every tunable number lives in `packages/core/src/config/thresholds.ts` (`DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS`,
documented field by field). The classifier itself contains no magic numbers; the rules it
applies are specified in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("Classification rules").

Two ways to tune:

1. **At runtime, per installation**: the Settings page (`/settings`) has a thresholds editor.
   Whatever you save is stored as a deep-partial override in the `settings` table and merged
   over the defaults (`PUT /api/settings { thresholds: { bands: { good: 0.06 } } }`;
   `DELETE /api/settings` resets). Changing thresholds does not invalidate cached engine
   positions, so re-analysing a game after a tweak is fast.
2. **Changing the defaults**: edit `thresholds.ts`, run `npx vitest run src/classify` in
   `packages/core` (the classifier is developed test-first against fixture positions; update the
   boundary tests when you move a band) and rebuild core.

Things worth knowing when tuning:

- Win probabilities are mover POV, 0..1, from a logistic on centipawns (`winProb.k`); mate scores
  are converted with `winProb.mateCp`. Band thresholds are win-probability losses.
- `brilliant.minSacrificeValue` is NET material (SEE loss minus what the move captures): 2 lets
  exchange sacrifices and the Greek gift through, 3 requires a clean minor piece.
  `brilliant.maxWinProbBefore` (0.95) withholds Brilliant once the game is already decided.
- `great.excludeRecaptures` / `great.excludeFreeCaptures` keep obvious captures (taking back a
  traded piece, grabbing a hanging one) from being Great; `miss.minOwnLoss` (0.10) means only a
  mistake-sized give-back after the opponent's mistake is a Miss.
- `rating.evalClampCp` clamps evals before centipawn loss is computed so that noise in decisive
  positions does not wreck the average; `rating.byTimeClass` is a deliberately simple linear
  model of ACPL to rating.
- Engine settings (depth, MultiPV, threads, hash, movetime, engine path) are on the same page;
  MultiPV must be at least 2 for Great / Brilliant detection.

### Calibration report

`scripts/calibrate.mjs` (`npm run calibrate -- ...`) runs the real pipeline (`analyzeGame`, the
default opening book, a fresh Stockfish per game) over a few games and prints, per game, the
players, result, opening, each side's accuracy / estimated rating and a classification count
table, then the totals and every Brilliant / Great / Miss with ply, SAN, win probability
before/after, loss, evals (white POV)

core+server: key the position cache by movetime as well

With settings { depth: 18, movetimeMs: 200 } a 200 ms search was cached under
depth 18; after clearing the movetime every position hit the cache, so a
"depth 18" analysis was built from 200 ms searches (and later movetime runs
reused real depth-18 lines). PositionCache.get/set now take the requested
movetime (0 for a depth search), analyzeGame passes it, and the
position_analyses primary key gains movetime_ms. Existing databases are
rebuil

server: end SSE streams in preClose so shutdown does not hang on connected clients

Fastify closes the HTTP server before running onClose hooks and only
force-closes idle sockets, so the onClose hook that ended the SSE responses
ran too late: with the web UI's permanent EventSource connected, Ctrl-C left
the process alive until the client dropped (heartbeats kept flowing). The
streams are now ended in a preClose hook, which runs before the server
closes. Test: app.close() resolves within 1.5 s w

server: a running analysis holds an engine lease; /api/health never restarts it

EngineManager.acquire() restarted the engine whenever the requested
enginePath/threads/hashMb differed from the running one, with no regard for
the job using it. GET /api/health calls acquire with the current settings
(the Settings page does so on mount), so saving engine settings and then
opening Settings while an analysis ran killed the job with "engine process
exited (code 0)".

klaymendel-art/tesla-flip.readme:
# Tesla Flip 🛹⚡

Tiny mobile-first browser game: a cartoon Elon rides a miniature Tesla Roadster like a skateboard through a dusk city while old V8 gas guzzlers block the road. Tap to kickflip over them. Crash = game over.

- Play: https://klaymendel-art.github.io/tesla-flip/
- Stack: vanilla HTML5 Canvas 2D, no frameworks, no build step.
- Art generated via OpenRouter (Gemini image models), audio synthesised procedurally with Python/numpy.


## Screenshots

| Title | Kickflip | Double flip over a pair |
|---|---|---|
| ![title](docs/screenshots/title.png) | ![flip](docs/screenshots/flip.png) | ![pair](docs/screenshots/pair.png) |

![flip burst](docs/screenshots/flip_burst.png)

## How it was made

Built in one session by a producer session coordinating five agents (dev, art, SFX, music, QA). The QA agent ran three review rounds with pixel and timing measurements — see `qa/REPORT.md`. Art via OpenRouter image models (≈ $1 total), audio synthesised with numpy; everything is re-renderable from `tools/`.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Tap / click anywhere (or the big FLIP button) | Kickflip |
| Two taps within 200 ms | Double flip — higher and longer, clears a close pair of cars |
| `Space` / `↑` / `Enter` | Kickflip (desktop) |
| `M` or the speaker icon (top-right) | Mute / unmute (remembered) |
| Tap on the GAME OVER panel | Retry |

+1 point for every car you clear. Speed ramps up with your score; the best score is kept in `localStorage`.

## Run locally

Audio is fetched via `fetch()`, so the game needs an HTTP server (from `file://` it runs silently):

```sh
python -m http.server 8077      # then open http://localhost:8077/
```

Append `?debug=1` to the URL to draw the collision boxes. `window.TF` exposes the game state for automated testing.

## Project layout

- `index.html`, `src/game.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/style.css` — the game.
- `assets/img`, `assets/sfx`, `assets/music` — art and audio (see `docs/DESIGN.md` for the asset contract).
- `tools/` — generators (`gen_image.py`, `placeholders.py`, audio scripts).
- `qa/` — QA report and screenshots.

## Note

The rider is a caricature made for parody. This project is a fan-made toy with no affiliation with, or endorsement by, Tesla, Inc. or any person depicted.

muhammedqais/blind-buzzer.readme:
# Blind Buzzer

A party game about feeling time. Each round names a target, say **20 seconds**.
You tap to start a hidden clock and tap again when you think the time is up.
Nothing on screen moves while it runs. Whoever stops closest to the target
takes the round; most rounds won takes the game (ties broken by total error).

## Play it

Open `index.html` from any web host (GitHub Pages works as is). No build
step, no server, no accounts.

**Online room.** One person taps *Online room*, picks rounds, target style
and the longest target (swipe the dial, 1s to 60s), and gets a 4-letter code.
Friends open the same link, type a name and the code, and tap *Ready*. The
host taps *Start* once everyone is ready (the button says who is not). Everyone
plays each round on their own phone; a round is revealed once every time is
in. *Play again* returns the room to the lobby, where the host can change the
settings before the next game. Rooms are peer to peer over WebRTC (PeerJS):
the host's browser runs the room, and if the host leaves or drops, the room
passes to the next player automatically. If a player stalls, anyone can tap
*Skip* next to their name; a player who reloads rejoins where they were.

**One device.** Pass a phone around. Players take turns on the same target;
every time stays sealed until the last player in the round has gone.

**Solo.** Play alone. Every round scores at once and the game keeps your best
average error on the device.

A reload never loses a game: hosts reopen their room, guests rejoin it, and
one-device and solo games pick up where they were.

## Rules

- Target style is chosen per game, all from 0.05s up to the dial: **Whole
  seconds** (2, 7, 15), **Decimals** (never a round number: 0.83, 2.69, 18.36,
  half of them under a second) or **Mixed** (half whole, half decimals). None
  repeats in a game.
- Every player in a round gets the same target.
- Closest absolute error wins the round. Equal errors share the point.
- Final order: round points, then lowest total error.
- Every player gets two retries per game: while your time is still sealed and
  others are thinking, you can withdraw it and run the round again. Play again
  resets the count.

## Files

- `index.html` – the whole game. PeerJS loads from a CDN; everything else
  is inline.

## Running locally

Open `index.html` in a browser. For a phone on the same Wi-Fi, serve the
folder (`python3 -m http.server`) and open the computer's address on the
phone.

RickMcIntyre/ncaa2mindrill.readme:
# NCAA Two-Minute Drill (ncaa2mindrill.com)

A college-football version of nfl2mindrill.com: one real late-game FBS drive a day (2023–2025), you call the snaps, and your win chance is compared with what the real head coach got.

## Layout

- `docs/` — the static site, ready to upload as-is. `index.html` is the page, `app.js` is the engine/UI, `anim.js` animates each snap (routes, coverage, pursuit, ball flight, big-play popups), `data.json` is generated. Bump `app.js?v=` in index.html when you change app.js so browsers refetch it.
- `build/build.py` — turns the raw play-by-play into `docs/data.json` (scenarios, pools of real snaps, win-probability and field-goal models, team ratings, lineups).
- `build/wiki_coaches.py` — caches each team-season's Wikipedia infobox in `raw/wiki/` so interim head coaches get credited game by game.
- `raw/` — downloaded inputs (not needed to run the site).

## Rebuild the data

```bash
cd build
python wiki_coaches.py     # optional, only for new team-seasons
python build.py

```

Inputs come from SportsDataverse GitHub releases (`cfbfastR_cfb_pbp`, `espn_cfb_coach_tendencies`, `espn_cfb_game_rosters`, `espn_cfb_schedules`, `espn_cfb_teams`). To add a season, download its files into `raw/` with the same names and add the year to `YEARS` in `build.py`.

## Run locally

```bash
python -m http.server 8765 --directory docs
```

Then open http://localhost:8765/. To deploy, upload the contents of `docs/` (index.html, app.js, data.json) to the ncaa2mindrill.com host.

## How the game works

- **Scenarios**: every FBS-vs-FBS drive that started in Q4 with 2:30 or less, trailing by 1–16 or tied, at least 20 yards from the end zone. The regular daily uses the one-score drives (trailing by 8 or fewer); **Saban mode** uses drives that start at 10% win chance or worse, or two scores down.
- **Outcomes**: each call draws a real 2023–2025 snap from a pool keyed by call type (depth × side for passes, inside/outside for runs), field zone and down. The draw is tilted by both teams' season EPA ratings and the chosen player's season numbers.
- **Trick plays**: the whole bag is on the board every down (flea flicker, halfback pass, reverse, jet sweep, wildcat, Statue of Liberty, hook and ladder, Philly Special, plus fake field goal in range and fake punt on fourth down). Each rides a base pool (deep pass, short pass, inside or outside run) with its own tilt by defensive look, its own sack/interception/fumble multipliers, and a chance of being blown up in the backfield. They are scored like every other option, so the grade says when a trick was the wrong call. Each has its own choreography in `anim.js`.
- **Two-point try**: a real snap from the 3, untimed. Every option's conversion chance comes from the goal-line pools, anchored so the board's average equals the measured college two-point rate; the call is animated and graded like any other snap.
- **Win probability**: a logistic model fitted on all Q4 FBS plays, by score bucket, with time, field position, down, distance, timeouts and pregame Elo gap. Calibrated within about one point in every decile.
- **Clock**: college rules. Stops on incompletions and out of bounds; restarts on the ready-for-play after a first down, except inside two minutes where it briefly stops.
- **Coach comparison**: the same model evaluated at the end of the real drive, plus a snap-by-snap grid of your calls against the coach's.
- **Defensive looks**: each snap the defense shows a look (base, loaded box, light box, blitz, prevent), sampled from the situation; it tilts every option and the animation aligns to it.
- **Penalties, scrambles, strip sacks, kicker quality**: flag rate and types from late-game snaps (pre-snap flags wipe the play, live-ball flags bring it back), QB scrambles at the measured rate, 1 in 10 sacks is a strip, and each team-season's kicker is rated against the distance model.
- **Tempo**: when the clock is running you choose hustle (≈5 s off), neutral (the measured median), or milk it (≈34 s), or burn a timeout.
- **Percentile**: 300 synthetic play-callers (different sharpness, run/pass lean, timeout habits) replay the same drive through the engine; your finish is ranked against theirs.
- **Coach resemblance**: your pass rate overall, on early downs and on passing downs is matched to the nearest real FBS head coach's 2023–25 tendencies.
- **Share**: a 1200×630 card (canvas) with Web Share / X intent / copy / save.
- **Grading and difficulty**: three settings (`DIFF` in app.js). Saban mode is the cliff: green only within half a point of the best call, yellow within 3, and a simulated room that barely misses. Cignetti loosens both a notch (green within 1 point, yellow within 4.5). Everything free (Daily, Survival, the library) is graded on the coach's own curve (green within 2 points, yellow within 6) against a room that makes human mistakes. A hard drive replayed from a library or reached deep in a Survival run uses its own setting. Trophies are judged on the cliff whatever the screen showed. The free daily pool is one-score drives starting at 30–75% win chance.
- **Personnel**: 10, 11, 12, 13, 21 or 22 on every snap. The build keeps 4 WR, 3 TE and 2 RB per team-game (padded from the game roster with league-average hands when a tight end or back never caught a pass). Heavy groups add run advantage and a little pass protection and cost pass advantage; four wide does the reverse. The defensive look is drawn again when you sub, with loaded boxes more likely against tight ends and extra DBs against four wide. The fullback leads through the hole in the animation.
- **Survival**: a run of random real drives, each round harder (rounds 1–2 start at 40%+ win chance, 3–4 at 28–45%, 5–6 at 25–36%, 7–9 from the Cignetti shelf, 10+ from the Saban pool). After each drive the rest of the game plays out at the model's odds: win to stay alive, one loss ends the run. Rounds 7+ need the unlock. The old Practice library lives under Survival → Drive library

# StackChan + RoverC Pro 制御 M5Stack 公式 StackChan のボディ（K151）に **Core2** を載せ、**M5StickC Plus** が制御する RoverC Pro に乗せた機体を PC から動かす。 ```mermaid flowchart LR PC -- "HTTP / USB シリアル" --> C[Core2
顔・声・首] C -- "ESP-NOW" --> S[StickC Plus
車輪・グリッパー] ``` PC は Core2 にだけ話しかける。turn 2 からは PC 上の常駐ハブ経由で操作する（下の「リアルタイム制御」）。走行系のコマンドは Core2 が ESP-NOW で StickC Plus に転送する。 StickC Plus に Wi-Fi 設定は不要で、Core2 のビーコンを探してチャンネルを自動で合わせる。 - `h3game/` DOF Reality H3（モーションプラットフォーム）で遊ぶ 3 シーンのゲーム。別物なので [h3game/README.md](h3game/README.md) と [h3game/INSTALL.md](h3game/INSTALL.md) を見る。 - `firmware/` Core2 用ファームウェア（PlatformIO）。顔、声、首、コマンド受付。 - `firmware-rover/` M5StickC Plus 用ファームウェア。車輪、グリッパー。 - `client/robot.py` PC 用 CLI 兼 Python ライブラリ（標準ライブラリのみ）。 - `docs/superpowers/specs/` 設計書。 ## 書き込み pioarduino は Python 3.10 以上が必要なので `uvx` 経由で実行する。 ```sh cd firmware cp include/secrets.h.example include/secrets.h # Wi-Fi を書く（省略可） uvx --python 3.12 platformio run -t upload --upload-port /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX # Core2 uvx --python 3.12 platformio device monitor cd ../firmware-rover uvx --python 3.12 platformio run -t upload --upload-port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY # StickC Plus ``` StickC Plus の画面は、Core2 と繋がると緑、探索中は黒、RoverC が見つからないと赤になる。 書き込み前の元ファームウェアは `backup/`（git 管理外）に保存してある。戻すには: ```sh uvx --python 3.12 esptool --port write-flash 0 backup/.bin ``` `secrets.h` が無い、または接続できない場合は、機体がアクセスポイントになる。 SSID は `stackchan-rover`、パスワードは `stackchan`、アドレスは `192.168.4.1`。 起動すると IP アドレスが吹き出しに出る。 ## 初回の確認手順 1. `python3 client/robot.py --host status` で `rover` `body` `servos` が `true` か見る。 - `rover` が `false` なら StickC Plus の電源と RoverC の電源スイッチを確認する。 2. `robot.py calibrate --default` で首を有効にする（実機で既定の原点が合うことを確認済み）。 校正するまで首は脱力していて動かない。`robot.py head --yaw 0 --pitch 45` で正面を向けば完了。 ずれている場合だけ、首を手で正面・水平に保持したまま `robot.py calibrate` を実行する。 3. `robot.py grip 0` と `robot.py grip 100` でグリッパーを確認する。 動かなければ `robot.py servo 1 90` を試し、`config.h` の `GRIPPER_CH` と角度を直す。 ## 使い方 ```sh export ROBOT_HOST=192.168.4.1 # または stackchan.local python3 client/robot.py say "こんにちは" # macOS の say で合成して再生、口パクする python3 client/robot.py face happy --text "やあ" python3 client/robot.py head --yaw 30 --pitch 45 python3 client/robot.py drive --y 50 --ms 1000 # 前進。指定時間で自動停止（最大 5 秒） python3 client/robot.py drive --x 50 # 右へ平行移動 python3 client/robot.py drive --rot 50 # 旋回 python3 client/robot.py grip 100 python3 client/robot.py stop # 画面下の左ボタンでも停止 ``` Python から: ```python from robot import Robot r = Robot("192.168.4.1") r.face("happy"); r.say("こんにちは"); r.drive(y=50, ms=1000) ``` ## プレゼンター（Canon PR7-HY）で操作する リモコンはキーボードとして見えるので、キー入力を機体のコマンドに変換する。 ボタンと動作の対応は `client/presenter.py` 冒頭の `BINDINGS` で変える。 ```sh uv run client/presenter.py --global --learn # 各ボタンが送るキー名を表示する python3 client/presenter.py --dry-run # 送るコマンドを表示するだけ python3 client/presenter.py # 機体に送る（このターミナルが前面のときだけ） uv run client/presenter.py --global # どのアプリが前面でも拾う（入力監視の許可が必要） ``` ## コマンド `POST /cmd` に JSON を送る。USB シリアル（115200 bps）に 1 行 1 JSON でも同じ。 `drive` `grip` `servo` `stop` は StickC Plus の USB シリアルに直接送ることもできる。 | cmd | 引数 | |-----|------| | `status` | なし | | `face` | `expression`: neutral / happy / angry / sad / doubt / sleepy、`text`: 吹き出し | | `head` | `yaw` -120〜120、`pitch` 5〜85（度）、`speed` 1〜1000 | | `calibrate` | `default`: true で既定値を採用 | | `torque` | `on`: true / false | | `drive` | `x` `y` `rot` -100〜100、`ms` 継続時間 | | `grip` | `percent` 0（開）〜100（閉） | | `servo` | `ch` 0/1、`angle` 0〜180（RoverC のサーボを直接） | | `stop` | 車輪、首、音声を止める | | `volume` | `value` 0〜255 | | `beep` | `freq` `ms` | `POST /speak` に 16bit PCM の WAV（2 MB まで）を送ると再生する。 ## toio を 9 台動かす StackChan とは別系統。Mac が BLE で toio コア キューブに直接つなぐ（Core2 は経由しない）。 ``` AI / スクリプト ──HTTP (127.0.0.1:8765)──▶ toio ハブ（常駐）──BLE──▶ キューブ 1〜9 ``` - `client/toio_hub.py` 常駐ハブ。接続を保持し、`POST /cmd` で JSON コマンドを受ける。 - `client/toio.py` CLI 兼 Python ライブラリ（標準ライブラリのみ）。 - `client/toio_config.json` マットの範囲と、キューブ名と番号の対応。 マットは toio 開発用プレイマットの表面（7 × 5 マスの面）を使う。座標は左上 (98, 142)、右下 (402, 358)。 マスは左から 1〜7 列、上から 1〜5 行。 ### 初回の準備 近くに他人の toio があっても触らないよう、名前（`toio-XXX` の末尾 3 文字）を指定した台にしか接続しない。 1. 自分のキューブの名前を調べる。接続はせず、電波の強い順（近い順の目安）に一覧を出す。 初回は macOS が Bluetooth の利用許可を求める。 ```sh uv run client/toio_hub.py --scan ``` 2. 全台の電源を入れてマットに載せ、接続を確かめる。 ```sh uv run client/toio_spike.py --names a1B,c2D --minutes 1 --move ``` 最後に `PASS` と出れば、この Mac で指定した全台を同時に扱える。 3. 番号を割り当てる。1 台ずつ白く光るので、その台に付ける番号（1〜9）を入力し、番号シールを貼る。 ```sh uv run client/toio_hub.py --assign --names a1B,c2D ``` ### 使い方 ```sh uv run client/toio_hub.py # ハブを起動（別のターミナルで動かしたままにする） python3 client/toio.py status # 全台の接続、位置、マス、電池 python3 client/toio.py move 3 --cell 4,2 # 3 番を 4 列 2 行のマスへ。到着まで待つ python3 client/toio.py move 3 --xy 250,250 --angle 90 python3 client/toio.py move-all 1:1,1 2:2,1 3:3,1 # 番号:列,行。まとめて動かす python3 client/toio.py drive 3 --left 50 --right 50 --ms 500 # マットの外でも使える python3 client/toio.py led all 0 255 0 python3 client/toio.py identify 5 # 5 番を点滅させて鳴らす python3 client/toio.py stop # 全台停止 ``` Python から: ```python from toio import Toio t = Toio() t.move(3, cell=(4, 2)) t.move_all({1: (1, 1), 2: (2, 1)}) ``` ### コマンド `POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/cmd` に JSON を送る。応答は `{"ok":true,...}` か `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`。 | cmd | 引数 | |-----|------| | `status` | なし | | `move` | `id`、`col` `row` または `x` `y`、任意で `angle` `speed`（10〜115、既定 80）`timeout`（秒、既定 10）`wait` | | `move_all` | `targets`: `[{id, col, row}]` または `[{id, x, y}]`、任意で `speed` `timeout` `wait` | | `drive` | `id`、`left` `right` -115〜115、`ms` 10〜2550 | | `led` | `id`、`r` `g` `b` 0〜255、任意で `ms` | | `sound` | `id`、`effect` 0〜10 | | `identify` | `id` | | `stop` | 任意で `id`。省くと全台 | `id` は 1〜9。`drive` `led` `sound` `stop` は `"all"` も取れる。 `move` の結果は `reached`（到着）、`timeout`、`off_mat`（マットから外れた）、`interrupted`（`s

omrigattegno/Imposter.readme:
# Imposter

A pass-the-phone party game for 4–10 people around a table. One phone, no cards, no second device,
no account. The app draws a secret word and secretly makes one player the Imposter; everyone lifts the
phone toward their face to see their role privately, gives one-word clues, discusses, votes in private,
and the Imposter gets a last guess if caught. Hebrew and English (the word language can differ from the app language), playable
fully offline as an installable PWA.

The product brief is in [`BRIEF.md`](BRIEF.md); the module contract and state machine are in
[`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Run it

```sh
npm install
npm run dev          # vite --host: prints a http://<LAN-IP>:5173 URL you can open on a phone
```

The lift-to-reveal gesture and the screen wake lock only work in a **secure context** (HTTPS or
`localhost`). A phone on the LAN opening `http://192.168.x.x:5173` gets the hold-to-reveal fallback and
no wake lock. To test the real thing on a device:

- run `npx vite --host` and put a tunnel in front of it (`npx localtunnel --port 5173`, `cloudflared
  tunnel --url http://localhost:5173`, ngrok, …), then open the HTTPS URL on the phone; or
- push to `main`/`master` and open the GitHub Pages URL (see *Deploy*):
  `https://omrigattegno.github.io/imposter/`.

On a desktop browser there are no motion sensors, so the reveal uses the hold-to-reveal button.

## Scripts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Dev server on the LAN (`vite --host`) |
| `npm run build` | `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` → `dist/` (service worker, manifest, icons included) |
| `npm run preview` | Serves `dist/` (`vite preview --host`) |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript only |
| `npm test` / `npm run test:watch` | Unit tests (vitest, node environment) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Playwright end-to-end tests against `dist/` (build first) |
| `npm run icons` | Regenerates `favicon.svg` and the PNG icons from `public/icon.svg` (`scripts/render-icon.mjs`) |

## Test

**Unit** (`src/**/*.test.ts`, vitest, node environment): the state machine, guess matching, RNG,
storage, sensors and the PWA helpers.

```sh
npm test
npx vitest run src/game/engine.test.ts   # one file
```

**End-to-end** (`e2e/`, Playwright, `playwright.config.ts`): a 390×844 mobile Chromium project with
touch, run against the production build served by `vite preview` on port 4173.

```sh
npm run build
npm run test:e2e                     # starts vite preview itself
PWDEBUG=1 npm run test:e2e           # inspector
npm run test:e2e:screenshots         # review captures -> ./screenshots/*.png (gitignored)
```

The specs: `round-hold.spec.ts` (a whole round with the hold button, resume after a reload, next round),
`round-lift.spec.ts` (the same round driven by synthetic `deviceorientation` events), `hebrew.spec.ts`
(RTL, Hebrew UI and card), `avatars.spec.ts` (one character per Setup row, the picker swap, avatars on
the ballot, the Imposter unmasked on Results, the Sound effects switch) and `offline.spec.ts` (the shell loads with the network cut once the service
worker is installed). Selectors are `data-testid` attributes on the screens, so the same helpers
(`e2e/helpers.ts`) drive both languages. Holding is simulated with synthetic touch pointer events, which
leaves the mouse free to tap a ballot name while the card is held, like a second finger would.

The config uses the Chromium preinstalled under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` (default
`/opt/pw-browsers`) when present, so `playwright install` is not needed there; on a machine without
it, Playwright resolves its own browser as usual. Build and preview must use the same `VITE_BASE`.

## Build and deploy

```sh
npm run build                            # base "/"
VITE_BASE=/imposter/ npm run build       # under a sub-path (GitHub Pages project site)
```

`VITE_BASE` sets Vite's base, the manifest `start_url`/`scope` and the service worker's navigation
fallback, so one build works from exactly one path.

Deployment is automatic: `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` builds the app on every push to
`main`/`master` (or on *Run workflow*) with Node 22 and publishes `dist` with `actions/deploy-pages`.
The workflow enables Pages itself on the first run; if that is refused, set **Settings → Pages →
Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions** once. The site then lives at
`https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/` (or at the root for a repo named `<owner>.github.io`).

### Offline and install

- Everything is precached by the service worker (Workbox via `vite-plugin-pwa`): app shell, styles and
  the word packs, which are static JSON imports bundled into the JavaScript. After the first visit no
  round needs the network, and the app makes no runtime network calls at all (no fonts, no CDNs, no
  analytics).
- Updates: `registerType: 'autoUpdate'`. A new build's worker is installed silently in the background
  and takes control of the page; `src/lib/pwa.ts` passes a no-op `onNeedReload`, so the page is
  deliberately not reloaded when that happens and the new build is used from the next launch.
- Install card (Home screen, `src/components/InstallPrompt.tsx`): on Android/desktop Chromium it
  triggers the native *Add to Home Screen* dialog; on iOS it explains *Share ▸ Add to Home Screen*.
  It hides when the app already runs standalone, and "Not now" remembers the dismissal on the device
  (`localStorage` key `imposter.v1.installDismissed`).
- Icons: `public/icon.svg` is the hand-drawn source of truth (Bolt from the avatar cast, masked, on the
  night-blue tile with a soft halo). `npm run icons` (`scripts/render-icon.mjs`) copies it to
  `public/favicon.svg` and screenshots the PNG set with the preinstalled Playwright Chromium (the same

  `icons/icon-512.png` (rounded tile, transparent corners, manifest purpose `any`),

TefMeister/hand-poser-vr.desc: UNTESTED, design stage - a compact desktop window of bone sliders that poses the player's hands in RE Engine games (REFramework), to be used inside the headset with Window View and Hand Freeze. Inspired by alphaZomega's EMV Engine poser. Started 2026-10-16.
TefMeister/hand-poser-vr.readme: # Hand Poser — pose the player's hands in RE Engine games with sliders > ⚠️ **UNTESTED.** Built on 2026-10-16 and proven only against a stand-in game (a script pretending to be the in-game > half), never yet inside a real RE game. The in-game script may find no character, name the joints differently, or hold > nothing. Removing the script's file from the game's `reframework\autorun` folder undoes everything it does. A small desktop window plus one REFramework script. Press **LEFT FINGERS** and every finger joint of the left hand gets a row with three sliders, X, Y and Z in degrees, already set to where the game has that finger right now. Move a slider and the finger follows, live, and stays there while the game's own animation keeps running around it. Add any other joint from the list (type part of its name to find it), take rows away with the cross, **RESET** one to zero. While you drag a slider, the rows of the joints it carries along light up amber. **UNDO** and **REDO** go back and forth through your last 200 changes. Every change is saved by itself and comes back next time; **SAVE BUILD** keeps a named pose to **LOAD** later. Close the window and the game has its hands back. Made for tuning hand and finger poses in our VR mods (2026-10-16): with Hand Freeze holding the controllers still and Window View hanging this window inside the headset, fingers can be posed without taking the headset off. Inspired by the poser inside alphaZomega's EMV Engine, which lives in REFramework's own menu; this one is a separate window so it can be used that way. ## Get it Download the zip from [Releases](https://github.com/TefMeister/hand-poser-vr/releases), unzip it, right-click `install.ps1` and choose **Run with PowerShell**. A **Hand Poser** icon appears on the desktop; no administrator rights are needed. Or build it yourself: `build.bat` (only the C# compiler that ships with Windows) then `install.ps1`. The game needs [REFramework](https://github.com/praydog/REFramework) installed (the `dinput8.dll` in the game folder). ## Use 1. Start the game (RE2, RE3, or any other RE Engine game with REFramework; only RE2 and RE3 are the ones we run). 2. Double-click **Hand Poser**. The top line names the game it found; if it found none, press **GAME FOLDER...** and pick the game's install folder. 3. Press **PUT THE SCRIPT INTO THE GAME** once. It copies `hand_poser.lua` into the game's `reframework\autorun` folder. Restart the game, or open REFramework's menu (Insert) and press **Reset scripts**. The top line turns green: *re3 · pl2000 · connected*. 4. Load into the game so there is a character, then press **LEFT FINGERS** or **RIGHT FINGERS** (all the finger joints) or **LEFT HAND** / **RIGHT HAND** (the wrist). Or type into **any joint**, pick one from the list and press **ADD**. 5. Drag the sliders. X, Y and Z are the joint's local turning angles in degrees, −180 to 180; arrow keys nudge by half a degree, Page Up/Down by five. 6. Type a name next to **build name** and press **SAVE BUILD** to keep the pose; pick it under **saved builds** and press **LOAD** to get it back. The autosave needs no button. Builds and the autosave live in `%APPDATA%\HandPoserVR\\`, one folder per game. ## How it works - **The window** (`app\`, C#) writes `command.json` into the game's `reframework\data\hand_poser\` folder on every change: which joints to hold, at what angles, and which joints it wants to read. It reads `state.json` from the same folder: the game name, the character, the whole skeleton (every joint and its parent) and the live angles of the joints it asked about. The parent links are what lights up the children while you drag. - **The script** (`reframework\autorun\hand_poser.lua`) finds the player the way EMV Engine does (the game's `PlayerManager`, with RE4, RE7 and RE8 fallbacks), lists the joints of its transform, writes `state.json` about once a second, reads `command.json` every three frames, and writes each held joint's local Euler angle at `LateUpdateBehavior` and again at `PrepareRendering`, after the animation has run: the timing EMV's poser proved. Joints that are not held are never touched. Its own small section in REFramework's menu shows what it is holding and has a **Let go of everything** button. - A freshly added joint is only *read* until the game has reported its angle; then it is held at that angle, so adding a finger never makes it jump. ## Tested - `dist\HandPoser.exe --selftest `: 22 checks on the parts that need no game (skeleton reading, children, first angles from the game, holding, clamping, undo, redo, builds, autosave, the command file, a half-written state file). All pass (2026-10-16). - `test\fake_game.py ` pretends to be the script; `HandPoser.exe --game \FakeGame --demo` adds the left fingers and turns one. The fake game saw both commands, with the first angles taken from it (2026-10-16). - Not yet run in a real game. The joint names the quick-add buttons look for (`l_hand_index_0` ... `r_hand_thumb_2`, `l_arm_wrist`, `r_arm_wrist`) are the ones RE2's player skeleton uses; other RE games may differ, and then the list under **any joint** is the way in. ## Limits (for now) - Holding is absolute: the held joint stays at the slider's angle whatever the animation wants. Blending with the animation, warning when fingers overlap, and nudging them apart automatically are later steps. - Hands first: the quick-add buttons know the hands; everything else is added one joint at a time from the list. - RE Engine games only, through REFramework. The window itself knows nothing about the game and could talk to another engine's script with the same two files. ## Credits - **alphaZomega** — [EMV Engine](https://github.com/alphazolam/EMV-Engine), whose poser (freeze joints, pose by local Euler angles, undo, saved poses) this tool is modelled on. Nothing is co

# RETRO DEUTSCH A1 BREAKOUT

復古風德語 A1 單字打磚塊，Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript。

## 開發

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # 輸出到 dist/
npm run preview  # 預覽 build 結果
```

## 結構

- `public/vocab.json`：單字庫（de / zh / gender / category），分類為使用情境；`scripts/recategorize.py` 是分類對照表
- `src/game/engine.ts`：遊戲引擎（磚塊、球、球拍、懸賞、補磚、碰撞、繪圖），不依賴 Vue
- `src/game/constants.ts`：尺寸、分數、球速等參數
- `src/game/audio.ts`：8-bit 音效與德語發音
- `src/composables/useGame.ts`：把引擎接到 Vue（載字庫、鍵盤滑鼠、HUD 狀態）
- `src/components/`：Hud、HitBar、GameCanvas、Controls
- `legacy/`：改版前的單檔版本，僅供參考

## 規則

- 懸賞單字只會從每欄最下方（亮框）的磚塊中挑選
- 命中懸賞 +30，該磚塊消失並補上該主題尚未出現過的單字
- 連續命中有 COMBO：每多一連擊 +20 分（最多疊 5 級，單次 110 分），特效與德文鼓勵語隨連擊增強；打錯或漏接就中斷
- 球每次碰到磚塊都會唸出該單字
- 打錯（非懸賞）的磚塊只反彈、不消失、不計分；畫面停頓一秒並震動，中央顯示該字與字義
- 沒有生命與 Game Over：漏接只是連擊歸零、重新發球
- 彈道可預測：球拍分 5 區固定角度（-50°/-25°/0°/25°/50°）、發球直上或按住左右鍵斜 25°、沒有隨機；發球前有預測軌跡與目標框，球下落時有落點標記
- 新手模式：接到球會黏住、移好位置再按空白鍵發射；球拍加寬、靠近球拍時慢動作、漏接自動降速、命中慢慢恢復
- 單字全部用完且清空才 STAGE CLEAR

TefMeister/window-view-vr.desc: UNTESTED - see your desktop windows inside any OpenXR game (D3D11/D3D12) and use them with the mouse and keyboard while the game only hears the controllers. Built 2026-10-16, proven on the OpenXR Simulator only.
TefMeister/window-view-vr.readme: # Window View — see your desktop windows inside any OpenXR game, and use them with the mouse > ⚠️ **UNTESTED.** Built on 2026-10-16 and proven only on the OpenXR Simulator with a stand-in game, never yet in a real > headset or a real game. It may do nothing, show the window in the wrong place, or need a restart to let your mouse go. > Page Down always hands the mouse and keyboard back; closing the app does too. A small desktop app plus an OpenXR layer. Pick any open window (say Hand Freeze, or a browser), and it hangs in front of your eyes inside the game like an in-game menu, about a metre away, turning with your head. You can add as many windows as you like, make each one more or less see-through, drag it aside by its dark header and resize it by its corner, all with the mouse. A switch, **MOUSE & KEYBOARD**, decides who gets your mouse and keyboard: normally the game, as always; switched on, the windows in VR get them and the game sees nothing, so you play with the motion controllers or the gamepad while you click and type in the floating windows. **Page Up** switches it on, **Page Down** off, from anywhere, without the game hearing the key. Made for tuning our VR mods from inside the headset (2026-10-16): with Hand Freeze holding the controllers still, the sliders of the hand poser can now be moved without lifting the headset. ## Get it Download the zip from [Releases](https://github.com/TefMeister/window-view-vr/releases), unzip it, right-click `install.ps1` and choose **Run with PowerShell**. A **Window View** icon appears on the desktop; no administrator rights are needed. Or build it yourself: `build.bat` (Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools for the layer; the app uses the C# compiler that ships with Windows) then `install.ps1`. After an update, open the app once: it checks that the layer registration still matches the files beside it (the 32-bit copy too) and mends it (v1.1, 2026-10-16, as Hand Freeze v3.2; an old registration without the 32-bit copy stops 32-bit OpenXR games from starting). ## Use 1. Double-click **Window View** on the desktop and press **VR LAYER: OFF** so it says **ON**. Leave it on. 2. Start the game. The layer must be on **before** the game starts (OpenXR add-ons load at start); a game that was already running needs one restart. The bottom line says *Connected: .exe (D3D11)* once the game draws. 3. Pick a window in the **Open windows** list and press **ADD TO VR** (or double-click it). It appears in the headset, straight ahead. Each added window gets a row under **In VR** with a **See-through** slider, a **Size** slider, a **Show** box and **REMOVE**. 4. Press **Page Up** (or the big button). Now your mouse moves a small arrow across the floating windows and your keyboard types into the one you last clicked. The game gets neither. Drag a window by its dark header to move it, drag the three little lines in its bottom-right corner to resize it. 5. Press **Page Down** to give the mouse and keyboard back to the game and the desktop. Windows come back where you left them next time (matched by program and title), from `%APPDATA%\WindowViewVR\layout.txt`. ## How it works - **The layer** (`layer/window_view_layer.cpp`, an OpenXR API layer registered for this Windows user, 64-bit and a 32-bit copy) sits between the game and the OpenXR runtime. At every `xrEndFrame` it appends one **quad layer** per shown window after the game's own layers, in a head-locked (`VIEW`) space, 1 m in front, blended by alpha. The pixels come from the app through shared memory; the layer copies a window's picture into a swapchain of its own only when it changed. D3D11 (`UpdateSubresource`) and D3D12 (upload buffer + copy on the game's queue) games are supported; a Vulkan or OpenGL game shows nothing and the app says so. - **The app** (`app/*.cs`) does the rest: `Capture.cs` photographs each window about 30 times a second with `PrintWindow` (works when the game covers it), puts our header strip above the client area and bakes the opacity into the alpha; `Desk.cs` is the imaginary desk in metres with the cursor, the hit test and the layout file; `InputRouter.cs` holds two low-level hooks on their own thread: Page Up / Page Down are always swallowed, and while on, every mouse and keyboard event is swallowed too. The real cursor is parked at the middle of the screen, the hook reads how far the mouse *wanted* to move, and that becomes the desk cursor. Clicks, moves and the wheel are posted to the real control under the desk cursor as ordinary window messages; letters go as `WM_CHAR`, other keys as `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP`. The game keeps the Windows focus the whole time, so controllers and the gamepad keep working. Closing the app always hands the mouse and keyboard back. - `shared.h` is the hand-over: one 500-byte header (8 slots: where, how big, which pixel buffer is finished, plus the layer's heartbeat, the game's name and graphics API, counters) and one double-buffered BGRA pixel block per slot. ## Tested On the dev PC with the OpenXR Simulator, 2026-10-16, `[verified-numerically 2026-10-16, n=1 each]`: - `test/view_test.py` (a stand-in game, `test/xr_test_app.cpp`, and a stand-in app, `test/fake_window.py`): D3D11 and D3D12 both PASS: frames ended, the layer named the right API and exe, pictures uploaded, quads submitted, no error; a mid-run resize swapped to the new picture. Photos of the preview window show the test picture in both eyes. - `test/input_test.py` (Notepad in VR through the layout file, the app started with `--test-input`, the real stand-in game): Notepad captured and shown, the real cursor stayed parked while on, `hello` typed into Notepad through the desk, the window dragged right by its header, the mouse moving again after Page Down. All six PASS. - A game started with no app running keeps running and shows nothin
