# FANVERSE — Your Story. Your Universe.

> **"Don't just follow the story. Become part of it."**
>
> An AI-orchestrated 3D interactive K-POP story universe & 10-cut Naver Webtoon studio powered by **Gemini 4 Argon (`gemini-4-argon`)**, **Blender 3D / MCP**, **React Three Fiber**, and a **Deterministic World Verification & Self-Correction Loop**. Deployed on **Google Cloud Run**.
>
> 🌐 **Live Google Cloud Run Demo:** [https://fanverse-dj3pyhgn3q-du.a.run.app](https://fanverse-dj3pyhgn3q-du.a.run.app)
> 📦 **Public GitHub Repository:** [https://github.com/hyunaeee/google-hackaton-argon](https://github.com/hyunaeee/google-hackaton-argon)

---

## 1. Overview & Problem Statement

Global K-POP fans, K-drama viewers, and webtoon readers want to step inside their favorite fictional universes. Yet current formats trap users between **static branching menus** (no freedom) and **unbounded LLM chatbots** (which hallucinate, ignore object preconditions, and lack a physical 3D world).

**FANVERSE** solves this by combining:
1. **A 5-Act Interactive 3D K-POP Backstage World** (`backstage_room.glb` built with rigged Rocketbox characters, animated Blender shape keys, see-through wall occlusion, and 10 cinematic camera presets in React Three Fiber).
2. **Gemini 4 Argon Story Director (`gemini-4-argon`)** using the `@google/genai` Interactions API (`ai.interactions.create`) with strict JSON Schema output, adaptive `thinking_level` (`low` → `medium`), per-tab `x-session-id` session isolation, and `previous_interaction_id` chaining.
3. **A Deterministic Verification & 2-Step Self-Correction Loop** (`validateAction()`) with a one-click **`Test Rule Guard`** button that blocks illegal state mutations and feeds exact rule violations back to `gemini-4-argon` so characters respond in-world without corrupting canonical state.
4. **A Long-Decode 2K 10-Style Naver Webtoon Studio** (`thinking_level: 'medium'`, `max_output_tokens: 16384`) with **English / Korean (`🇺🇸 EN` / `🇰🇷 한국어`) episode language selection** (100% English default) that transforms the player's verified playthrough into a downloadable **2K (`2048px` wide) vertical-scroll comic strip** across **10 Korean Webtoon visual presets** and **8 distinct NanoBanana Pro (`gemini-3-pro-image-preview`) comic cuts**.

---

## 2. Playable Episode: *Episode 01 — Five Minutes Before Showtime*

- **Setting:** VIP Backstage Dressing Room at the comeback concert of **LUMINA** (fictional K-POP girl group).
- **The Crisis (`05:00` to `00:00 — ON AIR`):** Five minutes before opening cue, lead vocalist **Hana**’s custom pearl-lilac Starlight wireless microphone is locked away after an emergency battery check.
- **5-Act Interactive Investigation & Two Canon Endings:**
  - **Act 1 — Backstage Briefing & Clue Log:** Speak with **Hana** (`npc_hana`) and Stage Manager **Jiho** (`npc_jiho`), and inspect the battery inspection cue sheet on the **Coffee Table** (`coffee_table`).
  - **Act 2 — Vanity Search & VIP Access Card:** Inspect the **Hollywood Bulb Mirror** (`vanity_mirror`) and **Vanity Table** (`vanity_table`) to discover and collect the holographic **VIP Staff Access Card** (`access_card`).
  - **Act 3 — Locker Breach or Acoustic Pivot:** Scan the VIP Access Card on the **Equipment Locker** (`equipment_locker`) to unlock its door and recover the **Custom Starlight Microphone** (`microphone`), OR tune the **Acoustic Guitar** (`acoustic_guitar`) in the lounge corner.
  - **Act 4 — Wireless IEM Sync & Handoff:** Sync the 648.55 MHz in-ear monitor pack on the **Velvet Lounge Sofa** (`lounge_sofa`) and hand the microphone to **Hana** (or approve the unplugged arrangement with **Jiho**).
  - **Act 5 — Grand Finale (`stage_door`):**
    - **Ending A (`SHOWTIME_SAVED`):** Hana takes the stage with her recovered Starlight Microphone under magenta/cyan concert lasers.
    - **Ending B (`UNPLUGGED_ENCORE`):** LUMINA performs an intimate, golden-lit acoustic encore with the tuned backstage guitar.

---

## 3. Architecture: Gemini 4 Argon + Deterministic Verification & Correction Loop

```text
Player Input (3D Object Click, Voice Input, or Free-Form Text)
   │
   ▼
Gemini 4 Argon Story Director (`gemini-4-argon` via `@google/genai` Interactions API)
   │  • 1st Pass: `thinking_level: 'low'` for snappy interactive gameplay
   │  • Proposes structured JSON (`AIActionProposalSchema`):
   │    { actionType, targetId, proposedStateChanges, speaker, npcResponse, narration, requestedEnding }
   ▼
Deterministic World Validator (`validateAction()`)
   │  Enforces canonical preconditions & blocks side-channel mutations:
   │  • Cannot UNLOCK `equipment_locker` without `access_card` (`MISSING_ACCESS_CARD`)
   │  • Cannot PICK_UP `microphone` while `lockerUnlocked === false` (`MICROPHONE_INACCESSIBLE_LOCKER_LOCKED`)
   │  • Cannot HAND_OVER `microphone` without holding it (`MISSING_MICROPHONE_TO_HAND_OVER`)
   │  • Cannot ENTER_STAGE (`stage_door`) before resolving the crisis (`CRISIS_UNRESOLVED_CANNOT_ENTER_STAGE`)
   ├──► [VALID] ──► Commit State Changes ──► Trigger 3D Scene Animation, Audio SFX & Act Progression
   │
   └──► [INVALID] ──► Automatic Self-Correction Loop (Up to 2 Retries)
                       │  • Escalates `thinking_level: 'low' -> 'medium'`
                       │  • Chains `previous_interaction_id` for stateful multi-turn reasoning
                       │  • Feeds exact deterministic rejection codes back to `gemini-4-argon`
                       ▼
                     Grounded In-Character Explanation Returned (Authoritative WorldState Unchanged)
```

Judges can inspect every proposal, rule evaluation, `thinking_level` escalation, `previous_interaction_id` chain, and an interactive **5-Step Architecture & Pipeline Walkthrough** live in the right-hand **Verifier (Verification Inspector)** drawer.

---

## 4. Local Setup & Verification

### Prerequisites
- **Node.js** `>= 20.x`
- **Google Gemini API Key** with access to `gemini-4-argon`

### 1) Install Dependencies
```bash

qn5530/phoenix-infinity.desc: A calculator shooter that evolves: faithful 1-bit TI-83 Phoenix → neon → DoDonPachi-style bullet hell. Play in browser, mod it via mods.js.
qn5530/phoenix-infinity.readme:
# PHOENIX ∞

**A calculator shooter that evolves** — from a faithful 1‑bit, 96×64 recreation of the classic TI‑83/84 shoot‑'em‑up *Phoenix* to a full‑blown, DoDonPachi‑inspired Japanese bullet hell. The whole game lives on the screen of a calculator, and the calculator itself evolves with it.

**▶ Play in your browser:** https://qn5530.github.io/phoenix-infinity/ — works on desktop and in portrait on phones (or open `index.html` locally).

**🎬 Trailer:** [phoenix_trailer.mp4](https://github.com/qn5530/phoenix-infinity/releases/download/v1.0/phoenix_trailer.mp4) (9:16, 60 fps, real gameplay)

## The four eras

| Era | Calculator | Look | New mechanics |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | **PX‑83** | 96×64 monochrome LCD, pixel ghosting, 3×5 font | Phoenix classic: cash per kill, shop between levels, 5 weapons, shields, Mothership boss |
| II | **PX‑84 CE** | 192×128 colour LCD | Coins, homing missiles, bombs, *The Divider* (splits at 50%) |
| III | **PX‑9000** | Neon vector glow, synthwave grid | Grazing, telegraphed lasers, ∫ Railgun, *Overflow* (3 phases) |
| IV | **PX‑∞** | Full bullet hell + particles | Tap = shot / hold = laser, hit chain, **HYPER**, ÷0 singularity bomb, *∞ Infinity* with four spell cards |

A green calculator‑LCD filter stays on top of every era, so it always feels like it's running on a calculator.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Calculator key | Touch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move | Arrows / WASD | ▲▼◀▶ | Drag anywhere on the screen |
| Fire (tap = shot, hold = laser in era IV) | Z / Space | 2ND | Auto while dragging |
| Bomb | X | ALPHA | ALPHA |
| Hyper (era IV) | V | STAT | STAT |
| Switch weapon | C | MODE | MODE |
| Focus (slow + show hitbox) | Shift | X,T,θ,n | X,T,θ,n |
| Select / pause | Enter / P | ENTER / GRAPH | Tap screen |
| Back | Esc | CLEAR / DEL | CLEAR |
| Mute | M | ON | ON |

On the title screen press **1–9** to jump to any level.

## URL options

```
index.html?level=8      start at level 8
index.html?god=1        invincible
index.html?speed=1.5    game speed (0.25 – 4)
index.html?money=9999   starting cash
index.html?trailer=1    play the in-engine trailer
```

## Modding

Everything is plain data and functions — open **`mods.js`**, uncomment an example, reload. It loads after `game.js` and before the game boots.

- **`TUNE`** — speed, enemy/boss HP, player damage, bullet speed, cash, wave pacing, starting shields, god mode.
- **`WEAPONS`** — each weapon is `{ id, name, cost, era, d, fire(player, dmg, focus) → cooldown }`. Push your own.
- **`T`** — enemy types: HP, radius, score, cash, AI (`form` / `path` / `chase`), sprite bitmap (eras I–II) or vector shape (III–IV), `fire(e)` and `die(e)` patterns.
- **`LEVELS`** — `{ era, waves: [spawn functions], boss }`. Spawners: `grid`, `stream`, `zigs`, `vform`.
- **Bullet patterns** — `shot(x, y, angle, speed, opts)`, `aim(e, speed, n, spread)`, `ring(x, y, n, speed, offset)`, `laser(x, y, angle, opts)`.
- **`HOOKS`** — `tick`, `kill`, `levelStart` callbacks.
- **`SHOTS`** — the trailer's shot list (camera, captions, transitions), if you want to cut your own trailer.

Everything is also reachable as `window.PHOENIX` from the browser console.

## Recording the trailer

The trailer is real gameplay, simulated deterministically and captured frame by frame (1080×1920, 60 fps, 9:16), with the soundtrack rendered by the game's own synth.

```bash
npm install
node record.mjs        # needs ffmpeg on PATH and Google Chrome (set CHROME=/path/to/chrome if elsewhere)
```

## Credits

Inspired by **Phoenix** by Patrick Davidson for TI‑82/83/84/85/86 calculators, and by Cave's **DoDonPachi** series. This is an independent fan tribute; no code or assets from either were used. Not affiliated with Texas Instruments.

MIT licensed.

munisht06/four-walls.desc: Four Walls: a first-person housework simulator in the browser (three.js, CC0 assets)
munisht06/four-walls.readme:
# Four Walls

A first-person housework simulator in the browser, inspired by *Woman Simulator* (Steam). You play Nora, five days into a marriage with Graham, in a house with a small room you're never to open. It's built with three.js, has no build step, and uses only CC0 assets (see [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md)).

## Run

ES modules need a local server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8123
```

Then open http://localhost:8123.

## How it plays

- **5 days.** Each day runs 07:00–22:00 (about 5 minutes), then a short night while he sleeps.
- **Chores** each have a deadline, and each happens in visible steps. Progress is kept if you let go of E:
  - Dishes: wash 6 items one by one, from the dirty pile into the drying rack.
  - Bed: make it.
  - Mopping: clean 3 spills placed at random around the house.
  - Laundry: load the washer, wait about 25 seconds while it runs, then unload.
  - Ironing: the shirts wait in the basket by the board. Iron 4 into a stack.
  - Dinner: from 16:00, chop 3 vegetables, then cook them on the stove.
- **He checks on you** every so often, and always at 19:00 about dinner. Overdue chores hurt his mood and your morale. Each reply shows what it does: apologise, say nothing, or talk back.
- **Secret actions** (purple prompts) raise his suspicion fast if he can see you. At night he sleeps, but working right beside the bed can wake him.
- **Help on screen:** the "Next" objective, amber, purple and green markers, a minimap that shows where he is, a highlight on whatever you can use, one-time tips, and +/− numbers on the meters.

## Settings

Open **Settings** from the main menu or the pause screen (Esc).

- **Presets:** Low, Medium and High set resolution, shadows, film effects, glow, anti-aliasing, reflections, and dust and steam together. Changing any one of them shows "Custom".
- **Controls:** field of view, mouse sensitivity and a frame-rate counter.
- **First run:** computers with 4 or fewer CPU cores, or 4GB of memory or less, start on Medium.
- **Automatic:** if play stays below about 28fps for a few seconds, the game steps down one level and says so. You can turn this off.
- Settings are saved in the browser.

## Story

Each day opens with a chapter drawn from a classic: *A Doll's House*, *The Yellow Wallpaper*, *Bluebeard*, *Gas Light* and *Jane Eyre*. Graham swings from possessive warmth to cold control, and after a bad day he brings flowers. Across the street, Ruth Kessler watches from her porch and signals back when you look out of the living-room window. Clara, Graham's first wife, never moved away. If his mood hits zero, he locks you in the small room for a few hours.

## Endings (8)

| Ending | How |
|---|---|
| A New Life | Find all 3 savings stashes, the spare key and a packed bag, then leave by the front door |
| Into the Night | Leave with the key but without everything else |
| Standing Tall | Reach 75 resolve, confront him and win the timing fight (the pan helps) |
| Not This Time | Lose the fight |
| Caught | His suspicion hits 100 |
| Fading | Your morale hits 0 |
| Another Week | Survive all 5 days without leaving |
| The Small Room (hidden) | Take the brass key from his key bowl, find Clara's note in the small room, then (resolve 50+, day 2+) tell him there's something he needs to see in there. When he turns his back, bolt the door |

Resolve comes from talking back, writing in the journal (bedroom desk), and calling your sister (bathroom cabinet).

## Code

- `src/house.js`: room layout, walls with real window openings, furniture and chore props, the street outside, sun and room lighting
- `src/assets.js`: CC0 model and texture loading, with primitive fallbacks if a file fails
- `src/textures.js`: procedural textures (rug, tiles, soft shadows, the yellow wallpaper, tally marks)
- `src/post.js`: bloom, vignette, grain and the dread effect
- `src/audio.js`: Web Audio sound (footsteps, clock, TV, water, washer, heartbeat)
- `src/husband.js`: Graham (animated model, pathfinding, poses) and Ruth
- `src/story.js`: all dialogue, chores, tips and ending text
- `src/hud.js`: minimap, tips, toasts, meter popups, room banner
- `src/settings.js`: graphics presets and saved preferences
- `src/main.js`: game loop, player, chore steps, markers, AI behaviour, dialogue, fight, HUD

After changing anything in `src/` or `style.css`, run `python3 tools/stamp.py` before publishing. It stamps `index.html` with a content version, so players' browsers never mix cached old files with new ones. Locally, `python3 -m http.server` also caches modules, so use a hard reload (Cmd+Shift+R) while developing.

`window.__game` exposes state for console debugging.

mrgiangleai/dot-bien-game.desc: Game bắn súng 3D góc nhìn thứ ba trên trình duyệt – đấu bot, chế độ Zombie & Đấu đội
mrgiangleai/dot-bien-game.readme:
# Đột Biến – Bắn súng góc nhìn thứ ba (đấu bot)

Game bắn súng 3D chạy trên trình duyệt (Three.js), không cần build.

## Chạy
```bash
python3 -m http.server 8765
```
Mở http://localhost:8765 (điện thoại cùng Wi‑Fi: http://<IP-máy>:8765, xoay ngang).

## Chế độ
- **Zombie (Người vs Đột biến)**: 10s chuẩn bị, sau đó ngẫu nhiên vài người thành Đột biến mẹ.
  Đột biến cào người để lây nhiễm. Đột biến hết máu sẽ bị hạ gục và hồi sinh sau 7s —
  con người phải dùng **dao (phím 2)** để kết liễu. Người thắng nếu sống sót hết giờ.
- **Đấu đội**: Xanh vs Đỏ, hồi sinh sau 3s, đội đạt 30 điểm trước thắng.
  - Luật **Deadmatch** (chọn trong menu khi bấm Đấu đội): không hồi sinh, đội nào hạ hết đối thủ
    thắng vòng (+1 điểm), rồi tự sang vòng mới. Hết 3 phút thì đội còn nhiều người hơn thắng.

Số bot (1–19) và độ khó chỉnh ở menu, hoặc trong menu tạm dừng (⚙ / Esc) → "Áp dụng số bot & chơi lại".

## Điều khiển
- PC: WASD, chuột xoay, chuột trái bắn, chuột phải hoặc giữ Q để ngắm, Space nhảy, C nằm, R nạp,
  1/2/3/4 vũ khí (4 = súng ngắm, ngắm x4, 10 viên, bắn từng phát), G lựu đạn, Tab bảng người chơi,
  V đổi góc nhìn 1/3, Esc/P cài đặt.
- Điện thoại: joystick trái, vuốt màn hình phải để xoay (giữ nút BẮN vừa bắn vừa xoay được), NHẢY / NẠP / NGẮM / NẰM / CAM, ☰ bảng người chơi.
- Bản đồ có cầu thang dẫn lên 6 khối cao để nằm bắn tỉa.

## Cấu trúc (chuẩn bị cho chơi mạng)
| File | Vai trò |
|---|---|
| `src/config.js` | Toàn bộ thông số cân bằng |
| `src/world.js` | Bản đồ, va chạm AABB, raycast |
| `src/actor.js` | Nhân vật: vật lý + trạng thái, nhận **lệnh điều khiển** (`blankCmd`) mỗi tick |
| `src/combat.js` | Bắn, dao, cào, lựu đạn, sát thương, lây nhiễm |
| `src/bot.js` | AI bot – chỉ sinh ra lệnh điều khiển giống người chơi |
| `src/input.js` | Bàn phím/chuột/cảm ứng → lệnh điều khiển |
| `src/game.js` | Vòng tick cố định 60Hz, luật chế độ chơi, camera |
| `src/hud.js`, `effects.js`, `audio.js` | Giao diện, hiệu ứng, âm thanh |

Mọi nhân vật đều được điều khiển qua một `controller.sample(dt)` trả về lệnh.
Để chơi mạng: thêm server Node + WebSocket chạy cùng vòng tick (server‑authoritative),
client gửi lệnh từ `LocalInput`, và người chơi khác dùng một `RemoteController`
nhận lệnh/trạng thái từ server. Bot vẫn chạy trên server để lấp chỗ trống.

## Mở nhanh bằng icon (macOS)
Bấm đúp **`Đột Biến.app`** (trong thư mục dự án hoặc trên Desktop) → game mở trong cửa sổ riêng,
không cần Terminal. Đóng cửa sổ là server tự tắt. Sửa code xong chỉ cần mở lại app (hoặc Cmd+R).
Nếu di chuyển thư mục dự án, chạy lại `./tools/build-app.sh` để tạo lại app.

## Cập nhật lên GitHub Pages
Trước khi đẩy code, chạy `python3 tools/stamp_version.py` để gắn số phiên bản vào đường dẫn file,
tránh điện thoại/trình duyệt dùng code cũ trong bộ nhớ đệm (GitHub giữ cache ~10 phút).

davidpobezal-debug/ocean-restorer-remake.desc: Ocean Restorer – vyčisti oceán jedným palcom (Three.js remake)
davidpobezal-debug/ocean-restorer-remake.readme:
# Ocean Restorer · Remake

A one-thumb 3D mobile game (Three.js, no build step). Wash the dirt off the seabed, rescue animals from ghost nets and watch the reef bloom back to life.

## Run locally
```bash
python -m http.server 8742
```
Then open http://localhost:8742. For GitHub Pages, upload the whole folder.

## Controls
- **Drag anywhere:** the diver swims and vacuums the seabed.
- **Let go:** sonar pulse. Scares sharks, pushes jellyfish away, cleans around you and pulls in trash. On a computer use WASD or arrows; Space is the pulse.

## Expedition (main mode)
- **One endless dive**, the goal is the highest score.
- **Four big regions, one after another**, each in its own colour: Tropical Reef → Shipwreck → Kelp Forest → Glowing Deep. Clean 70 % of a region and the next one opens. You get full oxygen, +1 ❤️ and a 1,000 × region bonus.
- **The upgrade dock is always at the bottom:** Reach, Power, Fins, Robot / Pulse, Shield, Lure, +25 s O₂. Buy with coins from the dive in one tap; every dive starts from zero so the score chase is fair.
  - **Robot** is a little helper drone that hunts the nearest dirt.
  - **Shield** blocks one hit. **Lure** is a decoy the sharks chase instead of you.
- **The world gets dirty again:** trash sinks from the surface and leaking barrels spread oil until you vacuum them up.
- **Treasure chests** sit out on the dirty seabed: swim over one for +55 ◈.
- Sharks join as the dive goes on; every 20 m² cleaned gives +1 s of oxygen.
- A random rescued friend joins every dive (picking one will later be a rewarded-ad perk).
- The minimap shows what is left to clean, the friend in the net, oil leaks, sharks and O₂.
- A friend challenge is `?e=<seed>&s=<score>&n=<name>`, so your friend plays the same seabed. The Daily Dive is the same expedition for everyone.

## Open Sea (like the original map)
- **One big continuous seabed**: the four biomes are bands side by side. Clean 80 % of a band and the next one opens.
- **It never ends**: after the last band a new, dirtier sea is generated (new biome order). Score, coins, run upgrades, the robot and rescued friends carry over.
- Same dock, sharks, leaks and chests as the Expedition; its best score is kept separately.

## Levels
- Levels take 1 to 3 minutes. ★ at 60 %, ★★ at 85 % and ★★★ at 100 % of the reef restored. Oxygen is the timer and O₂ bubbles top it up.
- **Combo:** clean without a pause and the multiplier grows ×2 to ×4, then **FEVER ×5** with a huge reach and rainbow music.
- **Trash:** bottles, cans, bags, boots, crates, tires and barrels. Heavy pieces need a moment of holding.
- **Rescue:** an animal in a net (turtle, seal, octopus, dolphin, whale) swims with you after you free it and helps clean. It joins your collection too.
- **Clams with pearls** are hidden under the dirt. Pearls are the premium currency for suits and a second chance.
- From level 4 come **sharks**: a red lane warns before the dash, so you can dodge or pulse. From level 6 come **jellyfish**.
- Near the end an arrow points to the leftover dirt, so 100 % is always reachable.

## Viral bits
- A **BEFORE / AFTER** share image (1080 × 1350) with score, stars, rescued animals and the game address.
- **Challenge links** `?l=7&s=12345&n=Name`: your friend sees "Name challenges you"; the winner gets +50 ◈.
- **Daily Dive:** the same reef for everyone that day, shared as a Wordle-style emoji grid.
- **Share & keep going:** after a loss, sharing gives a second chance. The first share of the day gives +50 ◈.
- Day streak 🔥 and a first-dive-of-the-day bonus.
- PWA: add it to your home screen, it works offline. Links in Messenger and WhatsApp have a preview (`og:image`).

## Look
Models follow the original game: chunky boxes, gems and faceted shapes with flat colours, crisp edges and smoothing (MSAA). The diver swims flat, buddies wear a thin gold ring and a small gold gem, and pickups (O₂, pearls, treasure) glow.
- `demo/models.html`: every model in a numbered lineup plus a small reef scene (`?look=lowpoly` shows the alternative low-poly look).
- `demo/compare.html`: both looks side by side. `demo/robot.html`: robot helper candidates.

## Files
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `js/main.js` | renderer, camera, screens, HUD, minimap, sharing |
| `js/game.js` | gameplay (movement, combo, trash, chests, rescue, sharks, jellyfish, robot, lure) |
| `js/world.js` | regions, the seabed shader with the dirt mask, corals |
| `js/boxy.js` | the game's models in the original style |
| `js/models.js` | shared materials, net, shadows and the older low-poly models |
| `js/lowpoly.js` | the alternative low-poly look (demo only) |
| `js/fx.js` | particles, shockwaves, floating numbers and coins |
| `js/audio.js` | procedural sounds and generative music |
| `js/save.js` | progress in localStorage, upgrades, suits, animals |
| `js/share.js` | share image, challenge links, daily text |
| `TRIPO.md` | prompts for Tripo 3D models |

## Possible next steps
- A global leaderboard and a "together we cleaned X m²" counter, e.g. with Supabase (free tier).
- Rewarded ads: pick your dive buddy, second chance.

skljoc/scamboy-arcade.readme:
# SCAMBOY Arcade

*Cheat the game. Own the score.*

A browser-based retro handheld built with **Next.js + TypeScript + Phaser 3**. The SCAMBOY console is drawn
entirely as layered SVG vectors, every button works with mouse, touch and keyboard, and three original games run
inside its 320×288 LCD:

| # | Game | What it is |
|---|------|------------|
| 01 | **Street Rampage** | Belt-scrolling beat-'em-up with a ridiculously muscular SCAMBOY. 3 stages, miniboss, Big Boss. |
| 02 | **Dirty Racing** | Top-down arcade racer vs 3 AI rivals. Win by finding visible and hidden shortcuts. 3 unlockable tracks. |
| 03 | **Shell Game** | Follow the stone under three cups through 10 levels. Fair, exactly-tracked shuffles. Points only. |

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
npm run build   # production build (Vercel-ready)
```

## Online leaderboard (Neon Postgres)

Every finished run is uploaded to a world leaderboard (`/api/scores`) when a database is configured. Each
browser gets an anonymous player id, so a player's scores stay linked to them; the world board shows every
player's best run, with your own entry highlighted. Without a database the console keeps scores locally and
the WORLD view simply shows "offline".

**On Vercel:** import the repo, then add **Neon** from the project's *Storage* tab (Marketplace). It sets
`DATABASE_URL` for you; the `scores` table is created automatically on the first request.

**Locally:** copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, set `DATABASE_URL` to any Postgres (a Neon branch or e.g.
`docker run -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw postgres`), then optionally create the table up front:

```bash
npm run db:setup
```

Scores are validated server-side (known game, 1–8 character name, integer score within a per-game maximum,
one submission per player every 3 s). Since scores come from the browser, treat the board as a fun arcade
board rather than a tamper-proof one.

## Controls

| Console | Keyboard |
|---|---|
| D-pad | Arrow keys / WASD |
| A | J / Z |
| B | K / X |
| START | Enter (pause) |
| SELECT | Escape (quit to menu) |

The on-screen buttons support mouse and multi-touch; optional haptics vibrate on supported phones.

## Architecture

```
src/
  app/                    Next.js app router (layout, page, global styles)
  components/             React console UI
    ScamboyConsole.tsx    the SVG handheld (body, bezel, logo, speaker, power switch)
    ConsoleButtons.tsx    D-pad, A/B, START/SELECT — independently interactive SVG groups
    ConsoleScreen.tsx     the LCD: Phaser canvas + OS layer + LCD grid / CRT effects
    BootSequence.tsx      power-on animation
    GameMenu.tsx, GameInfo.tsx, PauseMenu.tsx, NameEntry.tsx,
    ScoresScreen.tsx, TrophiesScreen.tsx, OptionsScreen.tsx   console "OS" screens
    GameDetails.tsx, Scoreboard.tsx, SettingsPanel.tsx         side panels
  games/
    engine/               shared: InputManager, AudioManager (synth chiptune), GameManager (single Phaser
                          instance), BaseScene, pixel-art toolkit, palette, SCAMBOY sprites, bridge to the OS
    street-rampage/       game 01
    dirty-racing/         game 02
    shell-game/           game 03
  server/                 Postgres pool + score queries for the online leaderboard
  app/api/scores/         GET world board / POST a finished run
  store/                  Zustand stores (console state, persisted progress & settings)
  lib/                    game metadata, achievements
```

* React owns the application UI; Phaser owns game rendering. Exactly one `Phaser.Game` exists at a time and is
  destroyed when leaving a game.
* All game art is generated at runtime as pixel art (`games/engine/pixel.ts`) and registered as Phaser textures /
  sprite sheets, so assets can later be swapped for PNG sheets with the same keys.
* All audio is synthesized with the Web Audio API — no audio files. Sound starts after the first user interaction
  (browser autoplay rules).
* Progress, high scores, achievements, unlocked tracks and settings are stored in `localStorage`.

etothesmith/city-squirrel.readme:
# City Squirrel: East End

A noir 2.5D beat-'em-up that runs in the browser. One squirrel with a grappling hook takes on the East End Syndicate across ten districts.

**▶ Play:** https://etothesmith.github.io/city-squirrel/

![City Squirrel: East End](assets/og.jpg)

## Features
- Belt-scroller brawling with four-layer parallax and arena lock-ins that open into 3D rooms
- Combos, counters, disarms, weapon throws and finishers
- Grappling hook: yank thugs, zip to heavies, pull crates, ride car roofs
- Rooftop detours in every level: swing across gaps, chain swings mid-air, knock thugs off the ledge (girders and catwalks on the indoor levels)
- Flying Squirrel power-up: glide, ride vents, dive-bomb
- Ten districts and ten bosses, a Street Cred rank system and an Acorn Stash for upgrades
- Keyboard, gamepad and touch controls; progress saves in your browser

## Controls
| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Move | WASD / arrow keys |
| Jump / glide | Space |
| Attack | J or Z |
| Heavy / counter | K or X |
| Grapple | L or C |
| Dodge | Shift or V |
| Pick up / throw | E / Q |
| Bio-Surge special | F or B |
| Pause / mute | Esc / M |

## Files
- `index.html`: landing page
- `play.html`: the whole game in one self-contained file (art and audio embedded)
- `assets/`: images for the landing page

All characters, art and story are original.

johnrstanley11-gif/word-tycoon-ecosystem.desc: Open-source word games for live streams: Chat Relay hub, Word Tycoon economy, and every game server (Searchle, RecTangled, Word500, Wordle, ...). MIT.
johnrstanley11-gif/word-tycoon-ecosystem.readme:
# Word Tycoon Ecosystem

The full source of [Word Tycoon](https://wordtycoon.live/): a set of word games built for live streams, where TikTok, YouTube and Discord chat play together. It includes a shared economy (coins, cosmetics, businesses) and a central chat hub.

Free and open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

## How it fits together

```
 TikTok / YouTube / Discord chat
              │
        ┌─────▼──────┐        ┌──────────────┐
        │ chat-relay │◄──────►│ word-tycoon  │  accounts, coins, cosmetics,
        │  :3000     │        │  :3020       │  reward/deduct API
        └─────┬──────┘        └──────▲───────┘
   Socket.IO  │  proxies every game page   │ GAME_API_SECRET
     ┌────────┼─────────┬──────────┬───────┘
  searchle  wordle  rectangled  word500 … (each game is its own Node server)
```

- **chat-relay** is the hub. It takes in chat from each platform, normalizes it, proxies all the game pages and owns the shared word bank (`/api/word-bank/*`). Start it first.
- **word-tycoon** is the economy service: accounts, coins, cosmetics and businesses. The games call it to give out rewards.
- **Games** each connect to chat-relay over Socket.IO and serve their own pages. Once the two core services are up, they can start in any order.

| Folder | Game | Default port |
|---|---|---|
| `chat-relay` | Hub, portal, overlays | 3000 |
| `word-tycoon` | Economy API and app | 3020 |
| `searchle` | Searchle (semantic guessing) | 3015 |
| `wikisearchle` | WikiSearchle | 3029 |
| `rectangled` | RecTangled (word grid) | 3016 |
| `erectangled` | eRecTangled / Sproutle | 3023 |
| `wikirectangled` | WikiRecTangled | 3031 |
| `word500` | Word500 | 3006 |
| `word1000` | Word1000 | 3018 |
| `wordle` | Wordle multiplayer | 3003 |
| `unwordle` | UnWordle | 3021 |
| `pixeletters` | PixeLetters | see `server.js` |
| `spellingbee` | SpellingBee | 3013 |
| `figural` | Figural | 3019 |
| `betwixt` | Betwixt | 3017 |
| `triangled` | Triangled | 3024 |
| `wordmine` | WordMine | see `server.js` |
| `colour500` | Colour500 | 3033 |

## Running it locally

Requirements: Node.js 20 or newer.

```bash
# 1. core services
cd chat-relay && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npm start
cd word-tycoon && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npm start

# 2. any game
cd wordle && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npm start

# searchle needs a client build first
cd searchle && npm install && npm run build && npm start
```

Each folder's `.env.example` lists every environment variable that service reads. Most can be left empty. The important ones:

- `GAME_API_SECRET` must be the **same value** in word-tycoon, chat-relay and every game. Generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`.
- `SESSION_SECRET` (chat-relay) and `LOOT_SECRET` (word-tycoon) should be set to stable random values. Otherwise a random one is generated on each start, which logs everyone out and changes daily loot rolls.
- Platform credentials (Discord, Spotify, TikTok, Google/GitHub OAuth, Stripe) are only needed for the features that use them.

Daily puzzles roll over on `America/Edmonton` time. Domain names such as `wordtycoon.live` are hardcoded in a few places; search and replace them for your own deployment.

## What's not included

- Player data, databases, live game state and backups
- Production secrets and deployment/infra configuration
- Android signing keys and store assets

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Word lists and Wikipedia-derived data keep their original sources' terms (Wikipedia content is CC BY-SA).

nweinberg97/Curious-Minds.readme:
# Curious Minds

A local-first arcade of quick brain games. Seven games in three families, playable from one link, with no account, no backend and no tracking.

> Have fun. Get sharper. Learn something new. Play again.

| Family | Game | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| Wordplay | **Word Rush** | Chain word associations against the clock |
| | **Alphabet Sprint** | One letter, three categories, as many answers as you can |
| | **Word Scramble** | Unscramble eight words that adapt to your pace |
| | **Define It** | Explain a word in your own words, then compare |
| World | **Flag Finder** | Name the country behind ten flags |
| | **Capital Quest** | Name the capitals of ten countries |
| Connections | **Word Web** | Find four hidden groups of four among sixteen words |

The home page is an arcade machine: press its buttons (or "Taste" on any game card) to try a 20-second taster of every game, hop to the next one, and jump into the full game when you like it. A games menu in every game, Esc, and a return to exactly where you were on the home page make it easy to go in and out. Every finished round earns tokens towards an arcade rank, and the workshop shows the next three games being built.

Every round ends with something to learn (definitions, flag stories, capital facts, why groups connect), and misses come back later through a light spaced-review queue. Every game is free and unlimited, with a relaxed or untimed mode.

Product thinking, naming and design direction: [docs/PRODUCT.md](docs/PRODUCT.md).

## Run it

Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.1 or newer.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # http://localhost:5173, rebuilds on save
bun test           # unit and content tests
bun run build      # static site in dist/
```

`bun run check` runs the type checker, the tests and a production build.

## Deploy

`dist/` is a static site. Upload it to any static host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, S3). It must be served over HTTPS for offline mode. All paths are relative, so it works from a sub-path such as `https://you.github.io/curious-minds/`.

A GitHub Actions workflow in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds, tests and publishes to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`. Enable it under **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**.

`bun run build:artifact` produces `dist-artifact/`, a single page (plus `flags/`) for hosting inside a Claude artifact. There, service workers aren't available, so the app explains that offline play needs the self-hosted version, and exports go through the viewer's download prompt.

## Architecture

```
src/
  engine/        shared framework: types, normalisation, scoring, timers, review schedule, sound, randomness
  storage/       IndexedDB backend, in-memory fallback, PlayerStore, export/import schema
  content/       typed content banks (+ countries.generated.ts from scripts/build-geo.ts)
  games/         one folder per game: pure logic (logic.ts / graph.ts / evaluate.ts) + a React component
  games/registry.ts   the catalogue: add a game here and it appears everywhere
  ui/            App shell, Home, GameScreen (intro → play → summary), Progress, Settings
  styles/app.css design tokens and all styles
  sw.template.js service worker template
scripts/         build, dev server, geography data generator
tests/           bun unit tests + an optional Playwright browser playthrough (tests/e2e)
```

**Game framework.** A game is a `GameDef` (metadata, how-to, modes, difficulties) plus a component that receives `PlayProps` (`config`, `store`, `paused`, `onScore`, `onFinish`). The shared `GameScreen` owns the intro card, mode and difficulty choice, pausing (on tab switch, blur or Esc), score display, persistence and the round summary. A game reports a `RoundResult`: score, stats, learning cards and review updates. Shared utilities cover timers (`useCountdown`, pausable), scoring (`speedBonus`, chain and streak multipliers), answer matching (`AnswerIndex`: accents, plurals, typos), fresh-question selection (`pickFresh`), and the review schedule.

**Adding a game:** write `src/games/<name>/<Name>.tsx` implementing `PlayProps`, add art in `src/ui/art.tsx`, register it in `registry.ts`. Home, routing (`#<id>`, `#play.<id>`, `#review.<id>`), records, progress and export pick it up automatically.

**State.** `PlayerStore` keeps the player's data in memory and writes through to IndexedDB. React reads it with `useSyncExternalStore`. If IndexedDB is blocked, a memory backend keeps the app playable and the UI says progress won't survive the tab.

## Data: schema and migrations

IndexedDB database `curious-minds`, version 1 (`src/storage/schema.ts`, `src/storage/db.ts`):

| Store | Key | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions` | `id` | One finished round: game, mode, difficulty, score, correct/attempted, duration, optional stats and region breakdown. Capped at 3,000. |
| `items` | `key` (`flag:fr`, `capital:fr`, `vocab:laconic`, `scramble:quixotic`) | Review state: Leitner box, due time, seen/correct/wrong counts, bookmark |
| `records` | `gameId:mode` | Best score, when it was set, plays |
| `meta` | `settings`, `profile` | Settings (sound, motion, relaxed default, per-game choices); profile (days played, recent games, recently served content ids) |

**Migrations.** Bump `DB_VERSION` and add an `if (oldVersion < N)` block to `migrate()` in `db.ts`. Never edit earlier blocks. Rows are validated on load; malformed rows are skipped and counted rather than crashing the app.

**Export/import.** Settings → Your data exports `curious-minds-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (`{ app, schema, exportedAt, data }`). Import validates the file, skips damaged rows, previews what it contains, then **merges** (keeps both devices' rounds, the better best per game, the most recent review state per item) or **replaces**. Files from a newer schema are refused with a clear message.

## Content

All content is typed data in `src/content/`, validated by `tests/content.test.ts`.

| Bank | File | Size |
|---|-

TylusKinas/QRG.readme:
# QRG – QR Game Engine **A whole game inside one QR code.** Scan it with any phone camera and it opens in the browser as a retro console game. No app, no account, no server-side storage: the game *is* the QR code. ``` https://your.host/path/# ← the text inside the QR code ``` The page at that address is one self-contained file, `index.php`. It reads the game from the URL fragment (which never leaves the device), decompresses it and runs it on a 256 × 240 pixel console with an on-screen pad, touch gestures and keyboard. * **Any game** – the engine has no genres or templates, only drawing, sound, input, storage and a small standard library. Tetris, a racing game, a turn-based strategy game and a pocket pet that lives in real time are all just programs ([`games/`](games/)). * **Tiny** – a custom compressor tuned for game code. Typical games are QR version 10–17; the two big demos (a tactics game and a pet) are about v30. Limit: about 2.9 KB of compressed code. Sizes: [docs/GAMES.md](docs/GAMES.md). * **Two ways to make games** – a code editor (live preview, suggestions, tap a sprite / color / sound in the code to edit it graphically) and a **visual editor** where you draw sprites, place them with Select / Place / Delete tools and describe behavior with WHEN / IF / DO rules; the program is written for you. * **Memory per game** – `save()` / `load()` keep data on the device, private to that one game, so a game can go on while it is closed (the pet needs feeding twice a day). * **A forever player** – the Reader scans any QRG code, whatever the link around it looks like. * **Safe to open** – every game runs in a sandboxed iframe with no network and no access to the page. See [Security](#security). * **PWA** – installable; after the first visit it opens instantly from the device (cache first) and updates itself in the background. MIT licensed. ## Gallery Real recordings of the demo games running on the engine (scripted player, 256 × 240, 16 colors). Each one is a single QR code. | | | | |---|---|---| |
**Tetris** |
**Racing** |
**Breakout** | |
**Snake** |
**Flappy** |
**Invaders** | |
**Tiny Pet** – a pet that lives in real time (hours sped up here) | | | Regenerate them with `npm run gifs`. ## Two files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `index.php` | **The player.** One small file (~48 KB, everything inline). Opens a game from the URL, or shows a short intro. The only PHP: it shows a link to `e.html` when that file exists next to it. | | `e.html` | **The extras.** Library of demo games, code editor, visual editor, reader (QR scanner). Optional: if you do not upload it, the player works alone. | Plus the PWA files `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`, `icon-*.png` (a service worker and a manifest cannot be inlined) and `vendor/jsQR.js` (a QR scanner for browsers that lack `BarcodeDetector`; only loaded when needed, Apache-2.0). ## Quick start 1. Run `npm install && npm run build`, then upload the **contents of `dist/`** to your server (HTTPS; PHP only for `index.php`). 2. Set `BASE` in [`src/app/config.js`](src/app/config.js) to the URL where you host it (it must end with `#`) *before* building, so the QR codes point to your server. 3. Open it, tap a demo (e.g. *Tetris*): a QR code appears. Scan it with another phone: the game opens. 4. Open `e.html` for the editors and the reader. Without PHP (static hosting) rename `index.php` to `index.html` and delete the three PHP lines; the link to the extras is then always shown. Opening the files straight from disk works for playing and editing; the camera needs HTTPS. ## Writing a game A game is the body of a JavaScript function that returns a per-frame function. The code editor starts with a small, fully commented example, and every demo game opens with explanatory comments (comments cost nothing in the QR code: they are removed before a game is packed). ```js let x = 120, y = 110, score = 0; return i => { // called 60 times per second cls(NAVY); if (i.l) x -= 2; // d-pad / arrow key / swipe left if (i.t) { x = i.x - 8; y = i.y - 8; } // finger on the screen if (i.A) { score++; s(600); } // A button / tap r(x, y, 16, 16, ORANGE); t('SCORE ' + score, 4, 4, WHITE); }; ``` The standard library has drawing, text, sprites, input helpers, random numbers, moving objects ("actors"), grids and path finding, sound and per-game memory. Everything is documented in **[docs/LANGUAGE.md](docs/LANGUAGE.md)** (also inside the app); the visual editor in **[docs/VISUAL.md](docs/VISUAL.md)**. ## How it fits in a QR code 1. **Minify** – comments and spaces removed by a scanner that understands strings, templates and regular expressions (`src/codec/minify.js`; tests prove the program still does exactly the same). 2. **Compress** – a context-mixing compressor (`src/codec/cm.js`, integer math only so every browser decodes identically), primed with a dictionary of typical code (`src/codec/prime.js`). The dictionary is **not** built from the demo games, so the sizes in [docs/GAMES.md](docs/GAMES.md) are what a brand-new game costs. 3. **Encode** – bytes → base-43 (`0-9 A-Z $ * + - . / :`: URL-safe and inside the QR alphanumeric set, 5.5 bits per character). 4. **QR** – `https://host/path/#` as a byte segment plus the payload as an alphanumeric segment, error correction level L (`src/qr/qr.js`, versions 1–40, verified against an independent decoder for every size class). ## Repository layout ``` dist/ what you upload (generated by `npm run build`) index.php e.html manifest.webmanifest sw

# Protect **A co-op tower defense you play with friends, on your phone, in one sitting.** Two rifts open on a floating island. Monsters pour out of both and wind their way toward a single castle. You and up to three friends share the same battlefield, the same castle and the same twelve build sites — and you either hold it together or lose it together. ▶ **Play now:** https://protect.huseyinglc0-946.workers.dev — nothing to install, works in the browser, best on a phone held sideways. ![Wave 13 under a Dark Sky: harpies and bats pour over a fully built defence](docs/hero.jpg) --- ## How a match works 1. **Make a room.** One tap creates a room with a five-letter code. 2. **Bring your friends in.** Anyone who has the game open shows up in the **Online** list. Tap **Invite** next to their name and they get a *Join* button on their screen — no code to type. (Sharing the code or the link still works if you prefer.) 3. **Get ready, call the wave.** You have 30 seconds to place your first towers. When everyone taps *Call the wave*, the next wave starts early and every second you skipped is paid out to the whole team as bonus gold. 4. **Survive 30 waves.** Each wave is bigger and tougher than the last. Beat wave 30 and the team wins — then keep going for as long as the castle stands, if you dare.

## Everyone defends, everyone pays their own way - The castle is shared. If a monster reaches the gate, it hurts all of you. - Gold is **not** shared. You earn it from your own kills plus a payout at the end of every wave. - The twelve build sites are split evenly: six each for two players, four each for three, three each for four. - You repair and sell only your own towers, but **anyone can pay to upgrade anyone's tower** — a rich teammate can boost the tower standing in the right spot. ## Six towers, ten levels, two paths Tap a glowing hex ring to open the build menu right on the spot. Tap a tower once to see its range, tap again to build.

| Tower | Role | | --- | --- | | **Arrow** | Cheap, fast, hits ground and air. The backbone. | | **Cannon** | Slow shells that splash a whole group. Ground only. | | **Frost** | Chills everything it hits so the rest of your towers get more shots in. | | **Flame** | Short range, very fast, sets monsters on fire — the burn keeps ticking after they leave. | | **Tesla** | Lightning that chains from monster to monster. | | **Sniper** | Huge single hits from very far away; always picks the toughest target. | Every tower upgrades through **ten levels**. Each level adds damage, range and fire rate, and the tower's signature — splash radius, slow strength, chain length, burn — grows with it. At level 10 a tower chooses one of two **specialisations**. The choice is permanent and changes what the tower *is*: | Tower | Path A | Path B | | --- | --- | --- | | Arrow | **Volley** — three arrows per shot, three targets | **Razor Tip** — 30% chance of a 2.5× critical hit | | Cannon | **Shockwave** — everyone in the blast is pinned for half a second | **Heavy Shell** — 1.7× damage and no falloff across the blast | | Frost | **Polar Storm** — the ice shatters and chills everyone nearby | **Absolute Zero** — chance to freeze solid; chilled targets take 1.8× damage | | Tesla | **Overload** — three more chain jumps that barely lose power | **Paralysis** — every monster in the chain stops dead for a moment | | Flame | **Inferno** — double burn, longer burn, and burning monsters that die ignite their neighbours | **Napalm** — wider cone, longer reach, 1.4× damage | | Sniper | **Execute** — 3× damage against anything below 35% health | **Piercing Round** — the shot goes straight through every monster on the line | After specialising, towers keep growing through **Mastery** ranks — a small, repeatable boost that always gives spare gold somewhere to go. ## Castle upgrades: the team's shared wallet Tap the castle in the corner. Four upgrades, three tiers each; whoever pays, everyone benefits. ![The castle sheet: Walls, Vault, Battlement Archers and Smiths with their tiers and prices](docs/castle.jpg) - **Walls** — the castle can take more hits (and heals when you build them). - **Vault** — every wave pays out more to everyone. - **Battlement Archers** — the castle itself shoots whatever gets close to the gate. - **Smiths** — towers repair themselves, and at the top tier wrecked towers stand back up on their own. Monsters walking past a tower chew on it. A wrecked tower stops firing until its owner repairs it, so keep an eye on the little health bars. ## The monsters | | Name | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | 👹 | **Ghoul** | The common foot soldier. | | 🐕 | **Runner** | Fast and fragile, comes in bursts. | | 🗿 | **Giant** | Slow, heavy, hits the castle hard. | | 🦇 | **Harpy** | Flies straight over the roads. Cannons can't touch it. | | 🧙 | **Shaman** | Walks behind the pack and heals everyone around it. Kill it first. | | 🛡️ | **Armored** | Shrugs off a fixed chunk of every hit — rapid weak shots barely scratch it, cannons and snipers do. | | 🦇 | **Bat swarm** | Tiny, quick, airborne, and there are a lot of them. | | 👑 | **Ancient Beast** | The ground boss. Every fifth wave. | | 🪽 | **Harpy Queen** | The flying boss, every tenth wave, and she brings her swarm. Without anti-air you will not stop her. |

Momonimome/xl-chess.desc: Chess game and engine in plain JavaScript: alpha-beta search in a Web Worker, verified against python-chess and perft.
Momonimome/xl-chess.readme: # XL Chess [![CI](https://github.com/Momonimome/xl-chess/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Momonimome/xl-chess/actions/workflows/ci.yml) A chess game and engine in plain JavaScript modules, with no bundler and no runtime dependencies. It has 0x88 move generation, an alpha-beta search running in a Web Worker, and a board set like a diagram from a pre-war chess manual. **Play it:** ![XL Chess at 1280px](docs/screenshot.png) ## Features - **Full rules:** castling, including rights lost when a rook is captured at home and no castling out of, through or into check; en passant, including the rank pin; underpromotion; checkmate, stalemate, threefold repetition (Zobrist hash, with the en-passant square counted only when the capture is legal), the fifty-move rule and insufficient material. - **Notation:** FEN in and out (round-trips exactly), SAN with correct disambiguation, and PGN import and export that survives comments, nested variations and NAGs. - **Engine:** negamax with alpha-beta, principal variation search, iterative deepening, a transposition table, MVV-LVA, killer and history ordering, null-move pruning and quiescence. It is deterministic and never plays a random move. - **Playing:** against the engine as either colour, two players, or engine against engine (autoplay) with adjustable depth and delay. Also: flip the board, undo, new game, a clickable SAN move list, an auto-queen toggle (off brings up a promotion picker), and highlighting for the last move, legal moves and check. - **Input and accessibility:** drag, click-to-move and full keyboard play, screen-reader move announcements, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and a layout that works at 360px wide. ## Run it ```sh npm install npm start # http://localhost:8080/ ``` No build step: any static file server pointed at the repository root works. ## Test and verify | Script | What it runs | | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `npm run lint` | ESLint (zero warnings allowed) and Prettier | | `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --checkJs --strict --noEmit` over JSDoc types | | `npm test` | 105 unit tests, one per rule, each from a minimal FEN (`node:test`) | | `npm run verify` | perft, python-chess difftest, mate-distance oracle, master PGN corpus | | `npm run e2e` | 17 Playwright tests: scripted game, engine, axe, layout | | `npm run lighthouse` | Lighthouse scores (needs `CHROME_PATH`) | | `npm run bench` | perft and search nodes per second | `verify` and the difftest need Python with python-chess: `pip install -r test/verify/requirements.txt`. To run the browser tests against an installed Chrome instead of Playwright's bundled Chromium, set `PW_CHANNEL=chrome`; `UPDATE_SCREENSHOTS=1` also refreshes the images in `docs/`. CI runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, perft to depth 4 and the 50,000-position difftest on every push, plus the browser tests. ## Verification results Every check compares against an external source. These are raw harness numbers from `node test/verify/*.js` on the development machine. ### Perft (Chess Programming Wiki, retrieved 2026-10-16) `--check-source` re-fetched the wiki and found every FEN and count below on the page. | Position | Depth | Expected | Actual | Result | | --------------------- | ----: | ----------: | ----------: | :----: | | Initial position | 5 | 4,865,609 | 4,865,609 | pass | | Initial position | 6 | 119,060,324 | 119,060,324 | pass | | Position 2 (Kiwipete) | 5 | 193,690,690 | 193,690,690 | pass | | Position 3 | 5 | 674,624 | 674,624 | pass | | Position 3 | 6 | 11,030,083 | 11,030,083 | pass | | Position 4 | 5 | 15,833,292 | 15,833,292 | pass | | Position 4 (mirrored) | 5 | 15,833,292 | 15,833,292 | pass | | Position 5 | 5 | 89,941,194 | 89,941,194 | pass | | Position 6 | 5 | 164,075,551 | 164,075,551 | pass | All 37 depth/position pairs (depths 1 and up) match: 626,461,214 nodes in total. ### Differential test against python-chess 1.11.2 ``` generated 166 games, 50389 positions in 10.4 s (seed 1) zobrist audit: 50223 moves checked, 0 mismatches oracle: python-chess 1.11.2 oracle: 166 games, 50389 positions, 1130919 legal moves (each with SAN) compared oracle: positions where each flag held: check 3002, mate 24, stalemate 10, insufficient 76, threefold 6, fifty 451 oracle: 0 disagreements ``` At every position the test compares FEN, the legal move set, the SAN of every legal move, check, checkmate, stalemate, insufficient material, threefold repetition and the fifty-move rule. ### Mate distance against a brute-force solver The solver shares only move generation with the search. The search must report the solver's exact distance, or no mate within 5 plies when the solver proves there is none. ``` oracle sampled 23872 positions from 259 games in 309.2 s class (plies) samples search-agrees mismatches mate in 1 40 40 0 mated in 2 40 40 0 mate in 3 40 40 0 mated in 4 40 40 0 mate in 5 40 40 0 none <= 5 40 40 0 mate oracle: search matches every sampled mate distance ``` ### Master games (pgnmentor.com collections) ``` Capablanca.pgn: 597 games, 46577 plies replayed in 2.3 s, 0 failures oracle: 597 games, final positions compared, 0 disagreements Carlsen.pgn: 7

raposocampos/radhija-rhaenyra.readme:
# Radhija & Rhaenyra

Aventura 3D curta e aconchegante com duas cachorrinhas de verdade, a Radhija (pequena, ágil, creme-dourada)
e a Rhaenyra (maior, forte, branca). Feita em Three.js + Vite, com tudo gerado em código: modelos, texturas e sons.

## Como jogar

**[Jogar no navegador](https://raposocampos.github.io/radhija-rhaenyra/)** — sem instalar nada.

Para desenvolver localmente:

```bash
npm install
```

```bash
npm run dev
```

Depois, abra `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`.

| Ação | Teclado | Controle (PlayStation · Xbox) |
|---|---|---|
| Mover | WASD / setas | analógico esquerdo / D-pad |
| Pular (Rhaenyra) | Espaço | ✕ · A |
| Interagir / latir | E | ○ · B |
| Latir | — | □ · X |
| Fica / Vem (companheira) | F | △ · Y |
| Superbafo (Radhija): segure para mirar, solte para soprar | R | L2 · LT |
| Arrancada (Radhija) / empurrar (Rhaenyra), segurar | Shift | R1 ou R2 · RB ou RT |
| Trocar de cachorrinha | Q | L1 · LB |
| Pausar | Esc | Options · Start |

A tela desenha os botões no estilo PlayStation; se o controle conectado for de Xbox, no estilo Xbox.

## Fases

1. **Operação Cenoura**: fim de tarde no jardim. Cerca com abertura, cordinha do portão e carrinho.
2. **Operação Bolinha**: crepúsculo na área de serviço. Tábua de pressão, calço, irrigador e caixote que vira ponte.
3. **Operação Pantufa**: noite no jardim do lago. Duas pedras com lanternas e a Dona Gansa guardando a ponte.
4. **Operação Patinho**: manhã no terraço do prédio, a fase do superbafo da Radhija. Um pombo cochila na única
   passagem (latido não adianta, bafo sim); depois a Rhaenyra encaixa o ventilador no trilho, a Radhija passa por
   baixo dos canos dos aparelhos e sopra no vento, o duto leva o cheiro até o pombo do portão e ele voa para a placa.
5. **Operação Ursinho**: tarde de chuva dentro de casa, a fase do pulo da Rhaenyra. Ela pula o portãozinho de bebê
   e abre a trava para a irmã, pula a barricada de caixas da mudança e empurra de dentro a caixa de almofadas (que
   desmonta); o ursinho está debaixo da mesa, atrás da toalha comprida, onde só a Radhija cabe.

Parâmetros úteis: `?level=2` (começa na fase 2), `?play` (pula a tela inicial), `?debug` (colisores e grafo de navegação),
`?stage=<etapa>` (pula etapas do puzzle).

Protótipos fora do menu (fases de desenvolvimento):

- **Arena do Pulo**: `http://127.0.0.1:5173/?level=pulo&play`. Troncos dá para pular; muretas altas, não.
- **Arena do Bafo**: `http://127.0.0.1:5173/?level=bafo&play`. O protótipo do puzzle do superbafo que virou a fase 4: a Rhaenyra
  encaixa o ventilador, a Radhija sopra no corredor, o vento leva o cheiro pelo duto, o pombo foge para o poleiro da
  placa e o portão abre.

## Estrutura

- `src/game/`: núcleo genérico (gerenciador de fases, entrada, colisão, navegação, companheira, câmera, kit de puzzle e mecânicas).
- `src/levels/faseN/`: cada fase (`index.js` com a definição, `layout.js` com as coordenadas, `lighting.js`, `world/` com o cenário, carregado sob demanda, e `puzzle.js` com a lógica).
  `src/levels/_modelo/` é um modelo de fase completo e testado, ponto de partida das fases novas.
- `src/dogs/` e `src/characters/`: personagens procedurais.
- `src/ui/` e `src/fx/`: interface, áudio sintetizado, partículas e feedback.
- `src/types.d.ts`: tipos das APIs públicas (checados pelo TypeScript sobre o JavaScript).
- `test/`: testes rápidos em Node; `tools/`: partidas automatizadas no navegador e ferramentas.

Documentação:

- [docs/ARQUITETURA.md](docs/ARQUITETURA.md): como as peças se encaixam, APIs, eventos, testes e convenções.
- [docs/COMO-CRIAR-UMA-FASE.md](docs/COMO-CRIAR-UMA-FASE.md): passo a passo de uma fase nova.

## Testes

Os testes automáticos rodam nos servidores do GitHub. Envie o código com `git push`: o workflow
**CI e publicação** instala as dependências, checa os tipos, executa os testes rápidos e gera a build.
Quando tudo passa no `main`, publica o jogo no link acima. Se falhar, a versão anterior continua no ar.
Não é preciso gerar ou enviar a pasta `dist/`, nem rodar os testes no PC antes de cada envio.

As partidas completas ficam separadas: abra [Actions → E2E manual](https://github.com/raposocampos/radhija-rhaenyra/actions/workflows/e2e.yml),
clique em **Run workflow**, escolha o branch e a suíte (`todas` para a bateria completa) e confirme. Elas rodam em máquinas Linux do GitHub,
com uma suíte por máquina. As capturas ficam nos artefatos da execução por 7 dias.
Como essas máquinas não têm GPU, o navegador dos testes usa resolução 3D reduzida, sem sombras
nem bloom, desenha a cada 30 quadros e força um desenho antes de cada captura. A simulação e os
controles continuam em todos os quadros; as esperas acompanham o tempo do jogo. Essas partidas
verificam a jogabilidade, não o desempenho gráfico. A qualidade visual do jogo publicado não muda.

Os comandos abaixo continuam disponíveis para quem quiser rodar testes **localmente**:

| Comando | O que faz |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | testes em Node, cerca de 30 s: as 5 fases jogadas inteiras num jogo headless, navegação e colisão de todas as fases, cenário sem z-fighting (faces no mesmo plano "tremendo"), equilíbrio do irrigador, dogs e regressões de bugs já corrigidos |
| `npm run typecheck` | checagem de tipos (TypeScript sobre os comentários JSDoc) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | partidas com teclas reais no Chrome (fases 1–5, controle, regressões, pulo e bafo), cerca de 15 minutos |
| `npm run build` | roda `typecheck` e `npm test` antes de gerar `dist/`: nenhum build sai quebrado |
| `npm run verify` | build + partidas no navegador |

O `test:e2e` sobe sozinho um servidor Vite sem recarga automática numa porta livre (sem atrapalhar o `npm run dev`
na 5173), roda as partidas em sequência e derruba o servidor no fim, inclusive em erro ou Ctrl+C. Ele usa o Chrome
(ou o Edge) instalado no sistema. No GitHub, usa o Chromium instalado pela versão fixada do Playwright.
Também é possível escolher um executável com a variável `CHROME_PATH`.

Thibaut-L214/hidden-supermarket.readme:
# Le Supermarché invisible

Jeu web à la première personne, porté par L214. Le joueur se promène dans un supermarché ordinaire avec un scanner. Chaque produit animal est une porte : un scan fait pivoter le rayon et révèle ce que l'emballage cache, **produit → élevage → transport → abattoir → retour en rayon**. Aucune image violente : bâtiments stylisés, silhouettes, chiffres et sons synthétisés.

Jalon en cours : **M3, monde vivant et sortie**. Huit clients font leurs courses, la porte d’entrée coulisse, des militants de L214 tiennent une action sur le trottoir et l’écran de fin conclut la visite. Restent pour M4 la revue d’accessibilité, les mesures de performance sur appareils et le README final.

## Lancer en local

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Puis ouvrir http://localhost:5173/hidden-supermarket/.

## Vérifier

```bash
npm test                       # tests unitaires (Vitest)
npm run typecheck              # types TypeScript
npm run build && npm run e2e   # test de bout en bout (Playwright, ordinateur et mobile)
npm run size                   # budget de chargement : 5 Mo gzip au plus
```

## Paramètres d'adresse

- `?qualite=haute` ou `?qualite=basse` force le niveau de qualité (par défaut : basse sur écran tactile).
- `?effets=aucun` coupe le tramage.
- `?debug=1` expose `window.__game` pour les tests et le diagnostic.

## Publication

Chaque push sur `main` lance les vérifications, puis publie sur GitHub Pages : https://thibaut-l214.github.io/hidden-supermarket/. Une vérification en échec bloque la publication.

## Contenu

Tous les textes et chiffres sont dans `src/content/`, rien n'est écrit en dur ailleurs :

- `chains.ts` : les rayons, leurs chiffres et les sources, repris du jeu existant ;
- `copy.ts` et `captions.ts` : les consignes, messages et gabarits de légendes ;
- `screens.ts` : les textes de l'accueil, de la pause, des écrans d'erreur et des boutons du HUD ;
- `scenery.ts` : les textes du décor du magasin (panneaux, bannière, affiches, étiquettes promo) ;
- `links.ts` : les liens sortants.

`index.html` ne porte que la structure de la page (plus le titre et la description de l'onglet) : les écrans sont remplis depuis ces modules au démarrage.

## Chiffres à valider avant publication

Ordres de grandeur pour la France, sauf mention. Les plus approximatifs :

- la part de poulets élevés en bâtiment (plus de 80 %) ;
- la part de cochons sur caillebotis (environ 95 %) ;
- le million de bovins exportés vivants ;
- la production laitière par vache (plus de 7 000 L/an) ;
- le total annuel de volailles tuées.

Sources : Agreste (ministère de l'Agriculture), directives 1999/74/CE, 2007/43/CE et 2008/120/CE, règlements (CE) 1/2005 et 1099/2009, enquêtes L214, fishcount.org.uk.

## Licences

Polices IBM Plex Mono et IBM Plex Sans : SIL Open Font License (`public/fonts/OFL.txt`).

kitmop/jewel-jam.desc: Jewel Jam: 10-level match-3 browser game + Linux home-server setup
kitmop/jewel-jam.readme:
# Jewel Jam

A mobile-friendly **match-3 puzzle game** that runs entirely in the browser, plus everything you need to host it yourself on any Linux machine or for free on the web.

**Play it now:** https://kitmop.github.io/jewel-jam/

## The game

Jewel Jam is a 10-level match-3 game in the spirit of classic "swap and match" puzzlers, built for phones (iOS Safari in particular) but playable on any modern browser.

- **Play:** swipe a gem toward a neighbour, or tap two adjacent gems, to swap them. Line up 3 or more of the same shape to clear them. Gems above fall down and new ones drop in, so chain reactions (combos) score more.
- **Special gems:**
  - Match **4** in a row to make a line gem that clears a whole row or column.
  - Match in an **L or T** shape to make a bomb that clears a 3×3 area.
  - Match **5** in a row to make a colour bomb. Swap it with a gem to clear every gem of that colour.
  - Special gems can set each other off for chain reactions.
- **Goals:** each level has a score target and, depending on the level, a number of gems to collect and/or **jelly** tiles to clear (some tiles take two hits). You have a limited number of moves.
- **Stars:** 1 to 3 stars per level, plus a bonus for leftover moves. Levels unlock in order, and progress is saved in your browser.
- **Helpers:** a hint button, and an automatic reshuffle if no moves are left.
- **Phone-friendly:** full-screen "Add to Home Screen" support, no scrolling or zooming, safe-area aware layout, portrait and landscape.

The repo also contains an older bonus game, **Gem Rush** (`public/gemrush.html`), a small 3D arena game made with Three.js.

## Codebase

```
.
├── public/                  # the whole website (static files, no build step)
│   ├── index.html           # Jewel Jam: HTML, CSS and JS in one file
│   ├── gemrush.html         # Gem Rush (Three.js loaded from a CDN)
│   └── apple-touch-icon.png # home-screen icon for iOS
├── server.js                # tiny Express server that serves public/ (optional)
├── ecosystem.config.js      # PM2 process definition for running server.js
├── setup.sh                 # one-shot self-hosting setup for apt-based Linux
├── netlify.toml             # config for hosting on Netlify
├── .github/workflows/pages.yml  # deploys public/ to GitHub Pages on every push
└── package.json
```

How the game is built (`public/index.html`):

- **No framework, no bundler, no dependencies.** Vanilla JavaScript and a 2D canvas for the board. Open the file in a browser and it works.
- **Rendering:** gem sprites are drawn once per cell size onto offscreen canvases, then blitted every frame. Animations use a small promise-based tween system.
- **Game logic:** the board is a grid of piece objects. Matching, special-gem creation, chain reactions, gravity, refill and reshuffle live in `findMatches`, `expand`, `clearSet`, `gravity` and `resolve`. Levels are plain data in the `LEVELS` array at the top of the script, so adding or tweaking a level means editing one object.
- **Input:** pointer events (swipe and tap-tap) on the canvas. iOS gestures such as pull-to-refresh, pinch zoom, double-tap zoom and text selection are disabled.
- **Saving:** progress and the sound setting go to `localStorage` (the game still works if storage is blocked).
- **Test hooks:** open the page with `?debug` to expose `window.__game` (used for automated play-testing), and `?debug&fast` to skip animations.

## Run it locally

You need Node.js 20 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kitmop/jewel-jam.git
cd jewel-jam
npm install
npm start                # http://localhost:3000
```

Jewel Jam has no server-side logic, so any static file server works too, for example `python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory public`. Opening `public/index.html` directly in a browser also works.

## Put it online

Because the game is just static files, the easiest options need no server of your own and are free. Pick one.

### Option 1: GitHub Pages (what the live link uses)

The included workflow publishes `public/` automatically.

1. Fork this repo, or push it to a new **public** GitHub repo.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Push to `main` (or run the workflow from the **Actions** tab). When it finishes, your site is at `https://<your-username>.github.io/<repo-name>/`.

### Option 2: Cloudflare Pages (free, URL ends in `.pages.dev`)

1. Sign in at the Cloudflare dashboard and go to **Workers & Pages → Create application → Pages → Connect to Git**.
2. Pick your GitHub repo and click **Begin setup**.
3. Set **Production branch** to `main`, leave **Build command** empty, and set **Build output directory** to `public`.
4. Click **Save and Deploy**. Your site will be at `https://<project-name>.pages.dev`, and every push redeploys it.

### Option 3: Netlify (free, URL ends in `.netlify.app`)

1. Sign in at netlify.com and choose **Add new site → Import an existing project**, then pick your GitHub repo.
2. `netlify.toml` already sets the publish directory to `public`. Leave the build command empty.
3. Deploy. You get `https://<site-name>.netlify.app`, and you can rename the site under **Site configuration**.

> Options 2 and 3 follow the providers' documentation but have not been test-deployed from this repo. Option 1 is the one that has been deployed and checked.

### Option 4: Host it on your own Linux machine

See the next section.

## Self-hosting on a Linux machine

Useful if you want full control, or want to keep the game on your own network. Any always-on Linux box works: a spare laptop, a mini PC, a Raspberry Pi, a home server or a VPS.

**What you need**

- A systemd-based distro. `setup.sh` targets **apt-based** ones (Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Raspberry Pi OS, and so on). On Fedora, Arch and others, follow the manual steps below with your own package manager.
- Node.js 20 or newer, and `sudo` access.

### The quick way (apt-based distros)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/

# Inklingo

*Ink* (mực vẽ) + *lingo* (ngôn ngữ) – vẽ, đoán và nhớ từ vựng TOEIC. Trước đây dự án có tên tạm “Scribble Words”.

Game web vẽ & đoán từ kết hợp lộ trình học **5 từ vựng TOEIC mỗi ngày theo chủ đề công sở** (trình độ B1–B2,
dành cho người chơi đã đạt TOEIC 450+).
Phát triển tiếp từ bản demo `scribble_words_v2.html` (bản gốc giữ tại `docs/scribble_words_v2_original.html`).

## Chạy game

Yêu cầu: Node.js ≥ 20, nên dùng 22 (không cần cài thêm thư viện nào; test WebSocket cần Node 22, bản cũ hơn sẽ bỏ qua các test đó).

```bash
npm start
```

Mở http://localhost:8787. Bạn bè trong cùng mạng LAN mở `http://<IP-máy-bạn>:8787` rồi nhập mã phòng
(hoặc mở link mời `…/#/join/MÃPHÒNG`). Đổi cổng: `PORT=9000 npm start`.

Kiểm thử tự động (luật chơi + server WebSocket thật):

```bash
npm test
```

Kiểm thử engine vẽ trong trình duyệt: mở `http://localhost:8787/dev/draw-test.html`, chạy trong console
`(await import('/dev/engine-tests.js')).run(T)`.

## Deploy (Render)

`render.yaml` mô tả dịch vụ: Node 22 (test tích hợp dùng `WebSocket` có sẵn từ Node 22), gói Starter (chạy liên tục), vùng Singapore, ổ đĩa 1 GB gắn tại `/var/data`
cho file nhóm học (`GROUPS_FILE=/var/data/groups.json`), kiểm tra sức khỏe `/api/health`, build bằng `npm test` (deploy
dừng nếu test lỗi), tự deploy khi push lên `main`, tên miền `inklingo.io.vn` và `www.inklingo.io.vn`.
Server chỉ chạy **1 instance** (phòng chơi realtime nằm trong bộ nhớ). DNS ở Tenten: bản ghi A cho `@` trỏ về IP Render
cung cấp và CNAME `www` trỏ về `<dịch vụ>.onrender.com`.

## Giao diện

- Phong cách “giấy & mực” (lấy cảm hứng từ doodlingam.com, không dùng lại logo, hình hay nội dung của họ): nền giấy kem
  `#f4eddc`, thẻ `#fbf7ec`, chữ nâu mực `#3b2a1e`, một màu nhấn đỏ đất `#bc4b24` và xanh rêu `#1c3a28`; tiêu đề font
  Fraunces (chữ nghiêng làm điểm nhấn), nội dung Source Sans 3 (Google Fonts); viền mảnh, bóng mềm, nút bo tròn.
  Toàn bộ màu nằm trong biến CSS ở đầu `public/css/app.css`.
- Không dùng emoji trong giao diện: mọi biểu tượng là icon SVG dạng nét tự vẽ (`public/js/ui/icons.js`), hiển thị giống
  nhau trên mọi hệ điều hành. Ảnh đại diện là vòng tròn màu với chữ cái đầu của tên (hồ sơ cũ dùng emoji được tự chuyển
  sang màu).
- Bố cục dashboard: **thanh bên** (Trang chủ · Học hôm nay · Chủ đề · Ôn tập · Nhóm · Thống kê | Cài đặt · Trợ giúp)
  và **thanh trên** (tìm kiếm ⌘K/Ctrl K theo từ tiếng Anh, nghĩa tiếng Việt không dấu hoặc chủ đề – từ chưa học bị khóa;
  số ngày học liên tiếp; menu hồ sơ để đổi hồ sơ). Tablet: thanh bên chỉ còn icon; điện thoại: thanh tab ở đáy.
  Trong phòng chơi thanh bên ẩn để bảng vẽ rộng hơn.
- Trang chủ: khối chào với 3 thẻ ảnh thật của từ hôm nay, nút “Bắt đầu học hôm nay” và “Chơi nhanh”; hàng chủ đề cuộn
  ngang; “Học nhanh” (Tạo phòng, Vào phòng, Học từ mới, Ôn tập); cột phải: tiến độ (vòng % chủ đề, số chủ đề, từ đã học,
  đang ôn, ngày liên tiếp) và danh sách 5 từ hôm nay có nút nghe và ô đánh dấu đã học.
- Trang **Thống kê** (tiến độ từng chủ đề, điểm kiểm tra, từ hay quên) và **Trợ giúp** (luật chơi ngắn + phím tắt).
- Không làm các phần của bản thiết kế chưa có cơ chế thật: cấp/XP, chuông thông báo, “Gợi ý chủ đề” (thay bằng “Chơi
  nhanh”); hình minh họa vẽ tay được thay bằng ảnh chụp thật của từ (GDD §12).
- Flashcard: chuyển từ bằng phím ← →; kết quả đúng/sai trong bài kiểm tra và ôn tập có màu và icon rõ ràng.

## Tài khoản & Cài đặt

- **Tài khoản** (`#/account`, của hồ sơ đang dùng): tên hiển thị; ảnh đại diện là **màu + chữ cái đầu** hoặc **tự vẽ**
  (khung vẽ tròn: bút, tẩy, đổ nền, hoàn tác; lưu PNG 128 px); các hồ sơ trên máy (đổi, tạo, xóa); nhóm học (mở trang nhóm,
  mã khôi phục, rời nhóm); xóa tiến độ.
  Ảnh tự vẽ có mã `p` + 16 hex (SHA-256 của PNG) và đi qua phòng chơi/nhóm như mã màu `c0…c11`; server lưu ảnh ở
  `POST /api/avatar` → `GET /api/avatar/<mã>` (thư mục `AVATAR_DIR`, mặc định cạnh `GROUPS_FILE`, tối đa 24 KB/ảnh, chỉ PNG,
  30 lần/giờ/IP). Khi offline ảnh vẫn hiện trên máy mình và được tải lên lại khi mở app có mạng.
- **Cài đặt** (`#/settings`, của thiết bị, lưu ở `localStorage` `sw:prefs`): giao diện **Sáng / Tối / Theo hệ thống**, cỡ chữ
  Nhỏ/Vừa/Lớn (không đổi kích thước phòng vẽ), giảm hiệu ứng chuyển động; **ngôn ngữ giao diện Tiếng Việt / English**;
  giọng đọc (chọn giọng tiếng Anh của trình duyệt, tốc độ, tự đọc từ khi hiện đáp án); nguồn ảnh; ngày giả lập (kiểm thử).
- **Ngôn ngữ:** chữ giao diện viết bằng tiếng Việt trong `tr('…')` (`public/js/i18n.js`), bản tiếng Anh ở
  `public/js/i18n/en.js` (giá trị có thể là `[số ít, số nhiều]`); câu server gửi về được dịch bằng `tServer()`. Đổi ngôn ngữ
  tải lại trang (giữ nguyên tiến độ và trang đang mở). Nghĩa/giải thích từ vựng vẫn bằng tiếng Việt. Kiểm tra thiếu bản dịch:
  `python3 tools/i18n_keys.py` (test `tests/i18n.test.js` cũng kiểm tra).

## Vẽ & đoán: gợi ý

- **Gợi ý chữ cái cho người đoán:** khi chưa ai đoán đúng ở 50 %, 70 % và 85 % thời gian vẽ, server mở thêm 1 chữ cái của từ
  (ô chữ hiện đúng chữ ở đúng vị trí, chat báo "Gợi ý: hiện thêm 1 chữ cái"). Tối đa 1/3 số chữ cái, từ ≤ 3 chữ cái không có
  gợi ý, và không bao giờ mở hết từ. Có người đoán đúng rồi thì dừng gợi ý.
- **Ghost Sketch (trợ lý vẽ cấp 5):** mặc định là **hình mẫu nét** vẽ tay riêng cho từng từ (nét viền sạch, ít chi tiết), hiện
  mờ dưới canvas chỉ người vẽ thấy. Vẫn chọn được "Đường viền từ ảnh thật" (lọc cạnh từ ảnh) hoặc bố cục người que.
  486/486 từ có mẫu nét: nguồn ở `tools/ghost_src/<chủ đề>.txt` (`=== <id>` + thân SVG 1600×1000), build bằng
  `python3 tools/ghosts.py build` ra `public/data/ghosts/<id>.svg`; `python3 tools/ghosts.py sheet <chủ đề>` dựng bảng duyệt,
  `missing` liệt kê từ thiếu mẫu. Mẫu do Inklingo tự vẽ bằng mã, không dùng AI hay tài sản của trò chơi khác.

## Ôn tập: Word Recall

Ôn bằng cách **tự nhớ lại và gõ từ** (không trắc nghiệm), mỗi phiên tối đa 10 từ, 2–4 phút.

- **3 thử thách luân phiên** cho mỗi từ: *Nghe và viết* (chỉ có âm thanh + số chữ cái) · *Nhớ nghĩa* (nghĩa và giải thích

# Deep Drill

A hold-to-drill mining game for Android. The game itself is a single HTML/canvas
file (`app/src/main/assets/index.html`) shown full-screen in a WebView.

## Run it

1. In Android Studio: **File > New > Project from Version Control**, paste this repo's URL.
2. Let Gradle sync (it downloads Gradle 8.7 and the Android Gradle Plugin automatically).
3. Plug in your phone with **USB debugging** on, pick it as the target, and press **Run**.

To get an installable file: **Build > Build Bundle(s) / APK(s) > Build APK(s)**.
The debug APK appears in `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/`.

## Requirements

- Android Studio with JDK 17 or newer (the bundled one is fine)
- Phone running Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer

## How to play

- Hold anywhere to lower the drill and dig. Rock breaks fast, gems take longer.
- Tap the **$100** note (top right) to upgrade the drill. Each level drills faster, up to level 10.
- Tap **SURFACE** (bottom right) to ride back up to the grass. Hold to go back down.
- Progress (cash, depth, upgrade level) is saved on the phone.

## Edit the game

Change `app/src/main/assets/index.html` and run again. No other files need to change.
